<title level="1" pfs="Standard">[Animated Broom](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2818)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

Animated brooms perform menial tasks of cleaning and upkeep, but they can step in to defend a room from intrusion if needed. These simple animated objects can be found with greater frequency than more complicated and costly objects.

<column gap="tiny">
**[Recall Knowledge - Construct](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**
([Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35), [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=37)): DC 13

**[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 11

**[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 8
</column>

</column>

<column gap="medium">
<image src="/images/Monsters/Animated_Broom.webp" />
</column>

</row>

<title level="2" right="Creature -1">[Animated Broom](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2818)</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Small" />
<trait label="Construct" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=563" />
<trait label="Mindless" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=652" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Monster Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=221) pg. 18 <sup>1.1</sup>

**Perception** +3; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59)

**Languages**

**Skills**
[Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) +5

<row gap="medium">
**Str** +0

**Dex** +1

**Con** +0

**Int** -5

**Wis** +0

**Cha** -5
</row>

</column>

---

<column gap="tiny">

<row gap="medium">
**AC** 15 (13 when broken)

**Fort** +3 

**Ref** +6 

**Will** +3 

construct armor
</row>

<row gap="medium">
**HP** 6

**Hardness**
2
</row>

**Immunities**
bleed, [death](/Traits.aspx?ID=571) effects, [disease](/Traits.aspx?ID=578), [doomed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=67), [drained](/Conditions.aspx?ID=68), [fatigued](/Conditions.aspx?ID=73), [healing](/Traits.aspx?ID=623), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647), [nonlethal](/Traits.aspx?ID=661) attacks, [paralyzed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=85), [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=669), [sickened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=91), [spirit](/Traits.aspx?ID=737), [unconscious](/Conditions.aspx?ID=95), [vitality](/Traits.aspx?ID=509), [void](/Traits.aspx?ID=510)

**Construct Armor** Like normal objects, an animated broom has Hardness. This Hardness reduces any damage it takes by an amount equal to the Hardness. Once an animated broom is reduced to less than half its Hit Points, or immediately upon being damaged by a critical hit, its construct armor breaks, removing the Hardness and reducing its Armor Class to 13.

</column>

---

<column gap="tiny">

**Speed** 15 feet

**Melee**
<actions string="Single Action" />
bristles +6 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103), [Finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=179)),
**Damage** 1d4 bludgeoning plus dust

**Dust**   A creature hit by an animated broom's bristles must succeed at a DC 15 Fortitude save or spend its next action coughing. Even if hit by multiple dust attacks, the creature has to spend only 1 action coughing to clear the dust out. A creature who doesn't breathe is immune to this effect.

</column>

<title level="1" pfs="">[Apprentice](/NPCs.aspx?ID=3411)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

Ambitious apprentices can be found in all cities. These individuals are generally younger and seek the approval of their masters as they learn their craft. Many yearn to exemplify the artistry behind their craft, one day becoming masters themselves. Depicted below is an apprentice cartographer.

<column gap="tiny">

([Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=47)): DC 13

</column>

</column>

</column>

</row>

<trait label="Humanoid" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=628" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [NPC Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=236) pg. 8

**Perception** +2

**Languages**
[Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1)

**Skills**
[Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) +3, [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=37) +5, [Geography Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) +5

<row gap="medium">
**Str** +1

**Dex** +2

**Con** +1

**Int** +3

**Wis** +0

**Cha** +0
</row>

**Items**
[Artisan's Toolkit](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2703), [assorted maps](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3585), [Dagger](/Weapons.aspx?ID=3), rugged clothes with tool belt (functions as [padded armor](/Armor.aspx?ID=40))

</column>

---

<column gap="tiny">

<row gap="medium">

**Fort** +5 

**Ref** +6 

**Will** +2

<row gap="medium">

</row>

---

<column gap="tiny">

**Melee**

<title level="1" pfs="Standard">[Compsognathus](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2914)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

The compsognathus is a small bipedal dinosaur that moves in swift, darting motions. Its bite injects a venom that causes numbness and weakness, a trait the animal uses to bring down larger prey, although it prefers to scavenge or snatch insects and other smaller creatures for its meals.

 The compsognathus is curious to a fault, often getting itself into trouble. It measures 3 feet long from head to tail and weighs 15 pounds—small enough to serve as a house pet or familiar for a spellcaster. In cases where magical links aren't involved, however, those keeping the creature would be well-advised to treat it with the same caution one might extend to a pet viper or other poisonous reptile, as they're partly tame at best.

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

Most giant centipedes (known as sewer centipedes when found in cities) nest in small groups but hunt alone when they seek out food. Attempts to domesticate giant centipedes for use as guardians or pets generally end poorly, but some communities of goblins, kobolds, and mitflits have developed effective methods of utilizing these vermin as guardians. Other groups roast and eat centipedes, often with pungent peppers as a savory delicacy, although care must be taken in preparing the meal to avoid tainting the flesh with the creature's venom.

<title level="1" pfs="Standard">[Giant Rat](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3162)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

Giant rats are enormous versions of the common vermin. They are typically found in abundant numbers, but since they cannot fit in the nooks where mundane rats typically hide, they are much easier to locate and exterminate. They mostly live in sewers where they can scavenge from the streets above, but some families of giant rats live in more remote locations, such as dank caves, forests or hills. Rats are incredibly adept survivors and can be found nearly anywhere in the world, though they tend to favor temperate or warm climates as opposed to cold regions.

 Although its bite alone is not lethal except to the very young or very old, the giant rat carries the putrid plague common to rodents around the world—a pestilence more than capable of ravaging rural communities.

text: Gnome Philomath The innate gnomish inclination to revel in new experiences leads gnome philomaths to delve as deeply as they can into the multitudes of knowledge contained within a library. These shrewd observers have encyclopedic memories and tend to surround themselves with piles of documents and trinkets pertaining to whatever subject currently holds their attention. As their interests branch from one topic to the next, a gnome philomath files away their discoveries to be referenced again another day. <row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

The typical guard dog is loyal and beloved by many communities. Often adored as pets, they excel as protectors and trackers, and can be fearless when defending a beloved master or family member. The statistics presented below work well for numerous breeds of dog ranging from 20 to 50 pounds in weight. Wild dogs can also use these statistics, but their untamed nature makes them far more unpredictable. Feral canines are perhaps even more dangerous, for unlike their wild cousins, feral dogs often lack the instinctual fear of humanity that stops wild creatures from interacting with people.

**Fated Doom**   Though harrow readers try to avoid combat, no throw of the cards can avoid fate, so a harrow reader learns how best to survive. In the harrow reader's first encounter each day, they gain a +1 status bonus to their initiative roll, attack rolls, and AC.

**Read the Harrow**  ([Exploration](/Traits.aspx?ID=66), [Occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=120), [Prediction](/Traits.aspx?ID=132)) The harrow reader can conduct a reading over the course of 10 minutes to duplicate the effects of the [_augury_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1445) spell. The harrow reader can conduct up to five readings per day, but the flat check DC increases by 2. This is cumulative, to a maximum of DC 14 for the fifth.

<title level="1" pfs="Standard">[Inkdrop](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2761)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

Not all handcrafts are intended for war. The inkdrop is an infiltrator used by spellcasters to learn secrets or alter documents. Embodied in a single fist-sized drop of ink, the inkdrop can glide across a page, changing characters or removing them altogether, with devastating consequences for statecraft.

<column gap="tiny">
**[Recall Knowledge - Construct](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**
([Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=2), [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=4)): DC 13

**[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 11

**[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 8
</column>

</column>

<column gap="medium">

</column>

</row>

<title level="2" right="Creature -1">[Inkdrop](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2761)</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Tiny" />
<trait label="Construct" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=35" />
<trait label="Mindless" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=108" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Tian Xia World Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=223) pg. 278

**Perception** +6; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=12)

**Languages**

**Skills**
[Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) +2, [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15) +3

<row gap="medium">
**Str** +0

**Dex** -3

**Con** +2

**Int** -5

**Wis** +0

**Cha** -5
</row>

**Perfect Memory** An inkdrop remembers the exact pattern of any ink it moves over physically.

</column>

---

<column gap="tiny">

<row gap="medium">
**AC** 7 

**Fort** +2 

**Ref** +6 

**Will** +5 

</row>

<row gap="medium">
**HP** 15

</row>

**Immunities**
critical hits, mental, precision, spirit, unconscious, vitality, void

**Weaknesses**
cold 5, fire 5

**Blotting** While a creature has the inkdrop [grabbed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=77) or [pinned](/Conditions.aspx?ID=54), it can destroy the inkdrop by smudging the inkdrop out with an Interact action.

</column>

---

<column gap="tiny">

**Speed** 10 feet, climb 10 feet

**Melee**
<actions string="Single Action" />
pseudopod +6,
**Damage** 1d4 bludgeoning plus blinding ink

**Blinding Ink**   A creature critically struck by the inkdrop's pseudopod is blinded by the ink until it clears its eyes using an Interact action.

**Ink Blot** <actions string="Single Action" />  The inkdrop leaves a pattern it remembers over a square foot of surface. If there's existing non-magical ink on the surface, the inkdrop erases the non- magical ink.

</column>

**Legal Specialist** In a legal proceeding, the judge is a 6th-level challenge. **Items** gavel (functions as a [club](/Weapons.aspx?ID=357)), judge's robes, _Law and Rhetoric_ --- **AC** 13 **Fort** +5 **Ref** +1 **Will** +12 **HP** 5 --- **Speed** 25 feet **Melee** gavel +4, **Damage** 1d6 bludgeoning **Melee** fist +4 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [Nonlethal](/Traits.aspx?ID=188), [Unarmed](/Traits.aspx?ID=199)), **Damage** 1d4 bludgeoning **Ranged** gavel +3 ([thrown 10 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=195)), **Damage** 1d4 bludgeoning **Remember, You're Under Oath** ([Auditory](/Traits.aspx?ID=16), [Concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32), [Emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=60), [Fear](/Traits.aspx?ID=68), [Mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=106)) The judge reminds a creature of the oath they swore to the court. The judge makes an [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=40) check against the target' s Will DC. On a success, the target takes a –2 status penalty to [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38) checks to [Lie](/Actions.aspx?ID=2389) for 10 minutes (or a –4 status penalty on a critical success). <title level="1" pfs="Standard">[Kobold Warrior](/NPCs.aspx?ID=3072)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

The typical kobold trains in tunnel fighting, learning to use simple weapons that are effective in narrow spaces. Kobolds are capable of landing sneaky strikes against unsuspecting foes, but are just as quick to scamper off to safety when they don't outnumber their enemies by at least two to one.

<column gap="tiny">
**[Recall Knowledge - Humanoid](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**
([Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=47)): DC 13

<trait label="Kobold" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=759" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Monster Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=221) pg. 210 <sup>1.1</sup>

**Perception** +3; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59)

**Languages**
[Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1), [Sakvroth](/Languages.aspx?ID=118)

**Skills**
[Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=1) +5, [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=4) +2, [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15) +5

<row gap="medium">

**Con** -1

<column gap="tiny">

<row gap="medium">

**Will** +3

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="tiny">

**Damage** 1d6+1 piercing

<title level="1" pfs="Standard">[Mitflit](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3031)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

Mitflits are self-loathing and pitiful cowards, easily bullied into servitude by other creatures or even slightly more powerful mitflit leaders. They tame insects, spiders, and other small vermin to serve as faithful allies. Mitflits have lost most of their ancestral magic, leaving them to feel incomplete and full of doubt and insecurity. Mitflits find companionship in the other base creatures of the world, and forge strong bonds of friendship with vermin, the only other beings that seem willing to accept them. A social structure, even one in which they are bullied, partially fills the hole within most mitflits' personalities, and they rarely rebel or last out unless their rage hits a breaking point.

Academia rewards specialization, and so the universities and athenaeums of the Inner Sea are full to the brim of sunlight-deprived scholars who are the world experts in such obscure topics such as the migratory habits of bogwids or the folklore of pre-Choral Brevoy. **[Recall Knowledge - Humanoid](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=47)): DC 13 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 11 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 8 [Obsessive Researcher](/NPCs.aspx?ID=3588) **Source** [NPC Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=236) pg. 138 **Perception** +3 **Languages** [Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1); up to 3 additional uncommon languages **Skills** [Academia Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) +19, [Library Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) +23, [Narrow Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) +25, [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=48) +5 **Str** +0 **Dex** +1 **Con** +2 **Int** +5 **Wis** +0 **Cha** -1 **Monomania** Each obsessive researcher is preoccupied with a hyper-specialized, niche body of knowledge (their Narrow Lore) in which they are the acknowledged world authority. The catch is that when such an expert goes wrong, they go badly wrong— if an obsessive researcher gets a success on a [Narrow Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) roll, they get a critical success instead. But if they roll a failure, then they get a critical failure instead.

**[Recall Knowledge - Ethereal](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=11)): DC 18 **[Recall Knowledge - Spirit](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=11)): DC 18 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 16 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 13 [Phantom Raven](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2730) **Source** [Pathfinder #196: The Summer That Never Was](/Sources.aspx?ID=214) pg. 15 **Perception** +5; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=12) **Languages** [Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1) **Skills** [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=1) +5, [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=7) +4 **Str** -5 **Dex** +3 **Con** +0 **Int** -3 **Wis** +3 **Cha** +0 **Walk the Ethereal Line** The phantom walks the thin line between the [Ethereal](/Equipment.aspx?ID=284) and [Material Planes](/Planes.aspx?ID=1) in order to exist on both planes simultaneously. They can shift back to solely the Ethereal Plane by using this ability again. --- **AC** 15 **Fort** +2 **Ref** +7 **Will** +5 **HP** 6 **Immunities** [disease](/Traits.aspx?ID=46), [paralyzed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=28), [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=126), precision **Resistances** all damage 1 (except [force](/Traits.aspx?ID=75) or [_ghost touch_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=297); double resistance vs. non-[magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103)) **Susceptible to Death** Though phantoms aren't alive, neither are they [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=160), and they are uniquely vulnerable to the effects of death. **Vulnerable to Kindness** Any creature within 30 feet that the phantom can see and hear can issue a calm and friendly greeting to it as a two-action activity with the [auditory](/Traits.aspx?ID=16), [concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32), [linguistic](/Traits.aspx?ID=101), and [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=106) traits. **Critical Success** The phantom takes 4d8 mental damage and is [stunned 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=36).

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

Hardy root leshies have the strength and stamina to dig furrows for planting seeds over long hours. Though they're humble even among leshies, they can be extremely stubborn even against powerful adversaries.

<column gap="tiny">
**[Recall Knowledge - Plant](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**
([Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43)): DC 13

**[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 11

**[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 8
</column>

</column>

<column gap="medium">
<image src="/images/Monsters/Root_Leshy_Groundskeeper.webp" />
</column>

</row>

<traits>
<trait label="Small" />
<trait label="Leshy" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=639" />
<trait label="Plant" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=668" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [NPC Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=236) pg. 200

**Perception** +5; [low-light vision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=69)

**Languages**
[Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1), [Fey](/Languages.aspx?ID=119); [_speak with plants_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1681) (root vegetables only)

**Skills**
[Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) +5, [Labor Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) +2, [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43) +5, [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=48) +4, [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=49) +5

<row gap="medium">
**Str** +3

**Dex** +0

**Con** +3

**Int** -1

**Wis** +2

**Cha** +0
</row>

**Items**
shovel (functions as [pick](/Weapons.aspx?ID=389))

</column>

---

<column gap="tiny">

<row gap="medium">
**AC** 14 

**Fort** +8 

**Ref** +2 

**Will** +5 

</row>

<row gap="medium">
**HP** 9

</row>

**Verdant Burst** ([healing](/Traits.aspx?ID=623), [primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=676), [vitality](/Traits.aspx?ID=509)) When the root leshy groundskeeper dies, a burst of primal energy explodes from their body, restoring 1d4 Hit Points to each plant creature in a 30-foot emanation. This area immediately fills with roots and vines, becoming [difficult terrain](/Rules.aspx?ID=453). If the terrain is not a viable environment for these plants, they wither after 24 hours.

</column>

---

<column gap="tiny">

**Speed** 25 feet

**Melee**
<actions string="Single Action" />
shovel +5 ([fatal d10](/Traits.aspx?ID=178)),
**Damage** 1d6+3 piercing

**Melee**
<actions string="Single Action" />
fist +5 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [Nonlethal](/Traits.aspx?ID=188), [Unarmed](/Traits.aspx?ID=199)),
**Damage** 1d4+3 bludgeoning

**Primal Innate Spells** DC 13
- **Constant (3rd)**
[Speak with Plants](/Spells.aspx?ID=294) (root vegetables only)

**[Change Shape](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=55)** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([Concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32), [Polymorph](/Traits.aspx?ID=127), [Primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=134)) The root leshy groundskeeper transforms into a Small root vegetable. This ability otherwise uses the effects of [_one with plants_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1618).

**Root in Place** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([Manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104), [Primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=134)) The root leshy groundskeeper roots themself into the ground, reducing their Speed to 0 and granting them a +1 circumstance bonus to AC and 2 temporary Hit Points until the start of their next turn.

</column>

<title level="1" pfs="Standard">[Sprite](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3210)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

Common sprites, sometimes called firefly sprites, are primeval guardians that latch onto a person, place, or object and defend it for their own inscrutable reasons. Their dispositions vary from kind to spiteful, but all sprites have a capricious streak. Being only about 9 inches tall, they are wary of animals that might hunt them, particularly house cats, and prefer flight to a fight. On the other hand, sprites are incredibly curious about all forms of magic and heedlessly gather around ley line nexuses or other places of power.

[cold iron](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2916) 2

**Plaque Burst** When killed, a tooth fairy bursts into sticky, foul-smelling white dust. Each creature in a 5-foot emanation must succeed at a DC 16 Fortitude save or become [sickened 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=91) (sickened 2 on a critical failure).

</column>

<column gap="tiny">

**Speed** 10 feet, fly 25 feet

<actions string="Single Action" />
pliers +7 ([Disarm](/Traits.aspx?ID=175), [Finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=179), [reach 0 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)),

**Primal Innate Spells** DC 13
- **Cantrips (1st)**
[Telekinetic Hand](/Spells.aspx?ID=1715)
- **1st**
[Sleep](/Spells.aspx?ID=288)

**Tooth Tug** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([Manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104)) **Requirements** The tooth fairy's last action was a successful pliers Strike against a creature with teeth; **Effect** The tooth fairy attempts a [Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=50) check against the creature's Fortitude DC, dealing 2 [persistent bleed damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29) on any result but a critical failure. On a critical success, it also pulls out one of the target's teeth. If the creature loses a tooth, it takes a –1 status penalty to Charisma-based skill checks and must succeed at a DC 5 flat check to Cast a Spell unless that spell has the [subtle](/Traits.aspx?ID=522) trait. These effects last for 1 day, or until the stolen tooth is returned and the target regains at least 1 Hit Point.

</column>

Although their escapades might be notorious, few urchins are thrill-seekers. For some urchins, when begging alone isn't enough to fill their bellies, theft becomes a viable survival tactic. An animated kite is perfect for spying, allowing observation from a great distance, although many are treated more like pets. The kite itself is a simple handcraft, easily created and destroyed, made of enchanted paper stretched over a fine bamboo frame. More advanced kites can be decorated with a variety of runes that allow the enchanter to see or hear from a distance. **[Recall Knowledge - Construct](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=2), [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=4)): DC 14 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 12 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 9 [Animated Kite](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2762) **Source** [Tian Xia World Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=223) pg. 278 **Perception** +6; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=12) **Languages** **Skills** [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=1) +7 **Str** +0 **Dex** +3 **Con** +0 **Int** -5 **Wis** +0 **Cha** -5 --- **AC** 15 (13 when broken); construct armor **Fort** +4 **Ref** +9 **Will** +4 **HP** 15 **Hardness** 1 **Immunities** bleed, death effects, disease, doomed, drained, fatigued, healing, mental, nonlethal attacks, paralyzed, poison, sickened, spirit, unconscious, vitality, void **Construct Armor** Like normal objects, an animated kite has Hardness. This Hardness reduces any damage it takes by an amount equal to the Hardness. Once an animated kite is reduced to less than half its Hit Points, or immediately upon being damaged by a critical hit, its construct armor breaks and its Armor Class is reduced to 13.
 --- **Speed** fly 30 ft **Melee** frame +7 ([Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103), [Finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=179)), **Damage** 1d6 bludgeoning **Attach Line** ([Manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104)) The animated kite gives its line to an adjacent ally with a free hand. The kite remains attached until the creature releases it or the kite flies more than 60 feet away. A creature between them can also sever the line with a successful Strike against AC 13 that deals any amount of slashing damage. **Sawing Line** **Requirements** The animated kite has its line attached to an ally; **Effect** Each creature along the line between the kite and its ally takes 1d6 slashing damage (DC 16 basic Reflex save).
name: Animated Kite

Kholos have a strong connection to their ancestors, often using their bones as art and weapons to further honor them. Bone scavengers are sent to the fields after a battle to collect the bones of their fellow allies. They often eschew the pack hunting techniques of other kholos, spreading out among their foes when encountered in groups.

The bottlenose dolphin is the most common and widespread species of dolphin. They are social predators who hunt shallow seas and rivers in large family groups called pods. Sailors are fond of bottlenose dolphins and frequently tell of how they've saved drowning mariners or protected crew from sharks with blows from their powerful snouts. **[Recall Knowledge - Animal](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43)): DC 14 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 12 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 9 [Bottlenose Dolphin](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2926) **Source** [Monster Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=221) pg. 103 1.1 **Perception** +7; aquatic echolocation 120 feet, [low-light vision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=69) **Languages** **Skills** [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) +6 **Str** +2 **Dex** +3 **Con** +2 **Int** -4 **Wis** +3 **Cha** +0 **Aquatic Echolocation** A bottlenose dolphin can use its hearing as a [precise](/Rules.aspx?ID=411) sense at the listed range, but only underwater.
**Deep Breath** A bottlenose dolphin can [hold its breath](/Rules.aspx?ID=468) for 2 hours. --- **AC** 15 **Fort** +6 **Ref** +7 **Will** +5 **HP** 16 --- **Speed** swim 60 feet **Melee** snout +6, **Damage** 1d6+2 bludgeoning **Melee** jaws +6, **Damage** 1d6+2 piercing **Ramming Speed** The bottlenose dolphin Swims twice and then makes a snout Strike. As long as it moved at least 20 feet, it gains a +1 circumstance bonus to its attack roll. A Large or smaller creature hit by this attack must succeed at a DC 16 Fortitude save or be [slowed 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=92) for 1 round.

Conspiracists misinform and falsify facts to further their own causes. Though they pose little physical threat, conspiracists can have more powerful allies, such as a [deluded mob](/NPCs.aspx?ID=3611) that respond to the conspiracist's signal. **[Recall Knowledge - Humanoid](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=47)): DC 14 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 12 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 9 [Conspiracist](/NPCs.aspx?ID=3606) **Source** [NPC Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=236) pg. 152 **Perception** +8 **Languages** [Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1) **Skills** [Conspiracy Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) +11, [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38) +10, [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=44) -1, [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=45) +10, [Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=47) +11 **Str** +0 **Dex** +2 **Con** +0 **Int** +3 **Wis** +0 **Cha** +4 **Compulsive Liar** The conspiracist can use [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38) instead of [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39) to [Make an Impression](/Actions.aspx?ID=2392) or [Request](/Actions.aspx?ID=2393). Any creature attempting a Perception check to [Sense Motive](/Actions.aspx?ID=2302) against the conspiracist gets a result one degree of success worse than they rolled.
**Social Specialist** For encounters involving deception and social manipulation, the conspiracist is a 4th-level challenge. **Items** [Signal Whistle](/Equipment.aspx?ID=50), [Writing Set](/Equipment.aspx?ID=63) --- **AC** 14 **Fort** +4 **Ref** +6 **Will** +10 **HP** 15 **Evoke Pity** ([auditory](/Traits.aspx?ID=541), [concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=590), [linguistic](/Traits.aspx?ID=642), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647)) **Trigger** An enemy reduces the conspiracist to below half their maximum HP; **Effect** The conspiracist begs their assailants to “see reason” and let them live. The conspiracist attempts a single Performance check against the Will DCs of all enemies in a 30-foot emanation. Any creature the attempt succeeds against takes a –2 circumstance penalty to damaging attacks without the [nonlethal](/Traits.aspx?ID=661) trait they make against the conspiracist for 10 minutes. --- **Speed** 25 feet **Melee** fist +4 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [Finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=179), [Nonlethal](/Traits.aspx?ID=188), [Unarmed](/Traits.aspx?ID=199)), **Damage** 1d4 bludgeoning **Sow Doubt** ([Auditory](/Traits.aspx?ID=16), [Concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32), [Emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=60), [Linguistic](/Traits.aspx?ID=101), [Mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=106)) The conspiracist argues that their enemies have been hoodwinked into attacking them by nefarious powers. The conspiracist attempts a single [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38) check against the Will DCs of all enemies that can hear them.
**Critical Success** The enemy fully believes the conspiracist, becoming [stupefied 2](/Conditions.aspx?ID=94) for 1 minute. If the creature was already stupefied 2, they become [controlled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=64) by the conspiracist until the end of the encounter.
**Success** The enemy has trouble disbelieving the conspiracist's logic, becoming stupefied 1 for 1 minute. If they're already stupefied 1, they become stupefied 2.
**Failure** The enemy is unconvinced, but a seed of doubt remains.
**Critical Failure** The enemy sees through the conspiracist's act, becoming immune to Sow Doubt for 24 hours.

They can continue to Grapple to keep their hold on the target so long as the target remains within 20 feet and they continue to hold the end of the lasso. Many dwarves become smiths as their attention to detail, lifestyles that keep them close to useful materials such as iron, and a pride in their work all come together to become a brilliant skill set for working with armaments. Though dwarves are capable of smithing most any kind of item, most focus on armaments as a way of creating objects to defend their fellow dwarves. **[Recall Knowledge - Humanoid](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=47)): DC 14 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 12 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 9 [Dwarf Smith](/NPCs.aspx?ID=3626) **Source** [NPC Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=236) pg. 174 **Perception** +5; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59) **Languages** [Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1), [Dwarven](/Languages.aspx?ID=3) **Skills** [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) +6, [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=37) +12, [Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=47) +6 **Str** +2 **Dex** +1 **Con** +2 **Int** +3 **Wis** +1 **Cha** -1 **Blacksmithing Specialist** For encounters involving blacksmithing, the dwarf smith is a 5th-level challenge.
**Temper Armament** ([downtime](/Traits.aspx?ID=580)) The smith spends 1 day tempering a single suit of metallic armor, metallic shield, or metallic weapon. Tempering armor or a shield increases its Hardness by 1. Tempering a weapon grants the weapon a +1 circumstance bonus to damage rolls. Regardless of the item, the tempering remains for 3 days, after which item is temporarily immune to further tempering for 1 week as the technique would otherwise damage it. **Items** [Artisan's Toolkit](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2703) (blacksmithing), [Clan Dagger](/Weapons.aspx?ID=13), leather apron (functions as [padded armor](/Armor.aspx?ID=40)), [Light Hammer](/Weapons.aspx?ID=384) --- **AC** 14 **Fort** +6 **Ref** +3 **Will** +5 **HP** 12 **Resistances** [fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=604) 1 --- **Speed** 20 feet **Melee** light hammer +6 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170)), **Damage** 1d6+2 bludgeoning **Melee** clan dagger +6 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [Parry](/Traits.aspx?ID=190), [versatile B](/Traits.aspx?ID=200)), **Damage** 1d4+2 piercing **Melee** fist +6 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [Nonlethal](/Traits.aspx?ID=188), [Unarmed](/Traits.aspx?ID=199)), **Damage** 1d4+2 bludgeoning **Ranged** light hammer +4 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [thrown 20 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=195)), **Damage** 1d6+2 bludgeoning **Crack the Shell** The dwarf smith makes a Strike to break a creature's defenses. If the Strike hits and the creature is wearing armor with Hardness 9 or lower, the armor is [broken](/Conditions.aspx?ID=60). This Strike doesn't further damage armor that's already broken.

Envoys are guests of a given court, representing the interests of another court or organization. Some envoys stay in one place so long they're practically considered locals, though those with whom they parley are swiftly reminded where their loyalty lies. **[Recall Knowledge - Humanoid](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=47)): DC 14 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 12 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 9 [Envoy](/NPCs.aspx?ID=3416) **Source** [NPC Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=236) pg. 12 **Perception** +7; (13 to [Sense Motive](/Actions.aspx?ID=2302)) **Languages** [Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1); plus two additional languages **Skills** [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38) +13, [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39) +15, [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=40) +7, [Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=47) +15 **Str** +0 **Dex** +1 **Con** +0 **Int** +4 **Wis** +3 **Cha** +3 **Diplomatic Specialist** When dealing with matters of statecraft and negotiation, the envoy is a 6th-level challenge. **Items** [Dagger](/Weapons.aspx?ID=3), [fine clothing](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2715), letter of diplomatic status, signet ring --- **AC** 13 **Fort** +2 **Ref** +3 **Will** +11 **HP** 12 --- **Speed** 25 feet **Melee** dagger +5 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [Finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=179), [versatile S](/Traits.aspx?ID=200)), **Damage** 1d4+2 piercing **Melee** fist +5 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [Finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=179), [Nonlethal](/Traits.aspx?ID=188), [Unarmed](/Traits.aspx?ID=199)), **Damage** 1d4+2 bludgeoning **Ranged** dagger +5 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [thrown 10 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=195), [versatile S](/Traits.aspx?ID=200)), **Damage** 1d4+2 piercing **Diplomatic Immunity** ([Auditory](/Traits.aspx?ID=16), [Concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32), [Emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=60), [Linguistic](/Traits.aspx?ID=101), [Mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=106)) The envoy invokes their diplomatic status. Until the end of the envoy's next turn, any creature that attempts to attack them must succeed at a DC 15 Will save or have their attack [disrupted](/Rules.aspx?ID=2342). The attacker gains weakness 2 to all damage from the envoy's allies while Diplomatic Immunity lasts, whether their attack was disrupted or not.
The envoy can Sustain this ability. If the envoy takes a [hostile action](/Rules.aspx?ID=300), Diplomatic Immunity ends and can't be used again for 1 hour.

<title level="1" pfs="Standard">[Grindylow](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3038)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

The top half of a grindylow vaguely resembles a [goblin](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=422), but from the waist down, their bodies split into a tangle of suckered, wriggling tentacles. Grindylows mostly dwell in shallow waters, fresh and briny, including lakes, rivers, coastal regions, and coral reefs. They generally organize into groups called schools, which can range from a few individuals to a few hundred. Smaller schools are sometimes taken over by a powerful aquatic creature, though such alliances only last until the school faces a major setback, at which point the surviving grindylows scatter and form smaller schools of their own.

 Grindylows aren't territorial, but they are pragmatic. While they rarely build permanent structures, they will adopt a good hunting ground for generations until driven away by predators. They often lair in mobile shelters, such as a sargasso of seaweed or hull of an abandoned ship. They are skilled scavengers and hunters who eat anything they can sink their teeth into.

 Grindylows respect the power of larger sea predators but have a special hatred for squids (or anything that resembles a squid). Sailors plying grindylow-infested waters often paint the images of squids on the bottoms of their hulls in hopes of warding off potentials raids. While this can keep smaller schools at bay, it can also backfire, potentially inciting larger groups to gather for a coordinated attack; this becomes especially likely if the ship's route is predictable. Their hatred of squids does not extend to other tentacled creatures; grindylows consider [octopuses](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=143)to be the epitome of grace and power.

They generally organize into groups called schools, which can range from a few individuals to a few hundred. Smaller schools are sometimes taken over by a powerful aquatic creature, though such alliances only last until the school faces a major setback, at which point the surviving grindylows scatter and form smaller schools of their own. Grindylows aren't territorial, but they are pragmatic. While they rarely build permanent structures, they will adopt a good hunting ground for generations until driven away by predators. They often lair in mobile shelters, such as a sargasso of seaweed or hull of an abandoned ship. They are skilled scavengers and hunters who eat anything they can sink their teeth into. Grindylows respect the power of larger sea predators but have a special hatred for squids (or anything that resembles a squid). Sailors plying grindylow-infested waters often paint the images of squids on the bottoms of their hulls in hopes of warding off potentials raids. While this can keep smaller schools at bay, it can also backfire, potentially inciting larger groups to gather for a coordinated attack; this becomes especially likely if the ship's route is predictable. Their hatred of squids does not extend to other tentacled creatures; grindylows consider octopusesto be the epitome of grace and power. The grabbed creature is not immobilized, but if it moves, the grindylow moves with it. If the creature is Medium or smaller, it takes a –5-foot status penalty to its Speeds while the grindylow is attached. The grindylow is off-guard while attached to a creature. <title level="1" pfs="">[Hardhead Mole](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3288)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

Mischievous, burrowing hardhead moles reside mainly in the grasslands and plains. One can often spot their burrowing by following the upended ground they leave behind, which can span for hundreds of feet. Their signature physiological feature is a shiny, gem-like cranium that's thick enough to endure repeated hits and emits a flash of colorful light with each impact.

 Agrarian [gnome](/Ancestries.aspx?ID=3) communities have a close relationship with hardhead moles. Gnome children especially hold a great fondness for the creatures, and indeed, gave them their name. When they wander into the fields to play with these moles—typically by hitting them with small sticks, mallets, or any semi-blunt object—the moles are more than happy to oblige, darting from burrow to burrow with every sparkling blow in friendly games of hide-and-seek or tag.

 Perhaps the most famous hardhead mole is the gnome goddess [Nivi Rhombodazzle's](/Deities.aspx?ID=44) planar servitor Rummbrrlar, a hardhead mole imbued by Nivi with the powers of an [earth elemental](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=409). Long ago, the mighty mole was slain while rescuing children from a Nivian orphanage. As a reward for his selfless actions, Rummbrrlar was transformed into a planar servitor with diamond skin and the ability to grow as large as a mighty dragon. When communities shared by gnomes and hardhead moles are threatened, Rummbrrlar often appears to whisk bystanders to safety in the face of natural hazards or stand guard against monstrous threats. For this reason, hardhead moles are seen as a good omen and a symbol of protection in gnome communities.

 The average hardhead mole grows up to about 3 feet in length, but some become shorter as they age, their hard skulls flattening slightly after years of entertaining young gnomes. As they play, their heads (and the flashes of light they emit) darken in color, spanning shades of pink, red, crimson, and mauve; at seeing these darker hues, gnomes often give the moles some time to recover, as this indicates that a mole's cranium isn't getting enough blood flow. Though mischievous, hardhead moles are otherwise docile and friendly creatures. If placed in a fight-or-flight situation, they escape by creating deep networks of tunnels, which can span up to hundreds of feet in any direction.

This creates a burrow hole at the beginning and end of the line.

<title level="1" pfs="Standard">[Homunculus](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3056)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

A homunculus is a tiny servitor construct created by a crafter to serve as a spy, scout, messenger, or assistant. When a crafter first begins to study the art of creating constructs, they often craft a homunculus first, since the creation process is simple and inexpensive due to a magical shortcut: the use of the creator's own blood. This forges a link between the homunculus and its master, causing the homunculus to gain a spark of the creator's intellect, as well as the same moral values and some of the creator's basic personality traits. Homunculi left to their own devices never stray far from their masters.

 In most cases, a homunculus doesn't survive the death of its master for long. Deprived of its creator, a homunculus loses focus and grows increasingly self-destructive, and some even end up battering themselves to annihilation. Rarely, a homunculus with a slain master survives the trauma with its mind intact, often seeing itself as its deceased creator's child or successor and attempting to further its creator's legacy as best it can. In such cases, and if the homunculus was in close proximity to its master upon that creature's death, a portion of the dead master's soul “infects” the surviving homunculus as they pass on to the afterlife.

 This doesn't result in a truly soulbound homunculus (see sidebar), since only a fragment of the soul is left behind, but this is still enough to grant the homunculus a greater personality, free will of its own, and perhaps most importantly, the ability to speak. Over time, a few of these “awakened” homunculi even go so far as to become convinced that they are the reincarnation of their prior masters, although their actual personalities never quite reach the depth and complexity of a truly living creature. They are, at best, caricatures of the master, and at worst, they become awful, bitter-minded parodies of life itself. Still, a free-willed homunculus might pursue studies in its creator's class, becoming a unique creature with the abilities of that class if time and fortune permit.

 Homunculi are created from a mixture of clay, ash, mandrake root, spring water, and a pint of the creator's own blood. It is possible for a separate donor to provide the blood, but the process is more difficult.

text: Homunculus A homunculus is a tiny servitor construct created by a crafter to serve as a spy, scout, messenger, or assistant. When a crafter first begins to study the art of creating constructs, they often craft a homunculus first, since the creation process is simple and inexpensive due to a magical shortcut: the use of the creator's own blood. This forges a link between the homunculus and its master, causing the homunculus to gain a spark of the creator's intellect, as well as the same moral values and some of the creator's basic personality traits. Homunculi left to their own devices never stray far from their masters. In most cases, a homunculus doesn't survive the death of its master for long. Deprived of its creator, a homunculus loses focus and grows increasingly self-destructive, and some even end up battering themselves to annihilation. Rarely, a homunculus with a slain master survives the trauma with its mind intact, often seeing itself as its deceased creator's child or successor and attempting to further its creator's legacy as best it can. In such cases, and if the homunculus was in close proximity to its master upon that creature's death, a portion of the dead master's soul “infects” the surviving homunculus as they pass on to the afterlife. This doesn't result in a truly soulbound homunculus (see sidebar), since only a fragment of the soul is left behind, but this is still enough to grant the homunculus a greater personality, free will of its own, and perhaps most importantly, the ability to speak. Over time, a few of these “awakened” homunculi even go so far as to become convinced that they are the reincarnation of their prior masters, although their actual personalities never quite reach the depth and complexity of a truly living creature. They are, at best, caricatures of the master, and at worst, they become awful, bitter-minded parodies of life itself. Still, a free-willed homunculus might pursue studies in its creator's class, becoming a unique creature with the abilities of that class if time and fortune permit. Homunculi are created from a mixture of clay, ash, mandrake root, spring water, and a pint of the creator's own blood. It is possible for a separate donor to provide the blood, but the process is more difficult. Hryngar sharpshooters serve both as ranged support for caravans and as snipers posted on guard towers overlooking quarries and other areas where workers toil away the hours. Hryngar sharpshooters also specialize in nonlethal methods of ranged combat—tactics they are often called upon to use when tracking down derelict debtors or those attempting to flee from their contractual obligations.

A metal wisp is a roiling sphere of rust particles and sharp metal fragments, all furiously orbiting a liquid metal core that resembles the skull of a mortal creature—usually a humanoid, but animal and even more fantastical skulls are not uncommon. They don't form attachments as easily as wisps from other elemental planes, which tend to view metal wisps as too morose, although they retain a certain curiosity since their return from the planar severance. **[Recall Knowledge - Elemental](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=2), [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=10)): DC 14 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 12 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 9 [Metal Wisp](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2642) **Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 152 2.0 **Perception** +6; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=12), rust vision **Languages** [Talican](/Languages.aspx?ID=112) **Skills** [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) +6, [Mining Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8) +4, [Plane of Metal Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8) +4 **Str** +2 **Dex** +1 **Con** +3 **Int** +0 **Wis** +2 **Cha** +0 **Rust Vision** A metal wisp ignores the [concealed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=4) condition from rust clouds. --- **AC** 16 **Fort** +7 **Ref** +3 **Will** +6 **HP** 15 **Immunities** bleed, [electricity](/Traits.aspx?ID=56), [paralyzed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=28), [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=126), [sleep](/Traits.aspx?ID=145) **Resistances** electricity 2 **Resonance** ([aura](/Traits.aspx?ID=206), [metal](/Traits.aspx?ID=505)) 30 feet. All wisps vibrate at a frequency attuned to their element, resonating with and empowering all creatures and effects sharing that trait. Creatures in the area gain a +1 status bonus to attack and damage rolls made with metal weapons or effects with the [metal](/Traits.aspx?ID=505) trait; a creature with the [elemental](/Traits.aspx?ID=57) and metal traits gains this bonus to all attack and damage rolls.
**Accord Essence** **Trigger** An ally within 30 feet that benefited from the wisp's resonance in the last hour is targeted by an attack; **Effect** The wisp detonates itself in a small elemental explosion. Allies within 30 feet that have benefited from the wisp's resonance in the last hour gain temporary Hit Points equal to half the wisp's current Hit Points. These temporary Hit Points last 1 hour.
A wisp that uses this reaction is permanently destroyed, and it can be restored only by a _wish_ ritual or similarly powerful effect. If an ability would prevent the wisp's destruction (for instance, if the wisp is summoned and would merely be dismissed), Accord Essence has no effect.
**Rust Cloud** A metal wisp is constantly surrounded by a cloud of rust flakes that cause it to be [concealed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=4) from creatures more than 5 feet away from it. --- **Speed** fly 25 feet **Melee** tendril +6 ([reach 10 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)), **Damage** 1d4 piercing plus 1 [persistent bleed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29) **In Concert** When a metal wisp rolls a critical failure on a check to [Aid](/Actions.aspx?ID=75), it gets a failure instead, and when it rolls a success, it gets a critical success instead.

These shapeless masses of quivering flesh are the least of devilkind. Pathetic creatures from Hell's first layer, orts roam alongside damned and suffering souls. Nessaris can combine the essence of a mob of orts to concentrate their collective wickedness within a single form, granting it an infernal sentience and transforming it into a more powerful devil (see the nessari's Shape Devils ability). **[Recall Knowledge - Fiend](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46)): DC 14 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 12 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 9 [Ort](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2905) **Source** [Monster Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=221) pg. 86 1.1 **Perception** +0; [greater darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59) **Languages** **Skills** [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) +6 **Str** +2 **Dex** +0 **Con** +3 **Int** -5 **Wis** +0 **Cha** -3 --- **AC** 13 **Fort** +9 **Ref** +6 **Will** +2 **HP** 20 **Immunities** [fire](/Domains.aspx?ID=76), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647) **Resistances** physical 3 (except [silver](/Equipment.aspx?ID=379)), [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=669) 5 **Weaknesses** [holy](/Traits.aspx?ID=517) 3 --- **Speed** 20 feet **Melee** claw +8 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103), [Unholy](/Traits.aspx?ID=521)), **Damage** 1d4+2 slashing **Subservience** Orts have little drive of their own, but other devils can take command of them. A non-ort [devil](/Traits.aspx?ID=575) can issue a command to all orts within 60 feet of it with a single action, which has the [auditory](/Traits.aspx?ID=541) and [concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561) traits. The devil picks one of the following orders orts can understand, and the orts follow that order. The command and its effects end once the commander is out of the ort's sight, when a new command is issued by the same or another devil, or when the ort dies.
  • **Kill** The ort attacks one target the commander singles out and gains a +1 circumstance bonus to attack rolls against the target.
  • **Defend** The ort circles the commander and attacks any creature that comes near. It gains a +1 circumstance bonus to AC and saves.
  • **Fetch** The ort gains a +10–foot circumstance bonus to its Speed and attempts to get an object or person the commander singles out. It attacks anyone and anything that gets in the way.
  • **Work** The ort performs drudge work dictated by the commander.

The prime minister is the leader of a nation's bureaucracy. They are experienced politicians in charge of the laws and regulations of their territory, answering only to a monarch, if there is one. Often, though, a vote of “No Confidence” or similar legal procedure exists for removing the prime minister. **[Recall Knowledge - Humanoid](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=47)): DC 14 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 12 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 9 [Prime Minister](/NPCs.aspx?ID=3550) **Source** [NPC Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=236) pg. 110 **Perception** +9; (19 to [Sense Motive](/Actions.aspx?ID=2302)) **Languages** [Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1); up to 3 additional languages spoken in their nation **Skills** [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38) +22, [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39) +22, [Guild Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) +17, [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=40) +19, [Legal Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) +19, [Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=47) +22 **Str** +0 **Dex** +2 **Con** +1 **Int** +3 **Wis** +3 **Cha** +4 **Political Specialist** For encounters involving politics, the prime minister is a 10th-level challenge.
**Unshakable Confidence** All attempts to [Coerce](/Actions.aspx?ID=3028) the prime minister have a result one degree worse. **Items** [Rapier](/Weapons.aspx?ID=36) --- **AC** 14 **Fort** +6 **Ref** +3 **Will** +19 **HP** 15 **Cutting Counterpoint** **Trigger** The prime minister hears a creature attempt a [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38), [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39), or an [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=40) check against any creature other than the prime minister; **Effect** The prime minister interrupts with a witty barb, cutting the credibility of the creature's argument. The prime minister attempts their own check of the same type. If the result is higher than that of the triggering check, the triggering check is considered a failure regardless of its roll.
In extended negotiations, like a [Victory Point](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) challenge, the prime minister can't use this ability again until every creature in the discussion has had an opportunity to attempt a check (even if they decide not to make one). --- **Speed** 25 feet **Melee** rapier +5 ([deadly d8](/Traits.aspx?ID=174), [Disarm](/Traits.aspx?ID=175), [Finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=179)), **Damage** 1d6 piercing **Melee** fist +5 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [Finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=179), [Nonlethal](/Traits.aspx?ID=188), [Unarmed](/Traits.aspx?ID=199)), **Damage** 1d4 bludgeoning

<title level="1" pfs="Standard">[Pugwampi](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3032)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

Mean, dog-faced, and craven, pugwampis take disproportionate enjoyment from the accidents and missteps of other creatures— something that happens often due to the supernatural aura of ill fortune these gremlins project. They enjoy preparing pranks involving spikes, excrement, pits full of spiders, and similar twisted torments. Pugwampis are somewhat deaf and thus often yell loudly to each other when not hiding. Many pugwampis worship [kholos](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=54) as gods and aspire to be more like them. Kholos, on the other hand, hate pugwampis because of their sycophantic fawning.

They enjoy preparing pranks involving spikes, excrement, pits full of spiders, and similar twisted torments. Pugwampis are somewhat deaf and thus often yell loudly to each other when not hiding. Many pugwampis worship kholos as gods and aspire to be more like them. Kholos, on the other hand, hate pugwampis because of their sycophantic fawning. The typical thatchling appears as a humanoid bundle of dry grass and twigs, held together by coils of what looks like glowing blue hair. These minor undead can't form bodies larger than those of a small human child. **[Recall Knowledge - Undead](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=13)): DC 16 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 14 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 11 [Thatchling](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2725) **Source** [Pathfinder #196: The Summer That Never Was](/Sources.aspx?ID=214) pg. 88 **Perception** +6; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=12) **Languages** [Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1) **Skills** [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=1) +5, [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15) +5 **Str** +0 **Dex** +3 **Con** +2 **Int** +0 **Wis** +2 **Cha** +3 --- **AC** 15 **Fort** +4 **Ref** +7 **Will** +6 **HP** 16 ([negative healing](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=42)) **Immunities** [death](/Traits.aspx?ID=40) effects, [disease](/Traits.aspx?ID=46), [paralyzed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=28), [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=126), precision, [unconscious](/Conditions.aspx?ID=38) **Resistances** bludgeoning 2, piercing 2 **Weaknesses** [fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=72) 5 **Distracting Giggle** ([auditory](/Traits.aspx?ID=16), [aura](/Traits.aspx?ID=206), [emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=60), [enchantment](/Traits.aspx?ID=61), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=106), [occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=120)) 15 feet. The thatchling's giggle echoes in the back of the mind. Creatures within the aura take a –1 status penalty to Will saves.
**Rejuvenation** ([divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=48), [necromancy](/Traits.aspx?ID=117)) When a thatchling is destroyed by damage other than fire, it attempts a DC 11 flat check. On a success, it reforms after 2d4 days within 120 feet of where it was destroyed, fully healed. A thatchling is always permanently destroyed if reduced to 0 Hit Points by fire damage or if the obstacle preventing the soul from reincarnating is removed. --- **Speed** 30 feet; thicket walker **Melee** frond +5 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [Finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=179)), **Damage** 1d6 slashing **Thatchling's Curse** ([Curse](/Traits.aspx?ID=38), [Enchantment](/Traits.aspx?ID=61), [Mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=106), [Occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=120)) The thatchling focuses its attention on a single target within 30 feet that it can see, and then begins muttering and whispering nonsense. The target must attempt a DC 16 Will save.
**Critical Success** The target is unaffected and is temporarily immune to Thatchling's Curse for 24 hours.
**Success** The target is momentarily disoriented and has difficulty moving in the right direction. The target takes a –5-foot status penalty to its Speeds for 1 round.
**Failure** As success, but the penalty to its Speeds lasts for 1 minute.
**Critical Failure** As failure, but the penalty to its Speeds lasts until the curse is removed or until the thatchling that created the effect is permanently destroyed, whichever comes first. In addition, when the cursed creature attempts a [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=16) check to [Sense Direction](/Actions.aspx?ID=64) or [Track](/Actions.aspx?ID=66), they use the outcome for one degree of success worse than the result of their check, and they can't take the [Scout](/Actions.aspx?ID=518) exploration activity. **Thicket Walker** Thatchlings ignore difficult terrain caused by brambles, tangled grass, and undergrowth, even those manipulated by magic.

text: Thatchling The typical thatchling appears as a humanoid bundle of dry grass and twigs, held together by coils of what looks like glowing blue hair. These minor undead can't form bodies larger than those of a small human child. Recall Knowledge - Undead (Religion): DC 16 Unspecific Lore : DC 14 Specific Lore : DC 11 Thatchling Source Pathfinder #196: The Summer That Never Was pg. 88 Perception +6; darkvision Languages Common Skills Acrobatics +5, Stealth +5 Str +0 Dex +3 Con +2 Int +0 Wis +2 Cha +3 --- AC 15 Fort +4 Ref +7 Will +6 HP 16 (negative healing) Immunities death effects, disease, paralyzed, poison, precision, unconscious Resistances bludgeoning 2, piercing 2 Weaknesses fire 5 Distracting Giggle (auditory, aura, emotion, enchantment, mental, occult) 15 feet. The thatchling's giggle echoes in the back of the mind. Creatures within the aura take a –1 status penalty to Will saves. Rejuvenation (divine, necromancy) When a thatchling is destroyed by damage other than fire, it attempts a DC 11 flat check. On a success, it reforms after 2d4 days within 120 feet of where it was destroyed, fully healed. A thatchling is always permanently destroyed if reduced to 0 Hit Points by fire damage or if the obstacle preventing the soul from reincarnating is removed. --- Speed 30 feet; thicket walker Melee Single Action frond +5 (Agile, Finesse), Damage 1d6 slashing Thatchling's Curse Two Actions (Curse, Enchantment, Mental, Occult) The thatchling focuses its attention on a single target within 30 feet that it can see, and then begins muttering and whispering nonsense. The target must attempt a DC 16 Will save. Critical Success The target is unaffected and is temporarily immune to Thatchling's Curse for 24 hours. Success The target is momentarily disoriented and has difficulty moving in the right direction. The target takes a –5-foot status penalty to its Speeds for 1 round. Failure As success, but the penalty to its Speeds lasts for 1 minute. Critical Failure As failure, but the penalty to its Speeds lasts until the curse is removed or until the thatchling that created the effect is permanently destroyed, whichever comes first. In addition, when the cursed creature attempts a Survival check to Sense Direction or Track, they use the outcome for one degree of success worse than the result of their check, and they can't take the Scout exploration activity. Thicket Walker Thatchlings ignore difficult terrain caused by brambles, tangled grass, and undergrowth, even those manipulated by magic.

<title level="1" pfs="">[Toady](/NPCs.aspx?ID=3607)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

These minions perform the thankless tasks that keep their master's vile machine running. Whether out of loyalty or fear, a toady serves their boss faithfully.

<column gap="tiny">
**[Recall Knowledge - Humanoid](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**
([Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=47)): DC 14

**[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 12

**[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 9
</column>

</column>

<column gap="medium">
<image src="/images/Monsters/Toady.webp" />
</column>

</row>

<title level="2" right="Creature 0">[Toady](/NPCs.aspx?ID=3607)</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Medium" />
<trait label="Human" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=627" />
<trait label="Humanoid" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=628" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [NPC Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=236) pg. 152

**Perception** +3; (9 to eavesdrop) 

**Languages**
[Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1); one additional language spoken by their boss

**Skills**
[Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) +4, [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38) +2, [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=48) +6, [Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=50) +4

<row gap="medium">
**Str** +2

**Dex** +2

**Con** +3

**Int** -1

**Wis** +1

**Cha** +0
</row>

**Master Sends Their Regards** A toady can deliver a message from their boss to [Demoralize](/Actions.aspx?ID=2395) using their boss's Intimidation modifier instead of their own.

**Items**
[Sap](/Weapons.aspx?ID=37), supplies for the boss

</column>

---

<column gap="tiny">

<row gap="medium">
**AC** 14 

**Fort** +9 

**Ref** +6 

**Will** +3 

</row>

<row gap="medium">
**HP** 20

</row>

**Weaknesses**
[mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647) 2

**Human Shield** <actions string="Reaction" /> **Trigger** The toady's boss takes damage from an attack, and the toady is adjacent to them; **Effect** The toady takes the damage instead, along with any secondary effects of attack. This damage can't be reduced in any way.

</column>

---

<column gap="tiny">

**Speed** 25 feet

**Melee**
<actions string="Single Action" />
sap +6 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [Nonlethal](/Traits.aspx?ID=188)),
**Damage** 1d6+2 bludgeoning

**Melee**
<actions string="Single Action" />
fist +6 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [Nonlethal](/Traits.aspx?ID=188), [Unarmed](/Traits.aspx?ID=199)),
**Damage** 1d4+2 bludgeoning

**Scurry** <actions string="Single Action" />  The toady Strides, then can [Hide](/Actions.aspx?ID=2404). They can attempt to Hide from creatures without [cover](/Rules.aspx?ID=459) or being [concealed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=62), but at a –2 circumstance penalty.

**Throw Cargo** <actions string="Two Actions" />  A toady carries a heavy load of supplies at their boss's behest. They hurl a heavy item they're carrying, which explodes on impact to deal 1d10 bludgeoning damage to all creatures in a 5-foot burst with a DC 14 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save.

</column>

Like other wisps, wood wisps roam their plane and attune to other wisps, wandering with them in symphonies. Because of their willingness to bond, wood wisps appear outside their home plane more than other wood elementals, though they're still relatively rare compared to other wisps. Wood wisps resemble coconuts trailed by thick nests of branches that cover and conceal even deeper webs of thorny vines. They are, unfortunately, both unaware of the pain these thorns can cause fleshy creatures and very physically affectionate in their eagerness to offer assistance. **[Recall Knowledge - Elemental](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=2), [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=10)): DC 14 **[Recall Knowledge - Plant](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=10)): DC 14 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 12 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 9 [Wood Wisp](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2668) **Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 204 2.0 **Perception** +6; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=12) **Languages** [Muan](/Languages.aspx?ID=108) **Skills** [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) +7, [Plane of Wood Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8) +4, [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15) +6 **Str** +3 **Dex** +1 **Con** +2 **Int** +0 **Wis** +3 **Cha** +0 --- **AC** 16 **Fort** +5 **Ref** +2 **Will** +8 **HP** 20 **Immunities** bleed, [paralyzed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=28), [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=126), [sleep](/Traits.aspx?ID=145) **Weaknesses** [axes](/WeaponGroups.aspx?ID=1) 2, [fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=72) 2 **Resonance** ([aura](/Traits.aspx?ID=206), [plant](/Traits.aspx?ID=125), [wood](/Traits.aspx?ID=508)) 30 feet. All wisps vibrate at a frequency attuned to their element, resonating with and empowering all creatures and effects sharing that trait. A creature in the area gains a +1 status bonus to attack and damage rolls for effects with the [plant](/Traits.aspx?ID=125) or [wood](/Traits.aspx?ID=508) trait; a creature with the [elemental](/Traits.aspx?ID=57) trait and either plant trait or wood trait gains this bonus to all attack and damage rolls. For wood wisps, this bonus also applies to nonmagical wooden weapons, such as staves and clubs.
**Accord Essence** ([plant](/Traits.aspx?ID=125)) **Trigger** An ally within 30 feet that benefited from the wisp's resonance in the last hour is targeted by an attack; **Effect** The wisp detonates itself in a small elemental explosion of leaves and pollen. This gives temporary Hit Points equal to half the wisp's current HP to all allies within 30 feet that have benefited from the wisp's resonance aura in the past hour. These temporary Hit Points last 1 hour.
A wisp that uses this reaction is permanently destroyed and can be restored only by a _wish_ ritual or similarly powerful effect. If an ability would prevent the wisp's destruction (for instance, if the wisp is summoned and would merely be dismissed), Accord Essence has no effect. --- **Speed** fly 20 feet, climb 40 feet **Melee** thorny vine +5 ([reach 10 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)), **Damage** 1d4 bludgeoning plus 1 piercing **In Concert** When a wood wisp rolls a critical failure on a check to [Aid](/Actions.aspx?ID=75), they get a failure instead, and when they roll a success, they get a critical success instead.

Because of their willingness to bond, wood wisps appear outside their home plane more than other wood elementals, though they're still relatively rare compared to other wisps. Wood wisps resemble coconuts trailed by thick nests of branches that cover and conceal even deeper webs of thorny vines. They are, unfortunately, both unaware of the pain these thorns can cause fleshy creatures and very physically affectionate in their eagerness to offer assistance. Recall Knowledge - Elemental (Arcana, Nature): DC 14 Recall Knowledge - Plant (Nature): DC 14 Unspecific Lore : DC 12 Specific Lore : DC 9 Wood Wisp Source Rage of Elements pg. 204 2.0 Perception +6; darkvision Languages Muan Skills Athletics +7, Plane of Wood Lore +4, Stealth +6 Str +3 Dex +1 Con +2 Int +0 Wis +3 Cha +0 --- AC 16 Fort +5 Ref +2 Will +8 HP 20 Immunities bleed, paralyzed, poison, sleep Weaknesses axes 2, fire 2 Resonance (aura, plant, wood) 30 feet. All wisps vibrate at a frequency attuned to their element, resonating with and empowering all creatures and effects sharing that trait. A creature in the area gains a +1 status bonus to attack and damage rolls for effects with the plant or wood trait; a creature with the elemental trait and either plant trait or wood trait gains this bonus to all attack and damage rolls. For wood wisps, this bonus also applies to nonmagical wooden weapons, such as staves and clubs. Accord Essence Reaction (plant) Trigger An ally within 30 feet that benefited from the wisp's resonance in the last hour is targeted by an attack; Effect The wisp detonates itself in a small elemental explosion of leaves and pollen. This gives temporary Hit Points equal to half the wisp's current HP to all allies within 30 feet that have benefited from the wisp's resonance aura in the past hour. These temporary Hit Points last 1 hour. A wisp that uses this reaction is permanently destroyed and can be restored only by a wish ritual or similarly powerful effect. If an ability would prevent the wisp's destruction (for instance, if the wisp is summoned and would merely be dismissed), Accord Essence has no effect. --- Speed fly 20 feet, climb 40 feet Melee Single Action thorny vine +5 (reach 10 feet), Damage 1d4 bludgeoning plus 1 piercing In Concert When a wood wisp rolls a critical failure on a check to Aid, they get a failure instead, and when they roll a success, they get a critical success instead.

Wood wisps resemble coconuts trailed by thick nests of branches that cover and conceal even deeper webs of thorny vines. They are, unfortunately, both unaware of the pain these thorns can cause fleshy creatures and very physically affectionate in their eagerness to offer assistance.

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

A pale blue head and paper-thin wings peek out from the cloud that clings to the air scamp. Air scamps are short-sighted and flighty, even relative to their kin; they are as likely to fly recklessly into battle as they are to whine in terror at a loud noise.

</column>

text: Ardande Ardandes are geniekin whose elemental birthright ties them to the Plane of Wood. Their elemental connection can take many different forms, all expressions of the different types and permutations of elemental wood. They might embody the life and vibrancy of a seedling, full of potential and ready to grow. Or, they could be strong and flexible, like the branches and roots of ancient trees, interconnected and all growing together. They could also possess power over death and decay, like decomposing logs ready to fertilize and feed the next generation. Common on the Plane of Wood, uncommon in the First World, and only on the cusp of a resurgence into the Universe, the ardandes often feel misplaced in the multiverse, born into the wrong place or the wrong time. Many spend their lives searching the planes for answers about themselves and their heritage. Ardandes are found in all major cities and civilizations on the Plane of Wood, though most live in Nodollin, the Glowing Infinity, a metropolis controlled by the powerful kizidhars. Some ardandes say life in Nodollin is filled with infantilization and belittlement from the kizidhars, the wood genies who rule the land and much of the plane. The kizidhars largely view ardandes as genies like them, but a lesser form of genie that ranks below kizidhar commoners in the same way they are lesser to the shuyookhs. Though a few ardandes rebel against this social order, the weight of culture tells them hierarchies are natural to the element of wood, and they should accept their place even if they chafe. Many planar ardandes moved to Shodokar when the new city was founded, hoping the influx of portals leading out of the Plane of Wood would let them visit the rest of the multiverse and learn about their lost mortal heritage. They delight in meeting visitors and showing off the beauty and wonders of their home plane. Some have even moved to the Universe, and they make invaluable mentors for the new ardandes only just discovering their elemental potential across Golarion. </traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Monster Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=221) pg. 44 <sup>1.1</sup>

**Perception** +7; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59)

**Languages**
[Boggard](/Languages.aspx?ID=27), [Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1)

**Skills**

**Int** -1

**Wis** +2

**Cha** +0
</row>

</column>

---

<column gap="tiny">

<row gap="medium">
**AC** 16 

**Fort** +9 

**Ref** +5 

**Will** +7 

</row>

<row gap="medium">
**HP** 24

</row>

</column>

---

<column gap="tiny">

**Speed** 20 feet, swim 25 feet; swamp passage

**Melee**
<actions string="Single Action" />
morningstar +8 ([versatile P](/Traits.aspx?ID=200)),
**Damage** 1d6+3 bludgeoning

**Melee**
<actions string="Single Action" />
tongue +8 ([reach 10 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)),
**Damage** tongue grab

**Ranged**
<actions string="Single Action" />
sling +7 ([Propulsive](/Traits.aspx?ID=191), [range increment 50 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=248), [reload 1](/Traits.aspx?ID=254)),
**Damage** 1d6+1 bludgeoning

**Swamp Passage**   A boggard scout ignores [difficult terrain](/Rules.aspx?ID=453) caused by swamp terrain features.

**Terrifying Croak** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([Auditory](/Traits.aspx?ID=16), [Emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=60), [Fear](/Traits.aspx?ID=68), [Mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=106)) The boggard scout unleashes a terrifying croak. Any non-boggard within 30 feet becomes [frightened 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=76) unless they succeed at a DC 17 Will save; those who critically succeed are temporarily immune for 1 minute.

**Tongue Grab**   If the boggard scout hits a creature with their tongue, that creature becomes [grabbed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=77) by the boggard. Unlike with a normal Grab, the creature isn't [immobilized](/Conditions.aspx?ID=81), but it can't move beyond the reach of the boggard's tongue. A creature can sever the tongue by hitting AC 13 and dealing at least 2 slashing damage. Though this doesn't deal any damage to the boggard, it prevents them from using their tongue Strike until they regrow their tongue, which takes a week.

</column>

A creature can sever the tongue by hitting AC 13 and dealing at least 2 slashing damage. Though this doesn't deal any damage to the boggard, it prevents them from using their tongue Strike until they regrow their tongue, which takes a week.

description: Often tasked with patrolling the borders of their lands, boggard scouts learn to speak another language (typically [Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=155)) to deal with trespassers.

Caligni dancers serve as intermediaries between caligni factions, carrying messages and negotiating deals between the notoriously independent groups. Although physically fragile, the dancers serve an important role within caligni society and are rarely seen without guards. **[Recall Knowledge - Humanoid](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=47)): DC 15 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 13 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 10 [Caligni Dancer](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2862) **Source** [Monster Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=221) pg. 48 1.1 **Perception** +6; [greater darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59), [light blindness](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=68) **Languages** [Caligni](/Languages.aspx?ID=28) **Skills** [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=1) +7, [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=6) +8, [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=12) +6, [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15) +7, [Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=17) +7 **Str** +0 **Dex** +4 **Con** +2 **Int** -1 **Wis** +1 **Cha** +3 **Items** baton (functions as [light mace](/Weapons.aspx?ID=360)), [Dagger](/Weapons.aspx?ID=3) --- **AC** 17 **Fort** +7 **Ref** +9 **Will** +4 **HP** 18 (final dance) **Distracting Frolic** ([fortune](/Traits.aspx?ID=612), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Trigger** An ally within 10 feet of the dancer rolls a saving throw against a [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647) or [illusion](/Traits.aspx?ID=629) effect; **Effect** The target ally can roll the save twice and take the better result.
**Final Dance** ([occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=662), [shadow](/Traits.aspx?ID=693), [visual](/Traits.aspx?ID=727)) When the dancer dies, their body dissolves into a swirling mass of darkness and light. All creatures in a 10-foot emanation must succeed at a DC 17 Will save or be [dazzled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=65) for 1d4 rounds. The dancer's possessions are left in a pile where they died. --- **Speed** 25 feet **Melee** baton +9 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [Finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=179), [Shove](/Traits.aspx?ID=193)), **Damage** 1d4 bludgeoning **Melee** dagger +9 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [Finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=179), [versatile S](/Traits.aspx?ID=200)), **Damage** 1d4 piercing **Ranged** dagger +9 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [thrown 10 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=195), [versatile S](/Traits.aspx?ID=200)), **Damage** 1d4 piercing **Occult Innate Spells** DC 16 - **Cantrips (1st)** [Courageous Anthem](/Spells.aspx?ID=1763) - **1st** [Counter Performance](/Spells.aspx?ID=381) (visual only) **Dancer's Curse** ([Curse](/Traits.aspx?ID=38), [Mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=106), [Occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=120)) The caligni dancer touches a foe and curses it. If the target fails a DC 18 Will save, it gains [clumsy 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=61) and [stupefied 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=94). The target is then temporarily immune for 24 hours. These conditions persist until the curse is removed. The victim can attempt a new DC 18 Will save once per hour to end the curse. **Sneak Attack** The caligni dancer deals 1d6 extra precision damage to [off-guard](/Conditions.aspx?ID=58) creatures.

The weakest of angels, cassisians usually serve as lackey messengers for more powerful angels or as spiritual guides for mortals. Despite their limited intellect, cassisians have a knack for precise recollection, particularly with scripture. <row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

Catfolk pouncers travel the world in search of new experiences. With a spring in their step and a positive attitude, a pouncer can usually lithely avoid or quickly bounce back from negative ordeals, much to their enemies' chagrin.

<column gap="tiny">

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Monster Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=221) pg. 52 <sup>1.1</sup>

[Amurrun](/Languages.aspx?ID=25), [Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1)

<row gap="medium">
**Str** +3

**Dex** +4

**Con** +1

**Int** -1

**Wis** +1

**Cha** +1
</row>

**Items**
[Dagger](/Weapons.aspx?ID=3) (3), [Greataxe](/Weapons.aspx?ID=21)

</column>

---

<column gap="tiny">

<row gap="medium">
