**Fort** +6 

**Ref** +9 

**Will** +4 

</row>

<row gap="medium">
**HP** 17

</row>

**Cat's Luck** <actions string="Reaction" /> ([fortune](/Traits.aspx?ID=612)) **Trigger** The catfolk pouncer fails or critically fails a Reflex saving throw; **Frequency** once per day; **Effect** Reroll that saving throw and take the better result.

</column>

---

<column gap="tiny">

**Speed** 30 feet

**[Recall Knowledge - Construct](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=2), [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=4)): DC 20 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 18 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 15 [Clockwork Serpent Spy](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2744) **Source** [Rusthenge](/Sources.aspx?ID=215) pg. 44 **Perception** +10; [low-light vision](/Traits.aspx?ID=100) **Languages** **Skills** [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=1) +7 **Str** +0 **Dex** +4 **Con** +0 **Int** -5 **Wis** +3 **Cha** +0 **Record Audio** The clockwork spy records all sounds within 25 feet onto a small gemstone worth 1 gp embedded in its body. The clockwork spy can record up to 1 hour of sound on a single gemstone.
Once it begins recording, it can't cease recording early, nor can it record onto a gemstone that already contains a recording. Some clockwork spies contain multiple gemstones to allow for a series of recordings. Since clockwork spies are not intelligent, they must be given simple commands regarding when to start recording sounds. A clockwork spy can differentiate between different kinds of creatures but not between specific individuals.
The spy can start or stop playback of recorded sound by spending a single action. Removing a gemstone from or installing a gemstone into a clockwork spy requires a successful DC 14 [Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=17) check to [Disable a Device](/Actions.aspx?ID=69); on a failure, the gemstone is undamaged, but any recorded sounds are erased and the gemstone still can't be used to make another recording.
**Wind Up** 24 hours, DC 17, standby --- **AC** 19 **Fort** +3 **Ref** +9 **Will** +6 **HP** 15 **Immunities** [death](/Traits.aspx?ID=40) effects, [disease](/Traits.aspx?ID=46), [doomed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=9), [drained](/Conditions.aspx?ID=10), [fatigued](/Conditions.aspx?ID=15), [healing](/Traits.aspx?ID=89), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=106), [necromancy](/Traits.aspx?ID=117), [nonlethal](/Traits.aspx?ID=188) attacks, [paralyzed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=28), [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=126), [sickened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=34), [unconscious](/Conditions.aspx?ID=38) **Weaknesses** [electricity](/Traits.aspx?ID=56) 3, [orichalcum](/Equipment.aspx?ID=378) 3 **Self-Destruct** A clockwork spy must use this reaction unless specifically programmed otherwise by its creator; **Trigger** The clockwork spy is reduced to 0 Hit Points; **Effect** The spy thrashes around and emits a tinny scream followed by a steady ticking sound. At the beginning of what would have been its next turn, the clockwork spy explodes, dealing 1d12 piercing damage in a 5-foot radius (DC 17 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save). Its gemstone is destroyed, along with any information contained inside it. An adjacent creature can cancel the self-destruct sequence by succeeding at a DC 17 [Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=17) check to [Disable a Device](/Actions.aspx?ID=69). --- **Speed** 25 feet **Melee** sharpened gear +7 ([Finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=179)), **Damage** 1d6–1 slashing plus bleeding gash **Bleeding Gash** On a critical hit with a sharpened gear Strike, the clockwork serpent spy also inflicts 1d4 [persistent bleed damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29) (DC 17 Fortitude save negates the additional bleed damage).

The cythnigot is a foul fungal parasite that grows and thrives in the corpses of small creatures. It wears these bodies like a suit, but also adjusts and tailors the fleshy covering to fit its needs, and the body ends up looking as alien as anything else spawned from the Chthonian depths. The cythnigot's most identifying feature is the long stalk of fungal material that extends from creature's body, ending in a surprisingly strong set of fanged jaws. **[Recall Knowledge - Fiend](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46)): DC 17 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 15 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 12 [Cythnigot](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3154) **Source** [Monster Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=221) pg. 280 1.1 **Perception** +5; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59) **Languages** [Chthonian](/Languages.aspx?ID=114); [telepathy](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=79) (touch only) **Skills** [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=1) +6, [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=11) +7, [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15) +6 **Str** +1 **Dex** +3 **Con** +4 **Int** +2 **Wis** +2 **Cha** +1 --- **AC** 16 **Fort** +9 **Ref** +6 **Will** +5 **HP** 14 **Immunities** [controlled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=64), [fear](/Traits.aspx?ID=598) **Resistances** [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647) 3, physical 3 (except [cold iron](/Equipment.aspx?ID=375)) --- **Speed** 30 feet, fly 40 feet **Melee** bite +8 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [Finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=179), [Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103), [reach 0 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192), [Unholy](/Traits.aspx?ID=521)), **Damage** 1d10+1 piercing plus and tangle spores **Occult Innate Spells** DC 17 - **Cantrips (1st)** [Daze](/Spells.aspx?ID=61), [Detect Magic](/Spells.aspx?ID=66) - **1st** [Phantom Pain](/Spells.aspx?ID=220) - **2nd** [Paranoia](/Spells.aspx?ID=214) - **4th** [Read Omens](/Spells.aspx?ID=247) **Sickening Display** ([Concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32), [Emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=60), [Fear](/Traits.aspx?ID=68), [Mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=106), [Occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=120), [Visual](/Traits.aspx?ID=163)) The cythnigot presents its awful appearance fully, and creatures in a 10-foot emanation must attempt a DC 17 Will save. Once a creature attempts this save, it's temporarily immune to further Sickening Displays for 1 minute.
**Critical Success** The creature is unaffected.
**Success** The creature is [off-guard](/Conditions.aspx?ID=58) until its next turn.
**Failure** The creature is [sickened 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=91) and is off-guard for as long as it's sickened.
**Critical Failure** As failure but sickened 2. **Tangle Spores** ([Disease](/Traits.aspx?ID=46)) A creature bitten by a cythnigot becomes afflicted by fast-growing spores that swiftly grow into twitching spikes and hideous pallid growths of hairlike fibers. These growths erupt from the bite wound and writhe and wrap around the creature's limbs. [Plant](/Traits.aspx?ID=668) creatures take a –2 circumstance penalty to save against tangle spores; **Saving Throw** DC 17 Fortitude; **Maximum Duration** 6 rounds; **Stage 1** [clumsy 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=61) (1 round); **Stage 2** clumsy 1 and [off-guard](/Conditions.aspx?ID=58) (1 round); **Stage 3** clumsy 2, off-guard, and if you attempt a [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645) action, you must succeed at a DC 5 flat check or it's lost; roll the check after spending the action, but before any effects are applied (1 round).

<title level="1" pfs="Standard">[Despairing Pall](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2617)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

Despairing palls are small, dark clouds that float aimlessly through the [Plane of Air](/Planes.aspx?ID=4), casting literal and emotional shadows wherever they go. Pranksters and mischievous elementalists often summon them to rain on a rival's parade.

<column gap="tiny">
**[Recall Knowledge - Elemental](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**
([Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=2), [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=10)): DC 15

**[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 13

**[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 10
</column>

</column>

<column gap="medium">
<image src="/images/Monsters/ElementalAir_DespairingPall.png" />
</column>

</row>

<title level="2" right="Creature 1">[Despairing Pall](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2617)</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Small" />
<trait label="Air" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=5" />
<trait label="Elemental" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=57" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 82 <sup>2.0</sup>

**Perception** +5; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=12)

**Languages**
[Sussuran](/Languages.aspx?ID=111)

**Skills**
[Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=1) +8, [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=7) +6, [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15) +8

<row gap="medium">
**Str** +0

**Dex** +4

**Con** +1

**Int** +0

**Wis** +0

**Cha** +2
</row>

</column>

---

<column gap="tiny">

<row gap="medium">
**AC** 17 

**Fort** +4 

**Ref** +10 

**Will** +7 

</row>

<row gap="medium">
**HP** 15

</row>

**Immunities**
bleed, [electricity](/Traits.aspx?ID=56), [paralyzed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=28), [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=126), [sleep](/Traits.aspx?ID=145)

**Duskflow** <actions string="Reaction" /> ([darkness](/Traits.aspx?ID=39)) **Trigger** The despairing pall is damaged by a melee Strike; **Effect** Darkness billows out from the despairing pall, covering its attacker in inky shadow. The despairing pall immediately Steps up to 15 feet in any direction. If the despairing pall took the triggering damage due to a reaction it provoked by moving, it can then finish the movement. For one round, the triggering attacker is cloaked in [darkness](/Rules.aspx?ID=409) and perceives light as one step lower ([bright light](/Rules.aspx?ID=407) becomes [dim light](/Rules.aspx?ID=408), for example), affecting its ability to sense creatures and objects accordingly.

</column>

---

<column gap="tiny">

**Speed** fly 50 feet

**Melee**
<actions string="Single Action" />
hot air +7 ([Air](/Traits.aspx?ID=5)),
**Damage** pushed 5 feet

**Ranged**
<actions string="Single Action" />
lightning bolt +7 ([Electricity](/Traits.aspx?ID=56), [range increment 50 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=248)),
**Damage** 1d6 electricity

**Downcast** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([Air](/Traits.aspx?ID=5), [Emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=60), [Mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=106)) The despairing pall [Flies](/Actions.aspx?ID=94) up to its Speed, then rains gloom and despair in a 15-foot line straight down. Creatures in the area must succeed at a DC 16 Will save or take a –1 status penalty to attack rolls until the end of the despairing pall's next turn.

</column>

<title level="1" pfs="Standard">[Dewdrop Jelly](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2659)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

Dewdrop jellies are small water elementals resembling jellyfish made of gelatinous bubbles. They typically travel in small schools, floating through the air or swimming through the endless seas of their home plane. When threatened, the jellies discorporate into a thin, vaporous mist, reconstituting into their bubble shape only after the danger has passed. Their clever elusiveness makes them hard to find, leading some to claim that dewdrop jellies are mythical flights of fancy told to entertain children.

<column gap="tiny">
**[Recall Knowledge - Elemental](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**
([Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=2), [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=10)): DC 15

**[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 13

**[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 10
</column>

</column>

<column gap="medium">
<image src="/images/Monsters/ElementalWater_DewdropJelly.png" />
</column>

</row>

<title level="2" right="Creature 1">[Dewdrop Jelly](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2659)</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Small" />
<trait label="Aquatic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=168" />
<trait label="Elemental" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=57" />
<trait label="Water" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=165" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 180 <sup>2.0</sup>

**Perception** +7; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=12)

**Languages**
[Thalassic](/Languages.aspx?ID=113)

**Skills**
[Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) +6, [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15) +7

<row gap="medium">
**Str** +2

**Dex** +3

**Con** +3

**Int** -4

**Wis** +1

**Cha** +0
</row>

</column>

---

<column gap="tiny">

<row gap="medium">
**AC** 16 

**Fort** +7 

**Ref** +10 

**Will** +4 

</row>

<row gap="medium">
**HP** 20

</row>

**Immunities**
bleed, [paralyzed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=28), [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=126), [sleep](/Traits.aspx?ID=145)

**Resistances**
[fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=72) 5

**Dissolve** <actions string="Reaction" /> **Trigger** The dewdrop jelly takes damage from a [hostile action](/Rules.aspx?ID=300); **Effect** The dewdrop jelly dissolves into a fine mist. Until the start of the jelly's next turn, it can't be attacked or targeted and doesn't take up space. At the end of the round, the jelly re-forms in any open space within 25 feet of where it Dissolved.

</column>

---

<column gap="tiny">

**Speed** fly 20 feet, swim 50 feet

**Melee**
<actions string="Single Action" />
tentacle +8,
**Damage** 1d6+2 bludgeoning

**Overflow** <actions string="Three Actions" /> ([Move](/Traits.aspx?ID=114)) The dewdrop jelly flattens its bell and shoots forward, [Flying](/Actions.aspx?ID=94) or [Swimming](/Actions.aspx?ID=39) twice in a straight line toward its target and attempting a tentacle Strike. On a success, the dewdrop attaches to the target's face, covering its mouth in the suspended water of its gelatinous body. If the target cannot breathe water, it begins to [drown](/Rules.aspx?ID=468). The DC to [Escape](/Actions.aspx?ID=79) is 16.

</column>

Dust bunnies in particular are prone to swarming. This can occur when a large number are left alone for a long period of time and are then disturbed by adventurers or a returning wizard. Other times, a singular dust bunny familiar grows in such numbers (and they will rapidly reproduce!) that a wizard cannot hope to keep them all placated with food and attention. In this situation, they will unionize in rebellion against their master. It is paramount that you do not allow a dust bunny to multiply, for once a swarm has formed, they are nigh impossible to get rid of. While relatively easy to disperse and unlikely to kill anyone, they will re-form within the week unless the area is immaculately cleaned. **[Recall Knowledge - Construct](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35), [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=37)): DC 20 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 18 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 15 [Dust Bunny Swarm](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3681) **Source** [Foolish Housekeeping and Other Articles](/Sources.aspx?ID=239) **Perception** +7 **Languages** **Skills** [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35) +3, [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) +3, [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=48) +7 **Str** +0 **Dex** +2 **Con** +0 **Int** -4 **Wis** +0 **Cha** +2 --- **AC** 13 **Fort** +7 **Ref** +5 **Will** +3 **HP** 16 **Immunities** bleed, [death](/Traits.aspx?ID=571) effects, [disease](/Traits.aspx?ID=578), [doomed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=67), [drained](/Conditions.aspx?ID=68), [fatigued](/Conditions.aspx?ID=73), [grappled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=77), [healing](/Traits.aspx?ID=623), [nonlethal](/Traits.aspx?ID=661) attacks, [paralyzed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=85), [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=669), precision, [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=88), [restrained](/Conditions.aspx?ID=90), [sickened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=91), [spirit](/Traits.aspx?ID=737), [swarm mind](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=78), [unconscious](/Conditions.aspx?ID=95), [vitality](/Traits.aspx?ID=509), [void](/Traits.aspx?ID=510) **Resistances** physical 6 (except bludgeoning) **Weaknesses** area damage 4, [splash](/Traits.aspx?ID=699) damage 4 **Cloud of Allergens** **Trigger** The swarm rolls initiative; **Effect** The dust bunnies stir, kicking up a cloud in a 15-foot burst centered on the swarm that lasts for 1 minute. Creatures who enter or start their turn in this cloud must attempt a DC 16 Fortitude save or take a –1 circumstance penalty to skill checks that have the [concentration](/Traits.aspx?ID=561) trait and all Perception checks as their sensory organs become impaired.
**Dust to Dust** When a dust bunny swarm is destroyed, it re-forms after 2d4 days in the area in which it was destroyed unless the location has been significantly cleaned of all dust and debris. --- **Speed** 30 feet **Pummeling Dust** Each enemy in the swarm's space takes 1d6 bludgeoning damage with a DC 16 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save. A creature that fails its save cannot use reactions for 1 round as they sneeze uncontrollably.

<row gap="medium">

An earth scamp's rocky exterior could camouflage it well among loose rocks if not for the scamp's large eyes and bat-like wings. Earth scamps can fly, but the act of flight is uncomfortable and unnerving to them—they rarely leave the ground if they can help it. In fact, most earth scamps would rather never visit the surface at all, staying nestled deeply within the rocks they resemble.

**Send Signal** The eyelet sends an emergency signal through its scrying sensor to a linked scrying station (see Witness) up to 10 miles away. This transmits the eyelet's distance and direction from the station at the time of sending.
**Witness** The eyelet records whatever it perceives, storing it in an embedded, marble-sized sensor. The eyelet can record up to 1 hour of events, starting and stopping across a longer period. Removing the sensor erases its records.
An eyelet can transfer everything it has recorded up to 10 miles to its linked scrying station, where the recordings are collected and can be viewed. <title level="1" pfs="Standard">[Fire Scamp](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2987)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

Although arguably quite friendly, fire scamps are considered far more dangerous than their kin. They delight in fire and playing pranks on everyone they befriend. Even given time to understand others' dislike of fire, most fire scamps enjoy the feel of flames enough to constantly test their limits. Compared to the nations of other scamps, the nations on the [Plane of Fire](/Planes.aspx?ID=31) are by far the strongest. This backing inspires fire scamps to challenge authority more quickly than the others.

They can tell you exactly where to find a rare medicinal fern, when to harvest it, and how to use it; just don't expect them to be up-to-date on the latest town gossip. <title level="1" pfs="Standard">[Giant Gecko](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3087)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

These roughly human-sized reptiles have amazing feet capable of clinging tenaciously to any surface. Giant geckos are typically docile and shy but can be aggressive when cornered or defending their territory. These large-eyed lizards are found in a wide variety of habitats, from rain forests and deserts to mountain slopes or even underground caverns. They spend most of their time climbing around in large trees or on rocky cliffs, whether hunting for small animals or hiding from predators. A giant gecko's scales are often quite brightly colored or decorated in intricate patterns. Giant geckos span nearly 8 feet in length from head to tail, and they weigh about 120 pounds.

 Giant geckos are sometimes used by smaller humanoids as guardians or mounts, as their docile nature makes them relatively easy to tame and train. Their superior climbing skills make giant geckos particularly popular within societies that dwell underground or near cliffs, such as [goblins](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=422) and [kobolds](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=435). Their bright coloration also makes them favorite pets in high society.

<column gap="tiny">
**[Recall Knowledge - Animal](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**
([Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43)): DC 15

**[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 13

**[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 10
</column>

text: Giant Gecko These roughly human-sized reptiles have amazing feet capable of clinging tenaciously to any surface. Giant geckos are typically docile and shy but can be aggressive when cornered or defending their territory. These large-eyed lizards are found in a wide variety of habitats, from rain forests and deserts to mountain slopes or even underground caverns. They spend most of their time climbing around in large trees or on rocky cliffs, whether hunting for small animals or hiding from predators. A giant gecko's scales are often quite brightly colored or decorated in intricate patterns. Giant geckos span nearly 8 feet in length from head to tail, and they weigh about 120 pounds. Giant geckos are sometimes used by smaller humanoids as guardians or mounts, as their docile nature makes them relatively easy to tame and train. Their superior climbing skills make giant geckos particularly popular within societies that dwell underground or near cliffs, such as goblins and kobolds. Their bright coloration also makes them favorite pets in high society. Gluttonous geodes form when natural forces crack open a geode that's steeped in elemental magic, causing a natural break that acts like a hinged jaw. Though seemingly unimportant and no larger than a common turtle, gluttonous geodes are bellicose and dogged in their pursuit of an enemy.

<actions string="Single Action" />
crystal teeth +9,
**Damage** 1d4+4 piercing plus Attach

**Attach** <actions string="Two Actions" />  The geode Leaps up to 15 feet and makes a crystal teeth Strike. If it hits a creature larger than itself, it can attach to that creature. Doing so is like [Grabbing](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=18) the creature ([Escape](/Actions.aspx?ID=79) DC 17), but the geode moves with that creature rather than holding it in place. The geode is [off-guard](/Conditions.aspx?ID=58) while attached. If the geode is killed or [pushed](/Rules.aspx?ID=451) away while attached to a creature, that creature takes 1 [persistent bleed damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29). Escaping the attached geode or removing the geode in other ways doesn't cause bleed damage.

**Gnaw** <actions string="Single Action" />  **Requirements** The geode is attached to a creature; **Effect** The geode deals 1d4+2 bludgeoning damage to the creature it's attached to (DC 17 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Fortitude save).

</column>

Goblins eat almost anything. Though they'll survive on raw or little-cooked meat, some prefer searing or frying their food first—or better yet, pickling it! A goblin chef can make anything edible (at least to a goblin). **[Recall Knowledge - Humanoid](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=47)): DC 15 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 13 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 10 [Goblin Chef](/NPCs.aspx?ID=3640) **Source** [NPC Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=236) pg. 186 **Perception** +7; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59) **Languages** [Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1), [Goblin](/Languages.aspx?ID=6) **Skills** [Cooking Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) +10, [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43) +7, [Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=47) +4, [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=48) +6, [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=49) +7 **Str** +1 **Dex** +1 **Con** +3 **Int** +2 **Wis** +2 **Cha** +0 **Good Enough to Eat** The goblin chef can turn otherwise inedible items into meals for others. They can provide food for any number of creatures without using the [Subsist](/Actions.aspx?ID=2368) downtime activity as long as garbage is readily available. A non-[goblin](/Traits.aspx?ID=618) who eats the goblin chef's food must attempt a DC 14 Fortitude save. On a failure, they suffer an upset stomach for 1 day; if they attempt to willingly ingest anything else during that period, they must first succeed at a DC 4 flat check or the action is [disrupted](/Rules.aspx?ID=2342).
**Kitchen Specialist** For encounters involving cooking, a goblin chef is a 3rd-level challenge. **Items** cleaver (functions as [dogslicer](/Weapons.aspx?ID=405)), leather apron (functions as [leather armor](/Armor.aspx?ID=41)), pickles (6) --- **AC** 16 **Fort** +10 **Ref** +6 **Will** +5 +2 circumstance bonus against [ingested](/Traits.aspx?ID=633) [poisons](/Traits.aspx?ID=669) **HP** 24 **Immunities** [sickened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=91) --- **Speed** 25 feet **Melee** jaws +7 ([Finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=179), [Unarmed](/Traits.aspx?ID=199)), **Damage** 1d6+1 piercing **Melee** cleaver +7 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [Backstabber](/Traits.aspx?ID=172), [Finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=179)), **Damage** 1d4+1 slashing **Eat a Pickle** **Effect** The goblin chef draws a pickle and eats it or feeds it to an adjacent ally. Goblins' eponymous pets aren't true canines at all but rather large, blunt-nosed rodents with thin bodies and long legs. Often as cowardly as they are ugly, goblin dogs prefer to lurk behind bushes or in deep shadows, only pouncing upon lone or wounded prey. Goblin dogs frequently roam in packs, but they are likely to flee from a fight if injured, even if it means abandoning their packmates. Goblin dogs take their name from a long association with [goblins](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=422), who breed the beasts as guard animals and mounts. Most goblins take issue with the name, as the average goblin is appalled at the suggestion that their favored mounts have anything at all to do with actual dogs. Of course, being goblins, they haven't bothered to come up with their own unique name for the creatures. Even the most pampered goblin dogs have itchy mange and prolific dander that tenaciously affects those who come in contact with them. This “goblin pox” causes itchy hives and festering sores that are as unsightly as they are irritating and distracting. Goblin dog dander causes allergic reactions in nearly all other creatures that don't share goblin dogs' terrible hygiene—with the notable exception being, of course, goblins, who remain entirely immune to the disease regardless of cleanliness. Hunger can drive goblin dogs to bouts of uncharacteristic violence, and crueler goblins sometimes purposefully starve their pets on the eve of battle. Goblin dogs subsist on whatever organic material they can scavenge; they particularly enjoy fresh carrion. Although goblins are far from picky eaters themselves, they value goblin dogs because the noisome animals will consume material that even goblins won't touch. In fact, “Will It Eat?” is one of the most popular games goblins play with their pets, where a wide range of morsels (not always edible or safe to consume) are dangled before a goblin dog's snout. Sadly, the game “Will It Die?” is often played after “Will It Eat?” Goblin dogs that survive the second game earn renown for their digestive prowess and often become favored tribal pets, treated even better than most of the rank-and-file goblins. **[Recall Knowledge - Animal](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43)): DC 15 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 13 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 10 [Goblin Dog](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3028) **Source** [Monster Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=221) pg. 176 1.1 **Perception** +6; [low-light vision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=69), [scent](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=74) ([imprecise](/Rules.aspx?ID=412)) 30 feet **Languages** **Skills** [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) +6, [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15) +7 **Str** +3 **Dex** +2 **Con** +2 **Int** -4 **Wis** +1 **Cha** -1 --- **AC** 15 **Fort** +8 **Ref** +8 **Will** +5 **HP** 17 **Irritating Dander** A creature that hits a goblin dog with an [unarmed](/Traits.aspx?ID=719) attack, tries to [Grapple](/Actions.aspx?ID=2376) it, or otherwise touches it is exposed to goblin pox.
**[Buck](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=54)** DC 17
**Juke** **Requirements** A creature must be mounted on the goblin dog; **Trigger** The rider issues a command to the goblin dog; **Effect** The goblin dog Steps before following the command. --- **Speed** 40 feet **Melee** jaws +9, **Damage** 1d6+3 piercing plus goblin pox **Goblin Pox** ([Disease](/Traits.aspx?ID=46)) [Goblins](/Traits.aspx?ID=618) and goblin dogs are immune to goblin pox; **Saving Throw** DC 17 Fortitude; **Stage 1** sickened 1 (1 round); **Stage 2** [sickened 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=91) and [slowed 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=92) (1 round); **Stage 3** sickened 2 and can't reduce its sickened value below 1 (1 day) **Scratch** ([Manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104)) The goblin dog vigorously scratches itself, exposing all adjacent creatures to goblin pox.

<title level="1" pfs="Standard">[Goblin Pyro](/NPCs.aspx?ID=3026)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

Some goblins take their people's admiration of fire fully into the realm of deadly obsession. These pyromaniacs can be a great boon to a band of goblin raiders eager to torch their enemies and wreak havoc. More often, however, their presence is a double-edged sword; in the heat of the moment, goblin pyros sometimes lose sight of their tribe's goals and simply set fire to anything that will burn—including their own allies. Goblin squads are also prone to distraction, and more than one goblin raid has failed because its members were too busy watching a massive blaze.

text: Goblin Pyro Some goblins take their people's admiration of fire fully into the realm of deadly obsession. These pyromaniacs can be a great boon to a band of goblin raiders eager to torch their enemies and wreak havoc. More often, however, their presence is a double-edged sword; in the heat of the moment, goblin pyros sometimes lose sight of their tribe's goals and simply set fire to anything that will burn—including their own allies. Goblin squads are also prone to distraction, and more than one goblin raid has failed because its members were too busy watching a massive blaze. <title level="1" pfs="Standard">[Gourd Leshy](/NPCs.aspx?ID=3080)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

Gourd leshies are guardians of fields, gardens, and farms. Many villages benefit from the protection of a gourd leshy, even if they are unaware of it.

<column gap="tiny">
**[Recall Knowledge - Plant](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**
([Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43)): DC 15

**[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 13

**[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 10
</column>

</column>

<column gap="medium">

</column>

</row>

<title level="2" right="Creature 1">[Gourd Leshy](/NPCs.aspx?ID=3080)</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Small" />
<trait label="Leshy" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=639" />
<trait label="Plant" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=668" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Monster Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=221) pg. 217 <sup>1.1</sup>

**Perception** +5; [low-light vision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=69)

**Languages**
[Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1), [Fey](/Languages.aspx?ID=119); [_speak with plants_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1681) (gourds only)

**Skills**
[Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=10) +5, [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15) +7

<row gap="medium">
**Str** +2

**Dex** +4

**Con** +2

**Int** -1

**Wis** +2

**Cha** +0
</row>

**Keepsake** ([primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=676)) The leshy can store an item of light Bulk or less in their head, concealing it as [_veil of privacy_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1739). If stored for 24 hours, the item benefits from [_mending_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1597).

</column>

---

<column gap="tiny">

<row gap="medium">
**AC** 17 

**Fort** +5 

**Ref** +9 

**Will** +7 

</row>

<row gap="medium">
**HP** 20

</row>

**Verdant Burst** ([healing](/Traits.aspx?ID=623), [primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=676), [vitality](/Traits.aspx?ID=509)) When a gourd leshy dies, a burst of primal energy explodes from their body, restoring 1d8 Hit Points to each [plant](/Traits.aspx?ID=668) creature in a 30-foot emanation. This area is filled with gourds, becoming [difficult terrain](/Rules.aspx?ID=453). If the terrain is not a viable environment for these plants, they wither after 24 hours.

</column>

---

<column gap="tiny">

**Speed** 25 feet

**Melee**
<actions string="Single Action" />
fist +7 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [Finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=179)),
**Damage** 1d4+2 bludgeoning plus ensnare

**Ranged**
<actions string="Single Action" />
seed +9 ([range increment 30 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=248)),
**Damage** 1d6+2 bludgeoning plus ensnare

**Primal Innate Spells** DC 15
- **Constant (3rd)**
[Speak with Plants](/Spells.aspx?ID=294) (gourds only)

**[Change Shape](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=55)** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([Concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32), [Polymorph](/Traits.aspx?ID=127), [Primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=134)) The leaf leshy transforms into a Small gourd-bearing plant. This ability otherwise uses the effects of [_one with plants_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1618).

**Ensnare**   When the gourd leshy damages a creature with a fist or seed Strike, vines lash out from the leshy (or seed) and wrap around the target's limbs. The target must attempt a DC 17 Reflex save. On a failure, the target takes a –10-foot status penalty to its Speed for 1 round; on a critical failure, the target is [immobilized](/Conditions.aspx?ID=81) for 1 round and the penalty to Speed lasts for 1 minute.

</column>

<title level="1" pfs="">[Gunsmith](/NPCs.aspx?ID=3456)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

Even though every gunslinger learns the basics of maintaining and repairing firearms as a part of their training, few would question the expertise of a master gunsmith regarding the weapons by which they live and die. Although professional gunsmiths are rarely found outside of settlements where firearms are common, such as Alkenstar or Dongun Hold, true masters of this specialized craft tend to quickly build reputations for themselves that extend well beyond the borders of whatever region they call home.

<column gap="tiny">
**[Recall Knowledge - Humanoid](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**
([Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=47)): DC 15

**[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 13

</column>

<trait label="Humanoid" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=628" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [NPC Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=236) pg. 42

**Perception** +6

**Languages**
[Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1)

**Skills**
[Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) +4, [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=37) +13, [Firearm Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) +13, [Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=47) +5

<row gap="medium">
**Str** +1

**Dex** +3

**Con** +0

**Int** +2

**Wis** +3

**Cha** +0
</row>

**Firearm Specialist** For encounters involving the crafting or maintenance of firearms, the gunsmith is a 6th-level challenge.

**Items**

</column>

---

<column gap="tiny">

<row gap="medium">
**AC** 16 

**Fort** +5 

**Ref** +8 

**Will** +6 

</row>

<row gap="medium">
**HP** 16

</row>

</column>

---

<column gap="tiny">

**Speed** 25 feet

**Melee**
<actions string="Single Action" />
fist +8 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [Finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=179), [Nonlethal](/Traits.aspx?ID=188), [Unarmed](/Traits.aspx?ID=199)),
**Damage** 1d4+1 bludgeoning

**Ranged**
<actions string="Single Action" />
dueling pistol +8 ([Concealable](/Traits.aspx?ID=327), [Concussive](/Traits.aspx?ID=401), [fatal d10](/Traits.aspx?ID=178), [range increment 60 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=248), [reload 1](/Traits.aspx?ID=254)),
**Damage** 1d6+2 piercing

**Crafty Reload**   The gunsmith can Interact to reload a firearm without a free hand if they have a firearm in each hand. In addition, each time the gunsmith reloads a firearm, they can attempt a [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=37) check against the hard DC for the firearm's level (DC 17 for a [dueling pistol](/Weapons.aspx?ID=520)). On a success, they gain a +1 circumstance bonus on the next attack roll they make with that firearm before the start of their next turn.

**Firearm Sabotage** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([Manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104)) **Requirements** The gunsmith is wielding or holding a one-handed firearm and has a free hand; **Effect** The gunsmith deftly makes a minor modification to a firearm that can be detected with a Perception check opposed by the gunsmith's [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=37) DC. If the sabotage is not reversed with a successful Crafting check against the gunsmith's Crafting DC, the firearm automatically misfires the next time it is used (the flat check is an automatic failure; see the Misfires sidebar).

</column>

**Graffiti Egg** <actions string="Single Action" />  the halfling troublemaker throws an egg filled with paint, glitter, and confetti at a creature within 30 feet. **Keen Eyes**   The halfling gains a +2 circumstance bonus when using the [Seek](/Actions.aspx?ID=2301) action to find [hidden](/Conditions.aspx?ID=79) or [undetected](/Conditions.aspx?ID=96) creatures within 30 feet of it. **[Sneak Attack](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=34)**   The troublemaker deals an extra 1d6 precision damage to [off-guard](/Conditions.aspx?ID=58) creatures.

<title level="1" pfs="Standard">[Hopping Head](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2770)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

<title level="1" pfs="Standard">[Hryngar Bombardier](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3062)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

Hryngar chemists have a knack for creating alchemical grenades. Their traditions often motivate them to constantly experiment and innovate, though the hostile nature of their environs tends to focus these innovations on weapons or other tools of war. Hryngar bombardiers eagerly steal notes and secrets from their underlings, pushing their students to cut corners to produce results while gleefully pillaging the credit and profits. For those hryngar bombardiers who find themselves pressed into combat service, each thrown grenade represents a new opportunity to observe the  suffering they inflict, before eagerly incorporating that data into their next experiment or innovation to create an even more terrible tool of torment.

<column gap="tiny">

<row gap="medium">
**AC** 17 

**Fort** +6 

**Ref** +9 

**Will** +5 

</row>

<row gap="medium">
**HP** 16

</row>

**Spring Upon Prey** <actions string="Reaction" /> **Requirements** Initiative has not yet been rolled; **Trigger** A creature touches the hunting spider's web while the spider is on it; **Effect** The hunting spider automatically notices the creature and Strides, Climbs, or Descends on a Web before it rolls initiative.

</column>

---

<column gap="tiny">

**Speed** 25 feet, climb 25 feet

**Melee**
<actions string="Single Action" />
fangs +9 ([Finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=179)),
**Damage** 1d6+2 piercing plus hunting spider venom

**Ranged**
<actions string="Single Action" />
web +7 ([range increment 30 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=248)),
**Damage** web trap

**Descend on a Web** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([Move](/Traits.aspx?ID=114)) The hunting spider moves straight down up to 40 feet, suspended by a web line. It can hang from the web or drop off. The distance it Descends on a Web doesn't count for [falling damage](/Rules.aspx?ID=402). A creature that successfully Strikes the web (AC 20, Hardness 3, 5 HP) severs it, causing the spider to fall.

**Hunting Spider Venom**  ([Poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=126)) **Saving Throw** DC 16 Fortitude; **Maximum Duration** 6 rounds; **Stage 1** 1d4 poison damage and [off-guard](/Conditions.aspx?ID=58) (1 round); **Stage 2** 1d6 poison damage, [clumsy 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=61), and off-guard (1 round); **Stage 3** 1d6 poison damage, clumsy 2, and off-guard (1 round)

**Web Trap**   A creature hit by the hunting spider's web Strike is [immobilized](/Conditions.aspx?ID=81) and stuck to the nearest surface until it [Escapes](/Actions.aspx?ID=2296) (DC 17).

</column>

<title level="1" pfs="Standard">[Hyena](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3065)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

Hyenas are cunning, powerfully built carnivores that bear a heavy resemblance to dogs and other canines, though they are not themselves canines. Though all hyenas are often maligned as cowardly carrion eaters, their tactics depend on their specific breed: spotted hyenas are active pack hunters that kill most of their prey themselves, while striped and brown hyenas are more likely to be loners and scavengers. Their jaws are exceptionally powerful, allowing hyenas to seize a victim and pull it to the rest of the pack.

<title level="1" pfs="Standard">[Imp](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3067)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

Imps are fiendish infiltrators and corrupters who, despite their diminutive stature, are more than capable of subtly influencing a weak-willed individual into performing increasingly evil acts over time. An imp will often agree to serve a mortal and act docile and loyal in a long-term plot to eventually get their master killed or damn their soul. Imps are born directly from the Outer Planes themselves, rather than from mortal souls, and thus they serve outside any fiendish hierarchies, granting them leeway to pursue their specialties.

 Despite standing a mere 2 feet tall, imps can be vicious combatants, flying out of reach and turning invisible to escape should the odds turn against them.

<column gap="tiny">
**[Recall Knowledge - Fiend](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**
([Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46)): DC 15

**[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 13

**[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 10
</column>

</column>

<title level="2" right="Creature 1">[Imp](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3067)</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Tiny" />
<trait label="Fiend" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=600" />
<trait label="Unholy" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=521" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Monster Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=221) pg. 206 <sup>1.1</sup>

**Perception** +7; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59)

**Languages**
[Chthonian](/Languages.aspx?ID=114), [Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1), [Daemonic](/Languages.aspx?ID=31), [Diabolic](/Languages.aspx?ID=117); [telepathy](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=79) (touch)

**Skills**
[Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=1) +7, [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=2) +6, [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5) +7, [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=13) +5

<row gap="medium">
**Str** -1

**Dex** +4

**Con** +0

**Int** +1

**Wis** +2

**Cha** +2
</row>

</column>

---

<column gap="tiny">

<row gap="medium">
**AC** 17 

**Fort** +5 

**Ref** +9 

**Will** +7 

</row>

<row gap="medium">
**HP** 15

</row>

**Resistances**
[poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=669) 3

**Weaknesses**
[holy](/Traits.aspx?ID=517) 3

</column>

---

<column gap="tiny">

**Speed** 20 feet, fly 30 feet

**Melee**
<actions string="Single Action" />
stinger +9 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [Finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=179), [Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103), [reach 0 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192), [Unholy](/Traits.aspx?ID=521)),
**Damage** 1d4–1 piercing plus imp venom

**Divine Innate Spells** DC 17
- **Cantrips (1st)**
[Detect Magic](/Spells.aspx?ID=66)
- **1st**
[Charm](/Spells.aspx?ID=34)
- **2nd**
[Invisibility](/Spells.aspx?ID=164) (at will; self only)
- **4th**
[Read Omens](/Spells.aspx?ID=247)

**[Change Shape](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=55)** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([Concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32), [Divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=48), [Polymorph](/Traits.aspx?ID=127)) The imp takes on the appearance of a Medium or smaller [animal](/Traits.aspx?ID=531) (page 358). While transformed, the imp loses their normal senses, innate spells, and special actions, but doesn't otherwise change their statistics and can still speak and use telepathy. The imp also gains any special senses of the animal and any Speeds the animal has. This doesn't change the attack and damage modifiers of their Strikes but might change the damage type their Strikes deal (depending on what kinds of attacks the animal has) and prevents them from exposing creatures to imp venom.

**Fiendish Healing** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([Concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32), [Divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=48), [Healing](/Traits.aspx?ID=89), [Vitality](/Traits.aspx?ID=509)) **Frequency** once per round; **Effect** The imp regains 1d6 Hit Points.

**Fiendish Temptation** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([Concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32), [Divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=48), [Fortune](/Traits.aspx?ID=76), [Unholy](/Traits.aspx?ID=521)) **Frequency** once per day; **Effect** The imp offers a non-[fiend](/Traits.aspx?ID=600) within 15 feet a bargain, granting a boon of good luck if the creature accepts voluntarily. The boon lasts for 1 hour once accepted. Once during the hour, the creature can roll an attack roll or saving throw twice and use the higher result. If the creature dies while the boon is in place, the imp decides where the creature's soul travels. This typically makes the soul bound for eternity in the imp's home plane, and the creature unable to be raised or resurrected except by the [_wish_](/Rituals.aspx?ID=125) ritual or similar magic.

**Imp Venom**  ([Poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=126)) **Saving Throw** DC 16 Fortitude; **Maximum Duration** 6 rounds; **Stage 1** 1d6 poison and [clumsy 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=61) (1 round); **Stage 2** 1d6 poison damage, clumsy 1, and [slowed 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=92) (1 round)

</column>

<title level="1" pfs="">[Innkeeper](/NPCs.aspx?ID=3496)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

The sight of an inn is a welcome one to any weary traveler. Innkeepers can often be found cleaning the common room, overseeing the evening meal, or settling in new lodgers. Innkeepers keep an eye on their neighbors' doings and are often excellent sources of information.

<column gap="tiny">
**[Recall Knowledge - Humanoid](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**
([Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=47)): DC 15

**[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 13

**[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 10
</column>

</column>

<column gap="medium">
<image src="/images/Monsters/Innkeeper.webp" />
</column>

</row>

<title level="2" right="Creature 1">[Innkeeper](/NPCs.aspx?ID=3496)</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Medium" />
<trait label="Human" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=627" />
<trait label="Humanoid" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=628" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [NPC Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=236) pg. 69

**Perception** +7

**Languages**
[Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1)

**Skills**
[Accounting Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) +5, [Alcohol Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) +7, [Cooking Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) +5, [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38) +6, [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39) +6, [Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=47) +7

<row gap="medium">
**Str** +2

**Dex** +0

**Con** +0

**Int** +2

**Wis** +2

**Cha** +3
</row>

**Font of Gossip** The innkeeper's business gives them insight into the neighborhood's happenings. A person can [Gather Information](/Actions.aspx?ID=2391) from an innkeeper in 30 minutes rather than canvassing an entire neighborhood. Each person can learn gossip from an innkeeper only once per day, and only if the innkeeper is [friendly](/Conditions.aspx?ID=75) or [helpful](/Conditions.aspx?ID=78) to that individual. Whatever information the innkeeper knows about a given topic doesn't change if someone else asks the innkeeper about that topic, unless the innkeeper has since learned more.

**Items**
broom (functions as a [staff](/Weapons.aspx?ID=367)), innkeeper's apron (functions as [leather armor](/Armor.aspx?ID=41)), ledger, [pewter mug](/Equipment.aspx?ID=36)

</column>

---

<column gap="tiny">

<row gap="medium">
**AC** 14 

**Fort** +7 

**Ref** +3 

**Will** +9 

</row>

<row gap="medium">
**HP** 20

</row>

</column>

---

<column gap="tiny">

**Speed** 25 feet

**Melee**
<actions string="Single Action" />
broom +7 ([two-hand d8](/Traits.aspx?ID=198)),
**Damage** 1d4+2 bludgeoning

**Melee**
<actions string="Single Action" />
fist +7 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [Nonlethal](/Traits.aspx?ID=188), [Unarmed](/Traits.aspx?ID=199)),
**Damage** 1d4+2 bludgeoning

**Ranged**
<actions string="Single Action" />
pewter mug +5 ([thrown 10 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=195)),
**Damage** 1d4+2 bludgeoning

**Home Base Brawler**   The innkeeper knows how to settle fights that break out. When the innkeeper is fighting in their establishment, their Strikes gain a +1 circumstance bonus to the attack roll, deal an additional 1d4 damage, and gain the [nonlethal](/Traits.aspx?ID=661) trait if they don't already have it. The innkeeper can choose not to gain this benefit.

**Innkeeper's Advice** <actions string="Three Actions" /> ([Auditory](/Traits.aspx?ID=16), [Fortune](/Traits.aspx?ID=76), [Linguistic](/Traits.aspx?ID=101), [Mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=106)) **Frequency** once per day; **Effect** The innkeeper gives some pertinent advice to a single creature other than themself. For 24 hours, when that creature fails a skill check or saving throw, they can recall this advice and reroll the check, using the second result instead. Once that creature uses this ability, its effect ends. A creature that receives the Innkeeper's Advice is temporarily immune to the ability for 1 month.

</column>

<title level="1" pfs="Standard">[Jinkin](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3033)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

Jinkins are sadistic tinkers who steal and sabotage items and take great pride in their power to curse precious objects. They hold grudges and create convoluted plans for revenge when they feel slighted, such as when a creature dares to remove one of their curses. Rarely content to wreak simple mayhem, jinkins also take immense pleasure in torture and murder, though they prefer to lead victims into traps designed to capture or incapacitate rather than just kill them outright. Deep pits are a preferred method, since victims who survive their fall face a slow death from starvation and thirst while jinkins gather at the edge of pits to tease and torment them.

<title level="1" pfs="">[Kholo Pragmatist](/NPCs.aspx?ID=3652)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

Due to their aggressive lifestyle, kholo warriors rarely live to an old age. When a kholo pragmatist enters a fight, they would prefer to see another battle, so they use any possible advantage they can get to survive. They keep foes at a distance with their longspears have developed techniques to better block attacks with the weapon. If the tide of battle turns against them, kholo pragmatists will run or surrender if it's the most practical option.

<title level="1" pfs="Standard">[Lava Otter](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2633)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

These fiery otters frolic and hunt in the lava streams of the [Plane of Fire](/Planes.aspx?ID=6). They're known to be highly territorial, instigating fights with rival otter families to compete for territory. Cautiously curious of strangers, entire packs have been known to descend upon anyone who attacks or event accidentally threatens a family member.

<column gap="tiny">
**[Recall Knowledge - Elemental](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**
([Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=2), [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=10)): DC 15

**[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 13

**[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 10
</column>

</column>

<column gap="medium">
<image src="/images/Monsters/ElementalFire_LavaOtter.png" />
</column>

</row>

<traits>
<trait label="Small" />
<trait label="Elemental" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=57" />
<trait label="Fire" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=72" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 129 <sup>2.0</sup>

**Perception** +7; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=12)

**Languages**

**Skills**
[Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=1) +7, [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15) +7

<row gap="medium">
**Str** +1

**Dex** +4

**Con** +1

**Int** -4

**Wis** +3

**Cha** +1
</row>

**Below the Crust** A lava otter can [Sneak](/Actions.aspx?ID=63) at its full Speed in lava.

</column>

---

<column gap="tiny">

<row gap="medium">
**AC** 15 

**Fort** +6 

**Ref** +9 

**Will** +5 

</row>

<row gap="medium">
**HP** 22

</row>

**Immunities**
bleed, fire, paralyzed, poison, sleep

**Weaknesses**
cold 3

**Molten Form** ([fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=72)) Any creature that hits the lava otter with an [unarmed](/Traits.aspx?ID=199) Strike or otherwise touches it takes 1 fire damage. If a gallon or more of water touches the lava otter, or if it's affected by a [water](/Traits.aspx?ID=165) effect, its outer layer of lava hardens to a rocky shell, deactivating its molten form and imposing weakness 5 to bludgeoning damage. Molten form reactivates if the otter swims in lava for 1 minute.

</column>

---

<column gap="tiny">

**Speed** 25 feet, swim 40 feet (in lava only)

**Melee**
<actions string="Single Action" />
jaws +9 ([Finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=179)),
**Damage** 1d4+1 piercing plus 1d4 fire

**Melee**
<actions string="Single Action" />
claw +9 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [Finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=179)),
**Damage** 1d4+1 slashing

**Scattering Magma** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([Fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=72)) **Requirements** The otter is in molten form, and its previous action was a successful jaws Strike; **Effect** The otter grips with its jaws and rapidly twists, flinging lava. The otter deals 1d4 fire damage to all creatures adjacent to it.

**Tight-Knit Family**   A lava otter can share the same space as another lava otter, but no more than two lava otters can occupy the same space.

</column>

A lizardfolk defender serves as a protector of the young, guardian of the settlement, and when no other options are available, a soldier in times of war. They eagerly rise to the defense of their kin but do not revel in battle. An iruxi defender would rather turn back intruders and allow them to flee with the knowledge they were beaten, in hopes that such word prevents further invasions, but they are not naive. <row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

Iruxi scouts are the lizardfolk most often encountered by adventurers, for these unsentimental  explorers and hunters spend most of their lives on the move, constantly patrolling the territories held by their enclave. If intruders are driven off, it is the responsibility of iruxi scouts to track them, observe them, and learn their ways and weaknesses so as to report back to the community and aid in the defense against potential reprisals.

Most join a secret lodge that teaches these ancient arts. **[Recall Knowledge - Humanoid](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=47)): DC 15 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 13 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 10 [Local Herbalist](/NPCs.aspx?ID=3481) **Source** [NPC Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=236) pg. 60 **Perception** +7 **Languages** [Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1) **Skills** [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=37) +6, [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39) +4, [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43) +7, [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=49) +7 **Str** +3 **Dex** +0 **Con** +1 **Int** +1 **Wis** +4 **Cha** +0 **Herbalism Specialist** For encounters involving collecting herbs or making medicine from them, the local herbalist is a 3rd-level challenge.

<title level="1" pfs="Standard">[Lyrakien (Wanderer Azata)](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2840)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

Lyrakiens are musical messengers and embodiments of free travel. They serve [Desna](/Deities.aspx?ID=281) and other deities and empyreal lords of [Elysium](/Planes.aspx?ID=40) but are quite fond of free time as a fundamental concept and are always on the hunt for opportunities to pause in their duties to enjoy music or appreciate a moment of beauty. They love contests, stories, and songs, and they often challenge mortals to musical contests or pester them to share grand tales of their exploits. Lyrakiens rely on their agility to avoid conflicts, but they do their best to defend places of great natural beauty, especially against foes they can damage with their starlight. Lyrakiens have an innate wanderlust and rarely stay in the same place for very long. Some travel alongside adventurers, often writing songs about their quests and feats of derring-do.

 Though light-hearted creatures, lyrakiens don't let their whimsical personalities get in the way of protecting breathtaking natural locations. Sometimes called “glistenwings” by gnomes and halflings, they are frequently mistaken for [sprites](/Monsters.aspx?ID=389) or similar [fey](/Languages.aspx?ID=119), a bit of confusion that many lyrakiens find amusing and fertile ground for shenanigans involving those they deem deserving of a bit of unexpected fun and discord in their lives.

No one knows how to get the most out of their equipment better than a mechanic. A mechanic can repair just about any mechanical device you put in front of them with aplomb. However, they can also push the device to achieve more than you ever could have hoped for, provided you do not mind a small explosion every now and again. Don't get distracted by their impressive work, or you might be blindsided by a fast-swinging wrench. **[Recall Knowledge - Humanoid](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=47)): DC 15 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 13 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 10 [Mechanic](/NPCs.aspx?ID=3457) **Source** [NPC Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=236) pg. 42 **Perception** +5 **Languages** **Skills** [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) +7, [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=37) +16, [Engineering Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) +16, [Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=50) +6 **Str** +4 **Dex** +1 **Con** +1 **Int** +3 **Wis** +0 **Cha** +0 **Mechanical Repair** The mechanic is trained in [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=37), but a master in Crafting for mechanical devices, siege weapons, and vehicles. They can [Repair](/Actions.aspx?ID=2384) in 1 minute instead of 10 minutes, or in 3 actions for a mechanical device, siege weapon, or vehicle.
**Mechanical Specialist** For encounters involving mechanical repair, the mechanic is an 8th-level challenge. **Items** [Arbalest](/Weapons.aspx?ID=432) (20 bolts), heavy wrench, [Repair Toolkit](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2747) --- **AC** 14 **Fort** +8 **Ref** +6 **Will** +3 **HP** 22 --- **Speed** 25 feet **Melee** heavy wrench +7 ([Shove](/Traits.aspx?ID=193)), **Damage** 1d6+4 bludgeoning **Melee** fist +7 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [Nonlethal](/Traits.aspx?ID=188), [Unarmed](/Traits.aspx?ID=199)), **Damage** 1d4+4 bludgeoning **Ranged** arbalest +8 ([Backstabber](/Traits.aspx?ID=172), [range increment 110 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=248), [reload 1](/Traits.aspx?ID=254)), **Damage** 1d10 piercing **Risky Upgrade** ([Concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32), [Manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104)) The mechanic pushes a mechanical device, siege weapon, or vehicle pasts its regular limits with a temporary upgrade chosen from the list below. An item can have only one risky upgrade at a time. If an item has an upgrade at the start of the mechanic's turn, the mechanic must attempt a DC 5 flat check. (These flat checks continue even if the mechanic is dead or otherwise can't take turns.) On a failure, the item explodes, dealing damage equal to the item's level to all adjacent creatures and ending the upgrade.
  • **Overheat Weapons** If the item would deal damage, it deals an additional 1d6 fire damage. This increases to 2d6 if the item is 8th level or higher.
  • **Pressured Plating** The item gains a +3 status bonus to its Hardness and gains temporary Hit Points equal to double its level that last for 10 minutes.
  • **Propelled Boost** If the item has a Speed, the item gains a +15-foot status bonus to Speed.

When a message, mail, or package needs to be delivered, messengers make deliveries—typically from large towns and cities or to other towns and cities. **[Recall Knowledge - Humanoid](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=47)): DC 15 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 13 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 10 [Messenger](/NPCs.aspx?ID=3497) **Source** [NPC Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=236) pg. 70 **Perception** +6 **Languages** [Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1) **Skills** [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=34) +8, [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) +5, [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39) +6, [Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=47) +7, [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=49) +4 **Str** +0 **Dex** +3 **Con** +4 **Int** +0 **Wis** +1 **Cha** +1 **Don't Shoot the Messenger** Messengers get a +2 circumstance bonus to [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39) checks to convince another creature not to blame them for any news they deliver.
**Road Runner** Messengers can use [Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=47) in place of [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=49) to [Sense Direction](/Actions.aspx?ID=2406) when they're on a road. **Items** [Dagger](/Weapons.aspx?ID=3), satchel of mail, [Sling](/Weapons.aspx?ID=72) (10 bullets) --- **AC** 16 **Fort** +7 **Ref** +10 **Will** +4 **HP** 20 --- **Speed** 30 feet **Melee** dagger +8 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [Finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=179), [versatile S](/Traits.aspx?ID=200)), **Damage** 1d4+2 piercing **Melee** fist +8 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [Finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=179), [Nonlethal](/Traits.aspx?ID=188), [Unarmed](/Traits.aspx?ID=199)), **Damage** 1d4+2 bludgeoning **Ranged** dagger +8 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [thrown 10 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=195), [versatile S](/Traits.aspx?ID=200)), **Damage** 1d4+2 piercing **Ranged** sling +8 ([range increment 50 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=248), [Propulsive](/Traits.aspx?ID=191)), **Damage** 1d6+2 bludgeoning **Express Messenger** Allies traveling with the messenger gain a +5-foot circumstance bonus to travel Speed, to a maximum of the messenger's travel Speed. If they use the [Hustle](/Actions.aspx?ID=2626) activity, they can Hustle for a minimum of 1 hour instead of the usual amount. **Special Delivery** The messenger Interacts to take an item of light Bulk or less held by a willing ally within reach, Strides, then delivers the item to a willing ally in reach at their new location.

<title level="1" pfs="Standard">[Metal Scamp](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2644)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

The capricious and destructive metal scamps are self-appointed forces of entropy, taking great pleasure in indiscriminately wrecking everything around them, sometimes even to their own detriment. Metal scamps have a severe appearance, with pointed facial features and angular limbs, and their skin can be the color of any metal, often heavily oxidized as if by years of exposure to the elements.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

</column>

<trait label="Metal" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=505" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Will** +5 

</row>

<row gap="medium">

([fast healing](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=15) 2 (while touching metal))

</row>

bleed, [paralyzed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=28), [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=126), [sleep](/Traits.aspx?ID=145)

**Resistances**
[electricity](/Traits.aspx?ID=56) 3

</column>

---

<column gap="tiny">

**Speed** 25 feet, fly 25 feet

**Melee**
<actions string="Single Action" />
claw +9,
**Damage** 1d6+2 slashing

**Arcane Innate Spells** DC 17, attack +9
- **2nd**
[Magnetic Attraction](/Spells.aspx?ID=944)

The metal scamp can't Breathe Shrapnel again for 1d4 rounds.

Naiads protect streams, ponds, springs, and other natural bodies of fresh water. While most naiads lead solitary lives close to their chosen home, sometimes they congregate in coven-like groups where river tributaries meet, performing great magic and blessing the waters of the land. Because naiads' bonds to their bodies of water permit more flexibility, they are the nymphs most likely to interact with humanoids—and even visit their settlements on occasion. Unlike other nymphs, naiads occasionally become adventurers, especially when dark forces seek to despoil nature or otherwise threaten the land, joining forces with others to prevent the corruption of the natural world. **[Recall Knowledge - Fey](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43)): DC 15 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 13 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 10 [Naiad](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3111) **Source** [Monster Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=221) pg. 244 1.1 **Perception** +6; [low-light vision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=69) **Languages** [Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1), [Elven](/Languages.aspx?ID=4), [Fey](/Languages.aspx?ID=119), [Thalassic](/Languages.aspx?ID=113) **Skills** [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=1) +6, [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) +3, [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=6) +7, [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=10) +6, [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15) +6, [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=16) +4 **Str** +0 **Dex** +3 **Con** +0 **Int** +1 **Wis** +1 **Cha** +4 **Animal Empathy** The naiad can ask questions of, receive answers from, and use the [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39) skill with [animals](/Traits.aspx?ID=531). --- **AC** 14 **Fort** +3 **Ref** +6 **Will** +8 **HP** 20 **Resistances** [fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=604) 3 **Weaknesses** [cold iron](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2916) 3 **Water Dependent** A naiad is bonded to a spring, pond, or similar-sized water feature. If she is more than 300 feet away from it for 24 hours or more, she gains the [weak](/Rules.aspx?ID=791) adjustments until she returns. She can perform a 24-hour ritual to bond herself to a new body of water.
Water Healing (healing, primal, vitality) For every 10 minutes a naiad spends soaking in her bonded body of water, she regains 7 Hit Points. --- **Speed** 25 feet, swim 25 feet **Melee** aqueous fist +8 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [Finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=179), [Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103), [Water](/Traits.aspx?ID=165)), **Damage** 1d8 bludgeoning **Ranged** water orb +8 ([Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103), [range 60 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=248), [Water](/Traits.aspx?ID=165)), **Damage** 1d6 bludgeoning **Primal Innate Spells** DC 17 - **1st** [Charm](/Spells.aspx?ID=34), [Create Water](/Spells.aspx?ID=53), [Hydraulic Push](/Spells.aspx?ID=154), [Tidal Surge](/Spells.aspx?ID=458) (at will)

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

These noppera-bos have mastered the art of disguise.

<column gap="tiny">
**[Recall Knowledge - Aberration](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**
([Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=11)): DC 17

**[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 15

**[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 12
</column>

</column>

<column gap="medium">

</column>

</row>

<title level="2" right="Creature 1">[Noppera-Bo Trickster](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2721)</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="CE" url="/Rules.aspx?ID=95" />
<trait label="Medium" />
<trait label="Aberration" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=1" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #196: The Summer That Never Was](/Sources.aspx?ID=214) pg. 84

**Perception** +5; no face

**Languages**
[Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1); [telepathy](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=37) 30 feet

**Skills**
[Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=1) +6, [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) +4, [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5) +8, [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15) +6

<row gap="medium">
**Str** +1

**Dex** +3

**Con** +2

**Int** +1

**Wis** +0

**Cha** +3
</row>

**No Face** Noppera-bos have no sense of vision, but their sense of hearing is [precise](/Rules.aspx?ID=411). They don't breathe and are immune to effects that require breathing. They gain sustenance by absorbing fluids through their skin—traditionally by immersing their hands or faceless head into the fluid to “drink” through osmosis; they can also benefit from [consumables](/Traits.aspx?ID=36), such as [potions](/Traits.aspx?ID=130) or [elixirs](/Traits.aspx?ID=59), in this way.

**Items**
[Leather Armor](/Armor.aspx?ID=4), [Shortbow](/Weapons.aspx?ID=77) (20 arrows), [Shortsword](/Weapons.aspx?ID=43)

</column>

---

<column gap="tiny">

<row gap="medium">
**AC** 16 

**Fort** +7 

**Ref** +8 

**Will** +5 

</row>

<row gap="medium">
**HP** 20

</row>

**Immunities**
[inhaled](/Traits.aspx?ID=96), [olfactory](/Traits.aspx?ID=246), [visual](/Traits.aspx?ID=163)

**Weaknesses**
sensitive hearing

**Sensitive Hearing** As long as a noppera-bo is [deafened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=8), they are [slowed 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=35).

</column>

---

<column gap="tiny">

**Speed** 25 feet

**Melee**
<actions string="Single Action" />
shortsword +8 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [Finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=179), [versatile S](/Traits.aspx?ID=200)),
**Damage** 1d6+1 piercing

**Ranged**
<actions string="Single Action" />
shortbow +8 ([deadly d10](/Traits.aspx?ID=174), [range increment 60 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=248)),
**Damage** 1d6 piercing

**Impersonate Shape** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([Concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32), [Occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=120), [Polymorph](/Traits.aspx?ID=127), [Transmutation](/Traits.aspx?ID=157)) The noppera-bo changes into a Small or Medium humanoid they've touched during the last 24 hours, and the noppera-bo gains the target creature's face and voice. While transformed and their face is covered, the noppera-bo gains a +2 circumstance bonus to Impersonate that creature. As long as the noppera-bo has a face, it loses its no face ability and its listed immunities. The noppera-bo can change back by using this ability again.

**Remove Face** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([Emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=60), [Enchantment](/Traits.aspx?ID=61), [Fear](/Traits.aspx?ID=68), [Mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=106), [Occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=120), [Visual](/Traits.aspx?ID=163)) **Requirements** The noppera-bo trickster is [Impersonating](/Actions.aspx?ID=46) a creature with a face; **Effect** The noppera-bo trickster's facial features melt into nothingness, and they menace a creature within 30 feet. The creature becomes [frightened 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=19) on a failed DC 17 Will save (frightened 2 on a critical failure).

**[Sneak Attack](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=34)**   The noppera-bo trickster deals an additional 1d4 precision damage to creatures that are [flat-footed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=16).

</column>

Recall Knowledge - Aberration (Occultism): DC 17 Unspecific Lore : DC 15 Specific Lore : DC 12 Noppera-Bo Trickster Source Pathfinder #196: The Summer That Never Was pg. 84 Perception +5; no face Languages Common; telepathy 30 feet Skills Acrobatics +6, Athletics +4, Deception +8, Stealth +6 Str +1 Dex +3 Con +2 Int +1 Wis +0 Cha +3 No Face Noppera-bos have no sense of vision, but their sense of hearing is precise. They don't breathe and are immune to effects that require breathing. They gain sustenance by absorbing fluids through their skin—traditionally by immersing their hands or faceless head into the fluid to “drink” through osmosis; they can also benefit from consumables, such as potions or elixirs, in this way. Items Leather Armor, Shortbow (20 arrows), Shortsword --- AC 16 Fort +7 Ref +8 Will +5 HP 20 Immunities inhaled, olfactory, visual Weaknesses sensitive hearing Sensitive Hearing As long as a noppera-bo is deafened, they are slowed 1. --- Speed 25 feet Melee Single Action shortsword +8 (Agile, Finesse, versatile S), Damage 1d6+1 piercing Ranged Single Action shortbow +8 (deadly d10, range increment 60 feet), Damage 1d6 piercing Impersonate Shape Two Actions (Concentrate, Occult, Polymorph, Transmutation) The noppera-bo changes into a Small or Medium humanoid they've touched during the last 24 hours, and the noppera-bo gains the target creature's face and voice. While transformed and their face is covered, the noppera-bo gains a +2 circumstance bonus to Impersonate that creature. As long as the noppera-bo has a face, it loses its no face ability and its listed immunities. The noppera-bo can change back by using this ability again. Remove Face Two Actions (Emotion, Enchantment, Fear, Mental, Occult, Visual) Requirements The noppera-bo trickster is Impersonating a creature with a face; Effect The noppera-bo trickster's facial features melt into nothingness, and they menace a creature within 30 feet. The creature becomes frightened 1 on a failed DC 17 Will save (frightened 2 on a critical failure). Sneak Attack The noppera-bo trickster deals an additional 1d4 precision damage to creatures that are flat-footed.

A nosoi resembles a whippoorwill, sparrow, or other small bird wearing a heavy leather plague doctor's mask. They are the clerks, messengers, and scribes of the [Boneyard](/Planes.aspx?ID=39), witnessing judgments, directing souls, and generally performing the administrative grunt work that keeps the Boneyard functioning. Most nosois are particularly chatty and eager to discuss how important they consider their individual assignments to be. [Nosoi](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3147) **Source** [Monster Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=221) pg. 274 1.1 **Perception** +6; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59), [lifesense](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=67) 60 feet **Languages** [Chthonian](/Languages.aspx?ID=114), [Diabolic](/Languages.aspx?ID=117), [Empyrean](/Languages.aspx?ID=115), [Requian](/Languages.aspx?ID=34) **Skills** [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=1) +6, [Boneyard Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8) +8, [Library Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8) +8, [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=12) +6, [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=13) +6, [Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=14) +2, [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15) +6 **Str** -1 **Dex** +3 **Con** +1 **Int** +1 **Wis** +1 **Cha** +3 --- **AC** 16 **Fort** +4 **Ref** +8 **Will** +6 **HP** 18 **Immunities** [death](/Traits.aspx?ID=571) effects, [disease](/Traits.aspx?ID=578) **Resistances** [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=669) 3, [void](/Traits.aspx?ID=510) 3 --- **Speed** 15 feet, fly 40 feet **Melee** beak +6 ([Finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=179), [Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103), [reach 0 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)), **Damage** 1d4–1 piercing plus 1d6 shepherd's touch **Divine Innate Spells** DC 16 - **2nd** [Invisibility](/Spells.aspx?ID=164) (at will; self only), [Noise Blast](/Spells.aspx?ID=1616) - **4th** [Read Omens](/Spells.aspx?ID=247), [Talking Corpse](/Spells.aspx?ID=329) **[Change Shape](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=55)** ([Concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32), [Divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=48), [Polymorph](/Traits.aspx?ID=127)) The nosoi takes the appearance of a raven or songbird. This doesn't change its Speed or its attack and damage modifiers with its Strikes. **Haunting Melody** ([Auditory](/Traits.aspx?ID=16), [Concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32), [Divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=48), [Incapacitation](/Traits.aspx?ID=93), [Mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=106)) The nosoi croons an entrancing song. Each living or [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=722) creature within a 60-foot emanation must attempt a DC 18 Will save. The effect lasts until the end of the nosoi's next turn, but the nosoi can Sustain it. A creature that succeeds at its save is temporarily immune for 24 hours. Despite being a [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647) effect, this ability affects [mindless](/Traits.aspx?ID=652) undead. Psychopomps are immune to this ability.
**Failure** The creature is [fascinated](/Conditions.aspx?ID=72) with the nosoi.
**Critical Failure** The creature is fascinated with the nosoi and must spend each of its actions on its turn to move closer to the nosoi as expediently as possible while avoiding obvious dangers. If a fascinated creature is adjacent to the nosoi, it stays still and doesn't act. If the creature is attacked, the fascination ends. **Shepherd's Touch** A nosoi's Strikes have the benefit of a [_ghost touch_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2840) property rune and deal an additional 1d6 void damage to living creatures or 1d6 vitality damage to undead.

<title level="1" pfs="">[Orc Agriculturalist](/NPCs.aspx?ID=3662)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

In the severe lands orcs occupy, there are no lush fields blooming with crops. An orc farmer must be tough and just as adept at foraging as planting and harvesting.

<column gap="tiny">
**[Recall Knowledge - Humanoid](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**
([Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=47)): DC 15

**[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 13

**[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 10
</column>

</column>

<column gap="medium">

</column>

</row>

<title level="2" right="Creature 1">[Orc Agriculturalist](/NPCs.aspx?ID=3662)</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Medium" />
<trait label="Humanoid" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=628" />
<trait label="Orc" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=666" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [NPC Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=236) pg. 206

**Perception** +7; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59)

**Languages**
[Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1), [Orcish](/Languages.aspx?ID=9)

**Skills**
[Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) +5, [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=37) +3, [Farming Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) +13, [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43) +11, [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=49) +7

<row gap="medium">
**Str** +2

**Dex** +1

**Con** +2

**Int** +0

**Wis** +4

**Cha** +0
</row>

**Farming Specialist** For encounters involving farming, harvesting, or identifying plants, the agriculturalist is a 5th-level challenge.

**Items**
[Blowgun](/Weapons.aspx?ID=66) (20 darts), pitchfork (as [longspear](/Weapons.aspx?ID=361)), poisonous herb (5), [Sickle](/Weapons.aspx?ID=9)

</column>

---

<column gap="tiny">

<row gap="medium">
**AC** 14 

**Fort** +9 

**Ref** +6 

**Will** +7 

</row>

<row gap="medium">
**HP** 25

</row>

</column>

---

<column gap="tiny">

**Speed** 25 feet

**Melee**
<actions string="Single Action" />
pitchfork +7 ([Reach](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)),
**Damage** 1d8+2 piercing

**Melee**
<actions string="Single Action" />
sickle +7 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [Trip](/Traits.aspx?ID=196)),
**Damage** 1d4+2 slashing

**Melee**
<actions string="Single Action" />
fist +7 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [Nonlethal](/Traits.aspx?ID=188), [Unarmed](/Traits.aspx?ID=199)),
**Damage** 1d4+2 bludgeoning

**Ranged**
<actions string="Single Action" />
blowgun +6 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [Nonlethal](/Traits.aspx?ID=188), [range increment 20 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=248), [reload 1](/Traits.aspx?ID=254)),
**Damage** 1 piercing

**Herbal Poison** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([Manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104), [Poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=126)) The agriculturalist quickly turns some of their supplies of poisonous herbs into an herbal poison, then applies it to a melee weapon or piece of ammunition in their possession. The next successful attack with a weapon poisoned this way deals an additional 1d6 poison damage. The applied poison fades after its damage is applied to an attack or 1 minute passes, whichever happens first.

**Poison Detector** <actions string="Two Actions" />  The orc agriculturalist attempts a [Farming Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) or [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43) check to determine whether an object is [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=669) or has been poisoned. The DC is the poison's DC (if any), or the standard DC of the poison's level. On a critical success, they also learn the number and types of poison involved.

</column>
