They can shift back to solely the Ethereal Plane by using this ability again. --- **AC** 15 **Fort** +5 **Ref** +8 **Will** +5 **HP** 15 **Immunities** [disease](/Traits.aspx?ID=46), [paralyzed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=28), [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=126), precision **Resistances** all damage 2 (except [force](/Traits.aspx?ID=75) or [_ghost touch_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=297)^ double resistance vs. non-[magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103)) **Susceptible to Death** Though phantoms aren't alive, neither are they [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=160), and they are uniquely vulnerable to the effects of death. A phantom whose Hit Points are reduced to 0 as a result of a [death](/Traits.aspx?ID=40) effect (such as from a spell like [_finger of death_](/Spells.aspx?ID=116)) is immediately whisked away to the River of Souls, where their soul resumes the usual path to the afterlife.
**Vulnerable to Kindness** Any creature within 30 feet that the phantom can see and hear can issue a calm and friendly greeting to it as a two-action activity with the [auditory](/Traits.aspx?ID=16), [concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32), [linguistic](/Traits.aspx?ID=101), and [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=106) traits. A creature greeting the phantom in this manner must attempt a DC 18 [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=6) check.
**Critical Success** The phantom takes 4d8 mental damage and is [stunned 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=36).
**Success** The phantom takes 2d8 mental damage.
**Failure** The phantom takes 1d8 mental damage.
**Critical Failure** The phantom is unaffected, and is not affected by this weakness for 1 round. --- **Speed** fly 25 feet **Melee** jaws +7 ([Finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=179), [Force](/Traits.aspx?ID=75), [Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103)), **Damage** 1d6+2 force

Raktavarnas are simple rakshasa incarnations of betrayal and assassination, often existing to test the mettle of those who were treacherous or poisonous in a previous life. <title level="1" pfs="Standard">[Reefclaw](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3166)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

Reefclaws are aquatic monsters that resemble huge shrimp or lobsters. As one might expect from its name, a reefclaw's oversized claws are powerful weapons with a viselike grip and the ability to inject potent venom into unfortunate prey.

 Though reefclaws can't speak, they are intelligent enough to understand the local language of humanoids near their hunting grounds. The creatures sometimes listen to conversations, either to gain intelligence on the best place to ambush aquatic or land-dwelling prey, or merely for entertainment value—reefclaws are particularly fond of listening to people with high-pitched voices. Reefclaws are usually solitary hunters, but small swarms of female reefclaws have been known to gather around a single male for mating purposes or together for the communal raising of their broods. In the latter case, the females will perform widespread hunts in order to bring back a large enough bounty to feed their young. Such hunting parties are extremely dangerous—they've been known to tip over small fishing boats and attack those who fall overboard.

 Once a reefclaw has decided upon a course of action, it follows through even if doing so spells its own end. More than one reefclaw survivor has said that the creature released its bone-crushing grasp only after the brains were leaking from its broken skull, and even then, the reefclaw was able to perform a terrible last slash as part of its dying breath. During mating season, female reefclaws are often a little more pragmatic and release their prey before endangering themselves and their offspring.

 Despite their intelligence and the accompanying moral quandaries, reefclaws frequently find their way onto the dinner plates of land-dwelling hunters such as humans and hobgoblins. According to those who have a taste for reefclaw flesh, the meat is either delectably sweet (for reefclaws raised in colder waters) or slightly tangy (in the case of warm-water reefclaws). Most people who know of reefclaws' intellect find the act of eating them distasteful, but this does not dissuade unscrupulous nobles in coastal regions, for whom reefclaw meat is a delicacy well worth the expense. Likewise, fishers whose focus is on the bottom line of their ledgers are more than willing to hunt the dangerous creatures—or, even better, hire out the task to naive adventurers.

according to those who have a taste for reefclaw flesh, the meat is either delectably sweet (for reefclaws raised in colder waters) or slightly tangy (in the case of warm-water reefclaws). most people who know of reefclaws' intellect find the act of eating them distasteful, but this does not dissuade unscrupulous nobles in coastal regions, for whom reefclaw meat is a delicacy well worth the expense. likewise, fishers whose focus is on the bottom line of their ledgers are more than willing to hunt the dangerous creatures—or, even better, hire out the task to naive adventurers. recall <row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

Riding dogs types include larger dogs, such as mastiffs, wolfhounds, and huskies, and are bred often by halflings and gnomes to serve as mounts. Riding dogs are as loyal and devoted to their masters as guard dogs and ferocious in battle, regardless of whether they bear a rider or not. As with guard dogs, these large hounds can be wild or feral in nature, and in such cases might rival wolf packs in the danger they pose to inhabitants of rural areas.

text: Talos The geniekin called taloses descend primarily from zuhra genies, metal elementals, and other denizens of the Plane of Metal. Many taloses mold their natural talent for metalwork into careers as tinkerers, miners, or smiths, although just as many leverage the luster of precious metals in a quest for fame and fortune. Taloses are among the most metropolitan of geniekin, often born in or drawn to cities of various sizes, especially those with advanced metalworking or technology trades. Metal often needs to be worked to find its form and function, which may explain why many taloses seem to enjoy living among people, if not necessarily socializing with them. They often find themselves stumbling into jobs somewhere along the production line of technology, whether it's mining the raw ore from the earth, working it into wires and gears, or constructing the devices themselves. Some taloses resent and reject the expectations that they fill such roles, but many embrace their fascination with tech, often going on to become expert inventors. Taloses are therefore far more likely than other geniekin to make use of clockwork technology in their communities. Despite having long inhabited Golarion, albeit in small numbers, taloses have only rarely been recognized as geniekin. The largest number of them, and also the largest number whose true nature is known, inhabit Tian Xia. The traditions of metal as an element have lived much longer there. Taloses often find themselves drawn to discussions and study of elemental metal the instant they hear of the concept. Historical records speak of renowned courtiers and diplomats with skin of flawless silver or bronze. In the Ivory Port of Goka, the smiths of the family-owned Dragon's Iron Forge craft their blades and firearms with magnetic techniques handed down from their zuhra sheikha ancestor. A talos gadgeteer is a clockwork tinkerer. When confronted, their preferred tactic is to lure opponents into traps using their lesser explosive mines before attempting to engage directly. Items artisan's toolkit, formula book, Leather Armor, light hammer (3) --- AC 17 Fort +6 Ref +6 Will +5 HP 17 (plus 5 temporary HP (from ablative armor plating)) Resistances electricity 1 Reflective Defense Reaction (light) Frequency once per round; Trigger A creature within 30 feet targets the talos gadgeteer, and they can see the attacker; Requirements The talos is in dim or bright light; Effect The talos gadgeteer reflects light off their metallic skin and into the enemy's eyes; it must succeed at a DC 14 Reflex save or be dazzled until the end of the talos's next turn. --- Speed 25 feet Melee Single Action fist +8 (Agile, Finesse, versatile S), Damage 1d6+1 bludgeoning Melee Single Action light hammer +6 (Agile), Damage 1d6+1 bludgeoning Ranged Single Action light hammer +8 (Agile, thrown 20 feet), Damage 1d6+1 bludgeoning Arcane Innate Spells DC 14 - Cantrips (1st) Detect Metal Traveling Tinkerers While there are no known permanent talos settlements in the Universe, there is a small nomadic community known as the Tinkerers' Caravan. Originally founded in Vudra and inspired by similar clans of janns and sulis, the caravan now travels throughout most of the eastern world, offering all taloses who wish to travel with them a sense of community and belonging that they might not find anywhere else.

Although the typical vampire bat has a wingspan of 7 inches and doesn't pose a significant threat to larger prey alone (and indeed, these blood-drinkers can feed without their sleeping victims ever noticing), some unusually aggressive species of these bats hunt in deadly swarms. A churning cloud of vampire bats is much more dangerous than the sum of its individual parts and is capable of inflicting an overwhelming number of bleeding wounds in a frighteningly short span of time.

<title level="1" pfs="Standard">[Vegetable Lamb](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2669)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

Vegetable lambs are gaining popularity as the first elemental to be summoned by spellcasters in training, as they're docile until provoked and easy to control. Casters must take care, however, to not let them germinate in the [Universe](/Planes.aspx?ID=1); they're a highly invasive species that can devour an entire forest within a decade.

 The healing and nourishing food that grows from vegetable lambs is appealing for adventurers and sedentary magical scholars alike. The taste is similar to the plants of the same kind that grow on Golarion, but not entirely. Many have noted that there's a slight similarity to meat—a bit of umami one wouldn't find in an ordinary flower.

<title level="1" pfs="Standard">[Velociraptor](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2915)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

A smaller cousin of the deinonychus, the velociraptor is a swift, cunning pack hunter. It has no fear of larger creatures, and a group of these dinosaurs won't hesitate to attack prey the size of a horse. They have manes of feathery plumage that extend down their backs and along the sides of their arms, legs, and tail, while their underbellies and flanks are scaly. These feathers allow them to blend into their natural terrain with ease, but when startled, a velociraptor can puff and frill this plumage to expose brighter colors normally covered by the longer feathers. A typical velociraptor is 1-1/2 feet tall, 7 feet long, and weighs 35 pounds.

Other proteans don't consider the flying, iridescent beings known as voidworms to be part of a protean caste at all, but instead merely a shameful side effect of the [Maelstrom's](/Planes.aspx?ID=43)constantly churning energy. To call a voidworm a protean in the presence of a more powerful protean is a sure a way to instigate combat. Voidworms themselves have little interest in whether anyone sees them as proteans. They maintain a thriving ecology in the Maelstrom, frolicking in schools of up to 20 and playing in the chaos of constantly shifting realities. Elsewhere (such as in [the Universe](/Planes.aspx?ID=26)), voidworms are mesmerized by the principle of object permanence; many latch onto specific features of a region (such as a hillside or pond) and flit through the air around it for months or even years as they wait for the object of their curiosity to change. Minor changes—such as a tree's change of color in the fall, a corpse's slow decay, or periodic venting of steam from a geyser—all fascinate voidworms. A voidworm is about 2 feet long and weighs 2 pounds. **[Recall Knowledge - Monitor](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46)): DC 15 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 13 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 10 [Voidworm](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3144) **Source** [Monster Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=221) pg. 270 1.1 **Perception** +4; entropy sense ([imprecise](/Rules.aspx?ID=412)) 30 feet, [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59) **Languages** [Chthonian](/Languages.aspx?ID=114), [Protean](/Languages.aspx?ID=33) **Skills** [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=1) +7, [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5) +6, [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=13) +4, [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15) +7 **Str** -1 **Dex** +4 **Con** +0 **Int** -1 **Wis** -1 **Cha** +1 **Entropy Sense** ([divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=579), [prediction](/Traits.aspx?ID=674)) A voidworm can anticipate the most likely presence of a creature through a supernatural insight into chaotic probabilities and chance. This grants them the ability to sense creatures within the listed range. [_Veil of privacy_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1739) prevents a creature from being detected via entropy sense automatically (without a counteract check). --- **AC** 17 **Fort** +5 **Ref** +9 **Will** +6 **HP** 16 ([fast healing](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=62) 1) **Resistances** precision 3, protean anatomy 5 **Protean Anatomy** ([divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=579)) A voidworm's vital organs shift and change shape and position constantly. Immediately after the voidworm takes acid, electricity, or sonic damage, they gain the listed amount of resistance to that damage type. This lasts for 1 hour or until the next time the protean takes damage of one of the other types (in which case their resistance changes to match that type), whichever comes first.
The voidworm is immune to [polymorph](/Traits.aspx?ID=670) effects unless they're a willing target. If [blinded](/Conditions.aspx?ID=59) or [deafened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=66), the voidworm automatically recovers at the end of their next turn as new sensory organs grow to replace the compromised ones. --- **Speed** 20 feet, fly 40 feet; [_unfettered movement_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1732) **Melee** jaws +9 ([Finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=179), [Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103), [reach 0 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)), **Damage** 1d8+1 piercing **Melee** tail +9 ([Finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=179), [Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103), [reach 0 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)), **Damage** 1d4+1 slashing plus confounding lash **Divine Innate Spells** DC 16 - **Cantrips (4th)** [Figment](/Spells.aspx?ID=1528), [Light](/Spells.aspx?ID=171), [Prestidigitation](/Spells.aspx?ID=229) - **2nd** [Blur](/Spells.aspx?ID=28) (self only), [Mist](/Spells.aspx?ID=1606) - **4th** [Read Omens](/Spells.aspx?ID=247) - **Constant (4th)** [Unfettered Movement](/Spells.aspx?ID=1732) **[Change Shape](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=55)** ([Divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=48), [Polymorph](/Traits.aspx?ID=127)) The voidworm takes on the appearance of a Tiny [animal](/Traits.aspx?ID=531). This doesn't change their Speed or their attack and damage bonuses with their Strikes but might change the damage type their Strikes deal. **Confounding Lash** ([Divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=48), [Emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=60), [Mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=106)) A creature hit by the voidworm's tail Strike is [stupefied 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=94) for 1 round (stupefied 2 on a critical hit). A successful DC 16 Will save negates this effect and grants temporary immunity to confounding lash for 1 minute.

Water scamps are marked apart from other scamps by sleek fur that traps a layer of water next to their skin. <title level="1" pfs="Standard">[Wolf](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3241)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

Wolves live and hunt in packs, which, contrary to popular belief, are not led by the strongest in the group, but typically consist of a mated pair, their pups, and juvenile offspring from previous mating seasons. Offspring generally leave their parents' pack upon reaching maturity, at which point they seek out mates of their own to form their own packs elsewhere.

 Humanoids are not traditionally viewed as prey animals by wolves, but extraordinary circumstances can lead these animals to attack people, especially in winter months and other situations where traditional prey (deer and elk mainly) is scarce. Some beings, such as powerful [vampires](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=480), can call upon wolves to aid them in combat.

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

A wood scamp's veiny, bat-like wings mimic the lamina and venules of a leaf. This, along with their stout green torsos and limbs, enables them to easily blend into the branches of a living tree. They're unusually social for scamps and prefer to work in groups when possible. By their nature, they find their home plane rather boring, and many of them are abuzz with excitement as the plane reopens. They're eager to travel to new places where they can cause mischief.

text: Wood Scamp A wood scamp's veiny, bat-like wings mimic the lamina and venules of a leaf. This, along with their stout green torsos and limbs, enables them to easily blend into the branches of a living tree. They're unusually social for scamps and prefer to work in groups when possible. By their nature, they find their home plane rather boring, and many of them are abuzz with excitement as the plane reopens. They're eager to travel to new places where they can cause mischief. <row gap="medium">

Xulgath warriors strike with fury and eager cruelty, always ready for the next fight. The taking of prizes from battle—including weapons and items stolen from defeated foes along with grislier trophies harvested from fallen victims' flesh—is a popular pursuit among these vicious reptiles, and those whose armor and scales are most adorned are awarded the greatest respect (and perhaps fear) from their kin.

<title level="1" pfs="Standard">[Zoaem (Ring Archon)](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2832)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

These endlessly curious archons are formed from spinning wheels of golden light given corporeal shape. They serve as lookouts and mobile support troops for the archon legions, at times uniting to form powerful warriors of light called gestalts. Larger collectives of zoaems can even temporarily fuse into greater archons, approaching the power of the first zoaem, which broke itself apart to serve [Heaven](/Planes.aspx?ID=41) more efficiently.

<title level="1" pfs="Standard">[Animated Armor](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2819)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

Suits of animated armor see use both as guardians and as training partners in high-end martial academies able to afford the extravagance. Often, a warrior's old suit of armor can be turned into animated armor once it accrues too much battle damage to provide adequate protection. They're found most often in wizard laboratories and ancient dungeons.

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

Supple but strong bamboo strips woven into intricate patterns form the base of the animated bamboo figure. These materials are plentiful and easy to come by, though they require great care and patience to prepare, making them ideal guardians for isolated communities. These hollow and pliable handcrafts can stretch or compress, jumping and springing farther than most humanoids.

<column gap="tiny">
**[Recall Knowledge - Construct](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**
([Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=2), [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=4)): DC 16

**[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 14

**[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 11
</column>

</column>

<column gap="medium">

</column>

</row>

<title level="2" right="Creature 2">[Animated Bamboo Figure](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2763)</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Medium" />
<trait label="Construct" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=35" />
<trait label="Mindless" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=108" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Tian Xia World Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=223) pg. 279

**Perception** +8; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=12)

**Languages**

**Skills**
[Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=1) +10, [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) +10

<row gap="medium">
**Str** +4

**Dex** +4

**Con** +3

**Int** -5

**Wis** +0

**Cha** -5
</row>

</column>

---

<column gap="tiny">

<row gap="medium">
**AC** 18 (16 when broken); construct armor

**Fort** +9 

**Ref** +10 

**Will** +6 

</row>

<row gap="medium">
**HP** 30

**Hardness**
3
</row>

**Immunities**
bleed, death effects, disease, doomed, drained, fatigued, healing, mental, nonlethal attacks, paralyzed, poison, sickened, spirit, unconscious, vitality, void

**Construct Armor** Like normal objects, an bamboo figure has Hardness. This Hardness reduces any damage it takes by an amount equal to the Hardness. Once an animated kite is reduced to less than half its Hit Points, or immediately upon being damaged by a critical hit, its construct armor breaks and its Armor Class is reduced to 16.

</column>

---

<column gap="tiny">

**Speed** 30 feet, climb 15 feet

**Melee**
<actions string="Single Action" />
fist +10 ([Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103), [reach 10 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)),
**Damage** 1d8+4 bludgeoning plus [Knockdown](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=46)

**Spring Forward** <actions string="Two Actions" />  The animated bamboo figure jumps up to 30 feet and makes two fist Strikes against different targets. It can use Knockdown following this activity, attempting to Trip each creature struck.

</column>

<title level="1" pfs="">[Arboreal Sapling](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3690)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

Young arboreals often appear lanky and uncoordinated. Their awkwardness belies their burgeoning strength and decades of natural studies.

<column gap="tiny">
**[Recall Knowledge - Plant](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**
([Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43)): DC 16

**[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 14

**[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 11
</column>

</column>

<column gap="medium">

</column>

</row>

<title level="2" right="Creature 2">[Arboreal Sapling](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3690)</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Large" />
<trait label="Plant" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=668" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #201: Pactbreaker](/Sources.aspx?ID=241) pg. 82

**Perception** +11; [low-light vision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=69)

**Languages**
[Arboreal](/Languages.aspx?ID=26), [Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1), [Fey](/Languages.aspx?ID=119)

**Skills**
[Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) +8, [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43) +5, [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=48) +6

<row gap="medium">
**Str** +4

**Dex** +0

**Con** +3

**Int** +0

**Wis** +3

**Cha** +1
</row>

</column>

---

<column gap="tiny">

<row gap="medium">
**AC** 17 

**Fort** +11 

**Ref** +6 

**Will** +9 

</row>

<row gap="medium">
**HP** 35

</row>

**Resistances**
bludgeoning 3, piercing 3

**Weaknesses**
axe vulnerability, fire 5

**Axe Vulnerability** An arboreal sapling takes 5 additional damage from [axes](/WeaponGroups.aspx?ID=1).

</column>

---

<column gap="tiny">

**Speed** 20 feet

**Melee**
<actions string="Single Action" />
fist +11,
**Damage** 1d10+4 bludgeoning

**Melee**
<actions string="Single Action" />
branch +10 ([reach 10 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)),
**Damage** 1d8+4 piercing

**Timber!** <actions string="Reaction" />  **Trigger** An arboreal sapling that is not [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=88) either becomes prone or is reduced to 0 HP; **Effect** The arboreal sapling topples over, dealing 2d6 bludgeoning damage to itself and to creatures in a 10-foot line (DC 16 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex). Creatures that critically fail the saving throw are also knocked prone.

**Shaky Footing**   When an arboreal sapling critically fails an attack roll or Reflex saving throw, it becomes [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=88) unless it succeeds at a DC 11 flat check.

</column>

<aside>

<title level="1" pfs="">[Archer Sentry](/NPCs.aspx?ID=3552)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

Archer sentries slightly outrank rank-and-file guards, taking positions on walls, garrisons, and other important locations where they can stay out of the fray and pick off criminals or assailants.

<column gap="tiny">
**[Recall Knowledge - Humanoid](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**
([Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=47)): DC 16

**[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 14

**[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 11
</column>

</column>

<column gap="medium">
<image src="/images/Monsters/Archer_Sentry.webp" />
</column>

</row>

<title level="2" right="Creature 2">[Archer Sentry](/NPCs.aspx?ID=3552)</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Medium" />
<trait label="Human" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=627" />
<trait label="Humanoid" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=628" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [NPC Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=236) pg. 111

**Perception** +11

**Languages**
[Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1)

**Skills**
[Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=34) +8, [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) +6, [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=40) +4, [Legal Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) +4

<row gap="medium">
**Str** +2

**Dex** +4

**Con** +1

**Int** +0

**Wis** +3

**Cha** +0
</row>

**Items**
[Composite Longbow](/Weapons.aspx?ID=74) (100 arrows), [Leather Armor](/Armor.aspx?ID=4), [Shortsword](/Weapons.aspx?ID=43), [Signal Whistle](/Equipment.aspx?ID=50)

</column>

---

<column gap="tiny">

<row gap="medium">
**AC** 17 

**Fort** +7 

**Ref** +10 

**Will** +7 

</row>

<row gap="medium">
**HP** 30

</row>

</column>

---

<column gap="tiny">

**Speed** 25 feet

**Melee**
<actions string="Single Action" />
shortsword +10 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [Finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=179), [versatile S](/Traits.aspx?ID=200)),
**Damage** 1d6+4 piercing

**Melee**
<actions string="Single Action" />
fist +10 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [Finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=179), [Nonlethal](/Traits.aspx?ID=188), [Unarmed](/Traits.aspx?ID=199)),
**Damage** 1d4+4 bludgeoning

**Ranged**
<actions string="Single Action" />
composite longbow +10 ([deadly d10](/Traits.aspx?ID=174), [Propulsive](/Traits.aspx?ID=191), [range increment 100 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=248), [reload 0](/Traits.aspx?ID=254), [volley 30 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=201)),
**Damage** 1d8+3 piercing

**Sentry's Aim** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([Concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32)) The archer sentry aims carefully and fires. They make a ranged weapon Strike with a +1 circumstance bonus. The Strike ignores the [concealed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=62) condition, [lesser cover, and standard cover, and reduces greater cover to standard cover](/Rules.aspx?ID=459).

</column>

<title level="1" pfs="">[Arms Dealer](/NPCs.aspx?ID=3506)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

A seedy arms dealer has access to all kinds of deadly weapons and can quickly provide them to clients in need… for the right price, of course.

<column gap="tiny">
**[Recall Knowledge - Humanoid](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**
([Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=47)): DC 16

**[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 14

**[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 11
</column>

</column>

<column gap="medium">
<image src="/images/Monsters/Arms_Dealer.webp" />
</column>

</row>

<title level="2" right="Creature 2">[Arms Dealer](/NPCs.aspx?ID=3506)</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Medium" />
<trait label="Human" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=627" />
<trait label="Humanoid" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=628" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [NPC Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=236) pg. 76

**Perception** +9; (11 to [Sense Motive](/Actions.aspx?ID=2302)) 

**Languages**
[Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1)

**Skills**
[Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=37) +7, [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38) +7, [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39) +7, [Firearm Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) +14, [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=40) +9, [Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=47) +9, [Underworld Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) +9

<row gap="medium">
**Str** +0

**Dex** +3

**Con** +0

**Int** +1

**Wis** +3

**Cha** +3
</row>

**Arms Dealing Specialist** For encounters involving the purchase of weapons, the arms dealer is a 5th-level challenge.

**Items**
[Flintlock Musket](/Weapons.aspx?ID=521) (20 rounds), [Hand Cannon](/Weapons.aspx?ID=193) (20 rounds), [sword cane](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2772)

</column>

---

<column gap="tiny">

<row gap="medium">
**AC** 17 

**Fort** +6 

**Ref** +7 

**Will** +9 

</row>

<row gap="medium">
**HP** 28

</row>

**You Call That a Gun?** The arms dealer seems unaffected by your attempts to threaten them. The arms dealer gains a +2 circumstance bonus to their Will DC against [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=40) checks while they're holding a [firearm](/WeaponGroups.aspx?ID=16).

</column>

---

<column gap="tiny">

**Speed** 25 feet

**Melee**
<actions string="Single Action" />
sword cane +9 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [Concealable](/Traits.aspx?ID=327), [Finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=179)),
**Damage** 1d6+2 piercing

**Melee**
<actions string="Single Action" />
fist +9 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [Finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=179), [Nonlethal](/Traits.aspx?ID=188), [Unarmed](/Traits.aspx?ID=199)),
**Damage** 1d4+2 bludgeoning

**Ranged**
<actions string="Single Action" />
flintlock musket +11 ([Concussive](/Traits.aspx?ID=401), [fatal d10](/Traits.aspx?ID=178), [range increment 70 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=248), [reload 1](/Traits.aspx?ID=254)),
**Damage** 1d6+3 piercing

**Ranged**
<actions string="Single Action" />
hand cannon +11 ([modular B](/Traits.aspx?ID=271), [or S; range increment 30 feet; reload 1](/Traits.aspx?ID=248)),
**Damage** 1d6+3 modular

**Take Stock** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([Auditory](/Traits.aspx?ID=16), [Concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32), [Linguistic](/Traits.aspx?ID=101), [Mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=106)) The arms dealer advises an ally on how to properly use a firearm. The arms dealer chooses an ally within 30 feet wielding a firearm. That ally can use a reaction to Interact to reload their firearm.

</column>

<document level="2" id="creature-family-541" />
name: Arms Dealer

<title level="1" pfs="">[Bleachling Survivor](/NPCs.aspx?ID=3636)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

It is almost unheard of for gnomes to survive the horrendous sickness known as the Bleaching, but those few who do are permanently altered. Having lived through the worst disease known to their kind, bleachling survivors often emerge jaded and reckless, traveling to seek out mind-bending experiences and heady thrills that will awaken something in them again. Though their experiences may toughen them, they are not unfriendly. Most try to help others they meet during their travels who might not be as unshakable.

<title level="1" pfs="Standard">[Boar](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2854)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

Boars are omnivorous mammals, hunted heavily because their meat is considered a delicacy. Boars are most likely to attack humanoids either in self-defense or during their mating season in the winter months, when the males grow an extra inch of tissue to protect their organs as they fight off rivals. Of course, in some cultures, boars are trained to become much more aggressive so they can fill the roles of warbeast and guardian. When such boars escape back into the wild, they can become true terrors in the region.

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

Boggard warriors exalt single combat and prefer to fight alone so that no one can contest their kills. They have been known to pursue enemies who flee combat with a single-mindedness that seems almost supernatural.

<column gap="tiny">
**[Recall Knowledge - Humanoid](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**
([Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=47)): DC 16

<traits>
<trait label="Medium" />
<trait label="Amphibious" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=529" />
<trait label="Boggard" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=743" />
<trait label="Humanoid" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=628" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Monster Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=221) pg. 44 <sup>1.1</sup>

**Perception** +8; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59)

**Languages**
[Boggard](/Languages.aspx?ID=27)

**Skills**
[Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) +8, [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=7) +5, [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15) +6

<row gap="medium">
**Str** +4

**Dex** +0

**Con** +4

**Int** -1

**Wis** +2

**Cha** +1
</row>

**Items**
[Club](/Weapons.aspx?ID=2), [Javelin](/Weapons.aspx?ID=71) (3), [Studded Leather Armor](/Armor.aspx?ID=5)

</column>

---

<column gap="tiny">

<row gap="medium">
**AC** 17 

**Fort** +10 

**Ref** +5 

**Will** +8 

</row>

<row gap="medium">
**HP** 38

</row>

</column>

---

<column gap="tiny">

**Speed** 20 feet, swim 25 feet; swamp passage

**Melee**
<actions string="Single Action" />
club +10,
**Damage** 1d6+6 bludgeoning

**Melee**
<actions string="Single Action" />
tongue +10 ([reach 10 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)),
**Damage** tongue grab

**Ranged**
<actions string="Single Action" />
javelin +6 ([thrown 30 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=195)),
**Damage** 1d6+4 piercing

**Ranged**
<actions string="Single Action" />
club +6 ([thrown 10 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=195)),
**Damage** 1d6+6 bludgeoning

**Swamp Passage**   A boggard ignores [difficult terrain](/Rules.aspx?ID=453) caused by swamp terrain features.

**Terrifying Croak** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([Auditory](/Traits.aspx?ID=16), [Emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=60), [Fear](/Traits.aspx?ID=68), [Mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=106)) The boggard unleashes a terrifying croak. Any non-boggard within 30 feet becomes [frightened 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=76) unless they succeed at a DC 18 Will save; those who critically succeed are temporarily immune for 1 minute.

**Tongue Grab**   If the boggard hits a creature with their tongue, that creature becomes [grabbed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=77) by the boggard. Unlike with a normal Grab, the creature isn't [immobilized](/Conditions.aspx?ID=81), but it can't move beyond the reach of the boggard's tongue. A creature can sever the tongue by hitting AC 15 and dealing at least 3 slashing damage. Though this doesn't deal any damage to the boggard, it prevents them from using their tongue Strike until they regrow their tongue, which takes a week.

</column>

<title level="1" pfs="Standard">[Caligni Skulker](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2863)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

Most often found on the surface are caligni skulkers, stealing staple goods and luxuries alike. When pressed into combat by more powerful caligni, skulkers will often be sacrificed in waves to wear down the enemy. Otherwise, skulkers are fairly cautious and prefer to flee unwinnable situations.

<column gap="tiny">
**[Recall Knowledge - Humanoid](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**
([Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=47)): DC 16

**[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 14

**[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 11
</column>

</column>

<traits>
<trait label="Medium" />
<trait label="Caligni" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=745" />
<trait label="Humanoid" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=628" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Monster Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=221) pg. 48 <sup>1.1</sup>

**Perception** +8; [greater darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59), [light blindness](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=68)

**Languages**
[Caligni](/Languages.aspx?ID=28)

**Skills**
[Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=1) +8, [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) +4, [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15) +10, [Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=17) +8

<row gap="medium">
**Str** +0

**Dex** +4

**Con** +3

**Int** -1

**Wis** +2

**Cha** +1
</row>

**Items**
darkening poison (3 doses), [Dagger](/Weapons.aspx?ID=3)

</column>

---

<column gap="tiny">

<row gap="medium">
**AC** 19 

**Fort** +9 

**Ref** +10 

**Will** +6 

</row>

<row gap="medium">
**HP** 30
(final night)

</row>

**Final Night** ([darkness](/Traits.aspx?ID=569), [occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=662)) When the caligni skulker dies, their remains dissolve into a 20-foot emanation of inky darkness before dissipating. The darkness extinguishes non-magical light sources and attempts to [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) magical [light](/Traits.aspx?ID=640) as a 1st-rank effect with a +10 counteract modifier. The skulker's possessions are left in a pile where they died.

</column>

---

<column gap="tiny">

**Speed** 25 feet

**Melee**
<actions string="Single Action" />
dagger +10 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [Finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=179), [versatile S](/Traits.aspx?ID=200)),
**Damage** 1d4+4 piercing plus darkening poison

**Ranged**
<actions string="Single Action" />
dagger +10 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [thrown 10 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=195), [versatile S](/Traits.aspx?ID=200)),
**Damage** 1d4 piercing plus darkening poison

**Sneak Attack**   The caligni skulker deals 1d6 extra precision damage to [off-guard](/Conditions.aspx?ID=58) creatures.

**Tumble Behind**   When the caligni skulker [Tumbles Through](/Actions.aspx?ID=2370) a creature's space, that creature is [off-guard](/Conditions.aspx?ID=58) against the next attack the skulker makes against it before the end of its turn.

</column>

<title level="1" pfs="">[Chetamog](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3695)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

In the pockets of old growth that form the most primeval and untamed regions of the Verduran Forest, there are trees of truly staggering size. The upper reaches of these gargantuan trees are the natural domain of the chetamog: a horse-sized arboreal rodent with a bulk belied by the preternatural grace with which it leaps through the canopy. Their speed and agility, as well as a natural intelligence and aptitude for training, have made chetamogs highly sought-after animal companions for those whose travels take them into the depths of the forest, a demand that has been recognized by enterprising ranchers who breed and raise the creatures for precisely this purpose.

 A fully grown chetamog resembles an enormous squirrel, roughly 9 feet long and 5 feet high at the shoulder. Properly trained chetamogs are capable of serving as combat mounts. Few sights can match the glory of chetamog cavalry gliding effortlessly through thick ground cover and striking down a legion of earthbound foes before vanishing back into the treetops with ease.

<actions string="Single Action" />

[Daze](/Spells.aspx?ID=61), [Figment](/Spells.aspx?ID=1528), [Light](/Spells.aspx?ID=171), [Prestidigitation](/Spells.aspx?ID=229), [Void Warp](/Spells.aspx?ID=1745)
- **1st**

**Witch Hex Spells 1 Focus Point,** DC 18
- **Cantrips (1st)**
[Shroud of Night](/Spells.aspx?ID=806)
- **1st**
[Needle of Vengeance](/Spells.aspx?ID=801)

Members of the temporary coven can cast [_charm_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1463), [_entangling flora_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1515), and [_illusory disguise_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1568) as 2nd-rank occult innate spells at will, using DC 17 or their spellcasting DC, whichever is higher. The coven is dissolved after 3 rounds or when all but one member is dead, whichever comes first. A creature can be a member of only one temporary coven at a time and can join a temporary coven no more than once per 24 hours.

<title level="1" pfs="Standard">[Crocodile](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2887)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

Crocodiles can be found basking on riverbanks, lurking in swamps, or floating in lakes. They are usually indistinguishable from logs when viewed from afar—at least until they attack. Alligators have similar statistics, but because they often live in more temperate climates, they endure cold temperatures better. Unlike alligators, crocodiles can tolerate salt water. Both are formidable predators that are likely to devour careless adventurers who fail to watch where they step.

<title level="1" pfs="Standard">[Deinonychus](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2916)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

Deinonychuses are wily hunters that attack in groups of up to a dozen individuals, ripping apart prey with sharp talons and powerful jaws. They are lean, muscular, and have two powerful legs and a long tail that helps them maintain balance. Although deinonychuses don't use their dexterous clawed forelimbs to attack, the dinosaurs can use them to pull aside small barriers. Although some of these dinosaurs have scaly skin, most have thatches of vibrantly colored feathers as well. A deinonychus is about 6 feet tall and weighs about 150 pounds.

With daring and charm, a driver is a professional operator of mechanical vehicles. Their skill and recklessness give them a reputation that puts even the quickest horse riders to shame. text: Dragonet Although they are much smaller than their larger dragon cousins, fey dragonets have many of the same physiological attributes, including long necks, toothy maws, sinuous tails, and sharp claws. They flit about on iridescent butterfly wings, the coloring of which changes based on where they live, giving them a natural camouflage. Unlike their larger kin, an adult fey dragonet remains the same size throughout their lifespan. The only visual clue to the age of a fey dragonet is the sheen on their scales, a glimmer that becomes more lustrous the older they get. Fey dragonets usually exhibit pleasant and good-natured temperaments, though they have a mischievous streak that leads them to play tricks on those around them. In search of amusement, they prefer harmless annoyances over wounding malice. While often spontaneous, they may also spend months, if not years, planning the perfect prank. Especially responsive targets endear themselves to fey dragonets and may create a lifelong bond. A fey dragonet's reputation as a trickster leads many to associate them with fey, with whom the tiny dragons have cordial relationships, and this association gives them their name. Peaceful by nature, fey dragonets don't enjoy confrontation. If faced with hostility, they prefer to remain at a distance and breathe euphoric gas at their foes, diffusing the skirmish by creating an atmosphere of bliss. If conflict escalates, they target their opponents with spells, using their renowned trickery to escape. If their companions are in danger, however, their desire to remain out of combat changes. Fey dragonets protect their friends by any means available, including physical combat. Sometimes, as fey dragonets grow older, their connection to the First World grows stronger. In addition to growing more lustrous and vibrant in appearance, these fey dragonets gain an increasing amount of magical primal power. Such fey dragonets increase in strength as appropriate—a fey dragonet of 20th level or even higher is possible, but it's exceptionally unusual to encounter a fey dragonet of 9th level or higher beyond the most remote regions of the First World. When creating a more powerful fey dragonet, change their spellcasting tradition to primal and grant them primal spells appropriate for a druid of their level. Fey dragonets don't grow much larger, regardless of how powerful they become. It's often difficult to tell how powerful one of these tiny dragons truly is at a glance! The fey dragonet can't use Euphoric Breath again for 1d4 rounds. Fey Dragonet Lairs Fey dragonets live in old forests or places where the veil between the First World and the Universe is thinnest. They often decorate their lairs with sparkly trinkets or groom the surrounding foliage into pleasing shapes. Fey Dragonet Treasure The dragons collect small treasures, including magical amulets or rings. Fey dragonet hide can also be made into armor for a Small creature.

<row gap="medium">

Forlorn elves, who spend their lives among shorter-lived peoples, often grow morose from constant loss. Some channel this melancholy into their art.

<trait label="Humanoid" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=628" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [NPC Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=236) pg. 178

**Perception** +7; (9 to notice unusual artwork) [low-light vision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=69)

**Languages**
[Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1), [Elven](/Languages.aspx?ID=4); one regional language

**Skills**
[Art Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) +11, [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=37) +11, [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39) +9, [Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=47) +8

<row gap="medium">
**Str** +0

**Dex** +3

**Con** -1

**Int** +4

**Wis** +1

**Cha** +3
</row>

**Art Specialist** For encounters involving crafting or evaluating art, the forlorn artist is a 4th-level challenge.

**Items**
art supplies, [Leather Armor](/Armor.aspx?ID=4), [Rapier](/Weapons.aspx?ID=36)

</column>

---

<column gap="tiny">

<row gap="medium">
**AC** 18 

**Fort** +3 

**Ref** +9 

**Will** +9 

+1 circumstance vs. [emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=590) effects
</row>

<row gap="medium">
**HP** 26

</row>

**Flick Ink** <actions string="Reaction" /> **Trigger** The artist is targeted with a melee or ranged Strike by a creature within 15 feet; **Effect** The artist flings ink in the attacker's eyes. The attacker must succeed at a DC 18 Reflex save or be [blinded](/Conditions.aspx?ID=59). This takes effect before the attacker targets the artist. The blindness lasts until the end of the target's next turn, but the creature can Interact to rub its eyes to attempt a new save to end the condition.

</column>

---

<column gap="tiny">

**Speed** 25 feet

**Melee**
<actions string="Single Action" />
rapier +9 ([deadly d8](/Traits.aspx?ID=174), [Disarm](/Traits.aspx?ID=175), [Finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=179)),
**Damage** 1d6+4 piercing

**Melee**
<actions string="Single Action" />
fist +9 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [Finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=179), [Nonlethal](/Traits.aspx?ID=188), [Unarmed](/Traits.aspx?ID=199)),
**Damage** 1d4+4 bludgeoning

**Arcane Innate Spells** DC 18
- **Cantrips (1st)**
[Figment](/Spells.aspx?ID=1528), [Prestidigitation](/Spells.aspx?ID=229), [Sigil](/Spells.aspx?ID=286)

**Cry of Ages** <actions string="Single Action" />  The artist channels their loneliness into a wordless wail that forces others to contemplate their mortality. Each enemy in a 30-foot emanation must succeed at a DC 17 Will save or be [frightened 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=76). A creature that critically fails is also [stupefied 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=94) for 1 minute. Each creature is then temporarily immune for 1 minute.

</column>

This ability otherwise uses the effects of [_one with plants_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1618).

**Spore Cloud** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([Poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=126)) A fungus leshy can unleash a cloud of spores that irritates the eyes and throats of non-fungus creatures in a 15-foot emanation. <title level="1" pfs="Standard">[Gennayn](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2687)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

Gennayns are minor genies who often serve as emissaries and messengers for greater elemental beings. While many find purpose in this humble mission, their true calling and interest is in the arts.

 They often appear as miniature, athletic humanoids with wisps of elemental energy continually dissipating from their bodies. These elemental energies often reflect their emotions and attuned element. Gennayns are also fond of ostentatious rings, amulets, and armbands.

 Gennayns eagerly assist powerful beings who reward and treat them well, but they're just as quick to abandon those they consider boring, stingy, or abusive. Beings who destroy artwork or mistreat artists will earn their eternal wrath.

<column gap="tiny">
**[Recall Knowledge - Elemental](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**
([Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=2), [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=10)): DC 16

**[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 14

**[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 11
</column>

</column>

<column gap="medium">

</column>

</row>

<title level="2" right="Creature 2">[Gennayn](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2687)</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Tiny" />
<trait label="Elemental" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=57" />
<trait label="Genie" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=216" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 226 <sup>2.0</sup>

**Perception** +8; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=12)

**Languages**
[Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1), [Muan](/Languages.aspx?ID=108), [Petran](/Languages.aspx?ID=109), [Pyric](/Languages.aspx?ID=110), [Sussuran](/Languages.aspx?ID=111), [Talican](/Languages.aspx?ID=112), [Thalassic](/Languages.aspx?ID=113)

**Skills**
[Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=1) +8, [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=2) +6, [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=6) +8, [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=10) +6, [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=12) +8, [Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=14) +6, [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15) +10

<row gap="medium">
**Str** -2

**Dex** +4

**Con** +0

**Int** +2

**Wis** +2

**Cha** +4
</row>

**Inspiring Influence** A gennayn automatically succeeds with the [Aid](/Actions.aspx?ID=75) action supporting any [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=12) or [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=6) skill check. Their Aid action automatically counts as a critical success while aiding in the creation of new art or a new performance.

</column>

---

<column gap="tiny">

<row gap="medium">
**AC** 17 

**Fort** +4 

**Ref** +10 

**Will** +8 

</row>

<row gap="medium">
**HP** 30

</row>

**Resistances**
attuned element 5 (see below)

</column>

---

<column gap="tiny">

**Speed** 15 feet, fly 15 feet

**Melee**
<actions string="Single Action" />
elemental fist +10 ([Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103), [Finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=179)),
**Damage** 2d6 damage (see attuned element)

**Primal Innate Spells** DC 18, attack +10
- **Cantrips (1st)**
elemental cantrip (see attuned element), [Guidance](/Spells.aspx?ID=142), [Prestidigitation](/Spells.aspx?ID=229), [Summon Instrument](/Spells.aspx?ID=721)
- **1st**
[Purify Food and Drink](/Spells.aspx?ID=241), [Heal](/Spells.aspx?ID=148)
- **2nd**
[Comprehend Language](/Spells.aspx?ID=46) (at will), [Invisibility](/Spells.aspx?ID=164) (at will; self only)

**Attuned Element**   Upon waking each day, a gennayn attunes to one planar element. They gain the corresponding trait, a movement Speed, a cantrip, resistance, and an elemental damage type for their energy fist attack based on their attuned element: **air** fly 30 feet, resist electricity 5, [_electric arc_](/Spells.aspx?ID=97), electricity damage; **earth** burrow 15 feet, resist bludgeoning 5, [_scatter scree_](/Spells.aspx?ID=990), bludgeoning damage; **fire** fly 30 feet, resist fire 5, [_ignition_](/Spells.aspx?ID=236), fire damage; **metal** burrow 15 feet, resist slashing 5, [_needle darts_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1375), slashing damage; **water** swim 20 feet, resist cold 5, [_frostbite_](/Spells.aspx?ID=245), bludgeoning damage; **wood** climb 15 feet, resist piercing 5, [_tangle vine_](/Spells.aspx?ID=330), piercing damage. The attunement lasts until the gennayn attunes to a different element.

**[Change Shape](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=8)** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([Arcane](/Traits.aspx?ID=11), [Concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32), [Polymorph](/Traits.aspx?ID=127)) The gennayn transforms into a Tiny [elemental](/Traits.aspx?ID=57) or [animal](/Traits.aspx?ID=9). This doesn't affect the gennayn's statistics, but it could change the damage type of their Strikes.

**Little Wish** <actions string="Reaction" /> ([Fortune](/Traits.aspx?ID=76)) **Trigger** A creature the gennayn can see that's within 60 feet attempts a saving throw or skill check; **Frequency** once per day; **Effect** The gennayn reshapes reality in a small way to twist fate, allowing the creature to reroll the saving throw or skill check and take the better result.

</column>

<title level="1" pfs="Standard">[Giant Bat](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2849)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

While big bats are certainly not uncommon in dark caves and abandoned ruins and may instill fear in squeamish spelunkers, the so-called giant bat is a true monster, weighing well over 100 pounds and having a wingspan of nearly 15 feet. It primarily eats fruit and bugs, but can be incited to violence through fear or hunger. Giant bat attacks can quickly give rise to rumors of more dangerous monsters—many mistake these massive animals for some sort of demon or vampiric monster. But like other bats, giant bats are simply social and intelligent mammals. They are sometimes used as mounts by smaller humanoids, commonly those who hail from or dwell in mountainous or underground regions.

<title level="1" pfs="Standard">[Giant Monitor Lizard](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3088)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

Large and seemingly ponderous, a monitor lizard is a deceptively swift and ruthless predator. It ambushes its prey by rushing out from cover and biting the target with its powerful jaws. A giant monitor lizard's saliva is venomous, allowing it to bring down prey larger than it can easily haul away in its jaws. Giant monitor lizards grow up to 14 feet long, including their long tails, and they weigh about 350 pounds. Their bodies are normally dark brown with patches of yellow or green.

 When nesting, a giant monitor lizard digs a deep burrow to hide in. The burrow serves as both a safe haven and a location from which the lizard can ambush larger prey such as deer, boars, or even humanoids. A giant monitor lizard can consume nearly its own body weight in a single meal, and its loosely articulated jaws allow it to swallow surprisingly large prey.

text: Giant Monitor Lizard Large and seemingly ponderous, a monitor lizard is a deceptively swift and ruthless predator. It ambushes its prey by rushing out from cover and biting the target with its powerful jaws. A giant monitor lizard's saliva is venomous, allowing it to bring down prey larger than it can easily haul away in its jaws. Giant monitor lizards grow up to 14 feet long, including their long tails, and they weigh about 350 pounds. Their bodies are normally dark brown with patches of yellow or green. When nesting, a giant monitor lizard digs a deep burrow to hide in. The burrow serves as both a safe haven and a location from which the lizard can ambush larger prey such as deer, boars, or even humanoids. A giant monitor lizard can consume nearly its own body weight in a single meal, and its loosely articulated jaws allow it to swallow surprisingly large prey. These mantises have grown to an unusual size, which makes their camouflage less effective in most environments. As such, they're usually found in areas where a blossom the size of an adult human could pass as normal, in the lushest rainforests, or in lands where rare medicinal herbs are cultivated. Renowned for their culinary expertise, halfling head chefs navigate the complex world of high cuisine with flavorful creations and fiery tempers. **[Recall Knowledge - Humanoid](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=47)): DC 16 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 14 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 11 [Halfling Head Chef](/NPCs.aspx?ID=3644) **Source** [NPC Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=236) pg. 190 **Perception** +7; (15 to smell and taste) keen eyes, [scent](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=74) ([imprecise](/Rules.aspx?ID=412)) 30 feet **Languages** [Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1), [Halfling](/Languages.aspx?ID=7) **Skills** [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=34) +7, [Baking Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) +15, [Cooking Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) +17, [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=40) +7, [Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=47) +6 **Str** +1 **Dex** +3 **Con** +2 **Int** +2 **Wis** +1 **Cha** +1 **Culinary Specialist** For encounters involving cooking and taste, the head chef is a 7th-level challenge.
**Keen Eyes** The halfling gains a +2 circumstance bonus when using the [Seek](/Actions.aspx?ID=2301) action to find [hidden](/Conditions.aspx?ID=79) or [undetected](/Conditions.aspx?ID=96) creatures within 30 feet of them. Whenever the halfling targets a creature that is [concealed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=62) or hidden from them, reduce the DC of the flat check to 3 for a concealed target or 9 for a hidden one. **Items** chef's hat, [Filcher's Fork](/Weapons.aspx?ID=51), [Frying Pan](/Weapons.aspx?ID=286), herbs and spices --- **AC** 17 **Fort** +8 **Ref** +7 **Will** +7 **HP** 36 **Dash of Spice** **Trigger** The head chef is targeted with a melee attack by an adjacent attacker they can see; **Effect** The head chef uses Spice Mix against the attacker. --- **Speed** 25 feet **Melee** hot frying pan +9 ([fatal d8](/Traits.aspx?ID=178)), **Damage** 1d4+3 bludgeoning plus 1d4 fire **Melee** filcher's fork +9 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [Backstabber](/Traits.aspx?ID=172), [deadly d6](/Traits.aspx?ID=174)), **Damage** 1d4+3 piercing **Melee** fist +9 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [Finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=179), [Nonlethal](/Traits.aspx?ID=188), [Unarmed](/Traits.aspx?ID=199)), **Damage** 1d4+3 bludgeoning **Ranged** filcher's fork +9 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [Backstabber](/Traits.aspx?ID=172), [deadly d6](/Traits.aspx?ID=174), [thrown 20 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=195)), **Damage** 1d4+3 piercing **Angry Rant** ([Auditory](/Traits.aspx?ID=16), [Emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=60), [Linguistic](/Traits.aspx?ID=101), [Mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=106)) **Frequency** once per round; **Effect** The chef shouts a flurry of insults and criticisms at either an ally or enemy within 30 feet with the following effects:
**Ally** The chef's assistant is shaken by the barrage of criticism but is determined to work faster and harder. The target becomes [quickened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=89) for 1 round but is also [frightened 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=76). They can use the extra action to Interact, Step, or Stride, or as part of an action or activity to prepare, cook, or serve food.
**Enemy** The target must succeed a DC 18 Will save or take 1d6 mental damage and become frightened 1 (or 2d6 mental damage and frightened 2 on a critical failure). **Spice Mix** The head chef throws a mixture of irritating spices into an adjacent creature's eyes, causing the creature to be [dazzled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=65) until it Interacts to clear its vision.
name: Halfling Head Chef

Harbor seals are the most common seals found in Golarion and famous for their soft, furry bodies. They're vicious hunters underwater, but typically shy of humanoids on the surface, preferring to hide among the waves rather than face down what seems to be a terrifying land predator. **[Recall Knowledge - Animal](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43)): DC 16 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 14 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 11 [Harbor Seal](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3305) **Source** [Howl of the Wild](/Sources.aspx?ID=226) pg. 178 2.1 **Perception** +9; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59), [scent](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=74) ([imprecise](/Rules.aspx?ID=371)) 20 feet, whisker sense 30 feet **Languages** **Skills** [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=34) +6, [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) +10, [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=48) +8 **Str** +4 **Dex** +3 **Con** +3 **Int** -4 **Wis** +1 **Cha** +3 **Deep Breath** A harbor seal can hold its breath for 30 minutes.
**Whisker Sense** A harbor seal can use its whiskers to sense vibrations as a [precise sense](/Rules.aspx?ID=411) at the listed range, but only underwater. --- **AC** 17 **Fort** +9 **Ref** +11 **Will** +5 **HP** 30 --- **Speed** 15 feet, swim 30 feet **Melee** jaws +9, **Damage** 1d8+4 piercing plus [Grab](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=45) **[Aquatic Ambush](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=51)** 40 feet **Aquatic Feast** **Requirements** The harbor seal has a Medium or smaller creature [grabbed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=77) in its jaws; **Effect** The harbor seal Swims up to 10 feet, carrying its grabbed creature along with it dealing 1d8 slashing damage (DC 18 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Fortitude save).
name: Harbor Seal

<title level="1" pfs="Standard">[Herexen](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3049)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

When a cleric rebels against their deity and dies in the grip of blasphemous rage, the heresies they committed in life may fuel their transformation into an undead herexen. Herexens seek vengeance against the deity they once worshipped, defiling temples, slaying the faithful, and rallying lesser undead and death cultists to aid them in their unholy quests. Though a herexen's divine gifts have mostly been corrupted into the vileness of undeath, they stubbornly cling to remnants of their former power, still wielding magic and armaments favored by the deity they so greatly despise.

 Groups of herexens that blasphemed against the same deity sometimes combine to form a mockery of a congregation, conducting blasphemous rites with something approaching euphoria. These congregations are often formed from a blasphemous cult whose members practiced their heresy together in life and died together, though some gather independent herexens of the same former faith.

The herexen is destroyed, so it doesn't gain any Hit Points from this use of harm, and it doesn't need to have any harm spells remaining to use this ability.

features.Heretic's Smite: ([Divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=48), [Unholy](/Traits.aspx?ID=521)) While wielding the favored weapon of its former deity (such as a [dagger](/Weapons.aspx?ID=358) for an ex-[Pharasmin](/Deities.aspx?ID=290) herexen), the herexen's Strikes deal an additional 1d6 spirit damage to creatures with the [holy](/Traits.aspx?ID=517) trait.

description:
When a cleric rebels against their deity and dies in the grip of blasphemous rage, the heresies they committed in life may fuel their transformation into an undead herexen. Herexens seek vengeance against the deity they once worshipped, defiling temples, slaying the faithful, and rallying lesser undead and death cultists to aid them in their unholy quests. Though a herexen's divine gifts have mostly been corrupted into the vileness of undeath, they stubbornly cling to remnants of their former power, still wielding magic and armaments favored by the deity they so greatly despise.

 Groups of herexens that blasphemed against the same deity sometimes combine to form a mockery of a congregation, conducting blasphemous rites with something approaching euphoria. These congregations are often formed from a blasphemous cult whose members practiced their heresy together in life and died together, though some gather independent herexens of the same former faith.

<title level="1" pfs="Standard">[Hippogriff](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3052)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

With the proud bearing of a great raptor and the magnificence of a powerful horse, hippogriffs are thought to be an accidental fusion of creatures or perhaps the creation of a flesh-warping wizard with a keen aesthetic sense. Regardless of their original source, these animals are now a common sight in the skies above their favored plains or hill country.

 Hippogriffs bear the wings, forelegs, and head of a bird of prey, with feather coloration similar to that of a hawk or eagle, though some breeders have managed to produce specimens with stark white or coal-black feathers. Their torso, hindquarters, and tail resemble those of a horse and usually are colored bay, chestnut, or gray, with some coats bearing black, pinto, or even palomino coloration.

 Hippogriffs are similar in size to large horses. Much like their equine cousins, hippogriffs often have to keep wary eyes on the skies above them, as both are preferred meals for hungry griffons and wyverns. Only hippogriffs' superior speed helps protect them from these predators.

 Hippogriffs are exceptionally territorial and fiercely protect the lands under their domain. They typically favor sweeping grasslands, rolling hills, and prairies. Exceptionally hardy hippogriffs make their homes nestled into niches on canyon walls, from which they comb the rocky deserts for coyotes, deer, and the occasional humanoid. Hippogriffs prefer mammalian prey, but they graze after every meal to aid in digestion.

 Since hippogriff hunting habits can be dangerous to both ranchers and their livestock, such communities often set bounties on hippogriffs. As a result, preserved hippogriffs frequently decorate frontier taverns and remote outposts alongside the taxidermied remains of deer, elk, and bears.

 However, other communities train hippogriffs from hatching to be ridden by elite soldiers in combat—the most notable among these groups in the Inner Sea region is the Sable Company Mercenaries in the city-state of Korvosa. Attempts are sometimes made to train adult hippogriffs in the same manner, but this often proves far more difficult. Hippogriff riders must use special saddles and combat techniques that allow them to act in concert with their mount, fighting effectively while avoiding interfering with the movement of their companion's wings.

<title level="1" pfs="">[Juggler](/NPCs.aspx?ID=3572)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

Jugglers are physical performers who master the art of manipulating props. Usually, this involves throwing multiple objects up in a flowing pattern, but some use ricocheting items, spinning items, or other objects to keep them aloft.

<column gap="tiny">
**[Recall Knowledge - Humanoid](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**
([Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=47)): DC 16

**[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 14

**[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 11
</column>

</column>

<column gap="medium">
<image src="/images/Monsters/Juggler.webp" />
</column>

</row>

<title level="2" right="Creature 2">[Juggler](/NPCs.aspx?ID=3572)</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Medium" />
<trait label="Human" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=627" />
<trait label="Humanoid" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=628" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [NPC Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=236) pg. 125

**Perception** +9

**Languages**
[Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1)

**Skills**
[Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=34) +8, [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) +8, [Circus Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) +8, [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=45) +11

<row gap="medium">
**Str** +2

**Dex** +3

**Con** +1

**Int** +0

**Wis** +1

**Cha** +3
</row>

**Juggling Specialist** For encounters involving juggling and other circus acts, the juggler is a 5th-level challenge.

**Items**
juggling club (3, functions as a [light hammer](/Weapons.aspx?ID=384)), [Dart](/Weapons.aspx?ID=68) (10), [Torch](/Equipment.aspx?ID=60) (3)

</column>

---

<column gap="tiny">

<row gap="medium">
**AC** 17 

**Fort** +6 

**Ref** +11 

**Will** +7 

</row>

<row gap="medium">
**HP** 30

</row>

**Return Throw** <actions string="Reaction" /> **Trigger** A physical ranged attack with a throwing weapon critically fails to hit the juggler; **Effect** The juggler snatches the weapon from the air and immediately makes a ranged Strike against the attacker using that weapon.

</column>

---

<column gap="tiny">

**Speed** 25 feet

**Melee**
<actions string="Single Action" />
juggling club +9 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170)),
**Damage** 1d6+4 bludgeoning

**Melee**
<actions string="Single Action" />
fist +10 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [Finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=179), [Nonlethal](/Traits.aspx?ID=188), [Unarmed](/Traits.aspx?ID=199)),
**Damage** 1d4+4 bludgeoning

**Ranged**
<actions string="Single Action" />
dart +10 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [thrown 20 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=195)),
**Damage** 1d4+4 piercing

**Ranged**
<actions string="Single Action" />
juggling club +10 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [thrown 20 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=195)),
**Damage** 1d6+4 bludgeoning

**Ranged**
<actions string="Single Action" />
torch +10 ([thrown 10 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=195)),
**Damage** 1d4+4 bludgeoning plus 1 fire

**Juggle** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([Concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32), [Manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104)) The juggler begins juggling up to three items of light or negligible Bulk. They can choose items in their hands or Interact to draw items on their person or pick up unattended items in reach. While juggling, they can Interact to add up to two items to their juggle, though they must drop an item for each one they add. The juggler is wielding all items they juggle, but the only actions they can take that require their hands are Return Throw, Juggling Bounce, Strike using a juggled weapon, Interact to add items to their juggle, or Dismiss to stop juggling. When the juggler Dismisses Juggle, they can choose to continue to wield, drop, or stow each juggled item, though they can't wield more items than they have hands. If at any point the juggler isn't wielding any items or becomes [restrained](/Conditions.aspx?ID=90) or [unconscious](/Conditions.aspx?ID=95), the juggle ends and the juggler drops all the items.

**Juggling Bounce** <actions string="Single Action" />  The juggler Strikes with a thrown weapon they're juggling. If the Strike hits, the weapon bounces to a different creature in the weapon's first range increment. The juggler repeats the Strike, which uses the same multiple attack penalty and doesn't increase their multiple attack penalty.

</column>

<title level="1" pfs="Standard">[Kobold Cavern Mage](/NPCs.aspx?ID=3074)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

Kobold cavern mages are born more than trained, hatching from eggs that absorbed particularly large amounts of primal earth energy. Although there are many elementals and even natural terrain features that can give rise to cavern mages, most are related to the cavern-dwelling earth nymphs known as [lampads](/Monsters.aspx?ID=1249). These lonely and capricious fey are as enthusiastic to receive the company of a kobold tribe as the kobolds are for the protection they receive in return.

<column gap="tiny">

light hammer +6 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [thrown 20 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=195)),

- **Cantrips (1st)**
[Caustic Blast](/Spells.aspx?ID=1461), [Detect Magic](/Spells.aspx?ID=66), [Figment](/Spells.aspx?ID=1528), [Know the Way](/Spells.aspx?ID=1582), [Tangle Vine](/Spells.aspx?ID=1713)
- **1st**
[Fleet Step](/Spells.aspx?ID=122), [Heal](/Spells.aspx?ID=148), [Pummeling Rubble](/Spells.aspx?ID=708), [Runic Weapon](/Spells.aspx?ID=1658) (4 slots)

<title level="1" pfs="">[Kobold Trapper](/NPCs.aspx?ID=3654)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

Kobolds are skillful artisans, always inventing new traps and snares to defend their territory and ambush enemies. Kobold trappers enjoy showing off their crafting prowess on the battlefield.

<column gap="tiny">
**[Recall Knowledge - Humanoid](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**
([Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=47)): DC 16

**[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 14

**[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 11
</column>

</column>

<column gap="medium">
<image src="/images/Monsters/Kobold_Trapper.webp" />
</column>

</row>

<title level="2" right="Creature 2">[Kobold Trapper](/NPCs.aspx?ID=3654)</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Small" />
<trait label="Humanoid" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=628" />
<trait label="Kobold" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=759" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [NPC Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=236) pg. 198

**Perception** +7; (9 to [Seek](/Actions.aspx?ID=2301) for [traps](/Traits.aspx?ID=715)) [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59)

**Languages**
[Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1), [Sakvroth](/Languages.aspx?ID=118)

**Skills**
[Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=34) +5, [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=37) +8, [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=48) +7, [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=49) +7

<row gap="medium">
**Str** +1

**Dex** +3

**Con** +1

**Int** +3

**Wis** +2

**Cha** +0
</row>

**Booby-Trapped** A kobold trapper protects items in their backpack with a booby trap. This booby trap requires a successful DC 18 Perception check to notice, and two successful DC 15 [Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=50) checks to disable. Accessing the backpack without disabling the trap destroys its contents, and splinters explode in a 10-foot burst centered on the backpack, dealing 3d6 piercing damage (DC 15 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save).

**Items**
[Backpack](/Equipment.aspx?ID=4), [Crossbow](/Weapons.aspx?ID=67) (20 bolts), formula book (containing formulas for three 1st- or 2nd-level [snares](/Traits.aspx?ID=809)), [Leather Armor](/Armor.aspx?ID=4), [Light Hammer](/Weapons.aspx?ID=384)

</column>

---

<column gap="tiny">

<row gap="medium">
**AC** 18 

**Fort** +5 

**Ref** +11 

**Will** +8 

+1 circumstance to all defenses vs. [traps](/Traits.aspx?ID=715)
</row>

<row gap="medium">
**HP** 32

</row>

</column>

---

<column gap="tiny">

**Speed** 25 feet

**Melee**
<actions string="Single Action" />
light hammer +7 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170)),
**Damage** 1d6+1 bludgeoning

**Melee**
<actions string="Single Action" />
claw +7 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [Unarmed](/Traits.aspx?ID=199)),
**Damage** 1d4+1 slashing

**Ranged**
<actions string="Single Action" />
crossbow +9 ([range increment 120 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=248), [reload 1](/Traits.aspx?ID=254)),
**Damage** 1d8 piercing

**Ranged**
<actions string="Single Action" />
light hammer +9 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [thrown 20 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=195)),
**Damage** 1d6+1 bludgeoning

**Construct Trap** <actions string="Three Actions" /> ([Manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104)) The kobold trapper creates a rudimentary trap on a surface in an adjacent square. The trap activates the next time a creature moves adjacent to it. The creature takes 2d6 bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing damage (determined by the trapper when the trap is constructed) with a DC 18 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save. On a failure, the creature also takes a –5 status penalty to all Speeds for 1 minute. The trap is destroyed when activated or after 8 hours, whichever comes first. A trapper typically carries enough raw materials to make six traps each day.

</column>

The tradition of astrology and looking to the stars for both navigation and prognostication is well-established in iruxi society, and their wise and observant stargazers are among the people's most respected members. markdown:
As the least of their kind, meokdans suffer a constant and painful hunger, for they lack the ability of more powerful nindorus to derive nourishment from a reincarnated soul. This hunger drives the meokdan to constantly seek food and often compels them to eat dirt, stones, and refuse that offer little (if any) nutritional value. Regardless of how much they eat, a meokdan always remains painfully thin in stature. Regardless of how hungry they get, they never starve to death. A meokdan's emaciated frame appears human in shape, with thick, tangled hair that grows directly from their face as well as the rest of their head, leaving only the meokdan's gaping mouth visible. Their arms appear to be broken and unnaturally long, with equally long fingers tipped with ragged nails. Small, open sores pockmark their skin. Meokdans epitomize the cycle of food, from consumption to the creature themselves being consumed in the end, be it by predators or the environment growing from their remains. **[Recall Knowledge - Fiend](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=13)): DC 16 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 14 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 11 [Meokdan](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2755) **Source** [Pathfinder #197: Let the Leaves Fall](/Sources.aspx?ID=222) pg. 84 **Perception** +9; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=12) **Languages** [Aklo](/Languages.aspx?ID=13), [Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1), [Necril](/Languages.aspx?ID=20) **Skills** [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) +8, [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5) +7, [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=7) +7, [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=11) +6 **Str** +4 **Dex** +3 **Con** +1 **Int** +0 **Wis** +3 **Cha** +3 **Items** [bone morningstar](/Weapons.aspx?ID=8) --- **AC** 17 **Fort** +5 **Ref** +9 **Will** +9 **HP** 32 **Immunities** death effects, fatigued (from the effects of starvation or thirst), sickened **Resistances** negative 5 **Weaknesses** silver 5 **Soul Shred** Creatures killed by a meokdan are difficult to bring back to life or animate as undead. The meokdan automatically attempts to [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) any attempt to resurrect or animate any creature that it has killed (counteract modifier +7, counteract level 2). If the meokdan who slew the creature is itself slain, the creature can be brought back from death or become undead normally.
 --- **Speed** 25 feet **Melee** bone club +10, **Damage** 1d6+6 bludgeoning **Melee** shattered bone club +10, **Damage** 1d4+6 slashing plus 1 bleed **Melee** bite +10 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170)), **Damage** 1d4+6 piercing **Occult Innate Spells** DC 18, attack +10 - **Cantrips (1st)** [Telekinetic Projectile](/Spells.aspx?ID=334) - **1st** [Illusory Disguise](/Spells.aspx?ID=159), [Phantom Pain](/Spells.aspx?ID=220) - **2nd** [Item Facade](/Spells.aspx?ID=166) **Manifest Bone Club** ([[concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)](/Traits.aspx?ID=32), [[conjuration](/Traits.aspx?ID=33)](/Traits.aspx?ID=33), [[occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=662)](/Traits.aspx?ID=120)) **Requirement** The meokdan isn't carrying a bone club; **Effect** The meokdan reaches down its throat into its stomach and pulls out a human femur that it can wield as a bone club. After the meokdan Strikes a creature, the bone club shatters, but its sharp fragments remain in roughly the same shape; Strikes with a shattered bone club inflict slashing and bleed damage. After the meokdan Strikes with a shattered bone club, or if the meokdan drops the bone club, the club is destroyed, and the nindoru can Manifest a new bone club. **Quick Snack** **Trigger** The meokdan critically hits a living creature with its bite; **Effect** The meokdan Snacks on the creature. **Snack** The meokdan attempts a bite Strike against an adjacent creature or chews on a handheld object they're carrying. If the creature is living or the object is food, the meokdan gurgles in delight and restores 1d8+8 Hit Points. If the creature is undead or a construct, or the object is inedible, the meokdan shrieks in frustration and gains a +1 status bonus to attack rolls and saving throws until the end of its next turn. The meokdan can't Snack again for 1 round.
