The misleadings, half-facts, and effortless spin propagandists cast over events create proof of whatever their bosses need them to prove. **[Recall Knowledge - Humanoid](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=47)): DC 18 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 16 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 13 [Propagandist](/NPCs.aspx?ID=3610) **Source** [NPC Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=236) pg. 154 **Perception** +10; (12 to [Sense Motive](/Actions.aspx?ID=2302)) **Languages** [Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1) **Skills** [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39) +11, [Legal Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) +8, [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=45) +10, [Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=47) +10 **Str** +0 **Dex** +2 **Con** +1 **Int** +1 **Wis** +3 **Cha** +4 **Nuanced Spin** The propagandist phrases everything loosely and vaguely enough that, though it's always misleading, none of it is false. The propagandist can use [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39) instead of [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38) to [Create a Diversion](/Actions.aspx?ID=2387) or [Feint](/Actions.aspx?ID=2390), and instead of [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=40) to [Coerce](/Actions.aspx?ID=2394). A creature attempting to [Sense Motive](/Actions.aspx?ID=2302) against the propagandist gets a result one degree of success worse than they rolled. **Items** [Dagger](/Weapons.aspx?ID=3) (3), [lute](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2737), [Shortsword](/Weapons.aspx?ID=43), [Writing Set](/Equipment.aspx?ID=63) --- **AC** 17 **Fort** +6 **Ref** +9 **Will** +12 **HP** 40 --- **Speed** 25 feet **Melee** shortsword +9 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [Finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=179), [versatile S](/Traits.aspx?ID=200)), **Damage** 1d6+4 piercing **Melee** dagger +9 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [Finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=179), [versatile S](/Traits.aspx?ID=200)), **Damage** 1d4+4 piercing **Melee** fist +9 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [Finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=179), [Nonlethal](/Traits.aspx?ID=188), [Unarmed](/Traits.aspx?ID=199)), **Damage** 1d4+4 bludgeoning **Ranged** dagger +9 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [thrown 10 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=195), [versatile S](/Traits.aspx?ID=200)), **Damage** 1d4+4 piercing **Occult Spontaneous Spells** DC 21, attack +13 - **Cantrips (2nd)** [Bullhorn](/Spells.aspx?ID=877), [Detect Magic](/Spells.aspx?ID=66), [Haunting Hymn](/Spells.aspx?ID=924), [Message](/Spells.aspx?ID=190), [Summon Instrument](/Spells.aspx?ID=721) - **1st** [Concordant Choir](/Spells.aspx?ID=886), [Fear](/Spells.aspx?ID=110), [Sanctuary](/Spells.aspx?ID=266) (3 slots) - **2nd** [Blistering Invective](/Spells.aspx?ID=674), [Paranoia](/Spells.aspx?ID=214) (2 slots) **Bard Composition Spells** DC 21, 2 Focus Points - **Cantrips (2nd)** [Courageous Anthem](/Spells.aspx?ID=1763), [Rallying Anthem](/Spells.aspx?ID=1773) - **2nd** [Hymn of Healing](/Spells.aspx?ID=728), [Lingering Composition](/Spells.aspx?ID=389) **No Hard Feelings** ([Auditory](/Traits.aspx?ID=16), [Concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32), [emotional](/Traits.aspx?ID=60), [Linguistic](/Traits.aspx?ID=101), [Mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=106)) The propagandist offers amnesty and other benefits to all who choose to join them. All enemies who can hear the propagandist must attempt a DC 19 Will save. If any of the propagandist's allies is currently benefiting from one of the propagandist's bard composition spells, any enemy who is aware of that takes a –2 circumstance penalty to the save.
**Critical Success** The creature sees through the propagandist's pitch and is temporarily immune for 24 hours.
**Success** The creature is unaffected.
**Failure** The creature's conviction stumbles. Until the end of its next turn, the creature must succeed at a DC 5 flat check to target the propagandist with a [hostile action](/Rules.aspx?ID=300).
**Critical Failure** The creature finds the propagandist's offer too good to pass up, switching sides in the combat and instantly gaining any benefits the propagandist is currently granting their allies. At the end of each of its turns, the creature can attempt another DC 19 Will save to snap out of it and rejoin their allies.

<title level="1" pfs="">[Rift Chameleon](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3271)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

Rift chameleons are best known for their unsettling ability to swallow creatures significantly larger than themselves, thanks to a digestive tract that connects to its own pocket of the [Ethereal Plane](/Planes.aspx?ID=34). When two or more rift chameleons remain in proximity for extended periods of time, their partially extradimensional nature begins to subtly warp the surrounding terrain. Direction and distance become confused to all but the lizards, making it easy for locals to get lost in places they once thought familiar.

<column gap="tiny">
**[Recall Knowledge - Beast](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**
([Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35), [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43)): DC 20

**[Recall Knowledge - Ethereal](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**
([Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=44)): DC 20

**[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 18

**[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 15
</column>

</column>

<column gap="medium">
<image src="/images/Monsters/Rift_Chameleon.webp" />
</column>

</row>

<title level="2" right="Creature 3">[Rift Chameleon](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3271)</title>

<trait label="Ethereal" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=593" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Howl of the Wild](/Sources.aspx?ID=226) pg. 146 <sup>2.1</sup>

**Perception** +9; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59), [scent](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=74) ([imprecise](/Rules.aspx?ID=412)) 30 feet

**Languages**
[Aklo](/Languages.aspx?ID=13); can't speak any language

**Skills**
[Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) +9, [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=48) +10, [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=49) +8

<row gap="medium">
**Str** +4

**Dex** +2

**Con** +3

**Int** -2

**Wis** +1

**Cha** +3
</row>

**Ethereal Camouflage** A rift chameleon can [Hide](/Actions.aspx?ID=2404), even if it doesn't have [cover](/Rules.aspx?ID=2372), but it cannot be [concealed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=62) from creatures on the [Ethereal Plane](/Planes.aspx?ID=34).

</column>

---

<column gap="tiny">

<row gap="medium">
**AC** 19 [all-around vision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=49)

**Ref** +9 

**Will** +8 

</row>

<row gap="medium">

</row>

</column>

---

<column gap="tiny">

**Speed** 25 feet, climb 20 feet

**Melee**
<actions string="Single Action" />
jaws +11,
**Damage** 1d10+4 piercing plus [Grab](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=45)

**Melee**
<actions string="Single Action" />
tail +11 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170)),
**Damage** 1d8+4 bludgeoning

**Melee**
<actions string="Single Action" />
tongue +11 ([reach 10 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)),
**Damage** tongue pull

**Extradimensional Gullet**  ([Extradimensional](/Traits.aspx?ID=67)) The rift chameleon's innards exist partially on the [Ethereal Plane](/Planes.aspx?ID=34), allowing it to swallow any number of creatures, even ones larger than itself. <title level="1" pfs="Standard">[River Drake](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2958)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

Although the glistening scales and sleek, fin-like wings on these drakes give them an appearance reminiscent of river fish, they are actually distant relatives of the dragons that rule the oceans. While smaller than most drakes, river drakes are more than capable of plaguing river travelers and are equally at home above and below the water's surface. This flexibility allows them to catch a wide variety of prey, from fish and boggards to deer and the occasional ferry passenger.

<column gap="tiny">

([Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35)): DC 18

</column>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

[acid](/Traits.aspx?ID=524) 10

fangs +12,

**Caustic Mucus** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([Acid](/Traits.aspx?ID=3), [Primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=134)) The river drake spits a ball of caustic mucus up to a range of 50 feet that explodes in a 10-foot burst. Creatures within the burst take 4d6 acid damage (DC 19 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save). Those that fail this save also take 1d6 [persistent acid damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29) and take a –5-foot status penalty to their Speed. This Speed reduction ends with the persistent acid damage. The river drake can't use Caustic Mucus again for 1d6 rounds.

Couatls are large, brightly colored serpents with feathered wings. Good-natured, these creatures aid mortals and oppose evildoers, but sighting one presents a momentous occasion—these magnificent, albeit reclusive creatures rarely appear. The smallest members of the couatl family, Scalliwings resemble their larger kin but are roughly the size of a house cat, and a irascible mischievous streak tempers their kindly nature. While most couatls seek to right the world's wrongs or guide mortal civilization toward societal advancement, scalliwings work on a more individual level. They claim their role is to teach goodhearted spellcasters the ways of magic, and indeed they sometimes serve—or “assist,” as they're swift to correct—such spellcasters as familiars. Sea hags specialize in transformation magic, preying on those who are desperate to change some aspect of their physical appearance. Targets often include those suffering from insecurity about their bodies or those desperate to reside in a different environment, such as aquatic creatures who wish to live on land. These hags are known for tempting desperate victims into tragic and excruciating bargains, though they're also happy to drown and eat mariners who stray too close to their dwellings. A sea hag has the upper half of a humanoid and the lower half of an octopus, with translucent skin and glowing lights visible beneath their flesh. Sea hags can join covens, but their aquatic nature often prevents them from joining mixed covens with other kinds of hags. **[Recall Knowledge - Humanoid](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=47)): DC 18 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 16 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 13 [Sea Hag](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3040) **Source** [Monster Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=221) pg. 188 1.1 **Perception** +10; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59) **Languages** [Aklo](/Languages.aspx?ID=13), [Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1), [Fey](/Languages.aspx?ID=119), [Jotun](/Languages.aspx?ID=8), [Thalassic](/Languages.aspx?ID=113) **Skills** [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=1) +8, [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) +11, [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5) +10, [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=11) +8, [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15) +8 **Str** +4 **Dex** +3 **Con** +4 **Int** +1 **Wis** +3 **Cha** +3 **[Coven](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=58)** A sea hag adds [_humanoid form_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1560), [_mariner's curse_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1593), and [_water walk_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1756) to their coven's spells. Their spell DC when leading a coven is 20. --- **AC** 19 **Fort** +11 **Ref** +8 **Will** +10 +1 status to all saves vs. [magic](/Traits.aspx?ID=644) **HP** 45 **Immunities** [polymorph](/Traits.aspx?ID=670) **Weaknesses** [cold iron](/Equipment.aspx?ID=375) 3 --- **Speed** 25 feet, swim 35 feet **Melee** claw +12 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103)), **Damage** 1d10+4 slashing **Dread Gaze** ([Curse](/Traits.aspx?ID=38), [Emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=60), [Fear](/Traits.aspx?ID=68), [Mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=106), [Occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=120)) The hag gazes upon a creature, afflicting it with a gnawing sense of impending doom, with a result depending on its Will save (DC 20). The target doesn't need to be able to see the sea hag.
**Critical Success** The creature is unaffected.
**Success** The creature is [frightened 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=76).
**Failure** The creature is frightened 1 and is [slowed 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=92) for 1 round. If the target was [dying](/Conditions.aspx?ID=69), it remains [unconscious](/Conditions.aspx?ID=95) for 1 day. At the end of the day, it must attempt a Fortitude save against the same DC; if it fails, it dies.
**Critical Failure** As failure, but the creature is frightened 2 and slowed 1 for 1 minute. **Sea Hag's Bargain** ([Concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32), [Exploration](/Traits.aspx?ID=66), [Occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=120), [Polymorph](/Traits.aspx?ID=127)) The sea hag can make a bargain with a willing creature who must be of sound mind. The creature gives away a special or cherished quality—such as its courage, its beauty, or its voice. In exchange, the sea hag spends 1 minute polymorphing the creature into a form the target desires.
This functions as [Change Shape](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=55). It might be a total transformation or just changing one or more aspects of the target's body, and it can't make the creature more than one size smaller or larger. The creature changes its Speeds as appropriate for the new form. It doesn't change the attack and damage bonuses with its Strikes, but it might change the damage type the Strikes deal. This has an unlimited duration, and as long as it's transformed, the creature is [sickened 2](/Conditions.aspx?ID=91) and can't reduce its sickened condition below 2. The creature can slowly and carefully eat and drink despite being sickened. The only way to restore the lost quality used as payment is to defeat the sea hag or make another bargain for its return. Ending the bargain in this way also removes the transformation.

Sibyls are oracular diviners who often fall deep into trances with their oracular curses to spur a frenzied mental state. These creatures resemble chubby bats covered in small overlapping metal plates. They can't exhale enough petrifying gas to paralyze a normal-sized humanoid, but it's effective on their usual prey of insects and other small animals, which they petrify before consuming. However, stony bats have learned how to use their petrification gas to defend themselves against larger creatures, freezing a limb or raining down pebbles of petrified water vapor. Further, they can work together to bring down larger creatures, petrifying and consuming them limb by limb. Stony bats generally live in caves in large groups, though they frequently fly out in small numbers for hunting. They typically aren't aggressive against non-prey they encounter outside, though they're very protective of their caves. [Oread](/Ancestries.aspx?ID=34) and others who don't fear petrification sometimes keep stony bats as pets. **[Recall Knowledge - Beast](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35), [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43)): DC 20 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 18 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 15 [Stony Bat](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3285) **Source** [Howl of the Wild](/Sources.aspx?ID=226) pg. 154 2.1 **Perception** +11; echolocation ([precise](/Rules.aspx?ID=411)) 30 ft **Languages** **Skills** [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=34) +11, [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=48) +11 **Str** +2 **Dex** +4 **Con** +2 **Int** -3 **Wis** +2 **Cha** +1 **Echolocation** The stony bat can use hearing as a [precise sense](/Rules.aspx?ID=411) with the listed range. --- **AC** 18 **Fort** +9 **Ref** +11 **Will** +7 **HP** 48 **Immunities** [petrification](/Conditions.aspx?ID=87) --- **Speed** 15 feet, fly 30 feet **Melee** jaws +11 ([Finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=179)), **Damage** 2d8+2 piercing plus stone feast **Petrify Vapor** ([Earth](/Traits.aspx?ID=55), [Primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=134)) The stony bat breathes petrifying gas in a 15-foot cone, too thin to harm creatures in the area. However, it petrifies ambient moisture, raining down a cascade of tiny stones onto any creatures in the space directly below the cone. The falling rocks deal 4d6 bludgeoning damage (DC 20 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save). The stony bat can't use Petrify Vapor again for 1d4 rounds. **Petrify Body Part** ([Earth](/Traits.aspx?ID=55), [Primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=134)) The stony bat breathes a puff of petrifying gas onto an adjacent creature, targeting a specific body part. The target must succeed at a DC 20 Fortitude save or be partially petrified for 1 minute, with an effect varying with the body part targeted.
  • **Face** The creature's face stiffens and a film of stone partially blocks its vision. It is [dazzled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=65).
  • **Hand** One of the creature's hands is petrified. It cannot [Release](/Actions.aspx?ID=2300) items from that hand or use the hand for fine manipulation. Attack rolls with weapons held in that hand take a –2 status penalty.
  • **Leg** A patch of the creature's leg becomes inflexible and heavy. It takes a –10 status penalty to its Speed. If all of the creature's legs become petrified in this way, the creature's Speed is reduced down to 5 feet. At the GM's discretion, a creature with movement that doesn't rely on legs, such as creatures that [Fly](/Actions.aspx?ID=2312) with wings, don't take a penalty to these other Speeds.
**Stone Feast** The stony bat specifically targets petrified body parts, which it can consume, unlike flesh. The stony bat's jaws deal an extra 1d6 damage against a creature that has been [petrified](/Conditions.aspx?ID=87), either partially or completely, and ignore the Hardness of petrified creatures.

<title level="1" pfs="Standard">[String Slime](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3126)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

Found underground or in dungeons, these quivering, slug-like ropes of slime continuously scour their domain for food. In addition to their shape, they are named for their ability to shoot out expanding ribbons of slime that resemble tangled strings.

<column gap="tiny">

**Weak Acid**   A string slime's acid damages only organic material—not metal, stone, or other inorganic substances.

<title level="1" pfs="">[Swarm Voice](/NPCs.aspx?ID=3668)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

The swarm voice is the secular leader of a ysoki warren or one family in a larger warren. If there is a dispute, the swarm voice resolves it. If there is a negotiation, they orchestrate it. If war is about to break out, they declare it. The swarm voice is the welcoming hand and the iron fist of their colony.

<column gap="tiny">
**[Recall Knowledge - Humanoid](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**
([Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=47)): DC 18

**[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 16

**[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 13
</column>

</column>

<column gap="medium">
<image src="/images/Monsters/Swarm_Voice.webp" />
</column>

</row>

<title level="2" right="Creature 3">[Swarm Voice](/NPCs.aspx?ID=3668)</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Small" />
<trait label="Humanoid" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=628" />
<trait label="Ratfolk" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=769" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [NPC Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=236) pg. 210

**Perception** +9; (18 to [Sense Motive](/Actions.aspx?ID=2302)) low-light vision

**Languages**
[Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1), [Ysoki](/Languages.aspx?ID=61)

**Skills**
[Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=34) +8, [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) +9, [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39) +17, [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=40) +15, [Legal Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) +16, [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=45) +15, [Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=47) +16, [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=49) +10

<row gap="medium">
**Str** +2

**Dex** +1

**Con** +0

**Int** +3

**Wis** +3

**Cha** +4
</row>

**Voice of the Swarm** For encounters involving negotiation or diplomacy, the swarm voice is a 7th-level challenge.

**Items**
[lesser acid flask](/Equipment.aspx?ID=74) (4), [Crossbow](/Weapons.aspx?ID=67) (20 bolts), [Longspear](/Weapons.aspx?ID=6)

</column>

---

<column gap="tiny">

<row gap="medium">
**AC** 18 

**Fort** +7 

**Ref** +8 

**Will** +11 

</row>

<row gap="medium">
**HP** 45

</row>

</column>

---

<column gap="tiny">

**Speed** 25 feet; swarming

**Melee**
<actions string="Single Action" />
longspear +11 ([Reach](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)),
**Damage** 1d8+5 piercing

**Melee**
<actions string="Single Action" />
jaws +11 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170)),
**Damage** 1d4+5 piercing

**Ranged**
<actions string="Single Action" />
alchemical bomb +10 ([range increment 20 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=248), [Splash](/Traits.aspx?ID=150)),
**Damage** 1d6 [persistent acid](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29) plus 1 acid [splash](/Traits.aspx?ID=699) damage

**Ranged**
<actions string="Single Action" />
crossbow +10 ([range increment 120 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=248), [reload 1](/Traits.aspx?ID=254)),
**Damage** 1d8+3 piercing

**Advise Swarm** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([Auditory](/Traits.aspx?ID=16), [Linguistic](/Traits.aspx?ID=101), [Mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=106)) The swarm voice issues orders to move. Each ratfolk from the same warren in a 15-foot emanation can spend a reaction to Step, Stride, or [Take Cover](/Actions.aspx?ID=2307).

**Chittering Terror** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([Auditory](/Traits.aspx?ID=16), [Emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=60), [Fear](/Traits.aspx?ID=68), [Mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=106)) The swarm voice chitters, creating a terrifying din, and encourages their allies to join in. Each enemy within 30 feet must succeed at a DC 19 Will save or be [frightened 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=76) (or frightened 2 on a critical failure). An enemy takes a –2 circumstance penalty to its save if it's adjacent to one or more [ratfolk](/Traits.aspx?ID=769) allied with the swarm voice. Regardless of the result of a creature's save, it's then temporarily immune for 1 hour.

**Swarming**   A ysoki can end their movement in the same square as an ally that also has this ability. Only two such creatures can share the same space.

</column>

A mob of tooth fairies working together can conduct forced dentistry in seconds. **[Recall Knowledge - Fey](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43)): DC 18 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 16 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 13 [Tooth Fairy Swarm](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3217) **Source** [Monster Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=221) pg. 327 1.1 **Perception** +8; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59) **Languages** **Skills** [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=1) +10, [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15) +10, [Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=17) +12 **Str** -2 **Dex** +3 **Con** +0 **Int** -1 **Wis** +2 **Cha** +2 --- **AC** 18 **Fort** +5 **Ref** +10 **Will** +7 **HP** 28 **Immunities** [grabbed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=77), precision, [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=88), [restrained](/Conditions.aspx?ID=90), [swarm mind](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=78) **Resistances** bludgeoning 2, piercing 5, slashing 5 **Weaknesses** area damage 5, [cold iron](/Equipment.aspx?ID=375) 5, [splash](/Traits.aspx?ID=699) damage 5 **Plaque Burst** When killed, a tooth fairy bursts into sticky, foul-smelling white dust. Each creature in a 15-foot emanation must succeed at a DC 20 Fortitude save or become [sickened 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=91) (sickened 2 on a critical failure). --- **Speed** 10 feet, fly 40 feet **Pinch** Tooth fairies pinch their victims' fingers, noses, ears, or similar protruding body parts. Each enemy in the swarm's space takes 2d6 bludgeoning damage (DC 20 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save). Creatures that critically fail this save are [sickened 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=91) from the pain. **Pry** The tooth fairies try to pry out one of their target's teeth. One enemy in the swarm's space takes 4d6 bludgeoning damage with a DC 20 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save. On a failed save, the target takes 2 [persistent bleed damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29) and loses a tooth.
If the creature loses a tooth, it takes a –1 status penalty to Charisma-based skill checks and must succeed at a DC 5 flat check to Cast a Spell unless that spell has the [subtle](/Traits.aspx?ID=522) trait. These effects last for 1 day, or until the stolen tooth is returned and the target regains at least 1 Hit Point.
name: Tooth Fairy Swarm

<title level="1" pfs="">[Toymaker](/NPCs.aspx?ID=3460)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

The whimsy of a toymaker is only matched by their ruthlessness when cornered. Most of their creations are designed solely for the enjoyment of others. However, every toymaker knows—whether through failed designs or intentional creations—how to turn their toys into dangerous weapons. They are often hesitant to use toys in such ways, and more often than not, they will attempt to solve problems with diplomacy first.

 Some toymakers have fully turned to the profession of making deadly toys. They often have dangerous patrons or nefarious intentions. Some use dangerous toys as a means of vigilantism, while others use them as a means to sneak weapons into guarded areas.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

</column>

<column gap="tiny">

<row gap="medium">

**Will** +10 

</row>

</row>

</column>

---

<column gap="tiny">

**Speed** 25 feet

**Melee**
<actions string="Single Action" />
fist +10 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [Finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=179), [Nonlethal](/Traits.aspx?ID=188), [Unarmed](/Traits.aspx?ID=199)),
**Damage** 1d4+4 bludgeoning

**Ranged**
<actions string="Single Action" />
hand crossbow +12 ([Nonlethal](/Traits.aspx?ID=188), [range increment 60 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=248), [reload 1](/Traits.aspx?ID=254)),
**Damage** 1d6+5 bludgeoning plus punchout bolts

**Punchout Bolts**   The toymaker's crossbow bolts are specially constructed with heavy, sap-like heads instead of piercing tips. Strikes with these bolts deal bludgeoning damage instead of piercing and have the [nonlethal](/Traits.aspx?ID=661) trait. In addition, a creature hit by one must succeed a DC 20 Fortitude saving throw or be [pushed](/Rules.aspx?ID=451) 10 feet back (or 20 feet on a critical failure).

**Scatter Blocks** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([Manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104)) The toymaker throws out a handful of toy building blocks of various sizes 20 feet away in a 5-foot burst. The area becomes [difficult terrain](/Rules.aspx?ID=453) and [hazardous terrain](/Rules.aspx?ID=454). A creature that moves on the ground through the area takes 1 piercing damage for every square of that area it moves into.

**Wind-Up Soldier** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([Manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104)) The toymaker releases a wind-up soldier that Strides 15 feet in a straight line. Whenever the soldier moves adjacent to a creature or a creature moves into a space adjacent to the soldier, the creature takes 2d8 slashing damage with a DC 20 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save as the soldier wildly slashes its sword. A creature can take damage from the wind-up soldier only once per round. At the start of each of the toymaker's turns, the solder Strides 15 feet further along the same path. The soldier falls apart after it moves three times.

</column>

An untrained eye might spot a sign or two of a wild creature's passing, but only a skilled tracker can identify several such signs and discern their relationship to each other, connecting one to the next until they form a trail of prints, scat, fur, feathers, and blood that leads to the quarry's lair. **[Recall Knowledge - Humanoid](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=47)): DC 18 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 16 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 13 [Tracker](/NPCs.aspx?ID=3471) **Source** [NPC Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=236) pg. 54 **Perception** +12 **Languages** [Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1) **Skills** [Forest Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) +5, [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43) +11, [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=48) +9, [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=49) +13 **Str** +2 **Dex** +4 **Con** +2 **Int** +0 **Wis** +4 **Cha** +0 **Expert Subsistence** While using [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=49) to [Subsist](/Actions.aspx?ID=2368), if the tracker rolls any result worse than a success, they get a success. On a success, they can provide subsistence living for themselves and eight additional creatures, and on a critical success, they can take care of twice as many creatures as on a success.
**Master Tracker** The tracker can [Track](/Actions.aspx?ID=2408) while moving at full speed. **Items** [Composite Longbow](/Weapons.aspx?ID=74) (60 arrows), [Dagger](/Weapons.aspx?ID=3), [Leather Armor](/Armor.aspx?ID=4) --- **AC** 19 **Fort** +7 **Ref** +11 **Will** +9 **HP** 40 --- **Speed** 25 feet **Melee** dagger +11 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [Finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=179), [versatile S](/Traits.aspx?ID=200)), **Damage** 1d4+6 piercing **Melee** fist +11 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [Finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=179), [Nonlethal](/Traits.aspx?ID=188), [Unarmed](/Traits.aspx?ID=199)), **Damage** 1d4+6 bludgeoning **Ranged** dagger +11 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [thrown 10 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=195), [versatile S](/Traits.aspx?ID=200)), **Damage** 1d4+6 piercing **Ranged** composite longbow +11 ([deadly 1d10](/Traits.aspx?ID=174), [Propulsive](/Traits.aspx?ID=191), [range increment 100 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=248), [reload 0](/Traits.aspx?ID=254), [volley 30 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=201)), **Damage** 1d8+5 piercing **On the Hunt** ([Concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32)) The tracker designates one creature they're observing or tracking as their prey. The tracker gains a +2 circumstance bonus to Perception checks to [Seek](/Actions.aspx?ID=2301) the prey and to [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=49) checks to [Track](/Actions.aspx?ID=2408) the prey. The first time the tracker hits the designated prey in a round, they deal an additional 1d4 precision damage. These effects last until the tracker uses On the Hunt again.

The life of a traveling actor is, contrary to belief, not one of glamor but effort. To be on the road going from town to town wearing a thousand faces invites little reward, save the adoration of the crowd. Even so, this is where they thrive. Actors typically travel in troupes, composed not only of other actors but also of stagehands, drivers, and assorted hangers-on. All of them fall under the thumb of a singular director, acting as both parent and manager to all within the troupe. **[Recall Knowledge - Humanoid](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=47)): DC 18 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 16 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 13 [Traveling Actor](/NPCs.aspx?ID=3574) **Source** [NPC Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=236) pg. 127 **Perception** +12 **Languages** [Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1); up to 4 other languages **Skills** [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=34) +7, [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) +7, [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38) +10, [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=45) +10, [Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=47) +9, [Theater Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) +9 **Str** +2 **Dex** +3 **Con** +0 **Int** +1 **Wis** +1 **Cha** +4 **Items** [Padded Armor](/Armor.aspx?ID=3), wooden sword (functions as a [light mace](/Weapons.aspx?ID=360)) --- **AC** 18 **Fort** +6 **Ref** +12 **Will** +9 **HP** 35 **Dramatic Death** **Trigger** The traveling actor takes any damage; **Effect** The traveling actor falls [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=88) and dramatically announces their death. They appear to have died. Anyone who is suspicious of this “death” can [Seek](/Actions.aspx?ID=2301) to attempt a [secret](/Traits.aspx?ID=690) Perception check against the traveling actor's [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=45) DC. On a success, they see through the ruse.
**Versatile Performance** The traveling actor can use [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=45) instead of [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39) to [Make an Impression](/Actions.aspx?ID=2392) and instead of [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=40) to [Demoralize](/Actions.aspx?ID=2395). --- **Speed** 25 feet **Melee** wooden sword +12 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [Finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=179), [Shove](/Traits.aspx?ID=193)), **Damage** 1d4+6 bludgeoning **Melee** fist +12 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [Finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=179), [Nonlethal](/Traits.aspx?ID=188), [Unarmed](/Traits.aspx?ID=199)), **Damage** 1d4+6 bludgeoning **Overacted Strike** ([Emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=60), [Fear](/Traits.aspx?ID=68), [Mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=106), [Visual](/Traits.aspx?ID=163)) The traveling actor puts all their expertise into an attack that strikes fear in those who witness it. The traveling actor Strikes. On a success, the traveling actor chooses another creature within 30 feet who can see the attack, who becomes [frightened 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=76) (or frightened 2 on a critical success).
name: Traveling Actor

A tumbleweed leshy's ability to move quickly across long distances with ease allows them to act as messengers and go-betweens. [Druids](/Classes.aspx?ID=6) often entrust these couriers with delivering important messages to their home druid circles or other druids they're acquainted with. Some even induct the couriers into the circle to teach them [Wildsong](/Languages.aspx?ID=116) for secure communication and basic magic for self-defense. **[Recall Knowledge - Plant](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43)): DC 18 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 16 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 13 [Tumbleweed Leshy Courier](/NPCs.aspx?ID=3657) **Source** [NPC Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=236) pg. 200 **Perception** +12; [low-light vision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=69) **Languages** [Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1), [Fey](/Languages.aspx?ID=119); [_speak with plants_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1681) (tumbleweeds and scrubland brush only) **Skills** [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=34) +11, [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39) +8, [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43) +10, [Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=47) +7, [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=48) +9, [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=49) +10 **Str** +1 **Dex** +4 **Con** +1 **Int** +0 **Wis** +2 **Cha** +2 **Tumbling Traveler** The tumbleweed leshy courier gains a +10-foot circumstance bonus to Speed while traveling during exploration mode. **Items** [Crossbow](/Weapons.aspx?ID=67) (20 bolts), [Dagger](/Weapons.aspx?ID=3) --- **AC** 19 **Fort** +6 **Ref** +12 **Will** +9 **HP** 35 **Spiny Burst** ([healing](/Traits.aspx?ID=623), [primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=676), [vitality](/Traits.aspx?ID=509)) When the tumbleweed leshy courier dies, a burst of primal energy explodes from their body, restoring 2d8 Hit Points to each plant creature in a 30-foot emanation. This area immediately fills with brambles and thistles, becoming [difficult terrain](/Rules.aspx?ID=453). Any creature that moves through the area takes 1 piercing damage per square traversed. If the terrain is not a viable environment for these plants, they wither after 24 hours.
**Nimble Dodge** **Trigger** The tumbleweed leshy courier is targeted with an attack by an attacker they can see; **Effect** The leshy gains a +2 circumstance bonus to AC against the triggering attack. --- **Speed** 30 feet **Melee** dagger +11 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [Finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=179), [versatile S](/Traits.aspx?ID=200)), **Damage** 1d4+5 piercing **Melee** fist +11 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [Finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=179), [Nonlethal](/Traits.aspx?ID=188), [Unarmed](/Traits.aspx?ID=199)), **Damage** 1d4+5 bludgeoning **Ranged** crossbow +12 ([range increment 120 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=248), [reload 1](/Traits.aspx?ID=254)), **Damage** 1d8+2 piercing **Primal Innate Spells** DC 17 - **Constant (3rd)** [Speak with Plants](/Spells.aspx?ID=294) (tumbleweeds and scrubland brush only) **[Change Shape](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=55)** ([Concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32), [Polymorph](/Traits.aspx?ID=127), [Primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=134)) The tumbleweed leshy courier transforms into a Small tumbleweed. This ability otherwise uses the effects of [_one with plants_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1618). Additionally, when the leshy uses their Change Shape ability, they still have a Speed of 10 feet for the purpose of travel during exploration mode.

<title level="1" pfs="Standard">[Unicorn](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3223)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

Symbols of grace and purity, unicorns resemble proud and noble horses. They typically have pure white coats, but they are best known for the single, delicate horn that extends from the center of their forehead. While unicorns often serve as protectors of unspoiled wilderness and sacred places, they are themselves highly sought after for their horns, which are said to possess potent magical properties. To many, the mere idea of hunting such a magnificent creature in the hopes of severing its horn is utterly reprehensible. Indeed, a dehorned unicorn is a sorry sight, and few such unicorns survive much longer in the wild.

 Unicorns are found almost exclusively in remote, unsullied areas of wilderness. Sometimes associated with good-aligned deities, other times associated with nature and the fey, unicorns are always known for their righteousness and nobility. They are wary, at best, of most humanoid creatures, due in large part to poachers' tendency to hunt them for their horns, but unicorns are often rumored to have a weakness for those who are pure of both heart and spirit. Despite some tales, unicorns are equally likely to recognize purity in people of all genders.

description:
Symbols of grace and purity, unicorns resemble proud and noble horses. They typically have pure white coats, but they are best known for the single, delicate horn that extends from the center of their forehead. While unicorns often serve as protectors of unspoiled wilderness and sacred places, they are themselves highly sought after for their horns, which are said to possess potent magical properties. To many, the mere idea of hunting such a magnificent creature in the hopes of severing its horn is utterly reprehensible. Indeed, a dehorned unicorn is a sorry sight, and few such unicorns survive much longer in the wild.

 Unicorns are found almost exclusively in remote, unsullied areas of wilderness. Sometimes associated with good-aligned deities, other times associated with nature and the fey, unicorns are always known for their righteousness and nobility. They are wary, at best, of most humanoid creatures, due in large part to poachers' tendency to hunt them for their horns, but unicorns are often rumored to have a weakness for those who are pure of both heart and spirit. Despite some tales, unicorns are equally likely to recognize purity in people of all genders.

A weremoose's tendencies toward stubbornness and a grumpy attitude make it difficult for them to get along with others. Most often, they live as hunters or hermits, taking in the peace of their natural surroundings. If their territory is invaded, they don't hide or retreat but are unlikely to attack. If someone else starts the fight, though, a weremoose retaliates without mercy. <title level="1" pfs="Standard">[Werewolf](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3236)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

The curse of the werewolf—known as lycanthropy to many—instills in its carriers the hungry bloodlust and predatory instincts of the wolf. Werewolves tend to dwell on the fringes of society or in small settlements where, in their humanoid forms, they work as laborers, hunters, farmers, or trappers. At night, however, these same villagers transform into violent killers and sadistic stalkers who prey on their neighbors. Werewolves are the quintessential werecreature, and the first that comes to mind when most people speak of such beings.

 Although most werewolves hide their curse by adopting solitary lifestyles, some retain the pack mentality of true wolves. A small group of such werewolves typically forms a family-like pack, with the eldest or most powerful werewolf serving as the leader. New pack mates are hand-chosen and inculcated into the family as its influence grows.

Wights are intelligent undead spawned through inescapable cycles of spite. This spite might come from their own malevolent will in life, or can be instilled by necromantic rituals, typically involving the desecration of burial sites. Wights usually haunt burial grounds, catacombs, or other places of the dead. Their hunger is targeted toward the living—those whose pumping hearts and ruddy warmth inspire visceral hatred. As many types of wights exist as types of people from which they might be created. Hulking brutes, skittering sneaks, and cunning tinkers all make for different wights with different niches to fill. The environment, too, plays a part in determining a wight's special abilities and defenses. Frost wights, for instance, can be found in parts of the world where exposure is a common end and the resentment of being left alone in the wild is a common source of spite. Durable and sustained by void energy, wights can last in harsh environments without decaying the way some lesser undead do. A single wight can wreak significant havoc if it is compelled to rise from its tomb. Because creatures slain under a wight's curse can become wights as well, all it takes is a single wight and a handful of unlucky graveyard visitors to create a veritable horde of these undead. Thus, canny priests and adventurers know that the best solution to a wight problem is swift and total eradication. Care must be taken, though, to destroy wight spawn before attempting to destroy the parent wight, for spawn without a master gain the ability to create spawn of their own. **[Recall Knowledge - Undead](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46)): DC 18 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 16 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 13 [Wight](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3239) **Source** [Monster Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=221) pg. 348 1.1 **Perception** +10; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59) **Languages** [Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1), [Necril](/Languages.aspx?ID=20) **Skills** [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) +10, [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=7) +9, [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15) +8 **Str** +4 **Dex** +1 **Con** +4 **Int** +0 **Wis** +3 **Cha** +2 **Grave Weapon** ([divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=579)) The wight is bound to a dagger it was buried with. Other wights can be bound to different weapons. **Items** [Dagger](/Weapons.aspx?ID=3) --- **AC** 18 **Fort** +11 **Ref** +6 **Will** +10 **HP** 40 (fueled by spite, [void healing](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=83)) **Immunities** bleed, [death](/Traits.aspx?ID=571) effects, [disease](/Traits.aspx?ID=578), [paralyzed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=85), [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=669), [unconscious](/Conditions.aspx?ID=95) **Final Spite** **Trigger** The wight is reduced to 0 Hit Points; **Effect** The wight makes a Strike before being destroyed. This Strike can inflict corrupting spite, but fueled by spite doesn't apply.
**Fueled by Spite** Each time a creature loses Hit Points due to a corrupting spite curse the wight inflicted, the wight gains 3 temporary Hit Points. --- **Speed** 25 feet **Melee** dagger +12 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [versatile S](/Traits.aspx?ID=200)), **Damage** 1d4+6 piercing plus corrupting spite **Melee** claw +12 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170)), **Damage** 1d4+6 slashing plus corrupting spite **Ranged** dagger +10 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [thrown 10 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=195), [versatile S](/Traits.aspx?ID=200)), **Damage** 1d4+6 slashing plus corrupting spite **Corrupting Spite** ([Curse](/Traits.aspx?ID=38), [Divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=48), [Void](/Traits.aspx?ID=510)) The wight's [unarmed](/Traits.aspx?ID=719) attacks and bound weapons inflict a curse that makes a creature grow weak and spiteful. If a wight inflicts corrupting spite on a creature already afflicted by it, the victim attempts a new save, ignoring the result if it's better than a failure. A living humanoid that dies while under the curse rises as a wight after 1d4 rounds, [controlled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=64) by the wight that killed it. The wight spawn can't inflict corrupting spite and is [clumsy 2](/Conditions.aspx?ID=61). If its creator dies or after roughly a month of existence, the new wight becomes autonomous and turns into a normal wight; **Saving Throw** DC 17 Fortitude; **Stage 1** [drained 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=68) (1 round); **Stage 2** drained 2 and doesn't treat any creatures as allies (1 round); **Stage 3** As stage 2, except drained 3 (1 round); **Stage 4** As stage 2, except drained 4 (1 round).

**[Recall Knowledge - Aberration](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=11)): DC 28 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 26 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 23 [Zoudou the Zealous](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2734) **Source** [Pathfinder #196: The Summer That Never Was](/Sources.aspx?ID=214) pg. 66 **Perception** +8; no face **Languages** [Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1); [telepathy](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=37) 30 feet **Skills** [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=1) +9, [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5) +11, [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=6) +9, [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=11) +10, [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=13) +9, [Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=14) +8 **Str** +2 **Dex** +4 **Con** +3 **Int** +3 **Wis** +2 **Cha** +4 **No Face** Noppera-bos have no sense of vision, but their sense of hearing is [precise](/Rules.aspx?ID=411). They don't breathe and are immune to effects that require breathing. They gain sustenance by absorbing fluids through their skin—traditionally by immersing their hands or faceless head into the fluid to “drink” through osmosis; they can also benefit from [consumables](/Traits.aspx?ID=36), such as [potions](/Traits.aspx?ID=130) or [elixirs](/Traits.aspx?ID=59), in this way. **Items** [_Fiend's Hunger_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2683) (page 81), tattered ledger, twisted knot of wood ([religious symbol](/Equipment.aspx?ID=41) of Kugaptee) --- **AC** 19 **Fort** +10 **Ref** +11 **Will** +7 **HP** 45 **Immunities** [inhaled](/Traits.aspx?ID=96), [olfactory](/Traits.aspx?ID=246), [visual](/Traits.aspx?ID=163) **Weaknesses** sensitive hearing **Identity Crisis** ([emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=60), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=106), [occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=120), [visual](/Traits.aspx?ID=163)) **Frequency** once per day; **Trigger** Zoudou successfully Steals the Face of an adjacent creature; **Effect** As Zoudou Steals the creature's Face, she telepathically draws at the creature's sense of identity and self. The creature must attempt a DC 20 Will save. On a failure, the creature questions their own identity and becomes [slowed 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=35) for 1 round. On a critical failure, they're slowed 1 for 1 minute.
**Oath of Anonymity** When Zoudou has a face, she can't cast divine prepared spells.
**Sensitive Hearing** As long as a noppera-bo is [deafened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=8), they are [slowed 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=35). --- **Speed** 25 feet **Melee** _Fiend's Hunger_ +9 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [Finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=179), [thrown 10 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=195), [versatile S](/Traits.aspx?ID=200)), **Damage** 1d4+4 piercing **Divine Prepared Spells** DC 20, attack +12 - **Cantrips (2nd)** [Chill Touch](/Spells.aspx?ID=35), [Daze](/Spells.aspx?ID=61), [Divine Lance](/Spells.aspx?ID=84), [Read Aura](/Spells.aspx?ID=246), [Shield](/Spells.aspx?ID=280) - **1st** [Bane](/Spells.aspx?ID=18), [Fear](/Spells.aspx?ID=110), [Heal](/Spells.aspx?ID=148) - **2nd** [Darkness](/Spells.aspx?ID=59), [Harm](/Spells.aspx?ID=146) **Rituals** - **2nd** [Consecrate](/Rituals.aspx?ID=8) **Impersonate Shape** ([Concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32), [Occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=120), [Polymorph](/Traits.aspx?ID=127), [Transmutation](/Traits.aspx?ID=157)) The noppera-bo changes into a Small or Medium humanoid they've touched during the last 24 hours, and the noppera-bo gains the target creature's face and voice. While transformed and their face is covered, the noppera-bo gains a +2 circumstance bonus to [Impersonate](/Actions.aspx?ID=46) that creature. As long as the noppera-bo has a face, it loses its no face ability and its listed immunities. The noppera-bo can change back by using this ability again. **Regain Anonymity** ([Occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=120), [Polymorph](/Traits.aspx?ID=127), [Transmutation](/Traits.aspx?ID=157)) **Requirement** Zoudou has a face; **Effect** Zoudou melts the face she's wearing and gains 3d6 temporary Hit Points. She can't Regain Anonymity again for 1d4 rounds. **Silent Casting** When Zoudou is faceless, she can substitute an additional somatic component for a verbal component. **Steal Face** ([Concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32), [Curse](/Traits.aspx?ID=38), [Incapacitation](/Traits.aspx?ID=93), [Occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=120), [Polymorph](/Traits.aspx?ID=127), [Transmutation](/Traits.aspx?ID=157)) **Frequency** once per day; **Requirements** The noppera-bo occultist is faceless; **Effect** The noppera-bo occultist targets one creature within 30 feet. The creature must attempt a DC 20 Fortitude save.
**Critical Success** The target is unaffected.
**Success** The target is [dazzled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=7) until the start of its next turn.
**Failure** The noppera-bo gains the target's face. The target's face vanishes until the end of its next turn. Until then, it is [blinded](/Conditions.aspx?ID=1), can't speak or ingest, and can't smell. The target must also hold its breath or begin to [suffocate](/Rules.aspx?ID=468).
**Critical Failure** As failure, but the effect doesn't end automatically. The target can attempt a new save at the end of each of its turns, and the DC cumulatively decreases by 1 on each such attempt.

Gambling devils, known also as agadazes, resemble horned humans crafted out of living gold in their natural forms, though their shapeshifting abilities let them move among mortals undetected. They're most commonly encountered in Erebus, the third layer of [Hell](/Planes.aspx?ID=42), where many serve [Mammon](/Deities.aspx?ID=399) as accountants. They're unusually impulsive and distractible for their kind. Other devils often view their Risk Aura as a hindrance, so they usually receive less important missions. They don't mind, for it gives them more time to meddle with mortals. **[Recall Knowledge - Fiend](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46)): DC 21 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 19 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 16 [Agadaz](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3744) **Source** [Pathfinder #205: Singer, Stalker, Skinsaw Man](/Sources.aspx?ID=246) pg. 86 **Perception** +10; [greater darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59) **Languages** [Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1), [Diabolic](/Languages.aspx?ID=117), [Empyrean](/Languages.aspx?ID=115); [telepathy](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=79) 100 feet **Skills** [Accounting Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) +11, [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38) +12, [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39) +11, [Games Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) +13, [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=40) +10, [Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=50) +11 **Str** +3 **Dex** +4 **Con** +4 **Int** +3 **Wis** +2 **Cha** +4 **Items** 20 gp --- **AC** 20 **Fort** +12 **Ref** +14 **Will** +10 **HP** 50 **Immunities** [fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=604) **Resistances** physical 5 (except [silver](/Equipment.aspx?ID=379)), [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=669) 5 **Weaknesses** [holy](/Traits.aspx?ID=517) 5 **Risk Aura** ([aura](/Traits.aspx?ID=542), [divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=579), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647), [misfortune](/Traits.aspx?ID=654)) 30 feet. A feeling of recklessness surrounds a gambling devil. When a non-fiend creature enters the aura or begins its turn in the aura, it must attempt a DC 21 Will save.
**Critical Success** The creature is unaffected and is temporarily immune to Risk Aura for 24 hours.
**Success** The creature is unaffected.
**Failure** The next time the creature rolls a d20, it must roll twice. If either roll is a natural 20, the creature uses that result; otherwise, it must take the lower of the two results.
**Critical Failure** As failure, but applies to all of the creature's d20 rolls as long as it remains in the aura. --- **Speed** 25 feet **Melee** fist +12 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [Finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=179), [Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103), [Unholy](/Traits.aspx?ID=521)), **Damage** 2d4+7 bludgeoning **Ranged** thrown coin +12 ([Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103), [Unholy](/Traits.aspx?ID=521)), **Damage** 2d4+5 bludgeoning plus 1d6 precision **Divine Innate Spells** DC 18 - **Cantrips (2nd)** [Figment](/Spells.aspx?ID=1528) - **1st** [Ill Omen](/Spells.aspx?ID=696) (at will) - **2nd** [Illusory Creature](/Spells.aspx?ID=158), [Illusory Object](/Spells.aspx?ID=160) **Rituals** - **1st** [Diabolic Pact](/Rituals.aspx?ID=143) **[Change Shape](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=55)** ([Concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32), [Divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=48), [Polymorph](/Traits.aspx?ID=127)) The agadaz adopts the appearance of any Small or Medium humanoid. An almiraj closely resembles a yellow hare in almost all ways... except for the 2-foot-long black horn jutting from its forehead. Though it shares this trait with the docile [unicorn](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=504), that's where their similarities end. Almirajes are vicious creatures, known to slaughter much larger cattle and, in times of desperation, people. Its stare is said to send even the bravest warrior running for their life. Unlike common hares, almirajes are solitary and intensely territorial. They're adaptable ambush hunters with the stamina and speed to chase down any prey. They attack with their jaws and claws but are primarily known for trying to gut their prey with a vicious stab from their horn. Many scholars believe that the terrifying magical aura the creatures exude originates from their horns. This line of thinking has led to an increase in almiraj attacks as local citizens try to capture the creature alive and remove the horn, hoping this will turn it into a more docile hare. These hopes have not proven fruitful, as an almiraj is just as aggressive, if not more so, after their horn has been removed. Adventurers often think themselves lucky if they manage to avoid the terrifying horn of this ferocious predator, but it's a much better alternative than being caught in its jaws. Almirajes have a nasty habit of grabbing their prey and vigorously shaking them until they go limp. If this fails, they'll drag their prey underground until they suffocate deep in the earth. Few have ever escaped the burrow of an almiraj. **[Recall Knowledge - Animal](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43)): DC 21 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 19 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 16 [Almiraj](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3253) **Source** [Howl of the Wild](/Sources.aspx?ID=226) pg. 124 2.1 **Perception** +14; [tremorsense](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=82) ([imprecise](/Rules.aspx?ID=412)) 40 feet **Languages** **Skills** [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) +13, [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=48) +10, [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=49) +8 **Str** +5 **Dex** +3 **Con** +4 **Int** -4 **Wis** +0 **Cha** +3 --- **AC** 20 **Fort** +14 **Ref** +11 **Will** +8 **HP** 63 **[Frightful Presence](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=64)** ([aura](/Traits.aspx?ID=542), [emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=590), [fear](/Traits.aspx?ID=598), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647)) 5 feet, DC 22. Creatures that critically fail are also [fleeing](/Conditions.aspx?ID=74) for 1 round.
**[Reactive Strike](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=48)** Horn only. [Fleeing](/Conditions.aspx?ID=74) creatures take an additional 1d6 [persistent bleed damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29). On a critical hit, the target is knocked [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=88). --- **Speed** 35 feet, burrow 25 feet **Melee** horn +13, **Damage** 2d8+7 slashing **Melee** jaws +13, **Damage** 2d6+7 piercing plus [Grab](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=45) **Melee** claw +13 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170)), **Damage** 2d4+7 slashing **Final Shake** **Requirements** The almiraj has a creature [grabbed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=77); **Effect** The almiraj clamps its jaws down on the creature and shakes it vigorously, attempting to finish it off. The creature takes 2d6 bludgeoning damage and must succeed at a DC 20 Fortitude save or become [enfeebled 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=71). Small or smaller creatures take a –2 circumstance penalty to their save. **Goring Charge** The almiraj lowers its head and moves with ferocity toward its selected prey. The almiraj Strides twice. If it ends its movement within melee reach of at least one enemy, it makes a horn Strike against that enemy. This Strike deals an additional 1d6 [persistent bleed damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29). **Into the Earth** **Requirements** The almiraj has a Medium or smaller creature [grabbed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=77); **Effect** The almiraj attempts to flee with its meal, burrowing into the ground. The grabbed creature must succeed at a DC 20 Reflex save or be dragged beneath the ground as the almiraj [Burrows](/Actions.aspx?ID=2310) up to its Speed. If the target succeeds at its save, it [Escapes](/Actions.aspx?ID=2296) and the almiraj continues burrowing as normal; if it fails, the grabbed creature must hold its breath or begin [suffocating](/Rules.aspx?ID=2436) under the dirt.

description:
An almiraj closely resembles a yellow hare in almost all ways... except for the 2-foot-long black horn jutting from its forehead. Though it shares this trait with the docile [unicorn](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=504), that's where their similarities end. Almirajes are vicious creatures, known to slaughter much larger cattle and, in times of desperation, people. Its stare is said to send even the bravest warrior running for their life.

 Unlike common hares, almirajes are solitary and intensely territorial. They're adaptable ambush hunters with the stamina and speed to chase down any prey. They attack with their jaws and claws but are primarily known for trying to gut their prey with a vicious stab from their horn. Many scholars believe that the terrifying magical aura the creatures exude originates from their horns. This line of thinking has led to an increase in almiraj attacks as local citizens try to capture the creature alive and remove the horn, hoping this will turn it into a more docile hare. These hopes have not proven fruitful, as an almiraj is just as aggressive, if not more so, after their horn has been removed.

 Adventurers often think themselves lucky if they manage to avoid the terrifying horn of this ferocious predator, but it's a much better alternative than being caught in its jaws. Almirajes have a nasty habit of grabbing their prey and vigorously shaking them until they go limp. If this fails, they'll drag their prey underground until they suffocate deep in the earth. Few have ever escaped the burrow of an almiraj.

Arboreal wardens are the rangers of arboreal society. These itinerant folk have an innate curiosity about the woodlands in which they dwell, and rarely stop to take root and rest in the same part of the forest twice. This wanderlust makes wardens ideal forest patrollers and scouts. While they are robust combatants, they know better than to confront dangerous foes on their own. Instead, they report any dangers to arboreal regents. In rare cases, large groups of arboreal wardens congregate to form a copse. Copses travel beyond the boundaries of a forest to investigate the hinterlands and gather intelligence on potential threats before returning to report their findings. Arboreal wardens do not pretend to understand to other creatures' motives—like most forces of the natural world, they are ambivalent about mortal affairs that do not involve their forest. **[Recall Knowledge - Plant](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43)): DC 19 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 17 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 14 [Arboreal Warden](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2829) **Source** [Monster Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=221) pg. 24 1.1 **Perception** +11; [low-light vision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=69) **Languages** [Arboreal](/Languages.aspx?ID=26), [Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1), [Fey](/Languages.aspx?ID=119) **Skills** [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) +13, [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15) +9 **Str** +5 **Dex** +1 **Con** +3 **Int** +1 **Wis** +3 **Cha** +1 **Items** large bark shield, stone [longsword](/Weapons.aspx?ID=386) --- **AC** 20 (22 with shield raised) **Fort** +13 **Ref** +9 **Will** +11 **HP** 75 **Resistances** bludgeoning 5, piercing 5 **Weaknesses** [axes](/WeaponGroups.aspx?ID=1) 5, [fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=604) 10 **[Reactive Strike](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=48)**
**[Shield Block](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=75)** --- **Speed** 25 feet **Melee** stone longsword +13 ([reach 10 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)), **Damage** 1d8+10 bludgeoning **Melee** shield bash +13, **Damage** 1d6+10 bludgeoning **Shield Push** The arboreal warden Strides and then makes a shield bash Strike. <title level="1" pfs="Standard">[Barghest](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2846)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

Barghests are canine beasts that take great joy in the hunt, often lurking near humanoid settlements to find prey that can provide a suitable challenge. Even in the deepest wilderness, barghests choose the most clever or difficult prey, searching endlessly for challenges like [giants](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=420), [nymphs](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=449), and [unicorns](/Monsters.aspx?ID=397). More than victory or even the possibility of a meal at the end, barghests enjoy the thrill of the chase and the fear they create within their prey. Particularly terrified targets of a hunting barghest might even be allowed to escape, spreading the terror and enticing hunters who can become the barghest's next victims. A handful of barghests resort to learning magical methods of causing fear directly, though they find such fear hollow and unsatisfying.

 Although they rarely tolerate the competition of another barghest's presence, these hunters will happily work with anyone who helps them find prey to torment and kill. This often involves enforcing the will of [hags](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=425) or particularly cruel [fey](/Languages.aspx?ID=119), but a bored barghest might also force a family of weaker humanoids to work as scouts and bait.

Typical barghests often make use of their shapechanging abilities to hide in plain sight, only taking their true forms to frighten their prey and exult in the hunt. However, they are often still exposed by their trail of victims or the curiously unhealing wounds they inflict, even in humanoid form. Tales of powerful barghests with invisible heads are sometimes told in remote and dwindling villages. These barghests generally dispense with hiding as a humanoid or dog, instead terrifying entire communities and openly hunting increasingly dangerous prey. Some also extend this pride to their intellect, insisting on matching wits with their prey or even with those who believe they're hunting the barghest.

However, they are often still exposed by their trail of victims or the curiously unhealing wounds they inflict, even in humanoid form. Tales of powerful barghests with invisible heads are sometimes told in remote and dwindling villages. These barghests generally dispense with hiding as a humanoid or dog, instead terrifying entire communities and openly hunting increasingly dangerous prey. Some also extend this pride to their intellect, insisting on matching wits with their prey or even with those who believe they're hunting the barghest.

<title level="1" pfs="Standard">[Caligni Hunter](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2864)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

Although caligni hunters are often pressed into leading their skulker kin, most hunters prefer to wander the Darklands or raid the surface free from those responsibilities. Their preferred assaults are usually done by solo caligni hunters or in small groups of two or three.

<column gap="tiny">
**[Recall Knowledge - Humanoid](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**
([Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=47)): DC 19

**[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 17

**[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 14
</column>

</column>

<column gap="medium">

</column>

</row>

<title level="2" right="Creature 4">[Caligni Hunter](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2864)</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Medium" />
<trait label="Caligni" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=745" />
<trait label="Humanoid" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=628" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Monster Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=221) pg. 49 <sup>1.1</sup>

**Perception** +10; [greater darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59), [light blindness](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=68)

**Languages**
[Caligni](/Languages.aspx?ID=28), [Sakvroth](/Languages.aspx?ID=118)

**Skills**
[Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=1) +13, [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) +8, [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15) +13, [Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=17) +11, [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=16) +12

<row gap="medium">
**Str** +2

**Dex** +5

**Con** +2

**Int** -1

**Wis** +2

**Cha** +1
</row>

**Items**
darkening poison (6 doses), [Leather Armor](/Armor.aspx?ID=4), [Shortsword](/Weapons.aspx?ID=43) (2)

</column>

---

<column gap="tiny">

<row gap="medium">
**AC** 21 

**Fort** +10 

**Ref** +13 

**Will** +8 

</row>

<row gap="medium">
**HP** 60
(final fate)

</row>

**Final Fate** ([occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=662), [spirit](/Traits.aspx?ID=737)) When the hunter dies, their soul leaves their body in an explosion of spiritual energy. All creatures in a 20-foot burst take 5d6 spirit damage (DC 19 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Will save). The hunter's possessions are left in a pile where they died.

</column>

---

<column gap="tiny">

**Speed** 25 feet

**Melee**
<actions string="Single Action" />
shortsword +13 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [Finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=179), [versatile S](/Traits.aspx?ID=200)),
**Damage** 1d6+7 piercing plus darkening poison

**Occult Innate Spells** DC 19
- **Cantrips (2nd)**
[Figment](/Spells.aspx?ID=1528)
- **2nd**
[Darkness](/Spells.aspx?ID=59) (at will), [See the Unseen](/Spells.aspx?ID=1663) (at will)

**Double Slice** <actions string="Two Actions" />  The caligni hunter makes two Strikes against the same target, one with each of their shortswords. The hunter combines the damage of any attacks that hit and applies precision damage, resistances, and weaknesses only once. Both attacks count toward the hunter's multiple attack penalty, but the penalty increases only after both attacks.

**Encircling Command** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([Auditory](/Traits.aspx?ID=16)) Each [caligni skulker](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2863) within 30 feet of the hunter can Step. Each skulker can benefit from Encircling Command only once per round.

**Sneak Attack**   The caligni hunter deals 1d6 extra precision damage to [off-guard](/Conditions.aspx?ID=58) creatures.

</column>

**[Recall Knowledge - Construct](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=2), [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=4)): DC 29 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 27 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 24 [Clockwork Belimarius](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2745) **Source** [Rusthenge](/Sources.aspx?ID=215) pg. 47 **Perception** +10; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=12) **Languages** **Skills** [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=1) +12 **Str** +2 **Dex** +4 **Con** +3 **Int** -5 **Wis** +2 **Cha** -5 **Wind-Up** 24 hours, DC 21, standby **Items** clockwork wand, _+1 [striking](/Equipment.aspx?ID=280) [halberd](/Weapons.aspx?ID=26)_ --- **AC** 20 **Fort** +11 **Ref** +12 **Will** +8 **HP** 45 **Immunities** [death](/Traits.aspx?ID=40) effects, [disease](/Traits.aspx?ID=46), [doomed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=9), [drained](/Conditions.aspx?ID=10), [fatigued](/Conditions.aspx?ID=15), [healing](/Traits.aspx?ID=89), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=106), [necromancy](/Traits.aspx?ID=117), [nonlethal](/Traits.aspx?ID=188) attacks, [paralyzed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=28), [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=126), [sickened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=34), [unconscious](/Conditions.aspx?ID=38) **Resistances** physical 5 (except [adamantine](/Equipment.aspx?ID=374), bludgeoning, or orichalcum) **Weaknesses** [electricity](/Traits.aspx?ID=56) 5, [orichalcum](/Equipment.aspx?ID=378) 5 **Clockwork Wand** The clockwork mage uses a mechanical wand as a focus to channel magical energy. This wand is built into the clockwork mage's chest, with only the crystal at the end exposed. The mage can Interact to the remove the wand, or someone else can remove it with a DC 25 [Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=17) check to [Disable a Device](/Actions.aspx?ID=69). The clockwork mage becomes unable to cast any spells except cantrips while the wand is removed.
When removed, the clockwork wand is a magic wand containing the last 1st-level innate spell the clockwork mage cast ([_fear_](/Spells.aspx?ID=110), if the clockwork Belimarius hasn't yet cast a 1st-level spell in this adventure). The spells are placed within the wand while the mage is created, and the creator can substitute other arcane spells of the appropriate level. --- **Speed** 25 feet **Melee** _halberd_ +16 ([Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103), [Reach](/Traits.aspx?ID=192), [versatile S](/Traits.aspx?ID=200)), **Damage** 2d10+4 piercing plus dispelling critical **Arcane Innate Spells** DC 21, attack +13 - **Cantrips (2nd)** [Daze](/Spells.aspx?ID=61), [Shield](/Spells.aspx?ID=280), [Tanglefoot](/Spells.aspx?ID=330) - **1st** [Color Spray](/Spells.aspx?ID=44), [Fear](/Spells.aspx?ID=110), [Mage Armor](/Spells.aspx?ID=176) - **2nd** [Magnetic Repulsion](/Spells.aspx?ID=945), [Resist Energy](/Spells.aspx?ID=256) **Dispelling Critical** On a critical hit with a halberd Strike, shards of [noqual](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1419) built into the clockwork Belimarius glow green for a moment. Instead of inflicting additional damage with the critical hit, the clockwork Belimarius instead attempts a [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) check with a +18 bonus against one magical effect active on the target.

Some serpentfolk undergo intense ritual training and practice to improve their innate ability to disguise themselves. These serpentfolk often identify as members of a sinister society known as the Coils of Ydersius, and the most devoted of their number seek out methods of reincarnating into new forms to infiltrate enemy societies even more efficiently. Coil spies train in methods of infiltrating other societies to such an extent that they might be capable of infiltrating a mammalian civilization for years. <title level="1" pfs="Standard">[Daeodon](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2855)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

Where the typical boar is merely ill-tempered and generally unfriendly, the towering daeodon is legitimately hateful and ruthlessly violent. Although omnivorous, the daeodon (known in some regions simply as a giant boar) prefers to feed on flesh. While it is primarily a scavenger, the daeodon isn't adverse to attacking creatures it encounters while searching for easier meals, or to protect any perceived encroachment into its lair or feeding grounds. Particularly brave or skilled [orcs](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=454) are fond of using daeodons as mounts or war-trained battle beasts; orc cavalry mounted on daeodons is a fearsome force indeed.

text: Daeodon Where the typical boar is merely ill-tempered and generally unfriendly, the towering daeodon is legitimately hateful and ruthlessly violent. Although omnivorous, the daeodon (known in some regions simply as a giant boar) prefers to feed on flesh. While it is primarily a scavenger, the daeodon isn't adverse to attacking creatures it encounters while searching for easier meals, or to protect any perceived encroachment into its lair or feeding grounds. Particularly brave or skilled orcs are fond of using daeodons as mounts or war-trained battle beasts; orc cavalry mounted on daeodons is a fearsome force indeed. A typical adult daeodon is 10 feet long and 7 feet tall at the shoulder. It weighs approximately 2,000 pounds. Pulled astray by lies, bribes, and propaganda, these desperate people are convinced to fight on their behalf of utter villains. Conspiracists, propagandists, masterminds, despots, and more take advantage of these mobs. **[Recall Knowledge - Humanoid](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=47)): DC 19 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 17 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 14 [Deluded Mob](/NPCs.aspx?ID=3611) **Source** [NPC Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=236) pg. 155 **Perception** +7 **Languages** [Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1) **Skills** [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) +12, [Conspiracy Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) +6, [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=40) +9 **Str** +6 **Dex** +1 **Con** +4 **Int** +0 **Wis** -1 **Cha** +1 **Irrational** The deluded mob is severely disconnected from reality. [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39) checks to [Make an Impression](/Actions.aspx?ID=2392) or otherwise sway their worldview automatically fail. --- **AC** 19 **Fort** +12 **Ref** +9 **Will** +7 victim complex **HP** 75 (4 segments) **Weaknesses** area damage 5, splash damage 5 **[Troop Defenses](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=44)**
**Victim Complex** As they lose members, the deluded mob takes the opposition against them as proof that they're right, bolstering their resolve. The deluded mob gains a +2 circumstance bonus to Will saves at 50 or fewer Hit Points, or a +4 circumstance bonus at 25 HP or fewer. --- **Speed** 25 feet; [troop movement](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=85) **Flail Desperately** **Frequency** once per round; **Effect** The deluded mob uses their fists, wooden planks, and anything else they can pick up to attack each enemy in a 5-foot emanation with fervor, if not coordination (DC 18 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save). The damage depends on the number of actions.
1d8 piercing or bludgeoning damage
1d8+6 piercing or bludgeoning damage
2d8+6 piercing or bludgeoning damage **Surrounded** When they feel cornered, the mob lashes out more recklessly. While the deluded mob is flanked, Flail Desperately and Throw Detritus are DC 17 and deal an additional 2 damage per action spent on the activity. **Throw Detritus** The deluded mob hurls detritus in a 10-foot burst within 30 feet that deals 2d8 bludgeoning damage with a DC 18 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save. When the mob is reduced to 2 or fewer segments, this area decreases to a 5-foot burst.

While most engineers take immense pride in their work constructing something that may survive many lifetimes, the demolitionist takes pride in destroying such pompous things in the most spectacular way possible. Every design has a flaw, and that flaw usually involves large quantities of explosives. Demolitionists are often pragmatic and calculated, taking great care to destroy whatever lies before them as efficiently as possible. **[Recall Knowledge - Humanoid](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=47)): DC 19 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 17 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 14 [Demolitionist](/NPCs.aspx?ID=3461) **Source** [NPC Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=236) pg. 45 **Perception** +10 **Languages** [Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1) **Skills** [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) +9, [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=37) +12, [Explosive Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) +14, [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=40) +10, [Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=50) +11 **Str** +1 **Dex** +3 **Con** +3 **Int** +4 **Wis** +0 **Cha** +0 **Items** bag of explosives, [Leather Armor](/Armor.aspx?ID=4), [Light Mace](/Weapons.aspx?ID=5) --- **AC** 20 **Fort** +11 **Ref** +13 **Will** +6 **HP** 60 **Resistances** fire 5 **Explosive Demise** ([fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=604)) When the demolitionist is reduced to 0 Hit Points while they have any explosives still in their bag, the remaining explosives detonate, unleashing an explosion of fire upon all creatures in a 30-foot emanation. Each creature in the area takes 3d6 fire damage with a DC 19 Reflex save.
**Replenish Explosives** The demolitionist can replenish their stock of explosives with 4 hours of downtime. --- **Speed** 25 feet **Melee** light mace +13 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [Finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=179), [Shove](/Traits.aspx?ID=193)), **Damage** 1d4+7 bludgeoning **Melee** fist +13 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [Finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=179), [Nonlethal](/Traits.aspx?ID=188), [Unarmed](/Traits.aspx?ID=199)), **Damage** 1d4+7 bludgeoning **Plant Mine** ([Fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=72), [Manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104)) The demolitionist plants a mine in an adjacent square. If a creature moves onto a space with a mine, the mine explodes. This deals 3d8 fire damage to the creature with a DC 21 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save. The demolitionist can use 2 actions to Plant a Mine to hide the mine, granting it a [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=48) DC of 21. Creatures that didn't see the mine as it was planted must actively search for it (using the [Search](/Actions.aspx?ID=2630) activity while exploring or the [Seek](/Actions.aspx?ID=2301) action in an encounter). **Toss Dynamite** ([Fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=72), [Manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104)) The demolitionist quickly throws a stick of dynamite up to 20 feet away that explodes in 5-foot burst. Creatures within the burst take 4d4 fire damage with a DC 21 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save. **Wall Charge** ([Fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=72), [Manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104)) the demolitionist plants a powerful wall charge on a flat surface such as a door or wall. Once the charge is planted, it explodes after 1 minute, dealing 60 fire damage to the surface and ignoring up to 15 of the surface's Hardness. The explosive also deals 5d6 fire damage to creatures within 30 feet of the explosive with a [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save DC 25.

<title level="1" pfs="Standard">[Dwarf Stonecaster](/NPCs.aspx?ID=2966)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

All dwarves share a connection to the earth, but stonecasters have focused and polished that connection. Their years of meditation have granted them the ability to create boulders and shake the very earth. These elemental specialists are often highly respected in their community, which prizes their art of geomancy. Young dwarves who show a stronger than normal connection to the earth might be sent to a stonecaster to train at an early age.

<title level="1" pfs="">[Enigmatic Conspiracist](/NPCs.aspx?ID=3536)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

Powerful organizations work out of public view, shaping lives while facing few consequences. Searching for these secret societies, whether to join them or destroy them, has given the enigmatic conspiracist uncanny insight.

<column gap="tiny">
**[Recall Knowledge - Humanoid](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**
([Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=47)): DC 19

**[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 17

</column>

</column>
