<title level="1" pfs="">[Spirit Priest](/NPCs.aspx?ID=3627)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

While dwarves worship gods like most any other ancestry, many dwarves also look to the spirits of the world for guidance and support. Most every object and environment in the world, from a simple rock to an expansive river to the largest of mountains, contains some kind of spirit. Dwarven spirit priests learn how to communicate with these spirits. This spiritual attunement allows these priests to use magic, as well as call on these spirits in times of need.

<column gap="tiny">
**[Recall Knowledge - Humanoid](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**
([Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=47)): DC 20

**[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 18

**[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 15
</column>

</column>

<column gap="medium">
<image src="/images/Monsters/Spirit_Priest.webp" />
</column>

</row>

<title level="2" right="Creature 5">[Spirit Priest](/NPCs.aspx?ID=3627)</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Medium" />
<trait label="Dwarf" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=584" />
<trait label="Humanoid" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=628" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [NPC Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=236) pg. 174

**Perception** +12; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59)

**Languages**
[Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1), [Dwarven](/Languages.aspx?ID=3), [Empyrean](/Languages.aspx?ID=115), [Fey](/Languages.aspx?ID=119), [Petran](/Languages.aspx?ID=109), [Pyric](/Languages.aspx?ID=110)

**Skills**
[Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) +12, [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39) +12, [Dwarf Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) +10, [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=44) +10, [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46) +14

<row gap="medium">
**Str** +2

**Dex** +0

**Con** +3

**Int** +0

**Wis** +5

**Cha** +2
</row>

**Items**
[Clan Dagger](/Weapons.aspx?ID=13)

</column>

---

<column gap="tiny">

<row gap="medium">
**AC** 19 

**Fort** +12 

**Ref** +9 

**Will** +14 

</row>

<row gap="medium">
**HP** 78

</row>

</column>

---

<column gap="tiny">

**Speed** 20 feet

**Melee**
<actions string="Single Action" />
clan dagger +11 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [Parry](/Traits.aspx?ID=190), [versatile B](/Traits.aspx?ID=200)),
**Damage** 1d4+6 piercing

**Melee**
<actions string="Single Action" />
fist +11 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [Nonlethal](/Traits.aspx?ID=188), [Unarmed](/Traits.aspx?ID=199)),
**Damage** 1d4+6 bludgeoning

**Divine Spontaneous Spells** DC 22, attack +14
- **Cantrips (2nd)**
[Detect Magic](/Spells.aspx?ID=66), [Divine Lance](/Spells.aspx?ID=84), [Guidance](/Spells.aspx?ID=142), [Shield](/Spells.aspx?ID=280), [Stabilize](/Spells.aspx?ID=307)
- **1st**
[Bless](/Spells.aspx?ID=25), [Fear](/Spells.aspx?ID=110), [Infuse Vitality](/Spells.aspx?ID=1574), [Spirit Link](/Spells.aspx?ID=302) (4 slots)
- **2nd**
[Augury](/Spells.aspx?ID=15), [Heal](/Spells.aspx?ID=148), [Noise Blast](/Spells.aspx?ID=1616), [See the Unseen](/Spells.aspx?ID=1663) (4 slots)
- **3rd**
[Noise Blast](/Spells.aspx?ID=1616), [Safe Passage](/Spells.aspx?ID=712), [Spiritual Armament](/Spells.aspx?ID=1687) (3 slots)

**Spirit's Interference** <actions string="Two Actions" />  The spirit priest calls out to a local spirit to assault the priest's enemies. The spirit unleashes a blast of rocks, attacks with a set of vines, or uses some other appropriate part of the environment to attack all creatures in a 10-foot burst within 30 feet of the priest. The attack deals 6d6 bludgeoning damage with a DC 18 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save. The spirit priest can't use Spirit's Interference for 1d4 rounds. The GM might have this ability deal a different damage type based on the local spirits, such as fire damage when calling on a fire spirit.

**Spiritual Edge** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([Concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32), [Spellshape](/Traits.aspx?ID=513), [Spirit](/Traits.aspx?ID=149)) The spirit priest aligns their spirit with their magical effects, enhancing the power of their spells. If their next action is to Cast a Spell that deals damage and doesn't have a duration, the spell deals additional spirit damage equal to the spell's rank.

</column>

<title level="1" pfs="">[Storm Snake](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3314)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

Storm snakes are reclusive creatures only seen in the wild during intense storms. The metallic scales that cover their bodies attract and absorb nearby lightning strikes, suffusing the creatures with a halo of blue or white light. Because storm snakes are most often sighted in solitude and disappear without a trace as soon as a storm recedes, a lot of folklore across Golarion considers them to be the emissaries of storm deities and harbingers of disaster.

 Before live clutches of storm snake young were first discovered, it was hypothesized that the creatures were made of mist and vapor; many assumed them to be illusory shapes within the clouds themselves or fleeting dragon sightings. New zoological research has found, however, that storm snakes are actually a distant cousin of dragons. Raised on mountaintops in small broods, storm snakes have underdeveloped limbs and lack any form of wing. Instead, they expand and contract their metallic scales to capture the static electricity in wind currents, which keeps them aloft during high winds and storms.

 Research has also shed light on the diet of these naturally shy creatures. Rather than consuming electricity, as many who'd observed them in storms believed, storm snakes are herbivorous, enjoying most varieties of grasses, plants, or tree leaves. This diet, considered alongside their flight patterns during thunderstorms, has been theorized to be a form of symbiosis; after all, any lightning strikes absorbed by a storm snake during a storm can't damage the plant growth below. Additionally, safely discharged electricity from a storm snake has been observed to stimulate growth in a wide variety of flora, all while having no adverse affects on the plants' palatability or nutritional benefits. Many farmers have tried in vain to capture, tame, or otherwise attract storm snakes to their fields to invigorate their crops during tough times, though few have succeeded.

description:
Storm snakes are reclusive creatures only seen in the wild during intense storms. The metallic scales that cover their bodies attract and absorb nearby lightning strikes, suffusing the creatures with a halo of blue or white light. Because storm snakes are most often sighted in solitude and disappear without a trace as soon as a storm recedes, a lot of folklore across Golarion considers them to be the emissaries of storm deities and harbingers of disaster.

 Before live clutches of storm snake young were first discovered, it was hypothesized that the creatures were made of mist and vapor; many assumed them to be illusory shapes within the clouds themselves or fleeting dragon sightings. New zoological research has found, however, that storm snakes are actually a distant cousin of dragons. Raised on mountaintops in small broods, storm snakes have underdeveloped limbs and lack any form of wing. Instead, they expand and contract their metallic scales to capture the static electricity in wind currents, which keeps them aloft during high winds and storms.

 Research has also shed light on the diet of these naturally shy creatures. Rather than consuming electricity, as many who'd observed them in storms believed, storm snakes are herbivorous, enjoying most varieties of grasses, plants, or tree leaves. This diet, considered alongside their flight patterns during thunderstorms, has been theorized to be a form of symbiosis; after all, any lightning strikes absorbed by a storm snake during a storm can't damage the plant growth below. Additionally, safely discharged electricity from a storm snake has been observed to stimulate growth in a wide variety of flora, all while having no adverse affects on the plants' palatability or nutritional benefits. Many farmers have tried in vain to capture, tame, or otherwise attract storm snakes to their fields to invigorate their crops during tough times, though few have succeeded.

<title level="1" pfs="">[Subaquatic Marauder](/NPCs.aspx?ID=3603)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

A new breed of pirate, these raiders strike at unsuspecting ships from beneath the cover of the waves. The bulky, reinforced diving suits they wear also serve as armor and clockwork mechanisms augment their strength.

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=721" />
<trait label="Medium" />
<trait label="Human" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=627" />
<trait label="Humanoid" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=628" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [NPC Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=236) pg. 149

**Perception** +12

**Languages**
[Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1)

**Skills**
[Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) +13, [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=37) +13, [Ocean Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) +12

<row gap="medium">
**Str** +4

**Dex** +2

**Con** +4

**Int** +2

**Wis** +1

**Cha** +0
</row>

**Sealed Diving Suit** The marauder's diving suit is a technological marvel. When sealed, it provides 1 hour of fresh air and protects the wearer from exposure to [inhaled](/Traits.aspx?ID=634) threats. Personalized modifications and a need for constant tinkering mean that other creatures are unable to take advantage of the special abilities of the diving suit and treat it as an ordinary suit of half plate.

**Items**
[Chain](/Equipment.aspx?ID=11) (30 feet), diving suit (functions as [half plate](/Armor.aspx?ID=49)), [Gauntlet](/Weapons.aspx?ID=4), [Javelin](/Weapons.aspx?ID=71)

</column>

---

<column gap="tiny">

<row gap="medium">
**AC** 23 

**Fort** +15 

**Ref** +7 

**Will** +12 

</row>

<row gap="medium">
**HP** 60

</row>

**Immunities**
gases and other [inhaled](/Traits.aspx?ID=634) effects

</column>

---

<column gap="tiny">

**Speed** 20 feet, swim 20 feet

**Melee**
<actions string="Single Action" />
gauntlet +15 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [Free-Hand](/Traits.aspx?ID=181)),
**Damage** 1d4+8 bludgeoning

**Ranged**
<actions string="Single Action" />
javelin +15 ([range 30 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=248), [Tethered](/Traits.aspx?ID=252)),
**Damage** 1d6+8 piercing

**Depth Charge** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([Air](/Traits.aspx?ID=5), [Manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104), [Sonic](/Traits.aspx?ID=147)) The marauder pulls a release valve on their suit, expelling a pressure wave that deals 3d6 sonic and 3d6 bludgeoning damage (DC 22 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Fortitude save) to all creatures in a 10-foot emanation. Creatures that fail the save take a –2 circumstance penalty to [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=34) checks to [Balance](/Actions.aspx?ID=2369) and [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) checks to [Swim](/Actions.aspx?ID=2381) for 1 minute as their inner ear is impaired. Creatures that critically fail the save are also [deafened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=66) for 1 minute. The marauder can't use Depth Charge again for 1d4 rounds.

**Retract** <actions string="Single Action" />  **Requirements** The marauder's last action was a successful javelin strike; **Effect** The marauder reels in a chain connected to the javelin, [pulling](/Rules.aspx?ID=451) the target up to 10 feet closer. They then Interact to return the javelin to their hand.

</column>

<title level="1" pfs="">[Taldan Cave Squirrel](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3315)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

Taldan cave squirrels, also known as tauhotis, are a curious cousin of the much smaller common ground squirrel, found anywhere with large, grassy flatlands. The creatures burrow underground, forming cave systems tall enough for giants in astonishingly little time. Once the caves are excavated, the squirrels turn their attention toward the largest quantities of gems or metals they can find—including those in the ground floors and vaults of nearby buildings. Nothing is off-limits, and no effort is too large when these squirrels go gem hunting.

 Cave squirrels' desire for these precious stones and ores arises not from greed, but rather productivity. After returning to the cave system, cheek pouches full of treasure, the males deposit the stolen goods before the females, who lick and spit on the piles of gems and metals to form them into structural pillars. Given the cave squirrels' tireless work habits, these pillars can solidify in a matter of hours, easily displacing existing stone and soil. Many an Opparan groundskeeper has stepped outside after a lovely teatime to find months of work undone in a scene of utter, glittering chaos. Architects throughout history have attempted to recreate or imitate these gleaming pillars; however, they rarely succeeded, for they often lacked a certain unpredictable pragmatism the cave squirrels seem to effortlessly achieve.

 When threatened, cave squirrels will let out a high-pitched scream to warn their colony. They can spit out any food or building materials in their cheek pouches with deadly speeds at attackers.

description:
Taldan cave squirrels, also known as tauhotis, are a curious cousin of the much smaller common ground squirrel, found anywhere with large, grassy flatlands. The creatures burrow underground, forming cave systems tall enough for giants in astonishingly little time. Once the caves are excavated, the squirrels turn their attention toward the largest quantities of gems or metals they can find—including those in the ground floors and vaults of nearby buildings. Nothing is off-limits, and no effort is too large when these squirrels go gem hunting.

 Cave squirrels' desire for these precious stones and ores arises not from greed, but rather productivity. After returning to the cave system, cheek pouches full of treasure, the males deposit the stolen goods before the females, who lick and spit on the piles of gems and metals to form them into structural pillars. Given the cave squirrels' tireless work habits, these pillars can solidify in a matter of hours, easily displacing existing stone and soil. Many an Opparan groundskeeper has stepped outside after a lovely teatime to find months of work undone in a scene of utter, glittering chaos. Architects throughout history have attempted to recreate or imitate these gleaming pillars; however, they rarely succeeded, for they often lacked a certain unpredictable pragmatism the cave squirrels seem to effortlessly achieve.

 When threatened, cave squirrels will let out a high-pitched scream to warn their colony. They can spit out any food or building materials in their cheek pouches with deadly speeds at attackers.

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

Tomb jellies are animate masses of protoplasm with a sickly combination of yellow, gray, and black hues. Their acidic bodies dissolve flesh but leave other materials, including a victim's gear and bones, intact. Some ancient cultures entombed bodies in stone sarcophagi with tomb jellies to allow the ooze to break down the flesh and clean and polish the bones.

<title level="1" pfs="Standard">[Venedaemon (Pact Daemon)](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2892)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

Those killed by magic or killed in the pursuit of magic can arise as venedaemons. Although among the weaker daemons, these robed figures can often be seen serving as researchers or clerks throughout the plane. Even within the mortal [Universe](/Planes.aspx?ID=26), scholars barter souls or arcane knowledge with venedaemons for their secrets and assistance.

<column gap="tiny">
**[Recall Knowledge - Fiend](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**
([Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46)): DC 20

**[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 18

**[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 15
</column>

</column>

<column gap="medium">
<image src="/images/Monsters/Venedaemon.webp" />
</column>

</row>

<title level="2" right="Creature 5">[Venedaemon](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2892)</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Medium" />
<trait label="Daemon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=568" />
<trait label="Fiend" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=600" />
<trait label="Unholy" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=521" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Monster Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=221) pg. 73 <sup>1.1</sup>

**Perception** +12; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59), smell magic ([imprecise](/Rules.aspx?ID=412)) 60 feet

**Languages**
[Aklo](/Languages.aspx?ID=13), [Chthonian](/Languages.aspx?ID=114), [Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1), [Daemonic](/Languages.aspx?ID=31), [Diabolic](/Languages.aspx?ID=117), [Draconic](/Languages.aspx?ID=2), [Requian](/Languages.aspx?ID=34); [telepathy](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=79) 100 feet

**Skills**
[Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=1) +13, [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=2) +16, [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5) +12, [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=11) +14, [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=13) +13, [Scribing Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8) +14

<row gap="medium">
**Str** +2

**Dex** +4

**Con** +2

**Int** +5

**Wis** +3

**Cha** +3
</row>

**Smell Magic** A venedaemon is aware of magical items and active spells as an imprecise sense. The subtle differences in these scents reveal the tradition and traits of the magic.

</column>

---

<column gap="tiny">

<row gap="medium">
**AC** 21 

**Fort** +9 

**Ref** +11 

**Will** +14 

+1 status to all saves vs. [magic](/Traits.aspx?ID=644)
</row>

<row gap="medium">
**HP** 75

</row>

**Immunities**
[death](/Traits.aspx?ID=571) effects

**Weaknesses**
[holy](/Traits.aspx?ID=517) 5

</column>

---

<column gap="tiny">

**Speed** 25 feet

**Melee**
<actions string="Single Action" />
tentacle +13 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [Finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=179), [Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103), [reach 10 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192), [Unholy](/Traits.aspx?ID=521)),
**Damage** 2d6+5 bludgeoning

**Arcane Spontaneous Spells** DC 22
- **Cantrips (3rd)**
[Electric Arc](/Spells.aspx?ID=97), [Shield](/Spells.aspx?ID=280), [Sigil](/Spells.aspx?ID=286), [Telekinetic Hand](/Spells.aspx?ID=1715), [Void Warp](/Spells.aspx?ID=1745)
- **1st**
[Enfeeble](/Spells.aspx?ID=1513), [Fear](/Spells.aspx?ID=110), [Force Barrage](/Spells.aspx?ID=1536), [Illusory Disguise](/Spells.aspx?ID=159) (4 slots)
- **2nd**
[Blazing Bolt](/Spells.aspx?ID=1450), [Dispel Magic](/Spells.aspx?ID=78), [Invisibility](/Spells.aspx?ID=164), [Noise Blast](/Spells.aspx?ID=1616) (4 slots)
- **3rd**
[Fireball](/Spells.aspx?ID=119), [Levitate](/Spells.aspx?ID=170), [Paralyze](/Spells.aspx?ID=213) (3 slots)

**Divine Innate Spells** DC 22
- **4th**
[Translocate](/Spells.aspx?ID=1724)

**Residual Force** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([Arcane](/Traits.aspx?ID=11), [Force](/Traits.aspx?ID=75)) **Requirements** The venedaemon's most recent action was to cast a spell; **Effect** Fading runes cling to the venedaemon's tentacles. The venedaemon makes a tentacle Strike that has a reach of 20 feet and deals 2d4 additional force damage.

**Soul Spell**   If a venedaemon ingest a soul gem from a [cacodaemon](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2891), they can recover an expended spell slot instead of gaining fast healing. The spell slot's rank can be no higher than half the level of the creature whose soul was consumed, rounded up.

**Twisted Whispers** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([Arcane](/Traits.aspx?ID=11), [Auditory](/Traits.aspx?ID=16), [Concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32), [Linguistic](/Traits.aspx?ID=101), [Mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=106)) The venedaemon whispers to a creature within 15 feet, which must succeed at a DC 22 Will save or be [stupefied 2](/Conditions.aspx?ID=94) for 1 minute (or stupefied 3 on a critical failure). Regardless of the results of the save, the creature is immune to Twisted Whispers for 24 hours.

</column>

The most common and numerous vescavors are the raving swarms. If left alone and unchecked, many believe they would eventually consume themselves once everything else in the immediate vicinity was consumed. What is even more vexing than their hunger is their song. While it sounds like gibberish at first, once bitten, the song will drive people into chaos. **[Recall Knowledge - Fiend](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46)): DC 20 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 18 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 15 [Vescavor Swarm](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3227) **Source** [Monster Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=221) pg. 338 1.1 **Perception** +11; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59) **Languages** [Chthonian](/Languages.aspx?ID=114) **Skills** [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=1) +13, [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) +10, [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15) +13 **Str** -2 **Dex** +5 **Con** +4 **Int** -3 **Wis** +1 **Cha** +1 --- **AC** 21 **Fort** +11 **Ref** +15 **Will** +9 **HP** 60 **Immunities** [grabbed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=77), precision, [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=88), [restrained](/Conditions.aspx?ID=90), [swarm mind](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=78) **Resistances** bludgeoning 5, piercing 5, slashing 2 **Weaknesses** area damage 5, [cold iron](/Equipment.aspx?ID=375) 5, [holy](/Traits.aspx?ID=517) 5, [splash](/Traits.aspx?ID=699) damage 5 --- **Speed** 20 feet, fly 40 feet **Devour All** The swarm eat away the very earth beneath their feet.  --- **Speed** 40 feet **Melee** hoof +13, **Damage** 2d6+6 bludgeoning **Gallop** The veteran war horse Strides twice. <title level="1" pfs="">[Vloriak (Despoiler Demon)](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2727)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

Vloriaks rise from the sinful souls of those whose acts of sabotage resulted in despair and terror, and they delight in the destruction of mortal artifice. Often called despoiler demons, vloriaks were the followers of Xar-Azmak. Their numbers have dwindled over the eons since the Lord of Rust's death; those that exist now are scattered throughout the [Abyss](/Planes.aspx?ID=13). Their chitinous bodies and faceted eyes give them an insectile appearance.

<column gap="tiny">
**[Recall Knowledge - Fiend](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**
([Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=13)): DC 22

**[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 20

**[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 17
</column>

</column>

<column gap="medium">
<image src="/images/Monsters/Demon_Vloriak.png" />
</column>

</row>

<title level="2" right="Creature 5">[Vloriak](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2727)</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="CE" url="/Rules.aspx?ID=95" />
<trait label="Medium" />
<trait label="Demon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=42" />
<trait label="Fiend" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=70" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Rusthenge](/Sources.aspx?ID=215) pg. 62

**Perception** +13; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=12)

**Languages**
[Abyssal](/Languages.aspx?ID=12), [Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1); [telepathy](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=37) 100 feet

**Skills**
[Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) +13, [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=7) +12

<row gap="medium">
**Str** +4

**Dex** +2

**Con** +4

**Int** -1

**Wis** +4

**Cha** +3
</row>

</column>

---

<column gap="tiny">

<row gap="medium">
**AC** 21 

**Fort** +15 

**Ref** +11 

**Will** +13 

+1 status to all saves vs. [magic](/Traits.aspx?ID=103)
</row>

<row gap="medium">
**HP** 90

</row>

**Resistances**
[acid](/Traits.aspx?ID=3) 5

**Weaknesses**
[cold iron](/Equipment.aspx?ID=272) 5, good 5

**Restoration Vulnerability** A vloriak suffers agonizing pain when a creature or object recovers from a debilitating effect in its proximity. The first time in a round in which a creature who is affected by a negative condition and is within sight of the demon reduces that condition's value, the demon takes 3d6 mental damage and cannot Lick Rust on its next turn.

</column>

---

<column gap="tiny">

**Speed** 25 feet

**Melee**
<actions string="Single Action" />
claw +15,
**Damage** 2d6+6 slashing plus 1d6 evil

**Melee**
<actions string="Single Action" />
tongue +15 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [reach 10 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)),
**Damage** 2d6 acid plus 1d6 evil and rust

**Divine Innate Spells** DC 22, attack +14
- **Cantrips (3rd)**
[Acid Splash](/Spells.aspx?ID=3)
- **2nd**
[Acid Arrow](/Spells.aspx?ID=2) (×3), [Shatter](/Spells.aspx?ID=279)
- **3rd**
[Paralyze](/Spells.aspx?ID=213)

**Lick Rust** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([Attack](/Traits.aspx?ID=15)) **Requirements** The vloriak rusted a metal item with its tongue this turn; **Effect** The vloriak attempts a tongue Strike on the same target it just attacked. If it hits, it deals no damage as it licks away the rust and heals 2d6 Hit Points (or 4d6 Hit Points if the Strike was a critical hit). It can't Lick Rust on its next turn.

**Rust**   A vloriak's saliva causes metal to rust rapidly. If it succeeds at a tongue Strike or [Disarm](/Actions.aspx?ID=41) attempt, the vloriak deals 2d6 damage (doubled on a critical hit) to a metal item the target is wearing or holding, ignoring its Hardness. If the vloriak hits an unattended metal item, the item takes this damage automatically. If a creature uses the [Shield Block](/Feats.aspx?ID=839) reaction with a metal shield against a tongue attack, the shield is automatically [broken](/Conditions.aspx?ID=2), but no other item is rusted on that attack.

**Spew Rusted Shards** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([Divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=48), [Evocation](/Traits.aspx?ID=65)) The vloriak spews a 15-foot cone of acid and rusted metal. Creatures in the area take 3d6 acid and 3d6 piercing damage (DC 22 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save). A creature that takes any piercing damage is exposed to [tetanus](/Diseases.aspx?ID=3). The vloriak can't Spew Rusted Shards for 1d4 rounds.

</column>

<title level="1" pfs="Standard">[Vordine (Infantry Devil)](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2906)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

The vast city of Dis trains endless legions of vordines to guard the upper layers of Hell and march across the planes at the archdevils' orders. Although quick to bend their knees to higher-ranking devils and even mortals favored by [Asmodeus](/Deities.aspx?ID=278), vordines are relentlessly cruel to [orts](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2905) and other devils they can call their subordinates.

 Although higher ranks in the infernal military are held by more powerful devils, like the nessari who serve as generals, a labyrinthine structure gives each vordine a rank and certain responsibilities. Some vordines are responsible for the battlefield command of squads, while others relay orders from above or are set to handling specific administrative tasks for their unit. The greatest gift one can offer a vordine is an increased rank to lord over other vordines.

A watchmage uses a mix of magic and martial training to enforce the law. They magically detect invisible criminals, locate stolen property, and counter illegal spells. **[Recall Knowledge - Humanoid](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=47)): DC 20 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 18 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 15 [Watchmage](/NPCs.aspx?ID=3559) **Source** [NPC Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=236) pg. 115 **Perception** +15 **Languages** [Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1) **Skills** [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35) +13, [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) +10, [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=40) +9, [Legal Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) +13, [Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=47) +11 **Str** +1 **Dex** +4 **Con** +2 **Int** +4 **Wis** +1 **Cha** +0 **Arcane Watch** The watchmage can either [Investigate](/Actions.aspx?ID=2627) or [Search](/Actions.aspx?ID=2630) while using the [Detect Magic](/Actions.aspx?ID=2624) exploration activity. **Items** [Leather Armor](/Armor.aspx?ID=4), [Shortbow](/Weapons.aspx?ID=77) (20 arrows), spellbook (contains all prepared spells plus [_earthbind_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1506), [_revealing light_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1653), [_sleep_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1675), and [_tailwind_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1711)) --- **AC** 21 **Fort** +9 **Ref** +12 **Will** +14 **HP** 70 **Counter Escape** ([arcane](/Traits.aspx?ID=534)) **Trigger** A creature Casts a Spell with the [teleportation](/Traits.aspx?ID=710) trait or as a reaction; **Effect** The watchmage expends a spell slot of the same rank or higher as the trigger creature's spell and attempts to [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) the triggering spell (counteract modifier +11). --- **Speed** 25 feet **Melee** fist +15 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [Finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=179), [Nonlethal](/Traits.aspx?ID=188), [Unarmed](/Traits.aspx?ID=199)), **Damage** 1d6+5 bludgeoning **Ranged** shortbow +15 ([deadly d10](/Traits.aspx?ID=174), [Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103), [range increment 60 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=248)), **Damage** 1d6+4 piercing plus 1d6 force **Arcane Prepared Spells** DC 20, attack +12 - **Cantrips (3rd)** [Detect Magic](/Spells.aspx?ID=66), [Frostbite](/Spells.aspx?ID=1539), [Ignition](/Spells.aspx?ID=1565), [Read Aura](/Spells.aspx?ID=246), [Tangle Vine](/Spells.aspx?ID=1713) - **1st** [Command](/Spells.aspx?ID=45), [Force Barrage](/Spells.aspx?ID=1536), [Sure Strike](/Spells.aspx?ID=1709) - **2nd** [Dispel Magic](/Spells.aspx?ID=78), [See the Unseen](/Spells.aspx?ID=1663) - **3rd** [Haste](/Spells.aspx?ID=147), [Slow](/Spells.aspx?ID=289) **Eldritch Arms** ([Concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32)) In a brief ritual that takes 10 minutes, the watchmage chooses a single weapon or unarmed attack through which they can focus their magic. Strikes the watchmage makes with that weapon are magical and deal 1d6 additional force damage. **Spellbound Strike** **Requirements** The watchmage is wielding the weapon chosen with Eldritch Arms; **Effect** The watchmage Casts a Spell that takes 1 or 2 actions to cast, imbuing that spell into the weapon. The watchmage Strikes with the required weapon. This counts as two attacks for the watchmage's multiple attack penalty. On a hit, the target is also affected by the spell, though the target gets any normal defenses allowed by the spell.
If the spell is targeted, it targets the creature that was hit and no one else. If the spell is an area, the target must be in the area. A burst is centered on a corner of the target's square if the target is Medium or smaller, or the corner of a square closest to the creature's center if it's Large or larger. A cone or line emits from a square of the watchmage's choice adjacent to the target.

Nearly a myth, a yeti is rarely seen—and even when it is, it is often too late. Yetis dwell amid the highest, most remote peaks of the world, coming down from their snowy mountain holds to raid, steal livestock, and sometimes feed their insatiable urges for slaughter and destruction. Those folks who live at the foot of a yeti-ruled mountain warn of the “abominable snowmen”: monstrous, fur-covered humanoids who leave strange and bloody tracks in the snow. In actuality, most yetis protect the world rather than hunt its other denizens, guarding eldritch portals that link the mortal Universe and other, much stranger dimensions of reality. From within these snow-covered arches and ancient stone doorways, aliens, living nightmares, fiends, and worse can emerge into the world. Yetis who guard these portals sometimes succumb to the horrors within, taking on the bloodthirsty urges and horrific behaviors of the very monsters they strive to guard against. Driven out of their clans and forced to wander alone, they give rise to the myth of the abominable snowman. These exiled yetis often fully embrace the corrupting elements that caused their exile in the first place, growing more powerful and more deadly. **[Recall Knowledge - Humanoid](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=47)): DC 22 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 20 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 17 [Yeti](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3247) **Source** [Monster Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=221) pg. 354 1.1 **Perception** +15; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59), [scent](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=74) ([imprecise](/Rules.aspx?ID=412)) 30 feet **Languages** [Aklo](/Languages.aspx?ID=13) **Skills** [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) +14, [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15) +12, [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=16) +11 **Str** +5 **Dex** +2 **Con** +4 **Int** -1 **Wis** +4 **Cha** -1 **Snowblind** When [Hiding](/Actions.aspx?ID=2404), the yeti is [concealed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=62) by any snowfall, even if it's not thick enough to make other creatures concealed. --- **AC** 21 **Fort** +15 **Ref** +11 **Will** +13 +4 status to all saves vs. [fear](/Traits.aspx?ID=598) and [dreams](/Traits.aspx?ID=582) **HP** 115 **Immunities** [cold](/Traits.aspx?ID=555) **Weaknesses** [fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=604) 10 **Nightmare Guardian** Yetis gain a +4 status bonus to saves against fear and against spells and abilities that affect dreams. A yeti who falls prey to a supernatural nightmare loses this ability and becomes permanently enraged, gaining a +1 status bonus to attack and damage rolls and a –1 status penalty to AC.
**Vanish** **Trigger** The yeti is [hidden](/Conditions.aspx?ID=79) or [undetected](/Conditions.aspx?ID=96) while not in combat, and a creature would observe it; **Effect** The yeti Strides or [Climbs](/Actions.aspx?ID=2374) up to half its Speed to a location where it can Hide, then Hides. If its new [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=48) check result meets or exceeds the triggering creature's Perception DC, the yeti remains hidden. --- **Speed** 35 feet, climb 20 feet; arctic passage **Melee** claw +15, **Damage** 2d10+5 slashing **Arctic Passage** The yeti ignores [difficult terrain](/Rules.aspx?ID=453) caused by ice or snow. **Grisly Arrival** ([Emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=60), [Fear](/Traits.aspx?ID=68), [Mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=106)) **Trigger** The yeti hits a creature in the first round of combat and the yeti was [hidden](/Conditions.aspx?ID=79) from that creature at the start of combat; **Effect** Each enemy within 30 feet that witnesses the attack (including the target of the attack) must attempt a DC 23 Will save. On a failure, the creature is [frightened 2](/Conditions.aspx?ID=76); on a critical failure, it's frightened 4. **[Rend](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=73)** claw

<title level="1" pfs="">[Alyce Quinley, Conflicted Champion](/NPCs.aspx?ID=3699)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

Alyce Quinley was born in the wilds of the Darkmoon Vale region in north-central Andoran. Her father, Erasmus Quinley, belongs to the Greenfire Circle, an order of druids in the Arthfell Forest who serve as intermediaries between the Vale's humans and fey. Her mother, Vandra Steiggerson, is a legacy member of the Fangwatch, a reclusive group of rangers dedicated to protecting Arthfell Forest locals from its many dangerous denizens, chiefly a large population of werewolves. Raised alongside other children of the Circle, Alyce and her peers grew up among the beasts and guardians of the wilderness, learning to spot, track, and stalk prey through the forest with a patient lethality.

 Alyce's father saw to most her needs, for her mother's patrols often ranged far from home for weeks at a time. Erasmus expected Alyce to follow in his footsteps, becoming a druid. However, he soon realized her talents lay elsewhere. By the time she reached adulthood, she had already distinguished herself as a messenger, scout, and envoy, earning friends throughout the region, including Andoran's frontier military forces. This included the Diamond Regiment, a frontier force tasked with guarding the roads (and valuable duskwood shipments) leading from Darkmoon Vale.

 It was in the course of delivering messages that Alyce learned of Eagle Knight Kelvan Drost, sole survivor of a recent hobgoblin ambush in northern Arthfell. The hobgoblins had grown tired of Drost after realizing their prisoner wouldn't surrender the information they wanted. Alyce realized that they would execute Drost soon, so she scouted the area, infiltrated the camp, dispatched the guards, and spirited the wounded prisoner to safety before anyone noticed anything amiss. Her actions earned her a special invitation from the Diamond Regiment's commander, commending her bravery and formally offering training and membership to Alyce.

 Over a decade later, having proven her mettle performing dozens of missions all across Andoran, Alyce serves the Diamond Regiment as ranking military officer in the city of Bellis, a remote settlement buried in the Verduran Forest on Andoran's far northeastern border. While few Diamond Regiment personnel are stationed so far from Darkmoon Vale, Alyce's Greenfire Circle background has equipped her to negotiate with druids, fey, and other forest folk. This will be her third year representing Andoran at the annual Greenwood Gala, and as much as she privately resents serving as the public face of the despicable Lumber Consortium, it's still a pleasant diversion from her day-to-day duties to assist the Bellisian militia in maintaining order, despite the best efforts of the city's large transient population of unruly lumberjacks.

 Alyce is a woman between two worlds in some ways, but she doesn't see it that way. She feels like she uses her deep knowledge of and experience with the wilderness to her advantage while serving her country. Many of her kin and friends don't fully recognize the Andoren state, and are content to live their lives hidden by the dense foliage of the forest. Alyce, however recognizes that the reach of Andoran is inevitable and the best way to make sure that the nation interacts with the wild in the best possible way is to put someone between these two worlds that have the wild in their best interest—a role she's happy to play. Alyce can come off as standoffish or too direct, but that's just her defense against the risk of giving too much away. In her daily life she has to negotiate between groups that are often diametrically opposed, and giving too much of yourself away in negotiations only leads to failure and exploitation.

 Raised as she was, Alyce has a fondness for athletic pursuits, particularly lone ones where she can test her own capabilities. Her childhood love for climbing trees or going on days-long hikes just to reach a particular point and then return home has carried over to her adult life. In the rare times she's not burdened by responsibility, Alyce goes on “a wander” by herself for days, or even weeks, at a time. It's during these wanders that she catches up with friends from her childhood and others she's met during her life. 

<title level="2" right="">Campaign Role</title> When the PCs first encounter Alyce in Chapter 1, she's on a diplomatic mission representing Andoren  interests at the Greenwood Gala and keeping a watchful eye on the other attendees so as to suss out any potential threats to those interests. Unlike Taldor, Andoran is not a signatory of the Treaty of the Wildwood, and its logging operations not officially under the Lodge's protection. Those operations have rapidly expanded in recent months to meet the ravenous shipbuilding industry's demands, driven by growing fears of imminent war with Cheliax. Complicating matters further, the infamously underhanded Lumber Consortium maintaining its stranglehold on Andoran's lumber industry continues to act with flagrant lack of regard for how its activities might provoke forest folk. Although disgusted by the Consortium leadership's unscrupulous behavior, Alyce remains well aware of the vital role they play in Andoren national security and the necessity of defending their operations, placing her in the unenviable position of having to attend the Gala as the unofficial representative of one of the Verduran Forest's most despised institutions.

 Alyce is initially standoffish and curt, expecting Gala attendees to regard her with the same loathing they have for the Consortium itself. If the PCs get past her defenses, they should come to see her as a potential ally, as her personal goals likely align with theirs more than expected. When they encounter her again in Chapter 2, they'll have the opportunity to help her resolve a crisis threatening both the interests she's sworn to protect and the overall stability of the region, further intertwining their loyalties. By the end of Chapter 3, she should be fully cemented as a supporter of their cause, having both witnessed firsthand the threat posed by Ruzadoya's Lodge and fought alongside the PCs to escape it.

 Alyce is an accomplished warrior, and won't hesitate to enter the fray if a fight breaks out in her presence. Although her title as an Eagle Knight holds little sway in the depths of the Verduran Forest, she'll use her position and authority to assist the PCs' efforts in any way possible should opportunities arise.

verduran forest on andoran's far northeastern border. while few diamond regiment personnel are stationed so far from darkmoon vale, alyce's greenfire circle background has equipped her to negotiate with druids, fey, and other forest folk. this will be her third year representing andoran at the annual greenwood gala, and as much as she privately resents serving as the public face of the despicable lumber consortium, it's still a pleasant diversion from her day-to-day duties to assist the bellisian militia in maintaining order, despite the best efforts of the city's large transient population of unruly lumberjacks. alyce is a woman between two worlds in some ways, but she doesn't see it that way. she feels like she uses her deep knowledge of and experience with the wilderness to her advantage while serving her country. many of her kin and friends don't fully recognize the andoren state, and are content to live their lives hidden by the dense foliage of the forest. alyce, however recognizes that the reach of andoran is inevitable and the best way to make sure that the nation interacts with the wild in the best possible way is to put someone between these two worlds that have the wild in their best interest—a role she's happy to play. alyce can come off as standoffish or too direct, but that's just her defense against the risk of giving too much away. in her daily life she has to negotiate between groups that are often diametrically opposed, and giving too much of yourself away in negotiations only leads to failure and exploitation. raised as she was, alyce has a fondness for athletic pursuits, particularly lone ones where she can test her own capabilities. her childhood love for climbing trees or going on days-long hikes just to reach a particular point and then return home has carried over to her adult life. in the rare times she's not burdened by responsibility, alyce goes on “a wander” by herself for days, or even weeks, at a time. it's during these wanders that she catches up with friends from her childhood and others she's met during her life. campaign role when the pcs first encounter alyce in chapter 1, she's on a diplomatic mission representing andoren interests at the greenwood gala and keeping a watchful eye on the other attendees so as to suss out any potential threats to those interests. unlike taldor, andoran is not a signatory of the treaty of the wildwood, and its logging operations not officially under the lodge's protection. those operations have rapidly expanded in recent months to meet the ravenous shipbuilding industry's demands, driven by growing fears of imminent war with cheliax. complicating matters further, the infamously underhanded lumber consortium maintaining its stranglehold on andoran's lumber industry continues to act with flagrant lack of regard for how its activities might provoke forest folk. although disgusted by the consortium leadership's unscrupulous behavior, alyce remains well aware of the vital role they play in andoren national security and the necessity of defending their operations, placing her in the unenviable position of having to attend the gala as the unofficial representative of one of the verduran forest's most despised institutions. alyce is initially standoffish and curt, expecting gala attendees to regard her with the same loathing they have for the consortium itself. if the pcs get past her defenses, they should come to see her as a potential ally, as her personal goals likely align with theirs more than expected. when they encounter her again in chapter 2, they'll have the opportunity to help her resolve a crisis threatening both the interests she's sworn to protect and the overall stability of the region, further intertwining their loyalties. by the end of chapter 3, she should be fully cemented as a supporter of their cause, having both witnessed firsthand the threat posed by ruzadoya's lodge and fought alongside the pcs to escape it. alyce is an accomplished warrior, and won't hesitate to enter the fray if a fight breaks out in her presence. although her title as an eagle knight holds little sway in the depths of the verduran forest, she'll use her position and authority to assist the pcs' efforts in any way possible should opportunities arise. recall knowledge - humanoid (society): dc 32 unspecific lore : dc 30 fort +15 ref +11 will +14 hp 95 liberating strike reaction requirements alyce is wielding a melee weapon; trigger a creature within alyce's reach attempts to apply the grabbed, immobilized, or restrained condition to an ally; effect alyce makes a melee strike against the triggering creature. if the attack is a hit, the triggering ally can immediately use a reaction to escape. if the attack is a critical hit, any grabbed, immobilized, or restrained conditions imposed by the triggering action are negated. reactive strike reaction --- speed 30 feet melee single action rapier +17 (deadly 1d8, disarm, magical), damage 2d6+6 piercing ranged single action crossbow +16 (range increment 120 feet, reload 1), damage 1d8+8 piercing hunt prey single action (concentrate) alyce designates a single creature as her prey and focuses her attacks against that creature. she must be able to see, hear, or otherwise detect the prey, or she must be tracking the prey during exploration. she gains a +2 circumstance bonus to perception checks when she seeks her prey and a +2 circumstance bonus to survival checks when she tracks her prey. alyce also ignores the penalty for making ranged attacks within her second range increment against the prey she's hunting. alyce can only have one creature designated as her prey at a time. if she uses hunt prey against a creature when she already has a creature designated, the prior creature loses the designation and the new prey gains the designation. her designation lasts until her next daily preparations.

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

Squat, heavily armored quadrupeds, ankylosauruses are stubborn and irascible. Although they're herbivores, ankylosauruses have been known to attack trespassers simply out of ill temper. Ankylosauruses have few natural predators, as their bony hides are covered in spiked nubs that jut in many different directions to discourage larger creatures from biting them. An ankylosaurus is about 30 feet long, 10 feet tall at the shoulder, and weighs over 3 tons.

Arboreal regents and other wielders of powerful primal magic grant temporary sentience to trees in order to protect the forest. Invested with a workable set of instincts and the ability to mobilize and attack, these awakened trees follow the commands of their master and fight to protect their home. markdown:
Big boss goblins order members of their band around and deal with any longshanks they come across—sometimes via violence or diplomacy, and sometimes by ordering another goblin to deal with them (in ways that the big boss goblin approves of if they work or claims were awful ideas they never would have tried if they don't). These goblin leaders often insist on impressive titles or sobriquets like “The Exceedingly Incendiary,” “Snake Singer,” or “Most Gluttonest,” though these can often be exaggerated by several degrees for dramatic effect or even change at the big boss goblin's whim (often to one-up a rival). **[Recall Knowledge - Humanoid](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=47)): DC 22 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 20 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 17 [Big Boss Goblin](/NPCs.aspx?ID=3643) **Source** [NPC Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=236) pg. 188 **Perception** +16; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59) **Languages** [Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1), [Goblin](/Languages.aspx?ID=6) **Skills** [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) +15, [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39) +13, [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=40) +15, [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=48) +11 **Str** +3 **Dex** +1 **Con** +3 **Int** +1 **Wis** +1 **Cha** +3 **Items** [battered crown](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1667) (or other symbol of authority), [Hide Armor](/Armor.aspx?ID=7), _+1 [horsechopper](/Weapons.aspx?ID=409)_, [Shortbow](/Weapons.aspx?ID=77) (20 arrows) --- **AC** 22 **Fort** +17 **Ref** +11 **Will** +14 **HP** 100 **[Reactive Strike](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=48)**
**Not Me!** ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Trigger** The big boss goblin is targeted with an attack, and a [goblin](/Traits.aspx?ID=618) is adjacent to them; **Effect** The big boss goblin yanks the goblin in front of the attack to face the consequences in their stead. The big boss goblin gains a +2 circumstance bonus to their AC against the triggering attack. If it hits, the big boss goblin takes half damage, and the other goblin takes the remaining half. --- **Speed** 25 feet **Melee** _horsechopper_ +17 ([Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103), [reach 10 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192), [Trip](/Traits.aspx?ID=196), [versatile P](/Traits.aspx?ID=200)), **Damage** 1d8+5 slashing **Melee** jaws +15 ([Finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=179), [Unarmed](/Traits.aspx?ID=199)), **Damage** 1d6+5 piercing **Ranged** shortbow +14 ([deadly 1d10](/Traits.aspx?ID=174), [range increment 60 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=248), [reload 0](/Traits.aspx?ID=254)), **Damage** 1d6+2 piercing **No Fight Fair** A big boss goblin fights dirty, slashing at a foe's hamstrings. Whenever the big boss goblin hits an [off-guard](/Conditions.aspx?ID=58) foe, the creature takes a –5-foot status penalty to its speed (–10-foot on a critical hit) until the creature regains any amount of Hit Points. As with all penalties to Speed, this can't reduce a creature's Speed below 5 feet. **Stab it! Stab it! Stab it!** The big boss goblin picks a target they can see within 30 feet and orders any allied goblins to attack. A single [goblin](/Traits.aspx?ID=618) with a lower level than the big boss goblin that is adjacent to the target can immediately use their reaction to Strike the target. In addition, until the start of the big boss goblin's next turn, their attacks against that target deal 1 additional damage dice as the big boss goblin leads them.

<title level="1" pfs="">[Bone Mother](/NPCs.aspx?ID=3669)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

The bone mother—a warren's oracle—cuts an imposing figure. Bone mothers can be any gender despite the name, wearing the skull of a giant rat and covering their clothing in dangling bones. When a member of the warren dies, they gift a bone (usually a finger bone) to the oracle, who exists as both a physical repository of those who came before and a living history of their warren.

<column gap="tiny">

**Swarming**   A ysoki can end their movement in the same square as an ally that also has this ability. Only two such creatures can share the same space.

</column>

The captain of the guard leads a troop of soldiers who serve as security forces for a powerful individual, most often a high-ranking noble or very rich merchant, though this stat block could also represent a lower-ranking captain of the guard for the leader of a nation. A formidable opponent in their own right, the captain of the guard skillfully employs their troops to protect the life and health of their ward. **[Recall Knowledge - Humanoid](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=47)): DC 22 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 20 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 17 [Captain of the Guard](/NPCs.aspx?ID=3560) **Source** [NPC Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=236) pg. 115 **Perception** +15 **Languages** [Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1) **Skills** [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) +15, [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39) +11, [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=40) +13, [Legal Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) +12, [Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=47) +10, [Warfare Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) +8 **Str** +5 **Dex** +0 **Con** +2 **Int** +0 **Wis** +3 **Cha** +3 **Items** [Crossbow](/Weapons.aspx?ID=67) (20 bolts), [Dagger](/Weapons.aspx?ID=3), [Full Plate](/Armor.aspx?ID=13), _+1 [longsword](/Weapons.aspx?ID=386)_, [Steel Shield](/Shields.aspx?ID=3) (Hardness 5, HP 20, BT 10) --- **AC** 24 (26 with shield raised) **Fort** +14 **Ref** +12 **Will** +15 **HP** 95 **Aura of Command** ([aura](/Traits.aspx?ID=542), [emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=590), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647)) 30 feet. The captain of the guard bolsters lower-level guards under their command, granting them a +1 status bonus to their attack rolls and a +2 status bonus to their Will saves.
**Bravery** When the captain rolls a success on a Will save against a [fear](/Traits.aspx?ID=598) effect, they get a critical success instead. In addition, any time they gain the [frightened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=76) condition, reduce its value by 1.
**Shield Warden** When the captain has their shield raised, they can [Shield Block](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=75) when an attack is made against an adjacent ally. If they do, the shield prevents that ally from taking damage instead of the captain.
**[Reactive Strike](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=48)**
**[Shield Block](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=75)** --- **Speed** 20 feet **Melee** _longsword_ +18 ([Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103), [versatile P](/Traits.aspx?ID=200)), **Damage** 1d8+11 slashing **Melee** fist +17 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [Nonlethal](/Traits.aspx?ID=188), [Unarmed](/Traits.aspx?ID=199)), **Damage** 1d4+11 bludgeoning **Ranged** crossbow +12 ([range increment 120 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=248), [reload 1](/Traits.aspx?ID=254)), **Damage** 1d8+6 piercing **Shielded Advance** **Requirements** The captain of the guard has their shield raised; **Effect** The captain of the guard presses forward, using their shield to push back foes. The captain Strides and [Shoves](/Actions.aspx?ID=2380), in either order. The multiple attack penalty doesn't apply to this Shove, though the Shove does count toward the captain's multiple attack penalty.

<title level="1" pfs="Standard">[Carved Beast](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2675)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

An untold number of stumps carved into roughly hewn animal shapes roam the [Plane of Wood](/Planes.aspx?ID=25). The statue portion of these carved beasts is incapable of articulated movement, though the living wood at their base is fully animate. When left to their own devices, carved beasts prefer to roughly mimic the behaviors of the animals they resemble, like children playing with inarticulate toys.

<column gap="tiny">
**[Recall Knowledge - Elemental](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**
([Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=2), [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=10)): DC 22

**[Recall Knowledge - Plant](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**

<title level="1" pfs="Standard">[Cave Bear](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2851)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

Larger, stronger, and far more aggressive than its smaller cousins, the cave bear is a behemoth that avoids civilized lands, preferring to dwell in remote places. As its name might suggest, the cave bear makes its den in natural caves, and like the grizzly bear, it is fiercely territorial. Unlike a grizzly bear, however, a cave bear is short tempered and will make sure its foe is dead before moving on, usually feasting on its prey's soft flesh once it has been incapacitated. Cave bears are often regarded as powerful guardian spirits by remote-dwelling people, though they are also utilized as beasts of war by [orc](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=454) or even [giants](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=420). [Stone giants](/Monsters.aspx?ID=221) in particular have an affinity for keeping trained cave bears as pets or guardians for their homes.

<column gap="tiny">

([Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43)): DC 22

<title level="1" pfs="Standard">[Choral (Choir Angel)](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2815)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

Choral angels are incredible singers who fill the halls of [Nirvana](/Planes.aspx?ID=44) with pious chants and sacred hymns. Most form from the souls of talented bards and other performers, though anyone who takes superlative joy in music might ascend to their ranks. Though their duties are typically to spread peace and joy through their music, their holy incantations also brim with mystic purpose, their songs bolstering angelic wards and strengthening the very fabric of the celestial planes themselves.

 While choral angels shy away from conflict, they will brave the mortal realm to deliver good omens and auspicious messages. Choral angels often serve the goddess [Shelyn](/Deities.aspx?ID=293), but they can also serve other good deities and empyreal lords.

Drthaks are aquatic predators with long trailing fins that are rarely seen, clinging to coasts and estuaries where the high silt content makes them practically invisible to predators and prey alike. Some have been known to come inland, tracking their prey miles upriver before striking. The underwater environment alters the typical dischoran hunting behavior, with drthaks creating bubbles that implode to stun prey. **[Recall Knowledge - Beast](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35), [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43)): DC 22 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 20 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 17 [Drthak](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3268) **Source** [Howl of the Wild](/Sources.aspx?ID=226) pg. 140 2.1 **Perception** +15; no vision, sensitive echolocation ([precise](/Rules.aspx?ID=411)) 120 feet **Languages** **Skills** [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) +16, [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=48) +17, [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=49) +13 **Str** +4 **Dex** +5 **Con** +4 **Int** -3 **Wis** +3 **Cha** -1 **Deep Breath** The drthak can [hold its breath](/Rules.aspx?ID=2436) for about 2 hours.
**Sensitive Echolocation** The drthak can use its hearing as a [precise sense](/Rules.aspx?ID=411) with the listed range. If the drthak takes sonic damage beyond its resistance, its senses are overloaded and all creatures are [concealed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=62) from it for 1 round. --- **AC** 23 **Fort** +14 **Ref** +17 **Will** +11 **HP** 110 **Immunities** [visual](/Traits.aspx?ID=727) **Auditory Hunter** **Trigger** A creature within 15 feet uses an [auditory](/Traits.aspx?ID=541) action; **Effect** The drthak Strides or [Swims](/Actions.aspx?ID=2381) towards the creature. --- **Speed** 20 feet, swim 40 feet **Melee** jaws +16, **Damage** 2d8+4 piercing plus [Grab](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=45) **Ranged** screech +17 ([range 60 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=248), [Sonic](/Traits.aspx?ID=147)), **Damage** 4d6 sonic plus resonant jaws **Bubble Burst** ([Sonic](/Traits.aspx?ID=147), [Water](/Traits.aspx?ID=165)) **Requirement** The drthak is underwater; **Effect** The drthak uses sonic power to push aside water in a 30-foot emanation, which then collapses in a crushing torrent. All creatures in the area, other than the drthak, take 3d10 bludgeoning damage (DC 24 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Fortitude save). **Pull Under** The drthak can [Swim](/Actions.aspx?ID=2381) at half Speed while it has a creature [grabbed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=77) or [restrained](/Conditions.aspx?ID=90) in its jaws, carrying the creature along with it. **Resonant Jaws** When the drthak misses a screech Strike against a creature [grabbed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=77) or [restrained](/Conditions.aspx?ID=90) in its jaws, it deals that creature 2d6 sonic damage.

Dwarven soldiers make formidable units, capable of holding their own against most enemies. In combat, a dwarf battalion is a well-oiled machine, unleashing coordinated attacks against foes. **[Recall Knowledge - Humanoid](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=47)): DC 22 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 20 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 17 [Dwarf Battalion](/NPCs.aspx?ID=3628) **Source** [NPC Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=236) pg. 175 **Perception** +13; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59) **Languages** [Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1), [Dwarven](/Languages.aspx?ID=3) **Skills** [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) +15, [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=49) +13, [Warfare Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) +11 **Str** +5 **Dex** +1 **Con** +4 **Int** +0 **Wis** +3 **Cha** -1 --- **AC** 22 **Fort** +16 **Ref** +11 **Will** +13 **HP** 105 (4 segments) **Weaknesses** area damage 5, [splash](/Traits.aspx?ID=699) damage 5 **Dwarven Doughtiness** Dwarves are often calm and collected in the face of imminent danger. At the end of the battalion's turn, reduce its [frightened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=76) condition by 2 instead of 1.
**[Troop Defenses](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=44)**
**[Reactive Strike](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=48)**
**[Shield Block](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=75)** --- **Speed** 20 feet; [troop movement](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=85) **Bombing Barrage** The dwarf battalion draws alchemical bombs, then hurls them at distant foes. This volley is a 10-foot burst within 60 feet that deals 3d6 damage with a DC 21 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save. The damage is either acid, fire, or electricity damage, depending on which type of bombs the battalion used. When the dwarf battalion is reduced to 2 or fewer segments, this area decreases to a 5-foot burst. **Coordinated Pummel** Frequency once per round; Effect The dwarf battalion unleashes a storm of warhammer blows against each enemy in a 5-foot emanation (DC 21 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save). The damage depends on the number of actions.
1d8 bludgeoning damage

<title level="1" pfs="Standard">[Elananx](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2972)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

These strange, fey felines resemble large, broad bobcats from a distance, but a closer view reveals something amiss. Their forms ripple and billow with heat, and their eyes glow from within as if they contained tiny, flickering flames. The pungent scent of rotting leaves smoldering in a bonfire clings to their fur. Yet those who have the chance to watch elananxes hunt or attack prey witness the greatest indication that these creatures are something more than mere predators, for they act with cruel and savvy instincts, reveling in the pain they inflict.

 Elananxes typically hunt alone, but sometimes these cunning and malicious hunters of the [First World](/Planes.aspx?ID=35) roam in packs called billows to take down large prey. Like many house cats, elananxes are not content to merely track and devour prey, but prefer to toy with their victims, drawing joy from the fear and pain of those they capture. To this end, elananxes rarely use their cinder dispersal ability to evade their targets, instead opting to foil their quarry just before the end of the hunt—though, as selfish creatures who wish to live to hunt again, elananxes often reserve one use of this ability, just in case.

 Because of their clever and malicious ways, elananxes are favored as hunting companions by [redcaps](/Monsters.aspx?ID=349), who go out of their way to befriend or make deals with these creatures. Redcaps also find great sport in hunts where competing elananxes chase a single creature. Although they're large enough to serve as mounts for redcaps, elananxes despise being ridden and resist such attempts—little is as sure to cause a supposedly friendly elananx to turn on its redcap ally as a foolhardy attempt to treat the fey cat as a horse!

 Elananxes have a strange affinity with forest fires. Because they are immune to the damage caused by flickering flames, they enjoy capering and caterwauling through the smoky, burning ruins of forest infernos. Some have even been known to use their burning bites to deliberately light undergrowth on fire, simply so they might experience the beauty of the flames combined with the inevitable pain such disasters inflict on other creatures.

**Cinder Dispersal** <actions string="Reaction" /> ([fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=604), [primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=676)) **Frequency** once per day; **Trigger** The elananx takes damage from a hostile source; **Effect** The elananx disperses into a cloud of smoke and cinders, filling its space and a 20-foot emanation. While in this form, the elananx can't be attacked or targeted, and it doesn't take up space. Anything inside this cloud is [concealed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=62), and any creature ending its turn there takes 2d6 fire damage. At the start of its turn, the elananx returns to its normal form in any square the cloud covered. If the elananx Strikes a creature using its first action after returning to its normal form, the target is [off-guard](/Conditions.aspx?ID=58) and the Strike deals an extra 1d6 fire damage.

**Mark for Death** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([Concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32)) The executioner marks a single creature they can see for death. Few are as prepared to be unprepared as a gadgeteer, who are masters at building seemingly impossible creations out of almost anything. They're always useful to have when a plan inevitably goes wrong because they can quickly craft the perfect tool needed to get out of even the stickiest predicament. Every now and again, someone tries to hire a gadgeteer to perfect a single design to replicate it and make more permanent versions of their thrown-together gadgets. This effort is often in vain, as even the most talented gadgeteers are unlikely to perfectly replicate a design they made in the moment, even with the same materials. In fact, when put on the spot, they will likely create a functional gadget differently every time, even if they have access to the same material. This process makes duplication nearly impossible. **[Recall Knowledge - Humanoid](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=47)): DC 22 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 20 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 17 [Gadgeteer](/NPCs.aspx?ID=3462) **Source** [NPC Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=236) pg. 46 **Perception** +14 **Languages** [Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1) **Skills** [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=37) +16, [Engineering Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) +18, [Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=47) +12, [Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=50) +14 **Str** +1 **Dex** +4 **Con** +1 **Int** +4 **Wis** +2 **Cha** +0 **Gadget Specialist** For encounters involving crafting gadgets, the gadgeteer is a 9th-level challenge. **Items** bag of junk, [Crossbow](/Weapons.aspx?ID=67) (10 bolts), heavy wrench (functions as a [mace](/Weapons.aspx?ID=362)), [Leather Armor](/Armor.aspx?ID=4) --- **AC** 23 **Fort** +11 **Ref** +16 **Will** +14 **HP** 95 --- **Speed** 25 feet **Melee** fist +16 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [Finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=179), [Nonlethal](/Traits.aspx?ID=188), [Unarmed](/Traits.aspx?ID=199)), **Damage** 1d4+7 bludgeoning **Melee** heavy wrench +13 ([Shove](/Traits.aspx?ID=193)), **Damage** 1d6+7 bludgeoning **Ranged** crossbow +16 ([range increment 120 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=248), [reload 1](/Traits.aspx?ID=254)), **Damage** 1d8+6 piercing **Create Gadget** ([Concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32), [Manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104)) The gadgeteer uses their bag of junk and nearby scraps to create one of the following gadgets. Gadgets created this way fall apart after a single use or after 1 hour, whichever happens first.
  • **Flash Bang** ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) The gadgeteer throws a flash bang up to 20 feet away that explodes in a 5-foot burst. Creatures in the burst must succeed a DC 24 Fortitude save or become [blinded](/Conditions.aspx?ID=59) for 1 round.
  • **Glider** ([move](/Traits.aspx?ID=658)) The gadgeteer leaps off a precipice with the glider in their hands. They fall only 60 feet per round, and for every 10 feet they fall, they can travel 5 feet forward.
  • **Makeshift Key** ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) The gadgeteer attempts to [Pick a Lock](/Actions.aspx?ID=2412) with a +4 item bonus to the check.
  • **Recorder** ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) The gadgeteer records up to 25 spoken words on this device. Activating this gadget causes it to either repeat the recorded words once before falling apart or play the message on a loop for up to 10 minutes before falling apart.
  • **Shocking Rod** ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) An adjacent creature takes 3d12 electricity damage with a DC 24 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save.

Gamekeepers know every beast that walks, slithers, flies, or swims in their territory and where to find them; try to keep up with the pack if you think you can. The land has chosen these people as guardians, giving them mysterious powers while in their territory. They are prepared to keep balance. **[Recall Knowledge - Humanoid](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=47)): DC 22 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 20 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 17 [Gamekeeper](/NPCs.aspx?ID=3475) **Source** [NPC Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=236) pg. 56 **Perception** +14 **Languages** [Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1) **Skills** [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) +13, [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39) +11, [Hunting Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) +11, [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=40) +13, [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43) +15, [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=49) +15 **Str** +3 **Dex** +4 **Con** +2 **Int** +0 **Wis** +2 **Cha** +1 **Move It!** The gamekeeper can [Hustle](/Actions.aspx?ID=2626) for 30 minutes longer and is not affected by [difficult terrain](/Rules.aspx?ID=453) while in their territory. **Items** [animal treats](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1705), _+1 [arbalest](/Weapons.aspx?ID=432)_ (40 bolts), [Club](/Weapons.aspx?ID=2) --- **AC** 23 **Fort** +17 **Ref** +13 **Will** +12 **HP** 95 **Sic 'Em!** ([auditory](/Traits.aspx?ID=541), [emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=590), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647)) **Trigger** An [animal](/Traits.aspx?ID=531) within 60 feet of the gamekeeper is killed; **Effect** The gamekeeper stokes the ire of the wild. Until the end of the gamekeeper's next turn, they and all animals in a 60-foot emanation gain a +1 status bonus to attack rolls and a +2 status bonus to damage rolls.
**Keeper's Revenge** ([curse](/Traits.aspx?ID=566), [primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=676)) When the gamekeeper dies, all creatures in a 60-foot emanation that have damaged the gamekeeper in the last minute must succeed a DC 24 Will saving throw or be cursed. All [animals](/Traits.aspx?ID=531) the cursed creature encounters have an initial attitude toward them that is one step worse. This curse can be removed only by an effect that specifically targets curses. --- **Speed** 25 feet **Melee** club +15, **Damage** 1d6+9 bludgeoning **Melee** fist +15 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [Finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=179), [Nonlethal](/Traits.aspx?ID=188), [Unarmed](/Traits.aspx?ID=199)), **Damage** 1d4+9 bludgeoning **Ranged** _arbalest_ +17 ([backstabber 1](/Traits.aspx?ID=172), [Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103), [range increment 110 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=248), [reload 1](/Traits.aspx?ID=254)), **Damage** 1d10+6 piercing **Leader of the Pack** The gamekeeper depends on a small pack of dogs or other pack animals suitable for the environment to patrol their area. Creatures that are adjacent to a [hostile](/Conditions.aspx?ID=80) [animal](/Traits.aspx?ID=531) are considered [off-guard](/Conditions.aspx?ID=58) to the gamekeeper.

<title level="1" pfs="">[Gnome Conservationist](/NPCs.aspx?ID=3639)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

The natural world boasts unsurpassed beauty and countless variety, and the gnome conservationist is devoted to experiencing and protecting as many examples of this grandeur as they possibly can. These gnomes are stalwart allies to animals and plants, and they find it exceptionally easy to build an outstanding rapport with almost all creatures they encounter on their travels.

<column gap="tiny">
**[Recall Knowledge - Humanoid](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**
([Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=47)): DC 22

**[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 20

**[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 17
</column>

</column>

<image src="/images/Monsters/Gnome_Conservationist.webp" />
</column>

</row>

<traits>
<trait label="Small" />
<trait label="Gnome" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=617" />
<trait label="Humanoid" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=628" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [NPC Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=236) pg. 184

**Perception** +17; [low-light vision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=69)

**Languages**
[Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1), [Gnomish](/Languages.aspx?ID=5)

**Skills**
[Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) +13, [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=37) +11, [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43) +15, [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=49) +15

<row gap="medium">
**Str** +2

**Dex** +1

**Con** +1

**Int** +2

**Wis** +4

**Cha** +2
</row>

**Animal Elocutionist** The conservationist can ask questions of, receive answers from, and use the [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39) skill with [animals](/Traits.aspx?ID=531).

**Items**
seeds (functions as [sling bullets](/Weapons.aspx?ID=430)), _+1 [sling](/Weapons.aspx?ID=430)_, trowel (functions as a [sickle](/Weapons.aspx?ID=364))

</column>

---

<column gap="tiny">

<row gap="medium">
**AC** 23 

**Fort** +17 

**Ref** +11 

**Will** +14 

</row>

<row gap="medium">
**HP** 100

</row>

</column>

---

<column gap="tiny">

**Speed** 25 feet

**Melee**
<actions string="Single Action" />
trowel +14 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [Finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=179), [Trip](/Traits.aspx?ID=196)),
**Damage** 1d4+8 slashing

**Melee**
<actions string="Single Action" />
fist +14 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [Finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=179), [Nonlethal](/Traits.aspx?ID=188), [Unarmed](/Traits.aspx?ID=199)),
**Damage** 1d4+8 bludgeoning

**Ranged**
<actions string="Single Action" />
_sling_ +16 ([Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103), [Propulsive](/Traits.aspx?ID=191), [range increment 60 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=248), [reload 1](/Traits.aspx?ID=254)),
**Damage** 1d6+7 bludgeoning

**Primal Prepared Spells** DC 24, attack +17
- **Cantrips (3rd)**
[Detect Magic](/Spells.aspx?ID=66), [Gouging Claw](/Spells.aspx?ID=920), [Know the Way](/Spells.aspx?ID=1582), [Light](/Spells.aspx?ID=171), [Tangle Vine](/Spells.aspx?ID=1713)
- **1st**
[Charm](/Spells.aspx?ID=34), [Gentle Landing](/Spells.aspx?ID=1542), [Runic Body](/Spells.aspx?ID=1657), [Spider Sting](/Spells.aspx?ID=300)
- **2nd**
[Animal Messenger](/Spells.aspx?ID=11), [Darkvision](/Spells.aspx?ID=60), [Entangling Flora](/Spells.aspx?ID=1515), [Oaken Resilience](/Spells.aspx?ID=1617)
- **3rd**
[Grease](/Spells.aspx?ID=140), [Mad Monkeys](/Spells.aspx?ID=702), [Safe Passage](/Spells.aspx?ID=712)

**Wild Leadership** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([Auditory](/Traits.aspx?ID=16), [Concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32), [Primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=134)) With a primal incantation, the gnome conservationist inspires a willing animal. The animal becomes [quickened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=89) for 1 round. It can use this additional action only to [Climb](/Actions.aspx?ID=2374), [Burrow](/Actions.aspx?ID=2310), [Fly](/Actions.aspx?ID=2312), Stride, or Strike.

</column>
