Hundreds of years ago, a cadre of powerful succubus assassins invaded the Abyssal realm of the demon lord of disease and fungus, Cyth-V'sug. These succubi sought to slay a powerful witch who had befouled a profane temple the assassins served. The succubi failed at their mission, but from their corpses grew the first fungus tyrants. Pleased with this development, the witch then seeded numerous worlds on the Material Plane with fungus tyrant spores, who have since grown and thrived in their new environments as rot thrives in a corpse. Today, hundreds of fungus tyrants inhabit the fouler locales of the Material Plane. They're particularly fond of large cave systems and ruined cities, but also can be found in corrupted woodlands where blighted fey rule or in the sewers of active cities that spew vast amounts of magical waste.
An encounter with a normally unintelligent plant monster acting with methodical intent can be evidence of a fungus tyrant's manipulations, but fungus tyrants are equally fond of keeping other types of creatures as pets and thralls—particularly attractive humanoids. Especially favored minions are given the gift of the fungus tyrant's embrace and are transformed into fungoid minions forever loyal to their pallid ruler. Yet most fungus tyrants realize that a diverse array of guardians is best, and they often choose to keep some non-fungus minions on hand to protect their lair.
Fungus tyrants are violently jealous. Any who attempt to lure away their dominated pets or cure those who have been infected by them earns their eternal ire. Yet it's succubi who enrage fungus tyrants the most. In these demons, the fungus tyrant sees a former glamour and power they no longer have access to, and only the brutal destruction of these mocking memories can salve a fungus tyrant's anger. A fungus tyrant faced with someone whom they suspect might be a succubus is terrible indeed, for in such battles, the fiendish fungal beings abandon their normal approach of subtle mental trickery and bring all of their power to bear in an attempt to rip the offending creature apart. Fungus tyrants also take great delight in transforming succubi into fungoid creatures under their control.
While their jealousy doesn't compel them to do battle with other fungus tyrants, they're always careful to maintain their own territories apart from any nearby kin, and they take great pains not to “poach” other tyrant's charmed and infested pets.
A fungus tyrant is 6 feet tall and weighs 150 pounds. **[Recall Knowledge - Fiend](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46)): DC 31 **[Recall Knowledge - Fungus](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43)): DC 31 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 29 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 26 [Fungus Tyrant](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3364) **Source** [Pathfinder #200: Seven Dooms for Sandpoint](/Sources.aspx?ID=229) pg. 190 **Perception** +19; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59) **Languages** [Abyssal](/Languages.aspx?ID=12), [Aklo](/Languages.aspx?ID=13), [Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1), [Undercommon](/Languages.aspx?ID=11); fungaltongue, [telepathy](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=79) 100 feet, [_tongues_](/Spells.aspx?ID=340) **Skills** [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) +19, [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38) +21, [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39) +19, [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=40) +19, [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46) +19, [Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=47) +18, [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=48) +19 **Str** +4 **Dex** +4 **Con** +4 **Int** +3 **Wis** +4 **Cha** +6 **Fungaltongue** A fungus tyrant can speak with all forms of fungus, be they fungal creatures or otherwise. Most normal fungi don't recognize details about creatures or know anything about the world beyond their immediate vicinity. A fungus tyrant gains a +3 circumstance bonus on all Deception, Diplomacy, or Intimidation checks made against fungus creatures.
 --- **AC** 27 **Fort** +21 **Ref** +17 **Will** +19 +1 status to all saves vs. magic **HP** 180 **Resistances** electricity 10 **Weaknesses** cold iron 10, good 10 --- **Speed** 20 feet **Melee** tentacle +19 ([Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103), [reach 10 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)), **Damage** 2d10+7 bludgeoning plus [Grab](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=45) **Melee** claw +19 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103)), **Damage** 2d12+7 slashing **Divine Innate Spells** DC 28, attack +20 - **Cantrips (5th)** [Daze](/Spells.aspx?ID=61), [Detect Magic](/Spells.aspx?ID=66) - **3rd** [Mind Reading](/Spells.aspx?ID=194), [Slow](/Spells.aspx?ID=289) - **4th** [Charm](/Spells.aspx?ID=34), [Hallucinatory Terrain](/Spells.aspx?ID=145), [Suggestion](/Spells.aspx?ID=315) - **5th** [Hallucination](/Spells.aspx?ID=144), [Mind Probe](/Spells.aspx?ID=193), [Veil](/Spells.aspx?ID=355) - **Constant (5th)** [Tongues](/Spells.aspx?ID=340) **Create Spawn** ([Divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=48), [Necromancy](/Traits.aspx?ID=117)) If a creature dies after being reduced to 0 HP by a fungus tyrant's Mind-Draining Kiss, the fungus tyrant can turn this victim into a spore thrall by donating some of their own fungal matter to the victim and leaving them to “ripen” within a patch of fungus for 24 hours. After this time, the creature is restored to life but gains the fungus trait and becomes a spore thrall. This prevents the creature's soul from continuing on to the afterlife in a similar manner to how undead are taken out of that cycle—as such, those who hold that cycle sacred (particularly worshipers of Pharasma) regard spore thralls as bad as the undead, despite them being living creatures. If the new spore thrall is a lower level than its creator, then it's under the creator's control. If a fungus tyrant controls too many spore thralls at once (as determined by the GM), strong-willed spore thralls can free themselves by succeeding at a DC 28 Will save. Typically, a fungus tyrant avoids creating spore thralls out of fallen foes who are too powerful to control, for they're only too aware of the compulsion for revenge such victims might harbor for those who wrenched them from the afterlife. **Grow Sporepod** ([Conjuration](/Traits.aspx?ID=33), [Divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=48)) The fungus tyrant causes a human-sized pod of fungal material to burst out of the ground at any point they can see within 60 feet. Once created, a sporepod lasts for 1 minute, until the fungus tyrant moves more than 120 feet away from it, or until it's destroyed (AC 28, Hardness 10, 20 HP). The fungus tyrant cannot Grow a Sporepod again for 1d4 rounds, but apart from this and a sporepod's 1 minute life, there is no hard limit to the number of sporepods a single fungus tyrant can have active at any one time. **Mind-Draining Kiss** ([Divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=48), [Emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=60), [Enchantment](/Traits.aspx?ID=61), [Mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=106)) **Frequency** once per round; **Effect** The fungus tyrant engages a creature they have grabbed in an act of passion in an attempt to drain its will and personality. The kiss makes the creature [stupefied](/Conditions.aspx?ID=94) 1 or increases its stupefied condition by 1, to a maximum of 4. The creature takes 4d6 poison damage and must then succeed at a DC 28 Will save or be affected by a suggestion to remain immobile rather than trying to [Escape](/Actions.aspx?ID=2296). **Sporestride** ([Conjuration](/Traits.aspx?ID=33), [Move](/Traits.aspx?ID=114), [Teleportation](/Traits.aspx?ID=156)) The fungus tyrant Steps into an adjacent sporepod and instantly teleports to any other active sporepod they've created, bursting out of the target sporepod and destroying it in the process. **Sporewarp** ([Attack](/Traits.aspx?ID=15)) The fungus tyrant attempts a tentacle Strike but treats a sporepod of their choice within 120 feet that they can see as the point of origin of that tentacle Strike.

description: Hundreds of years ago, a cadre of powerful succubus assassins invaded the Abyssal realm of the demon lord of disease and fungus, Cyth-V'sug. These succubi sought to slay a powerful witch who had befouled a profane temple the assassins served. The succubi failed at their mission, but from their corpses grew the first fungus tyrants. Pleased with this development, the witch then seeded numerous worlds on the Material Plane with fungus tyrant spores, who have since grown and thrived in their new environments as rot thrives in a corpse. Today, hundreds of fungus tyrants inhabit the fouler locales of the Material Plane. They're particularly fond of large cave systems and ruined cities, but also can be found in corrupted woodlands where blighted fey rule or in the sewers of active cities that spew vast amounts of magical waste.

A hryngar breccia squad is a group of hryngar martial combatants armed with melee weapons and steel shields. Though more likely to be encountered near large hryngar settlements, these strike forces see wide use throughout the Darklands. Hryngar breccia squads often serve as military units, mercenary companies, city patrols, and caravan guards. Like all warriors, the favored combat methods of a hryngar breccia squad change by location, often due to surrounding environment and popular equipment. **[Recall Knowledge - Humanoid](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=14)): DC 28 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 26 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 23 [Hryngar Breccia Squad](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2708) **Source** [Pathfinder #195: Heavy is the Crown](/Sources.aspx?ID=210) pg. 87 **Perception** +18; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=12) **Languages** [Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1), [Dwarven](/Languages.aspx?ID=3), [Undercommon](/Languages.aspx?ID=11) **Skills** [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) +21, [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=4) +18, [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=7) +16, [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=13) +18, [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=16) +18 **Str** +6 **Dex** +2 **Con** +4 **Int** +2 **Wis** +3 **Cha** +1 --- **AC** 28 **Fort** +20 **Ref** +15 **Will** +18 +2 status to all saves vs. magic **HP** 150 **Weaknesses** area damage12, [splash](/Traits.aspx?ID=150) damage 6 **[Light Blindness](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=22)**
**[Troop Defenses](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=44)**
**[Attack of Opportunity](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=3)**
**[Shield Block](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=32)** --- **Speed** 20 feet; troop movement **Bolt Barrage** The hryngar breccia squad draws or reloads its crossbows, then launches a ranged attack in the form of a volley. This volley is a 10-foot burst within 120 feet that deals 4d8 piercing damage (DC 28 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save). When the hryngar breccia squad is reduced to 8 or fewer squares, this area decreases to a 5-foot burst. **[Form Up](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=43)** **General Melee** **Frequency** once per round; **Effect** The hryngar breccia squad engages in a coordinated attack with its melee weapons against each enemy within 5 feet (DC 28 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save). The damage depends on the number of actions.
1d8+6 bludgeoning damage
2d8+10 bludgeoning damage
3d8+14 bludgeoning damage **Push Back** **Requirements** The hryngar breccia squad has its shields raised; **Effect** The hryngar breccia squad pushes against adjacent foes, knocking them back. The hryngar breccia squad attempts an [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) check to [Shove](/Actions.aspx?ID=38), comparing the result to the Fortitude DC of each enemy within 5 feet of the hryngar breccia squad. The hryngar breccia squad is not knocked [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=31) on a critical failure. **Raise Shields** The hryngar breccia squad raises [steel shields](/Shields.aspx?ID=3), with the effects of [Raise a Shield](/Actions.aspx?ID=98). **Troop Movement** Whenever the hryngar breccia squad Strides, it first [Forms Up](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=43) as a free action to condense into a 20-foot-by-20-foot area (minus any missing squares), then moves up to its Speed. This works just like a Gargantuan creature moving; for instance, if any square of the hryngar breccia squad enters [difficult terrain](/Rules.aspx?ID=453), the extra movement cost applies to the entire hryngar breccia squad.

Irnakurse are believed to be [elves](/Ancestries.aspx?ID=2) who have been subjected to particularly cruel and humiliating fleshwarping practices, though they are so corrupted by their transformation it is nearly impossible to tell. The process of crafting an irnakurse twists the unfortunate elf into a mass of misplaced limbs, loose flesh, and bony protrusions—parts that should be internal are often left on full display to the world. These beings periodically crawl to the surface from the deepest reaches of the Darklands, leading some elven scholars to the gruesome suspicion that these are remnants of the elves who traveled underground in order to escape Earthfall. **[Recall Knowledge - Aberration](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=44)): DC 26 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 24 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 21 [Irnakurse](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2998) **Source** [Monster Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=221) pg. 153 1.1 **Perception** +18; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59) **Languages** [Chthonian](/Languages.aspx?ID=114), [Elven](/Languages.aspx?ID=4), [Sakvroth](/Languages.aspx?ID=118); (can't speak any language) **Skills** [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=1) +20, [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) +20, [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15) +20 **Str** +5 **Dex** +5 **Con** +3 **Int** -2 **Wis** +3 **Cha** +4 --- **AC** 28 **Fort** +20 **Ref** +18 **Will** +16 **HP** 152 --- **Speed** 15 feet **Melee** jaws +20 ([reach 10 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)), **Damage** 2d12+11 piercing **Melee** tentacle +20 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [reach 20 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)), **Damage** 2d8+11 slashing plus mind lash **Mind Lash** ([Emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=60), [Mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=106), [Occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=120)) A creature hit by an irnakurse's tentacle is overwhelmed with corrupted images of a ruined life and must succeed at a DC 28 Will save or be [stunned 2](/Conditions.aspx?ID=93) (or stunned 4 on a critical failure). After attempting this save, the creature is temporarily immune to mind lash for 24 hours. **Soul Scream** ([Auditory](/Traits.aspx?ID=16), [Concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32), [Emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=60), [Mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=106), [Occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=120)) **Frequency** once per day; **Effect** The irnakurse unleashes an alien shriek of nightmarish horror and pain. All non-[aberration](/Traits.aspx?ID=523) creatures within a 10-foot emanation must attempt a DC 28 Will save. The irnakurse can Sustain Soul Scream for up to 6 rounds; each time it does, it repeats the effect without a new save.
**Critical Success** The creature is unaffected, and it's temporarily immune to Soul Scream for 24 hours.
**Success** The creature is [stupefied 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=94) for 1 round.
**Failure** The creature is stupefied 1. Further failed saves against Soul Scream increase the stupefied value by 1, to a maximum of stupefied 4. Each time the character gets a full night's rest, the stupefied condition gained from Soul Scream decreases by 1.
**Critical Failure** As failure, except the stupefied value increases by 2 instead of by 1. **Storm of Tentacles** The irnakurse makes up to four tentacle Strikes, each against a different target. These attacks count toward the irnakurse's multiple attack penalty, but the multiple attack penalty doesn't increase until after it makes all of its attacks.

Iruxi masked mummers bring lizardfolk myths to life, donning elaborate costumes and bone masks to enact stories featuring their ancestors, the gods, legendary dragons and dinosaurs, and nature spirits of all kinds. The most talented mummers claim their ritual dances invite these spirits inside them, suffusing their bodies with starlight and lending them primal power uniquely tied to the luminaries their masks represent. This magic can be seen even by those without magical ability, as they can see glowing motes shaped like distant stars seeming to float under the skin of the mummer. **[Recall Knowledge - Humanoid](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=47)): DC 26 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 24 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 21 [Iruxi Masked Mummer](/NPCs.aspx?ID=3661) **Source** [NPC Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=236) pg. 205 **Perception** +18 **Languages** [Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1), [Draconic](/Languages.aspx?ID=2), [Iruxi](/Languages.aspx?ID=32), [Thalassic](/Languages.aspx?ID=113) **Skills** [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=34) +17, [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) +17, [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=40) +19, [Iruxi Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) +20, [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43) +18, [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=45) +20, [Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=47) +16, [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=49) +18 **Str** +2 **Dex** +4 **Con** +0 **Int** +1 **Wis** +3 **Cha** +4 **Deep Breath** A masked mummer can [hold their breath](/Rules.aspx?ID=2436) for 20 minutes. **Items** [ceremonial skull mask](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1397), _+1 striking [handwraps of mighty blows](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3086)_, mummer's costume, [lesser maestro instrument](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3026) (hand drum) --- **AC** 27 **Fort** +15 **Ref** +19 **Will** +18 **HP** 155 --- **Speed** 25 feet, swim 20 feet **Melee** tail +20 ([Finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=179), [Sweep](/Traits.aspx?ID=194)), **Damage** 2d6+8 bludgeoning **Melee** claws +20 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [Finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=179), [versatile P](/Traits.aspx?ID=200)), **Damage** 2d4+8 slashing **Ranged** spectral roar +19 ([Primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=134), [range 30 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=248), [Sonic](/Traits.aspx?ID=147)), **Damage** 3d10 sonic **Don Mask** ([Primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=134)) **Frequency** once per 10 minutes; **Effect** The mummer dons a ceremonial skull mask, calling an ancestral spirit to come to their aid. The spirit answers with a spell the mummer can cast as a primal innate spell (5th rank, DC 27) as part of the Don Mask activity. The mummer also gains a primal boon that lasts for 1 minute. After the minute is over or the mask is removed, the spell and boon end if either is still active, and the mummer is [fatigued](/Conditions.aspx?ID=73). The most common legendary spirits the masks can invoke are:
  • **Fiery Akkarok** (tyrannosaurus mask); **Spell** [_blazing bolt_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1450) (3-action version); **Boon** The mummer's melee Strikes deal an additional 2d6 fire damage.
  • **Hazi Zephyr-Borne** (griffon or iruxi mask); **Spell** [_wall of wind_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1753); **Boon** The mummer gains a fly Speed of 20 feet.
  • **King of Storms** (roc or horned dragon mask); Spell [_howling blizzard_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1559); **Boon** The mummer gains the [Reactive Strike](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=48) reaction that can be used only with their tail.
  • **Nessek, the Wave Dancer** (mosasaur mask); **Spell** [_slither_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1676); **Boon** The mummer's claw Strikes deal an additional 2d4 [persistent bleed damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29).
  • **Zalok, Who was Called to Black Harbor** (naga or spinosaurus mask); **Spell** [_hydraulic torrent_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1562); **Boon** The mummer gains a +10-foot status bonus to their land Speed and swim Speed.
**Starry Presence** ([Aura](/Traits.aspx?ID=206), [Illusion](/Traits.aspx?ID=92), [Light](/Traits.aspx?ID=100), [Mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=106), [Primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=134)) 30 feet. With a quick dance, the iruxi masked mummer surrounds themself with a starlight image resembling a figure from legend. The image lasts until the start of the mummer's next turn. An enemy that enters or starts its turn in the aura must succeed at a DC 25 Will save or become [dazzled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=65) until the start of its next turn.

Regarded as the progenitors of geniekind, janns hold a position of esteem above the genies tied to specific planes. They possess an inborn ability to grant wishes, which the other branches of geniekind lack and greatly envy. Nomadic jann shuyookhs rarely hold court, preferring to gather only when the need arises to perform great deeds. Lesser janns respect and venerate these leaders for their wisdom and total dedication to preserving the honor and reputation of their people. A jann shuyookh reads portents and omens when dealing with duplicitous mortals. **[Recall Knowledge - Elemental](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=2), [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=10)): DC 28 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 26 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 23 [Jann Shuyookh](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2688) **Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 227 2.0 **Perception** +18; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=12) **Languages** [Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1), [Muan](/Languages.aspx?ID=108), [Petran](/Languages.aspx?ID=109), [Pyric](/Languages.aspx?ID=110), [Sussuran](/Languages.aspx?ID=111), [Talican](/Languages.aspx?ID=112), [Thalassic](/Languages.aspx?ID=113); [_truespeech_](/Spells.aspx?ID=340) **Skills** [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=1) +17, [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) +19, [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=2) +18, [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=4) +16, [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5) +17, [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=6) +19, [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=16) +18 **Str** +6 **Dex** +4 **Con** +4 **Int** +3 **Wis** +5 **Cha** +4 **Items** _+1 [striking](/Equipment.aspx?ID=280) [scimitar](/Weapons.aspx?ID=38)_, _+1 [striking](/Equipment.aspx?ID=280) [composite longbow](/Weapons.aspx?ID=74)_ --- **AC** 27 **Fort** +19 **Ref** +17 **Will** +18 **HP** 155 **Resistances** elemental resistance 10 **Commanding Presence** ([aura](/Traits.aspx?ID=206), [emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=60), [fear](/Traits.aspx?ID=68), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=106)) 20 feet. A creature that enters the aura must succeed at a DC 26 Will save or be [frightened 2](/Conditions.aspx?ID=19) (frightened 3 on a critical failure), and is then temporarily immune for 1 minute. A [genie](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=50) (with the exception of another jann) takes a –4 circumstance penalty to their save.
**Elemental Resistance** The jann shuyookh's elemental resistance applies to cold, electricity, and fire damage, as well as all damage from elemental sources (including [environmental damage](/Rules.aspx?ID=642) from the elemental planes and damage from anything with the [air](/Traits.aspx?ID=5), [earth](/Traits.aspx?ID=55), [fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=72), [metal](/Traits.aspx?ID=505), [water](/Traits.aspx?ID=165), or [wood](/Traits.aspx?ID=508) trait). --- **Speed** 25 feet, fly 20 feet **Melee** _scimitar_ +20 ([Forceful](/Traits.aspx?ID=180), [Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103), [Sweep](/Traits.aspx?ID=194)), **Damage** 2d6+12 slashing and All Made One **Melee** fist +19 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103), [Nonlethal](/Traits.aspx?ID=188)), **Damage** 1d8+9 bludgeoning and All Made One **Ranged** _composite longbow_ +18 ([deadly d10](/Traits.aspx?ID=174), [Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103), [Propulsive](/Traits.aspx?ID=191), [volley 30 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=201)), **Damage** 2d8+9 piercing and all made one **Arcane Innate Spells** DC 28 - **Cantrips (4th)** [Detect Magic](/Spells.aspx?ID=66), [Know Direction](/Spells.aspx?ID=169) - **4th** [Invisibility](/Spells.aspx?ID=164) (×2), [Read Omens](/Spells.aspx?ID=247) - **7th** [Plane Shift](/Spells.aspx?ID=222) (at will; to [Astral Plane](/Planes.aspx?ID=8), Elemental Planes, or the [Universe](/Planes.aspx?ID=1) only) - **Constant (5th)** [Tongues](/Spells.aspx?ID=340) **All Made One** The jann shuyookh calls upon all the elements that make up their being and chooses one. They gain an additional arcane spell they can cast at will and empower their Strikes with the element, dealing an extra 1d6 damage of the listed type. These benefits last until the shuyookh uses this ability again. **Air** [_lightning bolt_](/Spells.aspx?ID=172), 1d6 electricity; **earth** [_one with stone_](/Spells.aspx?ID=188), 1d6 bludgeoning; **fire** [_fireball_](/Spells.aspx?ID=119), 1d6 fire; **metal** [_noxious metals_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1376), 1d6 electricity; **water** [_wall of water_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1028), 1d6 bludgeoning; **wood** [_wall of thorns_](/Spells.aspx?ID=366), 1d6 piercing. **[Change Shape](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=8)** ([Arcane](/Traits.aspx?ID=11), [Concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32), [Polymorph](/Traits.aspx?ID=127)) The genie transforms into a Small or Medium [elemental](/Traits.aspx?ID=57) or [animal](/Traits.aspx?ID=9). This doesn't affect the genie's statistics, but it could change the damage type of their Strikes **Wanderer's Wish** **Frequency** three times per year; **Effect** The jann instantly grants the benefits of a critical success with the _wish_ ritual to a mortal creature. This has no cost. That creature specifies what they wish for, but the interpretation is up to the jann. A jann typically attempts to grant wishes in a way that encourages growth and exploration. A summoned jann can't use this ability.

<title level="1" pfs="">[Khasprickle, Sadistic Bully](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3714)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

Khasprickle is a sadistic bully who enjoys causing trouble. Like most pukwudgies, Khasprickle is incredibly proud and obsessed with being respected— he expects mortals to fawn over him, [fey](/Languages.aspx?ID=119) to admit his superiority, and everyone else to be content to simply bask in his presence and recognize his apparent greatness.

 Despite his fondness for tricks, pranks, and the unexpected, Khasprickle believes that a deal must be upheld, and he expects it to be so. Yet day after day, year after year, and decade after decade, Khasprickle has watched the greedy loggers and foresters of Andoran and Taldor reap the bounty of the Verduran Forest, cutting down the very trees under the protection of the Wildwood Treaty. This blatant breach of the Wildwood Treaty is downright disrespectful—and nobody hates disrespect like a pukwudgie!

 In retaliation for a lifetime of past slights and countless grave insults, Khasprickle resolved to smack some respect into the forest's neighboring nations of Andoran and Taldor. He eagerly joined the retaliatory expeditions and named his raiding party the “Last Stop.” Khasprickle considered this raiding party a part of the “wild hunt”—a blasphemous pronouncement sure to draw the ire of the true wild hunt if they ever found out.

 Despite the delusional audacity of these actions, Khasprickle became an outspoken voice against Andoran's and Taldor's illegal foresting practices and the countless, everyday people who take advantage of the Wildwood Treaty. Khasprickle commands growing influence among the Verduran Forests's offended inhabitants.

 When Ruzadoya Swiftmane was elected leader of the Wildwood Lodge, resulting in the founding of the Rootweft Lodge under Emorga-All-Seer, Khasprickle eagerly supported Ruzadoya and her “true” Wildwood Lodge. In the aftermath of this event, he was emboldened, and his attacks became deadlier and more virulent. Thanks to his dedication, Khasprickle has been both promoted—and emboldened—by Ruzadoya Swiftmane. If left unchecked, he's sure to cause havoc. 

<title level="2" right="">Campaign Role</title> Khasprickle is a bully, through and through, and like most pukwudgies, he's extremely sensitive to getting the respect he thinks he deserves. He despises being kept waiting, sees insult in every action and turn of phrase, and considers anyone who disagrees with him a fool. Hearty, nimble, and incredibly stubborn, Khasprickle is a formidable foe.

 Early in the campaign, Khasprickle is a social foil. He's a troublemaker who disagrees with the PCs and who should find himself on the opposite side of a conflict from them. His misdeeds are minor at first— mostly gripes, complaints, and colorful language. Soon, after receiving the encouragement of some other bitter, like-minded fey, Khasprickle forms his raiding party, Last Stop, and rampages through the forest, causing trouble and destruction. At this point, Khasprickle is accompanied by two of his close friends and cronies: Ashendeath the [elananx](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2972) and Sylvarindarian, a vicious [pixie](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3212). The trio feed off of one another's anger and ire, growing more brazen and bolder as time passes.

 At this point, Khasprickle becomes a bigger problem but still remains a social issue. He's someone to undermine, discredit, or win over. The PCs likely work hard here to earn Khasprickle's focus and keep it, in the hopes that he can be rehabilitated or can learn to feel remorse for his actions. Unfortunately for the PCs, Khasprickle can't be rehabilitated, though he can be influenced. Any self-improvements that Khasprickle performs are temporary.

 Later, after Ruzadoya's election to leader of the Wildwood Lodge, Khasprickle becomes a true villain. He leads his raiding party into the Verduran Forest to slaughter foresters, loggers, and anyone else he suspects has ties to Andoran or Taldor. He threatens and harms the inhabitants of the Verduran Forest in an attempt to coerce them into joining Ruzadoya. Many lives are lost. Soon, as the PCs focus on collecting objects and weapons that once belonged to Ghorus, the PCs discover that Khasprickle shares the same task, though he's working for the enemy. It should be clear that a dangerous weapon in Khasprickle's hands would be disastrous. It's at this point that the scales fully tip, and Khasprickle becomes downright villainous. Under Ruzadoya's leadership, he has gone from bad to worse, and now it's up to the PCs to bring an end to the misery he's causing.

 The PCs finally confront Khasprickle outside Ghorus's Garden, where he has captured and tormented the immortal [dweomercat](/Monsters.aspx?ID=643) Felivaine, an ally of the PCs. text: Khasprickle, Sadistic Bully Khasprickle is a sadistic bully who enjoys causing trouble. Like most pukwudgies, Khasprickle is incredibly proud and obsessed with being respected— he expects mortals to fawn over him, fey to admit his superiority, and everyone else to be content to simply bask in his presence and recognize his apparent greatness. Despite his fondness for tricks, pranks, and the unexpected, Khasprickle believes that a deal must be upheld, and he expects it to be so. Yet day after day, year after year, and decade after decade, Khasprickle has watched the greedy loggers and foresters of Andoran and Taldor reap the bounty of the Verduran Forest, cutting down the very trees under the protection of the Wildwood Treaty. This blatant breach of the Wildwood Treaty is downright disrespectful—and nobody hates disrespect like a pukwudgie! In retaliation for a lifetime of past slights and countless grave insults, Khasprickle resolved to smack some respect into the forest's neighboring nations of Andoran and Taldor. He eagerly joined the retaliatory expeditions and named his raiding party the “Last Stop.” Khasprickle considered this raiding party a part of the “wild hunt”—a blasphemous pronouncement sure to draw the ire of the true wild hunt if they ever found out. Despite the delusional audacity of these actions, Khasprickle became an outspoken voice against Andoran's and Taldor's illegal foresting practices and the countless, everyday people who take advantage of the Wildwood Treaty. Khasprickle commands growing influence among the Verduran Forests's offended inhabitants. When Ruzadoya Swiftmane was elected leader of the Wildwood Lodge, resulting in the founding of the Rootweft Lodge under Emorga-All-Seer, Khasprickle eagerly supported Ruzadoya and her “true” Wildwood Lodge. In the aftermath of this event, he was emboldened, and his attacks became deadlier and more virulent. Thanks to his dedication, Khasprickle has been both promoted—and emboldened—by Ruzadoya Swiftmane. If left unchecked, he's sure to cause havoc. Campaign Role Khasprickle is a bully, through and through, and like most pukwudgies, he's extremely sensitive to getting the respect he thinks he deserves. He despises being kept waiting, sees insult in every action and turn of phrase, and considers anyone who disagrees with him a fool. Hearty, nimble, and incredibly stubborn, Khasprickle is a formidable foe. Early in the campaign, Khasprickle is a social foil. He's a troublemaker who disagrees with the PCs and who should find himself on the opposite side of a conflict from them. His misdeeds are minor at first— mostly gripes, complaints, and colorful language. Soon, after receiving the encouragement of some other bitter, like-minded fey, Khasprickle forms his raiding party, Last Stop, and rampages through the forest, causing trouble and destruction. At this point, Khasprickle is accompanied by two of his close friends and cronies: Ashendeath the elananx and Sylvarindarian, a vicious pixie. The trio feed off of one another's anger and ire, growing more brazen and bolder as time passes. At this point, Khasprickle becomes a bigger problem but still remains a social issue. He's someone to undermine, discredit, or win over. The PCs likely work hard here to earn Khasprickle's focus and keep it, in the hopes that he can be rehabilitated or can learn to feel remorse for his actions. Unfortunately for the PCs, Khasprickle can't be rehabilitated, though he can be influenced. Any self-improvements that Khasprickle performs are temporary. Later, after Ruzadoya's election to leader of the Wildwood Lodge, Khasprickle becomes a true villain. He leads his raiding party into the Verduran Forest to slaughter foresters, loggers, and anyone else he suspects has ties to Andoran or Taldor. He threatens and harms the inhabitants of the Verduran Forest in an attempt to coerce them into joining Ruzadoya. Many lives are lost. Soon, as the PCs focus on collecting objects and weapons that once belonged to Ghorus, the PCs discover that Khasprickle shares the same task, though he's working for the enemy. It should be clear that a dangerous weapon in Khasprickle's hands would be disastrous. It's at this point that the scales fully tip, and Khasprickle becomes downright villainous. Under Ruzadoya's leadership, he has gone from bad to worse, and now it's up to the PCs to bring an end to the misery he's causing. The PCs finally confront Khasprickle outside Ghorus's Garden, where he has captured and tormented the immortal dweomercat Felivaine, an ally of the PCs. Khasprickle serves as a mini-boss that has been built up for quite some time. By this point, the PCs should despise Khasprickle and everything he stands for, and they should believe that, this time, they can't let him off with a warning—some people just can't be saved. These skull-headed, vulture-winged daemons are harbingers of pestilence and servants of their patron Apocalypse Rider, [Apollyon](/Deities.aspx?ID=134). Manifestations of evil souls who perished from disease in life, leukodaemons work tirelessly alongside one another to spread disease across all the worlds of the multiverse.

1d8+2 bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing
3d8+4 bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing

Seeking to be the most powerful and perfect creature in their domain, a mirror seer forges a deal with a nefarious entity for more power. Through a magic mirror called a [_malefic mirror_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2735), they communicate with this entity and spy on the events that unfold in their realm. **[Recall Knowledge - Humanoid](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=47)): DC 31 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 29 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 26 [Mirror Seer](/NPCs.aspx?ID=3541) **Source** [NPC Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=236) pg. 101 **Perception** +16 **Languages** [Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1), [Diabolic](/Languages.aspx?ID=117), [Fey](/Languages.aspx?ID=119), [Shadowtongue](/Languages.aspx?ID=21) **Skills** [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38) +21, [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39) +17, [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=44) +19, [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=45) +17, [Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=47) +17, [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=48) +17 **Str** +2 **Dex** +2 **Con** -1 **Int** +4 **Wis** +3 **Cha** +5 **Looking Glass Magic** The mirror seer accesses power from their wicked
benefactor through two mirrors: one full-sized _[malefic mirror](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2735)_ in their sanctum and an _enchanted hand mirror_ they can carry on their person.
  • **Malefic Mirror** The mirror seer must visit the _malefic mirror_ once per day to retain their spellcasting abilities, and they can activate the mirror for special [_scrying_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1662) and [_illusory disguise_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1568) spells as noted in the mirror's stat block.
  • **Enchanted Hand Mirror** Without their enchanted hand mirror on their person, the mirror seer takes a –2 circumstance penalty to spell attack rolls and DCs and can't cast their 7th-rank spells. If it's not attended by the mirror seer, the hand mirror has AC 10, Hardness 0, and 1 HP.
**Items** [_+1 dagger_](/Weapons.aspx?ID=3), [_enchanted hand mirror_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=35), [_scroll of false vision_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1522), _+1 [striking](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2829) [staff](/Weapons.aspx?ID=367)_ --- **AC** 27 **Fort** +14 **Ref** +17 **Will** +20 **HP** 140 **Rightfully Mine** **Trigger** The mirror seer observes a creature making a Strike, casting a spell of 4th rank or lower, or using a special action (the triggering action must take 2 actions or fewer); Effect The mirror seer expends a 4th-rank spell slot (or higher) to duplicate the triggering action. This mimicked action occurs immediately after the triggering action, using the triggering creature's statistics unless the mirror seer's are higher. The creature the mirror seer mimicked is then temporarily immune to this ability for 10 minutes. --- **Speed** 25 feet **Melee** _staff_ +19 ([Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103), [two-hand d8](/Traits.aspx?ID=198)), **Damage** 2d4+8 bludgeoning **Melee** dagger +19 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103), [versatile S](/Traits.aspx?ID=200)), **Damage** 1d4+8 piercing **Melee** fist +18 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [Nonlethal](/Traits.aspx?ID=188), [Unarmed](/Traits.aspx?ID=199)), **Damage** 1d4+8 bludgeoning **Ranged** dagger +19 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103), [thrown 10 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=195), [versatile S](/Traits.aspx?ID=200)), **Damage** 1d4+8 piercing **Occult Spontaneous Spells** DC 29, attack +21 - **Cantrips (5th)** [Daze](/Spells.aspx?ID=61), [Figment](/Spells.aspx?ID=1528), [Prestidigitation](/Spells.aspx?ID=229), [Telekinetic Projectile](/Spells.aspx?ID=334), [Void Warp](/Spells.aspx?ID=1745) - **1st** [Alarm](/Spells.aspx?ID=7), [Fear](/Spells.aspx?ID=110), [Item Facade](/Spells.aspx?ID=166) (3 slots) - **2nd** [Invisibility](/Spells.aspx?ID=164), [Revealing Light](/Spells.aspx?ID=1653), [Status](/Spells.aspx?ID=308) (3 slots) - **3rd** [Clairaudience](/Spells.aspx?ID=39), [Hypnotize](/Spells.aspx?ID=1564), [Locate](/Spells.aspx?ID=173) (3 slots) - **4th** [Clairvoyance](/Spells.aspx?ID=40), [Detect Scrying](/Spells.aspx?ID=68), [Peaceful Bubble](/Spells.aspx?ID=1624) (3 slots) - **5th** [Illusory Scene](/Spells.aspx?ID=161), [Shadow Blast](/Spells.aspx?ID=273) (2 slots) - **7th** [Illusory Disguise](/Spells.aspx?ID=159) (self only), [Scrying](/Spells.aspx?ID=268) (2 slots) **A Fairer Face** ([Concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32), [Emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=60), [Mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=106), [Occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=120)) The mirror seer chooses a creature within 100 feet that can see its own reflection in a mirror. The creature must succeed at a DC 29 Will save or become [fascinated](/Conditions.aspx?ID=72) by their reflection for 1 minute. The creature can attempt a new save to end the effect at the end of each of its turns. **Hall of Mirrors** ([Concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32), [Illusion](/Traits.aspx?ID=92), [Manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104), [Occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=120)) **Frequency** once per day; **Effect** The mirror seer causes all surfaces in a 30-foot burst within 100 feet to become reflective for 1 minute. Every creature in the area or that later enters the area must succeed at a DC 27 Will save or become [confused](/Conditions.aspx?ID=63) by the reflections and refractions. The confusion ends if the creature leaves the area, and the creature can attempt a new save to end the effect at the end of each of its turns. When the effect ends for a creature, that creature becomes temporarily immune for 10 minutes.
name: Mirror Seer

text: Mirror Seer Seeking to be the most powerful and perfect creature in their domain, a mirror seer forges a deal with a nefarious entity for more power. Through a magic mirror called a malefic mirror , they communicate with this entity and spy on the events that unfold in their realm. While mummy guardians are undead crafted from the corpses of sacrificed— usually unwilling victims—and retain only fragments of their memories, a mummy pharaoh is the result of a deliberate embrace of undeath by a sadistic and cruel ruler. The transformation from life to undeath beneath the scorching desert sand is only somewhat less awful, but as the transition is an intentional bid to escape death by a powerful personality who fully embraces the blasphemous repercussions of the choice, the mummy pharaoh retains its memories and personality intact. **[Recall Knowledge - Undead](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46)): DC 31 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 29 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 26 [Mummy Pharaoh](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3102) **Source** [Monster Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=221) pg. 235 1.1 **Perception** +20; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59) **Languages** [Necril](/Languages.aspx?ID=20); plus any two languages they knew while alive **Skills** [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5) +18, [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=7) +20, [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=11) +15, [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=13) +20, [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15) +13 **Str** +5 **Dex** +2 **Con** +4 **Int** +0 **Wis** +5 **Cha** +5 **Rejuvenation** ([divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=579)) When a mummy pharaoh is destroyed, necromantic energies rebuild its body in its tomb over 1d10 days. If the body is destroyed during that time, the process starts anew. A reforming mummy pharaoh is destroyed permanently if their tomb is [_consecrated_](/Rituals.aspx?ID=115). **Items** _+1 [striking](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2829) [longspear](/Weapons.aspx?ID=361)_ --- **AC** 27 **Fort** +19 **Ref** +15 **Will** +20 +1 status to all saves vs. [vitality](/Traits.aspx?ID=509) **HP** 175 (sacred wrappings, [void healing](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=83)) **Immunities** bleed, [death](/Traits.aspx?ID=571) effects, [disease](/Traits.aspx?ID=578), [paralyzed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=85), [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=669), [unconscious](/Conditions.aspx?ID=95) **Weaknesses** [fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=604) 10, [water](/Traits.aspx?ID=732) 10 **Undead Mastery** ([aura](/Traits.aspx?ID=542), [divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=579)) 100 feet. Commanded or allied [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=722) in the aura that have a lower level than the mummy pharaoh gain a +1 circumstance bonus to attack rolls, damage rolls, AC, saves, and skill checks.
**[Reactive Strike](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=48)** The mummy pharaoh can use Reactive Strike when a creature within its reach uses a [concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561) action, in addition to its normal trigger. It can disrupt triggering concentrate actions, and it disrupts actions on any hit, not just a critical hit.

This bizarre entity is actually a massive collective consisting of tens of thousands of constituent parts, each a tiny metal sphere barely the size of a pebble. Controlled by a single elemental spirit, the swarm is capable of flowing like liquid through the smallest openings before shaping itself into a powerful combatant, a solid wall, or any other form circumstances might require. **[Recall Knowledge - Elemental](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=2), [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=10)): DC 26 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 24 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 21 [Nanoshard Swarm](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2651) **Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 157 2.0 **Perception** +18; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=12) **Languages** [Talican](/Languages.aspx?ID=112) **Skills** [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=1) +21, [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) +19, [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15) +21 **Str** +6 **Dex** +6 **Con** +4 **Int** +3 **Wis** +3 **Cha** +3 --- **AC** 28 **Fort** +17 **Ref** +21 **Will** +16 **HP** 120 **Immunities** bleed, [paralyzed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=28), [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=126), precision, [sleep](/Traits.aspx?ID=145), [swarm mind](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=36) **Resistances** bludgeoning 5, electricity 10, piercing 10, slashing 10 **Weaknesses** area damage 10, [splash](/Traits.aspx?ID=150) damage 10 **Electromagnetic Dispersal** When a nanoshard swarm takes electricity damage, they automatically shift into swarm form. --- **Speed** none (barrier), 15 feet (battle), or 25 feet (swarm) **Melee** tendril +19 ([reach 60 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192), [versatile B](/Traits.aspx?ID=200)), **Damage** 2d8+9 piercing **Barrier Form** ([Concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32), [Polymorph](/Traits.aspx?ID=127)) **Requirements** The nanoshard swarm is in swarm form; **Effect** The nanoshard swarm forms a continuous 6-inch-thick solid wall, up to 60 feet long and 10 feet high, originating from any one square in its current space. The wall can follow any path, with each 5 feet being placed on the border between squares. It doesn't need to stand vertically, so it can form a bridge or set of stairs, for example. The wall must be formed in an unbroken open space where its edges don't pass through any creatures or objects.
A single 5-foot-by-5-foot section of the wall can be destroyed by dealing 18 points of damage to it, which also reduces the swarm's total Hit Points. A nanoshard swarm can't be knocked [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=31) or [forcibly moved](/Rules.aspx?ID=451) while in barrier form, nor can it voluntarily move. A nanoshard swarm in barrier form can originate tendril attacks from any square of its wall. **Battle Form** ([Concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32), [Polymorph](/Traits.aspx?ID=127)) **Requirements** The nanoshard swarm is in swarm form; **Effect** The nanoshard swarm coalesces into a Huge shape that looks like a humanoid or beast and can hold items. In battle form, its Speed is 15 feet, it's clumsy 1, and it has the following Strike.
**Melee** limb +19 ([reach 20 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)), **Damage** 4d8+9 bludgeoning **Swarm Form** ([Concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32)) The nanoshard swarm collapses into its natural form: a Huge sea of tiny metal spheres. It drops anything it's holding. While in swarm form, the nanoshard swarm's Speed is 25 feet, it can move through any area large enough for a single sphere to fit through without having to [Squeeze](/Actions.aspx?ID=31), and it gains Engulf.
[Engulf](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=14) DC 27, 2d8+6 bludgeoning, [Escape](/Actions.aspx?ID=79) DC 27, Rupture 18

The nightwoods are parts of the [Plane of Wood](/Planes.aspx?ID=25) permanently bathed in darkness due to an absence of fluorescent plants. Here, the flora and fauna require darkness, not light, to thrive. [Troll](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=96)-like creatures known as nightwood guardians patrol these woods to ensure they remain in perpetual shadow. Considering themselves righteous gardens, they care little for the excuses of anyone else—intruders or residents. The guardians absolutely loathe the light, though it doesn't harm them as it does some varieties of creatures. Though wary of both light and any interloping lifeforms in their natural habitat, a nightwood guardian's fear turns easily to wrath, making the guardian a force of fury who seeks to drive out intruders. **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 26 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 23 [Nightwood Guardian](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2685) **Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 216 2.0 **Perception** +17; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=12) **Languages** [Fey](/Languages.aspx?ID=119), [Jotun](/Languages.aspx?ID=8), [Muan](/Languages.aspx?ID=108) **Skills** [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) +23, [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=7) +21, [Nightwood Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8) +15 **Str** +6 **Dex** +3 **Con** +6 **Int** +0 **Wis** +2 **Cha** +2 **[Light Blindness](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=22)** **Items** [Club](/Weapons.aspx?ID=2), elemental wooden shield (Hardness 8, Hit Points 64, BT 32) --- **AC** 26 (28 with shield raised) **Fort** +21 **Ref** +16 **Will** +17 **HP** 200 (flesh of wood) **Weaknesses** [axes](/WeaponGroups.aspx?ID=1) 10, [fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=72) 10 **Fire-fueled Rage** When a nightwood guardian takes fire damage, they become enraged. The guardian gains 15 temporary Hit Points, deals 2 additional damage with melee Strikes, and has a –1 penalty to AC. They can't Raise their Shield or use actions with the [concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32) trait except for [Seek](/Actions.aspx?ID=84). This effect ends when the nightwood guardian no longer observes any fire for 1 round or when they fall [unconscious](/Conditions.aspx?ID=38), whichever comes first.
**Flesh of Wood** ([primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=134), [wood](/Traits.aspx?ID=508)) Wounds inflicted on a nightwood guardian turn their flesh to wood. When the guardian is reduced to 40 HP or fewer, their body becomes solid wood. They are [stunned](/Conditions.aspx?ID=36), have resistance 10 to all damage, and have [regeneration](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=26) 40 (deactivated by fire). This ends once the guardian has 100 HP or more, though they can choose to stay in this form indefinitely.
**Shield Eyes** When a nightwood guardian has their shield raised, they protect their eyes, losing the [blinded](/Conditions.aspx?ID=1) and [dazzled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=7) conditions from light blindness and other [light](/Traits.aspx?ID=100) effects.
**[Reactive Strike](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=48)**
**[Shield Block](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=32)** --- **Speed** 30 feet **Melee** club +21 ([reach 10 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)), **Damage** 3d8+6 bludgeoning **Melee** jaws +21 ([reach 10 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)), **Damage** 2d12+6 piercing **Nightwood Roar** ([Concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32), [Darkness](/Traits.aspx?ID=39), [Primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=134)) **Frequency** once per hour; **Effect** The guardian roars, snuffing out lights in a 30-foot cone. Ordinary flames and lights are extinguished, and the guardian attempts to [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) any magical light with a +21 counteract modifier and a counteract rank of 5.

text: Nightwood Guardian The nightwoods are parts of the Plane of Wood permanently bathed in darkness due to an absence of fluorescent plants. Here, the flora and fauna require darkness, not light, to thrive. Troll-like creatures known as nightwood guardians patrol these woods to ensure they remain in perpetual shadow. Considering themselves righteous gardens, they care little for the excuses of anyone else—intruders or residents. The guardians absolutely loathe the light, though it doesn't harm them as it does some varieties of creatures. Though wary of both light and any interloping lifeforms in their natural habitat, a nightwood guardian's fear turns easily to wrath, making the guardian a force of fury who seeks to drive out intruders. Unspecific Lore : DC 26 Specific Lore : DC 23 Nightwood Guardian Source Rage of Elements pg. 216 2.0 Perception +17; darkvision Languages Fey, Jotun, Muan Skills Athletics +23, Intimidation +21, Nightwood Lore +15 Str +6 Dex +3 Con +6 Int +0 Wis +2 Cha +2 Light Blindness Items Club, elemental wooden shield (Hardness 8, Hit Points 64, BT 32) --- AC 26 (28 with shield raised) Fort +21 Ref +16 Will +17 HP 200 (flesh of wood) Weaknesses axes 10, fire 10 Fire-fueled Rage When a nightwood guardian takes fire damage, they become enraged. The guardian gains 15 temporary Hit Points, deals 2 additional damage with melee Strikes, and has a –1 penalty to AC. They can't Raise their Shield or use actions with the concentrate trait except for Seek. This effect ends when the nightwood guardian no longer observes any fire for 1 round or when they fall unconscious, whichever comes first. Flesh of Wood (primal, wood) Wounds inflicted on a nightwood guardian turn their flesh to wood. When the guardian is reduced to 40 HP or fewer, their body becomes solid wood. They are stunned, have resistance 10 to all damage, and have regeneration 40 (deactivated by fire). This ends once the guardian has 100 HP or more, though they can choose to stay in this form indefinitely. Shield Eyes When a nightwood guardian has their shield raised, they protect their eyes, losing the blinded and dazzled conditions from light blindness and other light effects. Reactive Strike Reaction Shield Block Reaction --- Speed 30 feet Melee Single Action club +21 (reach 10 feet), Damage 3d8+6 bludgeoning Melee Single Action jaws +21 (reach 10 feet), Damage 2d12+6 piercing Nightwood Roar Two Actions (Concentrate, Darkness, Primal) Frequency once per hour; Effect The guardian roars, snuffing out lights in a 30-foot cone. Ordinary flames and lights are extinguished, and the guardian attempts to counteract any magical light with a +21 counteract modifier and a counteract rank of 5. Rare Gentleness Though most encounters with nightwood guardians end in violence, the Plane of Wood has many folktales about these giant creatures escorting youngsters lost in the nightwoods safely out of the darkness. Whether these stories are true or wishful thinking is debated, with some arguing that a nightwood guardian would only perform such a kindness on the orders of another creature

This construct is a walking alchemical nightmare capable of inflicting all manner of painful wounds. The noxious needlers' ability to follow orders is granted by the otherwise mindless humanoid brain that floats in their dome-like heads, allowing them to serve as laborers and guards for their creators. In exceptionally rare cases, the brain used in their creation might retain fragments of memories or even an actual intellect, resulting in a noxious needler with a personality and agenda of its own. Unwilling creations often hunt down their creators, venting their rage on similar targets if revenge is impossible. Others blankly replicate the experiments from their last memory. **[Recall Knowledge - Construct](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35), [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=37)): DC 28 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 26 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 23 [Noxious Needler](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3109) **Source** [Monster Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=221) pg. 242 1.1 **Perception** +15; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59) **Languages** **Skills** [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) +22 **Str** +6 **Dex** +4 **Con** +3 **Int** -5 **Wis** +0 **Cha** -5 --- **AC** 27 **Fort** +20 **Ref** +19 **Will** +15 **HP** 150 **Immunities** bleed, [death](/Traits.aspx?ID=571) effects, [disease](/Traits.aspx?ID=578), [doomed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=67), [drained](/Conditions.aspx?ID=68), [fatigued](/Conditions.aspx?ID=73), [healing](/Traits.aspx?ID=623), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647), [nonlethal](/Traits.aspx?ID=661) attacks, [paralyzed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=85), [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=669), [sickened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=91), [spirit](/Traits.aspx?ID=737), [unconscious](/Conditions.aspx?ID=95), [vitality](/Traits.aspx?ID=509), [void](/Traits.aspx?ID=510) **Resistances** physical 10 (except [adamantine](/Equipment.aspx?ID=374) or bludgeoning), spells 10 (except [sonic](/Traits.aspx?ID=697)) **Alchemical Chambers** A noxious needler's body contains six alchemical chambers filled with different substances. When a noxious needler's ability calls upon a randomly determined alchemical effect, roll 1d6 and consult the following (if you roll the result of a chamber that was shattered, there is no alchemical effect): 1 acid damage; 2 cold damage; 3 electricity damage; 4 fire damage; 5 poison damage; 6 sickness, with a DC 26 Fortitude save or [sickened 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=91) (sickened 2 on a critical failure).
**Alchemical Rupture** When a noxious needler takes physical damage from a critical hit or is affected by a [_shatter_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1670) spell, one glass chamber within its body shatters, spewing alchemical liquid in a 5-foot emanation. Roll on the alchemical chambers list (see above) to determine which one shatters—on a roll of 1–5, creatures in the area take 10d6 damage of the appropriate type (DC 28 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex). On a roll of 6, creatures must instead save against the sickness effect. --- **Speed** 25 feet **Melee** syringe +22 ([Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103), [reach 10 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)), **Damage** 2d10+6 piercing plus alchemical injection **Ranged** bomb +20 ([Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103), [thrown 20 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=195)), **Damage** see Generate Bomb **Alchemical Injection** When a noxious needler hits a creature with a syringe Strike, roll 1d6 on the alchemical chambers list to determine the additional effect of the attack. The syringe deals an additional 2d6 damage of the appropriate type (or exposes the target to the sickness effect, as appropriate). **Generate Bomb** ([Manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104)) The needler fills an empty vial from one of its alchemical chambers to create a bomb and then makes a bomb Strike. Roll 1d6 on the alchemical chambers list above. On a roll of 1–5, the bomb deals 3d10 damage and 3 [splash](/Traits.aspx?ID=699) damage, matching the damage type of the chamber; you can instead choose to create an alchemical bomb of 11th level or lower that deals the same damage type, such as an [acid flask](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2875) on a roll of 1. On a roll of 6, it creates a sickness bomb, which exposes the target and all creatures in the splash radius to the sickness effect; creatures hit by only the splash receive a +2 circumstance bonus to their Fortitude saves.

When pollution despoils a natural waterway, it draws the dreaded nuckelavee to it from the [First World](/Planes.aspx?ID=35). This spirit of wrath is a grisly sight to behold: a horselike monstrosity with the gnarled upper body of a humanoid growing directly from its back. Further enhancing its awfulness, not a patch of skin exists on the misshapen hybrid form, as though it survived its own flaying. When a nuckelavee rides forth from its domain, it wreaks a trail of destruction across the land surrounding its path. Nuckelavees are considered among the cruelest and most monstrous fey, seen by some as just desserts visited upon those who would befoul the waters of their homes. A nuckelavee, however, doesn't discriminate between those who pollute and those who merely have the misfortune to be in the wrong place at the wrong time. Despite their vile reputation among humanoids, nuckelavees are generally respectful of their fey counterparts. Once pollution has been cleansed and water fey like [naiads](/Monsters.aspx?ID=311) return to a body of water, nuckelavees will peacefully withdraw. **[Recall Knowledge - Fey](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43)): DC 26 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 24 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 21 [Nuckelavee](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3110) **Source** [Monster Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=221) pg. 243 1.1 **Perception** +16; [low-light vision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=69) **Languages** [Aklo](/Languages.aspx?ID=13), [Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1), [Fey](/Languages.aspx?ID=119) **Skills** [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) +19, [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=7) +19, [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=10) +16, [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15) +18, [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=16) +16 **Str** +6 **Dex** +3 **Con** +4 **Int** +1 **Wis** +3 **Cha** +4 **Items** _+1 [striking](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2829) [bastard sword](/Weapons.aspx?ID=370)_ --- **AC** 28 **Fort** +19 **Ref** +16 **Will** +20 **HP** 190 **Immunities** [disease](/Traits.aspx?ID=578), [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=669) **Weaknesses** [cold iron](/Equipment.aspx?ID=375) 10 **[Frightful Presence](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=64)** ([aura](/Traits.aspx?ID=542), [emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=590), [fear](/Traits.aspx?ID=598), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647)) 30 feet, DC 25
**Purity Vulnerability** Unpolluted fresh water burns a nuckelavee like acid, dealing 1d6 damage to it and causing it to be [sickened 2](/Conditions.aspx?ID=91). A nuckelavee can't heal from damage when it's in an area that isn't polluted (subject to GM discretion).
**[Reactive Strike](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=48)** --- **Speed** 40 feet, swim 40 feet **Melee** _bastard sword_ +21 ([Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103), [reach 10 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192), [two-hand d12](/Traits.aspx?ID=198)), **Damage** 2d8+12 slashing plus 1d6 poison and mortasheen **Melee** jaws +20 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170)), **Damage** 2d8+12 piercing plus 1d6 poison and mortasheen **Melee** hoof +20, **Damage** 2d6+12 bludgeoning plus mortasheen **Primal Innate Spells** DC 28 - **3rd** [Aqueous Orb](/Spells.aspx?ID=1443) - **5th** [Control Water](/Spells.aspx?ID=51) **Rituals** DC 28 - **4th** [Blight](/Rituals.aspx?ID=4) **Blight Breath** ([Disease](/Traits.aspx?ID=46), [Poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=126), [Primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=134)) The nuckelavee breathes a 30-foot cone of foulness, dealing 8d6 void damage to living creatures in the area with a DC 28 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Fortitude save. text: Nuckelavee When pollution despoils a natural waterway, it draws the dreaded nuckelavee to it from the First World. This spirit of wrath is a grisly sight to behold: a horselike monstrosity with the gnarled upper body of a humanoid growing directly from its back. Further enhancing its awfulness, not a patch of skin exists on the misshapen hybrid form, as though it survived its own flaying. When a nuckelavee rides forth from its domain, it wreaks a trail of destruction across the land surrounding its path. Nuckelavees are considered among the cruelest and most monstrous fey, seen by some as just desserts visited upon those who would befoul the waters of their homes. A nuckelavee, however, doesn't discriminate between those who pollute and those who merely have the misfortune to be in the wrong place at the wrong time. Despite their vile reputation among humanoids, nuckelavees are generally respectful of their fey counterparts. Once pollution has been cleansed and water fey like naiads return to a body of water, nuckelavees will peacefully withdraw. A creature that fails also takes 2d6 persistent bleed damage. The nuckelavee can't use Blight Breath again for 1d4 rounds. Mortasheen (Disease) The target can't recover from the fatigued condition caused by mortasheen until the disease is cured. At a distance, painted stags appear constructed in the general shape of male deer, their flanks and antlers decorated with unique, colorful patterns. But while they retain (and indeed, augment) the blueprints [Shumunue](/Deities.aspx?ID=275) imparted upon them, painted stags reject the confines of the Carved Lady's art of mimicry. Today, their cloven, hardwood hooves can crush bone and daub paint with equal skill, and their antlers snap together in a deadly vise. Their torsos rotate freely to navigate the latticed trees of their home plane—all the better to chase prey to their inevitable death. **[Recall Knowledge - Elemental](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=2), [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=10)): DC 26 **[Recall Knowledge - Plant](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=10)): DC 26 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 24 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 21 [Painted Stag](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2678) **Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 210 2.0 **Perception** +21 **Languages** **Skills** [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) +18, [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=7) +23, [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=10) +18 **Str** +7 **Dex** +3 **Con** +5 **Int** +2 **Wis** +1 **Cha** +4 --- **AC** 27 **Fort** +18 **Ref** +12 **Will** +21 **HP** 175 , regeneration 10 (deactivated by [fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=72)) **Immunities** bleed, [paralyzed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=28), [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=126), [sleep](/Traits.aspx?ID=145) **Weaknesses** [axes](/WeaponGroups.aspx?ID=1) 10, fire 10 --- **Speed** 45 feet, climb 60 feet **Melee** antler +20, **Damage** 2d12+7 piercing plus [Grab](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=45) **Melee** hooves +20, **Damage** 2d10+7 bludgeoning **Mauler** A painted stag gains a +5 circumstance bonus to damage rolls against creatures it has [grabbed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=20). **Painted Dance** ([Auditory](/Traits.aspx?ID=16), [Mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=106), [Plant](/Traits.aspx?ID=125), [Primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=134), [Visual](/Traits.aspx?ID=163)) The stag shakes the wooden plating along its body in a cacophonous clatter that sets its painted patterns dancing. All creatures within 60 feet of the painted stag who can see or hear it must attempt a DC 28 Will save; a creature [grabbed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=20) by the stag takes a –4 circumstance penalty to its save. Regardless of the result of its save, each creature is temporarily immune for 1 hour.
**Critical Success** The creature is unaffected.
**Success** The creature is [fascinated](/Conditions.aspx?ID=14) by the painted stag for 1 round.
**Failure** The creature is [stunned 2](/Conditions.aspx?ID=36) and fascinated by the painted stag for as long as it's stunned.
**Critical Failure** As failure, except stunned 4.

A putrifer is a decaying plant creature that refuses to die, even as its body rots away. Similar in shape and appearance to a rotting [ghoran](/Ancestries.aspx?ID=52), the flowers, leaves, bark, and rinds that compose a putrifer's body weep toxic black fluids. These disgusting secretions emit a foul-smelling miasma that surrounds the putrifer. Most putrifers arise spontaneously when a [gathlain](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=237), ghoran, [leshy](/Ancestries.aspx?ID=65), or other intelligent plant dies traumatically from an effect that causes swift rot and decay. Others are created, either purposefully by necromancers or incidentally during magical experiments. Regardless of origin, a putrifer loses much of its intelligence during the transformation, becoming aggressive, erratic, and easily confused. Putrifers act instinctively, often lingering around the places they frequented in life. They find comfort in patterns and usually form simple daily routines that they loathe to deviate from. Often, these routines echo those they performed in life. A putrifer's memories are distant and faded, returning only periodically in short, confusing bursts that drive the putrifer to reenact moments from their past lives. <title level="1" pfs="Standard">[Roc](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3170)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

These legendary, massive raptors, capable of carrying off elephants as prey, are typically about 30 feet long from beak to tail and have a wingspan of 80 feet or more. While their beaks are hooked to rip flesh from bone, their hunting strategy involves grabbing their prey in their powerful talons and then dropping it from great heights before feeding. This method creates a massive amount of carrion, which guarantees that rocs are followed by flocks of opportunistic scavengers, such as ravens and buzzards, who find it easy to steal bits of the larger birds' meals. Rocs, for the most part, don't mind these creatures, which sometimes get gobbled up along with the rest of the roc's food.

 Rocs usually nest among mountaintops and cliffs inaccessible to all but the bravest of terrestrial dwellers. They are long-range predators that hunt both land and sea in search for massive prey to sustain them and their young. Rocs are antisocial and lone hunters who compete with each other in fierce aerial battles to protect territory. But about once a decade, a mating couple pairs up to raise their chicks. Once the chicks are old enough to hunt on their own, the parents separate to once again engage in lone hunting. Particularly skilled druids or rangers might capture and train a roc to serve as a flying mount or hunting companion, though examples of such an incredible feat of domestication are few and far between. The easiest way to rear a roc is to do so from the moment it hatches, since the chick imprints on the first creature it sees. Acquiring a roc egg is by no means an easy feat, though, and is often a death sentence for the would-be egg-snatcher.

Rocs are antisocial and lone hunters who compete with each other in fierce aerial battles to protect territory. But about once a decade, a mating couple pairs up to raise their chicks. Once the chicks are old enough to hunt on their own, the parents separate to once again engage in lone hunting. Particularly skilled druids or rangers might capture and train a roc to serve as a flying mount or hunting companion, though examples of such an incredible feat of domestication are few and far between. The easiest way to rear a roc is to do so from the moment it hatches, since the chick imprints on the first creature it sees. Acquiring a roc egg is by no means an easy feat, though, and is often a death sentence for the would-be egg-snatcher.

Root rotters are all that remain of the unfortunate elven residents of Greengold. Some died in the initial bursts of Jeharlu spores, while others succumbed to infestation by sinmolds. Fungus now riddles their bodies, wrapping around their brains and nerves to reanimate them. **[Recall Knowledge - Fungus](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43)): DC 31 **[Recall Knowledge - Undead](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46)): DC 31 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 29 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 26 [Root Rotter](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3779) **Source** [Pathfinder #210: Whispers in the Dirt](/Sources.aspx?ID=253) pg. 85 **Perception** +18; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59), fungus sense 120 feet **Languages** [Chthonian](/Languages.aspx?ID=114), [Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1), [Elven](/Languages.aspx?ID=4); [telepathy](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=79) 30 feet ([fungi](/Traits.aspx?ID=614) only) **Skills** [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=34) +20, [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) +17, [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43) +15, [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=48) +18 **Str** +6 **Dex** +5 **Con** +4 **Int** +0 **Wis** +3 **Cha** +2 **Fungus Sense** A root rotter has imprecise tremorsense to detect the vibrations of creatures who are within a region of fungal terrain shared by the root rotter. --- **AC** 26 **Fort** +17 **Ref** +20 **Will** +16 **HP** 195 ([void healing](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=83)) **Immunities** bleed, [death](/Traits.aspx?ID=571) effects, [disease](/Traits.aspx?ID=578), [paralyzed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=85), [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=669), [unconscious](/Conditions.aspx?ID=95) **Weaknesses** [holy](/Traits.aspx?ID=517) 10, slashing 10 **Fungal Empowerment** If the root rotter is touching fungal terrain at the start of its turn, they regain 10 Hit Points and are [quickened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=89) that turn; they can use the extra action only to Stride or Strike.
**Fungal Mind** ([primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=676)) Root rotters communicate telepathically with each other. While within telepathic range of at least one other root rotter, they gain a +2 circumstance bonus to initiative rolls, Perception checks, and saving throws against [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647) effects. If one root rotter is aware of a combatant, all members of the fungal mind within range are aware of it. --- **Speed** 30 feet **Melee** jaws +21 ([Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103), [Poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=126), [Unholy](/Traits.aspx?ID=521)), **Damage** 2d8+9 piercing plus 1d8 poison and rotter infestation **Melee** fist +21 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103), [Unholy](/Traits.aspx?ID=521)), **Damage** 2d8+9 bludgeoning **Disperse** ([Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103), [Poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=126), [Unholy](/Traits.aspx?ID=521)) **Requirements** The root rotter has 25 Hit Points or fewer; **Effect** The root rotter destroys themself. Thorny fungal roots explode from their body, dealing 10d6 piercing damage in a 10-foot emanation (DC 25 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save). Any creature who fails the save is exposed to rotter infestation. **Fungal Root** ([Divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=48), [Poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=126), [Unholy](/Traits.aspx?ID=521)) Requirements The root rotter is standing in fungal terrain; Effect Fungal roots reach out to snag a nearby foe. An enemy within 30 feet of the root rotter takes 4d6 piercing damage and must attempt a DC 27 Reflex saving throw.
**Critical Success** The creature is unaffected.
**Success** The creature takes half damage and becomes clumsy 1 until the end of its next turn.
**Failure** The creature takes full damage and becomes clumsy 1 with an unlimited duration. In addition, the creature is restrained (Escape DC 27) for 1 minute.
**Critical Failure** As failure but double damage. In addition, the creature is exposed to rotter infestation. **Rotter Infestation** ([Disease](/Traits.aspx?ID=46), [Divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=48)) **Saving Throw** DC 27 Fortitude; **Onset** 1 day; **Stage 1** [drained 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=68) (1 day); **Stage 2** drained 2 and can sense the presence of root rotters within 30 feet as an [imprecise](/Rules.aspx?ID=412) sense (1 round); **Stage 3** as stage 2, but transformation into a root rotter upon death (1 day)

<title level="1" pfs="">[Soniphak](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3269)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

Often mistaken for drakes, soniphaks glide above rocky or barren ground, picking out prey with their hearing. A hunting soniphak disables its targets with concentrated bursts of sound before snatching them up and feasting on the move. Despite being able to speak, soniphaks are no more social than other dischorans, generally responding to even the quietest attempts at communication with destructive shouting.

<column gap="tiny">
**[Recall Knowledge - Beast](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**
([Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35), [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43)): DC 26

**[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 24

**[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 21
</column>

</column>

<column gap="medium">
<image src="/images/Monsters/Dischoran_Soniphak.webp" />
</column>

</row>

<title level="2" right="Creature 9">[Soniphak](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3269)</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Huge" />
<trait label="Beast" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=547" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Howl of the Wild](/Sources.aspx?ID=226) pg. 141 <sup>2.1</sup>

**Perception** +21; no vision, sensitive echolocation ([precise](/Rules.aspx?ID=411)) 120 feet

**Languages**
[Draconic](/Languages.aspx?ID=2)

**Skills**
[Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=34) +19, [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) +20, [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=49) +17

<row gap="medium">
**Str** +7

**Dex** +6

**Con** +4

**Int** -2

**Wis** +4

**Cha** +1
</row>

Sensitive Echolocation The soniphak can use its hearing as a [precise sense](/Rules.aspx?ID=411) with the listed range. If the soniphak takes sonic damage beyond its resistance, its senses are overloaded and all creatures are [concealed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=62) from it for 1 round.

</column>

---

<column gap="tiny">

<row gap="medium">
**AC** 27 

**Fort** +21 

**Ref** +21 

**Will** +15 

</row>

<row gap="medium">
**HP** 180

</row>

**Immunities**
[visual](/Traits.aspx?ID=727)

**Resistances**
sonic 10

**Disruptive Screech** <actions string="Reaction" /> **Trigger** A creature within 30 feet of the soniphak uses an [auditory](/Traits.aspx?ID=541) action; **Effect** The soniphak makes a screech Strike against the triggering creature. This disrupts a triggering [concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561) action if the Strike is a critical hit.

</column>

---

<column gap="tiny">

**Speed** 20 feet, fly 50 feet

**Melee**
<actions string="Single Action" />
jaws +19 ([reach 15 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)),
**Damage** 3d8+9 piercing

**Melee**
<actions string="Single Action" />
claw +19 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170)),
**Damage** 3d6+9 slashing plus [Grab](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=45)

**Ranged**
<actions string="Single Action" />
screech +19 ([range 60 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=248), [Sonic](/Traits.aspx?ID=147)),
**Damage** 6d6 sonic plus aftershock

**Aftershock**   Whenever a soniphak hits with a screech Strike, feedback deals each creature the soniphak has [grabbed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=77) or [restrained](/Conditions.aspx?ID=90) 1d6 sonic damage.

**Shattering Scream** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([Sonic](/Traits.aspx?ID=147)) The soniphak can focus its screech at a stone or rock surface within 60 feet to create an explosion in a 15-foot burst from the point of impact. Creatures in the area take 5d6 piercing damage (DC 28 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save), and the area becomes [difficult terrain](/Rules.aspx?ID=453) due to fragments of loose stone.

**Snatch**   The soniphak can [Fly](/Actions.aspx?ID=2312) at half Speed with a creature [grabbed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=77) or [restrained](/Conditions.aspx?ID=90) in its claws, carrying that creature along with it.

</column>
