The most iconic rakshasas, raja-krodhas are tiger-headed hunters of mortalkind. They are incarnations of all the malice people try to deny within themselves and instead wrongly ascribe to deadly predators of the wild. Their power and skill inspire fear, but also awe, and it is not unknown for some peoples to treat such a rakshasa as a guardian, if one to be treated with extreme caution. Despite their nature as brutal flesh-eaters, rajas are extremely eloquent and philosophical when they choose to be. This is simply another form of camouflage, one that allows them to blend into cities, much as their stripes allow them to fade into jungles, and it often lulls scholars and intellectuals into a false sense of security. While it is not in the nature of a raja-krodha to be a social schemer or a mastermind, it pleases them when others delude themselves into thinking they are. **[Recall Knowledge - Spirit](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=44)): DC 27 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 25 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 22 [Raja-Krodha](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3161) **Source** [Monster Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=221) pg. 287 1.1 **Perception** +18; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59) **Languages** [Chthonian](/Languages.aspx?ID=114), [Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1), [Diabolic](/Languages.aspx?ID=117), [Empyrean](/Languages.aspx?ID=115), [Sakvroth](/Languages.aspx?ID=118) **Skills** [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) +19, [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5) +21, [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=6) +21, [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=7) +21, [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=12) +19, [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=13) +18, [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15) +23 **Str** +6 **Dex** +6 **Con** +4 **Int** +2 **Wis** +2 **Cha** +5 **Items** _+1 [striking](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2829) taravari_ (functions as a [scimitar](/Weapons.aspx?ID=393)) --- **AC** 30 **Fort** +18 **Ref** +20 **Will** +18 +2 status to all saves vs. [magic](/Traits.aspx?ID=644) **HP** 180 **Weaknesses** [holy](/Traits.aspx?ID=517) 10, Immunities [fear](/Traits.aspx?ID=598), [fortune](/Traits.aspx?ID=612), [misfortune](/Traits.aspx?ID=654) **Knowledge of Delusion** ([divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=579)) A creature that fails a [Recall Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=2367) check or a Perception check to [Sense Motive](/Actions.aspx?ID=2302) on a rakshasa is [off-guard](/Conditions.aspx?ID=58) until the end of its next turn.
**Reassert Fate** ([divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=579)) **Trigger** A creature within 30 feet uses a [fortune](/Traits.aspx?ID=612) or [misfortune](/Traits.aspx?ID=654) effect; **Effect** The raja-krodha reasserts the ebb and flow of fate, instilling a deep dread in those who would attempt to cheat their written role. <row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

Rekheps are the living shields that defend [Heaven](/Planes.aspx?ID=41) against fiendish incursions. They tile together in massive formations capable of withstanding any onslaught. Given their tremendous strength and imposing stature, shield archons are ideal guardians of the meek and are sometimes summoned to the mortal [Universe](/Planes.aspx?ID=26)to ward off the attacks of great numbers of evildoers.

<column gap="tiny">
**[Recall Knowledge - Celestial](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**
([Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46)): DC 27

**[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 25

**[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 22
</column>

</column>

<column gap="medium">
<image src="/images/Monsters/Rekhep.webp" />
</column>

</row>

<title level="2" right="Creature 10">[Rekhep](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2835)</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Large" />
<trait label="Archon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=536" />
<trait label="Celestial" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=551" />
<trait label="Holy" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=517" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Monster Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=221) pg. 28 <sup>1.1</sup>

**Perception** +19; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59)

**Languages**
[Diabolic](/Languages.aspx?ID=117), [Draconic](/Languages.aspx?ID=2), [Empyrean](/Languages.aspx?ID=115), [Utopian](/Languages.aspx?ID=36); [_truespeech_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1728)

**Skills**
[Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) +21, [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=6) +19, [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=7) +19, [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=13) +19, [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=16) +17

<row gap="medium">
**Str** +5

**Dex** +1

**Con** +7

**Int** +2

**Wis** +3

**Cha** +3
</row>

**Items**
_+1 [striking](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2829) [lance](/Weapons.aspx?ID=383)_

</column>

---

<column gap="tiny">

<row gap="medium">
**AC** 31 [all-around vision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=49)

**Fort** +23 

**Ref** +15 

**Will** +19 

+1 status to all saves vs. [magic](/Traits.aspx?ID=644)
</row>

<row gap="medium">
**HP** 150

</row>

**Immunities**
[fear](/Traits.aspx?ID=598)

**Weaknesses**
[unholy](/Traits.aspx?ID=521) 10

**Archon's Protection** <actions string="Reaction" /> **Trigger** An enemy damages the archon's ally and both are within 15 feet of the archon; **Effect** The ally gains resistance 15 to all damage against the triggering damage and the archon can make a Strike against the enemy.

</column>

---

<column gap="tiny">

**Speed** 30 feet, fly 60 feet

**Melee**
<actions string="Single Action" />
_holy lance_ +22 ([deadly d8](/Traits.aspx?ID=174), [Divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=48), [Holy](/Traits.aspx?ID=517), [jousting d6](/Traits.aspx?ID=186), [reach 10 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)),
**Damage** 2d8+11 piercing plus 1d4 spirit (or 2d4 spirit vs. an [unholy](/Traits.aspx?ID=521) target)

**Divine Innate Spells** DC 27
- **Cantrips (5th)**
[Divine Lance](/Spells.aspx?ID=84), [Message](/Spells.aspx?ID=190)
- **1st**
[Sure Strike](/Spells.aspx?ID=1709) (×3)
- **2nd**
[Share Life](/Spells.aspx?ID=1669) (×3)
- **4th**
[Translocate](/Spells.aspx?ID=1724) (at will)
- **Constant (5th)**
[Truespeech](/Spells.aspx?ID=1728)

**Archon's Pursuit** <actions string="Two Actions" />  **Frequency** once per day; **Requirements** The rekhep saw another creature teleport within the last round and has at least one [_translocate_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1724) spell remaining; **Effect** The rekhep casts one of their _translocate_ spells, which is heightened to 5th rank and causes the rekhep to arrive in an unoccupied space it chooses within 30 feet of the creature it's pursuing. If the creature is too far away, the rekhep arrives as close as possible.

**Courageous Switch**   When a rekhep uses their [_translocate_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1724) innate spell, they can choose to move into the space of a willing ally they can see within range. If they do, the ally switches places with the archon, appearing in the space the archon just vacated, as if it too had cast _translocate_.

**Holy Armament**  ([Divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=48), [Holy](/Traits.aspx?ID=517)) Any weapon gains the [_holy_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2842) rune while the rekhep wields it.

**Living Shield** <actions string="Single Action" />  The rekhep grants an adjacent ally a +2 circumstance bonus to AC until they're no longer adjacent or until the start of the archon's next turn, whichever comes first. When the rekhep uses Archon's Protection against an attack against the shielded ally, the rekhep gains the resistance and takes the damage rather than the ally.

**Terrifying Smite** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([Emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=60), [Fear](/Traits.aspx?ID=68), [Mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=106)) The rekhep makes a Strike against an enemy that has one of the rekhep's allies within its reach. On a hit, the target takes an additional 2d8 mental damage and is [frightened 2](/Conditions.aspx?ID=76). The extra damage and frightened value are doubled on a critical hit.

</column>

Rezzelkis are curious-looking beasts native to the deserts of Osirion. Three feet tall at the shoulder and five feet long, rezzelkis are squat, mammalian quadrupeds with tawny red fur, with crystal-studded flat tails, and prehensile anteater-like snouts. Their long, pink tongues are covered with hundreds of tiny, razor-sharp bristles that allow them to rasp through flesh with unnerving ease, even before accounting for the effect of their acidic saliva. Rezzelkis are ferociously territorial and quick to attack anyone or anything they regard as intruding upon their territory. Yet they're also prone to strange gastronomic obsessions, and if someone can deduce a particular rezzelki's favorite food, it's possible to become the creature's ally by simply providing it regular access to its preferred meals. A specific rezzelki's favorite food is always a specific type of creature— some even prefer to dine exclusively on the dry bodies of undead like [mummies](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=445)—but most have a taste for a singular humanoid ancestry. Presented with a potential meal, the rezzelki moves quickly to smash its feast with its wide tail. Then it feeds upon the pulverized remains of the destroyed creature, slurping up battered flesh and powdered bones with a noisy gusto that has earned them a strange nickname in certain circles: “deathlicker.” **[Recall Knowledge - Beast](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35), [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43)): DC 29 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 27 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 24 [Rezzelki](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3742) **Source** [Pathfinder #204: Stage Fright](/Sources.aspx?ID=245) pg. 88 **Perception** +21; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59), glutton scent ([imprecise](/Rules.aspx?ID=412)) 60 feet **Languages** [Osiriani](/Languages.aspx?ID=40); (can't speak) **Skills** [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) +22 **Str** +6 **Dex** +3 **Con** +5 **Int** -3 **Wis** +3 **Cha** +2 **Glutton Scent** A rezzelki's scent ability becomes a [precise](/Rules.aspx?ID=411) sense against its favored meal. --- **AC** 29 **Fort** +21 **Ref** +17 **Will** +19 **HP** 175 **Resistances** [acid](/Traits.aspx?ID=524) 10 **Favored Meal** All rezzelkis have a favorite type of creature to feast upon (see the Rezzelki Hunger sidebar). Against a favored meal in combat, a rezzelki gains a +1 circumstance bonus to all Strikes and [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) checks.
**Reactive Taste** ([primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=676)) **Trigger** A creature within reach of the rezzelki's tongue uses a [manipulate](/Actions.aspx?ID=2229) or a [move](/Traits.aspx?ID=658) action, makes a ranged attack, or leaves a square during a move action it's using; **Effect** The rezzelki makes a tongue Strike against the triggering creature. --- **Speed** 25 feet, fly 20 feet **Melee** tail +22 ([Forceful](/Traits.aspx?ID=180)), **Damage** 2d12+10 bludgeoning plus [Knockdown](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=46) **Melee** tongue +22 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [reach 10 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)), **Damage** 2d6+6 slashing plus 1d6 acid **Primal Innate Spells** DC 29 - **Constant (5th)** [Fly](/Spells.aspx?ID=125) **Fracturing Smash** ([Attack](/Traits.aspx?ID=15)) The rezzelki Strikes a target with a particularly powerful blow from its tail, with enough force to potentially pulverize bone. This Strike treats any object it hits as if it had half as much Hardness as usual, unless the object's hardness is greater than the rezzelki's level. <title level="1" pfs="">[Shanty Chanter](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3746)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

Shanty chanters are known to dwell along the coasts of Garund or the eastern isles of the Shackles, living on small islands or cliffsides but rarely venturing too far inland. These capricious fey have humanoid torsos and seagull heads, wings, and feet, and they stand about 5 feet tall. Consummate performers, shanty chanters adore music, especially the sea shanties sung by ships' crews. The songs from these fey's aeries can be heard from miles away over the open sea. While some sailors claim these songs intentionally lure mortals to drown, most shanty chanters aren't outright malevolent and would be more inclined to investigate a foundering ship than to slaughter those aboard, even if they do relieve such a vessel of its valuables.

 Shanty chanters have a particular affinity for pirate ships, and a captain who wins an alliance with an aerie of shanty chanters is considered blessed with good luck. Of course, this attention can be a double-edged sword. If a captain fails to appease the ship's allied shanty chanters (generally by giving them a fair share of the plunder gained while they're on board), the affronted fey afflicts the captain with a mariner's curse before departing for more prosperous shores.

These enormous three-legged elementals resemble crows with flaming feathers, said to shine as bright as the sun. They nest in the smoldering Forest of Mulberry Coals, living in flocks of eight to a dozen, with ten being the most common. **[Recall Knowledge - Elemental](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=2), [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=10)): DC 27 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 25 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 22 [Solar Crow](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2634) **Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 128 2.0 **Perception** +19; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=12), smoke vision **Languages** [Pyric](/Languages.aspx?ID=110) **Skills** [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=1) +22, [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5) +21, [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=10) +19, [Sun Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8) +18, [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) +22 **Str** +2 **Dex** +6 **Con** +2 **Int** +0 **Wis** +3 **Cha** +5 **Smoke Vision** Smoke doesn't impair a solar crow's vision; they ignore the [concealed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=4) condition from smoke. --- **AC** 30 **Fort** +18 **Ref** +22 **Will** +17 **HP** 170 **Immunities** bleed, [fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=72), [paralyzed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=28), [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=126), [sleep](/Traits.aspx?ID=145) **Glow** ([aura](/Traits.aspx?ID=206), [fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=72), [light](/Traits.aspx?ID=100)) 25 feet. The solar crow casts [bright light](/Rules.aspx?ID=407) in a 25-foot emanation (and [dim light](/Rules.aspx?ID=408) for the next 25 feet).
**Glinting Wing** ([light](/Traits.aspx?ID=100), [visual](/Traits.aspx?ID=163)) **Trigger** A creature within 120 feet attempts to target the solar crow; **Effect** The solar crow defensively repositions a wing to shine light into the attacker's eyes. The target is [dazzled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=7) for the duration of the triggering effect, granting the solar crow [concealment](/Conditions.aspx?ID=4) against it. --- **Speed** 20 feet, fly 50 feet **Melee** beak +22 ([Finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=179)), **Damage** 2d10+8 piercing plus 2d6 fire **Melee** talon +22 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [Finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=179)), **Damage** 1d10+8 slashing plus 2d6 fire plus [Grab](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=45) **Blinding Heat** ([Fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=72), [Incapacitation](/Traits.aspx?ID=93), [Light](/Traits.aspx?ID=100), [Visual](/Traits.aspx?ID=163)) The solar crow expands its wings and unleashes blazing hot, blinding light in a 120-foot emanation. Each creature in the area takes 9d6 fire damage with a DC 29 Reflex save. The crow can't use Blinding Heat again for 1d4 rounds, and its glow aura is deactivated during this time.
**Critical Success** The creature is unaffected.
**Success** The creature takes half damage and is [dazzled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=7) for 1 round.
**Failure** The creature takes full damage and is [blinded](/Conditions.aspx?ID=1) for 1 round.
**Critical Failure** The creature takes double damage and is blinded for 1 minute. **Burning Talons** A creature [grabbed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=20) by the solar crow takes 1d4 [persistent fire damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29). It can't recover from this damage while grabbed by the crow. **Snatch** A solar crow can [Fly](/Actions.aspx?ID=94) at half Speed while it has a creature [grabbed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=20) or [restrained](/Conditions.aspx?ID=33) in its talons, carrying that creature along with it.
name: Solar Crow

Powerful deities and warlords strive for dominance over the [Plane of Fire](/Planes.aspx?ID=6) and the rest of the Inner Sphere in order to prove fire's supremacy. Armies of flaming soldiers go to war against each other on battlefields of smoke and smoldering char, all unable to bring their full power to bear. [Ymeri](/Deities.aspx?ID=108), the vicious and victorious Queen of the Inferno, commands legions of sootsoldiers: elementals capable of battling the armies of her foes and, even when destroyed, rising from the ashes of the Eternal Furnace, scorched and triumphant. **[Recall Knowledge - Elemental](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=2), [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=10)): DC 27 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 25 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 22 [Sootsoldiers](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2639) **Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 133 2.0 **Perception** +20; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=12), smoke vision **Languages** [Pyric](/Languages.aspx?ID=110) **Skills** [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=1) +21, [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) +21, [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=10) +18, [Plane of Fire Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8) +18, [Warfare Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8) +18 **Str** +7 **Dex** +5 **Con** +6 **Int** +2 **Wis** +4 **Cha** +0 **Smoke Vision** Sootsoldiers ignore the [concealed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=4) condition from smoke. --- **AC** 30 **Fort** +20 **Ref** +21 **Will** +18 **HP** 165 (16 squares) **Immunities** bleed, [fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=72), [paralyzed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=28), [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=126), [sleep](/Traits.aspx?ID=145) **Weaknesses** area damage 10, [cold](/Traits.aspx?ID=27) 10, [splash](/Traits.aspx?ID=150) damage 10 **Ashen Smoke** When the sootsoldiers are reduced by an HP Threshold or are reduced to 0 HP, the destroyed soldiers crumble to a cloud of ash-laden smoke in 20-foot burst centered on the sootsoldiers. All creatures within the cloud are [concealed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=4), and all creatures outside it are concealed to those inside. The smoke lasts for 1 minute or until dispersed by a strong wind.
**[Troop Defenses](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=44)** --- **Speed** 40 feet; [troop movement](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=85) **Incinerating Grasp** **Frequency** once per round; **Effect** The sootsoldiers reach to constrain each enemy in a 5-foot emanation in their fiery clutches (DC 26 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save). The damage and additional effects depend on the number of actions.
2d8 fire damage
3d8+7 fire damage plus [grabbed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=20)
4d8+7 fire damage plus grabbed **Seething Flash** ([Fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=72), [Primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=134)) The sootsoldiers reignite and rush across the battlefield, Forming Up and Striding twice. At the end of this movement, a wave of flame and heat pours off the sootsoldiers, dealing 4d8 fire damage to other creatures in a 10-foot emanation, with a DC 29 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save. A creature that critically fails its save is also knocked [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=31).

Only completing a consecrate ritual heightened to at least 6th level in the place where the spectral devil was defeated, which consecrates the site of the spectral devil's destruction to a good deity, can prevent the spectral devil from returning and haunting the world once more.

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

Spitting sawflies are enormous, bloated insects covered in tumor-like knots of spores. These ravenous pests sow disease and spores wherever they go, heralding the infestation of creeping cones.

<column gap="tiny">
**[Recall Knowledge - Beast](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**
([Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35), [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43)): DC 32

**[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 30

**[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 27
</column>

</column>

<column gap="medium">

</column>

</row>

<title level="2" right="Creature 10">[Spitting Sawfly](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3727)</title>

<traits>

<trait label="Medium" />
<trait label="Beast" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=547" />
<trait label="Mutant" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=763" />
<trait label="Wood" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=508" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #203 Shepherd of Decay](/Sources.aspx?ID=243) pg. 80

**Perception** +19; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59), wood scent ([precise](/Rules.aspx?ID=411)) 30 feet

**Languages**

**Skills**
[Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=34) +22, [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) +20

<row gap="medium">

**Con** +5

**Int** -5

**Wood Scent** A spitting sawfly can smell plants and wood as a precise scent at the listed range.

</column>

<row gap="medium">

**Ref** +22 

**Will** +16 

</row>

<row gap="medium">
**HP** 175

</row>

[acid](/Traits.aspx?ID=524)

[poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=669) 10

</column>

---

<column gap="tiny">

**Speed** 20 feet, climb 20 feet, fly 40 feet

**Melee**
<actions string="Single Action" />
mandibles +22 ([Finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=179), [Poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=126)),
**Damage** 2d12+10 piercing plus seizing venom

**Ranged**
<actions string="Single Action" />
acid spit +22 ([Poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=126), [range increment 30 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=248)),
**Damage** 4d8 acid plus seizing venom

**Consume Essence** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([Healing](/Traits.aspx?ID=89), [Manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104), [Primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=134)) **Frequency** once per day; **Requirements** The spitting sawfly is adjacent to a creature with the [wood](/Traits.aspx?ID=508) trait or to a coiled conifer; **Effect** The sawfly feasts upon the targeted creature or the coiled conifer's sap, regaining 5d6 Hit Points. A targeted creature must attempt a DC 29 Fortitude save or become [drained 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=68) (drained 2 on a critical failure).

**Creeping Sprout**  ([Disease](/Traits.aspx?ID=46)) A creature afflicted with creeping sprout is treated by the spitting sawfly as if it has the [wood](/Traits.aspx?ID=508) trait; **Saving Throw** DC 29 Fortitude; **Stage 1** carrier with no ill effect (1d4 days); **Stage 2** [drained 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=68) (1d4 days); **Stage 3** 12d6 acid damage, creeping cone swarm emerges (disease ends)

**Plant Spores** <actions string="Single Action" />  The spitting sawfly plants spores in an adjacent creature that's [paralyzed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=85) or [unconscious](/Conditions.aspx?ID=95), exposing it to creeping sprout disease.

**Seizing Venom**  ([Incapacitation](/Traits.aspx?ID=93), [Poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=126)) **Saving Throw** DC 29 Fortitude; **Maximum Duration** 6 rounds; **Stage 1** [off-guard](/Conditions.aspx?ID=58) and [slowed 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=92) (1 round); **Stage 2** off-guard and slowed 2 (1 round); **Stage 3** [paralyzed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=85) (1 round)

</column>

Razmir's most powerful priests deploy tithekeepers to ensure his followers don't develop sticky fingers. These ziggurat-like constructs have over two dozen legs and a trap-like mouth. At its top, a mask with a colored ribbon attached denotes its symbolic rank in the Church of Razmir. **[Recall Knowledge - Construct](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35), [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=37)): DC 32 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 30 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 27 [Tithekeeper](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3781) **Source** [Pathfinder #210: Whispers in the Dirt](/Sources.aspx?ID=253) pg. 87 **Perception** +16; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59) **Languages** **Skills** [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) +23 **Str** +7 **Dex** +3 **Con** +6 **Int** -5 **Wis** +0 **Cha** -5 **Eyes Behind the Mask** ([scrying](/Traits.aspx?ID=689)) A creature wearing the mask and garb of a priest of [Razmir](/Deities.aspx?ID=357) that outranks the tithekeeper's mask and ribbon rank can spend an hour Interacting with the tithekeeper's mask to connect with it. The creature's mask becomes an [invested](/Traits.aspx?ID=637) item that allows them to see and hear as though peering through the tithekeeper's mask. The creature must use a 3-action activity envisioning the tithekeeper to activate the [scrying](/Traits.aspx?ID=689) effect, and the effect can be Dismissed. Multiple creatures can create connections to the tithekeeper's mask simultaneously, and a creature can have connections to multiple tithekeepers with just one mask. Each connection ends after a week but can be renewed at any time.
**Locked Vault** The tithekeeper's body is a locked vault containing any tithes given to it. The vault's [_Pick Lock_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1589) DC is 29 and [Force Open](/Actions.aspx?ID=2375) DC is 33. --- **AC** 29 **Fort** +22 **Ref** +17 **Will** +14 **HP** 220 **Immunities** bleed, [death](/Traits.aspx?ID=571) effects, [disease](/Traits.aspx?ID=578), [doomed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=67), [drained](/Conditions.aspx?ID=68), [fatigued](/Conditions.aspx?ID=73), [healing](/Traits.aspx?ID=623), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647), [nonlethal](/Traits.aspx?ID=661) attacks, [paralyzed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=85), [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=669), [sickened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=91), [spirit](/Traits.aspx?ID=737), [unconscious](/Conditions.aspx?ID=95), [vitality](/Traits.aspx?ID=509), [void](/Traits.aspx?ID=510) **Accept Tithe** **Trigger** A creature drops or offers at least 750 gp in valuables within 15 feet of the tithekeeper; **Effect** The tithekeeper quickly uses its feet to scoop the valuables into its vault and is now indifferent toward the triggering creature unless that creature uses [hostile actions](/Rules.aspx?ID=300) against it or its allies. --- **Speed** 30 feet, climb 30 feet **Melee** body +23, **Damage** 2d12+13 bludgeoning **Melee** foot +23 ([reach 15 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)), **Damage** 2d8+13 piercing plus [Improved Grab](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=66) **Capacity for Punishment** The tithekeeper can have up to six creatures impaled and [grabbed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=77) with its feet at once. **Impale** **Requirements** The tithekeeper has grabbed a creature; **Effect** The tithekeeper stabs the target with a spike for 2d8+13 piercing damage (DC 29 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save). It no longer has to spend an action to extend the duration for the target it has grabbed. The target moves with the tithekeeper and takes 1d8 [persistent bleed damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29) until it [Escape](/Actions.aspx?ID=2296) (DC 29). **Rip Off** **Requirements** The tithekeeper has Impaled a creature; **Effect** The tithekeeper tears the creature loose from its spiky feet, releasing it. The creature takes 4d10 slashing damage (DC 29 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Fortitude save) and is no longer [grabbed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=77). On a failed save, the creature also takes 2d8 [persistent bleed damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29). **[Trample](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=81)** Medium or smaller, body, DC 29

Long-lived trolls sometimes force their way through the twin distractions of hunger and pain to learn more about the world around them. To manage their regeneration, they learn to cover themselves in crude armor that slowly becomes integrated with the top layer of their flesh. Marked by this armor and aided by their superior wits, these warleaders gather a variety of trolls to serve them in raiding parties. The warleader presented here is a forest troll, but warleaders can be other types of trolls as well. Many of them are adapted to battle tactics that are best suited to their home environments. **[Recall Knowledge - Humanoid](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=47)): DC 27 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 25 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 22 [Troll Warleader](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3220) **Source** [Monster Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=221) pg. 331 1.1 **Perception** +19; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59) **Languages** [Jotun](/Languages.aspx?ID=8) **Skills** [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) +21, [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=4) +15, [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=7) +22, [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=10) +17, [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=16) +17 **Str** +7 **Dex** +3 **Con** +7 **Int** -1 **Wis** +1 **Cha** +4 **Easily Misled** The troll warleader gets a –4 circumstance penalty to their Perception DC against [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38) checks. **Items** _+1 [striking](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2829) [battle axe](/Weapons.aspx?ID=371)_ (2), [Half Plate](/Armor.aspx?ID=12) --- **AC** 29 (26 plus [all-around vision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=49) after Shed Armor) **Fort** +23 **Ref** +17 **Will** +15 **HP** 240 , regeneration 20 (deactivated by [electricity](/Traits.aspx?ID=586) or [fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=604)) **Weaknesses** electricity 10, fire 10 **Furious Roar** **Trigger** The troll warleader takes electricity or fire damage; **Effect** The warleader uses their Primordial Roar and, if they're aware of the damage's source, can Stride toward it. If the warleader has [persistent fire damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29), they attempt a DC 15 flat check to remove it.
**[Reactive Strike](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=48)** --- **Speed** 30 feet **Melee** jaws +23 ([reach 10 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)), **Damage** 2d12+13 piercing **Melee** battle axe +24 ([Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103), [reach 10 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192), [Sweep](/Traits.aspx?ID=194)), **Damage** 2d8+13 slashing **Melee** claw +23 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [reach 10 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)), **Damage** 2d8+13 slashing **Primordial Roar** ([Auditory](/Traits.aspx?ID=16), [Emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=60), [Fear](/Traits.aspx?ID=68), [Mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=106)) The troll warleader unleashes a bestial roar. Each non-troll creature in a 100-foot emanation must attempt a DC 29 Will save. The creature is then temporarily immune for 10 minutes.
**Critical Success** The creature is unaffected.
**Success** The creature is [frightened 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=76).
**Failure** The creature is frightened 2.
**Critical Failure** The creature is frightened 3. **Shed Armor** ([Manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104)) The warleader cuts their armor loose from their flesh. They immediately heal 60 Hit Points in a surge of regeneration as they grow twisted limbs and malformed faces. Without their armor, the warleader's AC drops to 26 but they gain [all-around vision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=49) from the new faces. Putting the armor back on takes 10 minutes, and this ability can't be used again until 1 hour has passed. **Sweeping Axes** **Requirements** The troll warleader is wielding two battle axes; **Effect** The warleader makes a battle axe Strike against each creature in their reach and the bonus from [sweep](/Traits.aspx?ID=708) applies to each attack. These attacks count against their multiple attack penalty, but the multiple attack penalty doesn't increase until after all the attacks.

<title level="1" pfs="Standard">[Vicharamuni (Awakener Naga)](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3104)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

Awakener nagas are benevolent and wise teachers of people and places. They seek to guide and nurture the world around them, sensing mortals or locales with potential supernatural significance. Once located, these nagas provide instruction and divine trials to forge their wards toward strength and to impart a deeper understanding of right and wrong. Though considered stern and intimidating taskmasters by their students, those taught by a vicharamuni often go on to become great heroes.

 Awakener nagas are similarly attentive in guiding their young. Upon reaching adulthood, a naga is provided a final trial before being encouraged to depart the nest and seek out their own natural wonders or promising mortals. Sometimes generations of nagas might guard the same place or family line, passing the honor of such care from parent to child. In such cases, the parent nagas aim to have at least one of their children elect to stay behind and become the guardian of their ancestral ward, giving the parents peace of mind that the site they protect will continue to be guarded by their descendants.

<column gap="tiny">
**[Recall Knowledge - Beast](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**
([Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35), [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43)): DC 29

**[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 27

**[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 24
</column>

text: Vicharamuni (Awakener Naga) Awakener nagas are benevolent and wise teachers of people and places. They seek to guide and nurture the world around them, sensing mortals or locales with potential supernatural significance. Once located, these nagas provide instruction and divine trials to forge their wards toward strength and to impart a deeper understanding of right and wrong. Though considered stern and intimidating taskmasters by their students, those taught by a vicharamuni often go on to become great heroes. Awakener nagas are similarly attentive in guiding their young. Upon reaching adulthood, a naga is provided a final trial before being encouraged to depart the nest and seek out their own natural wonders or promising mortals. Sometimes generations of nagas might guard the same place or family line, passing the honor of such care from parent to child. In such cases, the parent nagas aim to have at least one of their children elect to stay behind and become the guardian of their ancestral ward, giving the parents peace of mind that the site they protect will continue to be guarded by their descendants. <title level="1" pfs="">[Vorvorak](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3820)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

Those trespassing on abandoned canals might come face-to-face with a vorvorak, a large creature that resembles a [dragon](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=395) or [crocodile](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=384). These territorial beasts keep hoards that they disguise with magical illusions, using their natural talent for spellcasting. Often mistaken for dragons, vorvoraks are commonly referred to as canal dragons or mud dragons. However, they aren't truly related to dragons but rather evolved from local crocodiles and exposure to innate magic in the region of Taldor. 

Vorvoraks are solitary creatures, preferring to hunt in the early morning or early evening. In general, vorvoraks make their lairs in areas with some submersion. Such places let them hide their hordes and use their brown, mossy bodies as a natural form of stealth. Due to their evolution and magical contamination, vorvoraks have limited innate magical abilities, allowing them to control the water around them and infuse it with their own poisonous bile. 

All vorvoraks share a common trait: hoarding treasure. Many fill their lairs with coins, gems, and anything shiny they take from their victims, with some older hoards containing relics of the surrounding imperial nations. The condition of the items is of no importance to the vorvoraks; a hoard is just as likely to contain junk as items of true value. 

A fully grown vorvorak is around 24 feet long and weighs approximately 3,000 pounds, with muddy brown scales, a serpentine neck, and hard fins on their back that resemble wings.

<title level="1" pfs="Standard">[Young Fortune Dragon](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2944)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

Fortune dragons have the innate ability to draw upon the raw magical energies that surround them. They constantly use these magical energies to empower their magical abilities and even their bodies, as the energy can heal wounds. A fortune dragon has a typical build for an arcane dragon, but their bodies sport a striking feature: their treasure. The dragon's nature of drawing upon magic causes coins, gems, and, most notably, magical items to cling to their body like iron drawn to magnets. A dragon constantly pulls magical energies from the items attached to their body and makes use of these energies to cast spells. The magical energies that flow through a fortune dragon constantly flow through the dragon's items as well, and in many cases, the items melt from the heat produced in this process. Fortune dragons are seekers of novel experiences. This desire for originality leads fortune dragons to approach visitors of other ancestries with curiosity, though this initial interest quickly wanes if a visitor lacks exciting qualities.

<column gap="tiny">

([Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35)): DC 27

**[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 25

**[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 22
</column>

**Languages**
[Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1), [Draconic](/Languages.aspx?ID=2)

**Skills**
[Accounting Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8) +22, [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=1) +21, [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=2) +22, [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) +21, [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=4) +22, [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=6) +19, [Mercantile Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8) +22, [Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=17) +21

<row gap="medium">
**Str** +5

**Con** +4

**Cha** +3
</row>

</column>

<column gap="tiny">

<row gap="medium">
**AC** 30 

**Fort** +18 

**Ref** +21 

**Will** +19 

+2 status to all saves vs. [arcane](/Traits.aspx?ID=534)
</row>

<row gap="medium">
**HP** 175

</row>

**Immunities**
[drained](/Conditions.aspx?ID=68), [paralyzed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=85), [sleep](/Traits.aspx?ID=696)

**Capture Spell** <actions string="Reaction" /> ([arcane](/Traits.aspx?ID=534)) **Trigger** The dragon succeeds or critically succeeds on a saving throw against a spell; **Effect** The dragon attempts to capture a portion of the spell's magic to feed themself. They attempt to [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) the spell (counteract rank 5, counteract modifier +20). If successful, the dragon is unaffected by the spell and regains one expended spontaneous spell slot; other subjects are affected by the spell normally.

</column>

---

<column gap="tiny">

**Speed** 60 feet, fly 100 feet

**Melee**
<actions string="Single Action" />
jaws +21 ([Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103), [reach 10 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)),
**Damage** 2d10+11 piercing plus 1d6 force

**Melee**
<actions string="Single Action" />
claw +21 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103)),
**Damage** 2d6+11 piercing plus 1d6 force

**Melee**
<actions string="Single Action" />
tail +19 ([Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103), [reach 15 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)),
**Damage** 2d10+11 bludgeoning plus 1d6 force

**Arcane Spontaneous Spells** DC 30, attack +22
- **Cantrips (5th)**
[Detect Magic](/Spells.aspx?ID=66), [Read Aura](/Spells.aspx?ID=246)
- **5th**
[Fireball](/Spells.aspx?ID=119), [Force Barrage](/Spells.aspx?ID=1536), [Slither](/Spells.aspx?ID=1676), [Unfettered Movement](/Spells.aspx?ID=1732) (1 slot)

**Disruptive Breath** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([Arcane](/Traits.aspx?ID=11), [Force](/Traits.aspx?ID=75)) The dragon unleashes a spray of magic-disrupting energies that deals 9d6 force damage in a 30-foot cone (DC 30 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save) Creatures that fail become [stupefied 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=94) (stupefied 2 on a critical failure) for 1 minute. The dragon can't use Disruptive Breath again for 1d4 rounds.

**Draconic Frenzy** <actions string="Two Actions" />  The dragon makes two claw Strikes and one tail Strike in any order.

**Draconic Momentum**   Whenever they score a critical hit with a Strike, the dragon chooses to either recharge Disruptive Breath or regain one expended spontaneous spell slot.

**Share the Wealth** <actions string="Two Actions" />  **Requirements** The dragon's body is covered in riches (this is typically the case when the dragon is first encountered); **Effect** The dragon shakes their body aggressively, sending coins and other riches flying in every direction, dealing 6d10 bludgeoning damage with a DC 29 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save to all creatures in a 30-foot emanation. The dragon's body is then no longer covered in riches.

**Treasure Dive** <actions string="Two Actions" />  **Requirements** The dragon's body isn't covered in riches and the dragon is adjacent to their hoard; **Effect** The dragon Strides or [Burrows](/Actions.aspx?ID=2310) through their hoard using their land Speed. They coat themself in coins, magic items, and other treasures. This contact with magical items revitalizes the dragon, causing them to regain one expended spontaneous spell slot. The dragon can move through other creatures while moving in this way. Creatures in the dragon's path, or above it if the dragon Burrows, must succeed at a DC 27 Reflex save or be [pushed](/Rules.aspx?ID=451) 10 feet (or pushed 20 feet and knocked [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=88) on a critical failure).

</column>

features.Share the Wealth: <actions string="Two Actions" />  **Requirements** The dragon's body is covered in riches (this is typically the case when the dragon is first encountered); **Effect** The dragon shakes their body aggressively, sending coins and other riches flying in every direction, dealing 6d10 bludgeoning damage with a DC 29 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save to all creatures in a 30-foot emanation. The dragon's body is then no longer covered in riches.
features.Treasure Dive: <actions string="Two Actions" />  **Requirements** The dragon's body isn't covered in riches and the dragon is adjacent to their hoard; **Effect** The dragon Strides or [Burrows](/Actions.aspx?ID=2310) through their hoard using their land Speed. They coat themself in coins, magic items, and other treasures. This contact with magical items revitalizes the dragon, causing them to regain one expended spontaneous spell slot. The dragon can move through other creatures while moving in this way. Creatures in the dragon's path, or above it if the dragon Burrows, must succeed at a DC 27 Reflex save or be [pushed](/Rules.aspx?ID=451) 10 feet (or pushed 20 feet and knocked [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=88) on a critical failure).

description: Fortune dragons have the innate ability to draw upon the raw magical energies that surround them. They constantly use these magical energies to empower their magical abilities and even their bodies, as the energy can heal wounds. A fortune dragon has a typical build for an arcane dragon, but their bodies sport a striking feature: their treasure. The dragon's nature of drawing upon magic causes coins, gems, and, most notably, magical items to cling to their body like iron drawn to magnets. A dragon constantly pulls magical energies from the items attached to their body and makes use of these energies to cast spells. The magical energies that flow through a fortune dragon constantly flow through the dragon's items as well, and in many cases, the items melt from the heat produced in this process. Fortune dragons are seekers of novel experiences. This desire for originality leads fortune dragons to approach visitors of other ancestries with curiosity, though this initial interest quickly wanes if a visitor lacks exciting qualities.

Fate is a fickle matter on Golarion. Even with prophecy broken on the world, there are ways to look to the immediate future or acquire a vague sense of long-term events. Omen dragons are bound to see the future—nebulous though it might be—at all times. Visions of the future hound them like a quiet song that never stops playing in their minds. While an omen dragon can focus on or ignore the music of fate at any time, the song plays all the same. At a glance, omen dragons resemble other occult dragons in appearance, save for the mirror-like interior membrane of their wings. An omen dragon's wings offer glimpses into the future. These glimpses are cloudy and vague, but generally correct, if only technically. Omen dragons have a natural compulsion to share the futures they see. These dragons have no compunctions about what the visions show and share their knowledge equally with innocent villagers as they do with wicked tyrants. **[Recall Knowledge - Dragon](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35)): DC 28 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 26 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 23 [Adult Omen Dragon](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2954) **Source** [Monster Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=221) pg. 124 1.1 **Perception** +21; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59), [scent](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=74) ([imprecise](/Rules.aspx?ID=412)) 60 feet **Languages** [Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1), [Draconic](/Languages.aspx?ID=2), [Fey](/Languages.aspx?ID=119), [Jotun](/Languages.aspx?ID=8) **Skills** [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=1) +21, [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) +22, [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=6) +20, [Fortune-Telling Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8) +26, [Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8) +24, [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=11) +24, [Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=14) +22 **Str** +7 **Dex** +4 **Con** +5 **Int** +7 **Wis** +6 **Cha** +3 --- **AC** 30 **Fort** +20 **Ref** +19 **Will** +23 +2 status to all saves vs. [occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=662) **HP** 185 **Immunities** [confused](/Conditions.aspx?ID=63), [doomed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=67), [paralyzed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=85), [sleep](/Traits.aspx?ID=696) **Untethered to Fate** The dragon can choose to negate any [fortune](/Traits.aspx?ID=612) or [misfortune](/Traits.aspx?ID=654) effects that would affect them; other creatures remain affected normally.
**Challenge Fate** ([misfortune](/Traits.aspx?ID=654), [occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=662)) **Trigger** The dragon is targeted by an attack; **Effect** This fate is not set in stone. The attacker rolls the triggering attack twice and uses the worse result. --- **Speed** 50 feet, fly 130 feet **Melee** jaws +22 ([Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103), [reach 10 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)), **Damage** 2d8+11 piercing plus 1d8 mental **Melee** claw +22 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103)), **Damage** 2d6+11 slashing plus 1d8 mental **Melee** tail +20 ([Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103), [reach 15 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)), **Damage** 2d8+11 bludgeoning plus 1d8 mental **Melee** wing +20 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103), [reach 10 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)), **Damage** 1d8+11 slashing plus 1d8 mental **Occult Innate Spells** DC 30 - **Cantrips (4th)** [Guidance](/Spells.aspx?ID=1549) - **5th** [Ill Omen](/Spells.aspx?ID=696) (at will), [Mindlink](/Spells.aspx?ID=195) (at will), [Sure Strike](/Spells.aspx?ID=1709) (×2) **Destiny Breath** ([Mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=106), [Occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=120)) The dragon breathes a translucent mist of potentialities that overwhelms creatures with visions of possible features, dealing 10d6 mental damage in a 30-foot cone (DC 30 Will save). A creature that fails its save is [slowed 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=92) for 1 round (or slowed 2 on a critical failure) as it struggles with the visions. The dragon can't use Destiny Breath again for 1d4 rounds. **Draconic Frenzy** The dragon makes two claw Strikes and one wing Strike in any order. **Draconic Momentum** The dragon recharges their Destiny Breath whenever they score a critical hit with a Strike. **Prophetic Wings** The dragon or any ally can glimpse into the future through the dragon's wings in a process that requires 10 minutes of concentration. This casts a 6th-rank [_augury_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1445) spell, except that the wings can predict results up to 1 day into the future and the dragon always speaks a few cryptic words related to the result of the prediction. The dragon can use their wings in this way only once per hour, and a given creature can seek a future in the wings only once per week. A creature can choose to predict events up to 1 month into the future—the dragon can view a month ahead in their own wings only once per day. **Walk the Timelines** ([Occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=120)) **Frequency** once per hour; **Effect** The dragon splits themself into two versions with different fates. Each copy Strides or [Flies](/Actions.aspx?ID=2312)from the dragon's current space, then takes a single action. If the actions are both attacks, they use the same multiple attack penalty and count as one attack toward the dragon's multiple attack penalty. After both actions, the dragon chooses one of the two locations as their actual destination and the other version of themself disappears.

description: Fate is a fickle matter on Golarion. Even with prophecy broken on the world, there are ways to look to the immediate future or acquire a vague sense of long-term events. Omen dragons are bound to see the future—nebulous though it might be—at all times. Visions of the future hound them like a quiet song that never stops playing in their minds. While an omen dragon can focus on or ignore the music of fate at any time, the song plays all the same. At a glance, omen dragons resemble other occult dragons in appearance, save for the mirror-like interior membrane of their wings. An omen dragon's wings offer glimpses into the future. These glimpses are cloudy and vague, but generally correct, if only technically. Omen dragons have a natural compulsion to share the futures they see. These dragons have no compunctions about what the visions show and share their knowledge equally with innocent villagers as they do with wicked tyrants.

This griffon is aptly named for both its majestic appearance in flight and its increased ferocity over the common griffon. Despite its size, the sheer muscle mass present in this creature makes flight seem effortless, if preposterous. It makes its home among the canopies of the most ancient forests and atop the peaks of the greatest mountains, hunting its prey from above with silent and deadly accuracy. The ascendant griffon prefers to hunt other large creatures within its territory, such as bears, but they will not hesitate to attack smaller prey they perceive as a threat to their territory. Whether an ascendant griffon is a new evolutionary development or a throwback to a more primeval version of the creature is difficult to determine. Further research into these exceptional creatures may provide insight into their origins and perhaps the origins of all griffons. **[Recall Knowledge - Animal](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43)): DC 33 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 31 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 28 [Ascendant Griffon](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3287) **Source** [Howl of the Wild](/Sources.aspx?ID=226) pg. 157 2.1 **Perception** +25; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59), [scent](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=74) ([imprecise](/Rules.aspx?ID=412)) 120 feet **Languages** **Skills** [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=34) +23, [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) +23, [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=40) +25, [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=48) +21, [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=49) +22 **Str** +7 **Dex** +6 **Con** +5 **Int** -4 **Wis** +3 **Cha** +7 --- **AC** 30 **Fort** +21 **Ref** +24 **Will** +18 **HP** 210 **Dread Gaze** **Trigger** A creature ends a [move](/Traits.aspx?ID=658) action within 30 feet of the ascendant griffon; **Effect** The ascendant griffon turns its head to stare down the triggering creature, and attempts to [Demoralize](/Actions.aspx?ID=2395) it. This use of Demoralize has the [visual](/Traits.aspx?ID=727) trait rather than the [auditory](/Traits.aspx?ID=541) trait, and the griffon does not take a penalty on its check for not sharing a language. --- **Speed** 25 feet, fly 40 feet **Melee** beak +24, **Damage** 4d8+10 piercing **Melee** talon +24, **Damage** 4d6+10 piercing plus [Improved Grab](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=66) **Melee** wing +24 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170)), **Damage** 4d6+10 slashing **Ranged** feather +25 ([range 60 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=248)), **Damage** 2d8+10 piercing **Carry Off** An ascendant griffon can [Fly](/Actions.aspx?ID=2312) at full speed with a creature [grabbed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=77) in its talons, moving that creature along with it. **Disembowel** **Requirements** The ascendant griffon has a creature [grabbed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=77) in its talons; **Effect** The griffon makes a beak Strike to rip at the flesh of its prey. description: This griffon is aptly named for both its majestic appearance in flight and its increased ferocity over the common griffon. Despite its size, the sheer muscle mass present in this creature makes flight seem effortless, if preposterous. It makes its home among the canopies of the most ancient forests and atop the peaks of the greatest mountains, hunting its prey from above with silent and deadly accuracy. The ascendant griffon prefers to hunt other large creatures within its territory, such as bears, but they will not hesitate to attack smaller prey they perceive as a threat to their territory. Whether an ascendant griffon is a new evolutionary development or a throwback to a more primeval version of the creature is difficult to determine. Further research into these exceptional creatures may provide insight into their origins and perhaps the origins of all griffons.

Blustering gales are among the least of air elementals: spirits of the small breezes who sometimes arise in the wake of mightier creatures, like the downdraft of a swallow's wing or the sharp expulsion of a vigorous cough. Unwilling or unable to act effectively alone, they form into “gales,” collections of weak elementals that use their combined power to hurl insults and pummel those who defy them in a misguided attempt to rise above their humble origins. Together, they force other creatures to do their bidding, then move on when they grow bored. While most gales claim their abandoned minions were useless, in truth, blustering gales lack the commanding presence and confidence to retain vassals for long. **[Recall Knowledge - Elemental](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=2), [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=10)): DC 28 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 26 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 23 [Blustering Gale](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2615) **Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 80 2.0 **Perception** +20; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=12) **Languages** [Sussuran](/Languages.aspx?ID=111) **Skills** [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=1) +20, [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) +22, [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=7) +22, [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15) +18 **Str** +7 **Dex** +5 **Con** +3 **Int** +0 **Wis** +1 **Cha** +5 --- **AC** 30 **Fort** +22 **Ref** +24 **Will** +18 **HP** 150 (16 squares) **Immunities** bleed, [paralyzed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=28), [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=126), [sleep](/Traits.aspx?ID=145) **Weaknesses** area damage 10, [splash](/Traits.aspx?ID=150) damage 10 **Bullying Bluster** ([auditory](/Traits.aspx?ID=16), [aura](/Traits.aspx?ID=206), [emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=60), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=106), [linguistic](/Traits.aspx?ID=101)) 30 feet. The blustering gale constantly unleashes a tirade of insults and aggressive taunts. Each enemy who enters or starts their turn in the aura must succeed at a DC 30 Will save or become [stupefied 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=37) for as long as they remain within the aura (stupefied 2 on a critical failure). The troop's members are collectively able to mimic a few curse words or insults in every language, allowing their Bullying Bluster to affect any creature who understands a language. A creature who succeeds at its save is temporarily immune for 1 hour. The blustering gale can activate or deactivate the aura with a free action, which has the [concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32) trait.

The graceful and regal cloud giants are fractious, with roughly half their clans believing they should rule over humanoids regardless of their size and the rest shying away from any contact with outsiders. Due to the physical and ideological distance between clans, most rely on [giant eagle](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2969) or [roc](/Monsters.aspx?ID=352) messengers, to arrange marriages and exchange art without setting foot in each other's territory. Cloud giants' skin color ranges from milky white to powdery blue. They make their homes anywhere veiled by the clouds, generally mountaintops or isolated valleys, but occasionally fog-shrouded swamps or misty rainforests. Legends persist of floating cities ruled by magically gifted cloud giant queens and kings. Spikes of rock rise up from all stone surfaces in the emanation, creating [difficult terrain](/Rules.aspx?ID=453). A creature moving in the terrain takes 2d8 piercing damage for each square of spikes it moves into (a Large or larger creature takes damage only once for each square it moves, even if its space covers multiple squares of spikes). Creatures with the [earth](/Traits.aspx?ID=585) trait ignore all effects within the area. The living avalanche can disable or activate this aura using a single action, which has the [concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561) trait.
**Crumble** Trigger The living avalanche takes damage from a hostile source while atop rock or earth; Effect The living avalanche crumbles into the ground, [Burrowing](/Actions.aspx?ID=2310)down 20 feet. This Burrowing does not trigger reactions. The living avalanche can't Crumble again for 1d4 rounds --- **Speed** 25 feet, burrow 25 feet; earth glide **Melee** fist +24 ([reach 20 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)), **Damage** 2d12+11 bludgeoning plus [Knockdown](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=46) **Ranged** rock +24 ([Brutal](/Traits.aspx?ID=249), [range increment 80 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=248)), **Damage** 2d12+7 bludgeoning **Earth Glide** The living avalanche can [Burrow](/Actions.aspx?ID=2310) through any earthen matter, including rock. When it does so, the living avalanche moves at its full burrow Speed, leaving no tunnels or signs of its passing. **Grinding Stones** The elemental avalanche deals 4d12 bludgeoning damage to each [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=88) creature within the elemental's melee reach with a DC 30 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save. **[Trample](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=81)** Large or smaller, fist, DC 30

Walking conflagrations of unimaginably hot fire, elemental infernos are harbingers of destruction and heedless chaos. More tactical than many elementals, the infernos will set entire cities ablaze to confuse enemies. **[Recall Knowledge - Elemental](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35), [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43)): DC 28 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 26 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 23 [Elemental Inferno](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2984) **Source** [Monster Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=221) pg. 145 1.1 **Perception** +20; darkvision, smoke vision **Languages** [Pyric](/Languages.aspx?ID=110) **Skills** [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=1) +21 **Str** +6 **Dex** +6 **Con** +5 **Int** +0 **Wis** +3 **Cha** +0 **Smoke Vision** The elemental inferno ignores the [concealed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=62) condition from smoke. --- **AC** 31 **Fort** +21 **Ref** +23 **Will** +19 **HP** 210 (explosion) **Immunities** bleed, [fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=604), [paralyzed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=85), [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=669), [sleep](/Traits.aspx?ID=696) **Weaknesses** [cold](/Traits.aspx?ID=555) 15, [water](/Traits.aspx?ID=732) 10 **Explosion** ([fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=604)) When the elemental inferno dies, it explodes, dealing 7d6 fire damage to each creature in a 10-foot emanation (DC 30 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save).
**[Intense Heat](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=53)** ([aura](/Traits.aspx?ID=542), [fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=604)) 10 feet, 7d6 fire, DC 28 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex --- **Speed** 70 feet **Melee** tendril +24 ([reach 15 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)), **Damage** 2d10+12 fire plus 3d8 [persistent fire](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29) **Ranged** fire mote +24 ([range increment 60 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=248)), **Damage** 2d10+6 fire **Blue Flames** When the elemental inferno scores a critical hit, its body surges with blue flames, increasing the damage of its intense heat and Inferno Leap by 3d6 until the start of its next turn. **Inferno Leap** ([Fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=72)) The elemental inferno jumps horizontally and vertically with a maximum height and distance each equal to its Speed. Its intense heat is suppressed until the end of the jump. Instead, at any point during the jump, flames explode from the elemental in a 30-foot emanation, dealing 12d6 fire damage to each creature within the area (DC 30 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save). The elemental inferno can't Inferno Leap again for 1d4 rounds.

<title level="1" pfs="Standard">[Goliath Spider](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3209)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

Goliath spiders dwell in the deepest jungles, where they build webs as big as temples and feast on prey as large as hippopotamuses.

<column gap="tiny">
**[Recall Knowledge - Animal](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**
([Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43)): DC 28

**[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 26

**[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 23
</column>

</column>

<column gap="medium">
<image src="/images/Monsters/Goliath_Spider.webp" />
</column>

</row>

<title level="2" right="Creature 11">[Goliath Spider](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3209)</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Gargantuan" />
<trait label="Animal" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=531" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Monster Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=221) pg. 321 <sup>1.1</sup>

**Perception** +22; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59), web sense

**Languages**

**Skills**
[Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=1) +18, [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) +23, [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15) +22

<row gap="medium">
**Str** +8

**Dex** +5

**Con** +7

**Int** -5

**Wis** +3

**Cha** -4
</row>

**Web Sense** The spider has [imprecise](/Rules.aspx?ID=412) [tremorsense](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=82) to detect the vibrations of creatures touching its web.

</column>

---

<column gap="tiny">

<row gap="medium">
**AC** 30 

**Fort** +25 

**Ref** +21 

**Will** +17 

</row>

<row gap="medium">
**HP** 220

</row>

**Spring Upon Prey** <actions string="Reaction" /> **Requirements** Initiative has not yet been rolled; **Trigger** A creature touches the goliath spider's web while the spider is on it; **Effect** The goliath spider automatically notices the creature and Strides, Climbs, or Descends on a Web before it rolls initiative.

</column>

---

<column gap="tiny">

**Speed** 45 feet, climb 30 feet

**Melee**
<actions string="Single Action" />
fangs +24 ([reach 10 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)),
**Damage** 2d12+12 piercing plus goliath spider venom

**Ranged**
<actions string="Single Action" />
web +22 ([range increment 60 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=248)),
**Damage** web tether

**Descend on a Web** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([Move](/Traits.aspx?ID=114)) The goliath spider moves straight down up to 120 feet, suspended by a web line. It can hang from the web or drop off. The distance it Descends on a Web doesn't count for [falling damage](/Rules.aspx?ID=402). A creature that successfully Strikes the web (AC 20, Hardness 5, 20 HP) severs it, causing the spider to fall.

**Goliath Spider Venom**  ([Incapacitation](/Traits.aspx?ID=93), [Poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=126)) **Saving Throw** DC 30 Fortitude; **Maximum Duration** 6 rounds; **Stage 1** 3d6 poison damage and **slowed 1** (1 round); **Stage 2** 3d8 poison damage and slowed 2 (1 round); **Stage 3** 3d10 poison damage and [paralyzed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=85) for 2d4 hours

**Web Tether**   A creature hit by the spider's web Strike is [restrained](/Conditions.aspx?ID=90) and tethered to the spider, preventing it from being moved farther away from the spider. The spider can have one creature tethered at a time. The DC to [Escape](/Actions.aspx?ID=2296) or [Force Open](/Actions.aspx?ID=2375) the web is 30. The tether can be severed with a Strike (AC 20, Hardness 5, HP 20), but this doesn't free the restrained creature.

</column>

Gosregs are agents of the Dominion of the Black who insinuate themselves into humanoid societies to implement the goals of their sinister masters. They're generally tasked with observing and waiting, hiding in disguised forms until their location is ripe for harvest. When this occurs, they reveal themselves as living psychic beacons, signaling their distant masters and guiding invasion forces. Over the years of an infiltration, a gosreg will assume dozens of roles, relishing any intense emotions it can inspire while laying the groundwork for future identities. In their natural form, gosregs dart about in a jerky gallop due to stumpy legs, gangly arms, and oversized heads. They take on the appearances of humanoids to infiltrate societies, and they drop these disguises only when they're compromised and must resort to physical violence to continue their mission. **[Recall Knowledge - Aberration](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=44)): DC 30 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 28 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 25 [Gosreg](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2931) **Source** [Monster Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=221) pg. 107 1.1 **Perception** +21; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59), thoughtsense 60 feet **Languages** [Aklo](/Languages.aspx?ID=13), [Sakvroth](/Languages.aspx?ID=118); [telepathy](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=79) 100 feet **Skills** [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5) +24, [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=6) +22, [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=11) +23, [Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=14) +19, [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15) +23 **Str** +3 **Dex** +6 **Con** +3 **Int** +6 **Wis** +5 **Cha** +7 **Borrow Languages** The gosreg can read and speak all languages known by creatures within range of its telepathy.
**Thoughtsense** The gosreg senses a creature's mental essence as a [precise](/Rules.aspx?ID=411) sense with the listed range; it cannot sense [mindless](/Traits.aspx?ID=652) creatures with thoughtsense. --- **AC** 31 **Fort** +18 **Ref** +23 **Will** +22 +1 status to all saves vs. [magic](/Traits.aspx?ID=644) **HP** 195 **Immunities** [confused](/Conditions.aspx?ID=63) **Resistances** [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647) 10 **Unsettled Aura** ([aura](/Traits.aspx?ID=542), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647), [occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=662)) 30 feet. Gosregs project a field of discordant energy that unsettles the minds of thinking creatures. Any non-[mindless](/Traits.aspx?ID=652) creature within 30 feet of a gosreg takes a –1 status penalty to Will saves. --- **Speed** 25 feet **Melee** jaws +21 ([Finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=179)), **Damage** 2d10+7 piercing plus 1d10 mental **Melee** claw +21 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [Finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=179)), **Damage** 2d8+7 slashing **Occult Innate Spells** DC 30, attack +22 - **Cantrips (6th)** [Telekinetic Hand](/Spells.aspx?ID=1715), [Telekinetic Projectile](/Spells.aspx?ID=334) - **4th** [Nightmare](/Spells.aspx?ID=208), [Suggestion](/Spells.aspx?ID=315) (×3) - **5th** [Mind Probe](/Spells.aspx?ID=193), [Sending](/Spells.aspx?ID=272), [Subconscious Suggestion](/Spells.aspx?ID=314), [Synaptic Pulse](/Spells.aspx?ID=327) - **6th** [Phantasmal Calamity](/Spells.aspx?ID=218), [Phantom Pain](/Spells.aspx?ID=220) **Broadcast Stance** ([Mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=106), [Occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=120), [Stance](/Traits.aspx?ID=152)) **Requirements** the gosreg is in its natural form; **Effect** The gosreg secures its limbs into the ground as its brain-like head crackles with psychic energy. The gosreg's unsettled aura extends to 60 feet, and it blocks all other creatures' [telepathy](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=79) in the aura. Its Mind Bolt can also affect any number of targets in 60 feet. These effects end when the gosreg uses its claw Strike, leaves its space, or is knocked [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=88). **[Change Shape](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=55)** ([Concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32), [Occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=120), [Polymorph](/Traits.aspx?ID=127)) The gosreg takes on the appearance of any Small or Medium [humanoid](/Traits.aspx?ID=628). The target takes 6d6 mental damage (DC 30 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Will save). On a critical failure, the creature is also [confused](/Conditions.aspx?ID=63) for 1 minute or until it takes damage.

One subspecies that some call unnatural is the gray worm. It is theorized that these cave worms hatched near the corpses of thousands of graves, perhaps deep in the layers of the Darklands that once held large populations at the moment of Starfall. The negative energy associated with the collective extinction of so much life has warped these worms so that they embody the misery and death caused by the cataclysm. They are unique among cave worms in that they prefer not to swallow prey alive, but to eat only dead flesh. **[Recall Knowledge - Beast](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=2), [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=10)): DC 33 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 31 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 28 [Gray Worm](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2704) **Source** [Pathfinder #194: Cult of the Cave Worm](/Sources.aspx?ID=209) pg. 67 **Perception** +19; blood scent, [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=12), [tremorsense](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=40) ([imprecise](/Rules.aspx?ID=412)) 100 feet **Languages** **Skills** [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) +24, [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=16) +19 **Str** +7 **Dex** -1 **Con** +7 **Int** -3 **Wis** +2 **Cha** -1 **Blood Scent** The gray worm can smell blood in the air from up to 1 mile away, or in the earth from up to 1,000 feet away. --- **AC** 28 **Fort** +24 **Ref** +16 **Will** +19 **HP** 248 ([negative healing](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=42)) **Weaknesses** positive 10 **Inexorable** The gray worm recovers from the [paralyzed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=28), [slowed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=35), and [stunned](/Conditions.aspx?ID=36) conditions at the end of its turn. It's also immune to penalties to its Speeds and the [immobilized](/Conditions.aspx?ID=24) condition, and it ignores [difficult terrain](/Rules.aspx?ID=453) and greater difficult terrain.
**Shake It Off** **Frequency** once per day; **Trigger** The gray worm would be affected by a condition or adverse effect (such as [_baleful polymorph_](/Spells.aspx?ID=17)); **Effect** The gray worm negates the triggering condition or effect. Effects from artifacts, deities, or a similarly powerful source can't be avoided in this way. --- **Speed** 20 feet, burrow 40 feet **Melee** jaws +24 ([deadly 1d10](/Traits.aspx?ID=174), [reach 15 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)), **Damage** 2d10+10 piercing plus 2d6 [persistent bleed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29) **Melee** stinger +24 ([deadly 1d10](/Traits.aspx?ID=174), [reach 15 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)), **Damage** 2d8+10 piercing plus paralysis **Melee** body +22 ([reach 15 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)), **Damage** 2d8+9 bludgeoning **Paralysis** ([Incapacitation](/Traits.aspx?ID=93), [Occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=120), [Necromancy](/Traits.aspx?ID=117)) Any living creature hit by a gray worm's stinger Strike must succeed at a DC 27 Fortitude save or become [paralyzed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=28). It can attempt a new save at the end of each of its turns, and the DC cumulatively decreases by 1 on each such save. **Thrash** The worm makes a Strike once against each creature in its reach. It can Strike up to once with its jaws and any number of times with its body. Each attack counts toward the worm's multiple attack penalty, but the multiple attack penalty doesn't increase until after it makes all the attacks.

features.Blood Scent: The gray worm can smell blood in the air from up to 1 mile away, or in the earth from up to 1,000 feet away.

features.Inexorable:

description: One subspecies that some call unnatural is the gray worm. It is theorized that these cave worms hatched near the corpses of thousands of graves, perhaps deep in the layers of the Darklands that once held large populations at the moment of Starfall. The negative energy associated with the collective extinction of so much life has warped these worms so that they embody the misery and death caused by the cataclysm. They are unique among cave worms in that they prefer not to swallow prey alive, but to eat only dead flesh.

The Immortal Trickster is an immortal spirit guide who always returns to life no matter how he's killed. After his death, he often recorporates in the same area, though if his body is destroyed in its entirety, he sometimes awakens in an entirely different continent. **[Recall Knowledge - Beast](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35), [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43)): DC 38 **[Recall Knowledge - Humanoid](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=47)): DC 38 **[Recall Knowledge - Spirit](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=44)): DC 38 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 36 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 33 [Immortal Trickster](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3405) **Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 183 **Perception** +24; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59) **Languages** [Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1); [_truespeech_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1728) **Skills** [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38) +26, [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39) +23, [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43) +21, [Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=47) +21, [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=48) +23, [Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=50) +26 **Str** +4 **Dex** +7 **Con** +4 **Int** +3 **Wis** +3 **Cha** +7 **Trickster's Network** The Immortal Trickster can extend his senses through any coyote, fox, or raven in [the Universe](/Planes.aspx?ID=26), making it his sensory animal. He cannot maintain his attention through more than three sensory animals at one time. He can speak through his sensory animals, but only in a single short phrase per animal of no more than two words. He has little control over his sensory animals' actions, though they usually act in a way that is consistent with his desires unless they have a specific reason not to. When extending his senses through a sensory animal, he can use that animal to determine line of effect for any of his spells or abilities. **Items** [_wandering pipe_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3513) --- **AC** 31 **Fort** +21 **Ref** +26 **Will** +23 **HP** 198 **Immunities** [disease](/Traits.aspx?ID=578), [paralyzed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=85) **Resistances** mythic resistance 11 **Immortal Tricks** When the Immortal Trickster is reduced to 0 Hit Points, he returns to life at full health and with all his powers and Mythic Points recharged after 24 hours. He usually, but not always, returns at the site of his death, though he can appear anywhere on the same world where there are coyotes, foxes, or ravens.

An imprecasia, commonly known as a curse eater, is a solitary fey drawn to the energy emanating from curses. They appear as emaciated humanoid creatures with shadowy wings, long thin hands with sharp claws, and insectile heads with feathery antenna. An imprecasia's appearance in a region signifies the land is troubled, but they're not unpopular creatures. On the contrary, an imprecasia's whereabouts are coveted information, as they have the ability to fully consume curses on objects and creatures. Many carrying the weight of a curse seek out curse eaters, most of whom will gladly accept doomed objects or charitably destroy an individual's curse. An imprecasia will never accept the idea of healing a cursed land or blighted region. One might even seek to strengthen the afflictions on a region simply to ensure a regular supply of food. A bolder imprecasia tracks cursed families over generations, feeding off their misfortune until the curse ends or the bloodline dies off. Any who attempt to destroy such curses may find themselves the enemy of an imprecasia defending their source of sustenance. **[Recall Knowledge - Fey](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43)): DC 30 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 28 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 25 [Imprecasia](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2802) **Source** [Pathfinder #199: To Bloom Below the Web](/Sources.aspx?ID=225) pg. 83 **Perception** +23; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59), scent curse **Languages** [Aklo](/Languages.aspx?ID=13), [Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1), [Sylvan](/Languages.aspx?ID=10) **Skills** [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=1) +21, [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=10) +23, [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=16) +23 **Str** +3 **Dex** +6 **Con** +5 **Int** +3 **Wis** +6 **Cha** +5 **Scent Curse** The imprecasia can smell the presence of curses of a level equal to or lower than their own level within 30 feet this is an imprecise sense.
 --- **AC** 31 **Fort** +18 **Ref** +23 **Will** +21 **HP** 180 **Immunities** cursed **Resistances** negative 10 **Weaknesses** cold iron 10 **Drink Death** ([necromancy](/Traits.aspx?ID=117), [primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=676)) **Trigger** A creature within 30 feet of the imprecasia is [dying](/Conditions.aspx?ID=69) **Effect** The imprecasia inhales, drawing a thin blue streak of vapor out of the dying creature's body into their mouth. The dying creature's dying condition is reduced by 1, and the imprecasia regains 2d10+9 Hit Points.
 --- **Speed** 25 feet, fly 25 feet **Melee** claws +23 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [Finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=179), [Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103)), **Damage** 2d12+9 slashing plus homeland's hostility **Primal Innate Spells** DC 32, attack +22 - **Cantrips (5th)** [Tanglefoot](/Spells.aspx?ID=330) - **3rd** [Earthbind](/Spells.aspx?ID=94) - **5th** [Blindness](/Spells.aspx?ID=26), [Deafness](/Spells.aspx?ID=62), [Hallucinatory Terrain](/Spells.aspx?ID=145), [Remove Curse](/Spells.aspx?ID=250) **Devour Curse** ([Abjuration](/Traits.aspx?ID=2), [Primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=134)) The imprecasia casts remove curse against a curse afflicting a creature, but with a cast of two actions rather than 10 minutes. If they succeed in removing the curse, they also drains vitality from the creature, causing it to become [drained](/Conditions.aspx?ID=68) 1 unless it succeeds at a DC 30 Fortitude save (drained 2 on a critical failure). If the curse is removed, the imprecasia doesn't expend that use of [_remove curse_](/Spells.aspx?ID=250) as a primal innate spell. **Homeland's Hostility** ([Curse](/Traits.aspx?ID=38), [Enchantment](/Traits.aspx?ID=61), [Primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=134)) A creature that takes damage from the imprecasia's claws must attempt a DC 30 Will save. On a failure, it treats all terrain within 60 feet of an imprecasia as difficult terrain.

A bolder imprecasia tracks cursed families over generations, feeding off their misfortune until the curse ends or the bloodline dies off. Any who attempt to destroy such curses may find themselves the enemy of an imprecasia defending their source of sustenance.
