On a failure, tiny sprouts burst from the creature's flesh, and it becomes [slowed 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=92) for 1 round. **Fractal Rot** ([Disease](/Traits.aspx?ID=46), [Primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=134)) The first time each round a creature takes damage from the warden's rotten bark, the target becomes [sickened 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=91) as the flesh where it was struck momentarily twists and rots, causing considerable pain.

<title level="1" pfs="Standard">[Sea Serpent](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3177)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

These fabled beasts resemble massive snakes with long rows of finned spines down their back. Temperamental and territorial, sea serpents can capsize a boat with ease, and most won't hesitate to do so when hungry or threatened. Stories abound of aggrieved captains who spend their entire lives hunting down the elusive monster that sunk their ships and took their livelihoods. These hunts rely on rumors and glimpses of the beasts, as few survive the catastrophes wrought by sea serpents.

 While many fishermen's tales paint sea serpents as divinely appointed guardians of the ocean or as evil and demonic agents, the truth is that most sea serpents are simply very large beasts with a knack for avoiding magical detection.

text: Sea Serpent These fabled beasts resemble massive snakes with long rows of finned spines down their back. Temperamental and territorial, sea serpents can capsize a boat with ease, and most won't hesitate to do so when hungry or threatened. Stories abound of aggrieved captains who spend their entire lives hunting down the elusive monster that sunk their ships and took their livelihoods. Shining children are wicked, enigmatic monsters that roam remote planes and untraveled corners of the universe in search of esoteric lore. With their abnormally gaunt frames, long white hair, and unnerving, four-fingered hands, shining children are both strangely familiar and otherworldly in appearance, though they are barely visible within the shroud of blinding light they continually emit. Their faces are truly horrible, however, as their overlarge eyes and distended, gaping mouths reveal their heads to be voids filled with unnatural light. Shining children use this light as a weapon, weaving illusions and focusing beams of fiery brilliance. Because of their reputation as scholars of the alien and the eldritch, shining children are sometimes summoned by powerful wizards or occultists in search of rare knowledge. The creatures never give away their lore without some price, though, and typically demand in return the performance of contemptible deeds that further their inscrutable, far-ranging plans. These mysterious beings are natives of the [Astral Plane](/Planes.aspx?ID=33). In that vast plane, accretions of metaphysical matter gradually accumulate and eventually coalesce into demiplanes. During this tumultuous process, sparks of living light sometimes shear off the newly formed planes, and these sparks of raw planar energy somehow transform into shining children. Every newly formed demiplane leaves a different mental imprint on its shining “offspring,” making it easy for shining children to telepathically recognize their brothers and sisters. Forever trapped in apparently adolescent bodies, shining children dedicate themselves to scholarship and violence with equal measure in a futile effort to understand their roles in the multiverse and the burning injustice of their births. Shining children confuse most other creatures with their refusal to use individual names in favor of alternating between referring to each other singularly and collectively. **[Recall Knowledge - Astral](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=44)): DC 30 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 28 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 25 [Shining Child](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3190) **Source** [Monster Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=221) pg. 308 1.1 **Perception** +23; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59) **Languages** [Aklo](/Languages.aspx?ID=13); [telepathy](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=79) 120 feet **Skills** [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=2) +18, [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5) +23, [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=6) +21, [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=7) +21, [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=11) +18 **Str** +2 **Dex** +5 **Con** +6 **Int** +2 **Wis** +5 **Cha** +7 **Radiance Dependence** The shining child is [off-guard](/Conditions.aspx?ID=58) while in areas of [darkness](/Rules.aspx?ID=409). --- **AC** 33 **Fort** +22 **Ref** +19 **Will** +19 **HP** 215 **Immunities** [blinded](/Conditions.aspx?ID=59), [dazzled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=65), [fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=604) **Blinding Aura** ([arcane](/Traits.aspx?ID=534), [aura](/Traits.aspx?ID=542), [incapacitation](/Traits.aspx?ID=631), [light](/Traits.aspx?ID=640)) 60 feet. The shining child sheds [bright light](/Rules.aspx?ID=407). Any creature that starts its turn in the aura must succeed at a DC 29 Fortitude save. If it fails, it is [blinded](/Conditions.aspx?ID=59) for 1 minute, and if it critically fails, it's permanently blinded. A creature that succeeds at its save is temporarily immune to this effect for 24 hours.
**Overwhelming Light** ([light](/Traits.aspx?ID=640)) **Trigger** The shining child enters an area of magical [darkness](/Traits.aspx?ID=569) or begins its turn in an area of magical darkness; **Effect** The shining child attempts to [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) the magical darkness (counteract rank 7, counteract modifier +23). --- **Speed** 30 feet, fly 50 feet **Melee** fist +25 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [Finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=179), [Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103)), **Damage** 3d4+5 bludgeoning plus 4d6 fire and 2d4 [persistent fire](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29) **Melee** fire ray +25 ([Arcane](/Traits.aspx?ID=11), [Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103), [range 100 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=248)), **Damage** 3d10+3 fire, plus 2d10 vitality damage if the target is [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=722) **Occult Innate Spells** DC 33 - **Cantrips (6th)** [Light](/Spells.aspx?ID=171) - **2nd** [Illusory Object](/Spells.aspx?ID=160) (at will) - **4th** [Translocate](/Spells.aspx?ID=1724) (at will) - **5th** [False Vision](/Spells.aspx?ID=109), [Mirage](/Spells.aspx?ID=1604), [Translocate](/Spells.aspx?ID=1724) - **6th** [Dispel Magic](/Spells.aspx?ID=78), [Vibrant Pattern](/Spells.aspx?ID=357), [Wall of Force](/Spells.aspx?ID=363) - **7th** [Sunburst](/Spells.aspx?ID=1707) (x2)

The shisagishin takes delight in infiltrating a community and then disguising itself as the horribly decayed or mutilated remains of a loved one or adored public figure, only to spring to life in its true form during funeral services. A shisagishin epitomizes the cycle of decay giving rise to new life. **[Recall Knowledge - Fiend](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46)): DC 30 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 28 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 25 [Shisagishin](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2804) **Source** [Pathfinder #199: To Bloom Below the Web](/Sources.aspx?ID=225) pg. 85 **Perception** +22; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59) **Languages** [Aklo](/Languages.aspx?ID=13), [Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1), [Necril](/Languages.aspx?ID=20) **Skills** [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=1) +25, [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5) +24, [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=7) +22, [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=11) +21, [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15) +25 **Str** +4 **Dex** +7 **Con** +4 **Int** +3 **Wis** +4 **Cha** +6 --- **AC** 33 **Fort** +22 **Ref** +25 **Will** +20 **HP** 214 **Resistances** negative 10 **Weaknesses** silver 10 [Attack of Opportunity](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=3)
**Burst From Death** ([attack **Requirement** Initiative hasn't yet been rolled](/Traits.aspx?ID=540), and the shisagishin is disguised as a corpse with Manifest Corpse Shell) **Trigger** A creature touches the disguised shisagishin or a coffin or other container the shisagishin has been placed into; **Effect** The shisagishin violently unfolds into its true form, shredding its decaying corpse shell, and attempts a claw Strike on an adjacent target before it rolls initiative.
**Soul Shred** Creatures killed by an shisagishin are difficult to bring back to life or to animate as undead. The shisagishin automatically attempts to counteract any attempt to resurrect or animate as undead any creature that it has killed (counteract modifier +21, counteract level 6th). If the shisagishin who slew the creature is itself slain, the creature can be brought back from death or become undead normally.
 --- **Speed** 40 feet **Melee** claw +25 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [deadly d6](/Traits.aspx?ID=174), [Finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=179), [Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103)), **Damage** 3d8+7 slashing plus 1d6 mental and [Grab](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=45) **Occult Innate Spells** DC 32, attack +24 - **Cantrips (6th)** [Daze](/Spells.aspx?ID=61), [Ghost Sound](/Spells.aspx?ID=132), [Message](/Spells.aspx?ID=190) - **2nd** [Death Knell](/Spells.aspx?ID=63) (at will), [Item Facade](/Spells.aspx?ID=166) - **5th** [Hallucination](/Spells.aspx?ID=144), [Phantasmal Killer](/Spells.aspx?ID=219) - **6th** [Vampiric Exsanguination](/Spells.aspx?ID=353) **Spread Decay** The shisagishin causes the flesh of any number of creatures grabbed or restrained by it to swiftly begin to decay. Each of those creatures must attempt a DC 32 Fortitude save. **Critical Success** The creature is unaffected.
**Success** The creature takes 2d8 negative damage.
**Failure** The creature takes 4d8 negative damage and is [enfeebled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=71) 1.
**Critical Failure** The creature takes 6d8 negative damage and is enfeebled 2 **Manifest Corpse Shell** ([Concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32), [Conjuration](/Traits.aspx?ID=33), [Occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=120)) The shisagishin tucks its arms and legs into its body, drops prone, and manifests a decaying and/or mutilated humanoid corpse around itself over the course of 10 minutes of concentration. The shisagishin can cause this corpse to appear to be the remains of a specific creature it has seen before by Impersonating that creature with Deception. Once its corpse shell has manifested, until the next time the shisagishin acts, it appears to be a corpse. It has an automatic result of 44 on Deception checks and DCs to pass as a corpse.

<title level="1" pfs="Standard">[Shuln](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3191)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

Scourges of the upper Darklands, these enormous, mole-like monstrosities slice and burrow through solid stone with massive forearms and adamantine-strong claws. Shulns grow to about 20 feet long and have four tiny, nearly imperceptible eyes; a long, pale snout; four thick-muscled legs that end in long, serrated claws; and a stubby pink tail. As a young shuln matures, its unique metabolism produces adamantine that becomes infused throughout its skeletal system. In addition to making their claws and fangs nearly unbreakable, this unique physiological trait makes shulns unparalleled burrowers and highly sought by monster hunters who hope to harvest the precious material from their corpses.

 Shulns have a ravenous appetite and eat nearly anything they can catch, but their preferred diet consists almost entirely of large invertebrates, especially [cave worms](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2871) (page 54). They rely on tiny sensory whiskers that cover their snouts and allow them to detect subtle movements in the air and ground without the use of vision. When they detect suitable prey, shulns bite their target at the first opportunity, injecting it with a potent paralytic toxin present in their saliva. So strong is this poison that it's capable of subduing even the near-unstoppable cave worm, making shulns a valuable (if dangerous) companion to anyone making excursions into worm-infested regions of the Darklands. Shulns' notoriously ill-tempered dispositions and their knack for digging into areas of an underground settlement where digging ought not to occur make them frustrating creatures to keep around, but when the alternative is an unpredictable but deadly visit from an enormous, hungry cave worm, the annoyances are well worth the trouble.

 Encounters with much larger shuln-like entities on the [Plane of Earth](/Planes.aspx?ID=30) suggest that these creatures may have originated from there. The larger shulns still retain their elemental qualities, are quite a bit smarter, and have their own suite of earth-themed innate primal spells—but for all that, they still love the taste of cave worm.

Sinmolds arise from the corruption wrought by [Treerazer](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3218) machinations. As the land transforms, it attracts souls bound for the Outer Realms. These souls coalesce bodies out of fungal slime, birthing amorphous fiends that ravenously hunt for more biological matter using club-like pseudopods or whiplike tendrils that can slice with ease through meat and bone alike. **[Recall Knowledge - Fiend](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46)): DC 35 **[Recall Knowledge - Fungus](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43)): DC 35 **[Recall Knowledge - Ooze](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=44)): DC 35 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 33 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 30 [Sinmold](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3780) **Source** [Pathfinder #210: Whispers in the Dirt](/Sources.aspx?ID=253) pg. 86 **Perception** +22; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59), [lifesense](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=67) ([imprecise](/Rules.aspx?ID=412)) 60 feet **Languages** [Chthonian](/Languages.aspx?ID=114), [Draconic](/Languages.aspx?ID=2), [Empyrean](/Languages.aspx?ID=115); [telepathy](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=79) 100 feet **Skills** [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) +24, [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46) +22, [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=48) +13 **Str** +6 **Dex** -5 **Con** +7 **Int** +0 **Wis** +4 **Cha** +2 --- **AC** 23 **Fort** +25 **Ref** +11 **Will** +22 **HP** 300 **Immunities** [acid](/Traits.aspx?ID=524), bleed, critical hits, [disease](/Traits.aspx?ID=578), precision **Weaknesses** [cold iron](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2916) 10, [holy](/Traits.aspx?ID=517) 10 **Desperation Vulnerability** Sinmolds are aware that they're in a vulnerable state as formless “newborn fiends” and are desperate to become stronger before they become prey to more powerful demons. text: Sinmold Sinmolds arise from the corruption wrought by Treerazer machinations. As the land transforms, it attracts souls bound for the Outer Realms. These souls coalesce bodies out of fungal slime, birthing amorphous fiends that ravenously hunt for more biological matter using club-like pseudopods or whiplike tendrils that can slice with ease through meat and bone alike. Recall Knowledge - Fiend (Religion): DC 35 Recall Knowledge - Fungus (Nature): DC 35 Recall Knowledge - Ooze (Occultism): DC 35 Unspecific Lore : DC 33 Specific Lore : DC 30 Sinmold Source Pathfinder #210: Whispers in the Dirt pg. 86 Perception +22; darkvision, lifesense (imprecise) 60 feet Languages Chthonian, Draconic, Empyrean; telepathy 100 feet Skills Athletics +24, Religion +22, Stealth +13 Str +6 Dex -5 Con +7 Int +0 Wis +4 Cha +2 --- AC 23 Fort +25 Ref +11 Will +22 HP 300 Immunities acid, bleed, critical hits, disease, precision Weaknesses cold iron 10, holy 10 Desperation Vulnerability Sinmolds are aware that they're in a vulnerable state as formless “newborn fiends” and are desperate to become stronger before they become prey to more powerful demons. Whenever the sinmold is in a combat encounter and ends its turn without dealing damage to another creature, the sinmold takes 3d6 mental damage and becomes frightened 1. Digestion (healing) The first time in a round when the sinmold damages a creature with Engulf, the sinmold immediately restores Hit Points equal to the damage dealt, gaining Hit Points in excess of its maximum as temporary Hit Points that last for 1 hour. As long as the sinmold possesses these temporary Hit Points, its surface hardens, and its AC increases to 30. --- Speed 30 feet, climb 30 feet, swim 30 feet Melee Single Action pseudopod +24 (Magical, Unholy), Damage 3d6+12 bludgeoning plus 2d6 acid Melee Single Action tendril +24 (Agile, Magical, reach 10 feet, Unholy), Damage 3d8+12 slashing plus sinmold infestation Engulf Two Actions DC 32, 3d10 acid plus digestion, Escape DC 32, Rupture 18 Sinmold Infestation (Poison) Saving Throw DC 32 Fortitude; Maximum Duration 6 rounds; Stage 1 2d8 poison damage (1 round); Stage 2 3d8 poison damage and can hear the thoughts of root rotters within 30 feet as an imprecise sense (1 round); Stage 3 as stage 2, but 4d8 poison damage and doomed 1 (1 round); Stage 4 as stage 3, and arise as a root rotter upon death (1 round) Spore Purge Single Action (Poison) Requirements The sinmold has temporary Hit Points from digestion; Effect The sinmold loses all temporary Hit Points and releases any creatures it currently has engulfed, pushing them into the nearest unoccupied spaces. It releases a cloud of spores from its body, dealing 5d8 poison damage (DC 29 basic Fortitude save) in a 20-foot emanation. Any creature that fails this save also must attempt a save against sinmold infestation. Demonic Transformation A sinmold who has devoured many creatures over a period of 1 to 2 weeks hardens their exterior into a cocoon and metamorphosizes into a demon. This transformation takes 3 days, during which time the sinmold is unconscious, increases their AC to 37 and maximum Hit Points to 400, and gains Hardness 10. Sinmolds look for a safe place to transform, such as an underground shelter or a dense treetop canopy, though some simply eat until they cocoon. The sins the soul committed in life determine the demon that a sinmold becomes, so the resulting form can become higher or lower level, as determined by the GM.

A servant of [Torag](/Deities.aspx?ID=18), Stoneriver resembles a pangolin with glowing blue eyes and brassy, rune-covered scales. Stoneriver burrows through Golarion's mantle and crust as he hunts down subterranean fiends, aids virtuous communities, and defends sacred sites, often collaborating with dwarves. **[Recall Knowledge - Celestial](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=13)): DC 40 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 38 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 35 [Stoneriver](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2709) **Source** [Pathfinder #195: Heavy is the Crown](/Sources.aspx?ID=210) pg. 88 **Perception** +23; (33 to detect lies and illusions) [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=12), [scent](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=33) ([imprecise](/Rules.aspx?ID=412)) 60 feet **Languages** [Celestial](/Languages.aspx?ID=16), [Dwarven](/Languages.aspx?ID=3); [_tongues_](/Spells.aspx?ID=340) **Skills** [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=1) +20, [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) +26, [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=6) +21, [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=7) +21, [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15) +20, [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=16) +23, [Torag Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8) +24 **Str** +8 **Dex** +4 **Con** +7 **Int** +4 **Wis** +5 **Cha** +5 --- **AC** 32 **Fort** +25 **Ref** +20 **Will** +21 +2 status to all saves vs. magic **HP** 220 , regeneration 30 (deactivated by [cold](/Traits.aspx?ID=27) or [evil](/Traits.aspx?ID=64)) **Immunities** [fear](/Traits.aspx?ID=68), [fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=72) **Weaknesses** cold 10 **Bolster Torag's Chosen** ([abjuration](/Traits.aspx?ID=2), [aura](/Traits.aspx?ID=206), [divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=48)) 20 feet. [Dwarves](/Traits.aspx?ID=54) and creatures that worship [Torag](/Deities.aspx?ID=18) in the area gain a +1 status bonus to AC and Will saves.
**[Retributive Strike](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=31)** --- **Speed** 30 feet, burrow 30 feet, swim 30 feet **Melee** tongue +26 ([Good](/Traits.aspx?ID=83), [Disarm](/Traits.aspx?ID=175), [Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103), [reach 30 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)), **Damage** 3d6+11 bludgeoning plus 1d6 good and [Improved Grab](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=27) **Melee** claw +26 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [Good](/Traits.aspx?ID=83), [Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103), [reach 20 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)), **Damage** 3d8+11 slashing plus 1d6 good and 1d6 fire **Melee** tail +26 ([Backswing](/Traits.aspx?ID=173), [fatal d12](/Traits.aspx?ID=178), [Good](/Traits.aspx?ID=83), [Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103), [reach 20 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)), **Damage** 3d8+11 slashing plus 1d6 good and 1d6 fire **Divine Innate Spells** DC 29, attack +24 - **Cantrips (5th)** [Light](/Spells.aspx?ID=171) - **1st** [Detect Alignment](/Spells.aspx?ID=65) (at will; evil only) - **2nd** [Remove Fear](/Spells.aspx?ID=252) (at will), [Restoration](/Spells.aspx?ID=258) - **3rd** [Heal](/Spells.aspx?ID=148) (×2) - **4th** [Divine Wrath](/Spells.aspx?ID=86), [Searing Light](/Spells.aspx?ID=269) (×2) - **5th** [Blazing Fissure](/Spells.aspx?ID=870), [Flame Strike](/Spells.aspx?ID=120) - **Constant (5th)** [Tongues](/Spells.aspx?ID=340) **Devour Magic** ([Divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=48), [Transmutation](/Traits.aspx?ID=157)) Whenever Stoneriver deals damage with [Swallow Whole](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=35), he consumes one of the swallowed creature's magical effects, as [_dispel magic_](/Spells.aspx?ID=78) with a +21 [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) modifier. **[Improved Grab](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=27)** **Measure Soul** ([Concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32), [Divination](/Traits.aspx?ID=47), [Divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=48), [Mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=106)) Stoneriver mentally pries through the mind of a creature within 60 feet, dealing 10d8 mental damage (DC 29 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Will save). Stoneriver can choose to make this damage nonlethal or choose not to damage the creature at all. For 1 minute, Stoneriver gains a +1 circumstance bonus to attack rolls, damage rolls, and Perception checks against that creature. self only), [Paranoia](/Spells.aspx?ID=214) (at will) - **3rd** [Soothe](/Spells.aspx?ID=291) (×3) - **4th** [Confusion](/Spells.aspx?ID=48), [Globe of Invulnerability](/Spells.aspx?ID=137) **Arcane Prepared Spells** DC 29, attack +21 - **Cantrips (6th)** [Daze](/Spells.aspx?ID=61), [Mage Hand](/Spells.aspx?ID=177), [Message](/Spells.aspx?ID=190), [Shield](/Spells.aspx?ID=280), [Telekinetic Projectile](/Spells.aspx?ID=334) - **1st** [Charm](/Spells.aspx?ID=34), [Fear](/Spells.aspx?ID=110), [Unseen Servant](/Spells.aspx?ID=352) - **2nd** [Hideous Laughter](/Spells.aspx?ID=150), [Humanoid Form](/Spells.aspx?ID=153), [Misdirection](/Spells.aspx?ID=198) - **3rd** [Haste](/Spells.aspx?ID=147), [Locate](/Spells.aspx?ID=173), [Slow](/Spells.aspx?ID=289) - **4th** [Dimension Door](/Spells.aspx?ID=69), [Phantasmal Killer](/Spells.aspx?ID=219), [Suggestion](/Spells.aspx?ID=315) - **5th** [Dimension Door](/Spells.aspx?ID=69), [Sending](/Spells.aspx?ID=272), [Wall of Stone](/Spells.aspx?ID=365) - **6th** [Baleful Polymorph](/Spells.aspx?ID=17), [Dispel Magic](/Spells.aspx?ID=78), [Flesh to Stone](/Spells.aspx?ID=123) **Body Thief** ([Manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104), [Necromancy](/Traits.aspx?ID=117), [Occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=120), [Possession](/Traits.aspx?ID=129)) The intellect devourer reduces in size and burrows into the brain of a creature dead for no longer than 1 day. At the start of the intellect devourer's next turn, the body revives at its maximum Hit Points, controlled by the devourer. The intellect devourer is conscious and can sense everything the possessed body could. Any effect that ends the possession kills the host body with the same effects as Exit Body. The intellect devourer can't use any of the host creature's spells with Body Thief but can use its own spells. The host body slowly decays while inhabited by the intellect devourer, becoming uninhabitable after 7 days unless preserved with [_gentle repose_](/Spells.aspx?ID=131) or a similar effect. **Exit Body** ([Move](/Traits.aspx?ID=114)) **Requirements** The intellect devourer is controlling a body with Body Thief; **Effect** The intellect devourer leaves its host body, which dies instantly and is no longer a suitable host for any Body Thief ability. The intellect devourer appears at full size in an adjacent space. **Nightmare Curse** ([Curse](/Traits.aspx?ID=38), [Illusion](/Traits.aspx?ID=92), [Incapacitation](/Traits.aspx?ID=93), [Mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=106), [Occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=120)) **Frequency** once per day; **Effect** Tiluatchek reaches out with his mind to infect the dreams of a single creature within 60 feet that he can see. The target suddenly experiences a brief but overwhelming memory of a harrowing nightmare it had at some point in the past and must attempt a DC 32 Will save. The effects of this curse are permanent until the target is cured (although any frightened condition values imparted by the curse pass and end normally). **Critical Success** The target is unaffected, and the nightmare vision passes as swiftly as it appears.
**Success** The vision causes the target to become [frightened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=76) 1. The target also becomes cursed. Every time it attempts to sleep, it's plagued by nightmares of being stalked through an endless maze of caverns by something that wants to steal its body and eat its brain. The cursed creature now requires 10 hours of rest (rather than 8) in order to be able to make its daily preparations and can't take the Long-Term Rest activity at all.
**Failure** As success, but frightened 2, and each time the target sleeps, it suffers the effects of a [_nightmare_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1615) spell (DC 32 Will save).
**Critical Failure** As failure, but frightened 3 and fleeing for as long as it remains frightened. If the cursed target ever rolls a critical failure against a _nightmare_ spell while it remains cursed (including those caused by the curse itself), it dies in its sleep. If at the time of this death Tiluatchek is also dead (but for no more than 1 year), the intellect devourer is restored to life inside of the target creature's body as if he'd used Body Thief to take the body over. **Ravage** The intellect devourer makes two talon Strikes against a [paralyzed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=85), [restrained](/Conditions.aspx?ID=90), or [unconscious](/Conditions.aspx?ID=95) creature, using the same attack modifier as its highest attack modifier. These Strikes gain the death trait. If Ravage kills the target, the intellect devourer may use Body Thief against it as a free action. **Stolen Identity** While an intellect devourer uses Body Thief, it gains the ability to understand and speak all languages known by the host, as well as knowledge of the host body's abilities, identity, role in society, and personality. However, it does not gain the specific memories or knowledge of the host body.

The powerful adamantine dragons are one of several dragons known as skymetal dragons. The innate magic that flows through these dragons causes them to draw particular metals to their bodies like magnets or, in some cases, naturally grow these skymetals on their bodies. Adamantine dragons begin their lives with tough scales that are naturally replaced with thicker and even tougher adamantine plating as they grow older. Adamantine dragons are typically steadfast and loyal. Once they commit to a certain purpose, changing their minds is nigh impossible. **[Recall Knowledge - Dragon](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35)): DC 31 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 29 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 26 [Adult Adamantine Dragon](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2933) **Source** [Monster Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=221) pg. 109 1.1 **Perception** +23; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59), [scent](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=74) ([imprecise](/Rules.aspx?ID=412)) 60 feet, [tremorsense](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=82) ([imprecise](/Rules.aspx?ID=412)) 90 feet **Languages** [Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1), [Draconic](/Languages.aspx?ID=2), [Fey](/Languages.aspx?ID=119), [Petran](/Languages.aspx?ID=109), [Sakvroth](/Languages.aspx?ID=118) **Skills** [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=1) +22, [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) +27, [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=7) +24, [Mining Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8) +24, [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=10) +23, [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=16) +25 **Str** +8 **Dex** +3 **Con** +6 **Int** +3 **Wis** +4 **Cha** +5 --- **AC** 33 **Fort** +25 **Ref** +20 **Will** +23 +2 status to all saves vs. [primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=676) **HP** 220 **Immunities** [paralyzed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=85), [petrified](/Conditions.aspx?ID=87), [sleep](/Traits.aspx?ID=696) **Resistances** physical 15 (except [adamantine](/Equipment.aspx?ID=374))

Mirage dragons are masters of illusion magic and use their powers to deceive others and further their own agendas. In addition to their magical prowess, mirage dragons possess a number of additional features to help them on hunts or mislead attackers, such as their camouflaging scales and a hallucinatory breath that can confound multiple foes at once. Mirage dragons are vain and egotistical figures. They ultimately care more about themselves than others. **[Recall Knowledge - Dragon](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35)): DC 31 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 29 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 26 [Adult Mirage Dragon](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2951) **Source** [Monster Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=221) pg. 122 1.1 **Perception** +25; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59), illusion sense, [scent](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=74) ([imprecise](/Rules.aspx?ID=412)) 60 feet **Languages** [Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1), [Draconic](/Languages.aspx?ID=2), [Fey](/Languages.aspx?ID=119) **Skills** [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=1) +25, [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=2) +24, [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) +25, [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=4) +24, [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5) +29, [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=6) +27, [Illusion Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8) +26, [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=12) +27, [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15) +27, [Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=17) +25 **Str** +6 **Dex** +6 **Con** +5 **Int** +5 **Wis** +6 **Cha** +8 **Camouflage** The dragon can [Hide](/Actions.aspx?ID=2404) in natural environments even if they don't have [cover](/Rules.aspx?ID=459).
**Illusion Sense** When the dragon moves within 30 feet of an [illusion](/Traits.aspx?ID=629) that can be disbelieved, they automatically attempt a [secret](/Traits.aspx?ID=690) check to disbelieve, even if they didn't spend an action to Interact. --- **AC** 33 **Fort** +22 **Ref** +23 **Will** +25 +2 status to all saves vs. [arcane](/Traits.aspx?ID=534) **HP** 235 **Immunities** [fascinated](/Conditions.aspx?ID=72), [paralyzed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=85), [sleep](/Traits.aspx?ID=696) **Scintillating Defense** ([visual](/Traits.aspx?ID=727)) **Trigger** The dragon is targeted with an attack; **Effect** The dragon flashes their iridescent scales at the triggering creature to throw off the attack. The dragon gains [concealment](/Conditions.aspx?ID=62)against the triggering attack. --- **Speed** 50 feet, climb 30 feet, fly 150 feet **Melee** jaws +25 ([Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103), [reach 15 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)), **Damage** 3d10+12 piercing **Melee** claws +25 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103), [reach 10 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)), **Damage** 3d6+12 slashing **Melee** tail +23 ([Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103), [reach 20 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)), **Damage** 3d8+12 bludgeoning **Arcane Innate Spells** DC 35 - **Cantrips (7th)** [Figment](/Spells.aspx?ID=1528), [Message](/Spells.aspx?ID=190) - **2nd** [Invisibility](/Spells.aspx?ID=164) (at will) - **4th** [Illusory Object](/Spells.aspx?ID=160) (at will), [Invisibility](/Spells.aspx?ID=164) - **6th** [Illusory Creature](/Spells.aspx?ID=158), [Illusory Scene](/Spells.aspx?ID=161), [Mirage](/Spells.aspx?ID=1604), [Vibrant Pattern](/Spells.aspx?ID=357) **Captivating Display** ([Arcane](/Traits.aspx?ID=11), [Visual](/Traits.aspx?ID=163)) **Frequency** once per 10 minutes; **Effect** The dragon opens the fins on their head, creating a radiant display of enthralling colors. Each creature in a 30-foot emanation must succeed at a DC 33 Will save or be [dazzled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=65) and [slowed 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=92) (or slowed 2 on a critical failure) for 1 round. Regardless of the result, a creature is then temporarily immune to Captivating Display for 1 minute. **Draconic Frenzy** The dragon makes two claw Strikes and one tail Strike in any order. **Draconic Momentum** The dragon recharges their Hallucinatory Breath whenever they score a critical hit with a Strike. **Hallucinatory Breath** ([Arcane](/Traits.aspx?ID=11), [Emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=60), [Mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=106)) The dragon breathes a cloud that assaults the senses and deals 12d6 mental damage in a 40-foot cone (DC 33 Will save). A creature that fails its save is also [confused](/Conditions.aspx?ID=63) for 1 round (1 minute on a critical failure) and is then temporarily immune to being confused by Hallucinatory Breath for 1 hour. The dragon can't use Hallucinatory Breath again for 1d4 rounds. **Lunging Bite** The dragon lunges their head forward, making a jaws Strike with an extended reach of 25 feet. **[Sneak Attack](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=34)** The dragon's Strikes deal an additional 2d6 precision damage to [off-guard](/Conditions.aspx?ID=58) targets.

Across the crooked folds of the [Dimension of Time](/Planes.aspx?ID=46), intense emotions gather like flotsam in the still waters of river pools. These accumulate over ages, harvesting stronger feelings during times of great change such as calamities and the rule of tyrannical despots, as well as periods of joy and pride. These accretions eventually give birth to siktemporas. The anguish siktempora is rare, even among others of their kind. They delight in seeking out creatures to inflict their suffering upon, the utterances of their dreadful wails relieve their anguish—if only for a fleeting moment. With a huge, malformed human head gaping in the act of screaming, their sickly hook-ended limbs hang limply below the neck. When an anguish siktempora bites foes with their jaws, they continue screaming, adding sonic damage to the already crushing punishment their numerous grinding teeth inflict. **[Recall Knowledge - Time](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=44), [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=44)): DC 36 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 34 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 31 [Anguish Siktempora](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3743) **Source** [Pathfinder #204: Stage Fright](/Sources.aspx?ID=245) pg. 89 **Perception** +26; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59) **Languages** [Aklo](/Languages.aspx?ID=13); (can't speak any language); [telepathy](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=79) 300 feet **Skills** [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=34) +24, [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) +27, [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38) +24, [Dimension of Time Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) +26, [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=40) +24 **Str** +8 **Dex** +5 **Con** +5 **Int** +5 **Wis** +7 **Cha** +5 **Temporal Sense** A siktempora can always roll [Dimension of Time Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) for initiative. When it does, it gains a +2 circumstance bonus to the roll. --- **AC** 34 **Fort** +24 **Ref** +22 **Will** +26 **HP** 180 , regeneration 40 (deactivated by [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647), [orichalcum](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2859), or [spirit](/Traits.aspx?ID=737)) **Immunities** [disease](/Traits.aspx?ID=578), [emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=590), [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=669) **Foster Fear** Creatures with the frightened condition are always off-guard to the anguish siktempora.
**Uncanny Pounce** **Trigger** The anguish siktempora rolls [Dimension of Time Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) for initiative; **Effect** The siktempora Strides once and makes a jaws Strike, in either order. --- **Speed** 10 feet, fly 40 feet **Melee** jaws +27, **Damage** 3d6+14 bludgeoning plus 2d6 sonic **Melee** claw +27 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170)), **Damage** 3d8+14 slashing **Occult Innate Spells** DC 33 - **4th** [Translocate](/Spells.aspx?ID=1724) (at will) - **7th** [Flicker](/Spells.aspx?ID=1532) - **Constant (7th)** [Fly](/Spells.aspx?ID=125) **[Rend](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=73)** claw **Scream of Despair** ([Emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=60), [Mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=106), [Occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=120), [Sonic](/Traits.aspx?ID=147)) The anguish siktempora emits a terrible scream in a 30-foot emanation. Creatures in the area must attempt a DC 33 Will save. The anguish siktempora can't use Scream of Despair for 1d4 rounds. **Critical Success** The creature is unaffected.
**Success** The creature takes 2d6 mental damage, 2d6 sonic damage, and is [frightened 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=76).
**Failure** The creature takes 6d6 mental damage, 6d6 sonic damage, and is frightened 2.

The frightened creature takes 6d6 mental damage (DC 30 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Will save).

Most nindorus are harmed by silver, but not the argyrzei. Instead, argyrzeis use silver as a method of spreading sickness and pain, and to help them manipulate the minds of those who unwittingly fall under the curse of their infected gifts. They delight in disguising themselves and then selling or giving infected silver to victims. Other nindorus particularly fear argyrzeis for their mastery over silver, knowing that they're capable of causing painful wounds with their silver blades. Argyrzeis appear humanoid, but their feet point backwards and they have no heads. Their glowing red neck stumps are stuffed with a wide assortment of knives, blades, and shards of metal. These nindorus represent the cycle of art being created, destroyed, and recycled into new art. **[Recall Knowledge - Fiend](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46)): DC 31 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 29 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 26 [Argyrzei](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2803) **Source** [Pathfinder #199: To Bloom Below the Web](/Sources.aspx?ID=225) pg. 84 **Perception** +23; cursesense, [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59) **Languages** [Aklo](/Languages.aspx?ID=13), [Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1), [Necril](/Languages.aspx?ID=20) **Skills** [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) +27, [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=4) +25, [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5) +24, [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=11) +25, [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15) +24 **Str** +8 **Dex** +5 **Con** +4 **Int** +6 **Wis** +4 **Cha** +5 **Cursesense** The argyrzei can see and hear through any silver object it cursed, as long as the object is within 1 mile.
 --- **AC** 34 **Fort** +23 **Ref** +24 **Will** +21 **HP** 240 **Resistances** negative 10, silver 10 **Headless** An argyrzei is headless but can still hear, speak, see, and smell as if it had a head. The argyrzei is immune to decapitation effects, such as those caused by [vorpal](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2853) weapons. **Soul Shred** Creatures killed by an argyrzei are difficult to bring back to life or to animate as undead. The argyrzei automatically attempts to counteract any attempt to resurrect or animate as undead any creature that it has killed (counteract modifier +23, counteract level 7th). If the argyrzei who slew the creature is itself slain, the creature can be brought back from death or become undead normally. --- **Speed** 25 feet **Melee** silver blade +28 ([Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103), [two-hand d12](/Traits.aspx?ID=198)), **Damage** 2d8+11 slashing plus 1d6 [persistent bleed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29) and 1d6 mental **Occult Innate Spells** DC 33, +25 attack - **Cantrips (7th)** [Daze](/Spells.aspx?ID=61), [Mage Hand](/Spells.aspx?ID=177), [Telekinetic Projectile](/Spells.aspx?ID=334) - **3rd** [Illusory Disguise](/Spells.aspx?ID=159) (at will), [Item Facade](/Spells.aspx?ID=166) - **5th** [Subconscious Suggestion](/Spells.aspx?ID=314) - **6th** [Dominate](/Spells.aspx?ID=87), [Illusory Scene](/Spells.aspx?ID=161) - **7th** [Phantom Pain](/Spells.aspx?ID=220) **Infect Silver** ([Concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32), [Curse](/Traits.aspx?ID=38), [Necromancy](/Traits.aspx?ID=117), [Occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=120)) **Frequency** once per day; **Effect** The argyrzei concentrates on an adjacent silver object that's no larger than Bulk 2. That object becomes cursed; if the object is being carried, the object's carrier can resist the object becoming cursed with a DC 33 Will save. The argyrzei can maintain up to five curses simultaneously; if it infects a sixth silver item, the oldest cursed item becomes uncursed. **Manifest Silver Blade** ([Concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32), [Conjuration](/Traits.aspx?ID=33), [Occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=120)) **Requirement** The argyrzei isn't carrying a silver blade; **Effect** The argyrzei pulls one of the broken silver weapons from the stump of its neck, transforming it into a _+1 striking [wounding](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2854) silver [bastard sword](/Weapons.aspx?ID=370)_. This weapon crumbles into sand if it leaves the argyrzei's possession.

text: Argyrzei (Headless Nindoru) Most nindorus are harmed by silver, but not the argyrzei. Instead, argyrzeis use silver as a method of spreading sickness and pain, and to help them manipulate the minds of those who unwittingly fall under the curse of their infected gifts. They delight in disguising themselves and then selling or giving infected silver to victims. Other nindorus particularly fear argyrzeis for their mastery over silver, knowing that they're capable of causing painful wounds with their silver blades. Argyrzeis appear humanoid, but their feet point backwards and they have no heads. Their glowing red neck stumps are stuffed with a wide assortment of knives, blades, and shards of metal. These nindorus represent the cycle of art being created, destroyed, and recycled into new art. The argyrzei is immune to decapitation effects, such as those caused by vorpal weapons. Soul Shred Creatures killed by an argyrzei are difficult to bring back to life or to animate as undead. The argyrzei automatically attempts to counteract any attempt to resurrect or animate as undead any creature that it has killed (counteract modifier +23, counteract level 7th). <title level="1" pfs="">[Azarpal](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3738)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

Azarpals resemble bipedal hogs with wide-tusked mouths, bloated bellies, and long, bristly tails. They can store food in their multiple stomachs for long periods of time, slowly infusing it with a signature poison that causes those afflicted to sweat profusely and succumb to intense nausea.

 Azarpals love spreading discontent via poisoned food. They delight in traveling caravan routes, disguised as merchants, constantly sampling regional cuisines, and choosing their favorites for stomach storage and poison infusion. Then, upon reaching a land where the dish is rare or sought after, they find a place to leave the meal out for an unwary traveler. They might also find a way to introduce the poisoned meal to a tavern or restaurant and hang back to watch the resulting fun.

**Culinary Alchemy**   The azarpal knows the formulas for all common and [uncommon](/Traits.aspx?ID=721) [alchemical foods](/Equipment.aspx?Category=6&Subcategory=92) of its level or lower in _Treasure Vault_ without needing a formula book. A typical azarpal carries about 700 gp of alchemical food.

**Gulp or Grab** <actions string="Three Actions" /> ([Manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104)) The Azarpal swallows a single meal or alchemical food and stores it in one of six stomachs. Therein, the food doesn't spoil (drinks must be swallowed in closed containers, or they spill and affect the azarpal normally). The azarpal can use this activity to reach into its mouth and retrieve a stored item as well. Any item that remains stored in an azarpal's stomach for at least 24 hours becomes laced with azarpal poison.

**Lasting Illusion**   When an azarpal casts [_illusory disguise_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1568) and only targets themselves, the duration increases to 24 hours.

**Twirl Tail** <actions string="Single Action" />  The azarpal lashes and twirls their confounding tail, snapping and lashing it in all adjacent squares. Until the start of the azarpal's next turn, all non-azarpals treat the squares adjacent to the azarpal as [difficult terrain](/Rules.aspx?ID=453).

**Spore Matrix** ([aura](/Traits.aspx?ID=542), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647), [primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=676)) 60 feet. The speaker in spores is surrounded by a strong concentration of spores. The speaker can communicate telepathically to any creatures in the aura who have breathed in their spores. This communication always uses the listener's native language and can't be used with a creature that doesn't breathe.
**Sporesight** The speaker in spores can see through spores drifting in the air, ignoring cover. This is an imprecise sense and functions only in areas without strong wind currents. Sporesight doesn't function underwater. --- **AC** 32 **Fort** +23 **Ref** +20 **Will** +27 **HP** 250 **Immunities** [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=669) **Resistances** bludgeoning 15, piercing 15 **Weaknesses** [fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=604) 15, slashing 15 **Blight Walker** The speaker in spores recovers from the [paralyzed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=85), [slowed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=92), and [stunned](/Conditions.aspx?ID=93) conditions at the end of their turn. They're also immune to penalties to their Speeds and ignore [cover](/Rules.aspx?ID=459), [concealment](/Conditions.aspx?ID=62), [difficult terrain](/Rules.aspx?ID=453), and greater difficult terrain resulting from plants or fungi.
**Toxic Spores** ([disease](/Traits.aspx?ID=578), [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=669), [primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=676)) **Trigger** A creature critically hits the speaker or the speaker dies; **Effect** The blighted speaker in spores releases a burst of toxic spores. Any creature within 10 feet of the speaker in spores takes 3d6 poison damage (DC 31 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Fortitude save). Creatures that fail their saving throw are exposed to [Ayrzul's Blight](/Diseases.aspx?ID=41). --- **Speed** 40 feet; [_fly_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1534) **Melee** tendril +28 ([reach 10 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)), **Damage** 3d10+13 bludgeoning plus 1d6 [persistent poison](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29) **Primal Innate Spells** DC 33 - **Constant (5th)** [Environmental Endurance](/Spells.aspx?ID=1517), [Fly](/Spells.aspx?ID=1534) **Rituals** DC 33 - **4th** [Blight](/Rituals.aspx?ID=4) **Accelerate Decay** ([Primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=134), [Void](/Traits.aspx?ID=510)) The speaker in spores unleashes void energy that forces desiccation in a 30-foot emanation. Each living creature in the area takes 14d6 void damage (DC 33 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Fortitude save). Creatures afflicted by a disease take a –2 circumstance penalty to this save. Zibik sheds these growths during his cycle of death and rebirth, and they sometimes emerge as a fungal creature that's independent of but innately connected to the green man. Often mistaken for [air elementals](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=41) due to their hazy, almost-imperceptible forms, a boiling spring is a humanoid water elemental made of scalding steam and bubbling water. When summoned to the [Universe](/Planes.aspx?ID=1), a boiling spring raises the ambient temperature around them, making the surrounding climate humid and muggy. They seem to enjoy the discomfort they cause, though some regard it as merely a fun prank while others truly revel in the misery and look for ways to cause more. **[Recall Knowledge - Elemental](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=2), [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=10)): DC 31 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 29 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 26 [Boiling Spring](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2661) **Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 181 2.0 **Perception** +23; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=12), steam vision **Languages** [Thalassic](/Languages.aspx?ID=113) **Skills** [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) +26, [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15) +26 **Str** +7 **Dex** +7 **Con** +7 **Int** +2 **Wis** +4 **Cha** +2 **Steam Vision** The boiling spring ignores the [concealed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=4) condition from mist and steam. --- **AC** 34 **Fort** +23 **Ref** +26 **Will** +20 **HP** 255 **Immunities** bleed, [fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=72), [paralyzed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=28), [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=126), [sleep](/Traits.aspx?ID=145) **Weaknesses** [cold](/Traits.aspx?ID=27) 15 **Freeze and Shatter** If the boiling spring is destroyed with cold damage, their body freezes over and explodes, sending out a wave of frigid air and ice shards that deal 4d6 piercing damage plus 4d6 cold damage to creatures in a 20-foot emanation (DC 36 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save).
**Sweltering Heat** ([aura](/Traits.aspx?ID=206), [fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=72)) 25 feet. The boiling spring radiates heat, raising the air temperature around them. A creature that starts its turn in the emanation must succeed at a DC 33 Fortitude save or become [fatigued](/Conditions.aspx?ID=15) while it remains in the area; creatures immune to [environmental heat effects](/Rules.aspx?ID=642) or with any fire resistance are immune.
**Evaporate** **Trigger** An effect would deal fire damage to the boiling spring, even if they would ignore the damage; **Effect** The boiling spring evaporates into the air. Until the beginning of the boiling spring's next turn, they can't be attacked or targeted. They still occupy their space, and their auras still function as normal. --- **Speed** fly 30 feet, swim 80 feet **Melee** blistering fist +27 ([Fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=72)), **Damage** 3d8+13 fire **Ranged** heat wave +27 ([Fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=72), [range increment 50 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=248)), **Damage** 3d12 fire **Scalding Breath** ([Fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=72), [Primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=134)) The boiling spring breathes out a cloud of steam in a 30-foot cone that deals 14d6 fire damage to each creature in the area (DC 33 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save). The boiling spring can't use Scalding Breath again for 1d4 rounds.

<title level="1" pfs="Standard">[Brochmaw](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2632)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

With bodies of fired clay, brochmaws look like walking cylindrical ovens split across the middle by their titular maws, which rage with the fires of culinary perfection. Behind their maw burns a powerful internal oven, where the elemental creatures roast their prey.

 Brochmaws are driven solely by their voracious appetites, only leaving their lairs to acquire new meals. Early attempts to force brochmaws into service resulted in their would-be captors being reduced to nothing more than ash on a plate, accompanied by a written review of how they tasted. Now, brochmaws are employed all across the Planes, lured by the sweet promise of new, fresh meat.

 Though brochmaws have no use for money, they do trade gifts for services. The only thing they have to offer is cooked meat from their own mouths, which they deem extremely valuable. Surprisingly, all who have tried brochmaw meat claim it to be a savory roasted delight. Given that brochmaws offer nothing but cooked meat and desire nothing but raw meat, trading with them is a simple if slightly dangerous affair, often coming down to the quantity and rarity of the meat offered.

The most common and infamous of the cave worms gives its name to the entire family—a much-feared monster wandering the twisting tunnels of the Darklands that is capable of carving out entire cave systems. Tunnels bored by a cave worm don't always last long after these creature's passage, and areas where they nest are maddening mazes of passageways that lead nowhere, yet navigating the labyrinth to find the worm's central nest often yields amazing treasures left behind by the worm's prior victims. **[Recall Knowledge - Animal](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43)): DC 31 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 29 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 26 [Cave Worm](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2871) **Source** [Monster Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=221) pg. 54 1.1 **Perception** +20; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59), [tremorsense](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=82) ([imprecise](/Rules.aspx?ID=412)) 100 feet **Languages** **Skills** [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) +30 **Str** +9 **Dex** -1 **Con** +7 **Int** -5 **Wis** -1 **Cha** -1 --- **AC** 32 **Fort** +28 **Ref** +21 **Will** +21 **HP** 270 **Inexorable** The cave worm recovers from the [paralyzed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=85), [slowed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=92), and [stunned](/Conditions.aspx?ID=93) conditions at the end of its turn. It's also immune to penalties to its Speeds and the [immobilized](/Conditions.aspx?ID=81) condition, and it ignores [difficult terrain](/Rules.aspx?ID=453) and greater difficult terrain.
**Slough Skin** **Frequency** once per day; **Trigger** The cave worm would be affected by a condition or adverse effect (such as [_cursed metamorphosis_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1479)); **Effect** The cave worm negates the triggering condition or effect by sloughing an outer layer of its skin. Effects from [artifacts](/Traits.aspx?ID=537), deities, or a similarly powerful source can't be avoided in this way. --- **Speed** 40 feet, burrow 40 feet, swim 20 feet **Melee** jaws +28 ([deadly 2d10](/Traits.aspx?ID=174), [reach 15 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)), **Damage** 3d10+15 piercing plus [Improved Grab](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=66) **Melee** stinger +28 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [Poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=126), [reach 15 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)), **Damage** 2d12+15 piercing plus cave worm venom **Melee** body +26 ([reach 15 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)), **Damage** 1d10+13 bludgeoning **Ranged** regurgitate +26 ([Brutal](/Traits.aspx?ID=249), [range increment 60 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=248)), **Damage** varies (see ability) **Cave Worm Venom** ([Poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=126)) **Saving Throw** DC 32 Fortitude; **Maximum Duration** 6 rounds; **Stage 1** 5d6 poison damage and [enfeebled 2](/Conditions.aspx?ID=71) (1 round); **Stage 2** 6d6 poison damage, and enfeebled 2 (1 round); **Stage 3** 8d6 poison damage and enfeebled 2 (1 round) **Fast Swallow** **Trigger** The cave worm [Grabs](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=45) a creature; **Effect** The worm uses Swallow Whole. **Regurgitate** The cave worm can violently regurgitate a creature or boulder it has swallowed to make a ranged Strike. The Strike deals bludgeoning damage depending on the size of the projectile: Tiny deals 2d6+13, Small 3d6+13, Medium 4d6+13, Large 5d6+13, and Huge 6d6+13. A regurgitated creature takes [falling damage](/Rules.aspx?ID=402) from the height of the target or from 20 feet, whichever is greater. Boulders occupy space in the worm's stomach as a creature of equivalent size, and cave worms often have several boulders swallowed. A cave worm can use a single action to swallow a new boulder. **Rock Tunneler** A cave worm can burrow through solid stone at a Speed of 20 feet. It can leave a tunnel if it desires, and it usually does. **[Swallow Whole](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=77)** ([Attack](/Traits.aspx?ID=15)) Huge, 3d6+9 bludgeoning, Rupture 24 **Thrash** The worm attempts one Strike against each creature in its reach. It can Strike up to once with its jaws, up to once with its stinger, and any number of times with its body. Each attack counts toward the worm's multiple attack penalty, but the multiple attack penalty doesn't increase until after it makes all the attacks.

Degholaus form from wretched souls who betrayed their societies to evil ends or for personal gain. These fiends resemble bloated, bestial humanoids with eyeless mole-like faces. They have five tails, all of which feature blood-red eyes. **[Recall Knowledge - Fiend](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46)): DC 33 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 31 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 28 [Degholau](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3776) **Source** [Pathfinder #210: Whispers in the Dirt](/Sources.aspx?ID=253) pg. 82 **Perception** +22; [greater darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59) **Languages** [Chthonian](/Languages.aspx?ID=114), [Draconic](/Languages.aspx?ID=2), [Empyrean](/Languages.aspx?ID=115); [telepathy](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=79) 100 feet, [_truespeech_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1728) **Skills** [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38) +27, [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=40) +25, [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46) +22, [Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=47) +22, [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=48) +26 **Str** +2 **Dex** +7 **Con** +6 **Int** +3 **Wis** +3 **Cha** +8 --- **AC** 33 [all-around vision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=49) **Fort** +23 **Ref** +26 **Will** +20 +1 status to saves vs. [magic](/Traits.aspx?ID=644) **HP** 290 **Weaknesses** [cold iron](/Equipment.aspx?ID=379) 10, [holy](/Traits.aspx?ID=517) 10 **Exposure Vulnerability** The first time each round that a creature critically succeeds at a save against a degholau's Veil of Lies or that a creature confronts the fiend on a falsehood immediately after the demon fails to Lie, the degholau takes 3d6 mental damage and becomes [frightened 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=76).
**Veil of Lies** ([aura](/Traits.aspx?ID=542), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647), [olfactory](/Traits.aspx?ID=664)) 15 feet. A degholau exudes a faint scent of rotting wildflowers in its aura—an odor that dulls the mind. A creature that ends its turn in the aura must attempt a DC 30 Will save.
**Critical Success** The creature is unaffected and is temporarily immune to Veil of Lies for 1 minute.
**Success** The creature is unaffected.
**Failure** The creature is [stupefied 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=94) while it remains in the aura and for 10 minutes after leaving the aura.
**Critical Failure** As failure, except stupefied 2. --- **Speed** 35 feet, burrow 15 feet **Melee** claw +26 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [Finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=179), [Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103), [Unholy](/Traits.aspx?ID=521)), **Damage** 3d12+8 slashing **Melee** tail +26 ([Finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=179), [Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103), [reach 10 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192), [Unholy](/Traits.aspx?ID=521)), **Damage** 3d6+8 bludgeoning plus 2d6 mental and conspiratorial thoughts **Ranged** spit +26 ([Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103), [range increment 30 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=248), [Unholy](/Traits.aspx?ID=521)), **Damage** 3d8+6 mental plus twisted loyalties **Divine Innate Spells** DC 33 - **4th** [Honeyed Words](/Spells.aspx?ID=1558), [Translocate](/Spells.aspx?ID=1724) (at will) - **5th** [Shadow Blast](/Spells.aspx?ID=273), [Subconscious Suggestion](/Spells.aspx?ID=314), [Translocate](/Spells.aspx?ID=1724) - **6th** [Dominate](/Spells.aspx?ID=87), [Rewrite Memory](/Spells.aspx?ID=1655) - **Constant (6th)** [Truespeech](/Spells.aspx?ID=1728) **Rituals** DC 33 - **1st** [Demonic Pact](/Rituals.aspx?ID=142) **Conspiratorial Thoughts** ([Divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=48), [Mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=106), [Poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=126)) **Saving Throw** DC 33 Will; **Maximum Duration** 6 rounds; **Stage 1** [slowed 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=92) (1 round); **Stage 2** slowed 2 (1 round); **Stage 3** [controlled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=64) by the degholau (1 round) **Twisted Loyalties** ([Curse](/Traits.aspx?ID=38)) **Saving Throw** DC 33 Will; **Onset** 1 day; **Stage 1** +1 status bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls, must succeed at a DC 10 flat check to use the [Aid](/Actions.aspx?ID=2292) reaction (3 days); **Stage 2** as stage 1, and +1 status bonus to skill checks, plus must succeed at a DC 10 flat check to heal an ally (1 week); **Stage 3** as stage 2, plus lose [sanctification](/Traits.aspx?ID=519) traits (1 week); **Stage 4** anathemas are now edicts, and former edicts are now anathemas—acting upon these new edicts causes loss of abilities and sanctification granted by classes and deities who consider them anathema (1 week)

An outcrop of dense stone that spends ages eroding can gain sapience and slowly awaken with the wisdom of nature. Such elemental beings are slow to action and difficult to anger, spurred only by immediate threats. **[Recall Knowledge - Elemental](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=2), [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=10)): DC 31 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 29 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 26 [Elder Outcrop](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2626) **Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 105 2.0 **Perception** +26; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=12), [tremorsense](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=40) 120 feet **Languages** [Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1), [Fey](/Languages.aspx?ID=119), [Petran](/Languages.aspx?ID=109) **Skills** [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) +29, [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=6) +25, [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=10) +26, [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=16) +26 **Str** +8 **Dex** -2 **Con** +8 **Int** +1 **Wis** +5 **Cha** +4 --- **AC** 33 **Fort** +29 **Ref** +19 **Will** +26 **HP** 295 **Immunities** bleed, [paralyzed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=28), [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=126), [sleep](/Traits.aspx?ID=145) **Dust Eternal** ([aura](/Traits.aspx?ID=206), [earth](/Traits.aspx?ID=55)) 30 feet. Dust swirls about the outcrop, rendering everything within its aura (including the outcrop) [concealed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=4). In addition, the dust at the outcrop's base creates [difficult terrain](/Rules.aspx?ID=453) on the ground within the aura. The outcrop can activate or deactivate this aura using a single action, which has the [concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32) trait.
**Unstoppable** The elder outcrop's [slowed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=35) condition can't exceed slowed 1, and it ignores penalties to its Speeds and the [immobilized](/Conditions.aspx?ID=24) condition. --- **Speed** 30 feet, burrow 30 feet; earth glide **Melee** column +27 ([reach 15 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)), **Damage** 3d10+14 bludgeoning plus [Knockdown](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=20) **Ranged** rock +27 ([Brutal](/Traits.aspx?ID=249), [range increment 120 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=248)), **Damage** 3d6+14 bludgeoning plus call of earth **Call of Earth** ([Primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=134)) A flying creature hit by the elder outcrop's rock ranged strike is affected by a 7th-rank [_earthbind_](/Spells.aspx?ID=94) spell (DC 33). **Earth Glide** The elder outcrop can [Burrow](/Actions.aspx?ID=93) through any earthen matter, including rock. When it does so, the elder outcrop moves at its full burrow Speed, leaving no tunnels or signs of its passing. **Natural Formation** ([Concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32)) Until the next time it acts, the elder outcrop appears to be a natural terrain feature. It has an automatic result of 47 on [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5) checks and DCs to pass as a natural outcropping of rock. The outcrop's dust eternal aura is deactivated while Natural Formation is being used. **Stone Grip** ([Earth](/Traits.aspx?ID=55), [Incapacitation](/Traits.aspx?ID=93), [Primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=134)) Great fingers of stone arise to grasp up to two Medium or smaller creatures on the ground in the outcrop's aura. Each target must succeed at a DC 33 Reflex save or be [grabbed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=20) by the stone hand (or [restrained](/Conditions.aspx?ID=33) on a critical failure; [Escape](/Actions.aspx?ID=79) DC 33). A creature grabbed or restrained by a stone hand at the end of its turn becomes [slowed 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=35) or increases its existing slowed condition by 1. When a creature is unable to act due to the slowed condition from this effect, the creature is permanently [petrified](/Conditions.aspx?ID=30). **[Throw Rock](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=38)**

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

In the tangled web of lineages, rivalries, and shifting alliances that is an elven noble court, aristocratic families employ bodyguards loyal to them alone.

<column gap="tiny">

<title level="2" right="Creature 13">[Elven Court Guard](/NPCs.aspx?ID=3634)</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Medium" />
<trait label="Elf" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=588" />
<trait label="Humanoid" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=628" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [NPC Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=236) pg. 180

**Perception** +24; plus vigilance

**Languages**
[Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1), [Elven](/Languages.aspx?ID=4), [Fey](/Languages.aspx?ID=119); plus one regional language

**Skills**
[Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=34) +26, [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) +23, [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=40) +24, [Heraldry Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) +21, [Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=47) +19

<row gap="medium">
**Str** +4

**Dex** +5

**Con** +2

**Int** +2

**Wis** +3

**Cha** +1
</row>

**Vigilance** A court guard gains a +1 circumstance bonus on Perception checks to [Sense Motive](/Actions.aspx?ID=2302) and [Seek](/Actions.aspx?ID=2301) creatures, and if they succeed, they get a critical success instead.

**Items**
_+1 [resilient](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2786) [chain shirt](/Armor.aspx?ID=43)_, _+1 [striking](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2829) [low-grade cold iron](/Equipment.aspx?ID=375) [elven curve blade](/Weapons.aspx?ID=406)_, _+1 [striking](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2829) [composite longbow](/Weapons.aspx?ID=434)_

</column>

---

<column gap="tiny">

<row gap="medium">
**AC** 35 

**Fort** +20 

**Ref** +27 

**Will** +23 

+1 status vs. [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647) effects
</row>

<row gap="medium">
**HP** 225

</row>

**Interposition** <actions string="Reaction" /> **Trigger** An ally within 15 feet of the guard would take damage; **Effect** The guard Strides. This movement does not trigger reactions, and the guard must end the Stride in a space adjacent to the ally. The guard then switches places with the ally, taking all damage and associated effects instead of the ally.

</column>

---

<column gap="tiny">

**Speed** 30 feet

**Melee**
<actions string="Single Action" />
_elven curve blade_ +27 ([Finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=179), [Forceful](/Traits.aspx?ID=180), [Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103)),
**Damage** 2d8+12 slashing

**Melee**
<actions string="Single Action" />
fist +26 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [Finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=179), [Nonlethal](/Traits.aspx?ID=188), [Unarmed](/Traits.aspx?ID=199)),
**Damage** 1d4+12 bludgeoning

**Ranged**
<actions string="Single Action" />
_composite longbow_ +27 ([deadly d10](/Traits.aspx?ID=174), [Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103), [Propulsive](/Traits.aspx?ID=191), [volley 30 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=201)),
**Damage** 2d8+10 piercing

**Avenge the Fallen** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([Fortune](/Traits.aspx?ID=76)) **Frequency** once per round; **Requirements** The guard is within 30 feet of the creature they were guarding, and that creature is either [dying](/Conditions.aspx?ID=69) or died since the guard's last turn; **Effect** The guard Strikes the creature that damaged their ally. They roll the attack roll twice and use the higher result.

**Dancing Blade** <actions string="Two Actions" />  The guard makes a Strike against a creature, then Strides. This Stride doesn't trigger reactions. If the guard ends this Stride in a different space adjacent to the same creature, they make another Strike against it. If both Strikes succeed, the creature is [off-guard](/Conditions.aspx?ID=58) until the start of the guard's next turn. Each attack counts toward the guard's multiple attack penalty, but the penalty doesn't increase until they've made both attacks.

</column>

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

It takes a particular kind of personality to leave the creature comforts of academia in order to explore trap-ridden ancient tombs or observe man-eating monstrosities in their native habitats. Resembling twisted lumps of fused gravel with oddly angled crystal limbs, gritblights are shock troops commonly used by [Ayrzul](/Deities.aspx?ID=102) to spread terror and disease to his enemies. These creatures are the gruesome result of experiments on crystalline elementals who were once the allies or servants of Ayrzul's rival lord of elemental earth, [Sairazul](/Deities.aspx?ID=107). Their crystalline body parts appear cracked and deformed, only their single “eye” left intact. **[Recall Knowledge - Elemental](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35), [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43)): DC 36 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 34 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 31 [Gritblight](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3732) **Source** [Pathfinder #203 Shepherd of Decay](/Sources.aspx?ID=243) pg. 84 **Perception** +23; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59), blight sense ([precise](/Rules.aspx?ID=411)) 60 feet, [tremorsense](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=82) ([imprecise](/Rules.aspx?ID=412)) 120 feet, grit vision **Languages** [Petran](/Languages.aspx?ID=109) **Skills** [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=34) +21, [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) +27 **Str** +8 **Dex** +4 **Con** +5 **Int** +0 **Wis** +4 **Cha** +1 **Blight Sense** A gritblight can detect the location of nearby creatures afflicted with [Ayrzul's Blight](/Diseases.aspx?ID=41) as a precise sense at the listed range.
**Grit Vision** A gritblight's vision is unaffected by clouds of sand, dirt, grit, or other earth materials in air or water. --- **AC** 33 **Fort** +26 **Ref** +19 **Will** +23 +1 status vs. [earth](/Traits.aspx?ID=585) effects **HP** 235 **Immunities** bleed, [disease](/Traits.aspx?ID=578), [paralyzed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=85), [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=669), [sickened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=91), [sleep](/Traits.aspx?ID=696) **Resistances** [acid](/Traits.aspx?ID=524) 15, physical 15 **Blight Cloud** ([aura](/Traits.aspx?ID=542), [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=669), [radiation](/Traits.aspx?ID=421)) 30 feet. A gritblight continually sheds tiny fragments of radioactive earth in a cloud around it. This cloud conceals the gritblight as a light fog and sheds [dim light](/Rules.aspx?ID=408) in the area. Any creature that begins its turn in the aura takes 2d6 poison damage with a DC 30 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Fortitude save. A creature that fails its save is exposed to [Ayrzul's Blight](/Diseases.aspx?ID=41) and a creature that critically fails is additionally [sickened 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=91). --- **Speed** 30 feet, burrow 30 feet; earth glide **Melee** claw +27 ([reach 10 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)), **Damage** 3d6+14 slashing plus 2d6 acid **Ranged** caustic shard +23 ([range increment 60 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=248)), **Damage** 3d6+10 piercing plus 2d6 acid **[Ayrzul's Blight](/Diseases.aspx?ID=41)** ([Disease](/Traits.aspx?ID=46), [Earth](/Traits.aspx?ID=55), [Primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=134)) but DC 33. **Earth Glide** The gritblight can [Burrow](/Actions.aspx?ID=2310) through any earthen matter, including rock. When it does so, the gritblight moves at its full burrow Speed, leaving no tunnels or signs of its passing. **Labyrinthine Vision** ([Mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=106), [Primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=134)) The gritblight forces disorienting visions of Ayrzul's Blistering Labyrinth into the minds of nearby creatures. All creatures in a 60-foot cone take 7d12 mental damage with a DC 33 Will save. Creatures [blinded](/Conditions.aspx?ID=59) by a gritblight's Labyrinthine Vision see only endless earthen tunnels in every direction. The gritblight can't use this ability again for 1d4 rounds.
**Critical Success** The creature is unaffected.
**Success** The creature takes half damage.
**Failure** The creature takes full damage and is blinded for 1 minute.
**Critical Failure** The creature takes double damage and is blinded permanently. **[Trample](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=81)** Medium or smaller, claw, DC 33

**Urban Legend** A brainchild is sustained only by the reputation that precedes them. Mindless creatures are immune to a brainchild and can't perceive them. The brainchild's size, features, and items, as well as the appearance of their attacks, match what the foes perceiving them expect. If foes expect to see different things, the brainchild chooses which to manifest. If any creature that can perceive the brainchild believes the brainchild has one of the abilities below, the brainchild has that ability. If foes expect different particulars, such as one believing the brainchild is immune to fire and another believing they're immune to divinations, the brainchild chooses one to have. When a group of diabolists or worshippers of an archdevil come to an ignominious end, their souls can sometimes be caught between life and death, unable or unwilling to pass on to the afterlife due to the humiliation of their untimely deaths. When enough closely-associated worshippers whose souls aren't already claimed in existing contracts meet such a fate, the spiritual “weight” of this shame can cause them to merge into a conglomeration of infernally-infused spirits—a hellshadow. Hellshadows look like a bank of fire and smoke, yet the flames themselves are made of distorted bodies and faces. Although made of multiple souls, a hellshadow is a singular creature with one mind and typically one goal: to defeat as many enemies of their faith as they can in order to repay the shame of their humiliating deaths. **[Recall Knowledge - Fiend](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46)): DC 36 **[Recall Knowledge - Undead](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46)): DC 36 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 34 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 31 [Hellshadow](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3740) **Source** [Pathfinder #204: Stage Fright](/Sources.aspx?ID=245) pg. 86 **Perception** +24; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59) **Languages** [Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1), [Diabolic](/Languages.aspx?ID=117) **Skills** [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=34) +25, [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=40) +27, [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=48) +25 **Str** -5 **Dex** +6 **Con** +5 **Int** +4 **Wis** +5 **Cha** +8 --- **AC** 33 **Fort** +23 **Ref** +25 **Will** +22 **HP** 175 ([void healing](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=83)) **Immunities** [death](/Traits.aspx?ID=571) effects, [disease](/Traits.aspx?ID=578), [fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=604), [paralyzed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=85), [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=669), precision, [unconscious](/Conditions.aspx?ID=95) **Resistances** all 10 (except [force](/Traits.aspx?ID=610), [ghost touch](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2840), or [vitality](/Traits.aspx?ID=509); double resistance against non-[magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=644)) **Weaknesses** [holy](/Traits.aspx?ID=517) 10 **Brimstone Cloak** ([aura](/Traits.aspx?ID=542), [divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=579), [fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=604), [sanctified](/Traits.aspx?ID=519)) 10 feet. The hellshadow constantly exudes a cloud of smoke that scorches flesh but leaves other materials unharmed. Living creatures who start their turn in this aura take 2d6 fire damage (DC 30 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex). On a critical failure, the creature is also [sickened 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=91). --- **Speed** fly 40 feet **Melee** brimstone tendrils +27 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [Finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=179), [Fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=72), [reach 15 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192), [Sanctified](/Traits.aspx?ID=519)), **Damage** 3d8+6 fire plus 2d6 void and clinging smoke **Divine Innate Spells** DC 33, attack +25 - **Cantrips (7th)** [Divine Lance](/Spells.aspx?ID=84), [Void Warp](/Spells.aspx?ID=1745) - **6th** [Crisis of Faith](/Spells.aspx?ID=55), [Divine Immolation](/Spells.aspx?ID=1496) - **7th** [Divine Decree](/Spells.aspx?ID=82), [Shadow Blast](/Spells.aspx?ID=273) (fire or spirit only) **Clinging Smoke** ([Divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=48)) A creature that takes damage from the hellshadow's brimstone tendrils Strike has coils of the creature's smoke solidify around their body, impeding movement. The creature must attempt a DC 33 Reflex save.
**Critical Success** The creature is unaffected.
**Success** The smoke solidifies as it coils around their limbs, imposing a –5-foot status penalty to all Speeds until the end of the creature's next turn.
**Failure** As success, except –10 feet to speed and the creature is also clumsy 1 until the end of their next turn.
**Critical Failure** As failure, except the creature is also slowed 1 until the end of their next turn.

description:
When a group of diabolists or worshippers of an archdevil come to an ignominious end, their souls can sometimes be caught between life and death, unable or unwilling to pass on to the afterlife due to the humiliation of their untimely deaths. When enough closely-associated worshippers whose souls aren't already claimed in existing contracts meet such a fate, the spiritual “weight” of this shame can cause them to merge into a conglomeration of infernally-infused spirits—a hellshadow.

 Hellshadows look like a bank of fire and smoke, yet the flames themselves are made of distorted bodies and faces. Although made of multiple souls, a hellshadow is a singular creature with one mind and typically one goal: to defeat as many enemies of their faith as they can in order to repay the shame of their humiliating deaths.

<title level="1" pfs="Standard">[Iron Warden](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3068)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

Traditionally crafted into the forms of giant suits of armor or powerful animals, iron wardens are products of exquisite artistry and skill. Their articulated joints and sturdy, armored bodies require great care and mathematical precision to craft, and regular cleaning and oiling ensure they don't rust over the ages. With proper care, iron wardens can remain in good shape for thousands of years, being passed down for generations, as long as they aren't destroyed by meddlesome adventurers. In addition to their incredible strength, iron wardens possess a potent toxic breath that is often more than enough to dispatch entire groups of opponents.

 Though their impressive stature prevents them from being inconspicuous, iron wardens are often placed in areas where they are easily mistaken for decorative objects. An iron warden might be hidden among decorative suits of armor or disguised as a statue in a city square. Occasionally, locals are shocked when something they assumed to be a historic landmark animates into an iron warden, called to action by an unknown mystic command. Stories tell of ancient civilizations, such as the Jistka Imperium, that created iron wardens of massive size. Most of these constructs have since been melted down for resources, but magicians and historians still chase down rumors of one of these lost colossi.

With proper care, iron wardens can remain in good shape for thousands of years, being passed down for generations, as long as they aren't destroyed by meddlesome adventurers. In addition to their incredible strength, iron wardens possess a potent toxic breath that is often more than enough to dispatch entire groups of opponents.

 Though their impressive stature prevents them from being inconspicuous, iron wardens are often placed in areas where they are easily mistaken for decorative objects. An iron warden might be hidden among decorative suits of armor or disguised as a statue in a city square. Occasionally, locals are shocked when something they assumed to be a historic landmark animates into an iron warden, called to action by an unknown mystic command. Stories tell of ancient civilizations, such as the Jistka Imperium, that created iron wardens of massive size. Most of these constructs have since been melted down for resources, but magicians and historians still chase down rumors of one of these lost colossi.
