The heavy suit of mechanical metal armor a juggernaut wears is custom-built and highly complex and specialized to its wearer. Other creatures can't make use of the armor unless they have similar skill and customize it thoroughly. **[Recall Knowledge - Humanoid](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=47)): DC 36 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 34 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 31 [Juggernaut](/NPCs.aspx?ID=3465) **Source** [NPC Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=236) pg. 49 **Perception** +21; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59) **Languages** [Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1) **Skills** [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) +27, [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=37) +26, [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=40) +26, [Engineering Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) +24 **Str** +8 **Dex** +3 **Con** +4 **Int** +2 **Wis** +2 **Cha** +2 **Integrated Weapon** A juggernaut's armor includes one integrated melee weapon, such as a diamond-tipped rotary saw blade, massive pneumatic drill, or heavy spiked gauntlet. The specifics don't change the damage dealt by its Strikes, but determines whether it deals bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing damage. A juggernaut with tools and a workshop can spend 2 hours to swap their armor's integrated weapon.
**Power Source** Juggernaut armor requires a power source built into the armor—such as a steam boiler, Stasian coil, or alchemical reservoir. This determines a damage type—cold, electricity, fire, or poison—for certain abilities. **Items** [Artisan's Toolkit](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2703) (blacksmithing), juggernaut armor, [Repair Toolkit](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2747) --- **AC** 33 **Fort** +25 **Ref** +19 **Will** +21 **HP** 250 **Resistances** galvanized plating **Galvanized Plating** The juggernaut has resistance 10 to the damage type of the armor's power source.
**Self-Destruct** **Trigger** The juggernaut is reduced to 0 Hit Points; **Effect** The juggernaut collapses and their armor emits a steady ticking sound. At the beginning of what would have been the juggernaut's next turn, the armor's power source explodes, destroying it completely and dealing 10d6 damage in a 30-foot emanation with a DC 33 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save. The explosion deals the damage type of the armor's power source. An adjacent creature can cancel the self-destruct sequence by succeeding at a DC 31 [Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=50) check to [Disable a Device](/Actions.aspx?ID=2411). --- **Speed** 20 feet **Melee** integrated weapon +27, **Damage** 3d8+12 and see integrated weapon **Melee** plated fist +27, **Damage** 3d4+14 bludgeoning **Energy Projector** ([Alchemical](/Traits.aspx?ID=6)) A juggernaut carries a powerful cannon-like projectile weapon that requires two hands to wield and deals 14d6 damage to all creatures in its area with a DC 31 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) save; the damage type, area, and save are based on the armor's power source, as listed below. Once activated, Energy Projector can't be used again for 1d4 rounds.
  • **Cold** 30-foot cone of cold (Reflex)
  • **Electricity** 60-foot line of electricity (Reflex)
  • **Fire** 30-foot cone of fire (Reflex)
  • **Poison** 30-foot cone of poison gas (Fortitude)
**Jump Jets** ([Alchemical](/Traits.aspx?ID=6)) The juggernaut gains a Fly speed of 15 feet until the end of their current turn. If the juggernaut isn't on solid ground when they lose their fly Speed, they fall. After the effect ends, the juggernaut can't use Jump Jets again for 1 round. **[Trample](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=81)** Medium or smaller, plated fist, DC 33

Living magmas can lie dormant for centuries below the earth before they awaken from their slumber in a fiery a volcanic eruption. This is especially dangerous when entire colonies of the molten elementals arise at the same time. **[Recall Knowledge - Elemental](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=2), [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=10)): DC 31 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 29 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 26 [Living Magma](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2635) **Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 129 2.0 **Perception** +22; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=12) **Languages** [Pyric](/Languages.aspx?ID=110) **Skills** [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) +27, [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=7) +23, [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15) +22 **Str** +8 **Dex** +5 **Con** +5 **Int** +4 **Wis** +5 **Cha** +4 --- **AC** 35 **Fort** +26 **Ref** +20 **Will** +22 **HP** 250 **Immunities** bleed, [fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=72), [paralyzed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=28), [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=126), [sleep](/Traits.aspx?ID=145) **Weaknesses** [cold](/Traits.aspx?ID=27) 15 **Molten Form** ([fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=72)) Any creature that hits the living magma with an [unarmed](/Traits.aspx?ID=199) Strike or otherwise touches it takes 10 fire damage. If a gallon or more of water touches the living magma, or if it's affected by a [water](/Traits.aspx?ID=165) effect, its outer layer of lava hardens to a rocky shell, deactivating its molten form and imposing weakness 15 to bludgeoning damage. Molten form reactivates if the living magma swims in lava for 1 minute.
**Volcanic Heat** ([aura](/Traits.aspx?ID=206), [fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=72)) 40 feet. Any creature that enters or starts its turn in the aura takes 15 fire damage (DC 33 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Fortitude save). A creature that fails its save is also [enfeebled 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=13) until it's no longer in the aura.
**Trap Weapon** ([fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=72)) **Frequency** once per round; **Trigger** A creature hits the living magma with a melee weapon; **Effect** The living magma attempts an [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) check against the triggering creature's Athletics DC. On a success, the living magma traps the weapon in its body and pulls it from the attacker's grasp. A creature can Interact to retrieve the weapon, but the attempt fails unless the creature succeeds at an Athletics check against the living magma's Fortitude DC (typically 36). If the living magma uses [Engulf](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=14), it also absorbs all trapped weapons, rendering them unreachable until it dies. --- **Speed** 40 feet, swim 60 feet (in lava only) **Melee** magma fist +27 ([reach 20 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)), **Damage** 3d8+11 bludgeoning plus 3d6 fire plus 2d4 [persistent fire](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29) **[Engulf](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=14)** DC 33, 2d10 bludgeoning plus 4d6 fire, [Escape](/Actions.aspx?ID=79) DC 33, Rupture 25 **Launch Lava** ([Fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=72)) The living magma hurls an exploding glob of lava up to 120 feet. Each creature in a 10-foot burst takes 7d6 fire damage (DC 33 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save). **Reignite** ([Fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=72)) **Requirements** The living magma is not in molten form; **Effect** The living magma returns to molten form.

With its mottled green-and-tan rubbery flesh, six short legs ending in two-clawed feet, and three circular mouths arrayed equidistantly around a disk-shaped head crowned by multiple bulbous eyes, the bizarre Darklands-dwelling ockomlire's strange appearance blurs the line between aberration and fungus. Ockomlires eat magic, and their specialized organs process and release that magic in the form of a mist that saps the willpower of those it touches. Originally created by [sekmin](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=468) occultists as a potent weapon against Azlanti wizards, since the serpentfolk empire's collapse thousands of years ago, ockomlires have spread upward through the Darklands. They often lair in sewers or abandoned basements in urban areas, drawn to society's use (and waste) of magical energy. Ockomlires are quite intelligent but tend to have bland personalities. They're fond of verbalizing their observations and experiences, speaking in unsettling piping voices through three mouths; they have a curious penchant for referring to themselves in the third person. They've little interest in having personal names and tend to refer to those they encounter by ancestry instead of name as well. **[Recall Knowledge - Aberration](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=44)): DC 36 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 34 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 31 [Ockomlire](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3741) **Source** [Pathfinder #204: Stage Fright](/Sources.aspx?ID=245) pg. 87 **Perception** +23; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59), [_detect magic_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1485) **Languages** [Aklo](/Languages.aspx?ID=13), [Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1), [Sakvroth](/Languages.aspx?ID=118) **Skills** [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) +27, [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=44) +24, [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=49) +23 **Str** +8 **Dex** +4 **Con** +5 **Int** +5 **Wis** +4 **Cha** +0 --- **AC** 33 **Fort** +26 **Ref** +21 **Will** +23 +1 status to all saves vs [emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=590) effects **HP** 235 **Resistances** [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647) 15 **Weaknesses** emotion vulnerability **Emotion Vulnerability** If an ockomlire fails a saving throw against an emotion effect, they loses their resistance to mental damage and gains an equal amount of weakness to mental damage (weakness to mental 15 for the typical ockomlire) until the end of their next turn. --- **Speed** 20 feet, climb 10 feet **Melee** jaws +27 ([Forceful](/Traits.aspx?ID=180)), **Damage** 3d10+14 piercing plus [Improved Grab](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=66) **Occult Innate Spells** DC 33 - **7th** [Calm](/Spells.aspx?ID=1458) (at will) - **Constant (7th)** [Detect Magic](/Spells.aspx?ID=66) **Devour Magic** ([Occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=120)) The ockomlire attempts to devour a spell effect from a creature they've [grabbed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=77). To successfully do so, they must [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) that effect with an [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=44) check. If the spell effect is an [emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=590) effect, the ockomlire gains a +2 circumstance bonus to this check.
**Critical Success** The spell is countered, the ockomlire gains temporary Hit Points equal to twice the spell's rank for 1 minute, and the grabbed creature becomes [stupefied 2](/Conditions.aspx?ID=94) for 1 minute.
**Success** As success but stupefied 1.
**Critical Failure** The attempt backfires, and the ockomlire becomes overwhelmed; their emotion vulnerability becomes active until the end of their turn. **Haze of Despair** ([Emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=60), [Mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=106), [Occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=120)) **Requirements** The ockomlire has temporary hit points gained from Devour Magic; **Effects** The ockomlire digests the magic and releases mist that stings the eyes and heart alike. The ockomlire loses any temporary Hit Points they have and all non-ockomlire creatures in a 30-foot emanation take 9d10 mental damage (DC 33 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Will save).

The shifting shapes of clouds in the sky have captivated the imaginations of mortal children for centuries. Pictures-in-clouds represent this pure possibility of air, transforming into anything the [Universe](/Planes.aspx?ID=1) imagines them to be. **[Recall Knowledge - Elemental](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=2), [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=10)): DC 31 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 29 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 26 [Picture-in-Cloud](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2619) **Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 83 2.0 **Perception** +20; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=12) **Languages** [Sussuran](/Languages.aspx?ID=111) **Skills** [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=1) +26, [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15) +24 **Str** +4 **Dex** +8 **Con** +5 **Int** +4 **Wis** +4 **Cha** +4 --- **AC** 35 **Fort** +21 **Ref** +26 **Will** +19 **HP** 175 **Immunities** bleed, [paralyzed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=28), [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=126), [sleep](/Traits.aspx?ID=145) **High Winds** ([air](/Traits.aspx?ID=5), [aura](/Traits.aspx?ID=206)) 60 feet. Air within the emanation is difficult terrain for [Flying](/Actions.aspx?ID=94) creatures that don't have the [air](/Traits.aspx?ID=5) trait.
**Disperse** **Trigger** The picture-in-clouds takes damage from a [hostile action](/Rules.aspx?ID=300); **Effect** The picture-inclouds disperses. Until the end of the current turn, they can't be attacked or targeted, they don't take up space, and any auras or emanations they have are suppressed. At the end of the turn, the picture-in-clouds re-forms in any sufficient space within 150 feet of where they dispersed; any auras or emanations they have are restored as long as the duration didn't run out while the elemental was dispersed. --- **Speed** fly 100 feet; swiftness **Melee** gust +26 ([Finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=179), [reach 20 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)), **Damage** 3d10+10 bludgeoning plus [Push](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=25) 15 feet **Ranged** lightning lash +26 ([range increment 100 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=248)), **Damage** 3d12 electricity **Cloudgaze** The picture-in-clouds shifts into their choice of an eagle shape, elephant shape, or sword shape. **Elephant Blast** **Requirements** The picture-in-clouds is in elephant shape; **Effect** The picture-in-clouds breathes out a 30-foot cone of air from their cloudy trunk. Creatures in the area must attempt a DC 30 Fortitude save to stand their ground. A creature [pushed](/Rules.aspx?ID=451) into a solid object stops moving and takes 4d10 bludgeoning damage.
**Critical Success** The creature is unaffected.
**Success** The creature is pushed 20 feet.
**Failure** The creature is pushed 40 feet.
**Critical Failure** The creature is pushed 40 feet and knocked [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=31). **Feather Storm** ([Move](/Traits.aspx?ID=114)) **Requirements** The picture-in-clouds is in eagle shape; **Effect** The picture-in-clouds [Flies](/Actions.aspx?ID=94) 125 feet, flapping their wings and creating a barrier along their path. This barrier has the effects of [_wall of wind_](/Spells.aspx?ID=367) (DC 30) and lasts until the end of the picture-in-clouds's next turn. **Slicing Wind** **Requirements** The picture-in-clouds is in sword shape; **Effect** The picture-in-clouds spins, forming a whirlwind that deals 5d8 slashing damage in a 15-foot emanation (DC 30 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save). **Swiftness** The picture-in-clouds's movement doesn't trigger reactions.

This big-headed beast is covered in glittering scales; its eyes are like large copper pots, and its mouth is full of sharp teeth. Despite its fish-like appearance, a quai dau to spends most of its time on land hunting along riversides or lakes. It uses its trunk to drain the nearby water before using it with deadly skill. A quai dau to can expel the water with a force strong enough to knock a knight off a horse, or gently enough to surround themself in a veil of mist. A quai dau to is extremely sensitive to sound. If they hear too much ruckus near their hunting grounds, they violently attack. Their silent movement allows them to sneak up on such distracted prey despite their massive size. Researchers have discovered, after much study, that quai dau tos don't have ears in the traditional sense. They have an organ in the upper part of their skulls that inflates to hold the water they use in their attacks. This organ is extremely sensitive to vibrations in the air and is used as a pseudo ear. **[Recall Knowledge - Beast](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35), [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43)): DC 31 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 29 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 26 [Quai Dau To](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3158) **Source** [Monster Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=221) pg. 284 1.1 **Perception** +25; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59), mist vision, [scent](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=74) ([imprecise](/Rules.aspx?ID=412)) 120 feet **Languages** **Skills** [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) +27, [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15) +25, [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=16) +24 **Str** +8 **Dex** +4 **Con** +8 **Int** -3 **Wis** +5 **Cha** -1 **Mist Vision** The quai dau to ignores the [concealed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=62) condition from mist and fog. --- **AC** 32 **Fort** +26 **Ref** +19 **Will** +21 **HP** 300 **Immunities** [blinded](/Conditions.aspx?ID=59), [dazzled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=65) **Weaknesses** [sonic](/Traits.aspx?ID=697) 15 **Frightful Sight** ([aura](/Traits.aspx?ID=542), [emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=590), [fear](/Traits.aspx?ID=598), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647), [visual](/Traits.aspx?ID=727)) 60 feet. This aura functions as a DC 32 [frightful presence](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=64) aura, but a creature doesn't attempt its save until it sees the quai dau to.
**Reflective Scales** **Trigger** A creature within 30 feet casts a spell with the [light](/Traits.aspx?ID=640) trait or uses an ability with the light trait; **Effect** The quai dau to adjusts its position to reflect the light off their scales in a blinding display. All creatures in a 30-foot emanation must succeed at a DC 33 Fortitude saving throw or become [blinded](/Conditions.aspx?ID=59) for 1 round. --- **Speed** 40 feet, swim 30 feet; Inflate **Melee** jaws +27 ([reach 10 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)), **Damage** 3d12+14 piercing **Melee** tail +27 ([reach 20 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)), **Damage** 3d8+14 bludgeoning **Melee** foot +27 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170)), **Damage** 3d8+14 bludgeoning **Drain Water** ([Manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104)) **Requirements** The quai dau to is within 10 feet of a body of water that's at least 10 feet deep and their water sac is empty; **Effect** The quai dau to sucks water through their trunk to fill their water sac, lowering the level in the body of water by 10 feet. All creatures in the water within a 30-foot emanation are [off-guard](/Conditions.aspx?ID=58) until the start of the quai dau to's next turn. **Inflate** The quai dau to inflates their body. They become Gargantuan, gain a fly Speed of 30 feet until the end of their next turn, and then [Fly](/Actions.aspx?ID=2312). They deflate if they fall [unconscious](/Conditions.aspx?ID=95) or Dismiss this effect. **Mist Breath** ([Primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=134), [Water](/Traits.aspx?ID=165)) **Requirements** The quai dau to's water sac is full; **Effect** The quai dau to empties their water sac to breathe out mist in a 10-foot emanation. All creatures within the mist become [concealed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=62), and all creatures outside the mist become concealed to creatures within it. The mist dissipates after 1 round. **Spout Water** ([Primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=134), [Water](/Traits.aspx?ID=165)) **Requirements** The quai dau to's water sac is full; **Effect** The quai dau to empties its water sac to blast water from its trunk, dealing 9d10 bludgeoning damage to all creatures in a 90-foot line, with a DC 33 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save. A creature that fails is [pushed](/Rules.aspx?ID=451) 10 feet (or 20 feet on a critical failure).

Despite its fish-like appearance, a quai dau to spends most of its time on land hunting along riversides or lakes. It uses its trunk to drain the nearby water before using it with deadly skill. A quai dau to can expel the water with a force strong enough to knock a knight off a horse, or gently enough to surround themself in a veil of mist. A quai dau to is extremely sensitive to sound. If they hear too much ruckus near their hunting grounds, they violently attack. Their silent movement allows them to sneak up on such distracted prey despite their massive size. Researchers have discovered, after much study, that quai dau tos don't have ears in the traditional sense. They have an organ in the upper part of their skulls that inflates to hold the water they use in their attacks. This organ is extremely sensitive to vibrations in the air and is used as a pseudo ear. All creatures in the water within a 30-foot emanation are off-guard until the start of the quai dau to's next turn. Inflate Single Action The quai dau to inflates their body. They become Gargantuan, gain a fly Speed of 30 feet until the end of their next turn, and then Fly. They deflate if they fall unconscious or Dismiss this effect. Mist Breath Single Action (Primal, Water) Requirements The quai dau to's water sac is full; Effect The quai dau to empties their water sac to breathe out mist in a 10-foot emanation. All creatures within the mist become concealed, and all creatures outside the mist become concealed to creatures within it. The mist dissipates after 1 round. A creature that fails is pushed 10 feet (or 20 feet on a critical failure). Impossible Flight Despite the laws of the natural world, this large headed creature can fly. Despite its fish-like appearance, a quai dau to spends most of its time on land hunting along riversides or lakes. It uses its trunk to drain the nearby water before using it with deadly skill. A quai dau to can expel the water with a force strong enough to knock a knight off a horse, or gently enough to surround themself in a veil of mist.

 A quai dau to is extremely sensitive to sound. If they hear too much ruckus near their hunting grounds, they violently attack. Their silent movement allows them to sneak up on such distracted prey despite their massive size. Researchers have discovered, after much study, that quai dau tos don't have ears in the traditional sense. They have an organ in the upper part of their skulls that inflates to hold the water they use in their attacks. This organ is extremely sensitive to vibrations in the air and is used as a pseudo ear.

The royal basilisk is aptly named, not for only the metal crown upon its head but also for the unique potency of its poison. The creature's poison manifests as a sort of cloying vapor that sticks onto and eats away at anything it touches. Their mastery of poison does appear to come at a cost, as the royal basilisk has no ability to petrify its prey. Although the royal basilisk can painstakingly shape a crown, some made of simple iron and others of rare skymetals, they much prefer to collect crowns crafted by other creatures. **[Recall Knowledge - Beast](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35), [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43)): DC 36 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 34 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 31 [Royal Basilisk](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3255) **Source** [Howl of the Wild](/Sources.aspx?ID=226) pg. 127 2.1 **Perception** +27; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59), [scent](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=74) ([imprecise](/Rules.aspx?ID=412)) 120 feet, [tremorsense](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=82) ([precise](/Rules.aspx?ID=411)) 60 feet **Languages** **Skills** [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=34) +24, [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) +27, [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=48) +24, [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=49) +25 **Str** +8 **Dex** +5 **Con** +7 **Int** -3 **Wis** +6 **Cha** +2 **Items** iron crown --- **AC** 33 **Fort** +26 **Ref** +22 **Will** +23 **HP** 290 **Immunities** [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=669) **Resistances** [acid](/Traits.aspx?ID=524) 15 **Crowned Royalty** The royal basilisk's crown is firmly attached to its head but can be [Disarmed](/Actions.aspx?ID=2383) as though it were a held item. Without a crown, the royal basilisk's mastery over poison is weakened enough that it loses its miasmatic shroud. The royal basilisk can equip a crown within its tail's reach as an Interact action. A royal basilisk's crown is normally made of iron and enables the basilisk to use miasmatic shroud, but crowns made of other, more exotic materials might confer different abilities.
**Miasmatic Shroud** ([aura](/Traits.aspx?ID=542), [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=669)) 15 feet. The poison in the breath of the royal basilisk makes the air around it a haze, [concealing](/Conditions.aspx?ID=62) it from all creatures outside the aura, but it cannot use this concealment to [Hide](/Actions.aspx?ID=2404) or [Sneak](/Actions.aspx?ID=2405). When a creature ends its turn within the aura, it is exposed to royal basilisk venom. --- **Speed** 30 feet, climb 30 feet, swim 30 feet **Melee** jaws +27 ([reach 10 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)), **Damage** 4d10+11 piercing plus Improved Grab and royal basilisk venom **Melee** tail +27 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [reach 15 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)), **Damage** 4d8+11 bludgeoning **Ranged** spit +24 ([Poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=126), [range 120 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=248)), **Damage** 5d10 poison plus royal basilisk venom **[Greater Constrict](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=65)** 4d8+3 bludgeoning, DC 32 **Royal Basilisk Venom** ([Poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=126)) **Saving Throw** DC 36; **Maximum Duration** 6 rounds; **Stage 1** 2d10 poison and [clumsy 2](/Conditions.aspx?ID=61) (1 round); **Stage 2** 3d10 poison and clumsy 3 (1 round); **Stage 3** 4d10 poison, clumsy 3, and [slowed 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=92) (1 round) **Stone-Hewing Spit** ([Acid](/Traits.aspx?ID=3)) The royal basilisk spits its poison with immense force, dealing 5d10 acid and 5d8 piercing damage (DC 32 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save) to creatures in a 240-foot line and exposing each creature that took damage to royal basilisk venom. The line penetrates barriers with Hardness of less than 20, ignoring any bonuses they'd provide from cover. The royal basilisk can't use Stone-Hewing Spit again for 1d4 rounds. **[Swallow Whole](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=77)** Large, 5d10 acid damage, Rupture 30 **Wrap in Coils** **Requirements** A Large or smaller creature is [grabbed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=77) or [restrained](/Conditions.aspx?ID=90) in the royal basilisk's jaws; **Effect** The royal basilisk moves the creature into its coils, freeing its jaws to make attacks, then uses [Greater Constrict](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=65) against the creature. The royal basilisk's coils can hold as many creatures as will fit in its space.

The briny depths of the Boundless Sea sometimes twist large groups of merfolk into swarms with vicious rows of teeth and sharp claws known as saltborn stalkers. Saltborn stalkers hunt in groups, using their drooping, tentacle-like appendages as bioluminescent lures, posing them as wisps or bubbles of planar energy to draw unsuspecting prey into clever ambushes. **[Recall Knowledge - Elemental](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=2), [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=10)): DC 31 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 29 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 26 [Saltborn Stalkers](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2666) **Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 186 2.0 **Perception** +24; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=12) **Languages** [Thalassic](/Languages.aspx?ID=113) **Skills** [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) +27, [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=7) +22, [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=10) +22, [Plane of Water Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8) +22, [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15) +26, [Warfare Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8) +22 **Str** +6 **Dex** +7 **Con** +5 **Int** +3 **Wis** +5 **Cha** +3 --- **AC** 34 **Fort** +22 **Ref** +26 **Will** +20 **HP** 240 (16 squares) **Immunities** bleed, [paralyzed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=28), [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=126), [sleep](/Traits.aspx?ID=145) **Weaknesses** area damage 10, [splash](/Traits.aspx?ID=150) damage 10 **Saline Crust** ([aura](/Traits.aspx?ID=206), [water](/Traits.aspx?ID=165)) 20 feet; **Requirements** The saltborn stalkers are in a body of water; **Effect** Layers of the saltborn's salty skin flake off to foul the water around them. A creature that ends its turn in the aura takes 2d6 acid damage with a DC 30 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save; creatures with the [amphibious](/Traits.aspx?ID=207) or [aquatic](/Traits.aspx?ID=168) trait are immune.
**[Troop Defenses](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=44)** --- **Speed** 10 feet, swim 60 feet; [troop movement](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=85) **Lightlure** ([Concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32), [Incapacitation](/Traits.aspx?ID=93), [Mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=106), [Primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=134), [Visual](/Traits.aspx?ID=163)) **Effect** The saltborn stalkers move their luminescent lures in an entrancing light show, drawing nearby creatures into their grasp. Each creature in a 100-foot emanation must attempt a DC 33 Will save; regardless of the result of its save, the creature is then temporarily immune to Lightlure for 24 hours.
**Success** The creature is unaffected.

<title level="1" pfs="Standard">[Shadow Giant](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3016)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

Shadow giants are natives of [the Netherworld](/Planes.aspx?ID=36), where they have dwelled in perpetual twilight for millennia. They live in familiar groups and uphold a nomadic way of life as they roam across ancestral lands between shadowy forests and misty chasms. These hunter-gatherers pass down lore through oral histories, conduct pilgrimages to unholy ziggurats of black stone, and bathe in the blood of their long-standing foes, including rival shadow giant clans and fiends of the Netherworld intent on enslaving their kind.

 Standing 15 feet tall, with gray skin and hair only a shade lighter, shadow giants are fearsome foes with a well-earned reputation as zealous warmongers and ruthless combatants. They rarely interact with outsiders, though they may treat with proven warriors who show the giants the respect and deference they feel they deserve.

**Pall of Shadow**  ([Divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=48), [Shadow](/Traits.aspx?ID=143)) When a shadow giant hits with a melee attack, the target must succeed at a DC 30 Fortitude save or become [drained 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=68) and take a –1 status penalty to Perception checks involving sight as long as they remain drained. On a critical failure, this condition doesn't heal naturally and can be removed only with magic.

Snow oni maintain their seething temperaments even in their icy homes. The isolation of their environment gives them trappings of asceticism, and many snow oni pursue physical perfection, reveling in the process of turning their bodies into powerful fighting machines. They are just as hedonistic and brutal as any of their brethren, however, and eager to indulge in warm baths, strong drink, and humanoid flesh. Like many oni, snow oni possess a third eye in the center of their forehead. This eye gives snow oni a mystical sense that allows them to peer through even the thickest flurries of snow. **[Recall Knowledge - Humanoid](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=47)): DC 31 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 29 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 26 [Snow Oni](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3122) **Source** [Monster Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=221) pg. 253 1.1 **Perception** +26; [greater darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59), snow vision **Languages** [Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1) **Skills** [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=1) +24, [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) +25, [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5) +27 **Str** +8 **Dex** +5 **Con** +5 **Int** +0 **Wis** +5 **Cha** +8 **Snow Vision** Snow doesn't impair the snow oni's vision; they ignore [concealment](/Conditions.aspx?ID=62) from snowfall. --- **AC** 33 **Fort** +23 **Ref** +25 **Will** +21 **HP** 290 **Immunities** [cold](/Traits.aspx?ID=555) **Weaknesses** bean panic, spirit 15 **Bean Panic** Oni are curiously afraid of beans, especially as the seasons begin to change. If a creature Interacts to throw a handful of beans at the oni, the oni becomes [frightened 2](/Conditions.aspx?ID=76). While frightened this way, their weakness to spirit damage is increased by 5. The oni then becomes immune to bean panic for 24 hours.
**Icy Deflection** **Trigger** The snow oni is targeted by a ranged Strike or spell attack roll that doesn't have the [fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=604) trait; **Effect** The snow oni creates a reflective blockade of ice, gaining a +4 circumstance bonus to AC against the triggering attack roll. If the attack misses, the snow oni redirects the attack to another creature within 20 feet of the snow oni. The attacker rerolls the attack roll against the new target.
**[Reactive Strike](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=48)** --- **Speed** 40 feet, fly 40 feet **Melee** fist +27 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103), [reach 10 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)), **Damage** 2d8+16 bludgeoning plus 2d6 cold **Melee** jaws +27 ([Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103), [reach 10 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)), **Damage** 2d6+16 piercing plus 1d6 [persistent bleed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29) **Ranged** ice dart +25 ([Cold](/Traits.aspx?ID=27), [Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103), [range increment 60 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=248)), **Damage** 3d10+4 cold plus 1d6 spirit **Primal Innate Spells** DC 31 - **2nd** [Invisibility](/Spells.aspx?ID=164) (at will; self only) **[Change Shape](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=55)** ([Concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32), [Polymorph](/Traits.aspx?ID=127), [Primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=134)) The snow oni can take on the appearance of any Medium or Large [humanoid](/Traits.aspx?ID=628) creature. This doesn't change their Speed or their attack and damage bonuses with their Strikes but might change the damage type their Strikes deal **Chilling Combo** ([Cold](/Traits.aspx?ID=27)) The snow oni makes two fist Strikes targeting the same creature. If they both hit, the target becomes [slowed 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=92) for 1 round. **Falling Frozen Lightning** ([Cold](/Traits.aspx?ID=27), [Primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=134)) The snow oni calls down a bolt of icy lightning, white as fallen snow. The bolt strikes a location within 60 feet, freezing the air into a cloud of snow that fills a 20-foot burst and lasts for 1 minute. All creatures within the snow become [concealed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=62), and all creatures outside the snow become concealed to creatures within it. A creature that enters the snow or begins its turn there takes 15 cold damage, with a DC 33 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Fortitude save.

The guillotine stands as the epitome of capital punishment in Galt. Yet despite its heinous reputation, most citizens consider it a clean and efficient means of political execution—at least, compared to the other options. One such alternative is the practice of drawing and quartering, a method where each of the victim's four limbs is tied to a different [horse](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=431). The horses are then spurred to run in opposite directions, with agonizing and gruesome results for the condemned. The locus of pain and resentment from such a death has been known to reanimate into an unusual conglomerate monster. Never again quite whole, a torn quartet is simplistic in its desire to mete out violence, usually starting with those responsible for its death. A torn quartet appears as four floating pieces of a humanoid cadaver, tethered together with ropes of spectral energy that each sport a single limb. One section might include a head, but it's largely nonfunctional. When one section is separated from its fellows, it drops to the ground and thrashes until reunited. **[Recall Knowledge - Undead](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46)): DC 33 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 31 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 28 [Torn Quartet](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3819) **Source** [Shining Kingdoms](/Sources.aspx?ID=265) pg. 185 **Perception** +23; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59) **Languages** [Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1), [Necril](/Languages.aspx?ID=20); (can't speak any language) **Skills** [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=34) +27, [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) +27 **Str** +5 **Dex** +8 **Con** +2 **Int** -2 **Wis** +4 **Cha** +2 --- **AC** 33 **Fort** +20 **Ref** +26 **Will** +23 **HP** 240 ([void healing](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=83)) **Immunities** [bleed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=86), [death effects](/Rules.aspx?ID=2331), [disease](/Traits.aspx?ID=578), [paralyzed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=85), [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=669), [unconscious](/Conditions.aspx?ID=95) **Weaknesses** slashing 10 **Bound Limbs** A torn quartet ordinarily has four severed limbs tethered to a central point by near-incorporeal ropes. A limb is essentially cut away from the central point and rendered nonfunctional each time the torn quartet loses 60 Hit Points (so at 180 Hit Points, the torn quartet has three functional limbs, at 120 Hit Points, it has two functional limbs, and so on. Each functioning limb can [Grapple](/Actions.aspx?ID=2376) separate creatures within reach, or multiple functioning limbs can Grapple the same creature) for each additional limb used to Grapple a creature, the [Escape](/Actions.aspx?ID=2296) DC increases by 2.
**Replacement Parts** A torn quartet can spend 1 minute tearing apart the corpse of a humanoid creature that was killed within the last hour to regain 60 Hit Points and restore one of its nonfunctioning limbs. A torn quartet can't have more than four limbs.
**Split Reactions** A torn quartet has a number of reactions per round equal to its number of still-functioning limbs, which it can use only to make Reactive Strikes. It can't use more than 1 reaction on the same triggering action, even if a creature leaves several squares within its reach, and the torn quartet must use a different limb for each Reactive Strike it makes. Whenever one of the torn quartet's limbs is rendered nonfunctional, the torn quartet loses one of its reactions.
**Reactive Strike** See Split Reactions. --- **Speed** 10 feet, fly 30 feet **Melee** limb +25 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103), [reach 15 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)), **Damage** 3d8+13 bludgeoning plus [Improved Grab](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=66) **Flurry of Limbs** The torn quartet makes a number of limb Strikes up to its number of functioning limbs, each against a different target. These attacks count toward the torn quartet's multiple attack penalty, but the multiple attack penalty doesn't increase until after the torn quartet makes all its attacks. **Tear Asunder** **Requirements** The torn quartet has a creature [grappled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=77) or [restrained](/Conditions.aspx?ID=90) by at least two limbs; **Effect** The creature takes 5d6 slashing damage for each limb currently grabbing or restraining it (maximum 15d6), with a DC 30 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=2297) Fortitude save. On a critical failure, the creature also loses a random body part, and one of the torn quartet's limbs is now no longer grabbing or restraining it.

text: Tree Singer Singers can speak the words of creation in song, a forgotten art from the First World. Their melodies turn grass into blades and make trees stir. Through their music, plants rise to defend and seek vengeance for nature. Taught by woodland spirits or fey agents of the First World, they master the magic of primal song. The lantern carried by the twins of rowan contains pure elemental life energy that resonates with and empowers all wood elementals. While within the emanation, a creature with the [elemental](/Traits.aspx?ID=57) trait and either the [plant](/Traits.aspx?ID=125) trait or [wood](/Traits.aspx?ID=508) trait gains [fast healing 10](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=15) and a +2 circumstance bonus to all attack and damage rolls. The most powerful zuhras draw followers and elemental metal with overwhelming force of personality and literal magnetism. When called upon to conduct _wish_ rituals, they use their long isolation from the other planes as an excuse to misinterpret requests outlandishly, claiming linguistic differences. **[Recall Knowledge - Elemental](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=2), [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=10)): DC 36 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 34 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 31 [Zuhra Shuyookh](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2656) **Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 161 2.0 **Perception** +23; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=12) **Languages** [Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1), [Talican](/Languages.aspx?ID=112); [_truespeech_](/Spells.aspx?ID=340) **Skills** [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=1) +27, [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) +24, [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=4) +26, [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5) +26, [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=7) +24, [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=12) +28, [Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=14) +22 **Str** +5 **Dex** +6 **Con** +8 **Int** +5 **Wis** +4 **Cha** +7 **Items** _+2 [striking](/Equipment.aspx?ID=280) [spiked chain](/Weapons.aspx?ID=60)_ --- **AC** 34 **Fort** +29 **Ref** +23 **Will** +21 **HP** 212 **Resistances** [electricity](/Traits.aspx?ID=56) 10 **Conductive Redirection** ([arcane](/Traits.aspx?ID=11), [concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32), [electricity](/Traits.aspx?ID=56)) **Trigger** The zuhra is hit by an attack, spell, or effect that deals electricity damage; **Effect** The zuhra conducts the electricity through their body, taking damage as normal, and redirecting a bolt at one target within 30 feet that they can see. The zuhra makes a ranged attack roll with a +27 modifier against the target's AC. On a hit or critical hit, the target takes electricity damage equal to the full damage of the triggering effect.
**Magnetic Field** ([arcane](/Traits.aspx?ID=11), [aura](/Traits.aspx?ID=206), [metal](/Traits.aspx?ID=505)) 10 feet. All squares in the aura are [difficult terrain](/Rules.aspx?ID=453) for creatures wearing metal armor or made of metal. Strikes with metallic weapons made by or against creatures in this aura take a –2 status penalty to the attack roll. Zuhras ignore these effects. --- **Speed** 30 feet, fly 35 feet **Melee** _spiked chain_ +27 ([Disarm](/Traits.aspx?ID=175), [Finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=179), [Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103), [reach 15 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192), [Trip](/Traits.aspx?ID=196)), **Damage** 2d8+11 slashing plus 1d12 electricity **Melee** hand blade +25 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [Finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=179), [Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103), [reach 15 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)), **Damage** 2d4+11 slashing plus 4d4 [persistent bleed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29) **Arcane Innate Spells** DC 32, attack +24 - **Cantrips (7th)** [Detect Magic](/Spells.aspx?ID=66) - **5th** [Invisibility](/Spells.aspx?ID=164) (×2), [Magnetic Acceleration](/Spells.aspx?ID=943) (at will), [Magnetic Attraction](/Spells.aspx?ID=944) (at will) - **6th** [Mercurial Stride](/Spells.aspx?ID=1374), [Wall of Metal](/Spells.aspx?ID=1379) - **7th** [Clad in Metal](/Spells.aspx?ID=1366) (can choose uncommon and rare metals), [Enthrall](/Spells.aspx?ID=104), [Plane Shift](/Spells.aspx?ID=222) (at will; to [Astral Plane](/Planes.aspx?ID=8), Elemental Planes, or the [Universe](/Planes.aspx?ID=1) only), [Weapon Storm](/Spells.aspx?ID=373) - **Constant (5th)** [Tongues](/Spells.aspx?ID=340) **[Change Shape](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=8)** ([Arcane](/Traits.aspx?ID=11), [Concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32), [Polymorph](/Traits.aspx?ID=127)) The zuhra transforms into a Small or Medium metal elemental or animal. This doesn't affect the zuhra's statistics, but it could change the damage type of their Strikes. **Magnetic Reposition** ([Arcane](/Traits.aspx?ID=11)) **Frequency** once per round; **Effect** The shuyookh targets any number of creatures affected by their magnetic field, and [moves](/Rules.aspx?ID=451) each target 10 feet in a direction the zuhra chooses. Each target can resist being moved if it succeeds at a DC 32 Fortitude save. **Magnetic Storm** ([Arcane](/Traits.aspx?ID=11)) **Requirements** The shuyookh's magnetic field is active; **Effect** The shuyookh electromagnetically flings razor-sharp metal scraps. Each creature in a 30-foot emanation takes 8d6 slashing damage and 3d12 electricity damage, with a DC 32 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Fortitude save. The shuyookh's magnetic field is deactivated for 1d4 rounds. **Mercurial Wish** ([Downtime](/Traits.aspx?ID=49)) **Frequency** three times per year; **Effect** The shuyookh conducts a _wish_ ritual for the benefit of a mortal, requiring no cost or secondary casters. The shuyookh's result is a success if they succeed at a DC 5 flat check or a failure if not. The shuyookh attempts to fulfill the wish in a way that creates an unstable or impermanent benefit.

The three major celestial planes—[Heaven](/Planes.aspx?ID=41), [Nirvana](/Planes.aspx?ID=44), and [Elysium](/Planes.aspx?ID=40)—each have their own respective dragons. Empyreal dragons have a direct connection to Heaven. Using the blessings of Heaven, empyreal dragons protect others and intercede against wickedness. Empyreal dragons are wise, considerate, and compassionate. When speaking with others, empyreal dragons are patient and understanding. **[Recall Knowledge - Dragon](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35)): DC 32 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 30 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 27 [Adult Empyreal Dragon](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2942) **Source** [Monster Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=221) pg. 115 1.1 **Perception** +27; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59), [lifesense](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=67) ([imprecise](/Rules.aspx?ID=412)) 30 feet, [scent](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=74) ([imprecise](/Rules.aspx?ID=412)) 60 feet **Languages** [Chthonian](/Languages.aspx?ID=114), [Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1), [Diabolic](/Languages.aspx?ID=117), [Draconic](/Languages.aspx?ID=2), [Empyrean](/Languages.aspx?ID=115); [_truespeech_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1728) **Skills** [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=1) +26, [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) +28, [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=6) +25, [Heaven Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8) +26, [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=7) +25, [Medicine](/Skills.aspx?ID=9) +28, [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=13) +28, [Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=14) +24 **Str** +8 **Dex** +4 **Con** +6 **Int** +4 **Wis** +7 **Cha** +5 --- **AC** 36 **Fort** +24 **Ref** +24 **Will** +26 +2 status to all saves vs. [divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=579) **HP** 250 **Immunities** [fear](/Traits.aspx?ID=598), [paralyzed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=85), [sleep](/Traits.aspx?ID=696) **Weaknesses** [unholy](/Traits.aspx?ID=521) 10 **Inspiring Presence** ([aura](/Traits.aspx?ID=542), [emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=590), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647)) 20 feet. The mere sight of an empyreal dragon motivates other creatures. Creatures within the aura gain a +1 status bonus to saving throws and skill checks. The empyreal dragon can't gain the benefit of their own aura or other actions that use the aura, and they can choose to exclude any creatures from any benefit of the aura or action that uses the aura.
**Divine Deflection** **Trigger** The dragon is critically hit by an attack; **Effect** Divine power intercedes, preventing some of the damage. The dragon gains resistance 10 to all damage against the triggering attack. --- **Speed** 70 feet, fly 180 feet **Melee** jaws +28 ([Holy](/Traits.aspx?ID=517), [reach 15 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)), **Damage** 3d10+11 piercing plus 1d8 spirit **Melee** claws +28 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [Holy](/Traits.aspx?ID=517), [reach 10 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)), **Damage** 3d8+11 slashing plus 1d8 spirit **Melee** tail +26 ([Holy](/Traits.aspx?ID=517), [reach 20 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)), **Damage** 3d10+11 bludgeoning plus 1d8 spirit **Melee** wing +26 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [Holy](/Traits.aspx?ID=517), [reach 15 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)), **Damage** 2d10+11 slashing plus 1d8 spirit **Divine Innate Spells** DC 34, attack +26 - **5th** [Holy Light](/Spells.aspx?ID=1557) (at will) - **7th** [Heal](/Spells.aspx?ID=148), [Interplanar Teleport](/Spells.aspx?ID=1576) (at will; self only) - **Constant (5th)** [Truespeech](/Spells.aspx?ID=1728) **Direct Halo** ([Concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32), [Divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=48), [Manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104)) The dragon tosses their halo to a square within 90 feet. While the halo is deployed in this way, the dragon loses their inspiring presence aura, and the aura instead emanates from the halo with the same emanation radius. The dragon can Sustain to recall the halo from any distance. The halo is made of pure light—it doesn't occupy space and can't be targeted or destroyed in any way. **Draconic Frenzy** The dragon makes two claw Strikes and one wing Strike in any order. **Draconic Momentum** The dragon recharges their Spirit Breath whenever they score a critical hit with a Strike. **Halo Pulse** ([Concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32), [Divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=48)) The dragon chooses one effect to impose on creatures in their inspiring presence aura. The dragon can't use Halo Pulse again for 1d4 rounds.
  • **Repulsion** Each creature must succeed at a DC 34 Fortitude save or be [pushed](/Rules.aspx?ID=451) until it's no longer in the aura.
  • **Restoration** ([healing](/Traits.aspx?ID=623), [vitality](/Traits.aspx?ID=509)) Each creature recovers 7d8 Hit Points.
**Spirit Breath** ([Divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=48), [Holy](/Traits.aspx?ID=517), [Spirit](/Traits.aspx?ID=149)) The dragon unleashes a blast of holy fire that deals 12d8 spirit damage in a 50-foot cone (DC 34 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save). The dragon can't use Spirit Breath again for 1d4 rounds.

Fortune dragons have the innate ability to draw upon the raw magical energies that surround them. They constantly use these magical energies to empower their magical abilities and even their bodies, as the energy can heal wounds. A fortune dragon has a typical build for an arcane dragon, but their bodies sport a striking feature: their treasure. The dragon's nature of drawing upon magic causes coins, gems, and, most notably, magical items to cling to their body like iron drawn to magnets. A dragon constantly pulls magical energies from the items attached to their body and makes use of these energies to cast spells. The magical energies that flow through a fortune dragon constantly flow through the dragon's items as well, and in many cases, the items melt from the heat produced in this process. Fortune dragons are seekers of novel experiences. The brutish and gluttonous augnagar live to feast—preferably on rotten flesh and, when possible, demon flesh. But to them, the greatest delicacy is the flesh of other augnagars. Augnagars have swollen, spiderlike legs with leathery membranes like a bat's wings, and three tails ending in hooked stings perfect for slicing flesh. An augnagar that gorges sufficiently, especially on other augnagars, can grow so massive it can't even move, thrashing and festering where it lies. It eventually flies into a frenzy of self-cannibalism as it rips apart its own flesh to feast on. <title level="1" pfs="Standard">[Brass Bastion](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2631)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

Brass bastions are formidable sentinels crafted from elemental fire and extraplanar brass. While they can be shaped into many forms, most depict muscular warriors with curving horns and stern or taunting expressions. Within each brass shell is a raging inferno—the source of its ceaseless heat. Though ifrits originally created brass bastions to act as servants and guards, the knowledge of how to craft them has spread throughout the [Plane of Fire](/Planes.aspx?ID=6). They can even be found on the [Plane of Earth](/Planes.aspx?ID=5) thanks to interplanar trade. In Medina Mudii'a, brass bastions walk the streets, tend shops, and stand guard. Bespoke brass bastions are passed down as family heirlooms or gifted to business partners and allies. Scions of the wealthiest ifrit lineages never travel without a train of brass bastions clad in family livery. Destroying a rival ifrit's brass bastion is a quick way to erode their political status, though anyone caught performing such sabotage faces swift retribution.

 Most brass bastions prominently display the sigil of their owner or maker, though magical methods can also determine who crafted a specific construct. Brass bastions forged by favored artisans are a status symbol in many ifrit communities. Ifrits consider a brass bastion crafted by a non-ifrit to be inherently inferior, barely worth the cost of its materials. Brass bastions obey magical programming imprinted at the time of their creation or follow commands from their owners. Most can't speak, but a few have magical voices and can parrot simple phrases, recite poetry, or tell bedtime stories at the crafter's fancy.

Bul-gaes are manifestations of the eclipsed sun and moon. They look like large canines, though their coloration and features change as they exercise their powers over heat and cold. Depending on whether they've most recently unleashed their lunar or solar powers, bul-gaes resemble either a crimson hound wreathed in flames or a cerulean, frostbitten fox, respectively. Legends say that the first bul-gae attempted to steal the sun from the sky. As they bit down on the burning sphere, though, the bul-gae was badly burned. Having failed, they then tried to retrieve the moon, but when they touched the moon, the bul-gae froze solid and fell to the ground. As hot-blooded as the lava that floods their homes, caldera oni have an incredible appetite for the thrill of war. While they engage in battle to conquer and control others, fire oni also love the thrill of combat, fighting for the sheer joy of it. Presenting a caldera oni with a true challenge can potentially earn their mercy and an offer to serve at their side. **[Recall Knowledge - Humanoid](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=47)): DC 32 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 30 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 27 [Caldera Oni](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3123) **Source** [Monster Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=221) pg. 254 1.1 **Perception** +26; [greater darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59) **Languages** [Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1) **Skills** [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=1) +23, [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) +27, [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=4) +25, [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5) +27, [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=7) +27 **Str** +8 **Dex** +6 **Con** +6 **Int** +0 **Wis** +6 **Cha** +8 **Items** _+2 [striking](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2829) [katana](/Weapons.aspx?ID=411)_, _+1 [resilient](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2786) [breastplate](/Armor.aspx?ID=47)_ --- **AC** 35 **Fort** +28 **Ref** +25 **Will** +23 **HP** 315 **Immunities** [fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=604) **Weaknesses** bean panic, [spirit](/Traits.aspx?ID=737) 15 **Bean Panic** Oni are curiously afraid of beans, especially as the seasons begin to change. If a creature Interacts to throw a handful of beans at the oni, the oni becomes [frightened 2](/Conditions.aspx?ID=76). While frightened this way, their weakness to spirit damage is increased by 5. The oni then becomes immune to bean panic for 24 hours.
**[Reactive Strike](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=48)**
**Stoke the Volcano** When the caldera oni is critically hit, the flames of anger grow within them. They recharge their choice of Ash Form or Dance of Burning War. --- **Speed** 40 feet, fly 40 feet **Melee** _katana_ +30 ([deadly d8](/Traits.aspx?ID=174), [Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103), [two-hand d10](/Traits.aspx?ID=198), [versatile P](/Traits.aspx?ID=200)), **Damage** 2d6+14 slashing plus 2d6 fire **Melee** jaws +28 ([Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103), [reach 10 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)), **Damage** 2d6+14 piercing plus 1d8 [persistent bleed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29) **Primal Innate Spells** DC 34 - **2nd** [Invisibility](/Spells.aspx?ID=164) (at will; self only) **[Change Shape](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=55)** ([Concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32), [Polymorph](/Traits.aspx?ID=127), [Primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=134)) The caldera oni can take on the appearance of any Medium or Large [humanoid](/Traits.aspx?ID=628) creature. This doesn't change their Speed or their attack and damage bonuses with their Strikes but might change the damage type their Strikes deal (typically to bludgeoning). **Ash Form** ([Polymorph](/Traits.aspx?ID=127), [Primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=134)) **Frequency** once per minute; **Effect** The caldera oni transforms into a cloud of sparking volcanic ash and then Flies. This movement doesn't trigger reactions, and the caldera oni can move through small gaps and spaces occupied by other creatures. The caldera oni then returns to its physical form, affected by a 4th-rank [_enlarge_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1514) spell with a duration of 1d4 rounds. **Dance of Burning War** **Frequency** once per minute; **Effect** The oni's heat becomes overwhelming, causing them to breathe out superheated ash and dance across the battlefield. The caldera oni Strides, then makes a melee Strike. If the Strike hits, the oni can Stride again and Strike again, repeating this until they have either missed with a Strike or made three Strikes total. The oni then finishes the dance by calling down volcanic lightning through the cloud of ash. Each creature hit by a Strike during the dance takes 3d6 fire damage and 3d6 electricity damage with a DC 34 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save.

<title level="1" pfs="">[Crowded Veil](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3787)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

Only one crowded veil exists, but it does so as separate entities in many different bodies. As each “individual” member shares a core extraplanar essence with the others, communication between them moves without regard to planar boundaries or the limitations of distance, allowing for swift transmission of information throughout Tanglebriar and beyond.

<column gap="tiny">
**[Recall Knowledge - Fiend](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**
([Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46)): DC 37

**[Recall Knowledge - Fungus](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**
([Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43)): DC 37

**[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 35

**[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 32
</column>

</column>

<column gap="medium">

</column>

</row>

<title level="2" right="Creature 14">[Crowded Veil](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3787)</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=683" />
<trait label="Medium" />
<trait label="Fiend" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=600" />
<trait label="Fungus" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=614" />
<trait label="Unholy" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=521" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #212: A Voice in the Blight](/Sources.aspx?ID=255) pg. 80

**Perception** +28; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59), [tremorsense](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=82) ([precise](/Rules.aspx?ID=411)) 120 feet

**Languages**
[Chthonian](/Languages.aspx?ID=114), [Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1), [Elven](/Languages.aspx?ID=4), [Fey](/Languages.aspx?ID=119); (cannot speak); spore telepathy

**Skills**
[Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) +26, [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43) +28, [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=44) +25

<row gap="medium">
**Str** +6

**Dex** +5

**Con** +5

**Int** +5

**Wis** +8

**Cha** +4
</row>

**Spore Telepathy** ([aura](/Traits.aspx?ID=542), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647)) 60 feet. A crowded veil communicates telepathically via spores. It can communicate telepathically with any creatures who are within its aura.

</column>

---

<column gap="tiny">

<row gap="medium">
**AC** 33 

**Fort** +25 

**Ref** +22 

**Will** +28 

</row>

<row gap="medium">
**HP** 300
(one mind)

</row>

**Immunities**
[blind](/Conditions.aspx?ID=59), [controlled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=64), [disease](/Traits.aspx?ID=578), [paralyzed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=85), [unconscious](/Conditions.aspx?ID=95)

**Resistances**
[mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647) 15

**Weaknesses**
[fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=604) 15, [holy](/Traits.aspx?ID=517) 15, slashing 15

**One Mind** A crowded veil is an individual creature that shares one mind with all other crowded veils. What one crowded veil experiences, all experience. If a crowded veil gains any conditions, all other crowded veils know this; they also know the direction to every other crowded veil and the distances between them. A crowded veil can communicate instantly and telepathically with any other crowded veil on the same planet. To crowded veils located on other planets, messages can take up to an hour or more to transmit. A message to a crowded veil on another plane takes 24 hours to transmit. A crowded veil is immune to [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647) effects that target only a specific number of creatures. If a mental effect targets all creatures in an area, only the crowded veils in that area are affected, although all other crowded veils sense all damage or conditions endured by those crowded veils.

</column>

---

<column gap="tiny">

**Speed** 20 feet; fly 30 feet

**Melee**
<actions string="Single Action" />
tentacle +28 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170)),
**Damage** 3d8+14 bludgeoning

**Ranged**
<actions string="Single Action" />
spore pod +28 ([Brutal](/Traits.aspx?ID=249), [Propulsive](/Traits.aspx?ID=191), [range 30 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=248)),
**Damage** 3d6+11 bludgeoning plus crowded veil spores

**Primal Innate Spells** DC 31
- **Constant (7th)**
[Truesight](/Spells.aspx?ID=1727)

**Crowded Veil Spores**  ([Poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=126)) **Saving Throw** DC 34; **Maximum Duration** 6 rounds; **Stage 1** [stupefied 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=94) (1 round); **Stage 2** 4d8 poison damage and stupefied 2 (1 round); **Stage 3** 4d8 poison damage and stupefied 3 (1 round); **Stage 4** 4d8 poison damage and [unconscious](/Conditions.aspx?ID=95) (1 round)

**Spore Trail** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([Manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104)) A crowded veil shudders, releasing toxic spores. Until the end of their turn, when the clouded veil moves, all spaces they leave are filled with spores. These spore trails persist until the start of the clouded veil's next turn, and can be dispersed immediately by wind in the area. The first time in a round when a creature enters this spore trail, that creature is exposed to crowded veil spores.

</column>

<title level="1" pfs="">[Curse Monger](/NPCs.aspx?ID=3544)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

Oracles who have been consumed by their visions and the divine gifts bestowed upon them turn to more sinister paths, becoming curse mongers. Seeking to rid themselves of the shadows that haunt them, curse mongers lash out and attempt to bind others to their fate.

Faydhaan shuyookhs are powerful faydhaans venerated as leaders, diplomats, and negotiators. As representatives of faydhaan-kind, they observe strict rules of etiquette and hospitality and hold the literary and performing arts in high esteem. A faydhaan shuyookh takes delight in greeting guests, and being greeted in return, to see how many different greetings they can demonstrate. Guests who creatively engage in this customary greeting game will impress a faydhaan shuyookh and receive magnificent hospitality. **[Recall Knowledge - Elemental](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=2), [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=10)): DC 37 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 35 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 32 [Faydhaan Shuyookh](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2662) **Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 182 2.0 **Perception** +23; (25 to [Sense Motive](/Actions.aspx?ID=85)) **Languages** [Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1), [Muan](/Languages.aspx?ID=108), [Petran](/Languages.aspx?ID=109), [Pyric](/Languages.aspx?ID=110), [Sussuran](/Languages.aspx?ID=111), [Talican](/Languages.aspx?ID=112), [Thalassic](/Languages.aspx?ID=113); [telepathy](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=37) 100 feet, [_truespeech_](/Spells.aspx?ID=340) **Skills** [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) +27, [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=4) +24, [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5) +26, [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=6) +28, [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=10) +25, [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=12) +28, [Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=14) +26, [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15) +27 **Str** +7 **Dex** +7 **Con** +5 **Int** +4 **Wis** +5 **Cha** +8 **Items** _+2 [striking](/Equipment.aspx?ID=280) jambiya_ (functions as a [dagger](/Weapons.aspx?ID=3)) --- **AC** 36 **Fort** +23 **Ref** +27 **Will** +25 **HP** 240 **Resistances** [fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=72) 15 **Aura of Hospitality** ([aura](/Traits.aspx?ID=206), [emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=60), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=106)) 60 feet. The faydhaan shuyookh dissuades those around them from hostility. Willing creatures in the emanation gain a +2 status bonus to [Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=14) and [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=6) checks. The shuyookh can suppress or resume the aura as a free action. If the shuyookh [acts hostile](/Rules.aspx?ID=300), the aura deactivates and can't be reactivated for 1 hour. When any other creature in the aura acts hostile, it must attempt a DC 35 Will save. On a success, it's unaffected and doesn't need to save again for 1 hour; on a failure, its current action is disrupted, as are any other hostile actions it attempts for 1 round.
**Turbulent Seas** ([aura](/Traits.aspx?ID=206), [water](/Traits.aspx?ID=165)) 60 feet. Water in the aura that is also in the same body of water as the faydhaan is [difficult terrain](/Rules.aspx?ID=453) for [Swimming](/Actions.aspx?ID=39) creatures. Creatures with the [water](/Traits.aspx?ID=165) trait are immune. --- **Speed** 25 feet, swim 60 feet **Melee** _jambiya_ +29 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [Finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=179), [Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103), [reach 10 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192), [versatile S](/Traits.aspx?ID=200)), **Damage** 2d4+13 piercing **Melee** fist +27 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103), [Nonlethal](/Traits.aspx?ID=188), [reach 10 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)), **Damage** 3d8+13 bludgeoning **Ranged** _jambiya_ +29 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103), [thrown 20 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=195), [versatile S](/Traits.aspx?ID=200)), **Damage** 2d4+13 piercing **Arcane Innate Spells** DC 34, attack +26 - **Cantrips (7th)** [Detect Magic](/Spells.aspx?ID=66) - **2nd** [Befitting Attire](/Spells.aspx?ID=867) (at will), [Create Water](/Spells.aspx?ID=53) (at will), [Invisibility](/Spells.aspx?ID=164) (at will), [See Invisibility](/Spells.aspx?ID=271), [Water Breathing](/Spells.aspx?ID=370) - **4th** [Hydraulic Push](/Spells.aspx?ID=154) (at will), [Invisibility](/Spells.aspx?ID=164) (×2), [Gaseous Form](/Spells.aspx?ID=129) - **5th** [Cone of Cold](/Spells.aspx?ID=47) (at will), [Control Water](/Spells.aspx?ID=51) (at will), [Hallucinatory Terrain](/Spells.aspx?ID=145), [Tongues](/Spells.aspx?ID=340) (at will) - **7th** [Hydraulic Torrent](/Spells.aspx?ID=155), [Planar Palace](/Spells.aspx?ID=1634), [Plane Shift](/Spells.aspx?ID=222) (at will; to [Astral Plane](/Planes.aspx?ID=8), Elemental Planes, or the [Universe](/Planes.aspx?ID=1) only), [Summon Elemental](/Spells.aspx?ID=320) - **Constant (7th)** [Tongues](/Spells.aspx?ID=340) **[Change Shape](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=8)** ([Arcane](/Traits.aspx?ID=11), [Concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32), [Polymorph](/Traits.aspx?ID=127)) The faydhaan transforms into a Small or Medium water elemental, aquatic animal, or humanoid. This doesn't affect the faydhaan's statistics, but it could change the damage type of their Strikes. **Diplomatic Wish** ([Downtime](/Traits.aspx?ID=49)) **Frequency** three times per year; **Effect** The shuyookh conducts a _wish_ ritual for the benefit of a mortal, requiring no cost or secondary casters. The shuyookh's result is a success if they succeed at a DC 5 flat check or a failure if not. The shuyookh interprets the wish to please the most people possible. **To the Hilt** The faydhaan shuyookh makes a melee jambiya Strike and buries the blade deep, dealing an extra 3d6 [persistent bleed damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29) on a hit (6d6 on a critical hit).

Stories of immense rocs swooping down to carry off livestock or strafing armies into bleeding ruin are popular in taverns, but what many don't realize is that there are even more dangerous magical rocs dwelling in the remote corners of the world. These oversized birds have supernatural abilities linked to the region they favor, but they share one thing with the common roc—their vast size. Frost rocs are owl-like predators adapted to life in arctic regions. They nest among the craggy peaks of snowcapped mountains or amid rifts of sprawling glaciers, treating the taigas and tundras as their sprawling hunting grounds. Frost rocs are nocturnal and tend to hunt nightly for a few weeks at a time, as the moon is waxing or waning full. They go into short periods of hibernation for the weeks on either side of a new moon, or during prolonged periods of cloud coverage, such as during a storm. They abandon these habits when they're trained to work as mounts or guardians—something that [giants](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=420) or the church of [Gorum](/Deities.aspx?ID=283) often does in the remote reaches of the Lands of the Linnorm Kings or the Realm of the Mammoth Lords. **[Recall Knowledge - Beast](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35), [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43)): DC 37 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 35 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 32 [Frost Roc](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3392) **Source** [Prey for Death](/Sources.aspx?ID=231) pg. 113 **Perception** +25; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59) **Languages** **Skills** [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=34) +24, [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) +29 **Str** +9 **Dex** +4 **Con** +6 **Int** -4 **Wis** +5 **Cha** +0 **Mist Sight** A frost roc can see through clouds, fog, mists, and other water vapors. --- **AC** 34 **Fort** +28 **Ref** +24 **Will** +23 **HP** 300 **Immunities** [cold](/Traits.aspx?ID=555) **Resistances** [electricity](/Traits.aspx?ID=586) 15 **Weaknesses** [fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=604) 15 **Wing Rebuff** **Trigger** A creature moves into the reach of the frost roc's wing; **Effect** The frost roc makes a wing Strike against the triggering creature. If the frost roc [Pushes](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=47) the creature, it disrupts the triggering [move](/Traits.aspx?ID=658) action. --- **Speed** 15 feet, fly 60 feet **Melee** beak +29 ([reach 15 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)), **Damage** 3d12+15 piercing **Melee** talon +29 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [reach 15 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)), **Damage** 3d8+15 slashing plus [Improved Grab](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=66) **Melee** wing +29 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [reach 30 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)), **Damage** 3d4+15 bludgeoning plus [Improved Push](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=66) 10 feet **Flying Strafe** The frost roc [Flies](/Actions.aspx?ID=2312) up to its Speed and makes two talon Strikes at any point during that movement. Each Strike must target a different creature. Each attack takes the normal multiple attack penalty. **Frozen Feathers** ([Cold](/Traits.aspx?ID=27), [Primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=134)) The frost roc spreads its wings and then flaps them furiously, unleashing a blast of ice-rimed feathers in a 60-foot cone. All creatures in the area must attempt a DC 34 Reflex save. The frost roc can't use Frozen Feathers again for 1d4 rounds.
**Critical Success** The creature is unaffected.
**Success** The creature takes 3d6 piercing damage and 5d6 cold damage.
**Failure** The creature takes 5d6 piercing damage and 10d6 cold damage.
**Critical Failure** The creature takes 8d6 piercing damage, 15d6 cold damage, and is [slowed 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=92) for 1 minute. **Snack** A frost roc gains a +2 circumstance bonus to hit with its beak Strike if the target is [grabbed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=77) or [restrained](/Conditions.aspx?ID=90) in its talon. **Snatch** A frost roc can [Fly](/Actions.aspx?ID=2312) at half Speed while it has a creature [grabbed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=77) or [restrained](/Conditions.aspx?ID=90) in either or both of its talons, carrying that creature along with it.

A mass of undulating tendrils and nerves, furnericos stalk sewer systems below large cities, reveling in the filth and rotting detritus created by those who dwell above the middens and sumps they call home. Fortunately for sanitation workers and other civil servants who ply their trade in sewer tunnels, furnericos are exceedingly rare and solitary. Their power is such that once one moves into a sewer system, it's often easier for urban planners to simply abandon that section to the monster and rebuild around it. A furnerico left to its domain like this is generally content to remain—as long as the filth keeps flowing. Furnericos are asexual, spawning a single offspring as they expire from natural causes. One that dies by violence does not perpetuate its kind, presenting a vexing question to sages: where do these creatures come from, and why haven't they gone extinct over the ages? **[Recall Knowledge - Aberration](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=44)): DC 37 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 35 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 32 [Furnerico](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3739) **Source** [Pathfinder #204: Stage Fright](/Sources.aspx?ID=245) pg. 85 **Perception** +24; [scent](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=74) ([precise](/Rules.aspx?ID=411)) 60 feet **Languages** **Skills** [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) +28, [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=48) +25 **Str** +8 **Dex** +5 **Con** +8 **Int** -4 **Wis** +4 **Cha** -3 --- **AC** 33 **Fort** +28 **Ref** +23 **Will** +24 **HP** 320 **Immunities** [acid](/Traits.aspx?ID=524), [disease](/Traits.aspx?ID=578) **Resistances** bludgeoning 15, piercing 15, [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=669) 15 **Weaknesses** slashing 15 **Fetid Aura** ([aura](/Traits.aspx?ID=542), [olfactory](/Traits.aspx?ID=664)) 80 feet. A creature entering or beginning its turn in a furnerico's fetid aura must succeed at a DC 31 Fortitude or be [sickened 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=91); the creature also becomes [enfeebled 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=71) until the end of their next turn. A creature that succeeds at its save is temporarily immune to all furnerico fetid auras for 1 minute.
**Hydrophobic** A furnerico avoids water and won't willingly approach within five feet of a body of water. It won't initiate an attack against any creature that's soaking wet with water or that has the [water](/Traits.aspx?ID=732) trait. A furnerico takes a –2 circumstance penalty to its attack rolls against such creatures who attack it.
**Susceptible to Water** A furnerico cleansed of filth becomes sluggish. If ever immersed fully in pure, clean water, or if it ever fails a saving throw against a [water](/Traits.aspx?ID=732) effect, the furnerico becomes [slowed 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=92) until it starts its turn in an area of filth or contaminated water. --- **Speed** 15 feet, climb 30 feet **Melee** pseudopod +28 ([reach 10 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)), **Damage** 3d12+14 bludgeoning **Ranged** acidic slime +25 ([range 60 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=248)), **Damage** 4d6 acid plus 3d6 [persistent acid](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29) **Feast on Illness** ([Occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=120)) **Requirements** The furnerico's last action was a successful pseudopod Strike against a creature with the [sickened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=91) condition; **Effect** The furnerico feeds off the sweet sickness of the creature, gaining 30 temporary hit points for 1 minute. **Sticky Slime** A creature that's critically hit by a furnerico's acidic slime becomes [immobilized](/Conditions.aspx?ID=81) until they [Escape](/Actions.aspx?ID=2296) (DC 34) or 1 minute passes, after which the slime dissolves.

text: Furnerico A mass of undulating tendrils and nerves, furnericos stalk sewer systems below large cities, reveling in the filth and rotting detritus created by those who dwell above the middens and sumps they call home. Fortunately for sanitation workers and other civil servants who ply their trade in sewer tunnels, furnericos are exceedingly rare and solitary. Their power is such that once one moves into a sewer system, it's often easier for urban planners to simply abandon that section to the monster and rebuild around it. A furnerico left to its domain like this is generally content to remain—as long as the filth keeps flowing. Furnericos are asexual, spawning a single offspring as they expire from natural causes. One that dies by violence does not perpetuate its kind, presenting a vexing question to sages: where do these creatures come from, and why haven't they gone extinct over the ages?
