Masque mannequins are a type of soulbound construct animated by a fragment of a once-living soul infused into an eerie, nearly featureless mask that's then affixed to a mannequin or dressmaker's dummy. Though similar in process to the creation of a soulbound doll or mannequin, creating a masque mannequin requires conducting ritualistic murder and extracting a soul shard during an unwilling victim's death, and only the vilest of crafters would consider attempting such a deed. Masque mannequins are popular among [Norgorberites](/Deities.aspx?ID=289), especially devotees of Father Skinsaw, as well as [Kuthites](/Deities.aspx?ID=296) who take pride in drawing out the ritual to gain the largest possible fragment of the soul. **[Recall Knowledge - Construct](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35), [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=37)): DC 36 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 34 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 31 [Masque Mannequin](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3745) **Source** [Pathfinder #205: Singer, Stalker, Skinsaw Man](/Sources.aspx?ID=246) pg. 87 **Perception** +26; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59) **Languages** one spoken in life (typically [Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=155); can't speak any language) **Skills** [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=34) +29, [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) +29, [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=48) +29 **Str** +8 **Dex** +6 **Con** +5 **Int** -2 **Wis** +3 **Cha** +0 **Soul Mask** The spark of the soul used to create a masque mannequin is infused into its mask. A creature can break a masque mannequin's soul mask with a DC 40 [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) check or steal it with a DC 40 [Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=50) check. If its mask is [broken](/Conditions.aspx?ID=60) or removed, a masque mannequin must attempt a DC 40 Fortitude save.
**Critical Success** The masque mannequin's animating spark shifts to infuse its body; it is unaffected and no longer has a soul mask.
**Success** The masque mannequin takes 2d6 [persistent mental damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29). If it regains its mask, it can place it back on its face as an Interact action to automatically stop this persistent mental damage.
**Failure** As success, but 4d6 persistent mental damage and [stunned 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=93).
**Critical Failure** As failure, but 8d6 persistent mental damage and stunned 3. --- **AC** 38 **Fort** +26 **Ref** +29 **Will** +24 **HP** 210 **Immunities** bleed, [death](/Traits.aspx?ID=571) effects, [disease](/Traits.aspx?ID=578), [doomed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=67), [drained](/Conditions.aspx?ID=68), [fatigued](/Conditions.aspx?ID=73), [healing](/Traits.aspx?ID=623), [nonlethal](/Traits.aspx?ID=661) attacks, [paralyzed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=85), [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=669), [sickened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=91), [unconscious](/Conditions.aspx?ID=95), [vitality](/Traits.aspx?ID=509), [void](/Traits.aspx?ID=510) **Resistances** bludgeoning 7, piercing 15, slashing 7 **Weaknesses** [fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=604) 15 **Awaken** **Requirements** The masque mannequin is in Pose; **Trigger** A creature unaware of the mannequin's true nature approaches within reach; **Effect** The mannequin makes a Strike against the triggering creature. --- **Speed** 30 feet, climb 30 feet **Melee** fist +29 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170)), **Damage** 3d8+16 bludgeoning plus [Improved Grab](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=66) **Occult Innate Spells** DC 33 - **Cantrips (7th)** [Daze](/Spells.aspx?ID=61) - **7th** [Spirit Blast](/Spells.aspx?ID=301) (×3) **Pose** ([Concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32)) Until the next time the masque mannequin acts, it appears to be an inanimate mannequin. It has an automatic result of 45 on [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38) checks and DCs to appear as an ordinary mannequin. **Refashion** ([Incapacitation](/Traits.aspx?ID=93), [Occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=120)) **Requirements** The masque mannequin is [grappling](/Conditions.aspx?ID=77) a living creature; **Effect** The grabbed creature must attempt a DC 36 Fortitude save.
**Critical Success** The creature is unaffected.
**Success** The creature is [slowed 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=92) for 1 round as its body grows more wooden.
**Failure** The creature is [petrified](/Conditions.aspx?ID=87) for the next 24 hours, but instead of turning to stone, it turns into a wooden mannequin. It can attempt a new save at the end of each of its turns.
**Critical Failure** The creature turns into a wooden mannequin permanently.

Mugrisants are manifestations of the [Outer Rifts'](/Planes.aspx?ID=45) capacity for destructive transformation. This qlippoth's cycle of never-ending transformation gives them an insatiable appetite. Fearsome centipede-like creatures, mukradis are three-headed predators with a devastating array of ways to kill, burn, and dismember. A version of the mukradi that dwells in the Darklands is rumored to exist. It's said these variant mukradis have black scales, and all of their heads spew a black, acidic goo that animates before being reabsorbed by the mukradis. **[Recall Knowledge - Beast](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35), [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43)): DC 34 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 32 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 29 [Mukradi](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3100) **Source** [Monster Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=221) pg. 233 1.1 **Perception** +24; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59), [tremorsense](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=82) ([imprecise](/Rules.aspx?ID=412)) 60 feet **Languages** **Skills** [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) +32 **Str** +9 **Dex** +0 **Con** +7 **Int** -3 **Wis** +3 **Cha** +0 --- **AC** 37 [all-around vision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=49) **Fort** +32 **Ref** +23 **Will** +26 **HP** 300 **Resistances** [acid](/Traits.aspx?ID=524) 20, [electricity](/Traits.aspx?ID=586) 20, [fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=604) 20 **Partitioned Anatomy** **Trigger** The mukradi would be [confused](/Conditions.aspx?ID=63), [paralyzed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=85), [slowed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=92), or [stunned](/Conditions.aspx?ID=93); **Effect** The mukradi confines the debilitating effect to a certain portion of its nervous system, ignoring the effect but causing a maw of its choice to go dormant for the effect's duration. That maw can't be used for a Strike or to Breathe Energy during that time. This ability can't be used if all the mukradi's heads are dormant.
**Spitting Rage** **Trigger** A creature scores a critical hit on the mukradi; **Effect** The mukradi's Breathe Energy recharges. It can use Breathe Energy immediately as part of this reaction. It can't use this reaction again until it recharges Breathe Energy naturally. --- **Speed** 60 feet, burrow 60 feet, climb 60 feet **Melee** acid maw +32 ([Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103), [reach 20 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)), **Damage** 2d12+17 piercing plus 3d6 acid **Melee** flame maw +32 ([Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103), [reach 20 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)), **Damage** 2d12+17 piercing plus 3d6 fire **Melee** shock maw +32 ([Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103), [reach 20 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)), **Damage** 2d12+17 piercing plus 3d6 electricity **Melee** leg +32 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103), [reach 15 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)), **Damage** 2d10+17 piercing **Melee** tail lash +32 ([Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103), [reach 30 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)), **Damage** 3d10+17 slashing plus [Knockdown](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=46) **Breathe Energy** ([Primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=134)) The mukradi breathes a blast of energy from one of its three heads; each creature in the area must attempt a DC 36 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save. The mukradi can't Breathe Energy again for 1d4 rounds.
  • **Acid Maw** ([acid](/Traits.aspx?ID=524)) 10-foot-wide, 60-foot line of acid dealing 16d6 acid damage.
  • **Flame Maw** ([fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=604)) 60-foot cone of fire dealing 16d6 fire damage.
  • **Shock Maw** ([electricity](/Traits.aspx?ID=586)) 120-foot line of electricity dealing 16d6 electricity damage.
**Pull Apart** The mukradi makes two Strikes with different maws against the same target. If both hit, the target takes an extra 2d12+13 slashing damage, with a DC 36 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Fortitude save. On a critical failure, the creature is torn to pieces and dies. The mukradi's multiple attack penalty increases only after all the attacks are made. **Thrash** The mukradi Strikes once against each creature in its reach. It can make one of these Strikes with each of its maws, one with its tail lash, and the rest with its legs. Each attack takes a –2 circumstance penalty and counts toward the mukradi's multiple attack penalty, but the multiple attack penalty doesn't increase until after all the attacks are made. **[Trample](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=81)** Huge or smaller, leg, DC 36

The phoenix is a primordial bird made of heat and flame that dwells in the most inhospitable regions of the desert. Though highly intelligent and usually brimming with compassion, phoenixes are best known for their iconic ability to resurrect themselves when slain, emerging reborn from the ashes of their own corpses. Phoenixes are often sought out for their knowledge of healing abilities, as they cannot abide the sight of suffering and deny their succor only to the most foul and irredeemable of creatures. Phoenixes enjoy the company of peaceful dragons, and the two can forge lifelong friendships, keeping each other updated on regional news. While most phoenixes are benevolent, they are not infallible. When a phoenix loses their way, they still retain their strong appetite for knowledge. Malevolent phoenixes are known to assault universities and libraries in their pursuit for power—not only to gain new information, but also to set fire to the texts and thus hoard that knowledge for themselves. **[Recall Knowledge - Beast](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35), [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43)): DC 39 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 37 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 34 [Phoenix](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3137) **Source** [Monster Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=221) pg. 264 1.1 **Perception** +27; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59), [_detect magic_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1485), [_see the unseen_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1663) **Languages** [Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1), [Empyrean](/Languages.aspx?ID=115), [Pyric](/Languages.aspx?ID=110), [Sussuran](/Languages.aspx?ID=111) **Skills** [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=1) +30, [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) +27, [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=6) +31, [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=7) +27, [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=10) +25 **Str** +6 **Dex** +7 **Con** +5 **Int** +7 **Wis** +6 **Cha** +6 --- **AC** 36 **Fort** +27 **Ref** +31 **Will** +28 +1 status to all saves vs. [magic](/Traits.aspx?ID=644) **HP** 300 , regeneration 20 (deactivated by [cold](/Traits.aspx?ID=555) or [unholy](/Traits.aspx?ID=521)) **Immunities** [fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=604) **Weaknesses** cold 10, unholy 10 **Shroud of Flame** ([aura](/Traits.aspx?ID=542), [fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=604), [primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=676)) 20 feet. 4d6 fire, DC 37 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save. While this aura is active, any adjacent creature that hits the phoenix with a melee attack or otherwise touches them takes 2d6 fire damage. The phoenix can activate or deactivate the aura with a single action, which has the [concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561) trait.
**Self-Resurrection** ([healing](/Traits.aspx?ID=623), [primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=676)) When a phoenix dies, they collapse into a pile of smoldering ashes before returning to life fully healed 1d4 rounds later, as if subject to a 7th-rank [_resurrect_](/Rituals.aspx?ID=123) ritual. Self-resurrection happens only if there are some remains to resurrect; for instance, a phoenix killed by a [_disintegrate_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1492) spell can't use this ability. A phoenix whose remains rest within an area devoted to an unholy deity by [_consecrate_](/Rituals.aspx?ID=115) can't self-resurrect until their remains are no longer in that area. A phoenix can self-resurrect only once per year. --- **Speed** 25 feet, fly 70 feet **Melee** beak +30 ([Finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=179), [Fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=72), [Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103), [reach 20 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)), **Damage** 1d12+9 piercing plus 3d8 fire and 2d10 [persistent fire](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29) **Melee** talon +30 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [Finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=179), [Fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=72), [Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103), [reach 20 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)), **Damage** 1d6+6 piercing plus 3d8 fire and 2d10 [persistent fire](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29) **Ranged** flame jet +30 ([Fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=72), [range increment 40 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=248)), **Damage** 6d6 fire plus 2d10 [persistent fire](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29) **Primal Inante Spells** DC 39 - **Cantrips (8th)** [Light](/Spells.aspx?ID=1585) - **6th** [Cleanse Affliction](/Spells.aspx?ID=1467) (x3) - **7th** [Dispel Magic](/Spells.aspx?ID=1493) (at will) - **8th** [Cleanse Affliction](/Spells.aspx?ID=1467), [Dispel Magic](/Spells.aspx?ID=1493) (x3), [Divine Immolation](/Spells.aspx?ID=1496), [Everlight](/Spells.aspx?ID=1518) (at will), [Heal](/Spells.aspx?ID=1554) (x3), [Wall of Fire](/Spells.aspx?ID=1748) (x3) - **Constant (6th)** [See the Unseen](/Spells.aspx?ID=1663) - **Constant (8th)** [Detect Magic](/Spells.aspx?ID=1485) **Flaming Strafe** ([Fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=72), [Primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=134)) The phoenix blazes with superheated flame and [Flies](/Actions.aspx?ID=2312) up to their Speed. They deal 6d6 fire damage to each creature within 20 feet of each square they move through (DC 37 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save).

<title level="1" pfs="Standard">[Quelaunt](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3159)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

This three-armed, three-legged monster has no discernible eyes, nose, ears, or mouth, and no visible means of ingesting food. Its limbs are distributed so evenly across its body that it's all but impossible to tell which way the creature is oriented at any given time. Few who witness a quelaunt linger on its alien looks for long though, as the invasion of their minds becomes a more pressing concern, sowing doubt, sorrow, and rage. This monstrosity not only delights in the negative emotions of its prey, but feeds on them, gaining strength and sustenance from their dismay. For the quelaunt, no act is too terrible or cruel to inflict on its victims, since the more a creature suffers, the more the quelaunt feasts.

 Quelaunts are known to associate with other aberrant horrors, including [jah-tohls](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2930) and other creatures associated with the [Dominion of the Black](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=394). However, the more prevalent theory paints them as more alien—perhaps invasive beings from another dimension of pure thought and feeling—and claims that in their natural state they have no physical bodies at all. Few dare speculate further; the only known autopsy of a quelaunt resulted in the researcher's suicide just days afterward and all the notes were mysteriously destroyed. Whatever secrets there are to be unlocked in the anatomy of these bizarre monsters are apparently important enough to warrant great protection from quelaunts, even after death.

text: Quelaunt This three-armed, three-legged monster has no discernible eyes, nose, ears, or mouth, and no visible means of ingesting food. Its limbs are distributed so evenly across its body that it's all but impossible to tell which way the creature is oriented at any given time. Few who witness a quelaunt linger on its alien looks for long though, as the invasion of their minds becomes a more pressing concern, sowing doubt, sorrow, and rage. This monstrosity not only delights in the negative emotions of its prey, but feeds on them, gaining strength and sustenance from their dismay. For the quelaunt, no act is too terrible or cruel to inflict on its victims, since the more a creature suffers, the more the quelaunt feasts. Quelaunts are known to associate with other aberrant horrors, including jah-tohls and other creatures associated with the Dominion of the Black. However, the more prevalent theory paints them as more alien—perhaps invasive beings from another dimension of pure thought and feeling—and claims that in their natural state they have no physical bodies at all. Few dare speculate further; the only known autopsy of a quelaunt resulted in the researcher's suicide just days afterward and all the notes were mysteriously destroyed. Whatever secrets there are to be unlocked in the anatomy of these bizarre monsters are apparently important enough to warrant great protection from quelaunts, even after death. The elusive rumindrol, an apex predator of the Darklands, lives deep below the surface of Golarion. Capable of emitting siren-like calls that reverberate far and wide through the tunnel systems surrounding its lair, a rumindrol feasts on the giant subterranean worms drawn to its call—as well as [shulns](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3191) and other creatures that feed in the worms' wake—by building up sickening subsonic vibrations within its targets until they are unable to move. **[Recall Knowledge - Beast](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35), [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43)): DC 39 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 37 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 34 [Rumindrol](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3303) **Source** [Howl of the Wild](/Sources.aspx?ID=226) pg. 176 2.1 **Perception** +28; motion sense 120 feet, no vision **Languages** **Skills** [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) +30, [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38) +27, [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=49) +25 **Str** +9 **Dex** +6 **Con** +7 **Int** -1 **Wis** +5 **Cha** -1 **Motion Sense** A rumindrol can sense nearby motion through vibration and air movement. --- **AC** 37 **Fort** +30 **Ref** +26 **Will** +23 **HP** 295 **Resistances** [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=669) 15, [sonic](/Traits.aspx?ID=697) 15 **Weaknesses** [cold](/Traits.aspx?ID=555) 10 **Dreadful Resonance** ([auditory](/Traits.aspx?ID=541), [aura](/Traits.aspx?ID=542), [incapacitation](/Traits.aspx?ID=631)) 60 feet. Each creature that enters or starts its turn in the emanation must succeed at a DC 36 Fortitude save or become [enfeebled 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=71) (enfeebled 2 on a critical failure) and take 3d8 sonic damage.
**Enthralling Call** ([auditory](/Traits.aspx?ID=541), [aura](/Traits.aspx?ID=542), [emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=590), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647)) 1 mile. Each non-rumindrol creature that enters or starts its turn within the emanation must succeed at a DC 26 Will save or become [fascinated](/Conditions.aspx?ID=72). The creature then becomes temporarily immune to this effect for 1 day (1 hour on a critical failure). Any creature fascinated in this way will attempt to find the source of the rumindrol's cry, mindlessly wandering towards it. --- **Speed** 20 feet, burrow 60 feet **Melee** jaws +30 ([reach 15 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)), **Damage** 3d12+15 piercing plus [Improved Grab](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=66) **Melee** leg +30 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [reach 15 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)), **Damage** 3d8+15 slashing **Ranged** focused resonance +30 ([range increment 120 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=248)), **Damage** 3d10+15 sonic **Entropic Cry** ([Auditory](/Traits.aspx?ID=16), [Incapacitation](/Traits.aspx?ID=93)) The rumindrol focuses its sonic emanations on a creature it's aware of within the area of its enthralling call aura. The target must attempt a DC 31 Fortitude save.
**Critical Success** The creature becomes temporarily immune to Entropic Cry for 1 hour.
**Success** The target is [sickened 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=91).
**Failure** The target is sickened 2.
**Critical Failure** The target is sickened 2, [enfeebled 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=71), and [stupefied 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=94). **Fast Swallow** **Trigger** The rumindrol [Grabs](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=45) a creature; **Effect** The rumindrol uses Swallow Whole. **Inexorable** The rumindrol recovers from the [paralyzed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=85), [slowed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=92), and [stunned](/Conditions.aspx?ID=93) conditions at the end of its turn. It's also immune to penalties to its Speeds and the immobilized condition, and it ignores difficult terrain and greater difficult terrain. **[Swallow Whole](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=77)** ([Attack](/Traits.aspx?ID=15)) Huge, 3d10+9 bludgeoning, Rupture 30 **Thrash** ([Attack](/Traits.aspx?ID=15)) The rumindrol attempts individual Strikes against each creature in its reach. It can attempt up to one jaws Strike and any number of leg Strikes. Each attack counts toward the rumindrol's multiple attack penalty, but the penalty doesn't increase until after it makes all the attacks. **[Trample](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=81)** Huge or smaller, leg, DC 36

Four-armed seraptis demons are radical nihilists at heart, despising other creatures out of bitter entitlement and laughing hysterically when others die or suffer. They arise from souls that engaged in dedicated campaigns of misery, driving their victims toward despair and suicide. After their awakening as a seraptis, the hungry mouths carved into their arms devour others' suffering, bringing a lively hue to the demon's cold skin. He also can't Conjure Weapon for 1 round.
**Fortification** Each time the First Blade is critically hit, he attempts a DC 17 flat check. On a success, it becomes a normal hit.
**[Halo of Blades](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=53)** ([aura](/Traits.aspx?ID=542), [divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=579)) 10 feet, 3d6 slashing damage (DC 33 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save)

If he drops a conjured weapon or it is disarmed, the weapon vanishes. If he throws a conjured weapon, it vanishes after it is thrown and potentially damages its target. The First Blade prefers using a [greatsword](/Weapons.aspx?ID=379) for melee Strikes and a [light hammer](/Weapons.aspx?ID=384) for thrown ranged Strikes, but cannot have more than one conjured weapon in his possession at any time. **Lord of Battle** The First Blade is highly skilled with all melee and thrown weapons, and gains the advantage of any such weapon's [critical specialization effects](/Rules.aspx?ID=235). He inflicts an additional 1d6 [persistent bleed damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29) with all melee Strikes made with melee weapons. **Whirling Blades** ([Divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=48), [Move](/Traits.aspx?ID=114)) **Frequency** once per minute; **Effect** To the faint sound of fell warhorns, the First Blade transforms into a Large cloud of whirling metal shards, then Strides twice. This movement doesn't trigger reactions, and while he can move through occupied spaces, he must end his movement in an unoccupied space, at which point he resumes his true form. All creatures who the First Blade moves through at least once during his Strides take 10d10 slashing damage (DC 36 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save).

Once a servitor of an ancient god of secrets, the Weaver of Webs now seeks to attain her own godhood. **[Recall Knowledge - Beast](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35), [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43)): DC 44 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 42 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 39 [Weaver Of Webs](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3410) **Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 214 **Perception** +32; [all-around vision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=49), [greater darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59), [tremorsense](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=82) ([imprecise](/Rules.aspx?ID=412)) **Languages** [Aklo](/Languages.aspx?ID=13), [Chthonian](/Languages.aspx?ID=114), [Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1), [Diabolic](/Languages.aspx?ID=117), [Draconic](/Languages.aspx?ID=2), [Dwarven](/Languages.aspx?ID=3), [Empyrean](/Languages.aspx?ID=115), [Jotun](/Languages.aspx?ID=8), [Sakvroth](/Languages.aspx?ID=118); [truespeech](/Feats.aspx?ID=2296) **Skills** [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=34) +25, [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) +30, [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=37) +21, [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38) +30, [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39) +27, [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=40) +30, [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43) +25, [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=44) +27, [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46) +27, [Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=47) +27, [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=48) +30 **Str** +6 **Dex** +4 **Con** +6 **Int** +8 **Wis** +6 **Cha** +6 **Countless Eyes** ([scrying](/Traits.aspx?ID=689)) The Weaver of Webs can see through the eyes of any spider, living or dead, in one of her many lairs. When the Weaver casts her [_scrying_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1662) spell and targets a spider in her lair, the spell is not expended, and the spider automatically critically fails its saving throw.
**Greater Web Sense** The Weaver of Webs' tremorsense also extends to any of her webs, regardless of distance or area, and her tremorsense is a [precise](/Rules.aspx?ID=411) sense against any creature in contact with one of her webs. --- **AC** 36 **Fort** +26 **Ref** +23 **Will** +29 **HP** 335 , regeneration 10 (deactivated by [bright light](/Rules.aspx?ID=407)) **Immunities** [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647), [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=669) **Resistances** [cold](/Traits.aspx?ID=555) 10, mythic resistance 15, [void](/Traits.aspx?ID=510) 10 **Mythic Resistance** The Weaver of Webs has resistance 15 to all attacks made with non-[mythic](/Traits.aspx?ID=835) weapons and unarmed attacks made by non-mythic creatures.
**Spilled Secrets** ([aura](/Traits.aspx?ID=542), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647)) 60 feet. Any creature that speaks within this aura must succeed at a DC 34 Will save or divulge some kind of secret instead of whatever speech they intended. [Linguistic](/Traits.aspx?ID=642) spells and effects gain the [concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561) trait if they didn't have it already and are wasted if the creature fails this save. On a critical failure, the character betrays a secret they least want to reveal to the Weaver or those present.
**Adopted Brood** **Trigger** A creature deals precision damage to the Weaver; **Effect** A spray of smaller spiders pours out of the open wound. These spiders deal 3d6 piercing damage to a single creature within 15 feet of the Weaver and expose that creature to Weaver venom before skittering away. --- **Speed** 60 feet, climb 60 feet **Melee** fangs +28 ([Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103), [reach 10 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)), **Damage** 2d8+16 piercing plus Weaver venom **Melee** tarsal claw +28 ([Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103), [reach 15 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)), **Damage** 2d6+16 slashing plus <%UMR%66>Improved Grab <%END> **Ranged** web +24 ([Nonlethal](/Traits.aspx?ID=188), [Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103), [range 120 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=248)), **Damage** 4d4+10 bludgeoning plus nightmare cocoon and Weaver venom **Occult Innate Spells** DC 36, attack +28 - **2nd** [See the Unseen](/Spells.aspx?ID=1663) (at will) - **3rd** [Dream Message](/Spells.aspx?ID=90), [Fear](/Spells.aspx?ID=110), [Mind Reading](/Spells.aspx?ID=194) - **4th** [Darkness](/Spells.aspx?ID=59) (at will), [Invisibility](/Spells.aspx?ID=164), [Nightmare](/Spells.aspx?ID=208), [Read Omens](/Spells.aspx?ID=247), [Web](/Spells.aspx?ID=374) (at will) - **5th** [Sending](/Spells.aspx?ID=272) (at will) - **6th** [Phantasmal Calamity](/Spells.aspx?ID=218), [Repulsion](/Spells.aspx?ID=254), [Scrying](/Spells.aspx?ID=268), [Teleport](/Spells.aspx?ID=338) - **7th** [Retrocognition](/Spells.aspx?ID=260), [Warp Mind](/Spells.aspx?ID=369) - **8th** [Dream Council](/Spells.aspx?ID=89) - **Constant (7th)** [Truespeech](/Spells.aspx?ID=1728) **Mythic Power** 3 Mythic Points
  • _Remove a Condition_ ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Cost** 1 Mythic Point; **Effect** The Weaver removes any one condition currently affecting her.
**Nightmare Cocoon** ([Incapacitation](/Traits.aspx?ID=93), [Mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=106)) A creature struck by the Weaver's web Strike must succeed at a DC 34 Reflex save or become [immobilized](/Conditions.aspx?ID=81) ([Escape](/Actions.aspx?ID=2296) DC 34). If the Weaver spends 1 Mythic Point as a free action when a creature fails this save, the creature is also [paralyzed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=85), experiencing terrible nightmares of their deepest-held anxieties. The Weaver can view these dreams using a Sustain action, which imparts a –2 circumstance penalty to any Will saves the target attempts against the Weaver's spells until the beginning of the Weaver's next turn. At the end of a paralyzed victim's turn, they can attempt a DC 34 Will save to end the paralyzed condition (though they are still immobilized until they Escape). **Weaver Venom** ([Poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=126)) **Saving Throw** DC 34; **Maximum Duration** 6 rounds; **Stage 1** 2d10 poison (1 round); **Stage 2** 2d10 poison and [slowed 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=92) (2 rounds); **Stage 3** 3d10 poison and slowed 2 (1 round); **Stage 4** 4d10 poison (1 round) and the target permanently forgets the Weaver exists, including any previous mention of her. **Webbed Conveyance** **Requirements** The Weaver is within 15 feet of a creature [paralyzed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=85) in her nightmare cocoon; **Effect** The Weaver grabs the paralyzed target, webs them to her back or one of her legs, and then Strides. As long as the creature is immobilized by the Weaver's nightmare cocoon, it shares the Weaver's space and moves with her. The DC to Escape the nightmare cocoon increases to 36.

text: Weaver Of Webs Once a servitor of an ancient god of secrets, the Weaver of Webs now seeks to attain her own godhood. Recall Knowledge - Beast (Arcana, Nature): DC 44 Unspecific Lore : DC 42 Specific Lore : DC 39 Weaver Of Webs Source War of Immortals pg. 214 Perception +32; all-around vision, greater darkvision, tremorsense (imprecise) Languages Aklo, Chthonian, Common, Diabolic, Draconic, Dwarven, Empyrean, Jotun, Sakvroth; truespeech Skills Acrobatics +25, Athletics +30, Crafting +21, Deception +30, Diplomacy +27, Intimidation +30, Nature +25, Occultism +27, Religion +27, Society +27, Stealth +30 Str +6 Dex +4 Con +6 Int +8 Wis +6 Cha +6 Countless Eyes (scrying) The Weaver of Webs can see through the eyes of any spider, living or dead, in one of her many lairs. When the Weaver casts her scrying spell and targets a spider in her lair, the spell is not expended, and the spider automatically critically fails its saving throw. Greater Web Sense The Weaver of Webs' tremorsense also extends to any of her webs, regardless of distance or area, and her tremorsense is a precise sense against any creature in contact with one of her webs. --- AC 36 Fort +26 Ref +23 Will +29 HP 335 , regeneration 10 (deactivated by bright light) Immunities mental, poison Resistances cold 10, mythic resistance 15, void 10 Mythic Resistance The Weaver of Webs has resistance 15 to all attacks made with non-mythic weapons and unarmed attacks made by non-mythic creatures. Spilled Secrets (aura, mental) 60 feet. Any creature that speaks within this aura must succeed at a DC 34 Will save or divulge some kind of secret instead of whatever speech they intended. Linguistic spells and effects gain the concentrate trait if they didn't have it already and are wasted if the creature fails this save. On a critical failure, the character betrays a secret they least want to reveal to the Weaver or those present. Adopted Brood Reaction Trigger A creature deals precision damage to the Weaver; Effect A spray of smaller spiders pours out of the open wound. These spiders deal 3d6 piercing damage to a single creature within 15 feet of the Weaver and expose that creature to Weaver venom before skittering away. --- Speed 60 feet, climb 60 feet Melee Single Action fangs +28 (Magical, reach 10 feet), Damage 2d8+16 piercing plus Weaver venom Melee Single Action tarsal claw +28 (Magical, reach 15 feet), Damage 2d6+16 slashing plus <%UMR%66>Improved Grab <%END> Ranged Single Action web +24 (Nonlethal, Magical, range 120 feet), Damage 4d4+10 bludgeoning plus nightmare cocoon and Weaver venom Occult Innate Spells DC 36, attack +28 - 2nd See the Unseen (at will) - 3rd Dream Message, Fear, Mind Reading - 4th Darkness (at will), Invisibility, Nightmare, Read Omens, Web (at will) - 5th Sending (at will) - 6th Phantasmal Calamity, Repulsion, Scrying, Teleport - 7th Retrocognition, Warp Mind - 8th Dream Council - Constant (7th) Truespeech Mythic Power 3 Mythic Points Remove a Condition Single Action (concentrate) Cost 1 Mythic Point; Effect The Weaver removes any one condition currently affecting her. Nightmare Cocoon (Incapacitation, Mental) A creature struck by the Weaver's web Strike must succeed at a DC 34 Reflex save or become immobilized (Escape DC 34). If the Weaver spends 1 Mythic Point as a free action when a creature fails this save, the creature is also paralyzed, experiencing terrible nightmares of their deepest-held anxieties. The Weaver can view these dreams using a Sustain action, which imparts a –2 circumstance penalty to any Will saves the target attempts against the Weaver's spells until the beginning of the Weaver's next turn. At the end of a paralyzed victim's turn, they can attempt a DC 34 Will save to end the paralyzed condition (though they are still immobilized until they Escape). Weaver Venom (Poison) Saving Throw DC 34; Maximum Duration 6 rounds; Stage 1 2d10 poison (1 round); Stage 2 2d10 poison and slowed 1 (2 rounds); Stage 3 3d10 poison and slowed 2 (1 round); Stage 4 4d10 poison (1 round) and the target permanently forgets the Weaver exists, including any previous mention of her. Webbed Conveyance Single Action Requirements The Weaver is within 15 feet of a creature paralyzed in her nightmare cocoon; Effect The Weaver grabs the paralyzed target, webs them to her back or one of her legs, and then Strides. As long as the creature is immobilized by the Weaver's nightmare cocoon, it shares the Weaver's space and moves with her. The DC to Escape the nightmare cocoon increases to 36.

Fate is a fickle matter on Golarion. Even with prophecy broken on the world, there are ways to look to the immediate future or acquire a vague sense of long-term events. Omen dragons are bound to see the future—nebulous though it might be—at all times. Visions of the future hound them like a quiet song that never stops playing in their minds. While an omen dragon can focus on or ignore the music of fate at any time, the song plays all the same. At a glance, omen dragons resemble other occult dragons in appearance, save for the mirror-like interior membrane of their wings. An omen dragon's wings offer glimpses into the future. These glimpses are cloudy and vague, but generally correct, if only technically. Omen dragons have a natural compulsion to share the futures they see. These dragons have no compunctions about what the visions show and share their knowledge equally with innocent villagers as they do with wicked tyrants. **[Recall Knowledge - Dragon](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35)): DC 37 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 35 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 32 [Ancient Omen Dragon](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2955) **Source** [Monster Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=221) pg. 125 1.1 **Perception** +29; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59), [scent](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=74) ([imprecise](/Monsters.aspx?ID=109)) 60 feet **Languages** [Aklo](/Languages.aspx?ID=13), [Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1), [Draconic](/Languages.aspx?ID=2), [Fey](/Languages.aspx?ID=119), [Jotun](/Languages.aspx?ID=8) **Skills** [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=1) +28, [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) +30, [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=6) +29, [Fortune-Telling Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8) +33, [Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8) +31, [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=11) +33, [Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=14) +31 **Str** +8 **Dex** +6 **Con** +7 **Int** +9 **Wis** +7 **Cha** +5 --- **AC** 38 **Fort** +27 **Ref** +28 **Will** +29 +2 status to all saves vs. [occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=662) **HP** 280 **Immunities** [confused](/Conditions.aspx?ID=63), [doomed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=67), [paralyzed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=85), [sleep](/Traits.aspx?ID=696) **Untethered to Fate** The dragon can choose to negate any [fortune](/Traits.aspx?ID=612) or [misfortune](/Traits.aspx?ID=654) effects that would affect them; other creatures remain affected normally.
**Challenge Fate** ([misfortune](/Traits.aspx?ID=654), [occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=662)) **Trigger** The dragon is targeted by an attack; **Effect** This fate is not set in stone. The attacker rolls the triggering attack twice and uses the worse result. --- **Speed** 60 feet, fly 180 feet **Melee** jaws +30 ([Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103), [reach 15 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)), **Damage** 3d8+14 piercing plus 1d8 mental **Melee** claw +30 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103), [reach 10 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)), **Damage** 3d6+14 slashing plus 1d8 mental **Melee** tail +28 ([Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103), [reach 20 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)), **Damage** 3d8+14 bludgeoning plus 1d8 mental **Melee** wing +28 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103), [reach 15 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)), **Damage** 2d8+14 slashing plus 1d8 mental **Occult Innate Spells** DC 39 - **Cantrips (8th)** [Guidance](/Spells.aspx?ID=142) - **7th** [Ill Omen](/Spells.aspx?ID=696) (at will), [Mindlink](/Spells.aspx?ID=195) (at will), [True Target](/Spells.aspx?ID=346) (×2) - **8th** [Retrocognition](/Spells.aspx?ID=260) **Destiny Breath** ([Mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=106), [Occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=120)) The dragon breathes a translucent mist of potentialities that overwhelms creatures with visions of possible features, dealing 15d6 mental damage in a 40-foot cone (DC 39 Will save). A creature that fails its save is [slowed 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=92) for 1 round (or slowed 2 on a critical failure) as it struggles with the visions. The dragon can't use Destiny Breath again for 1d4 rounds. **Impending Fate** The dragon's attacks bring their foes closer to their eventual fates. When the dragon critically hits with a Strike or a creature critically fails against the dragon's Destiny Breath, the creature becomes [doomed 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=67), or increases its doomed value by 1 if it was already doomed. **Draconic Frenzy** The dragon makes two claw Strikes and one wing Strike in any order. **Draconic Momentum** The dragon recharges their Destiny Breath whenever they score a critical hit with a Strike. **Prophetic Wings** The dragon or any ally can glimpse into the future through the dragon's wings in a process that requires 10 minutes of concentration. This casts a 8th-rank [_augury_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1445) spell, except that the wings can predict results up to 1 day into the future and the dragon always speaks a few cryptic words related to the result of the prediction. The dragon can use their wings in this way only once per hour, and a given creature can seek a future in the wings only once per week.
A creature can also choose to predict events up to 1 month into the future—the dragon can view a month ahead in their own wings only once per day.
A creature can also choose to predict events up to 1 year into the future—the dragon can view a year ahead in their own wings only once per day. **Walk the Timelines** ([Occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=120)) **Frequency** once per hour; **Effect** The dragon splits themself into two versions with different fates. Each copy Strides or [Flies](/Actions.aspx?ID=2312)from the dragon's current space, then takes a single action. If the actions are both attacks, they use the same multiple attack penalty and count as one attack toward the dragon's multiple attack penalty. After both actions, the dragon chooses one of the two locations as their actual destination and the other version of themself disappears.

Bloody Hands was no agent of [Gorum](/Deities.aspx?ID=283) when he first rose from the polluted swamps of a remote fen in the [Outer Rifts](/Planes.aspx?ID=45). For the first several millennia of his life, he fought for his own domain in the sprawling slime, eventually securing a realm the size of a small continent where his rule was unquestioned—at least, until it was invaded by a host of Gorum's [einherjar](/Monsters.aspx?ID=1141). Bloody Hands was taken aback at the aesirs' battle prowess, and he gloried in the fall of his empire to the extent that, by the end of the invasion, he was proudly fighting on their side, mercilessly destroying hordes of demons who had so recently served him out of fear. The einherjar admired his lust for battle but didn't quite know what to make of the frog-like demon, especially when he followed them back across the [Maelstrom](/Planes.aspx?ID=43) to Clashing Shore. After several centuries of brawling along the borders of that realm, growing increasingly less interested in sadism and more enthralled with the tactics of battle, Bloody Hands was granted permission by Gorum to become one of his servitors. Bloody Hands appears as a vaguely humanoid frog-like demon whose stance evokes that of a lumbering gorilla. His slimy green skin shifts to a bloody red along the length of his arms, so that his claws look as though they're constantly glistening with fresh blood. He has four beady eyes and a wide mouth filled with sharp teeth. **[Recall Knowledge - Fiend](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46)): DC 45 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 43 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 40 [Bloody Hands](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3393) **Source** [Prey for Death](/Sources.aspx?ID=231) pg. 114 **Perception** +28; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59) **Languages** [Chthonian](/Languages.aspx?ID=114), [Empyrean](/Languages.aspx?ID=115), [Jotun](/Languages.aspx?ID=8), [Protean](/Languages.aspx?ID=33); [telepathy](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=79) 100 feet **Skills** [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) +33, [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=40) +29, [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46) +28 **Str** +9 **Dex** +4 **Con** +8 **Int** +5 **Wis** +6 **Cha** +5 --- **AC** 39 **Fort** +30 **Ref** +24 **Will** +28 +1 to all saves vs. [magic](/Traits.aspx?ID=644) **HP** 300 **Weaknesses** [cold iron](/Equipment.aspx?ID=375) 15 **Battle Reek** ([aura](/Traits.aspx?ID=542), [olfactory](/Traits.aspx?ID=664)) 30 feet. Bloody Hands exudes the carrion stink of a sprawling battlefield—a cloying mixture of death and mud. Any creature entering the aura or starting its turn in the aura must succeed at a DC 34 Fortitude save or become [sickened 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=91) (plus slowed 1 for as long as it's sickened on a critical failure). While within the aura, affected creatures take a –2 circumstance penalty to saves against [fear](/Traits.aspx?ID=598) and to recover from the [sickened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=91) condition. A creature that succeeds at its save is temporarily immune for 1 minute. --- **Speed** 30 feet, swim 30 feet **Melee** jaws +33 ([Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103), [reach 10 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192), [Unholy](/Traits.aspx?ID=521)), **Damage** 3d12+17 piercing **Melee** claw +33 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103), [reach 10 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192), [Unholy](/Traits.aspx?ID=521)), **Damage** 3d6+17 slashing plus 1d6 [persistent bleed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29) **Divine Innate Spells** DC 34 - **Cantrips (8th)** [Divine Lance](/Spells.aspx?ID=84), [Telekinetic Projectile](/Spells.aspx?ID=334) - **4th** [Translocate](/Spells.aspx?ID=1724) (at will) - **5th** [Translocate](/Spells.aspx?ID=1724) - **6th** [Phantasmal Calamity](/Spells.aspx?ID=218) - **7th** [Divine Decree](/Spells.aspx?ID=82) - **8th** [Divine Wrath](/Spells.aspx?ID=86) **Bloody Mess** ([Divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=48)) **Frequency** once per day; **Effect** Bloody Hands slashes his claws out in all directions, causing blood from all living creatures within a 20-foot-radius to leap out and fill the air with a fine red mist. All creatures in the area must attempt a DC 37 Fortitude save—creatures that are already wounded take a –2 penalty to this saving throw. If more than 3 creatures fail this saving throw, the 20-foot-radius becomes so thick with bloody mist that all creatures in the area become [concealed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=62) until the end of Bloody Hands' next turn.
**Critical Success** The creature is unaffected.
**Success** The creature takes 8d6 slashing damage.
**Failure** The creature takes 8d6 slashing damage, 4d6 [persistent bleed damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29), and becomes [enfeebled 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=71) from blood loss for 1 minute.
**Critical Failure** The creature takes 12d6 persistent bleed damage and becomes enfeebled 2 from blood loss. **Leaping Slam** ([Incapacitation](/Traits.aspx?ID=93)) Bloody Hands Strides, then makes a [High Jump](/Actions.aspx?ID=2377) or a [Long Jump](/Actions.aspx?ID=2378), and can land in a space occupied by creatures. All creatures in the 10-foot space he lands in must attempt a DC 37 Reflex save.
**Critical Success** The creature dodges aside and takes no damage, and it can choose any square adjacent to Bloody Hands to immediately move into; this movement does not trigger reactions.
**Success** The creature takes 4d6 bludgeoning damage and is [pushed](/Rules.aspx?ID=451) into an adjacent space of Bloody Hands' choice.
**Failure** The creature takes 8d6 bludgeoning damage, is pushed into an adjacent space of Bloody Hands' choice, and is knocked [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=88).
**Critical Failure** The creature takes 8d6 bludgeoning damage, is knocked prone, and becomes pinned by Bloody Hands

description:
Bloody Hands was no agent of [Gorum](/Deities.aspx?ID=283) when he first rose from the polluted swamps of a remote fen in the [Outer Rifts](/Planes.aspx?ID=45). For the first several millennia of his life, he fought for his own domain in the sprawling slime, eventually securing a realm the size of a small continent where his rule was unquestioned—at least, until it was invaded by a host of Gorum's [einherjar](/Monsters.aspx?ID=1141). Bloody Hands was taken aback at the aesirs' battle prowess, and he gloried in the fall of his empire to the extent that, by the end of the invasion, he was proudly fighting on their side, mercilessly destroying hordes of demons who had so recently served him out of fear. The einherjar admired his lust for battle but didn't quite know what to make of the frog-like demon, especially when he followed them back across the [Maelstrom](/Planes.aspx?ID=43) to Clashing Shore. After several centuries of brawling along the borders of that realm, growing increasingly less interested in sadism and more enthralled with the tactics of battle, Bloody Hands was granted permission by Gorum to become one of his servitors.

 Bloody Hands appears as a vaguely humanoid frog-like demon whose stance evokes that of a lumbering gorilla. His slimy green skin shifts to a bloody red along the length of his arms, so that his claws look as though they're constantly glistening with fresh blood. He has four beady eyes and a wide mouth filled with sharp teeth.

Corbayrants are creations of the Green Mother, one of the fey called the Eldest. In the Age of Creation, she fashioned them from thorns and moss into deadly predators. When gnomes migrated to the mortal Universe, many corbayrants followed but found themselves poorly suited to life outside the First World. Corbayrants are historically solitary, territorial creatures. They're incapable of reproducing, and without the revivifying properties of the First World, their numbers are doomed to deplete. Recently, a number of corbayrants in the Verduran Forest have overcome their natures to band together. They've been known to take their prey alive, sacrificing their victims in vile experiments in an effort to find a way to propagate corbayrant numbers. Corbayrants look like massive clawless scorpions covered in bark and thorns. A rotting fog wafts from their bodies. In the rare instance when they deign to speak, they do so in a raspy whisper. **[Recall Knowledge - Beast](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35), [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43)): DC 40 **[Recall Knowledge - Fey](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43)): DC 40 **[Recall Knowledge - Plant](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43)): DC 40 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 38 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 35 [Corbayrant](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3822) **Source** [Shining Kingdoms](/Sources.aspx?ID=265) pg. 178 **Perception** +28; blindsight (precise) 100 feet **Languages** [Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=155), [Fey](/Languages.aspx?ID=119), [Muan](/Languages.aspx?ID=108) **Skills** [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) +33, [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43) +29, [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=48) +27, [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=49) +27 **Str** +9 **Dex** +5 **Con** +6 **Int** +4 **Wis** +5 **Cha** +1 --- **AC** 38 **Fort** +30 **Ref** +27 **Will** +27 **HP** 295 , regeneration 20 (deactivated by cold) **Immunities** blinded, visual **cold 15** Resistances fire 10, piercing 15
**Thorny Hide** A corbayrant's body is covered in jagged spines. Adjacent creatures that hit them with a melee attack, as well as creatures that touch them or hit them with an unarmed attack, take 4d6 piercing damage and are exposed to thorn paralysis.
**Vitriolic Miasma** ([aura](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=53)) 30 feet. Non-corbayrants take a –2 circumstance penalty to saves against poison effects and gain weakness 10 to poison damage while within the aura.
**Reactive Strike** --- **Speed** 40 feet, climb 40 feet **Melee** fangs +32, **Damage** 3d12+18 piercing plus [Grab](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=45) **Melee** stinger +32 ([reach 15 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=684)), **Damage** 3d10+15 piercing plus corbayrant venom **Ranged** spine +32 ([Propulsive](/Traits.aspx?ID=191), [range increment 40 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=248)), **Damage** 3d6+15 piercing plus thorn paralysis **Corbayrant Venom** ([Poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=126)) **Saving Throw** DC 37 Fortitude; **Maximum Duration** 6 rounds; **Stage 1** 8d6 poison damage (1 round); **Stage 2** 9d6 poison damage (1 round); **Stage 3** 9d6 poison damage and drained 1 (1 round) **Spine Volley** The corbayrant makes four spine Strikes, each against a differenttarget. These attacks all count toward the corbayrant's multiple attack penalty, but the penalty doesn't increase until after the corbayrant makes their attacks. **[Swallow Whole](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=77)** Large, 9d6 piercing plus thorn paralysis, Rupture 30 **Thorn Paralysis** ([Incapacitation](/Traits.aspx?ID=93), [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=669)) The corbayrant's spines are covered in a paralyzing toxin that cause verdurous thorns to sprout from their victim's body. When a non-corbayrant creature is exposed, it attempts a DC 37 Fortitude save.

Devasances are typically felt before they're seen, as they constantly sap vitality from creatures around them. On [the Void](/Planes.aspx?ID=28), a devasance's aura can be easily confused for a pocket of particularly potent planar energy, especially as they meld into the darkness around them. Legless and incorporeal with glowing red eyes, these vaguely humanoid creatures are commonly confused for [shadows](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3186), [wraiths](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3243), or other forms of [incorporeal](/Traits.aspx?ID=632) [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=722). **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 38 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 35 [Devasance](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3790) **Source** [Pathfinder #212: A Voice in the Blight](/Sources.aspx?ID=255) pg. 83 **Perception** +30; [greater darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59), [lifesense](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=67) 60 feet **Languages** [Aklo](/Languages.aspx?ID=13), [Necril](/Languages.aspx?ID=20), [Shadowtongue](/Languages.aspx?ID=21) **Skills** [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=34) +31, [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=40) +33, [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=48) +30 **Str** -5 **Dex** +6 **Con** +0 **Int** +5 **Wis** +6 **Cha** +9 --- **AC** 38 **Fort** +25 **Ref** +30 **Will** +28 **HP** 225 ([void healing](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=83)) **Immunities** bleed, [death](/Traits.aspx?ID=571) effects, [disease](/Traits.aspx?ID=578), [paralyzed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=85), [poison](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=70), precision, [unconscious](/Conditions.aspx?ID=95) **Resistances** all 15 (except [force](/Traits.aspx?ID=610), [_ghost touch_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2840), [spirit](/Traits.aspx?ID=737), or [vitality](/Traits.aspx?ID=509); double resistance vs. non-[magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=644)) **Weaknesses** [vitality](/Traits.aspx?ID=509) 15 **Aura of Malaise** ([aura](/Traits.aspx?ID=542), [void](/Traits.aspx?ID=510)) 30 feet. A living creature that starts its turn in the devasance's aura must succeed at a DC 34 Will save or become slowed 1 (or slowed 2 on a critical failure).
**Void Shadow** While on a plane with the void trait or in the area of an effect with the void trait, the devasance's form disappears. It is naturally invisible in this area, but becomes visible for 1 minute after it takes vitality damage.
**Drink Life** Trigger A living creature takes void damage from the devasance; Effect The devasance gains 25 temporary HP for 1 minute and becomes quickened until the end of its next turn. It can use the extra action to Strike or Fly. --- **Speed** fly 30 feet **Melee** void hand +30 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [Finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=179), [Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103)), **Damage** 3d6+8 void plus 2d6 spirit and living death **Occult Innate Spells** DC 37, attack +29 - **Cantrips (8th)** [Telekinetic Projectile](/Spells.aspx?ID=334), [Void Warp](/Spells.aspx?ID=1745) - **6th** [Vision of Death](/Spells.aspx?ID=1742) - **7th** [Paralyze](/Spells.aspx?ID=213), [Warp Mind](/Spells.aspx?ID=369) - **8th** [Spirit Blast](/Spells.aspx?ID=301) **Living Death** ([Curse](/Traits.aspx?ID=38), [Occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=120)) A creature hit by the devasance's void hand strike must attempt a DC 37 Fortitude save.
**Critical Success** The target is unaffected.
**Success** The target takes on the appearance of a rotted or nearly skeletal undead version of itself and becomes [drained 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=68) for 1 round. If the target assumes another shape through a [polymorph](/Traits.aspx?ID=670) effect, it continues to look undead in its new shape. This change in appearance persists for 10 minutes.
**Failure** As success, but with an unlimited duration. [Healing](/Traits.aspx?ID=623) effects on the target restore only half the Hit Points they normally would.
**Critical Failure** As failure, but drained 2. If a living creature dies while under the effects of this curse, their soul is transformed into a devasance upon death. The creature cannot be restored to life, nor can its soul move on to the afterlife, until it is slain again as a devasance. **Void Ray** ([Occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=120), [Void](/Traits.aspx?ID=510)) The devasance emits a ray of void energy from its chest in a 60-foot line. text: Devasance Devasances are typically felt before they're seen, as they constantly sap vitality from creatures around them. On the Void, a devasance's aura can be easily confused for a pocket of particularly potent planar energy, especially as they meld into the darkness around them. Legless and incorporeal with glowing red eyes, these vaguely humanoid creatures are commonly confused for shadows, wraiths, or other forms of incorporeal undead. Cave worm eggs that lie dormant for a long period may experience significant climactic shift. If the temperature falls below freezing, the worms may hatch as glacial worms, also called white worms. These creatures immediately migrate as far north as possible, seeking the glaciers or icebergs that will nourish and house them. Glacial worms lack stingers, as liquid venom is less effective in cold temperatures. Occasionally, such creatures are carried far south on icebergs that have carved off the main ice sheets of the polar regions. **[Recall Knowledge - Animal](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=10)): DC 37 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 35 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 32 [Glacial Worm](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2703) **Source** [Pathfinder #194: Cult of the Cave Worm](/Sources.aspx?ID=209) pg. 67 **Perception** +22; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=12), [tremorsense](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=40) ([imprecise](/Rules.aspx?ID=412)) 100 feet **Languages** **Skills** [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) +34 **Str** +10 **Dex** +0 **Con** +8 **Int** -5 **Wis** +0 **Cha** -1 --- **AC** 36 **Fort** +30 **Ref** +22 **Will** +22 **HP** 370 (cold healing) **Immunities** [cold](/Traits.aspx?ID=27) **Weaknesses** [fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=72) 15 **Cold Healing** When a glacial worm is in extreme cold or surrounded by ice, it gains [fast healing 10](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=15). When struck by a magical cold effect, a glacial worm regains Hit Points equal to half the cold damage the effect would otherwise deal.
**Inexorable** The glacial worm recovers from the [paralyzed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=28), [slowed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=35), and [stunned](/Conditions.aspx?ID=36) conditions at the end of its turn. It's also immune to penalties to its Speeds and the [immobilized](/Conditions.aspx?ID=24) condition, and it ignores [difficult terrain](/Rules.aspx?ID=453) and greater difficult terrain.

text: Glacial Worm Cave worm eggs that lie dormant for a long period may experience significant climactic shift. If the temperature falls below freezing, the worms may hatch as glacial worms, also called white worms. These creatures immediately migrate as far north as possible, seeking the glaciers or icebergs that will nourish and house them. Glacial worms lack stingers, as liquid venom is less effective in cold temperatures. Occasionally, such creatures are carried far south on icebergs that have carved off the main ice sheets of the polar regions. No one is quite sure what lesser deaths are, though some claim that they are avatars of the Grim Reaper. Unlike that strange hunter, however, lesser deaths hunt in packs on rare occasions. More often than not, they manifest from cursed magic items. Other times, they are just the enactors of death, hunting in the same way the Grim Reaper does—silently, with no remorse or quarter. Rarely, multiple lesser deaths work together to cull a large population, their scythes cutting through crowds and leaving entire cities devoid of life, inspiring (hopefully) false rumors of multiple Grim Reapers. **[Recall Knowledge - Undead](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46)): DC 40 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 38 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 35 [Lesser Death](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3037) **Source** [Monster Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=221) pg. 185 1.1 **Perception** +32; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59), [_see the unseen_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1663), status sight, [_truesight_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1727) **Languages** [Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1), [Necril](/Languages.aspx?ID=20) **Skills** [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=1) +33, [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) +28, [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5) +30, [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=7) +32, [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=13) +30, [Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=14) +26, [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15) +35 **Str** +6 **Dex** +9 **Con** +6 **Int** +4 **Wis** +6 **Cha** +6 **Status Sight** a lesser death automatically knows the Hit Points, conditions, afflictions, and emotions of all creatures it can see. **Items** [Scythe](/Weapons.aspx?ID=39) --- **AC** 39 **Fort** +30 **Ref** +33 **Will** +32 +1 status to all saves vs. [magic](/Traits.aspx?ID=644) **HP** 255 (death's grace, [void healing](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=83)) **Immunities** bleed, [death](/Traits.aspx?ID=571) effects, [disease](/Traits.aspx?ID=578), [paralyzed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=85), [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=669), [unconscious](/Conditions.aspx?ID=95) **Aura of Misfortune** ([aura](/Traits.aspx?ID=542), [divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=579), [misfortune](/Traits.aspx?ID=654)) 20 feet. Living creatures in the aura must roll twice on all d20 rolls and use the lower result.
**Death's Grace** A lesser death can choose whether or not it counts as [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=722) for effects that affect undead differently. Even if it does not count as undead, the lesser death still never counts as a living creature.
**Void Healing** A lesser death can choose whether or not it takes vitality damage.
**Lurking Death** ([divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=579), [teleportation](/Traits.aspx?ID=710)) **Trigger** A creature within 60 feet makes a ranged attack or uses an action that has the [concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645), or [move](/Traits.aspx?ID=658) trait; **Effect** The lesser death teleports to a square adjacent to the triggering creature and makes a melee Strike against it. If the Strike hits, the lesser death disrupts the triggering action. --- **Speed** 50 feet, fly 40 feet **Melee** keen scythe +32 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [deadly 2d10](/Traits.aspx?ID=174), [Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103), [reach 10 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192), [Trip](/Traits.aspx?ID=196)), **Damage** 3d10+14 slashing plus 1d12 void **Divine Innate Spells** DC 38 - **2nd** [See the Unseen](/Spells.aspx?ID=1663) - **Constant (6th)** [Truesight](/Spells.aspx?ID=1727) **Infuse Weapon** ([Divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=48)) Any scythe gains the [agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=526) trait, can't be disarmed, and becomes a _+2 [greater striking](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2829) [keen](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2843) scythe_ while the lesser death wields it.

When a powerful worshipper catches Norgorber's eye, he sometimes transforms that worshipper into one of his masks—supernatural incarnations who become powerful proxies to their god but sacrifice their free will. **[Recall Knowledge - Fiend](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46)): DC 40 **[Recall Knowledge - Humanoid](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=47)): DC 40 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 38 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 35 [Mask of Norgorber](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3748) **Source** [Pathfinder #206: Bring the House Down](/Sources.aspx?ID=247) pg. 84 **Perception** +32; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59), [_truesight_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1727) **Languages** [Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1); [_truespeech_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1728) **Skills** [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=34) +31, [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) +28, [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=37) +29, [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38) +30, [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39) +30, [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=40) +30, [Norgorber Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) +31, [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46) +28, [Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=47) +27, [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=48) +33, [Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=50) +31 **Str** +6 **Dex** +9 **Con** +5 **Int** +5 **Wis** +6 **Cha** +6 **Items** _+2 [greater striking](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2829) [shortsword](/Weapons.aspx?ID=398)_, _[true faith tattoo](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2207)_, _+2 [resilient](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2786) [leather armor](/Armor.aspx?ID=41)_ --- **AC** 39 **Fort** +25 **Ref** +33 **Will** +28 **HP** 290 **Secretive Tattoos** The mask keeps their _faith tattoo_ hidden (typically by wearing gloves to cover the palm). To use it as a divine focus, they must first Interact to uncover the tattoo. The tattoo then stays uncovered until the mask Interacts to cover it up. A mask's _faith tattoo_ only allows for the casting of [_harm_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1552). Upon the mask's death, the tattoo disappears.
**[Reactive Strike](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=48)** --- **Speed** 30 feet **Melee** _shortsword_ +33 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [Finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=179), [Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103), [versatile P](/Traits.aspx?ID=200)), **Damage** 3d6+14 slashing plus 1d6 persistent damage (see Aspect's Agony) **Divine Innate Spells** DC 37, attack +29 - **Cantrips (8th)** [Daze](/Spells.aspx?ID=61), [Detect Magic](/Spells.aspx?ID=66), [Message](/Spells.aspx?ID=190) - **4th** [Invisibility](/Spells.aspx?ID=164) (×3), [Silence](/Spells.aspx?ID=287) (×3) - **6th** [Sending](/Spells.aspx?ID=272) (×3), [Spellwrack](/Spells.aspx?ID=298) - **7th** [Cleanse Affliction](/Spells.aspx?ID=1467), [Divine Decree](/Spells.aspx?ID=82) - **8th** [Heal](/Spells.aspx?ID=148) (×3), [Shadow Blast](/Spells.aspx?ID=273) - **Constant (8th)** [Truesight](/Spells.aspx?ID=1727), [Truespeech](/Spells.aspx?ID=1728) **Aspect's Agony** When a mask of Norgorber Strikes a foe with a weapon, they inflict an additional 1d6 persistent damage of a type determined by their aspect. As long as a creature is taking this persistent damage, they're [off-guard](/Conditions.aspx?ID=58). **Sneak Attack** A mask of Norgorber deals 2d6 extra precision damage to creatures who are [off-guard](/Conditions.aspx?ID=58).

As long as a creature is taking this persistent damage, they're off-guard. Sneak Attack A mask of Norgorber deals 2d6 extra precision damage to creatures who are off-guard. Aspect Of Blackfingers These masks focus on the use of poisons to spread Norgorber's will. Blackfingers Aspect Aspect's Agony 1d6 persistent poison Additional Divine Innate Spells 8th toxic cloud ; 7th slither Evaporate Poison Single Action (divine, poison) Frequency once per day; Effect The mask blows out a breath and targets a creature within 30 feet that is currently poisoned or is taking persistent poison damage. The target must attempt a DC 37 Fortitude save as the mask attempts to transmute the poison afflicting them into toxic vapor. Critical Success The poison effect on the target immediately ends. Success The poison effect on the target immediately ends, but toxic vapor fills one of the target's adjacent squares, chosen by the mask. Father Skinsaw Aspect Aspect's Agony 1d6 persistent bleed Additional Divine Innate Spells 8th blood vendetta ; 7th mask of terror Invigorating Flense Single Action (divine) Frequency once per day; Effect The mask makes a quick striking motion, as if slicing flesh with a small knife, and targets a creature within 30 feet. The target immediately takes 12d6 slashing and 5d6 persistent bleed damage (DC 37 basic Fortitude save), and the mask becomes quickened as long as the target continues to take persistent bleed damage. The mask can use the extra action only to Stride or Strike. Aspect Of The Gray Master These masks focus on theft in all of its forms. Gray Master Aspect Aspect's Agony 1d6 persistent void Additional Divine Innate Spells 8th quandary ; 7th umbral graft Steal Life Two Actions (death, divine, void) Frequency once per day; Effect The mask makes a quick plucking gesture as they attempt to steal a creature's life. The mask gains temporary Hit Points equal to half the void damage the target takes (after applying resistances and the like), and loses any remaining temporary Hit Points after 24 hours. Aspect Of The Reaper These masks fracture trust and turn allies against each other. Reaper Of Reputation Aspect Aspect's Agony 1d6 persistent mental Additional Divine Innate Spells 8th suggestion ; 7th warp mind Insidious Secrets Single Action (auditory, divine, emotion, fear, linguistic, mental) Frequency once per day; Effect The mask whispers, then targets a creature within 30 feet. Success The mask whispers a horrific secret to the target, and though their mind recoils and forgets, the target still takes 8d6 mental damage and is frightened 1. Failure As failure, but 17d6 mental damage and frightened 2; the target is confused as long as they are frightened. Critical Failure As failure, but 30d6 mental damage and the target is confused for 1 minute. When Norgorber chooses someone to become a mask, a swift and nearly instantaneous blurring of the creature is the only indication of their change. Like most fiends, masks are immortal unless slain through violence or misadventure. Once slain, a mask's body decays as normal, and after a variable amount of time has passed, their soul returns to the Great Beyond to accrete its quintessence into Norgorber's realm of Duskfathom. **[Recall Knowledge - Ooze](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=44)): DC 45 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 43 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 40 [Niesha](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3385) **Source** [Prey for Death](/Sources.aspx?ID=231) pg. 65 **Perception** +30; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59) **Languages** [Aklo](/Languages.aspx?ID=13), [Azlanti](/Languages.aspx?ID=49); polyglot **Skills** [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) +30, [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38) +28, [Library Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) +31, [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=44) +29, [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46) +32, [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=48) +30 **Str** +8 **Dex** +6 **Con** +5 **Int** +4 **Wis** +5 **Cha** +5 **Polyglot** A mezlan can speak and understand any language they hear spoken after listening to the language for 1 minute. These languages fade from their mind after 24 hours. --- **AC** 36 **Fort** +25 **Ref** +28 **Will** +30 +1 status to all saves vs. [magic](/Traits.aspx?ID=644) **HP** 300 , regeneration 15 (deactivated by [acid](/Traits.aspx?ID=524)) **Immunities** critical hits, precision, [unconscious](/Conditions.aspx?ID=95) **Weaknesses** acid 15 **Absorb Spell** **Trigger** The mezlan succeeds at a saving throw against a single-target spell; **Effect** The mezlan absorbs the spell, nullifying its effect and storing it for later. They can Cast the Spell using the original caster's spell attack modifier and DC. They can store only one spell at a time, but they can absorb a new spell to replace the spell they currently have stored. A willing caster can allow the mezlan to Absorb a Spell without requiring a save.
**Discorporate** When the mezlan is reduced to 0 Hit Points, their body dissolves into colorless slime and begins seeping into nearby cracks or porous surfaces. If this material is not immediately contained or destroyed, the mezlan will eventually re-form, though they may lie dormant for years or even decades before doing so. --- **Speed** 30 feet **Melee** polymorphic appendage +32 ([Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103), [versatile P](/Traits.aspx?ID=200), [versatile S](/Traits.aspx?ID=200)), **Damage** 3d12+16 bludgeoning **Ranged** ooze globule +30 ([range increment 30 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=248)), **Damage** viscous trap **Access Pipe Ambush** **Trigger** Niesha emerges from one of the Sarzari access pipes; **Effect** Niesha makes a melee Strike against an adjacent creature as she emerges. **[Change Shape](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=55)** ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [polymorph](/Traits.aspx?ID=670), [transmutation](/Traits.aspx?ID=157)) The mezlan assumes the form of any Medium or Small creature, excluding those with the [elemental](/Traits.aspx?ID=587), [incorporeal](/Traits.aspx?ID=632), or [swarm](/Domains.aspx?ID=53) traits but including specific individuals whose appearance they've seen. This doesn't change the mezlan's Speed or their attack and damage bonus with their Strikes, but the damage type dealt by their Strikes might change based on their new form. **Extend Limb** The mezlan extends one of their limbs, granting themself a [reach](/Traits.aspx?ID=684) of 20 feet with their polymorphic appendages until the end of their next turn. **Navigate Pipes** Niesha can move though the Sarzari Access Pipes, even though they're only two feet wide; she treats these pipes as difficult terrain. **Up From Below** Niesha can [Shove](/Actions.aspx?ID=2380) or [Trip](/Actions.aspx?ID=2382) a creature that's standing atop a Sarzari access pipe grate while she's directly beneath that creature. **Viscous Trap** A creature hit by the mezlan's ooze globule takes a –15-foot circumstance penalty to all Speeds for 1 minute. On a critical hit, a target standing on a solid surface also becomes [immobilized](/Conditions.aspx?ID=81), while a target [Flying](/Actions.aspx?ID=2312) via wings falls to the ground and becomes unable to Fly. A target can end all effects by [Escaping](/Actions.aspx?ID=2296) (DC 34) or spending a total of 3 Interact actions to free itself

**[Recall Knowledge - Humanoid](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=47)): DC 45 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 43 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 40 [Ordulf Bladecaller](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3377) **Source** [Prey for Death](/Sources.aspx?ID=231) pg. 35 **Perception** +28 **Languages** [Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1), [Jotun](/Languages.aspx?ID=8), [Skald](/Languages.aspx?ID=42) **Skills** [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=34) +25, [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) +29, [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=37) +24, [Fishing Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) +24, [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=40) +31, [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46) +28, [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=49) +28, [Warfare Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) +26 **Str** +5 **Dex** +1 **Con** +4 **Int** +0 **Wis** +4 **Cha** +5 **Items** _+2 greater resilient [greater cold-resistan](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2788)t [full plate](/Armor.aspx?ID=50)_, _+2 greater striking [animated](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2831) [greataxe](/Weapons.aspx?ID=376)_, _+2 greater striking greater [frost](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2839) [greatsword](/Weapons.aspx?ID=379)_, _[greater potions of flying](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2948)_ (3) --- **AC** 38 **Fort** +30 **Ref** +25 **Will** +28 **HP** 300 **Resistances** cold 10 **Battle Arrogance** Ordulf hasn't met a significant combat challenge in ages, and even when facing deadly foes like the PCs his arrogance can be used against him. If a PC successfully disarms, feints, frightens, or trips Ordulf, his arrogance gets the better of him and he grows sloppy in his tactics, reducing his AC to 34 until the start of his next turn. A PC can also attempt to issue a more debilitating insult to Ordulf, as detailed in Insulting Ordulf. **Gorum's Major Boon** ([healing](/Traits.aspx?ID=623)) When Ordulf is reduced to 0 Hit Points, Gorum feeds him the zeal of his Aesir, allowing Ordulf to draw upon his own life force to fight on and on without falling. He is healed to 150 Hit Points and becomes [doomed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=67) 1 (or increases his doomed condition by 1), causing his features to look progressively more gaunt and scarred. Once he reaches doomed 4, he dies. **[Reactive Strikes](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=48)**
--- **Speed** 25 feet **Melee** _greatsword_ +32 ([Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103), [versatile P](/Traits.aspx?ID=200)), **Damage** 3d12+11 slashing plus 1d6 cold **Melee** _greataxe_ +32 ([Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103), [Sweep](/Traits.aspx?ID=194)), **Damage** 3d12+11 slashing plus 1d6 [persistent bleed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29) **Battle Cry** **Frequency** once per day; **Trigger** Ordulf rolls initiative; **Effect** Ordulf attempts to [Demoralize](/Actions.aspx?ID=2395) an observed foe. **Cleaving Blow** Ordulf Strikes two adjacent creatures within his reach. Both attacks count against his multiple attack penalty, but do not increase his penalty until he has made both attacks. **Crushing Insult** ([Auditory](/Traits.aspx?ID=16), [Linguistic](/Traits.aspx?ID=101), [Mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=106)) **Frequency** once per round; **Effect** Ordulf issues a devastating and humiliating insult to a creature within 30 feet that he can see. Ordulf attempts an Intimidation check against the target's Will DC. That character is then temporarily immune to Crushing Insult for 24 hours. **Critical Success** The insult is distracting and humiliating; the target is [stupefied](/Conditions.aspx?ID=94) 1 and [off-guard](/Conditions.aspx?ID=58) for 1 minute.
**Success** The insult is distracting, but its effects pass quickly; the target is stupefied 1 and off-guard until the start of Ordulf’s next turn.
**Failure** The insult barely cuts, but is distracting enough that the target is off-guard until the end of Ordulf’s turn.
**Critical Failure** Ordulf’s attempted insult fails spectacularly, and the PC who he was attempting to insult can instantly insult him back, using Insult Ordulf as a free action. **Deadly Display** **Requirements** Ordulf is wielding a melee weapon; **Effect** Ordulf brandishes his weapon in a threatening display. He [Demoralizes](/Actions.aspx?ID=2395) all enemies within 30 feet, rolling once and comparing the result to each target's Will DC. **Whirlwind Strike** Ordulf Strikes each enemy within his reach. Each attack counts toward his multiple attack penalty, but do not increase his penalty until he has made all his attacks.

If a PC successfully disarms, feints, frightens, or trips Ordulf, his arrogance gets the better of him and he grows sloppy in his tactics, reducing his AC to 34 until the start of his next turn. A PC can also attempt to issue a more debilitating insult to Ordulf, as detailed in Insulting Ordulf. Gorum's Major Boon (healing) When Ordulf is reduced to 0 Hit Points, Gorum feeds him the zeal of his Aesir, allowing Ordulf to draw upon his own life force to fight on and on without falling. He is healed to 150 Hit Points and becomes doomed 1 (or increases his doomed condition by 1), causing his features to look progressively more gaunt and scarred. Once he reaches doomed 4, he dies. Reactive Strikes Reaction --- Speed 25 feet Melee Single Action greatsword +32 (Magical, versatile P), Damage 3d12+11 slashing plus 1d6 cold Melee Single Action greataxe +32 (Magical, Sweep), Damage 3d12+11 slashing plus 1d6 persistent bleed Battle Cry Reaction Frequency once per day; Trigger Ordulf rolls initiative; Effect Ordulf attempts to Demoralize an observed foe. Cleaving Blow Two Actions Ordulf Strikes two adjacent creatures within his reach. Both attacks count against his multiple attack penalty, but do not increase his penalty until he has made both attacks. Crushing Insult Single Action (Auditory, Linguistic, Mental) Frequency once per round; Effect Ordulf issues a devastating and humiliating insult to a creature within 30 feet that he can see. Ordulf attempts an Intimidation check against the target's Will DC. That character is then temporarily immune to Crushing Insult for 24 hours. Critical Success The insult is distracting and humiliating; the target is stupefied 1 and off-guard for 1 minute. Success The insult is distracting, but its effects pass quickly; the target is stupefied 1 and off-guard until the start of Ordulf’s next turn. Critical Failure Ordulf’s attempted insult fails spectacularly, and the PC who he was attempting to insult can instantly insult him back, using Insult Ordulf as a free action. Deadly Display Two Actions Requirements Ordulf is wielding a melee weapon; Effect Ordulf brandishes his weapon in a threatening display. He Demoralizes all enemies within 30 feet, rolling once and comparing the result to each target's Will DC. Whirlwind Strike Three Actions Ordulf Strikes each enemy within his reach. Each attack counts toward his multiple attack penalty, but do not increase his penalty until he has made all his attacks.
