features.Pulp Quintessence:
([Divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=48), [Teleportation](/Traits.aspx?ID=156)) The rift pulper rapidly chews on reality itself, gnawing open a short-lived rift into the liminal space between planes in any adjacent square. The rift pulper becomes [quickened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=89) for 1 round, and can use the extra action to Stride, [Fly](/Actions.aspx?ID=2312), or Strike. If another creature occupies the square in which the rift pulper Pulps Quintessence, it takes 18d6 bludgeoning damage as portions of its body are stretched and distorted painfully by the tear in reality (DC 38 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Fortitude save). The rift pulper can't Pulp Quintessence again for 1 minute.
This ability is more effective in the Outer Sphere, and when used on any of these planes, the rift pulper becomes quickened for 2 rounds, the DC to resist being damaged by the rift increases to DC 40, and the rift pulper can't use Pulp Quintessence again for 1d4 rounds.
features.Pulp Soul: <actions string="Single Action" /> ([Divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=48)) The rift pulper chews on the flesh of a creature [grabbed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=77) or [restrained](/Conditions.aspx?ID=90) by it, pulping the quintessence that makes up their soul. The creature takes 3d10+10 spirit damage (DC 38 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Will save). If the creature is a native to the outer sphere (such as a [celestial](/Languages.aspx?ID=16) or [fiend](/Traits.aspx?ID=600)) the damage increases to 3d12+12 spirit damage.
features.Pulper Venom: ([Poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=126)) **Saving Throw** DC 38 Fortitude; **Maximum Duration** 6 rounds; **Stage 1** [enfeebled 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=71) (1 round); **Stage 2** enfeebled 2 (1 round), **Stage 3** enfeebled 2 and [slowed 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=92) (1 round)
features.Wood Cyst: The rift pulper spends 1 minute digging into a Huge or larger tree or wooden object, then forms a cyst around itself. While inside the cyst, the rift pulper can only sense its surroundings via [tremorsense](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=82) and is [immobilized](/Conditions.aspx?ID=81) until the cyst is broken open. The cyst has AC 40, 50 HP, and shares the rift pulper's weaknesses. If the cyst is broken open by any means other than Burst Cyst, the rift pulper must succeed at a DC 40 Fortitude save or become [stunned 3](/Conditions.aspx?ID=93). While inside its cyst, the rift pulper has an automatic result of 49 on [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38) checks and DCs to pass as nothing more than a large bulge on the wooden surface.

description: The rift pulper chews away at the planar structure of reality, eating quintessence to build their hideous hives. These bulbous structures look like partially melted wasp hives with the appearance of distorted faces, arms, and legs pressing against the walls from within.

<title level="1" pfs="">[Shinigami](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2723)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

Even immortals such as [kami](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=243) aren't immune to death. When a kami or equally powerful entity refuses the call of the [Boneyard](/Planes.aspx?ID=15), a shinigami is summoned to bring these stubborn souls to heel. Exact and swift, shinigami are known to dispense the judgment of death efficiently and dispassionately.

<column gap="tiny">
**[Recall Knowledge - Monitor](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**
([Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=13)): DC 38

**[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 36

**[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 33
</column>

</column>

<column gap="medium">
<image src="/images/Monsters/Shinigami.png" />
</column>

</row>

<title level="2" right="Creature 17">[Shinigami](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2723)</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="LN" url="/Rules.aspx?ID=95" />
<trait label="Large" />
<trait label="Monitor" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=111" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #196: The Summer That Never Was](/Sources.aspx?ID=214) pg. 86

**Perception** +31; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=12), [_detect alignment_](/Spells.aspx?ID=65) (chaotic and lawful only), [_true seeing_](/Spells.aspx?ID=344)

**Languages**
[Celestial](/Languages.aspx?ID=16), [Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1), [Draconic](/Languages.aspx?ID=2), [Infernal](/Languages.aspx?ID=19), [Necril](/Languages.aspx?ID=20), [Requian](/Languages.aspx?ID=34), [Utopian](/Languages.aspx?ID=36); [_tongues_](/Spells.aspx?ID=340)

**Skills**
[Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=1) +31, [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=2) +30, [Boneyard Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8) +32, [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=6) +32, [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=7) +34, [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=11) +30, [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=13) +33, [Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=14) +30, [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15) +31

<row gap="medium">
**Str** +8

**Dex** +6

**Con** +7

**Int** +5

**Wis** +6

**Cha** +9
</row>

**Items**
_+2 [greater striking](/Equipment.aspx?ID=280) [axiomatic](/Equipment.aspx?ID=291) [naginata](/Weapons.aspx?ID=297)_, pouch of four gems

</column>

---

<column gap="tiny">

<row gap="medium">
**AC** 40 

**Fort** +32 

**Ref** +29 

**Will** +31 

+1 status to all saves vs. magic
</row>

<row gap="medium">
**HP** 260
([fast healing](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=15) 40)

</row>

**Immunities**
[death](/Traits.aspx?ID=40) effects, [disease](/Traits.aspx?ID=46), [negative](/Traits.aspx?ID=118)

**Resistances**
all physical 15 (except chaotic and silver), [cold](/Traits.aspx?ID=27) 15, [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=126) 15

**Weaknesses**
[silver](/Equipment.aspx?ID=379) 15

**[Frightful Presence](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=17)** ([aura](/Traits.aspx?ID=206), [emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=60), [fear](/Traits.aspx?ID=68), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=106)) 60 feet, DC 35.

</column>

---

<column gap="tiny">

**Speed** 25 feet, fly 30 feet

**Melee**
<actions string="Single Action" />
_naginata_ +33 ([deadly d8](/Traits.aspx?ID=174), [Reach](/Traits.aspx?ID=192), [versatile P](/Traits.aspx?ID=200)),
**Damage** 3d8+16 slashing plus 1d6 lawful and spirit touch

**Divine Innate Spells** DC 38
- **7th**
[Enervation](/Spells.aspx?ID=687) (×3), [Plane Shift](/Spells.aspx?ID=222)
- **8th**
[Finger of Death](/Spells.aspx?ID=116) (×3), [Scrying](/Spells.aspx?ID=268)
- **9th**
[Bind Soul](/Spells.aspx?ID=21) (×3)
- **Constant (9th)**
[Detect Alignment](/Spells.aspx?ID=65) (chaotic and lawful only), [Tongues](/Spells.aspx?ID=340), [True Seeing](/Spells.aspx?ID=344)

**[Change Shape](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=8)** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([Concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32), [Divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=48), [Polymorph](/Traits.aspx?ID=127), [Transmutation](/Traits.aspx?ID=157)) The shinigami takes on the appearance of a specific Small or Medium [humanoid](/Traits.aspx?ID=91) creature. This doesn't change their statistics, other than to remove the [reach](/Traits.aspx?ID=192) trait from their Strikes. The shinigami's human shape is unique to the shinigami and can't be used to [Impersonate](/Actions.aspx?ID=46) a creature.

**Pouch of Four Gems**   Each shinigami carries a pouch containing four black sapphires for use with [_bind soul_](/Spells.aspx?ID=21). Each gem is capable of holding a soul of a maximum level equal to that of the shinigami. If the shinigami dies, the gems are destroyed as well, and any souls they contain are released harmlessly to travel to the [Boneyard](/Planes.aspx?ID=15).

**Release Soul** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([Manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104), [Necromancy](/Traits.aspx?ID=117)) **Requirements** One of the gems in the shinigami's pouch contains a soul from bind soul; **Effect** The shinigami crushes the gem, sending the soul to the [Boneyard](/Planes.aspx?ID=15) while releasing a wave of necromantic energy. All creatures within a 30-foot emanation take 18d6 damage (DC 38 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Fortitude save); the shinigami chooses whether this damage is positive damage or negative damage. A creature who takes damage from this effect and fails the saving throw is also [sickened 2](/Conditions.aspx?ID=34) and [drained 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=10) (or sickened 4 and drained 2 on a critical failure).

**Spirit Touch**   A shinigami's Strikes can affect [incorporeal](/Traits.aspx?ID=222) creatures with the effect of a [_ghost touch_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=297) property rune.

</column>

A swamp blight appears as a quivering blob of rancid brown and green mud from which dozens of hateful red eyes peer. **[Recall Knowledge - Ooze](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=44)): DC 41 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 39 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 36 [Swamp Blight](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3782) **Source** [Pathfinder #211: The Secret of Deathstalk Tower](/Sources.aspx?ID=254) pg. 84 **Perception** +29; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59) **Languages** [Aklo](/Languages.aspx?ID=13), [Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1), [Fey](/Languages.aspx?ID=119); [telepathy](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=79) (within cursed domain) **Skills** [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=34) +32, [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) +33, [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38) +30, [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=40) +30, [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43) +29, [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=48) +32, [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=49) +27, [Swamp Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) +29 **Str** +8 **Dex** +7 **Con** +8 **Int** +4 **Wis** +4 **Cha** +5 --- **AC** 38 **Fort** +33 **Ref** +26 **Will** +29 **HP** 300 ([fast healing](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=62) 30, rejuvenation) **Immunities** [acid](/Traits.aspx?ID=524), bleed, critical hits, precision **Mosquito Aura** ([aura](/Traits.aspx?ID=542), [primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=676)) 30 feet. Mosquitoes surround the blight. The mosquitoes ignore creatures the blight designates as allies as well as any who are at full HP. All other creatures who enter the aura or begin their turn within it take 2d6 persistent bleed damage with a DC 35 Fortitude save.
**Critical Success** The creature takes no damage.
**Success** The creature takes half damage.

The unholy terror known as the thruneosaurus rex is not a natural beast. They were created by Chelaxian diabolists who sought to combine the ferocity of dinosaurs with the power of [Hell](/Planes.aspx?ID=42), infusing a clutch of [tyrannosaurus](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2923) rex eggs from Mediogalti Island with [devil](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=389) ichor and naming the monstrous hatchlings after their patrons. Although few records and fewer survivors tell exactly how the experiment went awry, the experimental subjects escaped, and their descendants are now most often sighted in the Whisperwood in eastern Cheliax. **[Recall Knowledge - Beast](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35), [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43)): DC 41 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 39 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 36 [Thruneosaurus Rex](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3266) **Source** [Howl of the Wild](/Sources.aspx?ID=226) pg. 139 2.1 **Perception** +29; [greater darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59), [scent](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=74) ([imprecise](/Rules.aspx?ID=412)) 30 feet **Languages** [Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1), [Diabolic](/Languages.aspx?ID=117); (can't speak any language) **Skills** [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=34) +30, [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) +35, [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=40) +30 **Str** +10 **Dex** +3 **Con** +6 **Int** -2 **Wis** +6 **Cha** +5 --- **AC** 39 **Fort** +31 **Ref** +25 **Will** +29 **HP** 290 **Immunities** [fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=604) **Resistances** physical 15 (except [silver](/Equipment.aspx?ID=379)) **Weaknesses** [holy](/Traits.aspx?ID=517) 15 **[Frightful Presence](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=64)** ([aura](/Traits.aspx?ID=542), [divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=579), [emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=590), [fear](/Traits.aspx?ID=598), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647)) 90 feet, DC 38
**Instinctive Teleportation** ([divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=579), [teleportation](/Traits.aspx?ID=710)) **Trigger** The thruneosaurus takes damage from a [holy](/Traits.aspx?ID=517) effect; **Effect** The thruneosaurus teleports to an open space within 60 feet it can see, along with any creatures it has swallowed whole. --- **Speed** 40 feet **Melee** jaws +33 ([Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103), [reach 20 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)), **Damage** 3d12+16 piercing plus [Grab](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=45) **Melee** foot +33 ([Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103), [reach 15 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)), **Damage** 3d10+16 bludgeoning **Hellfire Blast** The thruneosaurus channels sulfurous hellfire in one of three ways. The thruneosaurus chooses the effect, but it can't make the same choice in two consecutive rounds.
  • **Blistering Sun** ([divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=579), [fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=604), [unholy](/Traits.aspx?ID=521)); The thruneosaurus ignites an orb of hellfire between its horns that radiates heat in a 30-foot emanation, dealing 2d8 [persistent fire damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29).
  • **Choking Fumes** ([divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=579), [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=669), [unholy](/Traits.aspx?ID=521)); The thruneosaurus exhales a 60-foot cone of sulfurous smoke that deals 6d8 poison damage (DC 38 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Fortitude save). Creatures that fail their saves are [sickened 2](/Conditions.aspx?ID=91).
  • **Fiery Beam** ([divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=579), [fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=604), [unholy](/Traits.aspx?ID=521)); A 120-foot line of hellish flame erupts from the thruneosaurus's eyes, dealing 6d10 fire damage (DC 38 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save).
**[Swallow Whole](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=77)** ([Attack](/Traits.aspx?ID=15)) Huge, 3d12+10 bludgeoning, Rupture 40 **[Trample](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=81)** Huge or smaller, foot, DC 38

While [valkyries](/Monsters.aspx?ID=1355) tend to travel alone or in small groups of two or three, they won't hesitate to rely on the old adage of “strength in numbers.” **[Recall Knowledge - Monitor](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46)): DC 41 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 39 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 36 [Valkyrie Tempest](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3397) **Source** [Prey for Death](/Sources.aspx?ID=231) pg. 119 **Perception** +28; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59) **Languages** [Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1), [Jotun](/Languages.aspx?ID=8); ravenspeaker, [_truespeech_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1728) **Skills** [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=34) +29, [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) +30, [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39) +29, [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=40) +29, [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46) +28 **Str** +9 **Dex** +6 **Con** +6 **Int** +4 **Wis** +5 **Cha** +6 --- **AC** 37 **Fort** +24 **Ref** +20 **Will** +23 **HP** 312 **Resistances** [electricity](/Traits.aspx?ID=586) 15 **Weaknesses** area damage 19, [splash](/Traits.aspx?ID=699) damage 10 **[Troop Defenses](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=44)** --- **Speed** 25 feet, fly 60 feet **Divine Innate Spells** DC 35 - **6th** [Blessed Boundary](/Spells.aspx?ID=1452), [Divine Wrath](/Spells.aspx?ID=86), [Weapon Storm](/Spells.aspx?ID=373) - **7th** [Interplanar Teleport](/Spells.aspx?ID=1576) (troop and mounts only) - **Constant (5th)** [Truespeech](/Spells.aspx?ID=1728) **Bolster the Wounded** ([Divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=48), [Healing](/Traits.aspx?ID=89)) **Trigger** The tempest ends its turn and is not at maximum HP; **Effect** The tempest restores 5d10 HP. This healing can't increase a tempest's Hit Points beyond the maximum of its current Hit Point threshold. **[Form Up](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=43)** **Troop Movement** Whenever the troop Strides or [Flies](/Actions.aspx?ID=2312), they first Form Up as a free action into a 20-foot-by-20-foot area (minus any missing squares), then move up to their Speed. This works just like a Gargantuan creature moving; for instance, if any square of the troop enters difficult terrain, the extra movement cost applies to the whole troop. **Troop Spellcasting** When the tempest Casts a Spell, its members combine their efforts into casting a more powerful version of the spell. When Casting a Spell that has an area of a burst, cone, or line and doesn't have a duration, increase the area of that spell. Add 5 feet to the radius of a burst that normally has a radius of at least 10 feet (a burst with a smaller radius is not affected). Add 5 feet to the length of a cone or line that is normally 15 feet long or smaller, and add 10 feet to the length of a larger cone or line. **Rain of Spears** **Frequency** once per round; **Effect** The tempest attacks with their electrified spears, targeting all adjacent enemies (DC 38 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save). The damage depends on the number of actions.
1d6+10 piercing damage plus 1d12 electricity
2d6+10 piercing damage plus 2d12 electricity
3d6+10 piercing damage plus 3d12 electricity **Tempest of Battle** ([Divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=48), [Electricity](/Traits.aspx?ID=56)) **Frequency** once per day; **Effect** The tempest calls down a massive lightning storm in a 60-foot emanation. Spears of lightning rain down upon enemies in the area, dealing 10d12 electricity damage (DC 38 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save).

The powerful adamantine dragons are one of several dragons known as skymetal dragons. The innate magic that flows through these dragons causes them to draw particular metals to their bodies like magnets or, in some cases, naturally grow these skymetals on their bodies. Adamantine dragons begin their lives with tough scales that are naturally replaced with thicker and even tougher adamantine plating as they grow older. Adamantine dragons are typically steadfast and loyal. Mirage dragons are masters of illusion magic and use their powers to deceive others and further their own agendas. In addition to their magical prowess, mirage dragons possess a number of additional features to help them on hunts or mislead attackers, such as their camouflaging scales and a hallucinatory breath that can confound multiple foes at once. Mirage dragons are vain and egotistical figures. The truth of life in the [Universe](/Planes.aspx?ID=1) is that weather controls the world. The life-giving water that flows across Golarion, the maintenance of healthy forests, and the snows, thaws, and rains that help crops flourish all rely on the weather—weather that's shaped at the whims of the winds. Anemoi are powerful beings from the [Plane of Air](/Planes.aspx?ID=4) tasked by ancient gods to guard the skies and shepherd the winds of every world across the planes. They guide the winds along their natural paths, and while neither malevolent nor malicious, an anemos has little regard for how a storm might affect any creature caught in its path. Anemoi can take several forms and shift between them as easily as they slip between the breezes. They wear humanoid guises to walk among mortals without drawing undue attention, and they transform into great, thunderous horses made of storm clouds and rain when they need to move quickly across the skies. Their true form, however, is wind coalesced into a humanoid shape, often with curling hair and feathery wings made of soft, drifting clouds. On Golarion, each of the four cardinal winds are created and directed by a quartet of cardinal anemoi. The cold north winds are guided by Boreal, bringer of winter. Austral shepherds hot winds from the south. Eural brings stormy winds from the east. Finally, the gentle winds of spring come at the call of Zephyr, from the west. These four cardinal anemoi, alongside their councils of lesser anemoi, shape and control the winds across all of Golarion. As far as anyone can tell, the cardinal anemoi don't answer to a greater authority. There are even more powerful maximal anemoi living in the Plane of Air, but they seem content to leave the Universe out of their plans. Though the cardinal anemoi try to keep a degree of separation from mortal affairs, lesser anemoi occasionally take a closer interest. Some monitor a single settlement or county, protecting, nourishing, or even vindictively destroying it. Each one has their own sets of interests. Many are vain or petty. Even more change attitudes just as quickly as the winds they guide. Pleasing an anemoi isn't a matter of following a set formula, but rather repeatedly changing course to give them what they desire for their mercurial current interests or perceived needs. **[Recall Knowledge - Elemental](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=2), [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=10)): DC 43 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 41 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 38 [Anemos](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2614) **Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 78 2.0 **Perception** +33; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=12) **Languages** [Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1), [Empyrean](/Languages.aspx?ID=115), [Sussuran](/Languages.aspx?ID=111); truespeech **Skills** [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=1) +38, [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=2) +31, [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=10) +33, [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=11) +31, [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=12) +38, [Planar Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8) +33, [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=13) +31, [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15) +36, [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=16) +33 **Str** +4 **Dex** +9 **Con** +7 **Int** +6 **Wis** +6 **Cha** +9 **Truespeech** An anemos can speak with and understand any creature that has a language.
**Wind Orchestra** ([air](/Traits.aspx?ID=5), [auditory](/Traits.aspx?ID=16)) An anemos does not require [instruments](/Equipment.aspx?ID=37) to perform music, instead using their winds to create and carry the sounds of any instruments they wish to duplicate. They can mimic any number of instruments simultaneously, creating and directing their own personal orchestra. --- **AC** 43 **Fort** +29 **Ref** +33 **Will** +30 **HP** 310 , regeneration 15 (deactivated by earthbane) **Immunities** bleed, [electricity](/Traits.aspx?ID=56), [paralyzed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=28), [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=126), [sleep](/Traits.aspx?ID=145) **Resistances** [cold](/Traits.aspx?ID=27) 20 **Blessed by the Winds** ([air](/Traits.aspx?ID=5), [aura](/Traits.aspx?ID=206)) 80 feet. The winds grow turbulent for those who would dare to fly in the same space as an anemos, but they take care to never harm or inconvenience their shepherd. Air within the emanation is [difficult terrain](/Rules.aspx?ID=453) for [Flying](/Actions.aspx?ID=94) creatures that do not have the [air](/Traits.aspx?ID=5) trait. While the aura is active, the anemos cannot be affected by environmental air or weather affects unless they choose to be.
**Earthbane** An anemos's regeneration is suppressed for 1 round if the anemos is affected by an [earth](/Traits.aspx?ID=55) effect, or for as long as they are in contact with the ground and 1 round thereafter. If an anemos is submerged in at least 1 inch of mud, dirt, or stone, the anemos's aura deactivates, and the anemos becomes [stunned 2](/Conditions.aspx?ID=36) and [clumsy 2](/Conditions.aspx?ID=3).
**Redirect Weather** ([divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=48)) **Requirements** The anemos's aura is active; **Trigger** A creature within the anemos's aura uses an [air](/Traits.aspx?ID=5) or [electricity](/Traits.aspx?ID=56) spell, or an air or electricity spell otherwise comes into effect within the anemos's aura; **Effect** The winds and weather of the spell obey the anemos's call. The anemos makes all the choices to determine the targets, destination, or other effects of the spell, as though they were the caster. --- **Speed** 25 feet, fly 200 feet; swiftness **Melee** thunderbolt +35 ([Electricity](/Traits.aspx?ID=56), [Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103)), **Damage** 3d8+12 electricity plus 3d6 sonic **Ranged** air blast +35 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [Air](/Traits.aspx?ID=5), [Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103), [range 100 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=248)), **Damage** 3d10+12 bludgeoning **Ranged** thunderbolt +35 ([Electricity](/Traits.aspx?ID=56), [Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103), [thrown 30 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=195)), **Damage** 3d8+10 electricity plus 3d6 sonic **Divine Innate Spells** DC 40 - **1st** [Air Bubble](/Spells.aspx?ID=5) (at will) - **4th** [Airlift](/Spells.aspx?ID=1303) (at will), [Gaseous Form](/Spells.aspx?ID=129) (at will), [Voice on the Breeze](/Spells.aspx?ID=1325) (at will) - **7th** [Humanoid Form](/Spells.aspx?ID=153) (at will) - **9th** [Cleanse Air](/Spells.aspx?ID=1313) **Divine Rituals** DC 40 - **6th** [Sky Signs](/Rituals.aspx?ID=102) - **8th** [Control Weather](/Rituals.aspx?ID=9) **Collect Thunder** ([Electricity](/Traits.aspx?ID=56), [Manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104)) **Requirements** The anemos has a hand free; **Effect** The anemos runs a hand through the winds that swirl around them, the sparks from their fingertips coalescing into a thunderbolt. The anemos creates a thunderbolt in their open hand. If the anemos spends an action to Collect Thunder, a bolt instead strikes their open hand, creating a booming peal that deafens all creatures within 20 feet for 1 round unless they succeed at a DC 40 Fortitude save; this adds the [auditory](/Traits.aspx?ID=16) trait to Collect Thunder. Any thunderbolts dissipate after 1 round. **Command the Breeze** When an anemos casts a ritual, they perform all aspects of the ritual themself, commanding their winds to complete all the ritual's components. They must fulfill any requirements for the ritual's additional casters and must attempt the checks normally performed by additional casters. In addition, anemoi can cast rituals faster than usual. If a ritual has a casting time measured in days, they can cast it in an equal number of hours. **Storm Strikes Twice** ([Air](/Traits.aspx?ID=5), [Teleportation](/Traits.aspx?ID=156)) The anemos throws a thunderbolt, then becomes a wind that carries them in an instant to the bolt's location to attack again. They make a ranged thunderbolt Strike against a creature within their first range increment, teleport to the creature's location as a gust of wind, then grasp the thrown thunderbolt and make a melee thunderbolt Strike against a creature within reach. Their multiple attack penalty doesn't increase until they've made both attacks. **Swiftness** The anemos's movement doesn't trigger reactions.

Anemoi are powerful beings from the Plane of Air tasked by ancient gods to guard the skies and shepherd the winds of every world across the planes. They guide the winds along their natural paths, and while neither malevolent nor malicious, an anemos has little regard for how a storm might affect any creature caught in its path. Anemoi can take several forms and shift between them as easily as they slip between the breezes. They wear humanoid guises to walk among mortals without drawing undue attention, and they transform into great, thunderous horses made of storm clouds and rain when they need to move quickly across the skies. Their true form, however, is wind coalesced into a humanoid shape, often with curling hair and feathery wings made of soft, drifting clouds. On Golarion, each of the four cardinal winds are created and directed by a quartet of cardinal anemoi. The cold north winds are guided by Boreal, bringer of winter. Austral shepherds hot winds from the south. Eural brings stormy winds from the east. Finally, the gentle winds of spring come at the call of Zephyr, from the west. These four cardinal anemoi, alongside their councils of lesser anemoi, shape and control the winds across all of Golarion. As far as anyone can tell, the cardinal anemoi don't answer to a greater authority. There are even more powerful maximal anemoi living in the Plane of Air, but they seem content to leave the Universe out of their plans. Though the cardinal anemoi try to keep a degree of separation from mortal affairs, lesser anemoi occasionally take a closer interest. Some monitor a single settlement or county, protecting, nourishing, or even vindictively destroying it. Each one has their own sets of interests. Many are vain or petty. Even more change attitudes just as quickly as the winds they guide. Pleasing an anemoi isn't a matter of following a set formula, but rather repeatedly changing course to give them what they desire for their mercurial current interests or perceived needs. Wind Orchestra (air, auditory) An anemos does not require instruments to perform music, instead using their winds to create and carry the sounds of any instruments they wish to duplicate. They can mimic any number of instruments simultaneously, creating and directing their own personal orchestra. --- AC 43 Fort +29 Ref +33 Will +30 HP 310 , regeneration 15 (deactivated by earthbane) Immunities bleed, electricity, paralyzed, poison, sleep Resistances cold 20 Blessed by the Winds (air, aura) 80 feet. The winds grow turbulent for those who would dare to fly in the same space as an anemos, but they take care to never harm or inconvenience their shepherd. Air within the emanation is difficult terrain for Flying creatures that do not have the air trait. While the aura is active, the anemos cannot be affected by environmental air or weather affects unless they choose to be. Earthbane An anemos's regeneration is suppressed for 1 round if the anemos is affected by an earth effect, or for as long as they are in contact with the ground and 1 round thereafter. If an anemos is submerged in at least 1 inch of mud, dirt, or stone, the anemos's aura deactivates, and the anemos becomes stunned 2 and clumsy 2. Redirect Weather Reaction (divine) Requirements The anemos's aura is active; Trigger A creature within the anemos's aura uses an air or electricity spell, or an air or electricity spell otherwise comes into effect within the anemos's aura; Effect The winds and weather of the spell obey the anemos's call. The anemos makes all the choices to determine the targets, destination, or other effects of the spell, as though they were the caster. --- Speed 25 feet, fly 200 feet; swiftness Melee Single Action thunderbolt +35 (Electricity, Magical), Damage 3d8+12 electricity plus 3d6 sonic Ranged Single Action air blast +35 (Agile, Air, Magical, range 100 feet), Damage 3d10+12 bludgeoning Ranged Single Action thunderbolt +35 (Electricity, Magical, thrown 30 feet), Damage 3d8+10 electricity plus 3d6 sonic Divine Innate Spells DC 40 - 1st Air Bubble (at will) - 4th Airlift (at will), Gaseous Form (at will), Voice on the Breeze (at will) - 7th Humanoid Form (at will) - 9th Cleanse Air Divine Rituals DC 40 - 6th Sky Signs - 8th Control Weather Collect Thunder Free Action or One Action (Electricity, Manipulate) Requirements The anemos has a hand free; Effect The anemos runs a hand through the winds that swirl around them, the sparks from their fingertips coalescing into a thunderbolt. The anemos creates a thunderbolt in their open hand. If the anemos spends an action to Collect Thunder, a bolt instead strikes their open hand, creating a booming peal that deafens all creatures within 20 feet for 1 round unless they succeed at a DC 40 Fortitude save; this adds the auditory trait to Collect Thunder. Any thunderbolts dissipate after 1 round. Command the Breeze When an anemos casts a ritual, they perform all aspects of the ritual themself, commanding their winds to complete all the ritual's components. They must fulfill any requirements for the ritual's additional casters and must attempt the checks normally performed by additional casters. In addition, anemoi can cast rituals faster than usual. If a ritual has a casting time measured in days, they can cast it in an equal number of hours. Storm Strikes Twice Two Actions (Air, Teleportation) The anemos throws a thunderbolt, then becomes a wind that carries them in an instant to the bolt's location to attack again. They make a ranged thunderbolt Strike against a creature within their first range increment, teleport to the creature's location as a gust of wind, then grasp the thrown thunderbolt and make a melee thunderbolt Strike against a creature within reach. Their multiple attack penalty doesn't increase until they've made both attacks. Swiftness The anemos's movement doesn't trigger reactions. The Cardinal Anemoi Anemoi who are particularly ancient and powerful often have their own unique capabilities. In addition to their standard abilities, Golarion's cardinal anemoi possess the following additional innate spells. Austral , the south wind: 8th flame vortex ; 5th geyser Boreal , the north wind: 8th frigid flurry ; 5th howling blizzard Eural , the east wind: 8th chain lightning ; 5th pressure zone Zephyr , the west wind: 8th field of life ; 4th petal storm , speak with plants The Shape of the Air Anemoi on the Plane of Air are typically genderless, while those who spend time in the Universe sometimes experiment with or develop preferences for one of the genders of the mortals they watch or live close to.

Aolazes are great beasts carved from stone and metal and magically imbued with the essence of life. The exact means of their creation is a long-lost secret, and they are so rare that scholars have little opportunity to study active specimens. The best-known aolazes are museum pieces or battlefield relics destroyed or deactivated centuries ago, though fragmented records suggest that many more were made and might remain, yet to be unearthed. Most aolazes are built in the shape of great land-bound beasts, such as [elephants](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=413), [rhinoceroses](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=464), or [dinosaurs](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=391). Regardless of the specific creature an aolaz has been constructed to resemble, it is not bound to walk the earth like its inspirations are—it's imbued with the magical ability to pursue across water and even through the air. Few can escape an aolaz's wrath once it is earned. **[Recall Knowledge - Construct](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35), [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=37)): DC 43 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 41 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 38 [Aolaz](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2826) **Source** [Monster Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=221) pg. 22 1.1 **Perception** +33; [low-light vision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=69), flawless hearing **Languages** **Skills** [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) +35 **Str** +9 **Dex** +4 **Con** +8 **Int** -4 **Wis** +6 **Cha** +3 **Flawless Hearing** An aolaz has an incredible sense of hearing. It can hear any sound made within 1,000 feet as though it were only 5 feet away from the source of the sound, and any sound within 1 mile as though it were only 30 feet away from the source of the sound. An aolaz's hearing is a [precise](/Rules.aspx?ID=411) sense. --- **AC** 42 **Fort** +35 **Ref** +27 **Will** +31 **HP** 255 **Immunities** bleed, [death](/Traits.aspx?ID=571) effects, [disease](/Traits.aspx?ID=578), [doomed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=67), [drained](/Conditions.aspx?ID=68), [fatigued](/Conditions.aspx?ID=73), [healing](/Traits.aspx?ID=623), [nonlethal](/Traits.aspx?ID=661) attacks, [paralyzed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=85), [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=669), [sickened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=91), [sonic](/Traits.aspx?ID=697), [spirit](/Traits.aspx?ID=737), [unconscious](/Conditions.aspx?ID=95), [vitality](/Traits.aspx?ID=509), [void](/Traits.aspx?ID=510) **Resistances** physical 15 (except [adamantine](/Equipment.aspx?ID=374)) --- **Speed** 50 feet, [_fly_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1534), [_water walk_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1756) **Melee** trunk +35 ([Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103), [reach 20 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192), [Sweep](/Traits.aspx?ID=194), [Trip](/Traits.aspx?ID=196)), **Damage** 5d10+17 bludgeoning plus [Grab](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=45) **Melee** foot +33 ([Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103), [reach 10 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)), **Damage** 5d8+15 bludgeoning **Arcane Innate Spells** DC 40 - **Constant (9th)** [Fly](/Spells.aspx?ID=125), [Water Walk](/Spells.aspx?ID=371) **Roll** The aolaz tucks its head down and rolls up into an armored sphere. While Rolling, an aolaz has AC 44, Fort +37, Ref +29, Will +33, and Speed 100 feet, but it can't use its trunk Strikes or its Ultrasonic Blast. It can make foot Strikes while rolling, but only as part of a Trample. The aolaz can use this action again to unroll and resume its standing form. **[Trample](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=81)** Huge or smaller, foot, DC 40 **Ultrasonic Blast** ([Arcane](/Traits.aspx?ID=11), [Sonic](/Traits.aspx?ID=147)) The aolaz releases a tremendous blast of sonic energy from its trunk in a 150-foot line, dealing 12d10 sonic damage. The frequency of this sound is such that it is completely imperceptible to humanoids, but the damage it wreaks is all too evident. Each creature in the area must attempt a DC 40 Fortitude save. The aolaz can't use Ultrasonic Blast again for 1d4 rounds.
**Critical Success** The creature is unaffected.
**Success** The creature takes half damage and is [stunned 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=93).
**Failure** The creature takes full damage and is stunned 2.
**Critical Failure** The creature takes double damage and is stunned 3.

The exact means of their creation is a long-lost secret, and they are so rare that scholars have little opportunity to study active specimens. The best-known aolazes are museum pieces or battlefield relics destroyed or deactivated centuries ago, though fragmented records suggest that many more were made and might remain, yet to be unearthed.

 Most aolazes are built in the shape of great land-bound beasts, such as [elephants](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=413), [rhinoceroses](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=464), or [dinosaurs](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=391). Regardless of the specific creature an aolaz has been constructed to resemble, it is not bound to walk the earth like its inspirations are—it's imbued with the magical ability to pursue across water and even through the air. Few can escape an aolaz's wrath once it is earned.

<title level="1" pfs="">[Barded Manticore](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3300)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

Barded manticores are treacherous and dangerous beasts, and the only known member of the manticore species with the innate ability to cast spells. Luckily, these creatures are incredibly rare, mostly found near battlefields and other sources of worked metal, though stories tell of a particularly clever barded manticore attempting to make herself a home deep under the Magaambya.

 Unlike the other members of the species, a barded manticore has a face that resembles a human's and a torso coated in scales of varying metals, the exact composition depending on their diet. Thanks to these materials, most barded manticores are able to fend off just about any being attempting to encroach upon their territories, especially fiends and other creatures with weaknesses to specific metals. Barded manticores sift through metals obtained from their victims, whether that be local villagers coerced into giving them tribute or unlucky travelers, and seek the rarest, most valuable types to make part of their next meals.

 This also includes armor and weapons inscribed with runes that grant a barded manticore the ability to cast spells, though these spells vary depending on the region the beast inhabits and what type of runes they consume. In rare areas where magic is suppressed, a barded manticore will be unable to grow their runed scales, rendering them less powerful than others of their kind. Pointing this out to such a barded manticore often ends in one's untimely demise at the manticore's claws and spines, no less sharp for the lack of enchantments.

These benefits last until the beginning of the manticore's next turn or they use Arrange Scales again.

**Metallic Coating**   A barded manticore's [unarmed](/Traits.aspx?ID=719) attacks (including spikes) count as [adamantine](/Equipment.aspx?ID=372), [cold iron](/Equipment.aspx?ID=375), [dawnsilver](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2857), and [silver](/Equipment.aspx?ID=379).

**Paired Spikes** <actions string="Single Action" />  The barded manticore flings two spikes from their tail, targeting up to two creatures within 20 feet of each other. They make a separate ranged Strike against each creature, which counts as a single Strike for the barded manticore's multiple attack penalty, and the penalty doesn't increase until they've made both Strikes. If the manticore targeted only one creature and hits, that creature takes normal damage for a single spike, but also gains weakness 15 to electricity damage until the spikes are removed with an Interact action.

Palinthanos formed from intelligent creatures tend to be scheming and envious opportunists who seek to possess mortal bodies. They appear as vortexes of twisted, misty faces from which ghostly limbs emerge, regardless of their appearance in life. **[Recall Knowledge - Undead](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46)): DC 43 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 41 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 38 [Echosyvne](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3750) **Source** [Pathfinder #206: Bring the House Down](/Sources.aspx?ID=247) pg. 87 **Perception** +31; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59) **Languages** [Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1), [Necril](/Languages.aspx?ID=20) **Skills** [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=34) +35, [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38) +32 **Str** -5 **Dex** +9 **Con** +0 **Int** +6 **Wis** +5 **Cha** +6 --- **AC** 39 **Fort** +24 **Ref** +33 **Will** +31 **HP** 255 ([void healing](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=83)) **Immunities** [death](/Traits.aspx?ID=571) effects, [disease](/Traits.aspx?ID=578), [paralyzed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=85), [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=669), precision, [unconscious](/Conditions.aspx?ID=95) **Resistances** all damage 15 (except [force](/Traits.aspx?ID=610), [ghost touch](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2840), or [vitality](/Traits.aspx?ID=509); double resistance vs. non-[magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=644)) **Reaction Reversal** Since an egarhowl appears to move backwards in time and the results of its actions manifest slightly out of sync, its [manipulate](/Actions.aspx?ID=2229) or [move](/Traits.aspx?ID=658) actions and Strikes don't trigger reactions normally. Whenever a reaction would be triggered by an egarhowl in this way, the reacting creature must attempt a DC 11 flat check. On a failure, their reaction does not trigger.
**Predestined Defeat** ([occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=662)) **Trigger** The egarhowl rolls initiative; **Frequency** once per day; **Effect** At the start of combat, an inverted, reversed explosion of spiritual and void energy implodes in a 30-foot emanation centered on the egarhowl—a reversal of the creature's spiritually explosive death. All creatures in the area take 15d8 spirit damage (DC 37 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Fortitude save); creatures that fail this save are also [slowed 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=92) for 1 round as time seems to distort around them. --- **Speed** fly 30 feet **Melee** claw +33 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [Finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=179), [Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103)), **Damage** 3d6+8 slashing plus 3d6 spirit **Occult Innate Spells** DC 40 - **9th** [Possession](/Spells.aspx?ID=225) (×3) **Distort Perception** ([Incapacitation](/Traits.aspx?ID=93), [Mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=106), [Occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=120)) **Frequency** once per round; **Effect** The echopsyvne targets a creature it can see within 30 feet and alters its perception of time. The target must attempt a DC 40 Will save. Regardless of success or failure, the creature then becomes temporarily immune to this ability for 24 hours.
**Critical Success** The creature is unaffected.
**Success** The creature perceives time to flow backward briefly and becomes [slowed 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=92) for 1 round.
**Failure** Time flows backward for the creature, leaving them unable to interact with the world around them. The creature is [stunned 3](/Conditions.aspx?ID=93), after which it is slowed 1 for 1 round.
**Critical Failure** The creature's mind becomes stuck in a time loop, and it becomes [paralyzed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=85) by the disorienting sight for 1 minute. At the end of each of its turns, it can attempt a new Will save to reduce the remaining duration by 1 round or end it entirely on a critical success. **Temporal Possession** When the echopsyvne casts [_possession_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1638) on a creature, that creature experiences time backward. When the echopsyvne controls the target, they function normally, but when the target takes their own actions while the echopsyvne is in partial control or riding along in their body, they become [clumsy 3](/Conditions.aspx?ID=61) and take a –10-foot status penalty to all of their Speeds. When the echopsyvne stops possessing the target, willingly or otherwise, the target must succeed at a DC 37 Will save or be [stunned 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=93) as they readjust to a more familiar flow of time.

text: Echosyvne Palinthanos formed from intelligent creatures tend to be scheming and envious opportunists who seek to possess mortal bodies. They appear as vortexes of twisted, misty faces from which ghostly limbs emerge, regardless of their appearance in life. Recall Knowledge - Undead (Religion): DC 43 Unspecific Lore : DC 41 Specific Lore : DC 38 Echosyvne Source Pathfinder #206: Bring the House Down pg. 87 Perception +31; darkvision Languages Common, Necril Skills Acrobatics +35, Deception +32 Str -5 Dex +9 Con +0 Int +6 Wis +5 Cha +6 --- AC 39 Fort +24 Ref +33 Will +31 HP 255 (void healing) Immunities death effects, disease, paralyzed, poison, precision, unconscious Resistances all damage 15 (except force, ghost touch, or vitality; double resistance vs. non-magical) Reaction Reversal Since an egarhowl appears to move backwards in time and the results of its actions manifest slightly out of sync, its manipulate or move actions and Strikes don't trigger reactions normally. Whenever a reaction would be triggered by an egarhowl in this way, the reacting creature must attempt a DC 11 flat check. On a failure, their reaction does not trigger. Predestined Defeat Reaction (occult) Trigger The egarhowl rolls initiative; Frequency once per day; Effect At the start of combat, an inverted, reversed explosion of spiritual and void energy implodes in a 30-foot emanation centered on the egarhowl—a reversal of the creature's spiritually explosive death. All creatures in the area take 15d8 spirit damage (DC 37 basic Fortitude save); creatures that fail this save are also slowed 1 for 1 round as time seems to distort around them. --- Speed fly 30 feet Melee Single Action claw +33 (Agile, Finesse, Magical), Damage 3d6+8 slashing plus 3d6 spirit Occult Innate Spells DC 40 - 9th Possession (×3) Distort Perception Single Action (Incapacitation, Mental, Occult) Frequency once per round; Effect The echopsyvne targets a creature it can see within 30 feet and alters its perception of time. The target must attempt a DC 40 Will save. Regardless of success or failure, the creature then becomes temporarily immune to this ability for 24 hours. Critical Success The creature is unaffected. Success The creature perceives time to flow backward briefly and becomes slowed 1 for 1 round. Failure Time flows backward for the creature, leaving them unable to interact with the world around them. The creature is stunned 3, after which it is slowed 1 for 1 round. Critical Failure The creature's mind becomes stuck in a time loop, and it becomes paralyzed by the disorienting sight for 1 minute. At the end of each of its turns, it can attempt a new Will save to reduce the remaining duration by 1 round or end it entirely on a critical success. Temporal Possession When the echopsyvne casts possession on a creature, that creature experiences time backward. When the echopsyvne controls the target, they function normally, but when the target takes their own actions while the echopsyvne is in partial control or riding along in their body, they become clumsy 3 and take a –10-foot status penalty to all of their Speeds. When the echopsyvne stops possessing the target, willingly or otherwise, the target must succeed at a DC 37 Will save or be stunned 1 as they readjust to a more familiar flow of time. Backward Speakers When a palinthanos vocalizes, the sounds it creates are reversed. For the egarhowl, this only results in unnerving backwards sounds of angry roars and bestial noises, but for those who can speak, it makes understanding them difficult. A palinthanos has no difficulty understanding any language it can speak, but when it speaks, listeners must succeed at a DC 30 Perception check made as a free action with the concentrate trait each round to quickly decipher the reversed conversation. This prevents a palinthanos from being able to easily utilize linguistic actions.

<title level="1" pfs="">[Enchanting Ritualist](/NPCs.aspx?ID=3545)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

Possessing great stores of knowledge on mental magic and rituals, enchanting ritualists can also be solitary and capricious, tricking and transforming their visitors. The GM can change the selection of rituals this NPC knows freely, choosing any rituals of 9th rank or lower.

<column gap="tiny">
**[Recall Knowledge - Humanoid](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**
([Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=47)): DC 40

**[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 38

**[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 35
</column>

</column>

<column gap="medium">
<image src="/images/Monsters/Enchanting_Ritualist.webp" />
</column>

</row>

<title level="2" right="Creature 18">[Enchanting Ritualist](/NPCs.aspx?ID=3545)</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=721" />
<trait label="Medium" />
<trait label="Human" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=627" />
<trait label="Humanoid" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=628" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [NPC Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=236) pg. 105

**Perception** +31

**Languages**
[Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1), [Diabolic](/Languages.aspx?ID=117), [Empyrean](/Languages.aspx?ID=115), [Fey](/Languages.aspx?ID=119)

**Skills**
[Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35) +34, [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39) +31, [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38) +35, [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43) +34, [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=44) +36, [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46) +34

<row gap="medium">
**Str** +4

**Dex** +3

**Con** +1

**Int** +6

**Wis** +6

**Cha** +8
</row>

**Ritual Caster** the enchanting ritualist gains a +2 circumstance to skill checks for rituals

**Items**
_+2 [greater striking](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2829) [club](/Weapons.aspx?ID=357)_, _[greater bands of force](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3058)_, ornate ritual book

</column>

---

<column gap="tiny">

<row gap="medium">
**AC** 40 

**Fort** +27 

**Ref** +28 

**Will** +33 

</row>

<row gap="medium">
**HP** 320

</row>

**Resistances**
[mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647) 20

**Aura of Contentment** ([aura](/Traits.aspx?ID=542), [emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=590), [incapacitation](/Traits.aspx?ID=631), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647), [occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=662)) 30 feet. A creature that enters or starts its turn in the aura must succeed at a DC 38 Will save or lose the desire to do anything except rest and relax. [Hostile actions](/Rules.aspx?ID=300) taken against creatures affected by the aura end the effect. If a creature in the aura succeeds on their Will save or is the subject of a hostile action, it's temporarily immune to the aura of contentment for 24 hours. The enchanting ritualist can exempt creatures from the aura's effects.

</column>

---

<column gap="tiny">

**Speed** 25 feet

**Melee**
<actions string="Single Action" />
_club_ +30 ([Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103)),
**Damage** 3d6+12 bludgeoning plus 2d6 mental and fool's feast

**Melee**
<actions string="Single Action" />
fist +28 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103), [Nonlethal](/Traits.aspx?ID=188), [Unarmed](/Traits.aspx?ID=199)),
**Damage** 1d4+12 bludgeoning plus 2d6 mental and fool's feast

**Ranged**
<actions string="Single Action" />
enchanting wisps +30 ([Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103), [Mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=106), [range 100 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=248)),
**Damage** 9d6 mental plus fool's feast

**Ranged**
<actions string="Single Action" />
_club_ +28 ([Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103), [thrown 10 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=195)),
**Damage** 3d6+12 bludgeoning plus 2d6 mental and fool's feast

**Occult Spontaneous Spells** DC 42, attack +34
- **Cantrips (9th)**
[Daze](/Spells.aspx?ID=61), [Detect Magic](/Spells.aspx?ID=66), [Light](/Spells.aspx?ID=171), [Read Aura](/Spells.aspx?ID=246), [Telekinetic Hand](/Spells.aspx?ID=1715)
- **1st**
[Alarm](/Spells.aspx?ID=7), [Fear](/Spells.aspx?ID=110), [Ill Omen](/Spells.aspx?ID=696), [Illusory Object](/Spells.aspx?ID=160) (4 slots)
- **2nd**
[Augury](/Spells.aspx?ID=15), [Darkvision](/Spells.aspx?ID=60), [See the Unseen](/Spells.aspx?ID=1663), [Status](/Spells.aspx?ID=308) (4 slots)
- **3rd**
[Dream Message](/Spells.aspx?ID=90), [Hypnotize](/Spells.aspx?ID=1564), [Illusory Disguise](/Spells.aspx?ID=159), [Levitate](/Spells.aspx?ID=170) (4 slots)
- **4th**
[Confusion](/Spells.aspx?ID=48), [Fly](/Spells.aspx?ID=125), [Honeyed Words](/Spells.aspx?ID=1558), [Translocate](/Spells.aspx?ID=1724) (4 slots)
- **5th**
[Dreaming Potential](/Spells.aspx?ID=91), [Hallucination](/Spells.aspx?ID=144), [Scouting Eye](/Spells.aspx?ID=1661), [Sending](/Spells.aspx?ID=272) (4 slots)
- **6th**
[Mislead](/Spells.aspx?ID=199), [Repulsion](/Spells.aspx?ID=254), [Truesight](/Spells.aspx?ID=1727), [Zealous Conviction](/Spells.aspx?ID=378) (4 slots)
- **7th**
[Mask of Terror](/Spells.aspx?ID=185), [Project Image](/Spells.aspx?ID=237), [Truespeech](/Spells.aspx?ID=1728), [Wave of Despair](/Spells.aspx?ID=1757) (4 slots)
- **8th**
[Canticle of Everlasting Grief](/Spells.aspx?ID=879), [Quandary](/Spells.aspx?ID=1644), [Spirit Song](/Spells.aspx?ID=303), [Uncontrollable Dance](/Spells.aspx?ID=347) (4 slots)
- **9th**
[Foresight](/Spells.aspx?ID=127), [Overwhelming Presence](/Spells.aspx?ID=212), [Synesthesia](/Spells.aspx?ID=328), [Telepathic Demand](/Spells.aspx?ID=336) (4 slots)

**Rituals** DC 44

- **2nd**
[Heartbond](/Rituals.aspx?ID=33)
- **3rd**
[Geas](/Rituals.aspx?ID=12)
- **4th**
[Atone](/Rituals.aspx?ID=2), [Rest Eternal](/Rituals.aspx?ID=36)
- **5th**
[Astral Projection](/Rituals.aspx?ID=29), [Fortifying Brew](/Rituals.aspx?ID=147), [Call Spirit](/Rituals.aspx?ID=5), [Planar Servitor](/Rituals.aspx?ID=120), [Resurrect](/Rituals.aspx?ID=20)
- **6th**
[Binding Circle](/Rituals.aspx?ID=110), [Commune](/Rituals.aspx?ID=6)
- **7th**
[Collective Memories](/Rituals.aspx?ID=113), [Planar Displacement](/Rituals.aspx?ID=119)
- **9th**
[Fantastic Facade](/Rituals.aspx?ID=32)

**Fool's Feast**   Recipients of the ritualist's generosity pay dearly if the ritualist decides to turn against them. The ritualist gets a +4 circumstance bonus to attack rolls against any creature that has willingly participated in or benefited from one of their spells or rituals conducted in the last 12 hours. A creature that didn't help conduct a ritual still qualifies if it benefited in other ways, such as drinking a serving of [_fortifying brew_](/Rituals.aspx?ID=147).

 When the enchanting ritualist damages such a creature with a Strike, the target is affected by a 9th-rank [_cursed metamorphosis_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1479) spell (DC 42). If the Strike was a critical hit, the creature gets a degree of success one worse than it rolled. Once a creature succeeds at a save against this spell, it is temporarily immune for 24 hours.

</column>

<title level="1" pfs="Standard">[Kraken](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3075)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

A kraken is an enormous, squid-like leviathan with a cruel intelligence. It hunts ships, whales, and heroes alike. The hatred and envy krakens hold for [alghollthus](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=358), their rivals, has led many krakens to make their lairs in sunken cities, where they can sift through ancient lore and uncover long-lost arcane secrets.

**Altered Weather** ([aura](/Traits.aspx?ID=542), [primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=676)) A kraken reshapes the weather within 2 miles of it, with the effect of the [_control weather_](/Rituals.aspx?ID=116) ritual centered on the kraken and based on its emotional state, at the GM's discretion. If the kraken dies, the weather returns to normal immediately.

</column>

**Melee**
<actions string="Single Action" />
tentacle +37 ([reach 60 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192), [Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103)),
**Damage** 3d10+17 bludgeoning plus [Grab](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=45)

**Melee**
<actions string="Single Action" />
beak +37 ([reach 20 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192), [Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103)),
**Damage** 3d10+17 piercing

**Primal Innate Spells** DC 40
- **7th**
[Resist Energy](/Spells.aspx?ID=256)
- **8th**
[Punishing Winds](/Spells.aspx?ID=240)
- **10th**
[Dominate](/Spells.aspx?ID=87) (animals only)

**[Constrict](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=57)** <actions string="Single Action" />  2d10+17 bludgeoning, DC 40 (page 358). On a failed save, a creature that is [holding its breath](/Rules.aspx?ID=468) loses 1d4 rounds worth of air.

**Double Attack** <actions string="Single Action" />  The kraken makes two Strikes with two different arms or tentacles, each limb targeting a different creature. Double Attack counts as two attacks toward the kraken's multiple attack penalty, but the penalty doesn't increase until after both attacks are made. If the kraken subsequently uses the [Grab](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=45) action, it Grabs any number of creatures it hit with Double Attack.

**Ink Cloud** <actions string="Single Action" />  The kraken releases a cloud of black, venomous ink in an 80- foot emanation. This cloud has no effect outside water. Creatures inside the ink cloud are exposed to kraken ink poison and are [undetected](/Conditions.aspx?ID=96) while inside the cloud. The kraken can't use Ink Cloud again for 2d6 rounds, and the cloud dissipates after 1 minute.

**Jet** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([Move](/Traits.aspx?ID=114)) The kraken moves through the water up to 280 feet in a straight line without triggering reactions.

**Kraken Ink**  ([Poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=126)) Krakens are immune to this poison; **Saving Throw** DC 39 Fortitude; **Maximum Duration** 10 rounds; **Stage 1** 4d6 poison damage and [sickened 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=91) (1 round); **Stage 2** 5d6 poison damage and sickened 2 (1 round)

Among the most dangerous of their kind are the fiery magma worms. In addition to being even larger than benthic worms, the magma worm has a penchant for burrowing through volcanic regions that, over the generations, have infused it with a supernatural link to the Elemental [Plane of Fire](/Planes.aspx?ID=31). The fiery heart of an active volcano is an attractive lair for a magma worm, as are the sprawling fields of molten rock found in the deepest reaches of the Darklands. Legends of ancient dwarven societies and colonists of the Elemental Planes populating moats of lava with magma worms likely have some basis in truth, although the methods used to keep these “moat worms” contained—and prevented from chewing their way through fortress foundations—must have been significant. Magma worms sometimes frequent areas on the surface where volcanism creates hot springs or other geothermal features, but even then they prefer to spend most of their time burrowing through the ground in their never-ending search for sustenance. Surface lands claimed by magma worms are notable for the mound-shaped burrows these creatures leave behind as they dig. **[Recall Knowledge - Beast](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35), [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43)): DC 43 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 41 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 38 [Magma Worm](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2873) **Source** [Monster Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=221) pg. 57 1.1 **Perception** +25; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59), [tremorsense](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=82) ([imprecise](/Rules.aspx?ID=412)) 100 feet **Languages** **Skills** [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) +38 **Str** +10 **Dex** -1 **Con** +9 **Int** -3 **Wis** -1 **Cha** -1 --- **AC** 40 **Fort** +36 **Ref** +25 **Will** +27 **HP** 410 **Immunities** [fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=604) **Weaknesses** [cold](/Traits.aspx?ID=555) 15 **Fire Healing** As long as a magma worm is in contact with a fire or body of magma at least as large as itself, it gains [fast healing](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=62) 20. When struck by a magical [fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=604) effect from anything other than itself, a magma worm regains Hit Points equal to half the fire damage the effect would otherwise deal.
**Inexorable** The cave worm recovers from the [paralyzed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=85), [slowed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=92), and [stunned](/Conditions.aspx?ID=93) conditions at the end of its turn. It's also immune to penalties to its Speeds and the [immobilized](/Conditions.aspx?ID=81) condition, and it ignores [difficult terrain](/Rules.aspx?ID=453) and greater difficult terrain.
**Slough Skin** **Frequency** once per day; **Trigger** The cave worm would be affected by a condition or adverse effect (such as [_cursed metamorphosis_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1479)); **Effect** The cave worm negates the triggering condition or effect by sloughing an outer layer of its skin. Effects from [artifacts](/Traits.aspx?ID=537), deities, or a similarly powerful source can't be avoided in this way. --- **Speed** 40 feet, burrow 40 feet, swim 20 feet **Melee** jaws +36 ([deadly 3d10](/Traits.aspx?ID=174), [Fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=72), [reach 20 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)), **Damage** 3d10+18 piercing plus 2d6 fire and [Improved Grab](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=66) **Melee** stinger +36 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [Fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=72), [Poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=126), [reach 20 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)), **Damage** 2d12+18 piercing plus 2d6 fire and magma worm venom **Melee** body +34 ([Fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=72), [reach 15 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)), **Damage** 2d10+16 bludgeoning plus 2d6 fire **Fast Swallow** **Trigger** The worm Grabs a creature; **Effect** The worm uses [Swallow Whole](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=77). **Fire Breath** ([Fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=72), [Primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=134)) The magma worm breathes a blast of flame in a 60-foot cone that deals 18d6 fire damage to all creatures in the area (DC 41 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save). It can't use Fire Breath again for 1d4 rounds. **Magma Worm Venom** ([Poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=126)) **Saving Throw** DC 41 Fortitude; **Maximum Duration** 6 rounds; **Stage 1** 1d6 poison damage and [drained 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=68) (1 round); **Stage 2** 2d6 poison damage and drained 1 (1 round); **Stage 3** 2d6 poison damage and drained 2 (1 round) **Rock Tunneler** A cave worm can burrow through solid stone at a Speed of 20 feet. It can leave a tunnel if it desires, and it usually does. **[Swallow Whole](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=77)** ([Attack](/Traits.aspx?ID=15)) Huge, 3d10+10 bludgeoning plus 2d6 fire, Rupture 36 **Thrash** The worm attempts one Strike against each creature in its reach. It can Strike up to once with its jaws, up to once with its stinger, and any number of times with its body. Each attack counts toward the worm's multiple attack penalty, but the multiple attack penalty doesn't increase until after it makes all the attacks.

As long as a magma worm is in contact with a fire or body of magma at least as large as itself, it gains [fast healing](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=62) 20. When struck by a magical [fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=604) effect from anything other than itself, a magma worm regains Hit Points equal to half the fire damage the effect would otherwise deal.
**Inexorable** The cave worm recovers from the [paralyzed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=85), [slowed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=92), and [stunned](/Conditions.aspx?ID=93) conditions at the end of its turn. It's also immune to penalties to its Speeds and the [immobilized](/Conditions.aspx?ID=81) condition, and it ignores [difficult terrain](/Rules.aspx?ID=453) and greater difficult terrain.

description:
Among the most dangerous of their kind are the fiery magma worms. In addition to being even larger than benthic worms, the magma worm has a penchant for burrowing through volcanic regions that, over the generations, have infused it with a supernatural link to the Elemental [Plane of Fire](/Planes.aspx?ID=31). The fiery heart of an active volcano is an attractive lair for a magma worm, as are the sprawling fields of molten rock found in the deepest reaches of the Darklands. Legends of ancient dwarven societies and colonists of the Elemental Planes populating moats of lava with magma worms likely have some basis in truth, although the methods used to keep these “moat worms” contained—and prevented from chewing their way through fortress foundations—must have been significant.

 Magma worms sometimes frequent areas on the surface where volcanism creates hot springs or other geothermal features, but even then they prefer to spend most of their time burrowing through the ground in their never-ending search for sustenance. Surface lands claimed by magma worms are notable for the mound-shaped burrows these creatures leave behind as they dig.

markdown:
Among the many unique creatures of the Inner Sea, the hydras known as mocking choruses that stalk the River Kingdoms may be one of the most reviled. While as ferocious in direct combat as others of their kind, chorusus are a singular type of challenge for warriors that hunt them due not to their sharp teeth, but instead a sharp and subtle tongue. Their strangely cunning tactics and power to turn longtime friends into bitter enemies brings doubt to even the closest of allies. Mocking choruses exhibit behavior that seem to indicate a more elevated intelligence than other hydras. They do not appear to eat in large quantities, leaving little sign they have passed by and spurring rumors that they prey on settlements more for sport than sustenance. Every few years sees a new story of a whole village turning on itself. Neighbor against neighbor, the village tears itself apart; some go missing, and only the sounds of hissing laughter precede the event. **[Recall Knowledge - Beast](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35), [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43)): DC 38 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 36 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 33 [Mocking Chorus](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3296) **Source** [Howl of the Wild](/Sources.aspx?ID=226) pg. 167 2.1 **Perception** +30; [scent](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=74) ([imprecise](/Rules.aspx?ID=412)) 60 feet **Languages** all (see uncanny mimicry) **Skills** [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) +35, [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38) +36, [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=45) +35 **Str** +9 **Dex** +4 **Con** +6 **Int** -2 **Wis** +2 **Cha** +4 **Uncanny Mimicry** While unable to communicate for prolonged periods, a mocking chorus can precisely imitate a humanoid voice. If a creature speaks within audible range of the mocking chorus, the mocking chorus can speak using the creature's voice, even if it says different words than what were spoken. Creatures that hear the mocking chorus speak this way can attempt a DC 40 Will save to recognize the source. On a success, creatures gain a +1 circumstance bonus to all saving throws against the mocking chorus' abilities for 1 minute. --- **AC** 41 [all-around vision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=49) **Fort** +33 **Ref** +30 **Will** +30 **HP** 340 ((body), hydra regeneration) **Immunities** [auditory](/Traits.aspx?ID=541), [sonic](/Traits.aspx?ID=697)
**HP** 35 (head), head regrowth; **Immunities** area damage; **Weakness** slashing 10 **Head Regrowth** A mocking chorus ordinarily has 10 heads. A creature can attempt to sever one of the hydra's heads by specifically targeting it and dealing damage equal to the head's Hit Points. A head that is not completely severed returns to full Hit Points at the end of any creature's turn.
A hydra can regrow a severed head using hydra regeneration. A creature can prevent this regrowth by dealing acid or fire damage to the stump, cauterizing it. Single-target [acid](/Traits.aspx?ID=524) or [fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=604) effects need to be targeted at a specific stump, but effects that deal [splash](/Traits.aspx?ID=699) damage or affect areas covering the hydra's whole space cauterize all stumps if they deal acid or fire damage. If the attack that severs a head deals any acid or fire damage, the stump is cauterized instantly. If all five heads are cauterized, the hydra dies.
**Hydra Regeneration** The mocking chorus has [regeneration](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=72) equal to 3 × the number of heads it has. If a hydra's body is missing any heads and the remaining stumps have not been cauterized, the hydra attempts a DC 43 Fortitude save after it regains Hit Points from regeneration. On a success, one uncauterized stump regrows two heads; on a critical success, two uncauterized stumps regrow into two heads each. The hydra can never grow more than double the number of heads it ordinarily has. The hydra's regeneration only fully deactivates if all its heads are severed and all stumps are cauterized, at which point it dies.
**Reactive Heads** A mocking chorus gains an extra reaction per round for each of its heads beyond the first, which it can use only to make Reactive Strikes. It can't use more than 1 reaction on the same triggering action, even if a creature leaves several squares within its reach, and the hydra must use a different head for each Reactive Strike it makes. Whenever one of the hydra's heads is severed, the hydra loses 1 of its extra reactions per round.
**[Reactive Strike](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=48)** --- **Speed** 35 feet, swim 35 feet **Melee** jaws +37 ([reach 15 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)), **Damage** 4d12+14 piercing **Ranged** harsh laugh +35 ([Auditory](/Traits.aspx?ID=16), [range increment 90 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=248)), **Damage** 4d10+14 sonic **Petty Whispers** ([Auditory](/Traits.aspx?ID=16), [Mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=106)) The mocking chorus adopts the voices of its enemies, spreading lies and jeers among would-be allies and tearing apart trusted friends. Creatures in a 60-foot emanation of the mocking chorus must attempt a DC 37 Will save. The mocking chorus can't use petty whispers again for 1 minute.
**Critical Success** The creature is unaffected and is temporarily immune for 1 day.
**Success** As failure, but the creature takes half damage and is not [confused](/Conditions.aspx?ID=63).
**Failure** The creature takes 12d10 mental damage and is confused for 1 minute. It can attempt a new save at the end of each of its turns to end the confusion.
**Critical Failure** The creature takes 15d10 damage and is confused for 1 minute, with no save to end early

This dragon is haughty and proud, often coming across as self-righteous. As the very embodiment of just wars, he feels he can't possibly be wrong. His polished steel scales make the distinctive sound of blade scraping against blade as he moves, and his needle-like spines clink against each other with every mighty flap of his broad wings. Saint Fang is war given a dragon's form, with the temperament of a master strategist. Of late, more and more of [Gorum's](/Deities.aspx?ID=283) followers have declared war for the sake of battle. They revel in causing bloodshed for any excuse, calling on Gorum's servants for aid, but Saint Fang doesn't answer those calls. He is more likely to appear for a group of villagers who band together to unseat a local bandit king or for a native population defending their homes against colonizers. He believes that war is inevitable as long as the greedy and bloodthirsty are given weapons, and he seeks to aid those whose justification for war is because they've run out of peaceful options. Saint Fang rarely takes a rider, but he obeys the commands of his Lord in Iron, Gorum. The god occasionally commands Saint Fang to take one of his faithful into battle, and he obeys him to the letter of his command, often unseating riders he finds unworthy once they reach the battlefield. **[Recall Knowledge - Dragon](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35)): DC 48 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 46 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 43 [Saint Fang](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3394) **Source** [Prey for Death](/Sources.aspx?ID=231) pg. 115 **Perception** +31; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59), forge vision, [scent](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=74) ([imprecise](/Rules.aspx?ID=412)) 60 feet **Languages** [Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1), [Draconic](/Languages.aspx?ID=2), [Dwarven](/Languages.aspx?ID=3), [Jotun](/Languages.aspx?ID=8) **Skills** [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=34) +30, [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) +35, [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39) +32, [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=40) +32, [Medicine](/Skills.aspx?ID=42) +29, [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46) +29, [Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=47) +28, [Warfare Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) +30 **Str** +9 **Dex** +4 **Con** +7 **Int** +4 **Wis** +5 **Cha** +6 **Forge Vision** Saint Fang ignores the [concealed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=62) condition from smoke and fire. --- **AC** 42 **Fort** +33 **Ref** +28 **Will** +29 +1 status to all saves vs. [magic](/Traits.aspx?ID=644) **HP** 365 **Immunities** [paralyzed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=85), [sleep](/Traits.aspx?ID=696) **[Frightful Presence](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=64)** ([aura](/Traits.aspx?ID=542), [emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=590), [fear](/Traits.aspx?ID=598), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647)) 90 feet, DC 37
**Spiked Scales** A creature that critically fails to Strike Saint Fang in melee takes 6d6 piercing damage (DC 40 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save).
**[Buck](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=54)** DC 37
**Wing Deflection** **Trigger** Saint Fang is targeted with an attack; **Effect** Saint Fang raises a wing, gaining a +2 circumstance bonus to AC against the triggering attack. If he is flying, he descends 10 feet after the attack is complete. --- **Speed** 40 feet, fly 130 feet **Melee** jaws +35 ([Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103), [reach 15 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)), **Damage** 3d12+17 piercing plus 1d6 fire **Melee** claw +35 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103), [reach 10 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)), **Damage** 3d6+17 slashing plus 2d6 [persistent bleed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29) **Melee** tail +33 ([Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103), [reach 20 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)), **Damage** 3d6+17 piercing **Dragon Breath** Saint Fang breathes in one of two ways. He can't use Dragon Breath again for 1d4 rounds.
  • **Blade Breath** ([arcane](/Traits.aspx?ID=534)) He breathes a 100-foot line of sharp blades that deals 19d6 slashing damage (DC 40 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save). The blades created by this breath vanish at the end of the round.
  • **Forge Breath** ([arcane](/Traits.aspx?ID=534)) He breathes a blast of embers and smoke, as if from an immense forge. Each creature within a 40-foot cone takes 6d6 fire damage and 12d6 poison damage (DC 40 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save). Smoke lingers in the area until the end of Saint Fang's next turn; all creatures within the smoke become [concealed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=62), and all creatures outside the smoke become concealed to creatures within.
**Draconic Frenzy** Saint Fang makes two claw Strikes and one tail Strike in any order. **Draconic Momentum** When Saint Fang scores a critical hit with a Strike, he recharges his Dragon Breath.

Shroud mosses are often confused for [ghosts](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=418), as they appear as a shimmering, insubstantial imprint of a deceased creature. In truth, nothing of the deceased remains within a shroud moss. Rather, what appears to be a ghost is an image created by clouds of shimmering spores surrounding the wispy tendrils of the moss itself. When not disguised by a stolen shape, a shroud moss appears as a mass of gray-green tendrils of moss capable of shifting its shape into the basic framework of a creature, looking not unlike a free-standing humanoid nervous system with a mass of tangles where a brain would be. **[Recall Knowledge - Fungus](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43)): DC 43 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 41 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 38 [Shroud Moss](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3795) **Source** [Pathfinder #212: A Voice in the Blight](/Sources.aspx?ID=255) pg. 88 **Perception** +31; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59) **Languages** [Chthonian](/Languages.aspx?ID=114); spore telepathy 100 feet **Skills** [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=34) +32, [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38) +35, [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=40) +35, [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=48) +32 **Str** -5 **Dex** +6 **Con** +9 **Int** +5 **Wis** +5 **Cha** +9 **Spore Telepathy** A shroud moss can communicate via telepathy with any creature within its sporecloud aura, doing so in that creature's native language. --- **AC** 42 **Fort** +36 **Ref** +30 **Will** +27 **HP** 400 **Resistances** bludgeoning 15, piercing 20 **Weaknesses** [fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=604) 15, slashing 15 **[Frightful Presence](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=64)** ([aura](/Traits.aspx?ID=542), [emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=590), [fear](/Traits.aspx?ID=598), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647)) 60 feet, DC 37; **Requirements** Assume Shape is active.
**Filament Body** A shroud moss's body is physical, but much lighter and flexible than normal. They can move through openings down to 1 inch in diameter with ease and are treated as Tiny creatures for all effects affected by a creature's size. A shroud moss adjusts its saving throws against wind-based effects down by one degree of success.
**Sporecloud** ([aura](/Traits.aspx?ID=542), [primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=676)) 60 feet. text: Shroud Moss Shroud mosses are often confused for ghosts, as they appear as a shimmering, insubstantial imprint of a deceased creature. In truth, nothing of the deceased remains within a shroud moss. Rather, what appears to be a ghost is an image created by clouds of shimmering spores surrounding the wispy tendrils of the moss itself. When not disguised by a stolen shape, a shroud moss appears as a mass of gray-green tendrils of moss capable of shifting its shape into the basic framework of a creature, looking not unlike a free-standing humanoid nervous system with a mass of tangles where a brain would be.
