features.Fated: When a creature is subject to a [fortune](/Traits.aspx?ID=612) effect from a norn and a [misfortune](/Traits.aspx?ID=654) effect from any source other than a norn (or vice versa), the norn's effect automatically [counteracts](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) the other effect and then takes place normally, rather than the two effects canceling each other out. If both the fortune and misfortune effect are from a norn, then the two cancel each other out as normal. At the GM's discretion, powerful entities related to fate or luck, like [Desna](/Deities.aspx?ID=281), [Magdh](/Deities.aspx?ID=97), or [Pharasma](/Deities.aspx?ID=290), can't have their effects negated by this ability.
features.Sever Fate: ([Occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=120)) When a norn deals void damage with a Strike, she regains 10 Hit Points. The target must succeed at a DC 39 Fortitude save or become [drained 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=68) (drained 2 on a critical failure). Further void damage dealt by the norn increases the drained condition value by 1 on a failed save (or by 2 on a critical failure), to a maximum of drained 4.
features.Shift Fate: <actions string="Reaction" /> ([Occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=120)) **Trigger** A creature within 120 feet attempts a saving throw; **Effect** The creature rolls the saving throw twice, and then the norn decides which result applies. If the norn chooses the lower roll, this is a [misfortune](/Traits.aspx?ID=654) effect; if she chooses the higher roll, it's a [fortune](/Traits.aspx?ID=612) effect; if they're the same, she decides which trait to apply.
features.Snip Thread: <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([Death](/Traits.aspx?ID=40), [Manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104), [Occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=120)) **Frequency** three times per day; **Effect** The norn produces a golden thread linked to the fate of a creature within 100 feet of her, then snips it short with her shears. The target takes 100 void damage (DC 42 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Fortitude save). If the target is reduced to 0 Hit Points from this damage, the thread is completely severed and the creature dies immediately. A creature slain by Snip Thread can't be restored to life except by a [_wish_](/Rituals.aspx?ID=125) ritual or similarly powerful magic; or by divine intervention. Regardless of the outcome of their saving throw, a creature targeted by Snip Thread then becomes temporarily immune for 24 hours. The norn can't use Snip Thread again for 1d4 rounds.

description:
Ancient beyond imagining, norns are powerful fey women who hold in their hands the physical manifestation of fate and destiny in the form of golden thread. They watch over all life, intervening with reluctance when called upon—or with a vengeance when the strands of fate are twisted and abused by lesser beings. They cut imposing figures, standing 14 feet tall and weighing 800 pounds.

 Norns' relationship with the Eldest of the [First World](/Planes.aspx?ID=35) is complex. Many among norns serve [Magdh](/Deities.aspx?ID=97) the Three, the triune Eldest who some norns believe to be the first norn triumvirate bound together into one entity, as Magdh has three bodies: a Maiden, a Mother, and a Matriarch. Magdh claims to be watching the threads of fate for some ominous prophesied cataclysm, and in addition to assisting in her divinations, Magdh expects the norns who serve her to follow her cryptic commands to help nudge the future away from the brink. However, norns are powerful beings in their own right, themselves capable of granting divine power, and many balk at serving the enigmatic demigod. These norns find the other Eldest even more alien and challenging to interact with, for they believe that while the Eldest wield great power, even these powerful beings should not be granted leave to meddle with fate as much as they desire.

 While even the weakest of the Eldest could destroy an unaffiliated norn with ease, they tend to obey the proclamations and judgments of norns when they are spoken. These norns, for their part, use their perceived neutrality judiciously. They know better than to issue too many demands to the Eldest, lest the capricious demigods grow frustrated. And so the balance of power remains tenuous between unaffiliated norns and the Eldest, as it has for eons. Norns know that it's merely a matter of time before the Eldest lose their respect for this tradition and start acting entirely as they please, despite norns' best efforts to rein in their most disruptive actions.

Among the most powerful of all the true aeons, pleromas are the ultimate manifestation of the duality of creation and destruction. Their physical manifestation is a constant state of flux between these two extremes; their forms are draped in a hooded, shifting cloak of night black where galaxies and other celestial objects flit in and out of existence at every moment, as if depicting the constant life, death, and rebirth of a miniature, self-contained universe. Pleromas see the multiverse as both eternal and cyclical, doomed and malleable, ending only if these cycles ever become unbalanced. They believe the current Convergence is necessary to obtain this essential balance, and act to ensure that the grand design of the Monad is carried out to the smallest detail. **[Recall Knowledge - Monitor](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46)): DC 40 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 38 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 35 [Pleroma](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2811) **Source** [Monster Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=221) pg. 10 1.1 **Perception** +37; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59), lifesense 120 feet, [_truesight_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1727) **Languages** [Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1); envisioning **Skills** [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=1) +33, [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=2) +38, [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5) +34, [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=6) +34, [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=11) +38, [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=13) +39, [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15) +35 **Str** +6 **Dex** +7 **Con** +6 **Int** +8 **Wis** +9 **Cha** +6 **Envisioning** ([aura](/Traits.aspx?ID=542), [divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=579), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647)) 100 feet. A pleroma can communicate mentally with any creatures in the aura using wordless psychic projections. They don't need to share a language, though the aeon's meaning to non-aeons can be vague and is often mysterious. An aeon can use this ability to communicate flawlessly with any other aeon on the same plane as itself. --- **AC** 45 **Fort** +32 **Ref** +31 **Will** +37 +1 status to all saves vs. [magic](/Traits.aspx?ID=644) **HP** 335 , regeneration 20 (deactivated by [spirit](/Traits.aspx?ID=737)) **Immunities** [vitality](/Traits.aspx?ID=509), [void](/Traits.aspx?ID=510) **Weaknesses** spirit 20 **Reality Twist **Trigger** The pleroma critically fails a saving throw** **Effect** The critical failure becomes a normal failure. --- **Speed** fly 40 feet; [_unfettered movement_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1732) **Melee** touch of creation ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103), [vitality +36](/Traits.aspx?ID=509)), **Damage** 5d8+16 vitality **Melee** touch of destruction ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103), [void +36](/Traits.aspx?ID=510)), **Damage** 5d8+16 void **Divine Innate Spells** DC 47, attack +39 - **Cantrips (10th)** [Vitality Lash](/Spells.aspx?ID=1744), [Void Warp](/Spells.aspx?ID=1745) - **1st** [Create Water](/Spells.aspx?ID=53) (at will) - **2nd** [Shape Wood](/Spells.aspx?ID=277) (at will) - **3rd** [Hypercognition](/Spells.aspx?ID=156) (at will) - **4th** [Create Food](/Spells.aspx?ID=52) (at will), [Shape Stone](/Spells.aspx?ID=276) (at will), [Unfettered Movement](/Spells.aspx?ID=1732) - **5th** [Creation](/Spells.aspx?ID=54) (at will) - **7th** [Interplanar Teleport](/Spells.aspx?ID=1576), [Retrocognition](/Spells.aspx?ID=260) - **8th** [Disintegrate](/Spells.aspx?ID=76) (×2), [Unrelenting Observation](/Spells.aspx?ID=351) - **9th** [Banishment](/Spells.aspx?ID=19), [Blessed Boundary](/Spells.aspx?ID=1452), [Detonate Magic](/Spells.aspx?ID=1488), [Overwhelming Presence](/Spells.aspx?ID=212) - **10th** [Manifestation](/Spells.aspx?ID=1592) - **Constant (8th)** [Truesight](/Spells.aspx?ID=1727) **Generate Sphere** ([Concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32), [Divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=48)) The pleroma manifests a 2-foot-diameter sphere of energy—either a white sphere of creation that hovers above their left hand or a black sphere of oblivion above their right. A sphere vanishes after 1 minute, when it is more than 300 feet from the pleroma, or when the pleroma Generates a Sphere of that type again. A sphere of oblivion destroys unattended objects it touches, though larger objects are destroyed at a rate of one 10-foot cube per round of contact.
The sphere can enter the space of a creature; when it does, the creature takes 20d6 damage with a DC 43 Fortitude save. This is an [incapacitation](/Traits.aspx?ID=631) effect.
**Success** The creature takes no damage and is pushed out of the sphere to the nearest open space of the GM's choice.
**Failure** The creature takes full damage; this is vitality damage for a sphere of creation or void damage for a sphere of oblivion, but it can damage any type of creature regardless of its normal immunities. The creature is then pushed out of the sphere as on a success. A creature reduced to 0 HP is slain instead of being pushed out, either merged with new matter for a sphere of creation or completely destroyed for a void of oblivion; the creature can be restored only via a [_wish_](/Rituals.aspx?ID=125) ritual or similarly powerful effect. This is a [death](/Traits.aspx?ID=571) effect.
**Critical Failure** As failure, but the creature takes double damage.

There are few creatures capable of such ecological destruction while staying as humorous and lighthearted as the Great Flood. The Great Flood towers with their giant serpent body and nine humanoid heads, each one with a different personality, though all serve the same purpose—to vanquish all signs of life that shouldn't be where they are. This creature intends to maintain the balance of the universe, ensuring that nothing takes up more space than necessary. Unfortunately, the judgment of where someone or something should be is only seen and weighed by the 18 eyes of the Great Flood, with little regard to mortal input. The Great Flood is an immortal, or at least ageless, being who hibernates for 12 years at a stretch. On the thirteenth year, they emerge from the depths of the oceans and begin weighing the state of the world and the environments closest to their resting place: should the first thing they see on dry land be destroyed? Each of the Great Flood's nine heads lends their thoughts and insights to this deliberation, and upon reaching a consensus, they'll either carry on to the next location or they'll drown the land, immersing miles of dry land in salty waters from the ocean. In instances where they perceive the excess life as particularly problematic, they'll even decide to poison the waters with their bitter breath to ensure that nothing survives the judgment they've decreed. The Great Flood, despite its inherently destructive nature, isn't actually bloodthirsty and will often afford an opportunity for poor townsfolk to state their case and beg for the lives of their town to be saved. While the Great Flood has the capacity for mercy and consideration, the godlike creature stands adamant once they've made their decision. One or two of the heads might feel a twinge of guilt and tell a small joke to the townsfolk, relieving themselves of the mental pressure, before murdering an entire village. The nine personalities of the serpentine creature often run into contention with each other. One is a perfectionist, while another is aloof; one is assertive, while another is playful; one is capricious, while another is suspicious; one is ambitious, while the other is a people pleaser. The last one is quiet and secretive, only ever whispering to the heads closest to them. Though the heads squabble like siblings, they eventually always make a compromise. Leading Head During each of the Great Flood's appearances, one head takes the lead once combat begins, chosen by the GM when initiative is rolled. Whichever head is in the lead grants a different action the Great Flood can use during its first turn each round (see Coordinated Actions).
**Aloof—The Flood's Command** (divine) The aloof head casts a 5th-rank [_command_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1470) (Will DC 42).
**Ambitious—Claim Position** (divine) The ambitious head declares a divine position above its station. It gains 100 temporary Hit Points for 1 minute. It also gains a weakness 20 to spirit damage and can't Claim Position again for 1 minute.
**Assertive—Rush In** The Great Flood Swims, then makes a melee Strike.
**Capricious—Changing Thoughts** ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) The capricious head [counteracts](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) each mental effect on themself as a 10th-rank effect with a +32 counteract modifier.
**People Pleaser**—Build Consensus ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) The heads discuss and audibly agree on a creature to target. Until they Build Consensus again, their Strikes deal an additional 20 precision damage to that creature.
**Perfectionist—Find Fault** ([auditory](/Traits.aspx?ID=541), [concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=590), [linguistic](/Traits.aspx?ID=642), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647)) The perfectionist head criticizes a creature within their aura. The creature must succeed at a DC 42 Will save or take 9d6 persistent mental damage.
**Playful**—Bad Jokes The playful head makes an ill-timed quip about the impermanence of life. They attempt to Demoralize each creature within their aura.
**Secretive**—Secret Movement ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=579), [teleportation](/Traits.aspx?ID=710)) The Great Flood is invisible until the end of their turn and teleports to an open space within their aura. **[Recall Knowledge - Beast](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=2), [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=10)): DC 50 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 48 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 45

Many of the heads will follow each other's leads, although which and how is a good thing to learn with Discover. description:
There are few creatures capable of such ecological destruction while staying as humorous and lighthearted as the Great Flood. The Great Flood towers with their giant serpent body and nine humanoid heads, each one with a different personality, though all serve the same purpose—to vanquish all signs of life that shouldn't be where they are. This creature intends to maintain the balance of the universe, ensuring that nothing takes up more space than necessary. Unfortunately, the judgment of where someone or something should be is only seen and weighed by the 18 eyes of the Great Flood, with little regard to mortal input.

 The Great Flood is an immortal, or at least ageless, being who hibernates for 12 years at a stretch. On the thirteenth year, they emerge from the depths of the oceans and begin weighing the state of the world and the environments closest to their resting place: should the first thing they see on dry land be destroyed? Each of the Great Flood's nine heads lends their thoughts and insights to this deliberation, and upon reaching a consensus, they'll either carry on to the next location or they'll drown the land, immersing miles of dry land in salty waters from the ocean. In instances where they perceive the excess life as particularly problematic, they'll even decide to poison the waters with their bitter breath to ensure that nothing survives the judgment they've decreed. The Great Flood, despite its inherently destructive nature, isn't actually bloodthirsty and will often afford an opportunity for poor townsfolk to state their case and beg for the lives of their town to be saved. While the Great Flood has the capacity for mercy and consideration, the godlike creature stands adamant once they've made their decision. One or two of the heads might feel a twinge of guilt and tell a small joke to the townsfolk, relieving themselves of the mental pressure, before murdering an entire village.

 The nine personalities of the serpentine creature often run into contention with each other. One is a perfectionist, while another is aloof; one is assertive, while another is playful; one is capricious, while another is suspicious; one is ambitious, while the other is a people pleaser. The last one is quiet and secretive, only ever whispering to the heads closest to them. Though the heads squabble like siblings, they eventually always make a compromise.

Powerful vrolikais command the untamed armies of demonkind, uniting them behind their one unifying desire for death and destruction. Unlike other demons, the dreaded vrolikai doesn't form directly from a single soul—they instead manifest when a demon devours so many damned souls that their own individual desires are lost in the sinful cacophony. A vrolikai who survives this process gains great power and can claim a region of the [Outer Rifts](/Planes.aspx?ID=45) as their own domain. Vrolikais' enthusiastic embrace of the multitude of sins makes them uniquely suited to lead and unite demons, such that even demon lords often must rely on vrolikais to command their forces. The Grim Reaper is the unflinching personification of death. Silent as the grave and inexorable as time itself, this legendary being hunts down creatures that have evaded death for too long. Sometimes the Grim Reaper comes without warning. Other times it comes to finish the work others could not. The Grim Reaper serves no god, [fiend](/Traits.aspx?ID=600), [aeon](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=357), or otherworldly being. It's both despised and feared by [psychopomps](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=458) and [celestials](/Languages.aspx?ID=16), but few—if any—dare stand in its way. Like some eternal plague, it kills any who try to cure the multiverse of its presence. It stands alone and keeps its own council. The pleas of mortals and immortals alike fall on deaf ears once the Grim Reaper chooses its quarry. Its reasoning is silent and inscrutable to the mortal mind, but no matter its choice, the result is final. While some legends claim that the Grim Reaper appears to everyone when they die, the truth is more disturbing. Such vigils are the providence of psychopomps, immortals charged with the protection and guidance of mortal souls through the afterlife. The Grim Reaper instead enacts the sinister agenda of [Abaddon](/Planes.aspx?ID=37), where the Apocalypse Riders rule. Indeed, there are many similarities in shape and form between the Grim Reaper and [Charon](/Deities.aspx?ID=135), the Rider of Death, but there are no recorded instance of these entities working together. Instead, the Grim Reaper serves as something of a manifestation of Abaddon itself, and in this regard, is believed to be an incarnation of the mysterious First Rider. When the Grim Reaper visits a world, it does so not as an angel of mercy but a relentless harvester of life. Those who fall to the Grim Reaper were not destined to die as much as they were selected, hunted, and murdered. Perhaps the most frightening detail surrounding the Grim Reaper's legend is its nature as a singular entity, for some believe that more than one exists in the Great Beyond. There are whispered rumors of a council of at least nine Grim Reapers, stalking reality and culling the living as in service to true entropy. According to the teachings of some death cults, the final goal of the Grim Reaper is to end the cycle of life and death and serve as a silent lord of an empty universe. **[Recall Knowledge - Undead](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46)): DC 52 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 50 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 47 [Grim Reaper](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3036) **Source** [Monster Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=221) pg. 184 1.1 **Perception** +41; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59), see the unseen, status sight, [_truesight_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1727) **Languages** [Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1), [Necril](/Languages.aspx?ID=20) **Skills** [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=1) +43, [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) +38, [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5) +40, [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=7) +43, [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=13) +39, [Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=14) +36, [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15) +43 **Str** +8 **Dex** +10 **Con** +8 **Int** +5 **Wis** +7 **Cha** +8 **Status Sight** The Grim Reaper automatically knows the Hit Points, conditions, afflictions, and emotions of all creatures it can see. **Items** [Scythe](/Weapons.aspx?ID=39) --- **AC** 47 **Fort** +37 **Ref** +41 **Will** +38 +1 status to all saves vs. [magic](/Traits.aspx?ID=644) **HP** 320 (death's grace, [void healing](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=83)) **Immunities** bleed, [death](/Traits.aspx?ID=571) effects, [disease](/Traits.aspx?ID=578), [paralyzed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=85), [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=669), [unconscious](/Conditions.aspx?ID=95) **Resistances** all damage 15 **Aura of Misfortune** ([aura](/Traits.aspx?ID=542), [divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=579), [misfortune](/Traits.aspx?ID=654)) 20 feet. Living creatures in the aura must roll twice on all d20 rolls and use the lower result.
**Death's Grace** The Grim Reaper can choose whether or not it counts as [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=722) for effects that affect undead differently. Even if it does not count as undead, the Grim Reaper still never counts as a living creature.
**Void Healing** The Grim Reaper can choose whether or not it takes vitality damage.
**Lurking Death** ([divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=579), [teleportation](/Traits.aspx?ID=710)) **Trigger** A creature within 100 feet makes a ranged attack or uses an action that has the [concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645), or [move](/Traits.aspx?ID=658) trait; **Effect** The Grim Reaper teleports to a square adjacent to the triggering creature and makes a melee Strike against it. If the Strike hits, the Grim Reaper disrupts the triggering action. --- **Speed** 50 feet, fly 75 feet **Melee** keen scythe +40 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [deadly 3d10](/Traits.aspx?ID=174), [Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103), [reach 10 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192), [Trip](/Traits.aspx?ID=196)), **Damage** 4d10+23 slashing plus death strike and energy drain **Divine Innate Spells** DC 47, attack +37 - **7th** [Interplanar Teleport](/Spells.aspx?ID=1576) - **10th** [Execute](/Spells.aspx?ID=1519) (×4) - **Constant (2nd)** [See the Unseen](/Spells.aspx?ID=1663) - **Constant (3rd)** [Haste](/Spells.aspx?ID=147) - **Constant (6th)** [Truesight](/Spells.aspx?ID=1727) **Death Strike** ([Death](/Traits.aspx?ID=40)) A creature critically hit by any of the Grim Reaper's attacks or that critically fails against any of its spells must succeed at a DC 47 Fortitude save or die. **Energy Drain** When the Grim Reaper hits and deals damage with its scythe, it regains 20 Hit Points, and the target must succeed at a DC 43 Fortitude save or become [doomed 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=67). If the target is already doomed, the doomed value increases by 1 (to a maximum of doomed 3). **Final Death** A creature killed by the Grim Reaper can't be brought back to life by any means short of divine intervention. **Infuse Weapon** ([Divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=48)) Any scythe gains the [agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=526) trait, can't be disarmed, and becomes a _+3 [major striking](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2829) [keen](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2843) scythe_ while the Grim Reaper wields it. If the Grim Reaper Strikes a creature with a weakness to any specific type of damage, the scythe's damage counts as that type of damage, in addition to slashing.

Silent as the grave and inexorable as time itself, this legendary being hunts down creatures that have evaded death for too long. Sometimes the Grim Reaper comes without warning. Other times it comes to finish the work others could not. The Grim Reaper serves no god, fiend, aeon, or otherworldly being. It's both despised and feared by psychopomps and celestials, but few—if any—dare stand in its way. Like some eternal plague, it kills any who try to cure the multiverse of its presence. It stands alone and keeps its own council. The pleas of mortals and immortals alike fall on deaf ears once the Grim Reaper chooses its quarry. Its reasoning is silent and inscrutable to the mortal mind, but no matter its choice, the result is final. While some legends claim that the Grim Reaper appears to everyone when they die, the truth is more disturbing. Such vigils are the providence of psychopomps, immortals charged with the protection and guidance of mortal souls through the afterlife. The Grim Reaper instead enacts the sinister agenda of Abaddon, where the Apocalypse Riders rule. Indeed, there are many similarities in shape and form between the Grim Reaper and Charon, the Rider of Death, but there are no recorded instance of these entities working together. Instead, the Grim Reaper serves as something of a manifestation of Abaddon itself, and in this regard, is believed to be an incarnation of the mysterious First Rider. When the Grim Reaper visits a world, it does so not as an angel of mercy but a relentless harvester of life. Those who fall to the Grim Reaper were not destined to die as much as they were selected, hunted, and murdered. Perhaps the most frightening detail surrounding the Grim Reaper's legend is its nature as a singular entity, for some believe that more than one exists in the Great Beyond. There are whispered rumors of a council of at least nine Grim Reapers, stalking reality and culling the living as in service to true entropy. According to the teachings of some death cults, the final goal of the Grim Reaper is to end the cycle of life and death and serve as a silent lord of an empty universe. The timber body of a second spawn cracks with each movement, as if its very frame protests its abominable mobility. Grown from [arboreals](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=364) native to the [Plane of Wood](/Planes.aspx?ID=25), the greatest of the second spawn—in effect, the “First Spawn”—is [Treerazer's](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3218) mobile fortress, the Witchbole. **[Recall Knowledge - Elemental](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35), [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43)): DC 47 **[Recall Knowledge - Fiend](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46)): DC 47 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 45 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 42 [Second Spawn](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3792) **Source** [Pathfinder #212: A Voice in the Blight](/Sources.aspx?ID=255) pg. 85 **Perception** +36; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59) **Languages** [Chthonian](/Languages.aspx?ID=114), [Muan](/Languages.aspx?ID=108); [telepathy](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=79) 100 feet **Skills** [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) +39, [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38) +35, [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43) +36, [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=48) +35 **Str** +10 **Dex** +6 **Con** +10 **Int** +0 **Wis** +7 **Cha** +6 --- **AC** 45 **Fort** +39 **Ref** +33 **Will** +36 **HP** 500 **Immunities** [paralyzed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=85), [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=669), [sleep](/Traits.aspx?ID=696) **Resistances** bludgeoning 20, piercing 20 **Weaknesses** [axes](/WeaponGroups.aspx?ID=1) 20, [fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=604) 20, [holy](/Traits.aspx?ID=517) 20 **Spray Sap** **Trigger** The second spawn takes damage; **Effect** A spray of bloody sap spurts from the second spawn's wound, targeting a creature within 30 feet of the second spawn's choice. That creature takes 10d6 poison damage (DC 41 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Fortitude save) and is exposed to corrupting sap. --- **Speed** 20 feet **Melee** branch +39 ([reach 20 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)), **Damage** 4d12+18 bludgeoning plus [Improved Knockdown](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=66) **Ranged** spirit splinter +39 ([Brutal](/Traits.aspx?ID=249), [Propulsive](/Traits.aspx?ID=191), [range increment 120 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=248), [Unholy](/Traits.aspx?ID=521)), **Damage** 4d4+13 piercing plus 2d6 spirit and corrupting sap **Corrupting Sap** ([Divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=48), [Incapacitation](/Traits.aspx?ID=93), [Mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=106)) The first time in a round a creature is exposed to the second spawn's corrupting sap, the creature must attempt a DC 44 Will save.
**Critical Success** The creature is unaffected, and is temporarily immune to corrupting sap for 1 minute.
**Success** Intrusive fiendish thoughts and cruel urges well up in the creature's mind, causing the creature to become [off-guard](/Conditions.aspx?ID=58) until the end of its next turn.
**Failure** The creature is [confused](/Conditions.aspx?ID=63) for 1 minute.
**Critical Failure** The creature is [controlled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=64) by the second spawn for 1 minute.

Tor linnorms dwell in the tallest volcanic mountains, either within naturally formed caverns or molten craters. A tor linnorm's temper can be as hot and destructive as the magma the creature resembles. **[Recall Knowledge - Dragon](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35)): DC 44 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 42 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 39 [Tor Linnorm](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3086) **Source** [Monster Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=221) pg. 222 1.1 **Perception** +37; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59), [scent](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=74) ([imprecise](/Rules.aspx?ID=412)) 60 feet, [_truesight_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1727) **Languages** [Aklo](/Languages.aspx?ID=13), [Draconic](/Languages.aspx?ID=2), [Fey](/Languages.aspx?ID=119) **Skills** [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=1) +35, [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) +40, [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15) +37 **Str** +11 **Dex** +8 **Con** +9 **Int** -1 **Wis** +8 **Cha** +9 --- **AC** 47 **Fort** +38 **Ref** +35 **Will** +33 +1 status to all saves vs. [magic](/Traits.aspx?ID=644) **HP** 440 , regeneration 20 (deactivated by [cold iron](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2916)) **Immunities** [curse](/Traits.aspx?ID=566), [fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=604), [paralyzed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=85), [sleep](/Traits.aspx?ID=696) **Weaknesses** cold iron 15 **Curse of Boiling Blood** ([curse](/Traits.aspx?ID=566), [fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=604), [primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=676)) When a creature slays the linnorm, it must succeed at a DC 48 Will save or gain weakness to fire 20 and [slowed 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=92) from the agonizing pain it now endures at all times, with an unlimited duration. As long as a character continues to suffer this curse, its slowed condition can never be reduced below slowed 1.
**Lava Affinity** The linnorm can breathe and swim freely while submerged in lava and magma.
**[Reactive Strike](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=48)** Tail only. --- **Speed** 35 feet, climb 35 feet, fly 100 feet, swim 60 feet; [_unfettered movement_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1732) **Melee** jaws +40 ([reach 30 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192), [Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103)), **Damage** 4d12+19 piercing plus tor linnorm venom **Melee** claw +40 ([reach 30 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192), [Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103)), **Damage** 4d8+19 slashing **Melee** tail +40 ([reach 30 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192), [Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103)), **Damage** 4d6+19 bludgeoning plus [Improved Grab](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=66) **Primal Innate Spells** DC 44 - **8th** [Truesight](/Spells.aspx?ID=1727) - **Constant (9th)** [Unfettered Movement](/Spells.aspx?ID=1732) **[Constrict](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=57)** 3d6+21 bludgeoning, DC 46 **Pyroclastic Breath** ([Fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=72), [Primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=134)) The tor linnorm expels a 60-foot cone of flame and ash dealing 20d6 fire damage to creatures within the area (DC 46 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save). The linnorm can't use Pyroclastic Breath again for 1d4 rounds. At the start of the tor linnorm's next turn, the area of the Pyroclastic Breath is covered in thick, scorching smoke that burns both the lungs and eyes, dealing an additional 10d6 fire damage to all creatures in the area (DC 46 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save). A creature that spends an entire round in the smoke with open eyes must succeed at a DC 44 Fortitude save or be [blinded](/Conditions.aspx?ID=59) for 1 minute. markdown:
Vulot is nascent demon lord of lies, loss of identity, and suffocation. If one of their forms is ever destroyed, they are able to reincorporate as one of their many stolen identities a day later. **[Recall Knowledge - Fiend](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46)): DC 52 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 50 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 47 [Vulot](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3404) **Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 177 **Perception** +38; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59), many eyes in many places, [_truesight_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1727) **Languages** [Chthonian](/Languages.aspx?ID=114), [Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1), [Draconic](/Languages.aspx?ID=2), [Empyrean](/Languages.aspx?ID=115); all languages spoken by their collective identities; [telepathy](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=79) 200 feet (unlimited range to other stolen identities worn by cultists of Vulot) **Skills** [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38) +43, [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39) +40, [Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=47) +40, [Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=50) +40 **Str** +4 **Dex** +6 **Con** +4 **Int** +7 **Wis** +7 **Cha** +10 **Absolute Surety** Vulot is dependent on deception and charm to achieve their goals. If Vulot fails to deceive someone, for example failing the [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38) check associated with a [_mislead_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1605) spell to convince an observer that an action came from the duplicate, Vulot takes 4d6 mental damage. This damage ignores Vulot's usual immunity.
**Many Eyes in Many Places** Vulot can extend their senses through any cultist wearing one of their stolen identities as long as the cultist is in [the Universe](/Planes.aspx?ID=26) or the [Outer Rifts](/Planes.aspx?ID=45). Vulot can't maintain their attention through more than three cultists at one time. Vulot can't speak through these cultists. --- **AC** 46 **Fort** +32 **Ref** +35 **Will** +38 **HP** 425 **Immunities** [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647), mythic immunity **Weaknesses** [cold iron](/Equipment.aspx?ID=375) 10, [holy](/Traits.aspx?ID=517) 15 **Another Face** When Vulot is reduced to 0 Hit Points, they regenerate themself from a stolen identity of their choice in 24 hours. If Vulot has no stolen identities remaining or is otherwise unable to reach them, they are killed permanently.
**Mythic Immunity** Vulot is immune to harmful spells cast by non-[mythic](/Traits.aspx?ID=835) creatures, Strikes made with non-mythic weapons, and unarmed Strikes from non-mythic characters.
**Suffocated by a Thousand Breaths** ([aura](/Traits.aspx?ID=542), [incapacitation](/Traits.aspx?ID=631)) 30 feet. Vulot's breath-stealing influence radiates out from their body, causing victims to feel like they are being smothered. Any creature that starts its turn within the aura must attempt a DC 41 Fortitude save.
**Critical Success**; The creature is unaffected.
**Success**; The creature becomes short of breath and is [off-guard](/Conditions.aspx?ID=58) until the beginning of its next turn.
**Failure** The creature finds it very difficult to catch its breath. It can't speak or use [auditory](/Traits.aspx?ID=541) actions until the beginning of its next turn; this prevents it from casting spells that don't have the [subtle](/Traits.aspx?ID=522) trait.
**Critical Failure** All the air immediately leaves the creature's lungs and it begins to [suffocate](/Rules.aspx?ID=2436). When it succeeds at the saving throw to regain consciousness at the end of its turn, it becomes [fatigued](/Conditions.aspx?ID=73) until it gets a full night's rest.
**Perfect Mimicry** ([magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=644), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647)) **Trigger** A spell is cast within 60 feet of Vulot; **Effect** Vulot copies the spell and may cast it once by spending a Mythic Point within the next 24 hours. Vulot can't hold more than two copied spells at one time. --- **Speed** 30 feet **Melee** claw +37 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [Finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=179), [Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103), [Unholy](/Traits.aspx?ID=521)), **Damage** 4d8+14 slashing plus 2d6 bleed **Ranged** thought spike +37 ([Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103), [Mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=106), [range increment 120 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=248), [Unholy](/Traits.aspx?ID=521)), **Damage** 4d6+14 mental plus steal thoughts **Divine Innate Spells** DC 44 - **Cantrips (10th)** [Daze](/Spells.aspx?ID=61), [Figment](/Spells.aspx?ID=1528) - **5th** [Translocate](/Spells.aspx?ID=1724) (at will) - **6th** [Mislead](/Spells.aspx?ID=199) (×3), [Repulsion](/Spells.aspx?ID=254) - **7th** [Divine Decree](/Spells.aspx?ID=82) (×2) - **9th** [Overwhelming Presence](/Spells.aspx?ID=212) - **10th** [Dominate](/Spells.aspx?ID=87), [Manifestation](/Spells.aspx?ID=1592), [Shadow Blast](/Spells.aspx?ID=273) (×2) - **Constant (6th)** [Truesight](/Spells.aspx?ID=1727) **Rituals** DC 44 - **1st** [Demonic Pact](/Rituals.aspx?ID=142) **Mythic Power** 3 Mythic Points
  • _Recharge Spell_ ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Cost** 1 Mythic Point; **Effect** Vulot gains an additional use of any of their innate spells.
  • _Remove a Condition_ ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Cost** 1 Mythic Point; **Effect** Vulot removes any one condition currently affecting them.
**Steal Face** **Cost** 1 Mythic Point; **Effect** Vulot makes a claw Strike. On a hit, Vulot attempts a Deception check against the target's Will DC to steal that creature's face; on a critical hit, Vulot treats the result of their Deception check as one degree of success higher. On a success, Vulot steals the target's face for 1d4 rounds (1 minute on a critical success); a creature whose face has been stolen isn't considered an ally by any creature. **Steal Thoughts** ([Emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=60), [Mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=106)) Vulot's mental attacks can confuse and disorient. A creature struck by Vulot's thought spike must attempt a DC 44 Will save. A creature [stupefied](/Conditions.aspx?ID=94) by this effect is [off-guard](/Conditions.aspx?ID=58) to Vulot's Steal Face ability.
**Critical Success** The creature is unaffected.
**Success** The creature becomes stupefied 1 for 1 round.
**Failure** The creature becomes stupefied 1 for 1 minute. If it's already stupefied, its stupefied value increases by 1 instead (to a maximum of stupefied 4).
**Critical Failure** As failure, plus the creature is [confused](/Conditions.aspx?ID=63) for 1 minute.

Spawns of Jeharlu typically drift in the skies above the realm of Jeharlu, content to enjoy blasphemous and horrific dreams and fancies while they watch the fungal world below for intruders. It isn't that far off the mark to equate a spawn of Jeharlu to a white blood cell, except in this case the body they defend is Jeharlu. Encountered beyond this realm, a spawn's role reverses—now they play the part of infective agents, seeking to spread corruption through soil, vegetation, and fleshy life wherever they go. **[Recall Knowledge - Fiend](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46)): DC 49 **[Recall Knowledge - Fungus](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43)): DC 49 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 47 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 44 [Spawn Of Jeharlu](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3796) **Source** [Pathfinder #212: A Voice in the Blight](/Sources.aspx?ID=255) pg. 89 **Perception** +40; [greater darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59), scent purity ([precise](/Rules.aspx?ID=411)) 120 feet, [_truesight_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1727) **Languages** [Chthonian](/Languages.aspx?ID=114) **Skills** [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=34) +36, [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) +43, [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43) +40, [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46) +42 **Str** +11 **Dex** +6 **Con** +8 **Int** +4 **Wis** +10 **Cha** +6 **Scent Purity** A spawn of Jeharlu can detect [holy](/Traits.aspx?ID=517) creatures with [scent](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=74) as a precise sense to 120 feet. --- **AC** 46 [all-around vision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=49) **Fort** +34 **Ref** +38 **Will** +40 **HP** 540 **Immunities** [disease](/Traits.aspx?ID=578), [paralyzed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=85), [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=669) **Weaknesses** [cold iron](/Equipment.aspx?ID=375) 20, [holy](/Traits.aspx?ID=517) 20 **Hallucinatory Spores** ([aura](/Traits.aspx?ID=542), [divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=579), [emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=590), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647)) 60 feet. The spawn is surrounded by spores that manipulate the thoughts of those exposed. When a creature ends its turn in the aura and isn't [holding its breath](/Rules.aspx?ID=2436), it must attempt a DC 42 Will save. If it fails, it becomes [confused](/Conditions.aspx?ID=63) until the end of its next turn (or for 1 minute on a critical failure).
**Grasping Strands** **Trigger** A creature within 60 feet of the spawn of Jeharlu uses a [move](/Traits.aspx?ID=658) action or leaves a square during a move action it's using; **Effect** A flurry of tendrils whips out, allowing the spawn of Jeharlu to attempt an [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) check to [Grapple](/Actions.aspx?ID=2376) the triggering creature. The spawn can [Pull](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=71) the creature if it remains grappled on its next turn. --- **Speed** 20 feet, fly 40 feet **Melee** tentacle +39 ([Forceful](/Traits.aspx?ID=180), [Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103), [reach 20 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192), [Unholy](/Traits.aspx?ID=521), [versatile P](/Traits.aspx?ID=200)), **Damage** 4d12+19 bludgeoning plus [Improved Grab](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=66) **Primal Innate Spells** DC 42, attack +34 - **Cantrips (9th)** [Caustic Blast](/Spells.aspx?ID=1461), [Tangle Vine](/Spells.aspx?ID=1713) - **4th** [Translocate](/Spells.aspx?ID=1724) (at will) - **5th** [Translocate](/Spells.aspx?ID=1724) - **8th** [Regenerate](/Spells.aspx?ID=248), [Teleport](/Spells.aspx?ID=338) (at will) - **9th** [Execute](/Spells.aspx?ID=1519), [Toxic Cloud](/Spells.aspx?ID=1722) (×3) - **10th** [Massacre](/Spells.aspx?ID=186) - **Constant (10th)** [Truesight](/Spells.aspx?ID=1727) **Soul** ([Death](/Traits.aspx?ID=40), [Divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=48)) The spawn extends feeding stalks to drain the spirit and life from an adjacent [restrained](/Conditions.aspx?ID=90) or helpless creature. The target takes 10d6 spirit damage and must attempt a DC 45 Will save. If the damage from Drain Soul reduces a creature to 0 Hit Points, that creature dies instantly.
**Critical Success** The target takes no damage.
**Success** The target takes half damage and becomes [drained 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=68).
**Failure** The target takes full damage and is drained 2. If it was already drained, its drained condition value increases by 1 to a maximum of drained 4.
**Critical Failure** As failure, but double damage and the target becomes [doomed 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=67). **[Pull](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=71)** 30 feet.

Before he became a deity, [Norgorber](/Deities.aspx?ID=289) gained Venomfist's eternal service by giving the disgraced [faydhaan shuyookh](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2662) poisons to exact revenge upon those who stripped the genie of their status. The vengeance transformed Venomfist into what they are now, an outcome Norgorber cautioned of, yet one Venomfist doesn't regret. Today in Duskfathom, Venomfist resides in the Sky Sea as the perfect defender of the unnamed islands. When summoned to other planes, only a part of them leaves while their main body remains behind. Venomfist's vivid green body is a testament to all the deals for poisons made with mortals and immortals alike over millennia. **[Recall Knowledge - Elemental](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35), [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43)): DC 54 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 52 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 49 [Venomfist](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3751) **Source** [Pathfinder #206: Bring the House Down](/Sources.aspx?ID=247) pg. 88 **Perception** +40; [greater darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59), [wavesense](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=84) ([precise](/Rules.aspx?ID=411)) 120 feet **Languages** [Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1), [Muan](/Languages.aspx?ID=108), [Petran](/Languages.aspx?ID=109), [Pyric](/Languages.aspx?ID=110), [Sussuran](/Languages.aspx?ID=111), [Talican](/Languages.aspx?ID=112), [Thalassic](/Languages.aspx?ID=113); [telepathy](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=79) 100 feet, [_truespeech_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1728) **Skills** [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) +43, [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=37) +39, [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39) +36, [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=40) +38, [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43) +38, [Norgorber Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) +41, [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46) +40, [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=48) +38 **Str** +11 **Dex** +8 **Con** +10 **Int** +9 **Wis** +8 **Cha** +6 --- **AC** 48 **Fort** +42 **Ref** +34 **Will** +36 **HP** 430 **Immunities** bleed, [paralyzed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=85), [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=669), [sleep](/Traits.aspx?ID=696) **Resistances** [acid](/Traits.aspx?ID=524) 20, bludgeoning 20, [fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=604) 20 **Toxic Downpour** ([aura](/Traits.aspx?ID=542), [primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=676)) Venomfist's presence alters the weather within 2 miles to heavy rainfall as long as they're located in a sizable body of water. When they become hostile, the rain in a 120-foot emanation from them becomes highly toxic and deals 8d8 poison damage (DC 42 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Fortitude half) to all creatures in the area.
**Vortex** ([aura](/Traits.aspx?ID=542), [water](/Traits.aspx?ID=732)) 120 feet. Water in the area that is in the same body of water as Venomfist is [difficult terrain](/Rules.aspx?ID=453) for [Swimming](/Actions.aspx?ID=2381) creatures that don't have the [water](/Traits.aspx?ID=732) trait. --- **Speed** 40 feet, swim 120 feet **Melee** fist +42 ([Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103), [reach 20 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)), **Damage** 4d6+21 bludgeoning plus 4d6 poison and [Improved Grab](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=66) **Divine Innate Spells** DC 45 - **Cantrips (9th)** [Caustic Blast](/Spells.aspx?ID=1461) - **8th** [Hydraulic Push](/Spells.aspx?ID=154) (at will) - **9th** [Toxic Cloud](/Spells.aspx?ID=1722), [Wrathful Storm](/Spells.aspx?ID=1759) - **10th** [Cataclysm](/Spells.aspx?ID=32) - **Constant (10th)** [Truesight](/Spells.aspx?ID=1727), [Truespeech](/Spells.aspx?ID=1728) **[Constrict](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=57)** 4d6 bludgeoning and 4d6 poison, DC 45 **Create Poison** **Frequency** once per day; **Effect** Venomfist transforms a portion of their watery body into a single dose of any type of common [poison](/Equipment.aspx?Category=6&Subcategory=9) of 20th level or lower—[tears of death](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3348) is their favorite. If they're holding a container, they can create the poison within that container, at which point the poison remains viable for 24 hours before it reverts to water. Alternatively, they can apply a [contact](/Traits.aspx?ID=565) or [injury](/Traits.aspx?ID=635)-created poison to their fist. **Surge** Venomfist expands their space to fill the area of their vortex. Creatures within the aura take 6d12+6 bludgeoning damage and 6d12+6 poison damage with a DC 45 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Fortitude save. A creature that fails this save is [pushed](/Rules.aspx?ID=451) 40 feet. Venomfist then retracts to their former space and cannot use Surge again for 1d4 rounds.

description:
Before he became a deity, [Norgorber](/Deities.aspx?ID=289) gained Venomfist's eternal service by giving the disgraced [faydhaan shuyookh](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2662) poisons to exact revenge upon those who stripped the genie of their status. The vengeance transformed Venomfist into what they are now, an outcome Norgorber cautioned of, yet one Venomfist doesn't regret.

 Today in Duskfathom, Venomfist resides in the Sky Sea as the perfect defender of the unnamed islands. When summoned to other planes, only a part of them leaves while their main body remains behind. Venomfist's vivid green body is a testament to all the deals for poisons made with mortals and immortals alike over millennia.

If the creature is still buried at the end of its turn, it takes 5d10 bludgeoning damage. **Called to Depths** The depths call to the warden, especially as they move through the air. When they [Long Jump](/Actions.aspx?ID=2378), they can use any unused movement from the Long Jump to [Burrow](/Actions.aspx?ID=2310). Additionally, the warden can Burrow through any earthen matter, including rock. When they do so, they move at their full burrow Speed. **Erupting Jump** ([Primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=134)) The warden draws out a stream of lava, then jumps off the solidifying mass as it cools. The warden [Leaps](/Actions.aspx?ID=2298) up to twice their Speed. When they land, the force of the impact deals 6d12 bludgeoning damage to all creatures within a 15-foot emanation with a DC 42 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Fortitude save. On a critical failure, the creature is also [pushed](/Rules.aspx?ID=451) 10 feet away from the warden. **Obsidian Cage** Rapidly cooling obsidian clings to the target's body and stiffens around their limbs. The target must attempt a DC 42 Reflex save. On a failure, the target is [immobilized](/Conditions.aspx?ID=81) until they [Escape](/Actions.aspx?ID=2296) (DC 42). On a critical failure, the target is [off-guard](/Conditions.aspx?ID=58) for as long as they remain immobilized. **Vibratory Excavation** ([Manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104), [Primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=134)) The warden screeches with a resonant call that tears apart earth and stone. They create a 10-foot-square, 50-foot-deep pit in earthen material or stone within 60 feet. **Wall Cling** The Warden of Caverns and Burrows clings to surfaces with their segmented feet. They do not need to use a hand to hold on to walls or ceilings.

**Warden's Crown** --- **AC** 47 **Fort** +39 **Ref** +36 **Will** +33 +1 to all saves vs. [primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=676) **HP** 540 **Immunities** [controlled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=64), [emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=590), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647), [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=669), precision **Resistances** bludgeoning 20, [cold](/Traits.aspx?ID=555) 20 **Weaknesses** [electricity](/Traits.aspx?ID=586) 15 **Bioluminescent Maelstrom** ([aura](/Traits.aspx?ID=542), [primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=676), [visual](/Traits.aspx?ID=727), [water](/Traits.aspx?ID=732)) 30 feet. Creatures in the area take 18d8 bludgeoning damage (DC 45 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Fortitude save). The warden can either [push or pull](/Rules.aspx?ID=451), and all creatures that fail this save move up to 40 feet in the direction chosen. The warden can't use I Am The Tide again for 1d4 rounds. **What Lurks Beneath** The warden attacks with their tentacles six times.

Agyra is a massive kaiju who protects Spinescar Island and its inhabitants. **[Recall Knowledge - Beast](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35), [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43)): DC 56 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 54 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 51 [Agyra](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3406) **Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 189 **Perception** +38; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59), stormsight **Languages** [Tien](/Languages.aspx?ID=43); (can't speak any language) **Skills** [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=34) +43, [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) +41 **Str** +10 **Dex** +11 **Con** +9 **Int** -2 **Wis** +6 **Cha** +6 **Stormsight** Wind, precipitation, and clouds don't impair Agyra's vision; she ignores the [concealed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=62) condition from storms, mist, precipitation, and the like. --- **AC** 49 **Fort** +37 **Ref** +40 **Will** +34 mythic resilience (Fort and Ref) **HP** 475 , regeneration 30 **Immunities** [death](/Traits.aspx?ID=571) effects, [disease](/Traits.aspx?ID=578), [drained](/Conditions.aspx?ID=68), [electricity](/Traits.aspx?ID=586), [fear](/Traits.aspx?ID=598), mythic immunity, [paralyzed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=85) **Resistances** [acid](/Traits.aspx?ID=524) 20, [fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=604) 20, [sonic](/Traits.aspx?ID=697) 20 **Electrified Rebirth** ([electricity](/Traits.aspx?ID=586), [primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=676)) **Frequency** once per year; **Effect** When Agyra dies, her corpse crackles and sparks with electrical energy. Any creature that touches Agyra's body within 1 hour of her death takes 11d6 electricity damage ([basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) DC 43 Reflex save). After being dead for 1 minute, Agyra is immediately resurrected in the same place, at full health, with all abilities fully restored. She normally takes advantage of this rebirth to flee to safety, using Thunderous Departure to retreat. If Agyra has already died and been reborn in the same year, she remains permanently dead upon being slain a second time.
**[Mythic Immunity](/Rules.aspx?ID=3341)** Strikes
**Mythic Resilience** Agyra treats her saving throws with Fortitude and Reflex saves as one step better than they actually are (so a critical failure is a failure, a failure is a success, and a success is a critical success). Whenever a character rolls a critical hit against Agyra, they must reroll the attack roll and take the new result. --- **Speed** 40 feet, fly 60 feet **Melee** talon +40 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103), [reach 15 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)), **Damage** 4d10+14 slashing plus 2d8 electricity **Melee** jaws +40 ([Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103), [reach 10 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)), **Damage** 3d12+14 piercing plus 2d8 electricity **Melee** tail +40 ([deadly d10](/Traits.aspx?ID=174), [Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103), [reach 20 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)), **Damage** 4d8+14 bludgeoning plus 2d6 [persistent bleed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29) **Ranged** spike +42 ([Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103), [range increment 60 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=248)), **Damage** 7d6+10 piercing **Mythic Power** 3 Mythic Points
  • _Recharge Ability_ ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Cost** 1 Mythic Point; **Effect** Agyra gains an additional use of lightning breath.
  • _Remove a Condition_ ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Cost** 1 Mythic Point; **Effect** Agyra removes any one condition currently affecting her.
**Blinding Flash** ([Light](/Traits.aspx?ID=100), [Manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104), [Primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=134), [Visual](/Traits.aspx?ID=163)) **Cost** 1 Mythic Point; **Effect** By spreading her wings while she stands upon the ground, Agyra can create a blinding flash of light that targets all creatures within 100 feet. Affected creatures must succeed at a DC 43 Fortitude check.
**Critical Success** The target is unaffected.
**Success** The target is [dazzled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=65) and [stupefied 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=94) for 1d4 rounds.
**Failure** The target is [blinded](/Conditions.aspx?ID=59) and stupefied 2 for 1 minute.
**Critical Failure** The target is blinded and stupefied 2 for 10 minutes. **Conjure Hurricane** ([Air](/Traits.aspx?ID=5), [Manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104), [Primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=134)) **Frequency** once per day; **Cost** 1 Mythic Point; **Effect** Agyra generates a hurricane that spreads across a 4-mile radius and lasts 24 hours, with a 500-foot calm eye of the storm at its center. Agyra is at the center of this hurricane when it is formed, but it moves normally (according to surrounding weather conditions and the GM's discretion) afterward. **Lightning Breath** ([Electricity](/Traits.aspx?ID=56), [Primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=134)) Agyra exhales a line of electricity from each of her two heads. Each line is 120 feet long and 10 feet wide, and the two lines may be pointed in different directions. A creature in a line takes 22d6 electricity damage ([basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) DC 44 Reflex save). On a failed save, the target is also [slowed 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=92) for 1d4 rounds. A creature can be affected only once by a line, even if they are in an overlapping area. A character slain by Agyra's Lightning Breath remains electrified for 2d4 rounds after death. A creature touching such a corpse takes 3d6 electricity damage (no save). Agyra can't use Lightning Breath for 1d4 rounds. **Stormflight** Agyra can move in strong winds with ease. She doesn't treat wind as [difficult terrain](/Rules.aspx?ID=453) or need to [Maneuver in Flight](/Actions.aspx?ID=2371) in high winds. **Thunderous Departure** ([Primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=134), [Sonic](/Traits.aspx?ID=147)) **Frequency** once per day; **Effect** Agyra Flies in a straight line at incredible speed, moving at least 120 feet but up to 1 mile. This movement doesn't provoke reactions. Her departure leaves behind a thunderous sonic boom, creating a 100-foot burst centered on her point of departure. All creatures in the area take 15d10 sonic damage ([basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) DC 46 Fortitude save). A creature who fails is also knocked [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=88), and a creature who critically fails is knocked prone and [deafened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=66) permanently.

darkvision, stormsight languages tien; (can't speak any language) skills acrobatics +43, athletics +41 str +10 dex +11 con +9 int -2 wis +6 cha +6 stormsight wind, precipitation, and clouds don't impair agyra's vision; she ignores the concealed condition from storms, mist, precipitation, and the like. --- ac 49 fort +37 ref +40 will +34 mythic resilience (fort and ref) hp 475 , regeneration 30 immunities death effects, disease, drained, electricity, fear, mythic immunity, paralyzed resistances acid 20, fire 20, sonic 20 electrified rebirth (electricity, primal) frequency once per year; effect when agyra dies, her corpse crackles and sparks with electrical energy. any creature that touches agyra's body within 1 hour of her death takes 11d6 electricity damage (basic dc 43 reflex save). after being dead for 1 minute, agyra is immediately resurrected in the same place, at full health, with all abilities fully restored. she normally takes advantage of this rebirth to flee to safety, using thunderous departure to retreat. if agyra has already died and been reborn in the same year, she remains permanently dead upon being slain a second time. mythic immunity strikes mythic resilience agyra treats her saving throws with fortitude and reflex saves as one step better than they actually are (so a critical failure is a failure, a failure is a success, and a success is a critical success). whenever a character rolls a critical hit against agyra, they must reroll the attack roll and take the new result. --- speed 40 feet, fly 60 feet melee single action talon +40 (agile, magical, reach 15 feet), damage 4d10+14 slashing plus 2d8 electricity melee single action jaws +40 (magical, reach 10 feet), damage 3d12+14 piercing plus 2d8 electricity melee single action tail +40 (deadly d10, magical, reach 20 feet), damage 4d8+14 bludgeoning plus 2d6 persistent bleed ranged single action spike +42 (magical, range increment 60 feet), damage 7d6+10 piercing mythic power 3 mythic points recharge ability single action (concentrate) cost 1 mythic point; effect agyra gains an additional use of lightning breath. remove a condition single action (concentrate) cost 1 mythic point; effect agyra removes any one condition currently affecting her. blinding flash three actions (light, manipulate, primal, visual) cost 1 mythic point; effect by spreading her wings while she stands upon the ground, agyra can create a blinding flash of light that targets all creatures within 100 feet. affected creatures must succeed at a dc 43 fortitude check. critical success the target is unaffected. success the target is dazzled and stupefied 1 for 1d4 rounds. failure the target is blinded and stupefied 2 for 1 minute. critical failure the target is blinded and stupefied 2 for 10 minutes. conjure hurricane three actions (air, manipulate, primal) frequency once per day; cost 1 mythic point; effect agyra generates a hurricane that spreads across a 4-mile radius and lasts 24 hours, with a 500-foot calm eye of the storm at its center. agyra is at the center of this hurricane when it is formed, but it moves normally (according to surrounding weather conditions and the gm's discretion) afterward. lightning breath two actions (electricity, primal) agyra exhales a line of electricity from each of her two heads. each line is 120 feet long and 10 feet wide, and the two lines may be pointed in different directions. a creature in a line takes 22d6 electricity damage (basic dc 44 reflex save). on a failed save, the target is also slowed 1 for 1d4 rounds. a creature can be affected only once by a line, even if they are in an overlapping area. a character slain by agyra's lightning breath remains electrified for 2d4 rounds after death. a creature touching such a corpse takes 3d6 electricity damage (no save). agyra can't use lightning breath for 1d4 rounds. stormflight agyra can move in strong winds with ease. she doesn't treat wind as difficult terrain or need to maneuver in flight in high winds. thunderous departure three actions (primal, sonic) frequency once per day; effect agyra flies in a straight line at incredible speed, moving at least 120 feet but up to 1 mile. this movement doesn't provoke reactions. her departure leaves behind a thunderous sonic boom, creating a 100-foot burst centered on her point of departure. all creatures in the area take 15d10 sonic damage (basic dc 46 fortitude save). a creature who fails is also knocked prone, and a creature who critically fails is knocked prone and deafened permanently.

Vault builders still possess the full power [Sairazul](/Deities.aspx?ID=107) instilled in them, capable of creating new life and shaping the world around them. A vault builder's life span is several millennia, but their memories are preserved within a crystalline generation stone when they die to be placed inside a newly constructed vault builder body. **[Recall Knowledge - Elemental](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=2), [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=10)): DC 51 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 49 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 46 [Vault Builder](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2630) **Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 109 2.0 **Perception** +37; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=12), [tremorsense](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=40) ([imprecise](/Rules.aspx?ID=412)) 120 feet **Languages** [Orvian](/Languages.aspx?ID=120), [Petran](/Languages.aspx?ID=109); [telepathy](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=37) 300 feet **Skills** [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=1) +39, [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=2) +42, [Architecture Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8) +42, [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) +39, [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=4) +44, [Engineering Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8) +42, [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=10) +37, [Planar Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8) +42, [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15) +41, [Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=17) +39 **Str** +8 **Dex** +10 **Con** +7 **Int** +11 **Wis** +6 **Cha** +8 **Craft Crystal Wand** ([exploration](/Traits.aspx?ID=66)) **Frequency** twice per day; **Effect** The vault builder spends 10 minutes creating a magic wand out of radioactive green crystal, containing any 8th-rank or lower [earth](/Traits.aspx?ID=55) spell of their choice. The wand can be used by other creatures, but it crumbles to sand at the end of the day and has no monetary value. The vault builder can expend both daily uses to instead make a _+3 [greater striking](/Equipment.aspx?ID=280) [major staff of earth](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2261)_.
**Item Caster** The vault builder can Cast a Spell from any item (such as a staff or wand) as though it were on their spell list, but the spell can be 8th-rank or lower. --- **AC** 47 **Fort** +36 **Ref** +41 **Will** +35 +1 status to all saves vs. spells ( +4 status vs. [earth](/Traits.aspx?ID=55)) **HP** 465 **Immunities** bleed, [paralyzed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=28), [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=126), [radiation](/Traits.aspx?ID=421), [sleep](/Traits.aspx?ID=145) **Resistances** physical 20 (except [adamantine](/Equipment.aspx?ID=374)) **[Reactive Strike](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=48)** --- **Speed** 35 feet, burrow 25 feet, climb 35 feet; earth glide **Melee** crystal staff +39 ([Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103), [Radiation](/Traits.aspx?ID=421), [two-hand d8](/Traits.aspx?ID=198)), **Damage** 4d4+12 bludgeoning plus 4d6 poison **Melee** crystal wand +37 ([Finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=179), [Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103), [Radiation](/Traits.aspx?ID=421)), **Damage** 4d4+12 piercing plus 4d6 poison **Melee** claw +37 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [Finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=179), [Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103)), **Damage** 5d10+12 slashing plus constraining crystal **Ranged** crystal shard +37 ([Earth](/Traits.aspx?ID=55), [Finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=179), [Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103), [range increment 100 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=248)), **Damage** 7d6+4 piercing **Arcane Prepared Spells** DC 50, attack +42 - **Cantrips (10th)** [Detect Magic](/Spells.aspx?ID=66), [Read Aura](/Spells.aspx?ID=246), [Scatter Scree](/Spells.aspx?ID=990), [Sigil](/Spells.aspx?ID=286), [Mage Hand](/Spells.aspx?ID=177) - **1st** [Ant Haul](/Spells.aspx?ID=13), [Quick Sort](/Spells.aspx?ID=978) (×2) - **2nd** [Knock](/Spells.aspx?ID=168), [Magnetic Attraction](/Spells.aspx?ID=944), [Magnetic Repulsion](/Spells.aspx?ID=945) - **3rd** [Meld into Stone](/Spells.aspx?ID=188) (×2), [Mending](/Spells.aspx?ID=189) - **4th** [Clairvoyance](/Spells.aspx?ID=40), [Engrave Memory](/Spells.aspx?ID=1330), [Grasping Earth](/Spells.aspx?ID=1334) - **5th** [Blazing Fissure](/Spells.aspx?ID=870), [Creation](/Spells.aspx?ID=54), [See Invisibility](/Spells.aspx?ID=271) - **6th** [Pave Ground](/Spells.aspx?ID=1338), [Flesh to Stone](/Spells.aspx?ID=123), [Wall of Force](/Spells.aspx?ID=363) - **7th** [Fly](/Spells.aspx?ID=125), [Haste](/Spells.aspx?ID=147) (×2) - **8th** [Earthquake](/Spells.aspx?ID=95) (×2), [Stoneskin](/Spells.aspx?ID=312) - **9th** [Disintegrate](/Spells.aspx?ID=76) (×2), [Heaving Earth](/Spells.aspx?ID=1335) **Arcane Innate Spells** DC 50, attack +42 - **4th** [Earthbind](/Spells.aspx?ID=94) (at will), [Shape Stone](/Spells.aspx?ID=276) (at will), [Dimension Door](/Spells.aspx?ID=69) (at will) - **8th** [Flesh to Stone](/Spells.aspx?ID=123), [Scrying](/Spells.aspx?ID=268), [Shatter](/Spells.aspx?ID=279) (at will), [Stone Tell](/Spells.aspx?ID=310) (at will), [Teleport](/Spells.aspx?ID=338), [Dimension Door](/Spells.aspx?ID=69) - **10th** [Summon Elemental](/Spells.aspx?ID=320) (earth only), [Wall of Stone](/Spells.aspx?ID=365) **Constraining Crystal** ([Earth](/Traits.aspx?ID=55), [Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103)) When the vault builder deals damage with a claw Strike, glowing green crystals cluster at the site of the attack. The target must succeed at a DC 31 Fortitude save or become [clumsy 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=3) for 1 hour (or clumsy 2 on a critical failure). If the creature is already clumsy due to constraining crystal, additional failures increase that clumsy value instead, to a maximum of clumsy 4. A target that fails its save while clumsy 4 is [petrified](/Conditions.aspx?ID=30) with an unlimited duration. **Crystal Burst** ([Arcane](/Traits.aspx?ID=11), [Earth](/Traits.aspx?ID=55)) An explosion of razor-sharp splinters deals 24d6 piercing damage in a 30-foot burst within 120 feet, with a DC 46 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save. The vault builder can't use Crystal Burst again for 1d4 rounds. **Earth Glide** The vault builder can [Burrow](/Actions.aspx?ID=93) through any earthen matter, including rock. When they do so, the vault builder moves at their full burrow Speed, leaving no tunnels or signs of their passing.

Once an [orc](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=454) god, Verex-That-Was has been reshaped into a towering creature of mangled flesh and bone. **[Recall Knowledge - Aberration](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=44)): DC 58 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 56 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 53 [Verex-That-Was](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3409) **Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 207 **Perception** +42; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59), [_truesight_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1727) **Languages** [Aklo](/Languages.aspx?ID=13), [Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1), [Orcish](/Languages.aspx?ID=9) **Skills** [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) +45, [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=40) +45 **Str** +12 **Dex** +9 **Con** +11 **Int** +7 **Wis** +7 **Cha** +4 --- **AC** 51 **Fort** +42 **Ref** +38 **Will** +36 mythic resilience (all saves) **HP** 550 , regeneration 30 (deactivated by sloughstone weapons) **Immunities** [acid](/Traits.aspx?ID=524), [death](/Traits.aspx?ID=571) effects, [disease](/Traits.aspx?ID=578), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647), mythic immunity, [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=669) **Resistances** [cold](/Traits.aspx?ID=555) 25, [fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=604) 25, physical 20 (except [sloughstone](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3515) and holy) **Weaknesses** [holy](/Traits.aspx?ID=517) 20 **[Frightful Presence](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=64)** ([aura](/Traits.aspx?ID=542), [emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=590), [fear](/Traits.aspx?ID=598), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647)) 150 feet, DC 45
**Mythic Immunity** Verex-That-Was is immune to harmful spells cast by non-mythic creatures, Strikes made with non-mythic weapons, and unarmed Strikes from non-mythic characters.

<title level="1" pfs="">[Zibik, Green Man of Decay and Fresh Starts](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3737)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

“[Zibik](/Deities.aspx?ID=685) shepherds death, and life follows.” A common greeting among Zibik's followers, this saying encompasses many aspects of the [green man](/Monsters.aspx?ID=1176)'s life and teachings. While typical green men concern themselves entirely with the wellbeing of plants, Zibik focuses on the persistent collapse and decomposition that allows environments to thrive. In many ways, he's the embodiment of a towering tree falling over, the loss of its expansive canopy allowing sunlight to reach a new generation of saplings. Fungus fascinates Zibik, and his long association with decay and regrowth has caused him to take on aspects of primal fungus.

 Ages ago, before the [Plane of Wood](/Planes.aspx?ID=25) was sealed off, Zibik traveled there hoping to study and understand how a plane of unfettered growth could sustain itself. While exploring [the Universe](/Planes.aspx?ID=26), he learned that many natural areas recovered from horrifying calamities to be stronger than before, while others stagnated after experiencing even mild changes to the environment. What allowed the Plane of Wood to eternally flourish? Did death and decomposition exist here as well, perhaps to an even greater degree? Or did the environment somehow thrive without natural cycles of decay? He learned much, but his investigations were short-lived, and he never returned to the Universe with his findings; the betrayal and conflict between the Elemental Lords sequestered the Plane of Wood, trapping Zibik there. However, these same events introduced [Ayrzul's Blight](/Diseases.aspx?ID=41), giving Zibik newfound purpose. The disease caused fascinating mutations, and even as it killed off swaths of plant life, it left new life in its wake.

 As the blight spread, eradicating entire ecosystems, Zibik's fascination turned to desperate terror; natural diseases are part of life, but Ayrzul's Blight is anything but natural. For thousands of years, he's fought the blight by destroying vibrant frontiers (forming the equivalent of firebreaks), decomposing afflicted material, and absorbing disease and radiation into his own body so that blighted areas might regrow. The cycle of fighting the blight (involving Zibik's own cyclical death and rebirth) has increasingly shaped his moral perspective; he sees that drastic action against a part is sometimes the only thing that can save the whole.

 Zibik focuses his efforts on remote areas of the plane, rarely interacting with settlements except to warn them of his intentions if they happen to be near an ecosystem he plans to transform. He often spends decades in a single blighted region before moving on. The Elemental Lords of Wood know to leave Zibik alone; he's largely helping the plane thrive, even when he must make sacrifices, and confronting him poses certain risks due to the tremendous levels of disease and blight afflicting the green man at any given time. Zibik's appearance shifts as he progresses through cycles of decay and regrowth. After rejuvenating, he looks stout and healthy, his stride and posture almost regal. As he absorbs diseases from the environment, sickly fungus sprouts all over his body, weighing him down and draining his energy, both physically and spiritually. However he appears, his voice always carries the same grim determination and pride. 

<title level="2" right="">Campaign Role</title> Zibik is by far the most powerful being the PCs encounter in the Wardens of Wildwood campaign. Thankfully for the PCs, they aren't likely to face him in combat, though he poses a grave threat to the Verduran Forest and nearby nations. In the adventure's final scene, the PCs must convince Zibik that Ruzadoya Swiftmane has deceived him. Should they fail to counter the graveknight's deceptive narratives about Avistan and its people, Zibik is sure to make his way through the portal to the Isle of Arenway. Once he does, few could stand in his way. In his current state, he would spread destruction, death, and disease. The blight would spread. Andoran and Taldor would be the first nations impacted, but without swift and decisive action, they would fail to stop Zibik. Most living things would be killed outright, survivors would experience agonizing disease, and decades of suffering would follow.

 But in time, life would return to southern Avistan, the region forever transformed into something new. Something better. Stronger. More resilient. Zibik, his work accomplished, would be long gone—unless the people of Avistan proved Ruzadoya Swiftmane was right all along. Should they mount an offensive against Zibik, rather than letting him destroy the region and bring about new life, he might decide he has no choice but to stay on Golarion a while longer. So be it. Zibik shepherds death, and life follows.

“[Zibik](/Deities.aspx?ID=685) shepherds death, and life follows.” A common greeting among Zibik's followers, this saying encompasses many aspects of the [green man](/Monsters.aspx?ID=1176)'s life and teachings. While typical green men concern themselves entirely with the wellbeing of plants, Zibik focuses on the persistent collapse and decomposition that allows environments to thrive. In many ways, he's the embodiment of a towering tree falling over, the loss of its expansive canopy allowing sunlight to reach a new generation of saplings. Fungus fascinates Zibik, and his long association with decay and regrowth has caused him to take on aspects of primal fungus.

 Ages ago, before the [Plane of Wood](/Planes.aspx?ID=25) was sealed off, Zibik traveled there hoping to study and understand how a plane of unfettered growth could sustain itself. While exploring [the Universe](/Planes.aspx?ID=26), he learned that many natural areas recovered from horrifying calamities to be stronger than before, while others stagnated after experiencing even mild changes to the environment. What allowed the Plane of Wood to eternally flourish? Did death and decomposition exist here as well, perhaps to an even greater degree? Or did the environment somehow thrive without natural cycles of decay? He learned much, but his investigations were short-lived, and he never returned to the Universe with his findings; the betrayal and conflict between the Elemental Lords sequestered the Plane of Wood, trapping Zibik there. However, these same events introduced [Ayrzul's Blight](/Diseases.aspx?ID=41), giving Zibik newfound purpose. The disease caused fascinating mutations, and even as it killed off swaths of plant life, it left new life in its wake.

 As the blight spread, eradicating entire ecosystems, Zibik's fascination turned to desperate terror; natural diseases are part of life, but Ayrzul's Blight is anything but natural. For thousands of years, he's fought the blight by destroying vibrant frontiers (forming the equivalent of firebreaks), decomposing afflicted material, and absorbing disease and radiation into his own body so that blighted areas might regrow. The cycle of fighting the blight (involving Zibik's own cyclical death and rebirth) has increasingly shaped his moral perspective; he sees that drastic action against a part is sometimes the only thing that can save the whole.

 Zibik focuses his efforts on remote areas of the plane, rarely interacting with settlements except to warn them of his intentions if they happen to be near an ecosystem he plans to transform. He often spends decades in a single blighted region before moving on. The Elemental Lords of Wood know to leave Zibik alone; he's largely helping the plane thrive, even when he must make sacrifices, and confronting him poses certain risks due to the tremendous levels of disease and blight afflicting the green man at any given time. Zibik's appearance shifts as he progresses through cycles of decay and regrowth. After rejuvenating, he looks stout and healthy, his stride and posture almost regal. As he absorbs diseases from the environment, sickly fungus sprouts all over his body, weighing him down and draining his energy, both physically and spiritually. However he appears, his voice always carries the same grim determination and pride.
